Title: Tak til politikkerne, fordi I har taget ansvaret på jer: Det gamle gode liv på Bornholm
Content:
I am and will always be Bornholmer, but I have lived over for 25 years. Right now on another small alternative energy island, namely Samsø. One of today's highlights is the consuming of Bornholm's Tidende together with today's news on TV2/ Bornholm via the web.

My husband and I expect to settle on Bornholm within a number of years. Therefore, of course, I also follow the pending debate about the island's nursing home and have wanted to give my concern. I would also like to encourage other younger Bornholmers to do the same. If we do not die before, we and our ancestors all become old and will need more help and a suitable place to stay, no matter how we are at that time.

Thank you to the policies for taking responsibility for you for making the important decisions for all of us and thus dare to expose yourself to a little of each. I hope that you do not stare blindly at finance and location, but also dare to include the following considerations: What gives your own life content, what makes you good, what gives you joy in everyday life? And then just try to put the answers into a nursing home context! I think the open, honest exchange of personal notions of what one would think of as old - possibly weak and senile - can be a way to find a good solution together across political divisions.

Also, consider the synergy effect that can arise when all citizens are involved and help to find a solution! For example, my mother of 75, who has worked for many years as a nurse in the nursing home sector at Bornholm.

When I asked her what she wanted to put highest as a resident of a nursing home, part of her answer was: “What to do with fine tea kitchens that the old ones can't use anyway and who just become dangerous to the demented . No, what you need is care, care, care You can as a politician and architect impossible to be in everything, so just remember to ask those who help users, including the relatives and the nursing staff '! Homemade is found not only among politicians, officials and architects, but also among professionals in the nursing home sector and among all of us.

Therefore, one must continue to investigate what others have done and use it to develop something new and better with themselves.

It does not necessarily cost more in the long run to think alternatively. With the courage to bet on the so -called "soft values" now Bornholm may in the future go and generate know -how regarding elderly care, which will even be able to export and thus also draw "nursing home tourists" and more capital to the island! Incidentally, the LAG funds are not only reserved for the Health of the younger on Bornholm? How about hiring an elderly ambassador? And what about using rural funds to launch a super-modern energy-ridic center that is in an inspiring building style that falls appropriately into the Bornholm nature and building stock, so that the Bornholmers can keep looking at it and looking forward to To use it and possibly live there. For example, based on citizens' received wishes for their old age, an architectural competition could be printed, after which citizens should debate and vote on the proposals received.

My contemporary Norwegian uncle helped start a large and fantastic elderly center wonderfully located down to a beautiful fjord in Norway.

He was subsequently for many years leader of Henie-Constad Age of Earth.

Dignity, equality and good elderly life were the starting point, and the center was the most epoch -making in Europe at that time. There was a library, physiotherapy with associated swimming pool, large creative workshop, cafeteria for staff, users and guests overlooking the fjord and the nearby art center.

There was a large cozy decorated palm garden in connection with reception and kiosk, concert and lecture hall, hairdresser, foot therapy as well as a permanent nurse and specialist doctors who showed up on certain days. In addition, there was a more intimate daycare center with living room and piano, offers of communal dining, walking and driving trips in the beautiful area with appropriate companionship.

In connection with the site, an extremely imaginative and professional staff was hired.

Among other things, they arranged large carnival events with dressed-up users, Opera Live, large-scale Christmas Eve parties and so on.

The employees and the elderly who had their own user councils were so self -managing and enthusiastic that my uncle claimed that his most important job as a leader was to tice around the wards, drink coffee and dampen the mutineers, or give up his mind.

All including the politicians were papal of what they had started here - and in connection with the center, older housing and nursing homes of different design were built - depending on the users' care needs and the municipality's economy.

But wonder if not the concept itself attracted money from foundations, wills and the Treasury. There were also delegations from all over the world to see this epoch -making institution for the elderly.

As a teenager, I was employed as a summer holiday aid for several years at the center, where I met Japanese politicians on a tour. The place could still be a study trip worth for the Bornholm decision makers and advisory professionals, although a smaller framework and other priorities can easily do as well.

Part of us will lose memory and ability for verbal communication as we grow old. But even though certain body parts and brain cells set out, the basic feelings and senses will probably still be there.

If I need to be able to thrive, even though I might become demented, then I have to have something beautiful to look at, some fresh air to breathe, feel the weather, hear the songs of the birds, touch something and be touched by caring hands, the warming rays of the sun or The shower of the organ in an old, spiritual church.

My greatest wish is that I can sometimes come out and be in the beautiful Bornholm nature. And the least must be that I live in a place where I can look out the window and see a tree and feel the change of seasons, see the mearse on the feeding board and feel the life around me.

I have to be among living creatures every day, whether it's just a little cat, maybe just a teddy bear I think is alive and can hug - or the sheep, who calls on its lamb and mowing the grass in the fence around my nursing home.

A living being in motion that makes me forget that I was on my way away from the safe and safe, thus preventing me from getting lost in the forest, being driven into town or dumping in the harbor.

But the most important thing of all: I would like to end my life where there are loving caring and insightful people around me who have patience, tenderness and lots of time, understand my situation and would like to help me even if I can't Do something in return! Thus, I never forget a broadcast on TV where a music educator got old dementia at a nursing home to remember, hum or even sing their childhood songs by heart. It was gripping to see an old lady who, due to his friendly stamina, slowly thought of the melody and the text - and ended up singing it out of the vessel bellows as you saw a big beautiful smile spread over the old face . Music and song can reduce mental and physical pain. We all know that.

How and in what environment would you like to live and what care would you like to receive when you get old and weak yourself? Join the debate and help the policies with the decisions.

Write down your thoughts and send it to the municipality or Bornholm's Journal.

It must be just as good, if not better than uncertain liquid pension savings during this time.

At least I will look forward to reading the posts if some should be fresh and take up the challenge here in the newspaper.

Title: El bliver den primære energikilde i vores samfund: El( re) volutionen er kommet til øen
Content:
The time is running from the dogma that electricity is a dirty evil. EL paves the way for a much cleaner, safer and more efficient way of using energy.

Østkraft works with the overall Danish energy sector to make electric CO2 neutral. Therefore, it makes sense to allow electricity to replace oil and gas in our cars and homes - and let the energy system and transport system merge.

In other words, we are on the threshold of a "electricity resolution", which is a significant change in the energy system on Bornholm, as well as in the rest of Denmark.

This means that in a few years we drive from Aakirkeby to Allinge-Sandvig in silent cars powered by electricity.

The electric car charges while we are at work or at home. Our home and loner gi consumption will be to a greater extent IT controlled, so for example, the washing machine only starts when the power is cheap or the freezer turns off briefly for the sake of the electricity grid.

Electricity becomes the primary source of energy in our society, because electricity is increasingly becoming pure, safe and effective alternative.

The electricity system will be the lifeblood of our energy supply and will play together with district heating, subside agricultural biomass and the proportion of wind turbine power, which is doubled in ten years.

Every day the current in the Bornholm sockets becomes greener.

In just ten years, half of Denmark's electricity consumption will be covered by renewable energy.

Already, renewable energy is 47 per cent. of Østkraft's production and included the private wind turbines, production on Bornholm is up to 63 per cent. However, the proportion of renewable energy in the Bornholm sockets is only approx. 40 per cent, as part of the energy is exchanged via the submarine cable.

We are thus well on our way to the goal that Bornholm should be free of fossil fuels in 2025. Eastern power has also earlier this year submitted applications to Bornholm Regional Municipality on setting up several wind turbines that will further increase this proportion.

Østkraft hopes that the municipality looks positively on these wind turbine projects, which will mean a lot to Bornholm and will help to fulfill the municipality's energy strategy on Bornholm as a green energy island.

But the biggest change is not in the way we produce the energy. It will be in how we use the energy wisely. It will mean a thorough change of how we think about energy and how we will use it. The advice from us is: Use the power when it blows - give back power when the wind is lying off.

In the future, the hunt for cheap power will become part of your everyday life. You're going to spend a little more time at the dining table studying electricity prices, and you're going to decide when you think your car should refuel from the web and whether you want to sell some of the power on the battery back to the electricity grid .

Electric cars will soon be part of everyday life when the ongoing electric car projects, such as Edison and Mycar, get a foothold.

The projects must bring electric cars up to eye level, and Bornholm has a good opportunity, based on its unique geography, to be a front runner in this process as a demonstra tion project.

Thus, Bornholm can show the rest of Denmark, even the world, why the "elvolution" is a unique opportunity to think new. An initiative that will also generate business growth opportunities and jobs in the long term.

Basically, we can go two ways to let the development roll. You can sit back and wait for politicians to give the optimal framework for this to happen or you can begin the development yourself.

Østkraft and the rest of the Danish energy sector have taken the first steps towards the "Elvolution", which will make our energy consumption cleaner and free us from the oil.

For each day the power becomes greener.

Title: Masser af omstilling i kommunerne
Content:
At Bornholm you have the Bright Green Island concept and a vision of a CO2-neutral society in 10 years. But Bornholm is far from alone in focusing on sustainable transition and far from a leader. A lot is happening all around.

The network change now had an event at the newspaper Municipality on Saturday, where a number of municipalities contributed information about their conversion projects.

In Aalborg Municipality you have, for example.

established a decided center for green transition, which is aimed at both citizens and business. Sustainable business development unfolds in partnerships and with sustainable supervision and case management by the municipality, while a green agent has been targeted at citizens and also holds a sustainability festival one week a year. There you show off what it is you can and what you want.

In Kalundborg, the Danish Symbiosis Center has been established, which is trying to organize industrial production by supporting cooperation between the companies. There is a special focus on what was previously designated waste products in the companies.

You don't call it anymore, but resources that can be used for something else. For example, you get a residual product by cleaning the smoke of sulfur from a cancer work. The residual product is industrial tips, and where it was previously run into landfill, it is now diminished by a nearby plaster factory, which makes plasterboard of it.

On Samsø you have come right and have long since declared a renewable energy island. Already 10 years after the vision of becoming CO2 neutral, it was, and this has been done in extensive cooperation through an energy academy, where both the municipality, the companies and the grass roots participate. Wind turbines, solar energy and most recently a municipal ferry driven on gas are among some of the many initiatives on the island. The plan is also to establish a biogas plant that can supply energy to the municipal -owned ferry.

On the other hand, Samsø is not so good at ecology and recycling yet, the mayor said at the meeting. It needs to be addressed now.

Sønderborg Municipality has a goal of being CO2 neutral in 2029, and a wide range of initiatives are well underway to achieve that goal. Among other things, by paying attention to the energy consumption of the municipality's properties, and for example, school students get a text message when they have saved the energy at their school.

The municipality has also written down a green curriculum, so that kindergarten children and school students learn from the start to think energy -efficient, and they also come out to visit the companies.

The next step in Sønderborg is to switch the public transport from diesel to gas.

Incidentally, there was a clear common feature in the four municipalities' change process: Everyone in the municipality must be involved, and that is, the citizens, the young people, the associations, the grass roots, the business and so on.

Title: Ørsted vil have staten til at sætte Nordsøen-projekt i bero: Bornholm kan få landets største havvindmøllepark
Content:
Denmark's largest wind farm to date may be based on the Baltic Sea off Bornholm.

The energy company Ørsted has proposed the government to build a gigantic wind farm off Rønne.

The wind turbines must initially be able to deliver a production of 1000 megawatts, also called a gigawatt. In the longer term, the Bornholm Mill Park will be able to increase production by up to three to five gigawatts - enough power for up to five million households.

The project will make Bornholm home to a converter station that can pass on the power. Ørsted's plan also includes an electrolysis factory that can turn excess power into green fuel for ships, aircraft and trucks. However, Ørsted will place Ørsted in the metropolitan area, because much more fuel is used in and around Copenhagen than on Bornholm.

The first stage of the project will supply Bornholm, Zealand and Poland with Strøm. If you later build the park out to 3-5 gigawatts, it will also be able to export power to Sweden and Poland.

The most recently adopted wind farm, Thor, which will be off West Jutland, will, by comparison, have an effect of 800 megawatts.

Ørsted's proposal for the government is for Denmark to send an offshore wind project off Bornholm in tender before the Thor project.

At Ørsted, offshore wind turbine manager Martin Neubert believes that the project will be both more attractive and faster to realize than to build an artificial energy island in the North Sea, as the Thor project will require. Both Thor and its artificial island are written into the so -called understanding paper that the new government this summer came up with its support parties.

- At Bornholm you do not have to build and drain as in the North Sea. So you can use the infrastructure that is already in place, he says to Politiken.

Climate and Energy Minister Dan Jørgensen (S) calls the proposal "very exciting".

- It is good to see that the private actors are at the forefront of the green front line, he writes in a comment on Politiken.

Professor of Energy Economics Brian Vad Matthiesen from Aalborg University also finds the idea of ​​using Bornholm better than the idea of ​​offshore wind turbines centered on an artificial island in the North Sea.

- It is far more realizable than these airy thoughts about a huge energy island far out in the sea. The challenge lies in finding suitable locations for large quantities of renewable energy, which are at the same time close to some large consumer centers. This is an example of the fact that you can, he says to Politiken.

Mayor Winni Grosbøll (S) is highly excited about the proposal.

- On the whole, such a building will get rid of workplaces and activity on the whole island.

- In addition, such an offshore wind farm Bornholm positions as an energy island in the middle of the Baltic Sea. It's a huge chance for us, she tells Politiken.

Title: Rønne Havns ledelse gør status på tærsklen til 2020' ernes ventede vindmølleeventyr: Et årti, hvor havnen sigtede efter skyerne og gjorde skeptikerne til skamme
Content:
The 2020s indicate to be a decade in which climate measures will create great headwinds for the offshore wind turbine industry.

The companies that can expect great growth when states are increasing ambitions were gathered in November for a large European offshore congress in Copenhagen.

Because Ørsted had published a large -scale proposal to build offshore wind farms at Rønne Banke a few days before, Bornholm with connections to Zealand and Poland, Bornholm Tidende went to Windoffshore 2019 in the Bella Center in November.

I meet Thomas Bendtsen, CEO of Rønne Havn A/ S since 2011, and Chairman Thomas Thors, who joined as chairman in 2012, in the Foyer of the Exhibition Center. They seem extremely pleased with how things have evolved. The proposal from Ørsted (a few days after the offshore congress was incorporated into the Finance Act) is the latest indication that the port's expansion to about half a billion kroner will bear fruit. And the bright views are in stark contrast to the state of Rønne Harbor at the beginning of the decade, says Thomas Thors, who has difficulty hiding that he is captivated by the progress that has been made.

- Now I have gone here at the fair and looked at things in giant dimensions. What are they called now, those hinges? - A crank hook, the professional Thomas Bendtsen inserts.

- Yes, a crank hook that is bigger than myself and weighs many times more. It's great that we become part of that. Not many people believed when we started, says Thomas Thors, thinking back to the reactions that the people of the port met when they started dreaming big on behalf of Bornholm.

- We actually made a report five years ago by the Ministry of Business. It was at Sass Larsen's request, and it said that we should become part of the offshore sector, we could forget about.

Why? Because it was too expensive? - Because it was unrealistic, replies Thomas Thors.

- Yes, you couldn't see the possibilities, adds Thomas Bendtsen.

- They couldn't see Bornholm as a center for offshore. Despite that, we have worked unabated. Here the organization has done a great job, says Thomas Thors.

As one of the crucial turning points, he highlights the Windforce conference that took place at the Green Solution House in January 2016. Here the Bornholm actors made aware of what they had to offer.

- And since then it has gone to battle, and it manifests itself in the first place with Siemens Gamesa's project, which will come by the end of 2020, says Thomas Thors.

The new port area has been built so that it can carry the heavy wind turbine parts to be placed at the harbor before being transported to Kriegers Flak. The offshore wind farm will be with a capacity of 604 megawatts - which according to Vattenfall can cover the power consumption in 600,000 households - Denmark's largest offshore wind farm when it is completed by 2021.

The fact that Rønne Harbor should play a role did not necessarily lie in the cards when the crisis in 2013 scratched in Rønne Harbor. A limited profit of DKK 230,000 in 2012 was followed by a thunderous loss of DKK 8.5 million, partly due to large depreciation on a failed investment in the elaboration vessel Njord. The port's debt of DKK 140 million was a boulder around the leg and had to be reduced at the same time as the harbor's fixed costs had to be greatly reduced.

Thomas Thors stated in the newspaper that it was "absolutely necessary to increase the operating profit, as the port would otherwise not be able to make necessary investments if new business areas appear".

Under Thomas Bendtsen's leadership, Rønne Harbor took cutlery of the situation. The tariffs were turned up and turned down for the less profitable parts of the business. It became significantly more expensive for the ferry operators to use the port, which has resulted in a pending trial with the shipping company The Ferry.

The management made several outsourcing, and today the port no longer has contractors and pilots on the payroll or its own elaboration ship. Instead, the harbor today buys several services out of the house when needed.

The rescheduling was to result in an annual profit of DKK 7.5 million within five years, Thomas Thors said in 2013, but it was only a few years before the bottom line reached the desired level, and in 2017 the result of the year showed a twice as large surplus.


The absence of modesty

In September, the Executive Board's second member, CFO Max Hansen, said in an interview with Bornholm's Journal that the absence of Bornholm modesty at Thomas Bendtsen helped make a difference.

- There we got a proper losing in the ass. I can say that. He had some completely different ideas and visions for the company, Max Hansen said of the time after the accession of the East Jutland director.

When Thomas Bendtsen himself has to give his bid on how the port could climb up the hole, he points to the composition of the port's board, which primarily consists of people with concrete industry knowledge and experience.

- We may well say that without the professionalization of Rønne Harbor's board of directors, we would not have been in the favorable situation that we are in now. These are people with market insights and financial insights, people who are used to dealing with strategies targeted and risks associated with investments.

I wouldn't think we had come so far without, he says.

That Rønne Harbor, despite skepticism ranging from the government's office to the Tidende's reader writers dared to strive for a weighty place in the offshore hierarchy, Thomas Bendtsen also attributes the qualities of the board.

- What triggered it to begin with was the picture of the planned areas for offshore winds found around Bornholm. But it also matters that we have had some people on the board who have previously hunted some of these opportunities and who know that it is about sticking to the gut - even when some wise academics write that we can forget That, says Thomas Bendtsen.

- That's what has made us stand here today. I have no doubt about this, emphasizes the Port Director, who was employed by Copenhagen and Malmö's common harbor before coming to Bornholm.

At the beginning of November, Rønne Harbor's Board of Directors was named the Public Board of the Year of the Director of the Year on the agenda of the day. Rønne Harbor was praised for having a competence -based approach to putting together the board with the use of consultants to recruit board members.

"Rønne Harbor invests in and spends a lot of money on ensuring an efficient and professional board, but the bottom line speaks for itself - from DKK 250,000 to DKK 20 million.

In surplus within relatively few years, "was part of the rationale.

Fees in 2018 paid Rønne Harbor a total of DKK 815,000 in fees to the board.

Chairman Thomas Thors, who himself received DKK 140,000, explains that the professional board members' extensive experience in the port's business areas has been of great importance.

- It gives me as chairman of the board a sense of confidence that we are able to uncover the risks associated with this in advance. The whole way the expansion is approached has its root in the discussions we have had the board and the executive board, he says.

The expansion of the port complied with both the budget and the schedule. Thomas Thors believes it is related to the expertise of some of the members of the board.

- From the start we said we can't stand to make excesses. And we succeeded.

Need for increased activity The big thoughts were thought and implemented.

Next year, the wind turbine adventure begins.

The port's debt, which was reduced to DKK 37 million in 2018, was increased to DKK 298 million with one stroke, the latest accounts show, so there is a need for increased activity.

Title: Bornholm vinder stor EUenergipris og 500.000 euro
Content:
There are more than 2,000 inhabited islands in the EU. Of these, it is Bornholm who runs with the EU Commission's honor as the most responsible island.

"Responsible Island Prize" is called the Energy Prize, which rewards the development of new technology and renewable energy on islands.

- It's great to put it mildly, says Mayor Winni Grosbøll (S) to Bornholm's Journal.

She believes that the price is "the biggest recognition of Bornholm as a green test island for renewable energy and innovative technologies".

What exactly do you think it is that makes Bornholm receive this honor? - The title goes to the work that has been done on Bornholm for some years now. It goes to the ambition to make Bornholm fossil -free and to base the energy system on renewable energy. It goes to the technological transition - that we today produce our energy with solar panels, wind, biomass and biogas - but also our way of involving citizens by trying to get them to take responsibility. For example, by providing grants for remodeling of houses, the training of green craftsmen and other things that have been done around Bright Green Island, says the mayor.


Prize must go to new pool

The price comes with just over DKK 3.7 million.

Winni Grosbøll suggests that the prize sum should go to create a new pool that can support the continued green transition.

The goal of a new pool is to ensure that "Bornholm remains the leading energy island, as such a position can lead to massive investments, jobs and be an attraction in itself and be attractive to the many thousands of tourists who visit Bornholm", It says in a press release issued by the regional municipality.

Winni Grosbøll tells Bornholm Tidende that projects focusing on the transport sector and the production of fuel using power from offshore wind turbines (Power-2-X) can be the next step for Bornholm.


Economically sustainable

The regional municipality has signed up for the competition together with Bornholm Energi and Forsyning (BEOF), where department head Klaus Vesløv is also excited about the award.

- We at Bornholm have been able to make a conversion of an energy system with sun, wind, biomass and biogas. This is what we can hear that the EU acknowledges quite strongly, says Klaus Vesløv, Beof.

- We have done it in a way that is financially sustainable. It is something that we Bornholmers must be extremely proud of. It's actually really big, because it's a huge pat on the shoulder, says Klaus Vesløv, who recalls that Bornholm's progress in the daily debate can be easily overlooked.

- When you stand in the middle of it, it can be difficult in everyday life to notice. But when you get a little distance, it is actually something that arouses attention.


Minister: Pioneing country

The title went to Bornholm in front of Samsø, which also profiles itself like Green Island. The fact that two Danish island communities apply at European level also excite the government.

- It's hard not to be very proud of Denmark when two Danish islands clear the table and sit in both first and second place.

It shows that Denmark - and not least Bornholm and Samsø - goes ahead and shows the world how green transition can succeed in practice. It is precisely the kind of initiative and real life that Samsø and Bornholm exhibit that helps to make Denmark a green pioneering country with climate solutions that make a difference at home and can inspire around the world, says climate and energy minister Dan Jørgensen (S ) in a press release.

Representatives from Bornholm should have been in Brussels soon to receive the award, but the award has been postponed by the autumn of 2020 due to the Coronavirus epidemic.

At Bornholm we have been able to make a conversion of an energy system with sun, wind, biomass and biogas.

This is what we can hear that the EU acknowledges quite strongly.

Klaus Vesløv, Head of Department at Beof.


Responsible Island Prize

Responsible Island Prize will be awarded by the European Commission in 2019 and 2020, and Bornholm is awarded the first place in the 2019 edition.

The first prize is 500,000 euros (about DKK 3.73 million), while second place (Samsø) and third place (Orkney Islands, the UK) receive 250,000 and 100,000 euros respectively.

The three highlighted initials "res" are an abbreviation for "Renewable Energy Solutions", renewable energy solutions.

It is an energy price that rewards local, renewable energy production in electricity, heating and cooling of housing and transport.

"There are more than 2,000 inhabited islands in the EU. They are ideal test laboratories to develop innovative energy technology and can serve as general models of energy conversion in smaller communities," the European Commission writes of the purpose of the competition.

The award is awarded on the basis of these criteria :? The proportion of renewable energy produced with innovative energy technologies? Environmental and socio -economic sustainability and impact? Involvement of citizens and the local community? The opportunity to replicate the solution elsewhere Source: The European Commission.

    Klaus Vesløv - is excited.

Title: Bornholm i ny hovedrolle
Content:
588 square meters - approximately 1.4 percent of Denmark's total area. A coastline of 158 kilometers - Denmark's fifth largest island. The distance to the nearest Danish coast is 135 kilometers. It is significantly shorter to Germany - 88 kilometers. And only 37 kilometers to Sweden.

There is nothing in the above data on Bornholm that indicates that in the future we should play a starring role in major national conditions, let alone international.

Although the Bornholmers are aware of their qualities and special conditions, and often smiles a little head -shaking and indulgent of them "over", self -awareness is often mixed with a kind of humility where one does not breathe unnecessarily.

And the question is whether we are mentally able to hijack the government's desire for Bornholm to be the foundation of one of the country's two future energy islands to play a starring role in a conversion of Danish energy policy, which is among the world's most ambitious .

We can shoot the chest out. There is no need for excessive humility. Bornholm can become a new center.

The hardest thing can be to get used to the new starring role.

Title: Power-to-x i mindre skala på Bornholm: Beof er med i elektrolyseprojekt
Content:
Bornholm Energi and Forsyning (BEOF) is working to participate in several projects where electrolysis will be tested on a smaller scale on Bornholm.

One of them - under the name Offshore Energy Hubs - the municipality's finance committee in March chose to support with a million kroner, and the project, which is led by the Technical University of Denmark and is an initial step on the road to the creation of an energy island, has a budget of over 30 Million kroner. It has the participation of large companies such as Ørsted, MAN Energy Solutions, Siemens, Haldor Topsøe in addition to Beof and the Danish energy authorities.

One of the goals of the research project, which has not yet received air under the wings, is to develop "prototypes for combined production and transmission of electricity and hydrogen from wind energy", says a fact sheet from DTU that the committee politicians related to when they granted Money for the project.


Starting to go strongly

Klaus Vesløv, Head of Department at Beof and a member of the municipality's newly created climate committee, says there is a great commercial interest in power-to-X technology, where the large quantities of the future electricity from offshore wind turbines are used to make hydrogen and synthetic fuel.

- It's starting to go strong. Therefore, we also find that interest and developmental crowns in looking at hydrogen as a real opportunity in the commercially available market are accelerating quite rapidly. That is one of the reasons why we are leaning into it now, because we have an interest in helping to move it - and of course at the same time help to attract investments to Bornholm, says Klaus Vesløv, who is adhering by the well -known partners.

- The partners who join the projects are those who help move the agenda.

They have enormous interests in making it succeed as soon as possible.


Active Ørsted

Ørsted has identified fuel production as a new business area, for electrolysis technology is a crucial prerequisite for the full potential of offshore wind to be utilized. Ørsted is also part of the consortium, which near Copenhagen will build a giant electrolysis plant, which will receive the energy from the future offshore wind turbines near Bornholm.

Klaus Vesløv believes it is logical that Ørsted, Copenhagen Airport and the other companies will place a large part of hydrogen production in Copenhagen.

Is there a risk of Bornholm being overlooked in this regard? - We work with BRK, Rønne Harbor and other good forces on not happening, and in the project there is a plan to explore the possibility of a larger electrolysis plant at Bornholm. But it is clear that one should not establish an electrolysis plant on Bornholm of a size that can be used with the airport and everything else.

It makes great sense at all levels to put it where consumption is greatest. It has never been expected that the world's largest electrolysis plant should be located on Bornholm. It would have been to shoot gray sparrows with guns, says Klaus Vesløv, and immediately emphasizes: - It is the aim that an electrolysis plant must also be established on Bornholm, but of course on a completely different scale than what one is talking about in Copenhagen.

Is an electrolysis plant with shipping in mind or the Bornholm energy consumption? - This is actually one of the things to try to find out in the experimental projects we are struggling to be linked to, says Klaus Vesløv.

In the project under the direction of DTU, the idea is for the parties to find out how hydrogen production can be organized most effectively, as well as assessing the potential of the various possible consumers.

- There is a very obvious opportunity to look at ship transport, both our own (ferries, ed.) And also the many ships that pass Bornholm. It is also obvious to look at heavy transport, and whether the surplus heat generated when producing hydrogen can be used in our district heating system, says Klaus Vesløv, who points out that BEOF's participation in the projects is based on the condition that they are cost neutral .

Beof's overall commitment to the Offshore Energy Hubs project is approximately DKK 1.7 million, equivalent to about three man-years over four years. The Innovation Fund is in the process of assessing the project.

The partners who join the projects are those who help move the agenda. They have enormous interests in making it succeed as soon as possible.

Klaus Vesløv Head of Department in BEOF and a member of the municipality's newly created climate committee.

Title: Lokalt havvindmølleprojekt ud for Arnager et stort skridt nærmere virkelighed: Statsgaranti giver lokal vindmøllepark vind i sejlene
Content:
In the Nitiative Group for Bornholm Havvindmøllepark has received a guarantee from the Danish Energy Agency. This is stated by the initiative group in a newsletter that has just been sent out.

Thus, the dream of establishing a folk -owned offshore wind farm on Rønnebakke has moved a big step closer to reality.

The idea of ​​a 100 percent locally owned offshore wind farm saw the light of day in March 2019, half a year before Ørsted launched his large project at Rønne Banke.

The Danish Energy Agency's guarantee is DKK 475,000. With it in hand, Bornholm's offshore wind farm can now take out a bank loan to be used to pay for the preliminary investigations that will determine the investment and operating costs of a coastal offshore wind farm next to Arnager.

Bornholm's offshore wind's project is proposed to be located approximately nine kilometers south of Arnager and Rønne Airport, while Ørsted's wind turbines are scheduled to be erected at least 20 kilometers from the Bornholm coast.

With its eight wind turbines, Bornholm's offshore wind's project is on a much smaller scale than Ørsted's billionaire project. But the national wind turbine project, which according to the government's plans will supply two gigawatts, does not make the folk -owned mill park superfluous, says the initiative group's person, Helle Munk Ravnborg.

- Their project is at least ten times larger than ours. But the Bornholm offshore wind project is at 100 megawatts, and it is still a large wind farm that will be able to produce enough energy to cover Bornholm's consumption and more, says Helle Munk Ravnborg.

- This means that Bornholm now has a real chance of fulfilling his goal of being self -sufficient with green and sustainable current in 2025.


Ready for the next step in July

Already this week, the initiative group will take out a bank loan at Merkur Andelskasse, which has shown interest in the project in advance.

Then sign a contract with the consultants who will make the initial calculations.

After that, it is expected to go strong: "It is our expectation that the result of the initial studies will be ready at the beginning of July. If they show that we can expect a sensible project economy, we can take the next step and start to start Prepare for an actual preliminary study permit for the Danish Energy Agency, while also taking steps to establish a Bornholm offshore wind turbine, ”the newsletter states.

Although it now seems that, among other things, Ørsted, Maersk and DSV will establish a large electrolysis plant near Copenhagen with electricity from the upcoming Energiø in the Baltic Sea, Bornholm's Small Wind Wind Farm will probably also start a collaboration with Bornholm Energi and Forsyning on to produce its own hydrogen -based fuel in the future. With the opportunity to make profits to the shareholders, ie Bornholm citizens, businesses and associations.

- Until now we have been limited by the search cable to Sweden, which can only transport just under 60 megawatts. So, of course, we are excited about whether the state and Energinet choose to establish a larger cable connection in the Baltic Sea, which also reaches Bornholm, which we can then get permission to connect us, says Helle Munk Ravnborg.

The two projects - the small folk -owned and the big private - in the opinion of Ravnborg do not exclude each other.

- They take place independently, but with benefits for us if we can devote excess energy via a new cable, she says.


Tang and mussel gardens

Bornholm's offshore wind is, according to the initiative group, a local initiative which aims to obtain local activity that extends beyond the production of wind energy.

The Danish Energy Agency's guarantee therefore also makes it possible to work on the plans to establish an electrolysis plant on Bornholm, and the initiative has already been taken to explore the possibilities of establishing seaweed and mussel gardens around the offshore wind farm.

Bornholm's offshore wind turbines are scheduled to start spinning in 2025.

This means that Bornholm now has a real chance of fulfilling his goal of being self -sufficient with green and sustainable power in 2025.

Helle Munk Ravnborg Initiative group for Bornholm's offshore wind farm.


The great vision

In 2008, Bornholm Regional Municipality adopted a goal that Bornholm should be CO2-neutral with a consumption based solely on sustainable and renewable energy in 2025.

In 2019, however, the municipal council decided to scrap plans to set up more wind turbines on land, and until recently it has made it uncertain whether the target for 2025 could be achieved.

Since then it has gone strong. In November 2019, Ørsted presented a large -scale plan to establish energy islands in the state offshore wind turbine areas in the North Sea and in the Baltic Sea, and both Mayor Winni Grosbøll and Port Director Thomas Bendtsen responded with enthusiasm when the government launched a new climate play two weeks ago, UP: Bornholm is now scheduled to be made to Energiø by establishing and connect up to 2 GW of offshore wind by 2030 with connections to Zealand and Poland.

In the long term, Ørsted's vision includes several mill parks and any cable connections to both Sweden and Germany in what can reach a capacity of 3-5 GW or more. The task must be in state tender.

Title: Energistyrelsen har udarbejdet en finscreening af fremtidens vindmølleområder med megen interessant information: 14 ting du bør vide om havvind ved Bornholm
Content:
LANDFORBINDELSE ELLER ENERGIØER? Fredag i sidste uge offentliggjorde Energistyrelsen en finscreening af fremtidens havvindmølleområder i det danske farvand. I screeningen er områderne opdelt i to grupper; tre havvindmølleparker med direkte forbindelse til land (Nordsøen I, Hesselø i Kattegat og Kriegers Flak ved Møn) og havvindmølleparker med forbindelse til energiøer (Bornholm I og II samt tre områder længere ude i Nordsøen).

De to områder ved Bornholm regnes for at tilhøre den sidste gruppe, energiøer/ hubs, selv om teknologien fra havvindmølleparkerne og ind til Bornholm er den samme som i den første kategori. Men i modsætning til de førstnævnte projekter vil parker i Østersøen yderligere kræve, at der anlægges nye eksportkabler til Sjælland og nabolandene, for at strømmen efter bearbejdelse på Bornholm kan fragtes videre.

I Nordsøen skal de funktioner, der mod øst finder sted inde på selve Bornholm, foregå på en kunstig ø.

Etableringen af energiøer giver mulighed for at bygge væsentlig flere havvindmølleparker i nye områder.

2 REGERINGEN SATSER PÅ BÅDE ØST OG VEST I dansk farvand findes der ifølge Energistyrelsen 14 etablerede havvindmølleparker med en samlet kapacitet på 1.699 megawatt (MW), og i de kommende år er flere nye på vej.

I den nye screening indgår ikke allerede besluttede projekter som første del af Kriegers Flak (600 MW) og Thor (800-1000 MW) i Nordsøen.

Under den tidligere regering blev det besluttet at opføre tre offshoreparker på hver mindst 800 MW, og Thor, som ventes at blive tilsluttet elnettet i 2025, er den første af disse parker. Den nuværende socialdemokratiske regering har føjet flere gigawatt til de grønne ambitioner. I udspillet til en klimahandlingsplan foreslår regeringen at opføre en energiø i Østersøen på to gigawatt samt en energiø i Nordsøen på to gigawatt med plads til mindst 10 gigawatt på sigt. Begge skal oprettes inden 2030.

3 EN, TO ELLER TRE GIGAWATT VED BORNHOLM I screeningen, som rådgivningsfirmaet Cowi har lavet for Energistyrelsen, undersøges tre scenarier ved Bornholm: En, to eller tre gigawatt. I det mindste eksempel er beregningerne lavet på baggrund af området Bornholm I, der ligger længst mod vest. Ved to gigawatt skal begge områder i brug, og der skal opføres 67 vindmøller i hvert felt. Og skal der opføres tre gigawatt, kræver det, at de screenede områder stort set udnyttes fuldt ud. Det indebærer, at der skal opføres 200 vindmøller i alt - fordelt på 78 i Bornholm I og 122 i Bornholm II-feltet, hvis centrum ligger stik syd for Rønne.

På de detaljerede kort over to GW-screeningen står der færre møller længst mod øst og syd i feltet Bornholm II.

Mellem de to områder ved Bornholm er et areal med høj følsomhed, der forhindrer opstilling af vindmøller.

4 MØLLERNE ER GIGANTISKE I screeningen opererer Cowi med, at vindmølleparkerne i Nordsøen og på Bornholm skal bestå af 15 megawatt-møller, den næste generation af offshore-vindmøller.

15 MW-møller forventes at være på markedet i 2030. I standardmodellerne, som den internationale organisation IEA Wind TCP har lavet for møller af den størrelse, er mølletårnet 150 meter højt, og vingerne har en diameter på 240 meter. Det vil sige, at vingespidsen på dets højeste punkt vil være 270 meter over vandet.

Under havoverfladen stikker tårnet yderligere 75 meter ned, og ved havdybder på 30 meter betyder det, at 45 meter skal fæstnes i undergrunden.

Den samlede vægt for en vindmølle kommer til at overstige 3.000 ton.

5 20 KILOMETER FRA KYSTEN - ELLER NÆSTEN Når myndighederne planlægger fremtidens enorme havvindmølleparker indgår et afstandskrav, der sætter en del begrænsninger. Parkerne skal ligge mindst 20 kilometer fra kysten, og som det ses på kortet udelukker dette krav en størstedelen af de indre danske farvande. Andre steder betyder havdybder over 50 meter, at disse dele af det danske territorialfarvand ikke indgår i screeningerne. Det gælder blandt andet en større del af Østersøen øst for Bornholm.

Omkring Bornholm efterlader det to områder på den underjordiske højderyg i retning af Rügen. Indtil i år har et tredje område længere mod sydøst indgået i planlægningen, men det er taget ud på grund af nærheden til polsk territorium.

De detaljerede kort over de tilbageværende områder - Bornholm I og Bornholm II - viser imidlertid, at de nordligste møller ligger lige inden for 20 kilomterzonen fra kysten, og der kan ikke være tvivl om, at møllerne vil blive synlige fra Rønne og den sydbornholmske kyst.

Mere kystnære havvindmølleparker kan dog fortsat bygges, hvilket det folkeejede projekt Bornholms Havvind med otte vindmøller cirka ni kilometer fra kysten er et eksempel på.

6 PROJEKTET ER MULIGT Screeningen viser overordnet, at det er muligt at bygge havmølleparker med forbindelse til en energiø/ hub i alle de undersøgte områder, hvilket inkluderer 10 gigawatt i de tre områder i Nordsøen, som skal kobles på en energiø, samt tre gigawatt i Bornholm I+ II.

Dertil kommer yderligere fem GW i parkerne med direkte landforbindelse, Kriegers Flak på 1 gigawatt, Hesselø på 1 gigawatt samt Nordsøen I på tre gigawatt. Screeningen har altså fundet plads til 18 gigawatt i alt.

Dog tager Energistyrelsen et par forbehold for områderne i Østersøen. Det anbefales, at " der i delområder ved Bornholm og Kriegers Flak gennemføres en mere detaljeret analyse af følsomheden af udvalgte fuglearter i forhold deres påvirkning ved opstilling af havvind, ligesom der også ved flere af de screenede områder vil skulle tages højde for blandt andet kabler, rørledninger og eksisterende sejruter", skriver Energistyrelsen i konklusionen.

7 KUNSTIG ENERGIØ ER KUN MARGINALT DYRERE Det anslås at koste 58,26 milliarder kroner at opføre havvindmølleparker ved Bornholm med en samlet kapacitet på tre gigawatt. Det er cirka 370 millioner kroner billigere end de beregnede investeringer til tre gigawatt i energiø-projektet i Nordsøen. Prisforskellen er under én procent.

På Bornholm er udgifterne til fundamenter cirka en milliard kroner lavere i forhold til i Nordsøen, og kabelforbindelserne til havs mellem mølleklynger og transformatoranlægget koster 2,4 milliarder kroner mindre i Østersøen.

Ved at udnytte Bornholm faste grund undgår man udgiften på 3,6 milliarder kroner til etablering af energiø, som kun indgår i regnestykket for Nordsøen. Men alt dette opvejes af, at udgifterne til nye eksportkabler til Sjælland og Polen for Bornholm er værdisat til 23,7 milliarder kroner - hvilket er 6,7 milliarder kroner mere end kabeludgifterne i Nordsøen.

" Eksportsystemet ved Bornholm forventes at blive noget dyrere end i Nordsøen grundet behovet for havbaserede AC-transformerstationer og længere eksportkabler til Bornholm og videre til DK2 (strømnettet i Østdanmark, red.) og udlandet", skriver Cowi i rapporten.

En enkelt ting er dog værd at bemærke ved regnestykket i Nordsøen. Udgifterne til anlæg af en kunstigt bygget energiø i Nordsøen er baseret på " et meget groft overslag". Med dette forbehold er en kunstig ø med en total kapacitet til 10 gigawatt prissat til 12 milliarder kroner, og i sammenligningen indgår 30 procent af disse udgifter, da de 3 gigawatt i screeningen svarer til 30 procent.

8 ... OG ER EN BEDRE ØKONOMISK CASE END BORNHOLM Cowi har rangordnet de undersøgte scenarier ud fra de langsigtede udgifter i forhold til de producerede strømmængder. " Levetidsomkostninger" kaldes nøgletallet. Beregningerne viser, at det - med de valgte forudsætninger - ser ud til bedre at kunne betale sig at investere i Nordsøen.

Nordsøen - tre GW: 461 kroner per MWh.

Bornholm - to GW (2 x 67 vindmøller i Bornholm I + II): 483 kroner per MWh Bornholm - tre GW (Totalt 200 havvindmøller i Bornholm I+ II): 492 kroner per MWh Bornholm - en GW (67 vindmølle i området Bornholm I): 495 kroner per MWh Beregningerne er baseret på, at havvindmølleparkerne har en levetid på 30 år og en diskonteringsrate på 8%.

Tre GW-projektet på Bornholm er mindre effektivt end to GW, fordi vindmøllerne vil komme til at stå tættere og dække for vinden, hvilket resulterer i et forhøjet skyggetab.

9 VINDEN ER BEDST I NORDSØEN Når anlæg i Nordsøen er billigere end alle tre eksempler ved Bornholm, skyldes dette en kombination af dårligere vindressource ved Bornholm og dyrere eksportforbindelser med øget tab ved Bornholm, skriver Cowi.

Vindens kvalitet bedømmes ud fra middelvindhastigheden i 150 meters højde. I Nordsøen blæser vinden med 10,73 meter per sekund, mens den syd for Bornholm i gennemsnit giver 9,92 meter per sekund.

Det elektriske tab i kabler og eksportsystemet anslår Cowi til at være ti procent større på Bornholm end i Nordsøen.

På bundlinjen resulterer det i en større enrgiproduktion i Nordsøen. Havvindmølleparker med en kapacitet på tre gigawatt vil i Nordsøen producere 13.478.374 MWh om året, og på Bornholm er produktionen beregnet til 12.396.929 MWh om året.

De store energimængder vil skabe et kæmpe overskud af el og lægge grunden for en omfattende elektrificering af samfundet. Den beregnede produktion ved en tre GW-park omkring Bornholm vil kunne forsyne over tre millioner husstande med strøm.

10 VIGTIGT FUGLEOMRÅDE Den vestlige del af Bornholm II ligger i et internationalt vigtigt fugleområde. I området overvintrer havlit, fløjlsand og sortand, der blandt andet lever af blåmuslinger, som der er store forekomster af i området. I denne del af Bornholm II kan der således være risiko for, at disse arter vil blive fortrængt fra et vigtigt fourageringsområde, hvis der opstilles havvindmøller, skriver Cowi. Området er et såkaldt IBA-område og er udpeget af den Internationale organisation Bird Life International, men det er ikke omfattet af internationale direktiver eller konventioner som for eksempel Natura 2000. Cowi anbefaler, at der gennemføres en detaljeret analyse af følsomheden af disse fuglearter.

Desuden er Østersøområdet mellem Danmark, Sverige og Tyskland vigtig for trane-og rovfugletræk.

I Bornholm I og II ligger i trækruterne for fugle, der yngler i Sverige og Norge, og som overvintrer mod syd. " Der kan være risiko for, at opstilling af havvindmøller kan forårsage en barrierevirkning eller udgøre en kollisionsrisiko for trækkende fugle", skriver Cowi, der også lægger op til en mere omfattende analyse af trækfugle.

11 HAVBUNDEN ER " MINDRE VELEGNET" VED BORNHOLM Mens undergrunden i Nordsø-områderne i screeningen betegnes som " velegnet", får havbunden i de to bornholmske felter bedømmelsen " mindre velegnet". " Bornholm I og Bornholm II er rangeret lavere end Nordsøen II og Nordsøen III grundet den mindre tykkelse af glaciale sedimenter og dermed mindre dybde til hårde bjergarter.

" Området vurderes som mindre velegnet for fundering med monopæle (fundamentet under vand, red.), idet installation af monopæle besværliggøres af mulig hårdt moræneler med sten, højtliggende, mulig hårdt og flintrig kalk, samt højtliggende, muligvis cementerede marine aflejringer", skriver Cowi.

Konklusionen er dog, at der på nuværende tidspunkt og vidensniveau ikke er fundet geologiske eller geotekniske faktorer, der vurderes at kunne forhindre placering af havvindmøllefundamenter. Alle områder kan derfor anvendes til opstilling af havvindmøller ud fra en geologisk og geoteknisk betragtning.

12 BEGRÆNSET PLADS I EL-NETTET De to danske el-net har en begrænset kapacitet.

I den seneste energiaftale fra 2018 er gjort plads til 5,3 gigawatt til udbygning af havvind - 3,3 GW i det vestlige net og to GW i det østlige (DK2), som Bornholm samt Hesselø og Kriegers Flak ville skulle levere til. På grund af kapacitetsloftet antager Cowi, at kun en GW produceret ved Bornholm skal tilgå det danske net, mens de resterende en-to GW skal sendes til udlandet, formentlig gennem den foreslåede forbindelse til Polen.

I screeningen er de forskellige havvindmølleparker gjort uafhængigt af hinanden. Men i praksis skal udbygningen af havvind i Nordsøen, Hesselø, Kriegers Flak samt Bornholm anskues i et samlet hele, " da valget af et bestemt område vil have direkte konsekvenser for øvrige belyste områder," skriver Cowi.

13 FRA VEKSELSTRØM TIL JÆVNSTRØM PÅ LAND I vindmøllernes turbiner produceres vekselstrøm med en spænding på 66 kilovolt. Til havs, nær vindmøllerne, skal der opføres transformerplatforme, hvor spændingen hæves til 220 kilovolt.

Herfra kommer eksportsystemet til at blive opbygget med parallelle kabelsystemer, der hver har en samlet installeret effekt på 500 megawatt.

Installeres der to gigawatt, skal der altså føres fire eksportkabler ind til land, hvor transformerstation nær kysten omformer vekselstrømmen til jævnstrøm.

I eksportkabler fragtes 220 kilovolt jævnstrøm til modtagerne af strømmen, hvilket sandsynligvis bliver Sjælland og Polen.

14 HASLE ER I SPIL Hvor på Bornholm skal landanlægget ligge? I screeningen er et område lige nord for Hasle udpeget som stedet, hvor strømmen skal føres i land. Det er her, Energinet har udpeget et areal på fire-seks hektar, hvor der er plads til anlægget.

" Ilandføringen er valgt i et område med marker og vurderes derfor velegnet til formålet. (...) Fremføring af eksportkablerne fra ilandføringsstedet til Ny Hovedstation Hasle vurderes til at have lav kompleksitet, der skal dog tages højde for klippegrund," skriver Cowi.

Til Bornholms Tidende oplyser Energinets chefprojektleder Poul-Jacob Vilhelmsen, at tegnestiften lige nord for Hasle skal opfattes som " et tankeeksperiment", der er lavet for at have nogle faste antagelser at gå ud fra til screeningen. Da anlægget skal forbinde kabler havvindmølleparkerne med forbindelse til både Polen og Sjælland, giver det mening at placere hovedstationen langs det meste af den bornholmske syd-og vestkyst, hvor der måtte være plads. Der er brug for et område på fire-seks hektar med åbne marker til lav bebyggelse.

- I realiteten kunne du tage stationen op og trække den rundt langs kysten. Det vil komme helt an på forprojektet, siger Poul-Jacob Vilhelmsen om placeringen af landanlægget.

    Øverst ses Cowis bud på, hvordan vindmøllerne kan placeres, hvis der skal installeres 2 gigawatt. Hver prik repræsenterer en 15 MW-mølle, og der planlægges med 67 Møller i hvert af de to områder. Den lilla linje er 20 km fra Bornholms kyst. På det nederste kort er fordelingen af de 200 Møller, der er behov for, hvis kapaciteten skal op på 3 gigawatt.

Title: Regionskommunen opretter ny grøn tilskudspulje til større projekter: Millioner fra EU-præmie skal uddeles i 2020 og 2021
Content:
A large cash prize of 0.5 million euros - or 3.73 million Danish kroner - fell into Bornholm Regional Municipality's turban in April, when the European Commission awarded Bornholm Responsible Island Prize 2019. Signed up and delivered material for the competition, which rewarded renewable energy solutions in European islands.

Now the money has to work out. Municipal Director Johannes Nilsson proposes that the prize be awarded to local energy projects.

The administration has submitted a list of criteria that the Economic, Business and Plan Committee must distribute the money. On Wednesday, the committee discussed which model pool should be organized after; Whether the office must select and divest applicants prior to political assessment or whether the whole process should be a pure political task for the members of the committee.

The choice fell on the recommended model, where the applications are received administratively, and it is assessed to be assessed whether they fall under the announced criteria in relation to, among other things, content, amount, coherence and co -financing.

If the administration considers that applications are within the criteria, they will be added to political treatment at the meeting of the Economic, Business and Plan Committee that fits into the process. That model recommends the committee to the municipal council.


At least a quarter of a million

The municipal director suggests that projects of a certain size should be taken into account.

"Since the pool has a strategic aim, applications under DKK 250,000 will, as a starting point, get an administrative refusal," writes the municipality's administration about the model, where the administration has influence.

The applications that the administration considers to be within the criteria must for political treatment at a meeting of the Financial, Business and Plan Committee.

BEOF will be taken on advice and provide professional assessments of the projects before political treatment.

"If Bornholm's Energy and Supply are the applicant itself, no professional assessment will be obtained from Bornholm's Energy and Supply," it is emphasized in the case.

The municipal director proposes that the pool be awarded three rounds at six months. At each application round, the pool will consist of DKK 1,240,000. It is proposed that the first application deadline will be in October 2020.

Since the pool has a strategic aim, applications under DKK 250,000 will, as a rule, receive an administrative refusal administration in the case.


Requirements for applicants

Associations and companies with CVR number have access to apply for grants from the new pool. The municipal administration proposes that the projects must meet these criteria: The project supports the municipal council's visions for green transition and the possibility of becoming a "Energiø" project to take place locally on Bornholm, and results must be delivered on Bornholm It must be stated that the project is promoting Innovation in green transition and requires local commitment positive derivative effects affect the Bornholm community including creating more jobs The purpose of the project must be compatible with the municipal authority and other Danish legislation Applications will be assessed by the Economic, Business and Plan Committee on the basis of: The effect on the green transition and Bornholm's opportunity to become an Energiø degree of innovation in the project Positive Derived Effects on the Bornholm Society Including workplaces Collaboration with local actors including Bornholm Energi and Supply the applied grant amount must be at a minimum 250,000 kr.

The grant is used for co -financing projects, and thus not full financing.

Title: Dansk Metal Bornholm kigger ind i svær øvelse ovenpå coronakrisen: De ledige skal blive på Bornholm
Content:
The Corona crisis has hardened on the Bornholm industry, where the exporting companies in particular are lagging behind.

This is noticed by the trade union Dansk Metal Bornholm, where you currently have 177 unemployed members.

Compared to a number that last year was on only 15 unemployed members, it is now another situation that is handled in the union.

- Course and qualification are the way forward.

Our unemployed must constantly dress better, so that when employment again signs up in the fall, they are ready and qualified to take on work, says chairman Klaus Holm.

Because although there is a long way between the jobs right now, the chairman has no doubt that Bornholm will soon lack qualified work power.

And here it is about maintaining the unemployed, he emphasizes.

- We are convinced that we will be missing labor within two years. I have no doubt at all when I look for our number of members and the age composition we have. So while many may feel tempted to travel over where the wheels get started faster, our message is: Beating cold water in the blood and stay here, says Klaus Holm.


Gaps in the labor market

For the past few months, Dansk Metal Bornholm has been busy guiding members.

Here, the exercise has also consisted of redirecting the unemployed to industries that were currently missing hands.

For example, 10 blacksmiths have helped take a large driver's license, because here and now there is a lack of labor for truck drivers.

- Many people have shopped online in the corona time, so truck drivers have been in demand, says Klaus Holm.

Dansk Metal Bornholm has also offered security courses to equip their employees for employment in the upcoming plans for Bornholm as Energiø and Home of Store Wind Farm Parks, and will, in collaboration with Campus Bornholm, qualify members with, among other things, welding and robot courses.

- We work purposefully here in the house to be ready as soon as the companies get started again. Then at least there are not some of our members who have to be left because they are missing a certain cerrated clerk, says Klaus Holm.

Title: Kystnær havvindmøllepark med i kommunens energipolitik
Content:
Later in the year, the municipal council is expected to adopt a new energy policy.

The regional municipality has hired the external company Logics to do an analytical preparation on which energy policy and strategy must be built. Three scenarios must be counted, and one of them is based on the succeeding that a coastal offshore wind farm of 90-100 megawatts is succeeded.

- Our offshore wind farm is included in two of the scenarios that are counted on the committee, so there is still political support for the project, says Helle Munk Ravnborg, who, in addition to being a person for the initiative group behind a locally owned offshore wind farm, has been appointed as one of two citizen representatives in the advisory climate and sustainability committee, which was formed in 2019.

One scenario includes the coastal offshore wind farm alone. In the second scenario, it is intended together with one or more larger offshore wind farms at a distance of at least 20 kilometers from the coast of Bornholm - ie the large -scale Energiø project.

The last scenario is "no new wind turbines".

The presentation for the analysis work states that the simulation of the coastal offshore wind farm must be based on a model where "the energy is brought ashore on Bornholm and transformed and added to the current electricity grid to be reinforced. Possible commissioning 2025.

The scenario is prepared within the capacity frame of the current submarine cable. "The analysis must uncover what consequences an offshore wind farm on Rønnebakke will have for the total energy system and how the energy from the wind turbines can be used for the production of hydrogen and synthetic fuels - a process that Often called "Power-to-X".

The possibilities in, for example, the storage and transformation of excess energy as well as green change of transport and buildings will also be described and evaluated in the analysis of the three scenarios that will soon be handed over to the municipality.


Benefits with Energiø

Since the commissariat of energy policy was adopted in March, the most ambitious scenario has moved much closer, as a large political majority in Christiansborg decided in June that offshore wind farms should be erected at two gigawatts near Bornholm. If the Energiø project is realized, new cable connections can be an advantage for the locally anchored offshore wind turbine, says the person for the group, who has taken the initiative for the project.

- It will give some safer cable connections and a lifeline of security of supply. BEOF is positive about both projects, says Klaus Vesløv, Head of Department at Bornholm Energi and Supply (BEOF) and a member of the municipality's advisory committee.

Helle Munk Ravnborg also sees opportunities in the synergy effect between the two parks.

"They take place independently, but with advantages for us if we can devote excess energy via a new cable," she said in June about the prospect of two offshore wind projects.

Establishing the offshore wind farm is neither cheaper nor more expensive because the park is folk -owned.

Helle Munk Ravnborg Personal for the initiative group.


The local offshore wind turbine project

The initiative group will establish a folk -owned offshore wind farm on Rønnebakke, an underwater elevation that is about ten kilometers from the south coast (see map) and is therefore considered to be a coastal offshore wind farm.

Currently, eight wind turbines are planned with a total capacity of 90-100 megawatts.

The initiative group consists of Helle Munk Ravnborg, Kirsten June, Peter Haag, Kenn Kjellberg, Mads Meisner, Stine Mikkelsen, Steffen Olsen, Morten Riis, Bitten Sohn Thomsen, René Larsen Vilsholm, Søren Randbøll Wolffog Hisham Wael Zaki.

Their idea of ​​a 100 percent locally owned offshore wind farm saw the light of day in the spring of 2019, after it became clear that there was a political majority in the municipal council against setting up several wind turbines on land.

    The Bay of Sose turned out from its most beautiful side last Saturday, when the sky and sea walked in one out on the horizon. In five years, an offshore wind farm can be added to the view for a dozen kilometers from the beach if Bornholm's offshore wind turbine succeeds with its plans.

Title: Klimaminister Dan Jørgensen (S) om det gigantiske havvindmølleprojekt i Østersøen: Vi har tiltro til, at Bornholm kan løfte opgaven
Content:
On the night of Monday, June 22, a majority of the parliamentary parties entered into an agreement, which means that Bornholm becomes Energiø with an offshore wind farm 20 kilometers out in the Baltic, where Power-to-X, as it is called, must ensure that the power, which is made on the sea, can also be stored and converted.

A gigantic project that must necessarily create thousands of jobs, but how many? We ask Climate, Energy and Supply Minister Dan Jørgensen.

Can you say anything about what the wind farms at Bornholm and in the North Sea give of jobs - and not least on Bornholm? - I can't start putting numbers on, it's clear, says Dan Jørgensen.

- But I can say it's huge. And there are a lot of jobs we are talking about. And it is first and foremost good for Bornholm, I think, because there are so many different types of jobs.

Can one imagine that the government will shoot some money after some continuing education of the Bornholm workforce? - Of course, we will have to look at how we have to make these very large extensions in the coming years in the coming years - not only on Bornholm, but also elsewhere in the country - get a trained workforce for what it is clear. But I can't sit here and promise accurate money to precise parts of the country, it gives itself, but it's clearly something we're going to look at - how can we secure a workforce. And of course this must also be done in collaboration with business and in particular with the trade union movement.

Is it Bornholm who has to be a little advanced in the shoe and say "Could we have some continuing education money to Bornholm"? - I would say that Bornholm is in the shoes in general, and Winni (Grosbøll, mayor, ed.) Do an excellent job to take care of the island's interests. So there are never any of us here in Copenhagen who have doubts about what Bornholm thinks and what is needed. So of course you have to continue the good work, and of course we will be very responsive. It is also part of our overall strategy. Once we have chosen Bornholm to be one of these two destinations for energy islands, which is a huge venture for Denmark, then of course there are geographical reasons for it, but there is also the fact that we feel confident, That Bornholm is a place that can hijack this. Which can lift it. It is a huge opportunity for Bornholm, but it is also a huge challenge.

Can you describe the nature of the work Bornholm has done in relation to the political decision that was made - that is how competent has it been, and is it something that others can learn from? - Well, it has definitely be incredibly competent. Of course with the mayor at the forefront, but also your office work, parliamentary politicians - I must say that it has been a pleasure to work with actually everyone we have in my ministry had contact with from Bornholm. You can definitely learn from that.


Next step

- Of course, it is clear that this is also about something else that is out of the hands of politicians and the officials. Some geographical, windy and other conditions that matter.

But one still had to choose where the energy island should be placed? - That's what you should do, and it's clear that we have confidence that Bornholm can lift this task.

Now there are energy islands on the way, but they are not doing it all, so what is the government's next step? There must be more actions and will Bornholm play a role in them? - First of all, I have to say that this with energy islands does not, of course, do it alone, but it is a very big thing, a whole new era in offshore wind. We were also the first country to make offshore wind farms - we had the first in 1991 when the whole world looked at us and people shook their heads and said it is too expensive and why do it. But it was good we did it, because it was the starting point for the development that has now meant that offshore wind can actually compete with coal and nuclear power in many places in the world on price. We are now doing offshore wind farms without giving public support for the construction.

It could only happen because we took the first steps. Now we take the next first step with these islands.

- But there is clear, there are other things that need to be done as well. We must have made a green tax reform, we must have created a sector strategy for our transport sector and for our food sector, ie agriculture specifically.

And there it is clear that there is something that will have an impact on Bornholm, especially food production is great on Bornholm, but that is also my impression, I would say - also from my time as food minister a few years back - That I know Bornholm and the Bornholmers as a place and some people who want the green transition and where the focus is on it. Wide, also in business and in food production, so I clearly expect that Bornholm will also join that fight.

Do you have a personal relationship with Bornholm? Have you come there? - Nothing but so many other Danes. I love the island and have come there on holidays and to public meetings and all that, says Dan Jørgensen.

More pages 4-5.

There are never any of us here in Copenhagen who have doubts about what Bornholm thinks.

Dan Jørgensen Minister.

Title: Nu bliver hensættelser tilbagebetalt af Rønne Vand og Varme: 43,3 millioner kroner er på vej tilbage til RVV's andelshavere
Content:
There is reason to be happy if you are a customer of Rønne Water and Heat (RVV). Rønne residents who have checked their latest heating bill have been able to see it by self: the heat had become considerably more expensive. But now RVV announces that there is DKK 43.3 million on the way back to the cooperatives.

In other words: The heat does not get cheaper as such, but the bill diminishes because the 43.3 million are deducted from over one or two bills.

The fact that the heating bill suddenly increased significantly in the spring was an indication that RVV per day. On March 1, the price raised by as much as 47.8 percent.

And why now it? The price from Beof increased from about 80 kroner to about 164 kr. Gigajoule, a price increase, RVV necessarily had to pass on to customers.

It is a complicated case, as the price increase is due to a year -long trouble between RVV and Bornholm's Energy and Supply (BEOF), which RVV buys heat from. It has been fought on both arguments and in courtrooms, and so far they are the only ones who have immediately won on it, the accountants, consultants and lawyers who have received millions of dollars in fees when the companies have crossed blades.

The dispute may seem slightly daunting for outsiders, but has been about Beof's pricing of district heating and about the DKK 124 million, the remodeling of block 6 cost - without RVV having given its commitment to it, which is why the company did not think it should pay 92 percent of depreciation, as Beof subsequently required.

Since then, RVV has also been dissatisfied with the price that Beof charges for the heat, and wanted to let its allocations of DKK 43.3 million, which the company had earmarked for investments in the cogeneration, enter into the negotiations for a new heating delivery agreement.

The provisions are approved by the Supply Authority in 2017 and -18.

- They must only be used for investment or reversing to the customers, says RVV Erik Steen Andersen, director of Bornholm Tidende.

According to a legal requirement, allocations must not be retained for more than five years before either being used or returned to customers, and RVV has also been under pressure from, among other things, political side not to hold its customers as hostages in the case, But bring the millions back to the users, ie the cooperatives.

And in any case, they had to return to customers during 2022 and 2023 due to the five -year rule.

A crucial aspect of the dispute has been that RVV believes that heat customers unnecessarily pay for electricity production on block 6, as the argument from RVV has been that the heat customers in Rønne do not have to pay for costs due to an electricity production, and Now, explains Erik Steen Andersen, RVV has reached the conclusion that it is better to return the money to the customers: - The investment we should be pay for at Beof or BEP, Bornholm EL production, we do not want to participate in. The economy looks so dilapidated at the moment that we will not put neither 50 or 100 million kroner into that box. The money will be better in the pockets of heat customers, and then we have to pay our share of the investment in block 6 above the heating price as we receive the heat, he says.


The bad economy

The situation arising is not least provoked by the energy settlement that was entered into in the Folketing on June 22, which means, among other things, that Bornholm will be Energiø with the construction of a gigantic wind farm on Kriegers Flak out in the Baltic Sea. The consequence is that RVV sends the provisions back to the cooperatives.

In a press release, RVV explains as follows: "The board of directors of Rønne Water and Heat (RVV) has for some time considered whether it is in the interest of the cooperatives to pay a larger million amount to Bornholm El Production A/ S (BEP) for a contribution to the heat production at Block 6. The reason is Beps apparently very poor economy, where you say, among other things, that you only have a liquid readiness year out.

Most recently you can read that BEOF might want to sell the electricity grid to make the total debt in the group smaller.

The energy island at Bornholm became a fact in connection with the Folketing adopted the energy settlement of June 22. This is immediately gratifying for Bornholm, but means for BEP that a fixed annual subsidy from the state of about DKK 40 million will disappear, because there will no longer be needed that BEP is a reserve load on Bornholm. This will naturally further press BEP's economy.

It is therefore timely care from the RVV Board of Directors to consider whether it is in the interest of the cooperatives to pay a considerable amount for a future right to receive heat from the BEP.

In the context of this, it is also important that with the adoption of the energy settlement of June 22, 2020, the cogeneration requirement in Rønne has been removed.

The conclusion of the RVV Board of Directors is that it is not in the interest of the cooperatives to make a greater stretch payment for a future right to receive heat. The already placed DKK 43.3 million will therefore be returned to the cooperatives.

Title: ENERGISIMULERINGERNE
Content:
An external consulting firm has submitted a report on the energy situation and CO2 emissions at Bornholm with Bornholm Energy and Supply Assistance. The report has been lived using the "Bright Green Test Island model" - a simulation model that has previously been used to prepare Bornholm energy scenarios.

The calculations are based on three basic scenarios of the development of the wind turbine market: 1. Status quo without offshore wind turbines.

2. An offshore wind farm of 100 megawatts (corresponding to Bornholm's offshore wind's project nine kilometers from Arnager).

3. An offshore wind farm of 2 gigawatts (corresponding to the government's Energiø about 20 kilometers southwest of Bornholm).

In addition, the simulations contain many other scenarios, including the installation of several solar cells, introduction of geothermal to district heating, power-to-x systems, where the excess heat can be used for district heating, and fuel is produced for industrial companies and heavy land transport. Simulations are also made where the energy consumption is also made by calculating the consequences of removing all oil boilers or making all passenger cars electric powered.

The final version of the report has not yet been handed over, and Bornholm's Journal is waiting to present the results in detail until it is ready.
