Title: ' Næste gang jeg kommer, håber jeg, at jeg har en tysk og en polsk kollega med'
Content:
According to Pernille Weiss (K) of the European Parliament, many overlook in Brussels Baltic Sea when talking about the coming years of billion investments in offshore wind turbines and green fuels. For Rønne Harbor, it is important that the Baltic Sea gets a central place in the strategies that the EU is preparing.

A hub for cable connections between Sweden, Poland, Denmark and Germany, the center of an energy island with two gigawatt offshore winds and the future supplier of green fuel to the Baltic Sea ships, which can fill the tanks with methanol or ammonia produced with wind turbine energy.

Bornholm's future is drawing to light when you hear the advocates describe the possibilities in the energy field. On Friday it was European Parliamentarian Pernille Weiss, who listed the possibilities during his visit to Rønne Harbor. After a tour of the harbor area, the conservative politician took a conversation with Bornholm's Tidende about the great potential for Bornholm, which in Weiss's words can dream of having a role as both "roundabout" (for the electric cables in a grid between the Baltic Sea) and "gas station" (by the production of Power-to-X using wind energy) With one question on the block, the Journal had driven down to the new port office: How can the EU benefit the Bornholm efforts to become a central dot on the European Card of Energy? - We can help the cooperation across borders in the European Parliament promote by pushing, says Pernille Weiss initially.

- It is useful that I can tell my colleagues that there is this hub on an island in the Baltic Sea.

When talking offshore winds in Brussels, many North Sea sees themselves - or maybe some floating wind turbines in the Mediterranean. What happens in the Baltic Sea area is a very important piece, she states.

The priority of the Baltic Sea area from the EU is very important for the Port of Rønne, which performs lobbying aimed at the EU apparatus, says Port Director Thomas Bendtsen.

- First of all, we need to point out that there is a full swing in the development of the Baltic Sea.

Therefore, it is important that you not only focus on what is happening in the North Sea and the English Channel.

In addition, the Port Director points out that the EU should contribute to putting turbo on the establishment of a better cable network between the countries in the Baltic Sea and developing methods for storing energy.

- You have to make sure that the legislative framework needed to facilitate this is in place well in advance so that it will not be what hinders the development, says Thomas Bendtsen.

Industrial policy EU countries have a goal is to reduce CO2 emissions by 55 percent in 2030 compared to the 1990 level. This goal requires early action, emphasizes Pernille Weiss, who will soon have to deal with a new EU strategy for offshore wind.

She is currently involved in part of a larger work to ensure that the regulatory and legal framework comes in place within a few years. "Fit for 55" is called the plan, which will regulate everything from energy efficiency and renewable energy to standards for cars and CO2 quotas.

The Folketing has adopted an even more ambitious target for 2030 with a CO2 reduction of 70 percent, but Pernille Weiss believes that the Danish government is hesitant to take action and rely on technological quantum jumps. One way to achieve great progress is to make the green transition attractive to invest in, says Pernille Weiss, who believes that European politicians should perceive the area as industrial policy.

- Green energy is a new industry. For us, it's about how we get a business strategy so that the potent capital of investors can come into play, she explains.

30 gigawatts a year in July increased the European Commission's ambitions by setting a target that renewable energy sources in nine years should make up 40 percent of energy production - before the target was 32 percent. The new goals cause a strong acceleration in the set up of wind turbines.

Every year until 2030, the EU countries will install 30 gigawatts. This corresponds to 15 parks a year the size of the Bornholm Energiø project.

Pernille Weiss recalls that decision makers must already think even further forward and lay the foundation for Europe to become a power factor in the development of the fuels of the future.

- We have to lift our eyes to after 2030 and go for Europe at some point to become an exporter of energy, she says.

In that field Bornholm dreams big. The hope is - as the regional municipality writes in a consultation response to the Danish Maritime Authority, which is in the process of designing a new Danish sea plan - that "Rønne Havn can become a green bunker hub that will be able to supply sustainable fuel from a locally located Powerto -X plant to Some of the 60,000 ships that pass each year in the waters between Bornholm and Sweden, "so the Port Director naturally supports the EU High targets.

- We go away from the oil we have picked up from the underground for 170 years and over to the new: What we call the X in Power to X. It is a global energy market that is under transformation.

We really need to make sure that the EU is placed correctly in that race, because it benefits all member states, including Denmark and Bornholm, says Thomas Bendtsen.

The North Sea strategy for the Baltic Sea countries has a high degree of sovereignty in the energy field, one example is Germany's agreement to receive Russian gas with the Nord Stream 2 pipeline, which was not popular in neighboring countries to the east. The agreements on cable connections are also a task that the countries are individually included with each other. This is done by the Danish system operator, Energinet, working with their counterparts in Germany, Sweden and Poland. Despite national self -determination, the EU can have an impact on the Bornholm dreams of becoming a hub for cable connections and a specific strategy for the Baltic Sea will be particularly valuable, says Thomas Bendtsen.

- The EU is a good forum to handle these interstatic interests. It's just to turn your head and work on something similar to the North Sea manifesto you have prepared in the North Sea. We believe that we have to work according to the same strategy and mindset in the Baltic Sea, says the Port Director.

So far, Denmark has entered into a prior agreement with Germany, while there has been quiet about the Polish interest so far. In January, Energinet told Bornholm Tidende that the Poles at that time had not wanted to make a collaboration.

Pernille Weiss has previously been on energy visits in Poland and says that the Poles are much longer more keen to invest in the green transition than many people think.

- Poland and Germany are some enormous countries, and Denmark places itself with its experience and technology in offshore wind really well. So it's also Denmark's really big chance of putting in that field, she says.

On Friday, the Funen European Parliamentarian, who sits in Parliament's major EPP group for conservative and Christian Democratic parties, alone at Rønne Harbor.

Pernille Weiss would like to come again - with company: - Next time I come, I hope I have a German and a Polish colleague.

    Pernille Weiss has been a member of the European Parliament since 2019. She visited Bornholm this weekend, and on the program was a meeting with Port Director Thomas Bendtsen and a tour of Rønne Harbor.

Title: Større energiø i sigte: Havvindmøller kan rykke fem kilometer tættere på kysten
Content:
Energinet will investigate the possibility of expanding the energy island from two to three gigawatts, Dan Jørgensen (S) has decided.

One of the initial steps that can make the wind turbine projects in the Baltic Sea even greater, Climate, Energy and Supply Minister Dan Jørgensen has taken Thursday. He has given Energinet an order to expand the preliminary study area at Energiø Bornholm, the Danish Energy Agency says.

In these months, Energinet is in the process of doing a preliminary study, and the ships that are investigating seabed and environmental conditions are now being tasked with sailing closer to land and examining a larger area up to 15 kilometers from the coast. In the previous studies, it has been based on the fact that it has been decided that the wind farms should be at least 20 kilometers from land.

With the addition, the area examined becomes so large that there can be room for three gigawatts (GW) offshore wind. In the current climate agreement from 2020, the conciliation parties have committed to set up to GW on the Bornholm Energiø. There are two main reasons for the new decision, explains the Danish Energy Agency's director, Kristoffer Böttzauw.

- First and foremost, it is an expression of timely care because the area that is being examined is not very large in terms of being able to accommodate the two gigawatts that the politicians have decided.

If the feasibility studies show that there is a mud floor or something else that makes offshore winds, then there is not much to give, says the director of the Journal.

Problems at Hesselø - In addition, the offshore wind farm, which we are planning up at Hesselø, has been challenged by the fact that just up there is very mud bottom, which makes the foundation of offshore wind turbines more cumbersome and much more expensive if it can be done at all .

So if it turns out that Hesselø cannot be done, we need alternative locations for one gigawatt that Hesselø should make up. That is why we are investigating an expansion of Bornholm, says Kristoffer Böttzauw.

The Danish Energy Agency will also investigate areas in the Kattegat, the North Sea and around Kriegers Flak if a replacement is needed for the planned Hesselø-Park north of the North Coast of Zealand. The offering at Hesselø has been paused due to the results of the detailed bottom surveys.

The Danish Energy Agency believes that it makes good sense to put the Bornholm studies early because Energinet is already underway in the waters.

- Bornholm is distinguished by the fact that we have ships in the lake at the moment, so it is far more financially sensible to ask them to sail in a slightly larger area than to do it in half a year when they have docked, says Kristoffer Böttzauw.

The area within the 20 kilometer zone of the coast can also become relevant if it is decided from the political side to erect more offshore wind farms and for that reason expand the energy island to three gigawatts, the Danish Energy Agency points out.


No political decision

The order from the Danish Energy Agency to Energinet does not mean that the energy island becomes 1 gigawatts or that the mills must stand closer to the coast.

- I would like to emphasize that no political decision has been made for the area to be used. It is only a technical preliminary examination of whether you can use the area if you need it, says the Danish Energy Agency's director.

Energinet's work in the Baltic Sea also includes preliminary studies for cable connections between Bornholm and the offshore wind farms, export cables to Zealand and foreign connections to neighboring countries. A prerequisite for the energy island is that new connections are established between Denmark, Germany, Sweden and Poland.

- As I understand on Energinet, there is enough space in the cable area to have three gigawatts. So that shouldn't mean much, says Kristoffer Böttzauw.

After the preliminary studies, more detailed geophysical, geotechnical and environmental studies must be made.

The Danish Energy Agency will hold a virtual consultation on an upcoming strategic environmental assessment to be prepared for Energiø Bornholm.

    The green area is the new area that will be included in the feasibility study in the future. Energinet was already conducting the feasibility studies in the orange area. The gray area within 15 kilometers distance to the coast is also laid out as a "development zone for renewable energy and energy islands" in the draft of Denmark's new sea plan. It will make really good sense for the whole of Bornholm.

Title: Energiøen skal føres i land syd for Aakirkeby
Content:
The Danish Energy Agency plans to carry the cables from Energiø Bornholm ashore on the south coast between Sose Odde and Raghammer Odde, and a few kilometers away there must be room for a transformer station that may require an area of ​​up to 90 hectares.

The energy authorities have narrowed the area where the electricity from the energy island's offshore wind farms can be led ashore. In a new note that precedes environmental planning, the Danish Energy Agency highlights a stretch between Sose Odde and Raghammer Odde on the south coast.

In the past, some people have believed that the Hasle area was in play as the place where the power was to be carried ashore because COWI had marked fields north of Hasle as an opportunity in a report with a drawing pin.

To the Journal, Energinet stated in the summer of 2020 that large parts of the south and west coast were in play.

Within a handful of kilometers of the coast, a transformer station must be erected, and it may be as far away as in Aakirkeby, the map from the note, which bears the title "The framework for the upcoming plan proposal for Energiø Bornholm for use in environmental assessment" shows.

For the transformer station, a plan area of ​​about 90 hectares must be allocated if the energy island gets a capacity of 3 gigawatts, the Danish Energy Agency reports.

"On the southern part of Bornholm, a high-voltage station will be established, which can collect wind energy from the offshore wind farms, convert the power, and export it to 400 kV electricity transmission network in Zealand and abroad," the note states.

350 meters altitude The areas for offshore wind parks are approximately 15 kilometers from Bornholm's south coast. In the memo, the Danish Energy Agency comes with an indication of what height of the future mills will get: "It is not unlikely that the offshore wind turbines will be able to have a total height of more than 350 meters and take up a total area for the 3 GW of up to 660 square kilometers".

By total height is meant the distance up to the wing tip when pointing straight up into the air.

Until October, the intention was that the offshore wind turbines should stand at least about 20 kilometers from the coast, but to potentially expand the capacity from two to three gigawatts decided to climate, energy and supply minister Dan Jørgensen to move the area, which is currently undergoing energy-savering. five kilometers closer to land.

In addition to the transformer station, it is possible to build coastal coupling stations the place where the cables from the offshore wind turbine areas are laid ashore. These coupling stations will only be necessary if no transformer platforms are established on the sea at the two separate offshore wind turbine areas, Bornholm I and Bornholm II.


Hearing in progress

A five -week consultation period was started on November 8 and lasts to 13.

December. This is an idea hearing that precedes the environmental assessment. All stakeholders have the opportunity to make questions and comments on the consultation material, as well as suggestions and ideas for topics that must be included in the further work. The material can be found on the Danish Energy Agency's website.

The Danish Energy Agency and Energinet will hold an online information meeting on November 25 at. 15: 30-17: 00 on the planned environmental assessment.


Energiø Bornholm

It is intended for Energiø Bornholm to consist of:? A sea -based plant in the Baltic Sea; offshore wind turbines with internal cable network, possibly.

Offshore transformer stations, export cable connection from the offshore wind farms to Bornholm, sea cables from Bornholm to Zealand and Interconnector cables from Bornholm abroad.

? A land -based plant on Bornholm; buried land cables, possibly coupling station and a high voltage station incl. CHANGE SYSTEM HVAC/ HVDC (concerting of AC for DC, ed.)? A land -based plant in Zealand; Buried land cables, high voltage station incl. Conversion system HVDC/ HVAC and possibly net reinforcements.

Source: The Danish Energy Agency.


Plan areas

The planning areas on Bornholm are expected to include: - Plan areas on the south coast of Bornholm to land the landing of export cables from the offshore wind farms - Plan areas on the southern part of Bornholm to establish possible coastal coupling stations close to the landing of cables from the offshore wind turbines - planning areas on the southern part of Bornholm for establishing of a high -voltage station with HVAC/ HVDC Converter system.

- Plank corridors for burial of land cables between landing points and station systems on land.

In the Baltic Sea, these planning areas must be worked on: - Two planning areas in the Baltic Sea of ​​333 and 413 square kilometers respectively for the establishment of two offshore wind farms with internal cable network and with a total power of up to 3 GW, possibly. Offshore transformer station and corridors of approx. 2,000 meters width to export cables connecting the offshore wind farms with Bornholm.

- A number of corridors of approx. 2,000 meters width connecting Bornholm and Zealand. In the corridors, search cables can be established for grid connection of Energiø Bornholm to 400 kV electricity transmission network in Zealand.

- A number of corridors of approx. 1,500 meters width connecting Bornholm to cooperative countries, including connections to the existing corridors for sea cables in German waters. In the corridors, search cables can be established for the transfer of electricity to cooperative countries (Interconnectors).

Source: The Danish Energy Agency.

Too often it happens that the plans have come a long way before the citizens are involved. It has repeatedly stopped good projects because the importance of citizens is recognized.

In order to avoid such situations, we propose that in the development of Bornholm, as a sustainable society and the establishment of Bornholm as a lighthouse for green energy, an innovation method that has citizens as a focal point - from the start of the transition, and not only reaches the mandatory consultation phase must be implemented just before realization. The procedure is internationally recognized and is based on design methods described as "Human-Centered Design" or "Citizen-driven Innovation". These nerdy terms say quite precisely what it is about, namely people, the citizens, the Bornholmers at the center of the development.

The municipality's committee for climate and sustainability has been a so -called section 17 paragraphs for the past two years. 4 committees, a committee form where 'non -elected' can sit with. The way the committee has gone to its tasks has largely involved the Bornholmers, both by virtue of two citizen representatives, but also by holding a lot of engaging activities early in the processes. It is quite clear that the results have been lifted by this approach to work.

An overall committee has sent the recommendation to the municipal council that when the municipality has to work with strategic processes that the energy islands will entail, it is a good form of organization with a broad compiled committee. However, it is also very important that strategic decisions are rooted well in the permanent political committees that must implement the work.

The upcoming municipal council must organize itself, in the political committees and in the administration, so that one can be as agile as a co -player as possible, for the Bornholmers and the great actors in association.

Title: Begejstret borgmester: Et Nationalt Center for Grøn Energi kan ligge i Elværket

With the Technical University of Denmark and Energinet as potential partners, the regional municipality and a string of Bornholm actors go to create an ambitious research center that brings students, researchers and business people to Bornholm.

B Ornholm as home to the National Center for Green Energy.

- We must have a lighthouse called "Bornholm as Energiø" and being a bunker hub for sustainable fuel and that we must take advantage of the opportunity to be Testø.

Base for students

To the center, the plan is to associate a college for students from DTU - a so -called Residential College.

Energinet's chairman, Social Democrat Mogens Lykketoft, has expressed support for the proposal, because Bornholm stands to become the first real experiment for Energiø projects. The fact that Energinet sees itself as partners in a national center is Thomas Thors very pleased with.

Title: Energiø uden forbindelse til Bornholm
Content:
There is still green hope without connection to the new large energy island. But it is important that politicians fight for a connection.

It is amazing that the large energy island south of Bornholm, which will spread economic growth and green development for us and the rest of the world, took another step in the right direction on Wednesday.

Here, Energinet agreed with the German company 50 Hz and the Belgian company Elia on a cooperation agreement that makes it possible to connect the two planned energy islands in the Baltic Sea and the North Sea with Germany and Belgium respectively.

Such connections are crucial for making sense to build the giant wind farms. If the power cannot reach out to customers, then it makes no sense to produce it.

But it is worrying that the connection to the Bornholm electricity network is not mentioned in the new agreements. Bornholm must forge, while the iron is hot, and get its own electricity grid with wind turbines on the upcoming energy motorway towards Germany. Then we can both buy and sell electricity on even better terms. Such a link will make the current submarine cable to Sweden not become a bottleneck for wind turbine and solar cell power from Bornholm.

According to Mayor Thomas Thors, it is the economy that stands in the way of connecting the wires. Here lies a political challenge for both the old and the new municipal councils.

It must be lifted to help our green hope.

Fortunately, the connection between the two electricity networks is not crucial to our green growth adventure, although it may be smaller without. The large energy island, which on Wednesday moved one step closer to Bornholm, will still be able to demand lots of off-shore activity in Rønne Harbor, just as the wild quantities of offshore wind turbine are still drawing to round Bornholm in a gigantic transformer system of 90 hectares or large football fields. It allows you to transform the power into fuel for ships and aircraft -the so -called Power to X -can create our financial future.

Wednesday was a day of joy for that plan.

Bornholm must forge, while the iron is hot, and get its own electricity grid with wind turbines on the upcoming energy motorway towards Germany.

Title: Bornholmsk delegation: Overskriften er den positivisme, der er omkring energiøerne
Content:
One of the themes at a major industry fair for wind energy is how the production of wind turbine parts and other components for the offshore sector can be made more sustainably and locally.

Key people from the European wind energy industry have this week gathered at the Bella Center in Copenhagen for the event Windeurope Electric City.

A Bornholm delegation with representatives from Rønne Harbor, BHS Logistics and Offshore Center Bornholm (OCB), among others, participated, and they returned home with the knowledge that the rapid development of the past few years has seriously brought Bornholm and the Baltic Sea a location on the industry map of the industry.

- It's just cool when you walk around with signs on your stomach where Bornholm says.

You meet some people who already know something about you. It provides some comfort in relation to all the work we have been doing for many years, says Lone Reppien Thomsen, who has the title of Business & Innovation Developer at OCB.

The Bornholm reputation is also helped by how it went with the shipping of the 72 mills from Rønne Harbor to Kriegers Flak earlier this year.

- The success that Siemens Gamesa has had on Bornholm has really noticed. Our companies have solved all tasks that were possible for us to UG, says Lone Reppien Thomsen to the Journal.

The Danish Energiø project arouses international attention, and the three days in the Bella Center have only increased the Bornholm optimism among the participants.

- The headline is clearly the positivism that is around the Energy Islands. It is clear that the industry is working for it, says Lone Reppien Thomsen.

One of the themes at the large industry fair is how the production of wind turbine parts and other components for the offshore sector can be made more sustainably and locally.

The fact that there is a willingness to put production in the immediate areas rather than the Far East can also accommodate opportunities for Bornholm, says Lone Reppien Thomsen.

- You talk a lot about innovation, and I look a lot at how our Bornholm companies can come into play, she says.

She can also tell of great political will to carry out large offshore wind turbine investments within a short time horizon.

The same view has offshore Center Bornholm Chairman Jens Hjul-Nielsen, who was part of the Bornholm delegation.

- I listened to especially two interesting sessions. One about the energy islands with both Danish, German, Polish and English panelists as well as participants from several of the large companies in the industry, and I really have to say that Bornholm as Energiø and the international opportunities in energy islands are generally focus areas that are being worked very hard for to succeed. And as one participant expressed it; The goal is to transform wind into welfare, says the chairman of the board.

After a panel debate, Jens Hjul-Nielsen greeted Stefan Kapferer, director of 50Hertz, the German pendant to Danish Energinet, who is responsible for cable connections.

- He talked about Bornholm as Energiø and mentioned, among other things, that he saw the 2 GWs as a beginning, says Jens Hjul-Nielsen.

-He really saw some potentials, adds Lone Reppien Thomsen about the 50Hertz director's announcements, which she sees as an expression of the Germans' dedication to the roll-out of offshore wind projects in the Bornholm immediate area.

The 50Hertz and Energinet signed under Electric City a cooperation agreement that lays another layer on the foundation that will make it possible to realize the huge construction project south of Bornholm with large transformer systems on land. The fact that the agreement does not contain anything new about a link with the Bornholm electricity grid is quite natural, says Lone Reppien Thomsen, as the link to the Bornholm electricity network is a purely national matter.

- These are two very different discussions, she emphasizes.

Title: Energiøen blev en tand mere konkret
Content:
Questioning Bornholmers got answers to some questions - but certainly not everyone - at the first citizen meeting on the energy island. It was stated that the power-to-X dreams depend on private forces and that there are Bornholmers who are concerned that the mills will be too close to land.

On Monday, the Bornholmers were given the chance to ask questions to the state energy authorities working to realize the political adopted plan to erect a huge offshore wind farm south of the coast and a station facility south of Aakirkeby. From here, the mill stream must be converted into DC and transformed into high voltage before it is sent out into the world - to Zealand and probably Germany.

This afternoon's Citizens' Meeting, which will not be the last in the series, will take place, while the first consultation phase prior to the environmental assessment is underway.

- The consultation is on a completely overall idea plan. I don't think today I have as many answers with as you might think. But we think it is important to stand up to an early stage, says the Danish Energy Agency's Mads Krogh, who is the office manager of the Center for Energy Islands.

Before receiving questions from the hall at the Green Solution House in Rønne, he gives a presentation where he enters the dimensions of the energy island and the schedule. Two million households can be provided electricity from the offshore wind farm, which will be in two separate fields south and southwest of Bornholm.

- The challenge is that if you want to build offshore winds, you will typically build it on a very large scale that much more is produced than you can use locally.

- With pretty much certainty we can say that Bornholm is put into operation before the Energiø North Sea, and therefore it becomes the world's first energy island.

The energy island on Bornholm will supply electricity from 2030, the politicians have decided. The Danish Energy Agency expects that a two gigawatt park, which according to the assumptions in a pre -screening made by COWI will require 134 mills last year, will be ready until that time.

- That's what the plan says, and we think that is certainly possible, says Mads Krogh.

The Eiffel Tower The nearest mills are expected to stand 15-20 kilometers from the coast, and this distance is taken up by several questioners.

Henrik Espersen is one of the first to take the floor. Like all other audience who grabs the microphone, he is basically positively faced with the project and its possibilities.

- We should not make mistakes, says the businessman before raising his concerns.

- If we hear a little on the West Jews, they have been through the same debate three years ago.

Then Søren Gade (V) said that the mills must stand where you cannot see them. Today we can see here at Bornholm see the mills down in German area - both during the day and at night. They stand 45 kilometers from Rønne and no one thinks right about them because they stand so far away. But they are only half as tall as the mills we are talking about today. With 300 meters up to the mill tip, they are as high as the Eiffel Tower. And if we are going all the way to 15 kilometers, it will be a completely different visual impression, says Henrik Espersen.

The Danish Energy Agency's representative recognizes that the mills will be visible, but since no picture examples are included in the illustration, one cannot get an impression of how the mills will look out from the south coast.

- Of course, you will probably be able to see the mills to some extent. How to see them in clear weather and rain, we do not know yet. Visualization lies a little later in the process, says Mads Krogh.

Michael Trolle, chairman of the Canon's Support Association, and who has previously been critical of the ongoing port expansion in Rønne, would like to know why the Danish Energy Agency does not focus on floating wind turbines that can be placed further away from land.

- The development of the floating offshore wind turbines is not at all as mature as they are on the bottom. The part of the offshore wind turbine production is fully industrialized and there are the floating wind turbines not today. But it may be that that technology is more mature in x years and that you see some other options there. We don't have time to wait for that, explains Mads Krogh.

Until a month ago, the mills were intended to be placed at least 20 kilometers by country, but to be sure to find a lot of space and possibly expand capacity to three gigawatts, the government decided to move the area currently being examined by Energinet, five kilometers closer to the coast.

PTX on private initiative cables must be brought ashore somewhere between Arnager and Raghammer Odde. On the Danish Energy Agency's map, the landing site is marked with a blue line, and behind the strip is marked a green area where the large land plant is to be erected.

Lars-Ole Hjorth-Larsen, the chairman of Bornholm Agriculture and Food, is one of the landowners who may need to add land to the cable work.

- Part of the land I own is in the blue stripe. Of course, it can be a good pension scheme if I can sell the same price as cottage areas, he notes before asking his question.

He wants to know why the authorities do not tell more about the likelihood that Bornholm may become a place where the future alternative fuels for agricultural machinery, ships and other purposes can be produced at a local power-to-x plant.

- When do you come up with more opportunities?, Asks the agricultural chairman.

There is a good reason why the Danish Energy Agency's panelist in its presentation has not said much about a potential Bornholm hydrogen adventure.

-The energy island allows other players to establish Power-to-X (PTX). It is private actors who have to take the initiative. The state can only set the framework conditions.

What is politically decided is offshore wind.

In short, PTX must be a private initiative, says Mads Krogh.

Esben Ørberg from the Bornholm Citizens' Association's Samvirke is not entirely happy with the answer - you must be able to say what we could expect from development opportunities, says Ørberg to the Danish Energy Agency's office manager.

- When I am not more concrete, it is also because I will not provide a state guarantee for the number of jobs, says Mads Krogh.

To be seized locally he reminds the hall that there is a billion project, and emphasizes that all existing Danish offshore wind farms have together a capacity installed 2.3 gigawatts. Energiø Bornholm will get a capacity of two gigawatts, maybe three gigawatts if politicians choose to turn up the ambitions.

- When it happens southwest of Bornholm, there are some really great opportunities, but they have to be seized locally, emphasizes the Danish Energy Agency's office manager, before noting: - Where we as a board can help with advice and deed, we do, of course, says Mads Krogh .

Aksel Sonne, who has objections to the size and impact of the mills and the land facility, had hoped to get more information about the state's ambitions for the production of hydrogen and fuels via electrolysis.

- I thought that land plant was one that could change the power so we could use the energy when it doesn't blow, he says.

Mads Krogh repeats that investments in PTX plants on Bornholm depend on private companies. A large electrolysis system for PTX does not have to be located in connection with the transformer station, he elaborates. A plant is located in several places on Bornholm, where easy access to the power from the offshore wind farms can be provided.

What about Poland and Sweden? Along the way, the participants from Energinet and the Danish Energy Agency emphasize that the project's schedule will depend on whether Germany will end up investing in a cable connection to Bornholm. Last week, a cooperation agreement was signed between the system operator Energinet and the German counterparty, 50Hertz. If it does not end with a binding agreement, it is possible that the energy island is not built in full size, as Denmark cannot subside two gigawatts.

- If we do not get a foreign connection ready by 2030, politicians have to decide whether to build offshore wind farms step by step. That decision is coming in 2022, as it looks now, says Mads Krogh.

When the energy island first came to speak in 2019, Poland and Sweden were also mentioned as customers of the flow, and this aspect asks Helene Rask Green in.

- Why are Sweden and Poland not drawn in when they are much closer than Zealand? - They are not currently. Interested, replies Energinet's panelist, Deputy Director Marian Kaagh.

She concentrated in her presentation on the land plant and cable work on land and ended up calling on those present to submit consultation responses and contact Energinet if they have questions about the work.

"Call once too much than once too little," said Marian Kaagh.

The consultation period runs until December 13, after the consultation, the Danish Energy Agency will, among other things, on the basis of the consultation responses decide which issues and environmental impacts should be elucidated in the environmental assessment of Energiø Bornholm.

- When I am not more concrete, it is also because I will not provide a state guarantee for the number of jobs Mads Krogh office manager, the Danish Energy Agency.


Preliminary schedule

2021-24: Preliminary studies and environmental assessment of the plan: The environmental assessment of the overall plan for Energiø Bornholm has begun in the fall of 2021.

Energinet conducts feasibility studies until 2024.

2022-24: Planning basis and EIA of projects on land: Energinet carries out an environmental impact assessment of the project on land, both Zealand and Bornholm, from 2022-24.

2024-26: Tendering process: Who is to set up the offshore wind must be clarified through one or more tenders.

2026-28: EIA of the offshore wind farms: The winner of the supply carries out an environmental impact assessment of the project at sea from 2026-28. This will include information on the type of mill and height as well as location.

2028-30: Establishment permit and setup The Danish Energy Agency expects to grant establishment permit in 2028. It gives the winner the right to commence the construction work.

Title: Firkantede byggeklodser vil rage 25 meter op i landskabet
Content:
The land plant to be built south of Aakirkeby was the subject of many of the questions that the participants from the Danish Energy Agency and Energinet had to answer at the Citizens' Meeting.

25 meters in height and a floor plan of 103 x 60 meters.

These are the goals of the type of buildings that the Bornholmers can expect for the land facility south of Aakirkeby.

Energinet announced at Monday's Citizens' Meeting that an area of ​​between 30 and 50 hectares must be fenced. In addition to a cluster of buildings where the current is transformed into direct current, the fenced area must house open high -voltage systems. In the plan work, the aim is to set aside an area of ​​90 hectares (0.9 square kilometers), and outside the fence, just in its presentation, Energinet's deputy director, Marian Kaagh, will showcase several examples of how a station plant for an offshore wind farm of two gigawatts can get to look.

- Now it comes; What does existing plants look like? she says when she reached the time of the presentation with relevant comparisons.

On screen, photographs of the Endrup plant in West Jutland are tuning. Here, Energinet has established a direct current connection to the Netherlands. "The plant on Bornholm will be several times larger," says the screen.

- Is it the standard of aesthetics, notes an listener spontaneously about the square buildings and the open high -voltage coils and masts.

The slideshow also includes pictures from Energinet's existing plants in Jutland.

- The plant in its entirety fills just about 20 hectares and there are 15,000 square meters under roof. The plant to be established on Bornholm will be a little bigger, says Marian Kaagh about the Viking Link station, which is near the road.

Viking Link is decorated with facades with Viking motifs, and the area around the plant has Energinet made sure to plant with local vegetation to hide the building a little. Marian Kaagh says that Energinet has begun to work with not hiding the station facilities completely behind a wall of trees, as there may be a view of the large buildings. Other tools are used to decorate or obscure the large plants. For example, Viking Link is decorated with Viking motifs, and Energinet has somewhere else signed a forest edge on the facade of a hall that stands near a forest area.

In the presentation there are two suggestions on what a two -gigawatt offshore wind farm may look like - a large and a small version. The square buildings are located in a West Jutland landscape, as Bornholm visualizations have not yet been prepared. A few of the audience comments on the square bricks that will protrude well into the landscape. This particular geometric form is chosen because it requires the least space, explains chief project manager Poul-Jacob Vilhelmsen.

- The smallest building is square. All other shapes - round or oval structures - would make the building appear larger, he explains.

The size is related to the advanced machines inside the hall for safety reasons need six meters of air to all sides.

One of the questioners is engineer Lasse Steen Jepsen, who he finds the opportunity to mention that he has had his fingers in all power plants in East Zealand and North Zealand ".

- It looks fine and cubic, he says of the buildings and looks at the high -voltage components that are under the open sky.

- On the other hand you have the transformer part itself, where the masts stand. It always looks out of h to. Efforts must be made to get them locked in somehow, says Lasse Steen Jepsen.

It is possible to wrap high-voltage components into buildings using gas, explains Poul-Jacob Vilhelmsen.

It requires quite a potent SF6 gas that has a climate footprint that is 22,000 times larger than CO2, which is why avoiding emissions is crucial. To the high voltage level, which the power from the offshore wind turbines must be turned up to Energiø Bornholm, the gas solution is not yet possible.

- The technology is not present today to make it at 400,000 volts, says the chief project manager, who repeatedly supplemented the panel with technical answers.

It emerges along the way that the station facility will not be manned on a daily basis and that it will not be informed at night. Energinet will comply with the indicative noise limits and similar station systems do not have for the cables, a working belt of 30-40 meters must be used during the construction phase. In some places on the stretch, from the cables are led ashore to the large converter station, the working width can be up to 100 meters.

- It is especially in the first public phase in the spring of 2022 that we start to go into detail.

Our environmentalists have already been here and explored the conditions, says Marian Kaagh.

As early as 2022, the Bornholmers will be much wiser on where the land plant should be located, and the regional municipality will be involved in the work of making a supplement to the municipal plan and a new local plan. Energinet's Deputy Director promises to listen to the locals and the neighbors of the land plant and the cable connections.

- I acknowledge that it is a large plant and I consider it an important task that we can jointly find a good solution with you, says Marian Kaagh.

    At the end of the Citizens' Meeting, participants were able to talk more informally with the traveling officials and local actors. Title: Finanslov rykker energiøen tættere på
Content:
In connection with the financial law negotiations, a majority of parties in the Folketing have agreed to investigate whether the establishment of offshore wind farms at Bornholm can be advanced.

The much -talked about Energiø with offshore wind turbines off Bornholm can come earlier than hitherto planned.

It is clear after the government, the Unity List, the SF, the Radical Left, the Alternative and the Christian Democrats at Christiansborg on Saturday agreed on a partial agreement on the Finance Act for 2022.

Mayor Thomas Thors (S) believes that the Finance Act is making it clearly clear that the large -scale energy island plans are now becoming a reality - even perhaps before expected.

- For me to see, there is no doubt that this will turn into something, which the financial law agreement is cementing. The government and the Folketing have set the goal that 70 percent of Denmark's CO2 emissions should be reduced by 2030, and it is seen as necessary for the energy island to become a reality.

-It now seems to be a realistic possibility that the establishment of the parks will get started -I would like to be -in the next 4-5 years, says Thomas Thors.


Must produce more power than expected

In addition, it is planned that the energy island now has to produce more power than previously expected. The idea was originally that it should produce two gigawatts of power, but now it indicates that three gigawatts should be produced.

- That question becomes clearer now. It has been rumbling for a while that it will be three gigawatts.

But now a lot suggests that it will actually be so and that one will speed up the establishment of the transformer station on Bornholm and speed up the establishment of the wind turbine fields, says Thomas Thors.

THORS: Bornholm is clear the mayor previously as chairman of Rønne Harbor helped to bet that the port should be a shipping port for wind turbines.

A strategy that now seems to bear fruits of the very big ones. But one thing is what Rønne Harbor can deliver. Something else is whether the Bornholm community is ready to benefit from the fact that with the establishment of the energy island it can get all the energy it can use. However, Thomas Thors estimates that Bornholm will be ready to handle the energy island's coming.

- I definitely mean that the Bornholm community is set and ready to go into this. Of course, our local business community should be able to seize the chance. It must stick to and build the expertise needed to become part of the supply system that must also be. Because one thing is to install wind turbines. Something else is to have a sustained agreement with wind turbine manufacturers to contribute to the maintenance of them. This offers great opportunities for Bornholm, says Thomas Thors.


33 hectare large transformer station

However, the roses come with thorns. The more gigawatts, the wind turbines on the sea produce, the greater a transformer station you have to build here on Bornholm.

- There are many many benefits. But also disadvantages. They are that we must have established some very extensive plants. Title: Energiferieøen
Content:
The coastal area all the way around Bornholm at a distance of at least 20 kilometers must be protected and permanently kept free of wind turbines.

Dear reader If you want to influence Bornholm's future, it is important to decide on what is going on right now regarding the establishment of Bornholm as Energiø.

The project is in consultation now and the consultation period is over on December 13.


The wind turbines

Denmark, the Danish Energy Agency and the Bornholm Regional Municipality will establish two large offshore wind farms south of Bornholm, which can be seen from Rønne to Dueodde.

The wind turbines are located at least 20 kilometers from land, which is a very short distance when the height of the wind turbines becomes over 260 meters, which is more than twice as high as the German wind turbines at Rügen.

The wind turbines at Rügen are 102 meters high, so ours will be about 2.5 times as high! Even before this consultation is completed, an examination of the possibility of expanding the area has been initiated so that the wind turbines can be placed at least 15 kilometers from land.

Does this hearing then make sense when it is the salami method used in terms of distance from the coast? One of the reasons why the wind farm south of Bornholm is to be expanded is that Hesselø Vindjøllepark north of Zealand may not turn into anything due to soil conditions in the sea. (Or is it because the cottage owners in North Zealand do not want the view of wind turbines?) As if it is not enough that we get huge wind turbines on the horizon on the whole of South Bornholm, then Helle Ravnborg and her Bornholm Vavvind will make a coastal wind farm, so we Getting wind turbines almost all the way to the coast.

It must and must be stopped. If we get the large wind farms planned by the Danish Energy Agency, I think we must demand that the coastal area together with the bird protection zone between the wind farms will be protected and kept free of wind turbines and other hardware.

If Bornholm's offshore wind wants more wind turbines, they must build them between Gudhjem and Svaneke.

No, I don't mean that. I feel that when I don't want coastal wind turbines where I live, I don't want it for others.

We should not have coastal wind turbines at all.


The transformer station

A land plant must be built, which is a transformer station that will be very large.

There have been different figures on the size and I have read and heard that it will be somewhere between 50 and 90 hectares.

90 hectares = 136 football fields or 0.9 km2 Transformer station must be placed at least three km from the coast and according to the project description located somewhere south of Aakirkeby.

I mean, the designated area for the entire project needs to be expanded.

One could hope that the third of the wind turbines, which will supply electricity to Germany, could supply directly from the wind turbine to the transformer station at Rügen. In this way, the Bornholm land plant can be slightly smaller.

The offshore wind farm to be built in the North Sea must be 80 km from the coast.

Why is it not enough with 20 kilometers off Jutland? Are the Jews just better at negotiating? An energy island also has to be built, which costs 38 billion, probably because the wind turbines have to go so far out on the sea, or perhaps because the Jews do not want more transformer stations and PTX factories on land.

At Bornholm, the Earth is just expropriated, and in this way we give the land away at market price. On the other hand, we have to pay for the energy island of the North Sea! When Bornholm has to add land, why is it not Bornholm to decide where the Transformer Station and the PTX factory should be located? .


Power-to-X

Or PTX, as it is also called, is something everyone talks about a lot and it is a necessary part of the whole project. Still, (or will) nobody can say anything about what PTX is and what it looks like and where it should be built.

Thomas Thors and Beof have a plan for us to manufacture and sell PTX fuel for ships from Bornholm.

The fuel of the future for ships will probably be ammonia, and therefore we must build an ammonia and possibly hydrogen factory at Bornholm. Such is very large and looks like an oil refinery. Not something I would like to live near.

The PTX plant or ammonia factory can be next to the transformer station, which then gets even bigger or it can be in Rønne near the harbor, so the ships can refuel directly from the factory. Play with the thought.

You read and hear largely only positive news in connection with this whole project, because the stories are told by, for example.

The Danish Energy Agency, Thomas Thors or employees at Beof, whose job it is to sell the project to us.

I wonder that there are no other citizens of Bornholm who have something to object.

Is it that if we do not become the nearest neighbor of this great industry ourselves, then we do not care about the project and with our neighbors and citizens? .


Nature

Nature I can at least find that everyone is totally indifferent.

We can have long opinions whether to build a hut in a tree, but if we get our entire marine environment destroyed and large industry buildings on land as a huge transformer station and ammonia factory with smoking chimneys, then it doesn't even hustle us, just it can be called Green energy so fucking be with the rest. Where Lord is preserved, as Egon Olsen would have said.

What do the nature associations say? The Danish Society for Nature Conservation does not say anything, but they may only protect nature in the rest of Denmark, and then it may be nice to build industry on and around Bornholm.

The marine environment is probably not something the Danish Nature Conservation Association goes up.

Who does then? .


The holiday island

Bornholm is a holiday island because we have a fantastic nature on land and at sea, and a significant income comes from our tourists, many of whom are Germans. The Germans have a lot of wind turbines and they hate them, so they enjoy coming to Bornholm, where we have not nearly as many wind turbines as at home in Germany. But we get that.

I believe in the long term that the offshore wind turbines south of Bornholm and the large land facilities will make many of the German tourists and others find new holiday destinations.

The few permanent workplaces Energiøen give Bornholm, are nothing against the jobs we will lose in the tourism industry in the long term, I think.

We haven't heard anything from the tourism industry in this case either, but they may have stood on the winning team and cheer on the energy island project? Prices of cottages can be reduced.

What do the cottage owners say at Sydbornholm? .


Fishing

It will be difficult to fish south of Bornholm, and the sailors will probably also change the course so as not to collide with a wind turbine.

What do the fishermen say to this project? They may be able to do just like the Sami, run litigation afterwards, so when all the wind turbines are set up, they can peel them down again.


Myself

I live south of Aakirkeby, and I am against the development that is underway that I think goes too fast for us to follow.

I mean, the part of the wind farm located south of the large cottage areas in the stalls, Pedersker and Dueodde must be dropped or moved east of Bornholm at least 20 kilometers from the coast and more.

The coastal area all the way around Bornholm at a distance of at least 20 kilometers I think should be peaceful and permanently kept free of wind turbines.

The distance of the 20 kilometers should also be related to the height of the wind turbines, so the higher the wind turbines the longer they have to get away from the coast and not the other way around as the development is now.

There are enormous money interests in making these huge offshore wind farms, and if we do not, the citizens, say, wind turbines are set up everywhere all the way around Bornholm all the way to the coast.

Would we like it? Dear reader, if you do not want to have a view of offshore wind turbines or a huge transformer station so please say from now, even if you do not live in Sydbornholm.

We can only have influence if many say something.

Title: Betro udformningen af transformerstationen til kompetente arkitekter
Content:
Print an architectural competition so that the Bornholm landscape is not raped, but on the contrary is enriched with an architectural masterpiece.

Last Monday, a civic meeting was called on Bornholm Energiø at the Green Solution House. Many expectant citizens had, despite Corona, showed up, and sat close to the bench and were notified by representatives from Energinet, the Danish Energy Agency and local representatives from the municipality and our utility company on various opportunities at the upcoming Energiø. Expectations were high before the meeting.

The reason for the meeting is that the Folketing has decided to build an energy plant south of Bornholm with huge offshore wind turbines, called Energiø, which will be able to supply over two million European households with electricity.

In addition, you need a large transformer station on land, which can receive the power produced, reshape and stabilize it, and then send it out onto the large European electricity grid. You will place the plant south of Aakirkeby, close to the coast and seize about 90 hectares.

However, it does not appear clear whether we Bornholmers will have access to the power. We are too few electric customers and our networks are too small, outdated and unsuitable to receive power from the energy island. In addition, any use of residual heat from the transformer station will become impractical and expensive, as well as it is unclear who will pay for the residual heating system, which we may be able to connect to our common district heating network.

It is also stated that we at Bornholm will be able to use cheap electricity from the energy island to produce climate -neutral fuel in the form of hydrogen or ammonia for aircraft or sea transport.

But it is uncertain whether there are private investors who can see a business idea in producing fuel from pyrolysis or so-called power-to-x, which is called the process.

Power-to-X is still under development and, in addition to power, will require a lot of biomass in order to be manufactured. But where should the biomass come from? Finally, it is also not certain who will be responsible for the construction work for the transformer system. Of course, the task will go to a group from the outside that has the expertise and the economic muscles. So it is doubtful how many Bornholm jobs the Energy Island will bring.

The citizens present at the Green Solution House had many specific questions and basically worked benevolent and well -informed.

But as the submissions and various visualizations were presented, like a change of mood went through the hall. We audience were increasingly troubled when it dawned on us how things are interconnected: can it really fit that Bornholm just has to put area into a huge industrial plant that most of all resembles warehouse magazines in the middle of our beautiful nature and cultural landscape - Without we at Bornholm get more out of it?; No green workplaces, no prospect of sustained green energy supply, no modernization of our district heating or electricity grid, no CO2-free fuel production for our agriculture or transport sector? I would like to point out that we at Bornholm have shown that we would like to work purposefully for the green transition, which most recently emerged during the municipal election campaign. Previously, work has been done with a brigger Green Island strategy here on the island, where we have all been encouraged to formulate personal and common Bornholm goals. The municipality has continuously incorporated citizens' goals in its energy and nature policy. Most recently, even Bornholm agriculture has come into the fight with serious climate -driving shops for its members.

How often have we not experienced these "citizen meetings" that add to foresight co -influence and progress for Bornholm? Where convened experts in fact inform citizens about the actual technical and financial conditions, which unfortunately will have a major impact on our surroundings and everyday life, but where we have so little influence or benefit - just think of the debates, for example, about the nuclear storage or set up of landmill .

It may appear that citizens and authorities are mistaken for each other and that the green transition is thereby being put back.

Citizens are left with the impression that the authorities are in fact not interested in real co -involvement of the local community in a collaboration on the common green ambitions.

The least we Bornholm Citizens should demand, to lay soil for a huge transformer plant, must be that the state co-finances the modernization of our small local electricity system, so that it can partly receive the flow and partly integrate it into our Bornholm electricity grid. As well as we can use the residual heat from the transformer station in our district heating network, so that we become a visibility project that shows how to integrate persistent wind energy at sea by producing district heating on land in the local environment.

If this is not possible, the state, the municipality and the local utilities should work to expand the cable to Sweden and release a suitable area so that Bornholm can integrate its own electricity production from a local offshore wind farm of 100mw.

In addition, I would suggest that we trust the architectural design of the transformer station to competent architects. The design of buildings is too important to leave to engineers. Bornholm risks having to lay land for a huge industrial plant, which will be a violent foreign element in our characteristic nature and cultural landscape.

It should be the task of the state as the developer to print an architectural competition so that the Bornholm landscape is not raped, but on the contrary is enriched with an architectural masterpiece. A masterpiece that can be met with the technological ambitions of the sea on land. A masterpiece of a kind that can create international attention and become an example of the combination of architectural and technological vision and skills. Alternatively, one could purposefully invite world names such as Zaha Hadid, Frank Gehry, Norman Forster or Bjarke Ingels, who throughout their careers have just dealt with sustainability and large green construction projects. The Academy Council should of course be included in the decisions as an advisor to the state.

    You will place the transormator station south of Aakirkeby, close to the coast and seize about 90 hectares.

Title: Erhvervskonsulent om energiøen: ' Hele Bornholm skal i spil'
Content:
The companies out on the island must also look for orders on the large wind turbine projects, says Business Center Bornholm.

There are plenty of opportunities for companies throughout Bornholm, when Energiø Bornholm is reportedly realized in a few years with a gigantic offshore wind farm in two parts south and southwest of Bornholm as well as a land facility on Sydbornholm for transmission of electricity to Zealand and to neighboring countries in the Baltic Sea .

And the opportunities for orders - and thus earnings and jobs - must not only be gripped by companies in and around Rønne or exclusively by large companies, says Business Center Bornholm, but also by smaller companies on the island.

Business Consultant Jørn Pedersen from Business Center Bornholm called for this, as a large number of mainly East Bornholm Business People on Wednesday evening gathered for an information meeting on the energy island at the furniture factory in Nexø.

Jørn Pedersen urged the smaller East Bornholm companies to join forces and to work with the Offshore Center Bornholm and Business Center Bornholm to take part in the tasks of the construction and operation of the energy island, and the derived tasks.

- The energy island is not a Rønne project, he stated. We can also see the rest of Bornholm come into play. For example, Nexø Harbor could come into play as a service port, Jørn Pedersen pointed to and determined that even smaller companies can get a bite of the tasks.

"Maybe you can't get a collaboration with Vestas, but then maybe with one of their subcontractors," said Jørn Pedersen.

Business Center Bornholm offers an ISO certification course for ten Bornholm companies at the beginning of next year.

Lone Reppien Thomsen, Offshore Center Bornholm, also stated at the meeting that it is crucial that the Bornholm companies are getting ready for the demands of the offshore companies for their partners. Below is special security in focus, she emphasized.

She briefed on the experiences made with Kriegers Flak, which has been an absolute success, says Offshore Center Bornholm. Partly because they have succeeded in marketing Bornholm as an offshore island. To gain insight into what the offshore industry wants and to a large extent to have been able to meet the requirements.

Kriegers Flak gives a hint of the perspectives of the Bornholm business community if the energy island is realized. The work of collecting and shiping the offshore wind turbines from Rønne Harbor to Kriegers Flak showed both that many Bornholm companies were involved and that they made money when Siemens Gamesa and Muehlhan used Rønne Havn and Bornholm as a base for the offshore wind farm at Kriegers Flak.


Opportunities for many industries

As mentioned in June, a report from the consultancy Ramboll showed that a number of local companies, due to Kriegers Flak, received an increasing turnover in the order of DKK 100,000 up to one million kroner a month. The growth meant that in some companies more were hired, while for other companies it meant that they could keep employees they might otherwise have had to dismiss.

The realized financial effect of Kriegers Flak was at least DKK 50 million for Bornholm companies, the report stated in June.

Earnings have not only occurred on transport, preparation, repairs and, for example, the rental of tools, but also on accommodation, shopping and restaurant visits, Lone Reppien said Thomsen.

Therefore, there is the possibility of earnings for many industries on Bornholm when the large wind turbine companies move into the island.

The meeting was organized by Nexø Rotary and the business group Østbornholm to inform about the perspectives in the energy island.

    Nexø Harbor can come into play as a service port, pointed out business consultant from Business Center Bornholm, Jørn Pedersen.

Title: Energinet opfylder stort ønske: Bornholm kan få el direkte fra energiøen
Content:
It may be worthwhile to carry the flow from the Energy Island's offshore wind turbines into the smaller Bornholm electricity grid, concludes Energinet, which undertakes to work for a local connection to the high voltage station.

For several months, the regional municipality and Bornholm's Energy and Supply have tried to convince the national energy authorities that the electricity from the energy island's offshore wind turbines should be brought into the Bornholm electricity grid.

It would require an advanced technological solution to create a constant balance in the electricity level, and therefore Energinet did not want to commit to this solution.

On Friday morning, Energinet announces in a press release that Energinet is ready to design the upcoming high -voltage station in Sydbornholm in a way that allows the Bornholm electricity network to be linked to the energy island's new power connections.

- In Energinet we have had a good and close dialogue with Bornholm Region Municipality.

We have a great understanding of the Bornholmers' desire to reap the benefits that Bornholm can get out of a connection - both in relation to the consumption and the production of green electricity on the island. That is why I am super happy that we can now work towards a connection of the Bornholm electricity grid to the energy island's electricity connections, says Hanne Storm Eldlefsen, Deputy Director of Energy Islands in Energinet.

Social economic saving

"First, the analysis shows that it is likely to be technically possible to connect the energy island's electricity cables to the Bornholm electricity grid without compromising neither stability nor security of supply in the total electricity grid on Bornholm or elsewhere.

Just as it is estimated, it can happen without compromising the schedule for the overall project. Secondly, the analysis shows that there will be a socio -economic saving by connecting the Bornholm electricity grid to the energy island's upcoming power connections, ”Energinet writes in a press release.

Bornholm's only power connection is currently the cable cable to Sweden, which in any case was in front of a renovation.

In order to maintain the security of supply, Energinet pays for a Bornholm power plant to produce power in case of fracture or fault on the electric cable to Sweden. This cost to Bornholm's Energy and Supply of approximately DKK 32 million a year can be saved if the Bornholm electricity network is connected to the energy island's cables.

Not a standard item Energinet will now start developing the technological solutions. There will be innovative plants - "in no way standard products that can be taken down from the electrical technology shelves," Energinet writes.

- It has not been done before that a large level of DC at a very high voltage level has been linked to a small local alternating current at relatively low voltage level.

Therefore, we must also have a dialogue in the process of market players and researchers as soon as possible on how to best solve the task, says Kim Søgaard Mikkelsen, Energinet's project manager for Energiø Bornholm.

    Energinet is ready to design the upcoming high -voltage station, whereby the Bornholm electricity grid can be connected to the energy island's new power connections.

Title: Tilkobling af elnet giver nye muligheder
Content:
Access to sell electricity via the energy island's export cables to Zealand, Germany and perhaps Sweden will have a number of benefits. Several photovoltaic systems and wind farms are one of the side benefits, and it will be more obvious to place power-intensive systems such as data centers and power-to-X companies on Bornholm grounds.

For the Bornholm society, there is reason to rejoice if Energinet's assessment that it is technically possible and economically advantageous to connect the Bornholm electricity grid with the Energy Island's offshore wind turbines via the future high -voltage plant in South Bornholm, proves to hold water. The crucial thing is that Bornholm as a island will be much better connected to the outside world in the future, states Energinet Deputy Director Hanne Storm Eldlefsen, who is responsible for energy islands.

The restriction that cable connections today make up will no longer exist.

-Both producers of green electricity, but of course also larger consumers such as data centers and power-to-X systems will have much more space to romp on than before with this solution, says Hanne Storm Edlefsen.

The director of Bornholm Energi and Forsyning (BEOF), Claus M. Andersen, has been one of the proponents of the interconnection of the electricity networks.

- I personally think we have to be able to tell "What's in IT for Bornholm?" When doing a project of that size, said Claus M. Andersen on that occasion.

The group's intention of erecting a coastal offshore wind farm on just 100 megawatts was that this was the amount of current, which according to the calculations could be used on Bornholm or sent to Sweden with the submarine cable. With new cable connections, Bornholm's offshore wind will be less bound by the limitations of the existing infrastructure.

- It will also mean that we are not limited by the fact that it must be 100 megawatts.

Should it become a project of 120 megawatts, it will do nothing, says Helle Munk Ravnborg.

At Bornholm's Energy and Supply, Claus M. Andersen estimates that a connection of the energy island can bring very differently with it to the group when looking a decade.

He mentions the decrease in surplus heat from energy -heavy companies and new investments in more renewable energy and integration of it as examples of areas that align with Beof's strategy. In order to utilize the waste heat most optimally, it is likely that the BEOF will invest in tying the different cities' district heating networks with new pipe connections.

- I very much believe that we have to work on the energy system of the future being as integrated, coherent and agile as possible.

I mean clearly that we are looking into a future where our heating system is tied together in a different way than today when it makes sense. And that is the interconnection helps to support because we go away from having a few large heat sources for several different types. It requires that you can send the heat more back and forth in a continuous energy system, says Claus M. Andersen.

The technological solution to be invented and executed to link the electricity networks requires innovative companies and researchers to join forces. Energinet's Deputy Director foresees that companies with growth dreams will have a great interest in engaging in the Bornholm pioneer project.

- It's probably not the only place in the world where there will be this desire. Therefore, we very much hope that we can bring some players who would like to help develop this technological innovation because they imagine they could sell it elsewhere.

On the whole, Hanne Storm Edlefsen sees great perspectives in the fact that the Energiø project on Bornholm - not just in relation to the interconnection of the electricity networks - can be used as a demonstration that it is possible elsewhere in the world to build this type of groundbreaking energy plant.

Despite the need for newly developed technology, Energin has a presumption that it is possible to satisfy the Bornholm hopes.

- It's something you've looked into for a while because you knew these energy islands were on the way. I have a pretty high expectation that we can solve this in collaboration with market players and the entire development environment in the sector. We have had very talented people to analyze the - boats with us and outside Energinet - who believe they have the assurance that it can be solved, says Hanne Storm Eldlefsen.

- I have to make a reservation when something completely new is developed, but I have a really good feeling that we will probably get to the finish.

Title: Sådan gør vi Bornholm Great Again
Content:
