Next to the cow, which was removed on Friday by the municipality, on January 1st stood a sign with the slogan "Make Bornholm Great Again".

It slogan refers to Donald Trump's "Make America Great Again" or the Maga movement, which the vast majority of Danes distance ourselves from because we do not largely believe in Trump's understanding of democracy and solution to the US challenges.

We have so far tried to find at the editorial staff to find the backman and have the thoughts behind "Make Bornholm Great Again". Until the success of the Tidende's suggestions on how Bornholm can become Great.

The key to a Great Bornholm is a healthy and self -driving economy. Today, the rest of Denmark pays almost half of all Bornholm's municipal expenses if we count the ferry subsidy. With a new green growth, more jobs and inhabitants, it is an opportunity to stand on your own.

Although there is a very long way there, we have already taken some very big steps in that direction. The government's goal of advancing and expanding the energy island of Bornholm is a huge step, just as Friday's happy news about the interconnection of the big and the small electricity network helps us well.

The future of Bornholm depends on whether we can have jobs on our island in the middle of the Baltic Sea. Here are Jensen, Espersen and Beckpack brilliant examples of companies that, with Bornholm labor, compete with the whole world market and have success. We and their like -minded people must take good care of and help to grow. Business is the economic engine that draws us forward.

The green future with wind turbines, electricity grids, green fuel for the ships and hopefully also green traffic to, from and on the island is the fuel that our financial engine uses. The harbor, the municipality and the state have set the tone with green offshore, green branding and energy island in mega format.

Now the trip has come to all of us others on Bornholm.

How do we help develop Bornholm to become the world's most green island? Only in this way can we protect and develop our unique nature and culture. Can our agriculture become more climate-friendly and at the same time get started on the sustainable gourmet image that the small food producers have already created? If Bornholm be Great we must be green. But that's not enough. The island's children should also feel much better. We need to create a society where far fewer have serious diagnoses and distracted, where young children do not drink full, and young people do not die from drugs or kill in the forest. One grip is to give the children leisure clubs so that they can be included in healthy communities after school. But the effort requires far more than that. The majority in the new municipal council has promised voters to rectify the conditions for the children, so fortunately it also draws promising here.

Make Bornholm Green Again and focus on our children and business.

Title: Udsigt til store havvindmøller vækker bekymring: Kom kritikken i forkøbet - vis hvordan de ser ud
Content:
Most Bornholmers who, as individuals, have submitted the consultation response about the energy island to the Danish Energy Agency, care about the project's dimensions and the mills' distance to the coast, which goes down to 15 kilometers. The only visualizations of the mills are based on old prerequisites.

The 53 consultation response contains a mixture of very technical objections and reminders from other state authorities, warnings from nature and environmental organizations, recommendations from Bornholm organizations and calls from ordinary Bornholmers.

In the last category, the project's dimensions are the predominant concern.

A handful of Bornholmers have submitted this similar answer with criticism of the decision, which opens up for the nearest mills to stand just 15 kilometers from the coast. In the original agreement, 20 kilometers were determined as the distance requirement.

“I would like to object to the deviating from the adopted recommendation, Nov.

2020, to place the wind turbines 20 km from the coast. There should be a minimum of 20 km from the coast to the wind turbine. The height and amount of wind turbines will dominate the coastline and the view of the horizon totally. The problem will be big even at 20 km's distance, but 15 km is absolutely unacceptable, ”writes several residents.

Impact on the landscape Some of the consultation responses are written by people who attended a well -attended civic meeting in November.

Several of them miss information from the Danish Energy Agency and Energinet about the size of the mills and the transformer station as well as the impact of the plants on the landscape.

At the Citizens' Meeting no visualizations of the mills were presented.

"No one answered how the Eiffel Tower height actually looks when standing on the Bornholm coast. It is then pearl to work out a simulation - and I think the parties in Offshore Bornholm are good at getting prepared and presented.

To be criticized, ”writes Esben Ørberg, who indicates that he wholeheartedly supports the energy island.

The only publicly available visualizations were made in 2020, and Tidende today brings examples of the simulated images where the consulting firm Urland has signed the offshore wind turbines, as expected to tone on the horizon. The premise is 260 meters high mills in a park of 2 gigawatts, where the distance to land is at least 20 kilometers. These prerequisites are at the last point different from reality today, with state authorities planning to move the mills five kilometers closer to the coast. At the Citizens' Meeting in November, it also emerged that the height of the future offshore wind turbines to the energy island - from sea surface to wing tip - can be higher than the 260 meters on which the visualization is based. Finally, it is conceivable that the Folketing can choose to expand the energy island from 2 to 3 gigawatts.

Birgitte Tolstrup also wants more information about the dimensions. She was present at the Citizens' Meeting, which she left "overwhelmed and harmful," she writes.

"We have to produce green energy, I am involved. That Bornholm has been given the dubious honor of becoming the world's first energy island, I am despairing, but must resign. But just to resign without being heard without protesting, can I do not accept, ”writes Birgitte Tolstrup, who believes that the debate up to the first initial hearing has been deficient.

"Has there been a thorough public information about the size and consequences of the project? No. Have politicians ensured that the Bornholmers understand the scope of the project? No. Has there been any kind of dialogue? No. Have we had any influence on the project's design? No ", writes Birgitte Tolstrup.

Second-Tourist Dimensions and Noise Several other concerned Bornholmers emphasize in their response that they support investments in offshore wind farms.

"We would like to point out that we are supporters of the green transition. But we would strongly urge to place upcoming wind farm (s) as far away from the Bornholm coastline as possible.

Further out on the sea than 20 km from the coast, "writes Poul Holm and Christine Holst, elaborating on their point of view:" Wind turbines, which are twice as high as the highest point on Bornholm, the Rytterknægten 162 meters above sea level, will have enormous visual consequences if if they are placed close to land. We fear that the lovely Sydbornholm beaches with associated tourist currents will develop into a second-tourist goal or an area that is completely deselected ".

They need to go further away Tom Christensen and Kate Nielsen believe that the mills should be moved further away from the coast, so you can be sure to avoid noise nuisance.

"The mills in Germany stand further away from the coast, and they are a bit lower than those you expect to be set up at Bornholm. (...) We are not against the installation of the mills, but against the noise nuisance that results in both residents and residents and residents and residents Tourists, ”writes the couple, who encourage the Danish Energy Agency to make and obtain calculations made by the Germans.

The consultation round was linked to the framework for the impending strategic environmental assessment.

The deadline for submitting answers was 13.

December, and only after the New Year has the Journal gained access to the consultation responses. A new consultation round is waiting later this year.

Title: Efter at have gennemført udviklingsprojekter på Bornholm for omkring en milliard kroner: Denne gang har DTU-projekt også fokus på udviklingen af det lokale erhvervsliv
Content:
DTU plans to intensify the university's presence on Bornholm and link young, wise heads with the Bornholm companies to a much greater extent than before.

The Technical University of Denmark (DTU) has since the 00s engaged in research projects on Bornholm, and from the very beginning Professor Jacob Østergaard has participated in the collaboration with Bornholm actors as Østkraft/ Bornholm Energi and Forsyning (BEOF). DTU also plays an important role in a promising project that the regional municipality has helped to start with a number of other local institutions and large companies. On the threshold of the energy island, the consortium extends after a million support from the Danish Business Authority for the establishment of a National Center for Green Energy.

The fact that public support is flowing to DTU's projects on Bornholm is far from any news. The new this time is that DTU, together with BEOF and the other key players, asks this question: - How can we get it useful in relation to the Bornholm business community?, As Jacob Østergaard explains.

A large part of the projects that DTU has participated in with the Bornholm energy system over the years have been funded by national or EU-based technology development programs in the energy field.

- There have been projects for about a billion kroner, says Jacob Østergaard, head of the Center for Electricity and Energy at the university, which is headquartered in Lyngby north of Copenhagen.

- Many of the activities have been a lot about the development of technologies - and also about how to use them. It can be with the electricity customers in the Ecogrid project, for farmers or at the port that has had equipment installed. We are now looking at energy islands and bunkerhub, ie how Bornholm can become a gas station for green energy in the Baltic Sea.

So far, hasn't there been much focus on the local business community? - No, the money is given to develop new technology. But it has also benefited Bornholm that all these projects have been conducted. People have been employed and paid for the projects, electricians have been out to set up, and customers at the energy companies have got smart heat pumps, solar cells, says Jacob Østergaard.

Extra interesting to be here the new collaboration goes after utilizing Bornholm's momentum from the roles of Testø, Energiø and Bunkerhub to improve the conditions for companies, explains the DTU professor.

- DTU as a whole wants business development throughout the country, but we can just see some synergies for what is going on at Bornholm, and which makes it extra interesting for us to be present at Bornholm and work closely with Bornholm in the energy field, says Jacob Østergaard and elaborates why the university has joined the collaboration on a national center for green energy.

- With DTU glasses, Bornholm is really interesting, because we can accelerate the development of some of the technologies that we help develop. We can also use Bornholm in development contexts by using the island as a case in teaching. We really want to expand that. We work a lot with energy islands and power-to-x, which is closely related to the plans to make a bunker hub, and we also want to be more present around Denmark. All that goes hand in hand with developing Bornholm commercially in this area.

Young, wise heads In November, the municipality submitted the application to the Danish Business Authority. If it is accommodated, the money will lay down the reason why it will be possible to establish the National Center for Green Energy. If you succeed in attracting the approximately DKK 50 million required, DTU will soon have a permanent presence on Bornholm. As part of a National Center for Green Energy, the university plans to open a so -called residential college - a college and educational satellite who can welcome students who go to Bornholm to investigate aspects of the Bornholm energy system or do projects with local businesses.

It is in the cards that the National Center itself will deal with projects within the three main areas that the regional growth team has paid attention to: 1) to become the Baltic Sea Center for offshore wind, 2) to become the Baltic Sea Green Transport Hub, and 3) to be an international test island.

- Or continue to be, because it is Bornholm today, the professor notes the third point.

- These are the three recommendations from the growth team, but in order to utilize it commercially, some more things are needed. One is to connect some young smart heads to all this, so that they can both come to Bornholm, work with the companies and work with the Bornholm system, says Jacob Østergaard.

In this way, students can learn something as part of their education, while their work can benefit the Bornholm business community.

- Some of them will - from the business perspective - maybe see some opportunities in getting a job on the island afterwards. Some may even think of doing a start-up company with some new technological solution and placing themselves on Bornholm, says the DTU professor about the students.

He emphasizes that the innovation project is both about helping the existing Bornholm companies and about attracting new companies from outside to a region that does not have many large energy companies to draw the big load.

New business opportunities In this way, a national center has the potential to become a big gain for the Bornholm community, which the new mayor, Jacob Trøst (K) also highlighted last Friday when he welcomed Energinet's announcement that it is realistic to connecting the Bornholm electricity grid to the energy island.

- We have also sought growth team funds for us to find these innovative solutions under the auspices of the National Center for Green Energy. So there can also be new business opportunities here, Jacob said.

Applicants have a hope that Rønne's old power plant on Lille Madsegade may form the framework for the national center.

- We would like to gather everything in a living house that can be a meeting place and a display site for visitors, an innovation house and the meeting point for the students. We have had a look at the old electricity plant where you could make a pretty cool environment - and as historically some threads have back to a function that makes pretty good sense in relation to the project, says Jacob Østergaard, who has high expectations of what The collaboration - as over 30 DTU students this week will have a taste of during a visit to Bornholm - can lead to.

- It is all the elements together that allow the different actors to see themselves in this. The students will be able to get something out of it and it will enrich the other parts.


Three recommendations

The headings on the three recommendations from the Bornholm Growth Team describe where the local actors see great business opportunities in the coming years: 1.


National Center for Green Energy

The center's vision is "Bornholm as a hub for green energy, which in the intersection of technology, innovation and business development will expand Denmark's green leadership position." The total project is expected to get a budget around DKK 50 million.

In November 2021, the regional municipality allocated two million kroner as co -financing for the application. The municipality expects up to 85 percent of the cost of the project to be covered by the Danish Business Authority's grant pool, which targets the initiatives of the regional growth teams.

The following organizations have worked actively to write the application, but in addition, several large companies and Energinet had stated up to the sending that they support a national energy center on Bornholm: Bornholm Regional Municipality Business Center Bornholm Bornholm Energi and Forsyning Rønne Harbor Denmark's Technical University Center for Regional and Tourism Research Campus Bornholm Bornholms Agriculture and Food Business Clusters, including Marlog (Maritime Business and Logistics) Business House Capital Destination Bornholm.

He welcomes the green energy development on Bornholm, which could mean that he returns after completing his education as a civil engineer to live and work at Bornholm. Photographer Berit Hvassum

Title: Ørsted, Siemens og Danfoss er med i storstilet energiprojekt
Content:
The industry's heavy boys, together with DTU and Energinet, support the creation of the National Center for Green Energy at Bornholm, among others.

Ørsted, Siemens Gamesa, Danfoss and Haldor Topsøe are among the renowned companies that have entered the National Center for Green Energy project.

In total, 19 very different actors have the status of financial partners. The Journal brought a list of the co -applicants who were confirmed on Wednesday in early November, but since then agreements have fallen with, among other things, the four large companies.

Among the local partners is Bornholm's Regional Municipality, which in November on behalf of the partners in November sent an application to the Danish Business Authority with the desire to take part in a pool of DKK 600 million. The money comes from EU structural funds and must be distributed between Danish projects selected by the seven regional growth teams.

Geographically, the Bornholm Growth Team is clearly the smallest of the seven, but because of the importance of energy island and the national outlook, the partners hope that it can be possible to get an amount that clearly exceeds the share that would case Bornholm if the Danish Commerce Agency exclusively related to the region's almost 40,000 inhabitants.

- Our application of 50 million is shooting over the proportion of the population, but on the other hand, the project proposal is a national center that is not only for the benefit of the Bornholm business community, but which must also expand the whole of Denmark's leading position within green energy, explains development consultant Mads Boss, There is the regional municipality's project manager.

- The national angle is what justifies the application, he says of the ambition of DKK 50 million.


Innovative technology

The Energy Islands will force the industry to develop new technology, and this has led many large companies to join as economic partners. One of the innovations will be the way with HVDC technology (a high-voltage network at DC) at the transformer station can connect the offshore wind turbines with the electricity grid.

- Testing new solutions to be built into the transformer stations has had great interest from DTU, but also for the energy fighters in the application such as Ørsted and Siemens, explains Mads Boss.

Energinet has also joined the project as a state authority as well as the owner of the high -voltage network and larger transformer plants will play an important role. By having the status of financial partner, companies and organizations can cover the costs of the work.

- In order for you to cover consultancy or salary expenses in the project, you have to be what the Danish Business Authority calls financial partners, explains Mads Boss.

- If you find out that more partners are needed, you can add them at a later date, he adds.


New company

The money from the EU pools distributed by the Danish Business Authority can cover up to 85 percent of the applicants' expenses. The remaining 15 percent must co -finance the project.

"In addition to co-financing, a circle of founding partners is expected to deposit between DKK 10-15 million in starting capital to a newly created company called the National Center for Green Energy," the municipality wrote in November before the application was shipped. The Finance Committee then allocated two million kroner to the municipality's co -financing.

Bornholm Region Municipality is the operator of the application and the project until an independent company for the National Center for Green Energy is established. Listed on the list of applicants is this future company, which will therefore be entitled to receive financial support.

- It is planned to establish the National Center for Green Energy as a form of company that participates on an equal footing in the project as other partners. The company is intended for the role of the future driving force and the meeting point for working with all the different development tracks, explains Mads Boss.

In February, the Danish Business Authority is expected to distribute the growth team funds that originate from the EU Regional Fund and Social Fund. The money must be spent and the project reported by June 30, 2023.


Seven areas

In the Bornholm growth team application, seven focus areas - or "work packages", as it is called in the project material, have been appointed.

The seven areas are thus distributed. In parentheses it says which organization is responsible as head of each of the seven work packages: National Center for Green Energy (Bornholm Regional Municipality) Energiø (Bornholm Regional Municipality) Power-to-X (Rønne Harbor) Test Island (Bornholm Energy and Forsening ) Innovationhub (Business Center Bornholm) Residential College (Technical University of Denmark) DataHub (Technical University of Denmark).


19 economic partners

A mix of large companies, research institutions, industry organizations and local players have joined forces to the application to the Danish Business Authority: Ørsted Siemens Gamesa Danfoss Haldor Topsøe Energinet Skovgaard Invest Business Center Bornholm Bornholm Regional Municipality Bornholm Energi and Supply Rønne Harbor DTU Center for Regional and Tourism Research Campus Bornholm National Center for Green Energy.

Title: Energiøen i Østersøen er kommet godt fra land
Content:
In 1991, Denmark was the first country in the world to build an offshore wind farm.

And in a few years, Denmark will also be the first country in the world with an energy island.

The idea of ​​an energy island in the Baltic Sea is only a few years old, but already the vision has come off well. And just as important, it has created the basis for plans and development that can create growth locally and nationally.

As we say on Bornholm, we have already built the island. And we are also ready to reap the many benefits that the energy island will provide for Bornholm, the island's residents and the local businesses.

The other day the news of a connection of the energy island came to the Bornholm electricity grid.

This means that Bornholm no longer needs to have diesel generators standing as a reserve capacity for the search cable to ensure security of supply.

When a socio -economic saving benefits from the connection of the Bornholm electricity grid, the flow from the wind turbines at the same time benefits the Bornholm citizens and businesses.

The same is true when it comes to reaping the benefits a connection can provide compared to the production of green power on the island.

The port of Rønne is working on a project to make Bornholm a green gas station for the many ships that sail annually on and off and around Bornholm.

The idea of ​​a green gas station is based on the fact that imports, production and export of green fuels can be made to ships.

But the production of green fuels requires that part of the energy from the Energy Island is also considered in local power-to-X-production of green energy.

In order for it to succeed, there are still many uncertain questions that need to be answered. What type of fuel should be produced, where and how to refuel? But just as much the answers to the questions, the project sends a signal that we at Bornholm as a starting point see the possibilities of the energy island.

If the opportunities are to become specific projects and jobs, there is no doubt that it requires political support and support. Locally, but to a great extent also nationally.

For support from the island's citizens and businesses there is - we are sure that as long as it is clear that the energy island also creates value locally.

Title: Bornholmske indvendinger mod landanlæg: Udskriv en arkitektkonkurrence og grav hallerne ned
Content:
In the consultation response about Energiø Bornholm, among others, the Architects Association and a couple of newly elected local politicians are calling for the authorities to make an effort to involve architects when the land facility in Sydbornholm is to be drawn.

At the first civic meeting on the energy island in November, Energinet unveiled what the type of land plant usually looks like. In the presentation, Deputy Director Marian Kaagh from Energinet showed pictures of Jutland transformer stations that are slightly smaller than the energy island. The attendees were told that the converter plant on Bornholm will be between 23 and 25 high. Several buildings will be built in Energinet's examples were square bricks with a floor plan of 103 x 60 meters. In total, there is a need to find area of ​​about 90 hectares (0.9 square kilometers) for the land plant, which will be fenced in.

The expected appearance in the South Bornholm Landscape records many, you can read in the consultation responses that the Journal has gained access to. Several responds to Energinet's presentation at the Green Solution House in November, where Marian Kaagh told about what to do to get the big ones to get the big ones power systems to fit into the surroundings.

Usually, Energinet plants trees and other local vegetation around the transformer stations, but it will be wrong to forget about the buildings and the large installations that will be in the open sky, believes Gugga Zakariasdottir, who has written a consultation response on behalf of the Architect Association's Bornholm Department.

"Planting can do a lot, but the starting point must always be to design buildings and facilities so that they are functionally and visually in the surrounding environment.

The Architects Association at Bornholm will therefore call for an architectural competition to be printed before the impending planning process (preparation of municipal plant supplements and local plan proposals) is initiated, ”Gugga Zakariasdottir writes on behalf of the Architects Association.

She proposes to print an open, international competition, which must take into account how the buildings can be aesthetically designed and how buildings and the outdoor high -voltage installations can be adapted to the landscape.

"There is a need for the creativity of the architectural profession to solve a task and form typologies for future construction - to create a project that would like to inspire others around the world when the green transition is massively investing in the green transition in the coming years. of the energy sector, ”writes the Architects Association's local department.


Masterpiece

Mikael Benzon, newly elected municipal councilor from the Unity List, agrees that the architects must not be forgotten when the transformer-and-converter station is to be designed.

"The design of buildings is too important to leave to engineers," he writes.

"Bornholm risks having to lay land to a huge industrial plant, which will be a violent foreign element in our characteristic nature and cultural landscape. It should be the state's task, as the developer, to print an architectural competition so that the Bornholm landscape is not raped, but on the contrary enriched with an architectural masterpiece. International attention and become an example of the combination of architectural and technological vision and skills, ”writes Mikael Benzon.

His party partner Stig Westermann, who is also new to the municipal council, urges the Danish Energy Agency to involve "one of our strongest brands on the island - namely our great tradition of world -class crafts", which he writes: "Maybe you could print a competition among the Bornholm Craftsmen.

Who can 'wrap' all or part of the building (s) in the most creative and beautiful way? What is not buildings could then be 'wrapped' in nature in the form of trees, ramparts and lakes. A story of persistent green energy - art and nature. It is not better off, "summarizes Stig Westermann.


IMMERSION

Another way to reduce the visual impact of the big bricks would be to dig them down. This proposes, among others, Michael Trolle, who believes that the regional municipality and other Bornholm players should work to camouflage the land plant.

"Establishing Energiø Bornholm must keep up with high demands on the visual load from the plant on the part of Bornholm. Not least in relation to a immersion in the terrain of the entire plant, as far as the establishment of a visually acceptable area with planted ramparts around the plant, so - so - Over time - will disappear as trees on the new ramparts grow louder, ”writes Michael Trolle in his consultation response.

Bornholm's Environment and Energy Association (BOMEF) also recommends that the feasibility studies look at the possibility of a partial burial or immersion in the terrain to minimize the visual genes. At the same time, the association's chairman Peter Haag calls on the authorities to place the land facility in fields with agricultural operations.

"Nature on South Bornholm is already burdened. Bomef therefore proposes that existing agricultural land be taken primarily for the construction area instead of natural areas," writes President Peter Haag, he also proposes that the preliminary surveys include whether the many roof surfaces of the predicted plant can made available for the location of solar cells - instead of such solar cells being placed directly in rural areas ".

The wind turbine industry follows the Bornholm objections has already been listed by the wind turbine industry's interest organization, Wind Denmark, which calls on the state authorities to be interested in "the visual conditions".

The South Bornholm area, designated to lay ground for the transformer station, "can be said to characterize the Bornholm idyll with rolling fields in an open landscape with very little buildings," writes Wind Denmark.

"A country plant that will be able to handle up to 3 GW of offshore wind, everything else will be of considerable size and will therefore also have a significant visual impact where it will be established. For that reason, and especially due to some Bornholmers expressed Concern about what effect a large industrial plant can have for local tourism and Bornholm's image as a tourist island, Wind Denmark recommends that the visual conditions should have a high degree of detail, ”writes Wind Denmark in the consultation response.

The consultation, which lasted until December 13, was about collecting ideas and suggestions prior to the strategic environmental assessment set by the Danish Energy Agency this year. During 2022, the regional municipality will also start the planning work. Within a few months, the area where the land plant is to be erected will be found.

The Danish Energy Agency has so far appointed a zone on Sydbornholm between Arnager and Raghammer Odde as the place, where the cables from the offshore wind farms are led ashore. The land plant can be placed up to five kilometers from the coast.

It should be the task of the state, like Byg Lord, to print an architectural competition so that the Bornholm landscape is not raped, but on the contrary is enriched with an architectural masterpiece.

The landscape of the illustration is not Bornholm, but in the spring of 2022 Energinet is expected to have narrowed the location for the transformer and transformation station so that more precise visualizations can be made.

Title: Thors til Energistyrelsen: Så få som muligt skal generes
Content:

With reference to the ambitions to transition to CO2-neutral energy sources in 2025 and make Bornholm fossil-free in 2040 the regional municipality commits to contributing to the energy island.

Bornholm therefore wants to go constructively into the work of realizing Energiø Bornholm and agrees that it requires Bornholm to lay areas for the installation of land facilities for the offshore wind farm, "wrote then mayor Thomas Thors (S) in the consultation response that the municipality submitted In November.

We look forward to the Danish Energy Agency presenting visualizations and landscape adaptation in several locations prior to the final selection of location. In this context, it is important that areas with special protection status are taken into account as f.

The real area of ​​the consultation response asks the municipality four relevant questions about the content of the plan. The municipality. It plays a crucial role that as few as possible get nuisance and that the impact In landscape and nature are minimized as much as possible, ”the municipality writes in the consultation response.

Title: Stort millionbeløb til grønt fyrtårnsprojekt
Content:
27 million from the Danish Business Promotion Board gives the dream of a national center for the utilization of green energy from offshore wind turbines, planned for a location in the old power plant in Rønne, a push in the right direction.

Bornholm takes the first, big step on the road to the founding of a center for green energy.

A new, broad consortium with a number of public and private actors is behind the commercial fire tower Bornholm and has just received DKK 27.2 million from the Danish Business Promotion Board.

Along with the work for the Center for Green Energy, a number of other main activities in the commercial lighthouse Bornholm must be started, and the goal is to contribute to Denmark's green transition and at the same time create growth and jobs on Bornholm, according to a press release.

Mayor Jakob Trøst (K) is excited because the lighthouse project will "open up large business opportunities for Bornholm".

- We must take advantage of our status as Energiø and our unique location in the Baltic Sea close to the upcoming offshore wind farms to play a significant role in Denmark's green transition. Both in the short and long term, the lighthouse project contains activities that will give companies opportunities to generate revenue and jobs. And the work starts with preparing a roadmap for the implementation of Bornholm as the Baltic Sea Center for offshore wind energy, he says according to the press release.

The lighthouse project includes a number of major main activities and many smaller projects to be rolled out during 2022 and 2023.

The most striking is the National Center for the Utilization of Green Energy from offshore wind turbines, which is planned for a location in the old power plant in Rønne.

The ambition of the center is that it must be national and international hub for green energy and draw actors, activities and investments in green energy to Bornholm.

Among the other projects in the Bornholm Commercial Lighthouse, which can be realized with the funds from the Danish Business Promotional Board are :? Realization of Energiø Bornholm with a focus on the business opportunities in Bornholm as the center of the Baltic Sea for offshore wind energy.

? Bornholm as the Baltic Sea Green Transport Hub.

Preliminary study, which, among other things, illustrates the possibility of a Power2X pilot system on Bornholm.

? Further development of Bornholm as a test island, where local, national and international players develop the future energy technology solutions.

? Residential College for students and researchers from DTU, other universities and educational institutions develop and share knowledge.

? Establishment of data platform that enables the collection, storage and sharing of relevant measurement data.


Commercial Lighthouse Bornholm

The new consortium consists of private companies such as Siemens Gamesa, Ørsted, Haldor Topsøe, Skovgaard Invest and Danfoss as well as a number of public actors, clusters and knowledge institutions: Bornholm Regional Municipality, DTU, Rønne Harbor, Bornholm Energy and Supply, The Local Business House branch and the clusters Marlog, Digital Lead and Energy Cluster Denmark.

It is Bornholm Region Municipality that leads the consortium.

Title: Kæmpe store havvindmøller vil ødelægge vores kystnære miljø
Content:
The Bornholm politicians need to think carefully and do what they can to get balance and sustainability into the energy island.

The battle for the green transition is in full swing and it is now that plans are made and decisions are being made that will change Bornholm for the next 50-100 years.

The government, together with most of the parliamentary parties, has decided that two offshore wind farms will be built south of Bornholm called Bornholm I and II.

So the Folketing has decided for me to see without asking the Bornholmers.

There has not been a public debate about the Energy Island, which in my opinion should have been up to the municipal elections, so that one could vote for politicians according to their attitude.

You totally want to consider Bornholm Self-Government after this energy-island lap.

Dan Jørgensen claims that strong forces on Bornholm have been pushing to get started in the offshore wind turbine projects.

I do not know who the strong powers are, but I know that many Bornholmers are against this development because of the size of the project and because of everything we cannot be informed at this time.

Here I think about how many gigawatts should be established in Bornholm in total? It affects how close the wind turbines should on the coast and the size of the land plant, etc.

The land plant is filling 90 hectares, which corresponds to an area of ​​more than half of Aakirkeby! The other we need to know is what should the power-to-X system look and where it should be? In Ekstra Bladet you could read about suggestions for the location of nuclear power plants.

If we once needed to build them, it was suggested that they be near the Powet-to-X system.

Does that mean we can look forward to getting nuclear power on Bornholm as well? I certainly hope not.

The point of these questions is to try to find out what the consequences of the energy-island project will have for Bornholm in the longer term beyond a center for green energy.

So, is there a limit to how big the whole project can be, or should we just keep building the energy industry on and around Bornholm until there is no more space? I realize that wind turbine and power-to-x enthusiasts are happy with this development, but not everyone is delighted.


The height

We cannot know the height of the wind turbines either. The day after the end of the consultation period, the Danish Energy Agency announced that the wind turbines could be 350 meters high and perhaps even higher because the development is going so quickly in this area.

This is like a whole lot of other things about the Energiø project elastic in meter dimensions.

The Danish Energy Agency is constantly changing the framework as needed, and we cannot be sure of anything.

For me to see, during the consultation period, there was talk of wind turbines of up to 268 meters, which are included in the visualization report, and therefore they must not be higher.

If they are to be higher, they need to go further away from the coast and a new consultation is needed, I mean.

I wonder that the Danish Energy Agency is already talking about wind turbines that are far higher than 268 meters, which is the height that is currently being tested in Østerild.

There is probably not enough knowledge about wind turbines that are 350 meters high and therefore it can give the impression that we become part of a great experiment when we become part of Energi Ø Bornholm.

The need for green power will be huge in the future, and if we are not to have destroyed all our marine environment around Bornholm, we have to say to this development.

Unfortunately, it is necessary to establish large offshore wind farms, but it is important that we do at the same time, everything we can to preserve as much nature as possible and fredera areas for wind turbines.

It is important for wildlife, for tourism, for ourselves and Bornholm.

In a 2007 report on the future offshore wind turbine locations, it can be read that a distance of 34 kilometers to the coast is recommended at a wind turbine height of 260 meters.

It also says that quote: The turbulent effect can be felt up to 20 kilometers from the offshore wind farm.

So it is currently happening that elastic in meter dimensions or salami methods are popular because the state, together with the wind turbine industry, is working to be allowed to set up offshore wind turbines everywhere.


Coastal

As if it is not enough with giant state offshore wind farms south of Bornholm, there are (probably the same) strong forces that work for us to also have a privately owned coastal offshore wind farm near Bornholm.

Such a coastal offshore wind farm must range from 4 to 15 or 20 km from the coast, and these wind turbines will thus become even more visible, and in my opinion they will destroy our coastal marine environment.

This privately owned offshore wind farm should be able to make about 120 MW.

120 MW corresponds to five to six of the large wind turbines that the state stands.

I would suggest that the state sets six extra wind turbines up 20-30 kilometers from the coast and pull the cables from these mills directly to Bornholm's Energy and Supply.

The state is responsible for the maintenance and operation of the mills, and we will decrease the power and of course pay a little for it.

I think coastal wind farms should be banned throughout the country, and I think it is unworthy that we need these fighting matches throughout Denmark about our marine environment that we should protect.

One would think that the Danish Environmental Protection Agency would protect our marine environment and nature, but they seem more interested in building offshore wind farms, understanding who can.


Jutland

In Jutland, in my opinion, they have a sensible approach to their Energiø project, where they will build the offshore wind farms 80 to 100 kilometers from the coast, so that you cannot see the wind turbines from land.

The Jews obviously go more into protecting their nature and marine environment than we do on Bornholm, and the Jutland politicians with Søren Gade at the head have succeeded in saving their coastal nature.

However, it costs a lot of money - 50 billion plus to build an artificial energy island in the North Sea and part of that money, we will probably have to pay over the tax.

I agree that offshore wind turbines should be so far out to sea that you can't see them, and therefore I would suggest that when we have to pay for their energy island, the offshore wind turbine park Bornholm II has to be moved to the North Sea, such that We do not get ruined Bornholm's largest cottage areas and thus our tourism.

In this way we will be able to just establish Bornholm in the offshore wind farm, and the land plant on Bornholm will be reduced in size and fit better our island.


Arguments

At Bornholm we are a few who try to argue for and against the Energiø project, and in my opinion some arguments are better than others. Tidende's editor -in -chief believes that we should sacrifice Bornholm for the green energy, and he writes that because we use energy -wicking fast ferries, we have to let the state build Energiø on land and in the sea south of Bornholm.

I mean, it's a strange argument, but there are thousands of arguments that we need a lot of green energy and then time must show how green it is.

The ferry service of Bornholm is, like much else, a complex case, and I am sure that the Ministry of Transport has expected a lot to find the best solution with regard to ferry type and more.

I have read that fast-moving conventional ferries use more fuel than our fast ferries, so if we are to have a solution that uses less fuel, it should probably be of the POVL anchor-type, and then there will be enough trouble reaching the capacity we Has with Express 1.


CHOICE

Unfortunately, we do not yet have much to choose from when it comes to renewable energy, and therefore offshore wind is unfortunately our best bid at present.

I have lived close to onshore wind turbines for many years, without having been a problem, but I know that when 130 giant wind turbines are to be set up, it can't be on land.

The wind turbines have to get out to sea, but I think it is important that we place them as far out on the sea as possible so that they do not create new problems.

As I said, I am not against offshore wind turbines, but they must be placed wisely and not destroy our nature.

It is and will be a balance between the green transition and our nature, and if we do not find that balance, the green transition will destroy too much and ultimately become a burden on our society.

The birds I am concerned that especially the Bornholm II offshore windshield park will block the road and take the lives of many migratory birds coming from the south, and I think it is wrong to place offshore wind farms right up to bird protection areas like the south of Bornholm.

I think there should be a wide bird corridor south of Bornholm, and that the offshore wind farm Bornholm II should be moved to the North Sea or to East of Bornholm.


The Minister

Dan Jørgensen said we are complaining because we do not want the offshore wind turbines close to land and close to where we live, and he is absolutely right.

The wind turbines should be as far out on the sea as possible - 20 and preferably 30 kilometers from land. I can guarantee that it will look like they are close to land, even if they are getting 20-30 kilometers away because they are getting huge.

The next time you drive past one of our onshore wind turbines, try to imagine it is three times as high.

As Henrik Espersen said, they will not be removed again once they are set up.

So it is a matter of timely care and to find a balance, and even if the reason for the wind turbines is that we are trying to save the climate, we should not destroy nature and our coastal marine environment in the process.


Politicians

Bornholm politicians have from the beginning either been supporters of the Energy Island, but I think it is about to go up for many of them that unfortunately there are not only benefits, but also disadvantages associated with the project.

I mean Bornholm politicians need to think carefully and do what they can to get balance and sustainability into the energy island. In this way, they should relate to the Energiø project with a healthy skepticism and take into account all stakeholders and citizens on the island.

That is why we have voted for you! If the wind turbine enthusiasts are allowed to decide it all, I think we will ruin too much of our unique Bornholm nature, and this will have negative consequences for tourism and for Bornholm's population.


HEARING

The first hearing is over, and unless it has to go due to new height of wind turbines, we can look forward to the next hearings when placements etc. become concrete.

Politicians, the Danish Energy Agency and the Minister say they will listen to the input of the citizens, but if they do not target any of those we say and write, then hearings make no sense but are a waste of time.

Unfortunately, you can get the idea that hearings, bird examinations and EIA reports are just some paperwork that needs to be done and that the authorities then just continue the construction work.

I hope that is not right. I hope and believe that they will really listen.

Title: Havvindmøllepark kan blive fatal for kritisk truet marsvinebestand
Content:
The Danish Society for Nature Conservation and the WWF World Nature Fund are concerned about the construction of offshore wind turbines at Rønne Banke, as it can have fatal consequences on the heavily endangered population of Baltic Guinea pigs. Also when it comes to bird life, the project triggers concerns.

From a climate perspective, the nature associations are, as a starting point, supporters of the fact that 2 GW of offshore wind turbines are being set up as part of the upcoming project, Energiø Bornholm, which the government has proposed. The offshore wind turbines can help meet the need for green and renewable energy that will only grow in the future.

However, the Danish Nature Conservation Association (DN) and the WWF World Nature Fund also have some concerns about what the project can mean for biodiversity. In particular, the associations are concerned about what the project can have of consequences for Baltic Sea Guinea pigs.

This is stated in consultation responses to the environmental assessment of the plan for Energiø Bornholm.

"... DN is also concerned about the consequences of the construction of the heavily endangered population of Baltic Sea Guinea pigs, and especially in the area where you want to set up offshore wind turbines, the population has its winter stay," says DN in its consultation response.

According to DN, the population of Baltic Sea is a guinea pig of about 500 individuals, of which less than 100 of them are childbearing females. Therefore, it does not take much until the population is threatened with its existence. DN states that according to a report from ICES1, losses in, for example, by -catch (or other death due to human influence) of less than 1 individual could have "fatal negative impact on the entire population" annually.

Underwater noise must be examined as Denmark is obliged to protect and secure the species, no matter where it exists, the DN encourages that one is very thorough in connection with the environmental assessment and that one relates to how to secure guinea pig population against, for example, underwater noise .

"Since there is a massive expansion over many years, it is important to assess what effect this elongated impact will have on the designation species throughout the construction period and the operational phase," says DN.

The WWF World Natural Fund also believes that it is important that a strict precautionary principle is maintained in connection with the establishment of the offshore wind farm.

The association points out that the Baltic Sickness of Guinea Pigs has been rated as "critically threatened" by The International Union for Conservation of Nature.

"The loss of just a single individual is critical of this stock. The environmental assessment of the sea plan concluded that Energiø Bornholm and offshore wind farms can have significant negative impact on guinea pigs and even potentially prevent guinea pigs from achieving a favorable conservation status. It is therefore WWF's assessment that there must be made an extremely thorough preparation in the form of setting up and analyzing scenarios and Fine mesh preliminary study of guinea pig deposits in and around the project area, ”says the consultation response.

Suggestions for hunting bans also when it comes to bird life, the project triggers concerns. Rønne Banke is a Natura 200 area, which is newly designated as a bird protection area.

"For DN, it is extremely important that it is very thoroughly investigated what consequences the expansion of offshore wind, in an area where this is not found, and clutched by a protected area, will have for the Natura 2000 area designation species. Among other things about the seabirds that use the area and where it appears from the environmental assessment of the sea plan that there will be a risk of displacement of seabirds (of Example sea lit, black duck and velvet sand) and that this can become more or less permanent.

If this happens, it will be in violation of the Habitats Directive, "DN reports.

The Danish Ornithological Association BirdLife also wants an assessment of the project's impact on bird life, just as the association wants an assessment of how negative influences of bird life on and around Rønne Banke can be compensated.

"For example, there may be a hunting ban (especially motorboat hunting around Bornholm), Fisheries and Sailing Restriction or other regulations of other disturbing activities that result in caught up and other disturbance of the waterfly, which are then even more displaced from the areas." in the consultation response.

However, the mills can improve nature The offshore wind turbines at Rønne Banke are not only the disadvantage of nature. DN Bornholm believes that if the establishment of the mills is done properly, then they can even be an advantage for nature.

"We suggest that at the land plant not only take all considerations to protect and preserve the existing flora and fauna. Opportunities must be taken to improve conditions for nature in connection with the plant," says DN Bornholm's chairman Anna Sofie Poulsen in her consultation response .

The DN Bornholm chairman proposes, for example, that soils and stone piles can be made in selected places along the cable trace of agricultural land, so that the conditions for Flora and Fauna be improved. She also points out that the conditions surrounding the transformer station and possibly coupling systems should be designed to give the greatest possible natural value.

DN Bornholm finds it appropriate that assessments of the impacts on the environment be made in the short and long term, so that the mills can be established in the most nature -friendly way.

"We assume that the impacts on the environment in the short term will be large and negative, while in the long term they should improve conditions for the marine flora and fauna, also in relation to the current state if the sea systems are designed properly," says Anna Sofie Poulsen, who has many other ideas on how this can be achieved.

For example, the wind turbine foundations can be made with hollows and stone accumulations so that they provide optimal conditions for the marine flora and fauna, she suggests in the consultation response.

DN is also concerned about the consequences of the construction of the heavily endangered population of Baltic Sea Guinea pigs, and especially in the area where you want to set up offshore wind turbines, the population has its winter stay.


No to red flash at night

It is not only concerns about the wildlife that the nature associations mention in the consultation responses to the environmental assessment of the plan for Energiø Bornholm. DN Bornholm also mentions things at the offshore wind turbine park, which can become disruptive to people.

The association is particularly concerned about the visual influence that the high wind turbines can have when looking out at the sea from the southern and western coasts on Bornholm.

"In terms of the possibility of expansion of Energiø Bornholm and the installation of wind turbines up to 15 km from the island, we would urge that all opportunities to set up the many wind turbines as far to sea as possible, and in a way that diminishes the visual impression. from Bornholm as much as possible, ”writes DN Bornholm's chairman, Anna Sofie Poulsen, in the consultation response. She adds that it should be a requirement for the upcoming project that no 2-3 GW of offshore wind is established with flashing red light markings at night, but that the aviation marking is solved in an alternative way.

She points out that today from large parts of South and Westbornholm and as far north as north of Hasle you can clearly see the red flashing light markings from the Wikinger offshore wind farm, although the German offshore wind farm is 60 kilometers from Bornholm.

"The experience of the German mills has surprised many Bornholmers," writes DN Bornholm, who therefore believes it is important that in the feasibility studies for Energiø Bornholm, which will be somewhat closer to Bornholm than Wikinger, a visualization of the flashing effects will be made in the form of a video that gave a true impression of the light impact at night.


Bornholm should not just be a conveniently lying rocky

The Bornholm local branch of the Danish Nature Conservation Association believes that it is vitally important for acceptance of the changes that the energy island will cause the Bornholm society to become part of the project.

"It is important that we are fitted with power from the wind turbines and heat from the transformer station. It is important that Bornholm is not seen as a conveniently lying rocky knot that enables the establishment of a hub without having to build an artificial island as in The North Sea, but is seen as a society that would like to help realize the green transition with all that it entails, ”says DN Bornholm's chairman, Anna Sofie Poulsen, in her consultation response to the environmental assessment of the plan for Energiø Bornholm. The main organization in the Danish Nature Conservation Association also supports this.

"DN in particular emphasizes local anchoring and popular ownership, which is crucial to implementing the green transition and large renewable energy projects, as is the case here.

Bornholm's communities should be involved in creating the most ownership of the project and to find the best solutions in the construction phase, ”says DN in his consultation response.

Title: Området er indsnævret til 260 hektar: Her vil Energinet lægge enorm højspændingsstation

The gross area is later narrowed to 70-90 hectares.

In the letter, the residents of the area west of Limensgaden are informed and between Søndre Landevej and Vasegårdsvej about the next steps in the process.
