Title: Frederik kan blive nabo til kæmpe højspændingsstation: Jeg er ked af det
Content:
Frederik Tolstrup loves the southbornholm landscape. That is why he is that he is likely to be a neighbor of Energiø Bornholm's planned transformer station.

Farmer Frederik Tolstrup lives close to the 260 square meter area southwest of Aakirkeby, which has been appointed to accommodate Energiø Bornholm's planned transformer station. It does not affect him that the quiet farmland must be changed for posterity.

- I'm sorry. It's going to change the area completely, says Frederik Tolstrup.

- It will be a huge, huge big building.

I know a little about construction through my work as a farmer, and 70 to 90 hectares in scope and and 25 meters in height is very large. In addition, a lot of cables must be dug down. I often drive past the area on the way to Rønne, and it is a little daunting to imagine the quiet and quiet farmland being plowed up by large excavators and that something so big has to be built, says Frederik Tolstrup.

Breaks with the rhythm of generations It was something else entirely that he and the family moved to Bornholm after.

- I moved back to Bornholm because I wanted to live where I grew up and see things develop quietly. I have nothing against the fact that a single agricultural building is being made or that a house is being removed or built. But these are not huge changes that you move to Bornholm after - not at all to Sydbornholm.

- I'll probably look at that transformer station for the rest of my days. There will be one before and one after. The pristine and the situation that things just continue as they have done for generations is just over, says Frederik Tolstrup.

Money is not so important to the farmer it is a thin patch on the wound that he is likely to be able to reap personal financial gain from the project.

- I own land, and it may be that the land in the area increases in value because there is less of it. Therefore, it may well be that we are going to make a lot of money on it.

But I would have liked to be besides, says Frederik Tolstrup.

However, from a community perspective, he can easily see that the transformer station can contribute positive things - even if they come with a high price.

- We can get an electrification of the Bornholm community that we would otherwise not have received. It is also good that there will be less CO2 emissions and hopefully a lot of jobs, says Frederik Tolstrup.


Facts

The layer and flag schemes are managed by local action groups, which are associations with members from the local area's business community, associations, public authorities and local citizens.

At the beginning of each program period, the local action groups prepare a local development strategy for the LAG and the flag, which in the following years sets the framework for what is granted.

At the annual general meeting of the association, 14 board members are elected for a two -year term. All board members work voluntarily and unpaid for LAG/ Flag-Bornholm. The board hires a coordinator as general manager.

Overall, it is about promoting the growth and establishment of new jobs in the designated rural areas and fishing areas and strengthening the framework conditions in the designated areas.

During the current plan period 2015-2022, Lag-Bornholm has given a commitment to support for 75 projects with a total budget of more than DKK 27 million.

In the flag area, there have been commitments to support 17 projects with a total budget of DKK 10.5 million.

    Frederik Tolstrup is likely to get used to living close to a huge transformer station.

Title: Hvordan ville København reagere?
Content:
Six hours is a long time without power. How do you think the residents of our capital would respond if they - as a recurring problem - should find themselves in such large holes in the stream?

At 17 minutes over six Saturday morning, the power went.

Those who had been up early had had their morning coffee or -te. But most of us had to go to a dry morning, offset them by gas stove, hot stove or good bonfires.

If you are happy with your morning ritual such a cozy, sunlit on Saturday, then the hours stayed long. Only at a quarter past 12 - six hours after the power cut! - There was power in all the Bornholm sockets.

It's really, really long.

How do you think the Copenhageners would respond if they - as a recurring problem, should keep in mind - should go a quarter day without power? And then a Saturday! We live in a modern society on Bornholm. We want everything that all other Danes have. We have cozy cafes and mega shops. We quickly have internet and smart technology. We have great visions.

But when the flow goes, as it does on a regular basis, we are reminded of how isolated we are actually out here in the Baltic Sea.

It is super annoying for us as private consumers, but it is also much more than just that of people and industries that are directly dependent on electricity.

We should move towards something where such a thing is not a theme, and fortunately we are also on our way with our energy island and the green ambitions.

But right now and in the coming years we are living with the regular holes in the stream, and although it is initially something that is irritating, we can spend the six -hour respite on reflecting on the life we liver.

It is basically very healthy, because it gives us the opportunity to just feel why we live right here.

But then: It is strange that it takes two hours for our local utility company to be activated by the State Energinet Denmark and can start the island operation - as we write here in the Journal. Shouldn't one think "the flow has gone - what is the worst possible scenario?" And then get started in the boilers as the first? Then we could avoid coffee -thirst Bornholmers all Saturday morning, and we could avoid people being without the opportunity to use emergency telephone, without important information and without many of the necessities we associate with being a modern society - like the rest of the country.

Title: Her kan der blive lagt kabler til energiøen - biologer går snart i gang med forberedelserne
Content:
Lot owners in a 15 square kilometer area of ​​South Bornholm can expect to be visited by biologists who will register animal and plant life in the coming time.

In February, Energinet published, where the large high -voltage station to the energy island is expected to be erected. The affected landowners were told in a letter. This week, a larger group of landowners at Sydbornholm have received mail from Energinet with an information that they own land in the zone where it may be possible to put cables to or from the high voltage station.

The area is bounded to the west by the place between Arnager and Sose, where Søndre Landevej is closest to the coast, while the eastern border is at the stalls. There are just over seven kilometers between the extremes. The cable area extends up to 2.5 kilometers into land. It is within this area that Energinet plans to carry all cables ashore.

The information has the Journal of an overview card in the letter Energinet has sent. The total planning area for cables fills about 1,500 hectares - or 15 square kilometers.

"Far from the entire gross area will ultimately be affected, but here early in the planning phase it is necessary to investigate a larger area before the precise locations are determined," Energinet writes in the letter.

Animals and plants The reason to orient affected residents and farmers is that biologists from the consulting firm that Energinet has hired is starting to study the South Bornholm nature.

“The studies will be carried out by 1-2 biologists moving around the area on foot.

They will not intervene, but simply observe, take photos and make registrations of animals and plants, ”Energinet writes.

-It will to a large extent be biologists who register plant and wildlife, but there will also be many other different studies, says project manager Bent Sømod from Energinet's environmental and geoscience department to the Journal.

He mentions cultural monuments, dikes, soil conditions, surface water systems and streams as other things that need to be described in the coming months and years.

- We go out and do studies to get some knowledge about how to work on the project, among other things in terms of establishing the cables, he says.

In the area there must be room for both the cables from the offshore wind turbines to the high voltage station and the export cables, which are scheduled to be carried to Germany and Zealand.

On the map there are five places along the coast marked with yellow lines where it may be the case to lead the cables ashore. However, Energinet has not settled on where on the 7-8 kilometer stretch of coastline that the cables should go.

- It requires further examinations. We are investigating the entire blue line for the landing, says Bent Sømod the results of the study must be included in the overall environmental impact assessment that the Danish Environmental Protection Agency is responsible for preparing about the Energy Island project.

This assessment will also outline the consequences in the municipalities of Zealand, where cables must be carried ashore and a high -voltage station will be built to reshape the electricity transported from Bornholm as DC.

In the letter to the landowners, Energinet announces that during the spring a new citizen meeting will be held on the Energiø project.

The field surveys at Sydbornholm are expected to take place until mid -2023. However, no one should expect the excavators to start for the time being. The construction work is a few years out in the future, for the central environmental permits will only come into place in 2024 if the existing schedule holds.

- Nothing happens until 2024 - and probably another year or more will be.

For example, archaeological feasibility studies must also be done before, says Bent Sømod.


Cable Corridors

On Energinet's website, the state -owned system operator, who becomes the builder and owner of the land plants (both cables and the high -voltage station), answers more questions about the land plant to the energy island.

One of them is: - What happens to the areas where cables underground should carry the flow from Energiø Bornholm to the plant on land? "The cables are not visible after the construction phase when they are in operation. However, for each cable, however, there will also be use restrictions in a belt of about 7 meters (for example, restrictions against planting, etc.).

Establishment of cables is aimed at avoiding forest and larger planting belts, as cables will prohibit the planting of trees and shrubs with in -depth roots after the establishment of cables. If it cannot be avoided to cross forest or larger coherent plantings, the cable lines are established so that visual division of the vegetation is avoided as far as possible.

Plank corridors for establishing cables will have a width of approx. 1,000 meters, while the final working widths of each cable in most cases will be 30-40 meters. Why is there such a big difference between plank corridors of the 1000 meters and the 30/40 meters? It is there because plank corridors are a gross area designated to be able to investigate this whole area for how precisely the 30-40 or 100 meters wide cable trace can be placed. The 30-40 meters are for each cable the width where there will be a construction site along the way.

Source: Energinet.dk.

    It is this area of ​​1,500 hectares that Energinet will investigate in more detail in 2022 and 2023, because it may be possible to put cables to the energy island. The high voltage and inverter station itself must be placed north of Sdr. Road in the central part of the area.
    The cables from the offshore wind farms are expected to be brought ashore in several places on the stretch between Arnager and the stalls. Here in the Bay of Sose, conditions will be examined in the coming months. Photo: Jacob Jepsen
    The high voltage station will be placed north of Sdr. Road. The two front of the wind turbines at Vasegårdsvej are within the gross area that Energinet has selected for the land plant if buildings can grow up to 25 meters high

Title: Kritik af energiø: ' Vil ødelægge landskabet for altid'
Content:
Bornholm Agriculture & Food supports the plans to make an energy island in the Baltic Sea south of Bornholm, but at the same time wonder that the gigantic large transformer station will be placed in fields on South Bornholm rather than in an industrial area in Rønne.

Lars-Ole Hjorth-Larsen is positive about the project Energiø Bornholm, which is about putting off offshore wind turbines in the Baltic Sea south of Bornholm. It told the outgoing chairman when Bornholm Agriculture & Food held a general meeting on Wednesday evening.

- We are positive about the project.

- Bornholm gets a huge push in the green transition, and in fact many possibilities open up. We will be able to be at the forefront, and if investors can be found, a power-to-X system may also be an opportunity where it will all create jobs, he said.

However, the agricultural organization is not so much for the Danish Energy Agency's plans to carry the cables from Energiø Bornholm ashore on the south coast between Sose Odde and Raghammer Odde, and a few kilometers from there set up a transformer station that may require an area of ​​up to 90 hectares.

"However, I am surprised that the large plant that covers 70-90 ha with 26 meters high buildings should not be close to Rønne, in an industrial area," he said.

- Instead, you will dump it down in the middle of southbornholm arable land. It may not be well thought out. After all, the landscape is destroyed forever. When we resident and our tourists come driving along Søndre Landevej, the large industrial plant removes the whole experience by driving along the south coast.

Therefore, he came up with this call.

- Again - Think from the front! He added finally.

- I would say, as Ulf Lundell writes so beautifully: I can best with open spaces. Near the sea I will live.

We will be able to be at the forefront, and if investors Lars-Ole Hjorth-Larsen outgoing chairman, Bornholm Agriculture & Food can be found.

Title: Kommende nabo til enorme energianlæg er modstander af energiø-projektets nuværende udformning: Skalaen i det her er så stor, at folk ikke kan forstå det
Content:
This project will destroy the sea view of the largest cottage areas on Bornholm. That's what Torben Westh Jensen says from Sydbornholm. He believes that the Energiø project should be halved in size and that local politicians should fight more for Bornholm's nature interests.

- I agree that we need power from wind turbines, but ..

This is what Torben Westh Jensen says, who can become one of the closest neighbors to the high -voltage station in South Bornholm.

He lives south of Søndre Landevej, and if he turns his eyes the opposite way, in eight to nine years he will be able to look out at the wind turbines that will supply several millions of northern Europeans with electricity and make it possible to make hydrogen and synthetic fuels that will become a crucial piece in the more troublesome part of society's green transition.

Torben Westh Jensen stands pretty alone with his criticism of the upcoming Energiø.

- It seems like it's a formality.

Some reports need to be written and then just get started digging. It is a Danish -historical building, and I do not understand that there are no more people talking about it, says Torben Westh Jensen to the Journal.

Politicians only see the benefits of public opposition to the green mega project has been limited ever since the plans emerged in the light a few years ago.

- The scale of this is so great that people cannot understand it, says Torben Westh Jensen, who, as one of the few, has written several critical reader letters about the energy island.

The size also creates many opportunities for the Bornholm community and business.

Why don't you focus on the positive sides? - I'm trying to look at the back of the medal - I'm well aware of that. The problem is that all our politicians are happy about the prospects for this. They only see the front of the medal.

Torben Westh Jensen has contacted politicians in the municipal council and the Folketing in the hope that the size of the energy island could become a topic in the election campaign. It didn't happen.

When the energy island was mentioned, it happened with reference to the future of business adventures and the number of new jobs.

- They go up in tree -huts. But this project is going to destroy the sea view of the largest cottage areas on Bornholm - from Dueodde over the Seamarch to the stalls, he says.

Torben Westh Jensen is also skeptical of how many people the energy island on a permanent basis will be employed.

- What are some jobs that you are talking about? If we get such a box up, it's going to go beyond the tourism industry - and it will cost jobs, he says of the land plant, which Energinet plans to erect near Torben Westh Jensen's property.

The worst, he has by understanding why Bornholm should lift such a burden and laying waters to two - and potentially three - gigawatt offshore winds.

- Where does it end? We never get enough power. We are talking about a transformer station that is half the size of Aakirkeby, he says, citing that the plan area for the high voltage system is 90 hectares.

Torben Westh Jensen calls for visualizations of both the transformer station in the Bornholm landscape and the offshore wind turbines, which according to the Danish Energy Agency can get a total height of over 350 meters. Even without visualizations, he does not hesitate to characterize the land facility near Søndre Landevej as "a huge eyeball that tourists must look at when driving to the cottage". He mirrors that Energinet has designated a highly located open area.

- If you moved it further west, there is a hilly terrain with forests that could hide large transformer buildings.

West of Sose there is also a large uninhabited area where the cables could come ashore without a nuisance to residents, he says.

Move half to the North Sea He proposes to move the easternmost of the two offshore wind farms - Bornholm II - to the North Sea. The remaining park will be able to accommodate with a total of about 1 gigawatt.

With such a capacity, about a million households can be supplied with electricity. This must be a sufficient contribution for Bornholm, says Torben Westh Jensen.

- By Bornholm I think we will take our part of the load. My point is that there is no room for more wind turbines down here.

Then they have to put some more up in the North Sea, where they can place them so far from land that you can't see them. Søren Gade (former Left Minister, ed.) Has said they are going out where you can't see them. And I give him completely right. A halving means, similarly, that the transformer station will fit better with Bornholm's size.

Torben Westh Jensen believes that one of the worst things about the project in its current form is that the wind turbines may be set up just 15 kilometers from the beaches on the south coast.

Until in the fall, the 20 kilometer was the limit, but to make room for sufficient wind energy, the government moved the preliminary study area five kilometers closer to land.

The distance to the mills should be twice as large, thinks Torben Westh Jensen, who finds it thoughtful that the energy island of the North Sea should be placed 80-100 kilometers from the coast and that politicians are willing to spend unimaginable sums on sparing the West Jews from the sight of the offshore wind turbines .

- I think sea views are absolutely amazing, and that's probably one of the reasons why I go into this so much. For me, wind turbines on the horizon will destroy the view.

I know someone has it differently.

Don't you say like that because you live out to the coast? - As I have, I would have it over with wind turbine projects all over.

I assume that we must protect Bornholm and Bornholm's nature.

Calls for a folk mood Torben Westh Jensen recognizes that he thinks that the property value likes a crack, but at the same time states that there is far more at stake for him than crowns and ears.

- We all live together only for rent - no matter where we live. So it is not only some like me, it goes beyond, but also all those who in the future would like to live on the Bornholm south coast.

If the high voltage station has to be built on Søndre Landevej, Torben Westh Jensen will hope that politicians will work for a power-to-X system to produce hydrogen and fuels using power may be another place on Bornholm so that the loads of nature are distributed as much as possible.

- All these hydrogen factories and industrial plants I think is not good for Bornholm.

Torben Westh Jensen was not only about writing critical letters to the Danish Energy Agency during the initial consultation phase in December 2021. But the criticism in the public debate has been sparse, he must frustrated acknowledges.

- We don't know what we say yes to. So it's a matter of writing a consultation response when you don't know anymore, says Torben Westh Jensen, who thinks the plans would be suitable for a referendum.

- We haven't been asked about anything. Bornholm has just been used. I would like a better debate about these coastal mills.

    On December 21, Energinet was allowed to extend the preliminary study area to cover parts of the cable routes that had previously been omitted. The map also shows the two offshore wind turbine areas separated by a habitat area and a newly designated Natura 2000 area. The Natura 2000 area, which houses several important bird species, is not marked on the map, but borders Bornholm II and extends almost all the way to the southwest from Dueodde to Hasle. Title: Borgmester om energiøens påvirkning af naturen på og omkring Bornholm: ' Det er nok den pris, vi må betale'
Content:
Jacob Trøst (K) recognizes that the energy island will affect nature and coastline in South Bornholm, but are comfortable with the fact that professionals will find the right solutions.

The energy island in the Baltic Sea has so far been a national project with decisions made by the parliamentary politicians and processes guided by the Danish Energy Agency and Energinet.

In the coming days and weeks, the energy island moves into the local agenda.

The municipal political process has begun in March, and at the municipal council's next meeting, politicians will start a consultation phase on the energy island's high -voltage station. After that, there will be four weeks to submit ideas and suggestions for what will happen to the large land plant with up to 25 meters high buildings in Sydbornholm, which the regional municipality is responsible for making a local plan.


It will bother someone no matter what

An expiry of the colossal energy project comes into focus already today, when the ambitious business project National Center for Green Energy, which has received EU support of DKK 27.2 million, is launched at the old power plant in Rønne.

Jacob Trøst (K), who will speak at Monday's event, tells the Journal that the municipality under his management will focus on utilizing the energy project to strengthen the Bornholm community as much as possible.

- I think it's really good that we can be at the forefront. Overall, the energy island helps to substantiate our green development and our image as a green island. It has a strong focus from all over the world that the small island in the Baltic Sea can be so far ahead, says the new mayor and highlights his interviews with foreign journalists and visits from energy -interested delegations from all over the world as examples of Bornholm's attractiveness and good starting point.

What will be the mayor's line for the next four years? - Of course, it will be that we at Bornholm have to have as much as possible out of it. It is in several areas, he says, citing a few examples - partly there is our security of supply where we have just seen an example of how dependent we are. If we get a sea cable more for, for example, Germany, we will still have a submarine cable if one is torn over. I also hope it will attract some programs to Bornholm.

DTU wants to put parts of their education on Bornholm, and that is very positive, he says.

Recently, the area at Sydbornholm, where cables will be buried and a land plant will be built.

Is it part of your agenda that you will try to work for the land system to become as small as possible for the sake of the influences of nature? - I have no influence on how big it will be, but I want to work for them to make as open a process as possible and that citizens get involved in the choice of location. It is positive that you hear the different landowners whether there are local conditions to take into account that are not shown in maps or by official sources. But it will bother someone wherever it lies. What I emphasize is that you involve the citizens of the solutions.

Understand the concern of the wind turbines at sea: Do you have the view that if it becomes possible to get a park of three gigawatts, then Bornholm should go after it? Or do you want to be careful about getting big mills closer to the coast than 20 kilometers? - The closer to the coast, the more they fill. But it is always preferable to land wind turbines. Green change costs - it costs some money and some disadvantages. I have acknowledged that this is probably the price we have to pay. I would hope that you put them a little off the coast so that at least we are not bothered by noise from them.

Want to consider 15 kilometers to be sufficient? - It's hard to say, and that's what the environmental studies must show.

I will lean on the studies where the project is visualized and the impacts of wildlife and migratory birds are being investigated. I am quite confident that the environmental studies are thoroughly done by some experts in the field.

I have interviewed one of the relatively few public critics, Torben Westh Jensen.

If it is up to him, you should halve the size of the project and drop the part of the offshore wind farm that will be erected closest to Sydbornholm and the cottage areas along the coast - and instead put several offshore wind turbines far out in the North Sea.

His main point is that Bornholm even with an offshore wind farm of 1 gigawatt will still draw a very large part of the green load compared to the size of the island.

What do you say to such a suggestion? - I can understand that some are worried about how much it should fill, but I also think there is a price we have to pay for the green transition.

It is always a trade -off, and there is also lost power if you place the plant far away. I am probably so arranged that I trust that we have some professionals who make these assessments. It is a good and thorough process that is being made.

With the knowledge you have now, is there something that seems alarming to you? - No. But it is clear that two gigawatts are more edible because it is 20 kilometers out. There should be no worries. With three gigawatts you will reach 15 kilometers from the coast, but it is difficult to relate to. I want to wait for the visualizations and the studies, but I also think it will be edible.

Several highlighted in the first consultation phase concerns on behalf of the tourist industry if offshore wind turbines and high voltage plants are erected.

Do you expect the offshore wind turbines to have negative consequences for tourism? - I don't think anyone will choose Bornholm because we have green energy and offshore wind turbines. On the contrary, I think many will say, "fine enough, we can use power over here with good conscience because it is produced green," says Jacob Trøst (K).


2 or 3 gigawatts

The parliament has decided that by 2030 an offshore wind farm will be built on two gigawatts to the Energiø Bornholm. In the first plans, the mills had to stand at least 20 kilometers from the coast.

In the fall, it was decided to expand the feasibility study to 15 kilometers from the Bornholm south coast. This was partly due to a concern about whether there would be room for two gigawatts after a new nature protection area had made up in the suitable areas for offshore wind. In addition, climate, energy and climate minister Dan Jørgensen introduced an opportunity to erect offshore wind turbines with a total capacity of three gigawatts because there was uncertainty as to whether a 1 GW park at Hesselø in Kattegat can be realized.

Title: Wermelin, DTU og Beof forventer turbo på energiøen og grønne investeringer
Content:
Several of the partners behind the National Center for Green Energy pointed out at Monday's launch that the war in Ukraine and the recognition that the West should not depend on Russian energy will create opportunities for Bornholm by virtue of the location as an energy hub in the Baltic Sea.

The war in Ukraine and the sanctions against Russia will have an impact on the speed of the green transition and thus also the energy island and the National Center for Green Energy, which was launched on Monday. Several of the consortium partners agree.

"In recent weeks' terrible events have made it clear that security policy is energy policy," said Bornholm Energy and Supply's director, Claus M. Andersen, who expects the conflict with Russia to get the governments of the European countries to invest more in renewable energy.

- Thus, the National Center for Green Energy has become even more relevant, he says.

This assessment is shared by DTU's Executive Vice President Carsten Orth Gaarn-Larsen, who spoke on behalf of the university, whose students and researchers are increasingly on Bornholm in the coming years.

- The enormous demand that will be for more green energy will make us look at our big projects in a slightly different way, says Carsten Orth Gaarn-Larsen.

- It may have to go faster and there may have to be more green energy. And we may not only have to look at Danish interests - there are Polish, Swedish, Baltic and Finnish here in the Baltic Sea.

- I think it gets a crop and it may well be that it will not be tomorrow, but where it was before the end of the 20s, it may have moved in the mid -20s, he says of the consequence of the war and the energy crisis.

WERMELIN: More wind energy The ambition to become independent of gas has come high on the agenda of the governments of Europe.

The Danish Government's representative at the launch at the Electricity Works, Environment Minister Lea Wermelin (S), - The situation we are now in with Russia's terrible attack on Ukraine emphasizes why it is so important that we have not only the green transition but also puts turbo on it, she says to the Journal.

She emphasizes that the government already had one of the world's most ambitious climate targets with a CO2 reduction of 70 percent by 2030 and a declared goal of becoming independent of Russian gas. In the integrated energy markets, it can only be possible to shield the Danes from high prices if neighboring countries also find alternative energy sources.

- Not only Denmark has to be independent of gas, so should the rest of the EU, and that will mean that we have to set up even more wind energy than expected so far, says Lea Wermelin.

Brand new situation Right now there is a political agreement that two Gigawatts of offshore winds should be set up at Bornholm from 2030, and it can be increased to three gigawatts.

In a situation where you want as much green energy as possible, could one imagine that the mills should stand closer or that the speed could be increased? Are there any things that have changed for the government? - We are in a whole new situation. The green ambitions that Denmark has long pressed for are one of the things we need to have screw up for now. Denmark possesses some skills, and our energy islands, which become the world's first, is a way of showing how to do it. So it's going to have an impact on Denmark. Exactly how are we going to discuss with the other parties.

As an Environment Minister, you have top responsibility for some of the environmental studies that will be made for the land plants for the energy island over the next few years. Is there anything in the work that can be accelerated in the light of what is going on in Ukraine and Russia? Or is it that the process cannot be changed and therefore it takes the time it takes? - On the whole, we are looking at the situation we are in. Many things we will need to accelerate and get ready early, among other things in terms of becoming independent of Russian gas. We look at many companies and how we can help them switch to another source of energy.

We also look at whether there are some processes we can speed up. Something we can do with national requirements, otherwise we must have the other EU countries. With our own projects (such as Energiø Bornholm, ed.) We must also always look at how we can do it in a good way, where we both ensure the involvement of the Bornholmers and make sure that our green ambitions are rolled out as soon as possible .

There is a knuckle for what the Minister of the Environment followed the launch and was not even as a speaker or the government's official representative or cord clipper.

She told the series of speech that she, as a Bornholmer, was "unbelievably proud" that she has succeeded in raising money to the national center and that several large companies are backing up.

- So it's not something that has just ended up in our turban. We have been struggling for many years to make Bornholm a green island and seize the potential. The launch today is just another example of doing great.

One should not be mistaken that the fact that a national center is now being made is a huge gift to Bornholm, says Lea Wermelin.

    Claus M. Andersen from Bornholm Energi and Forsyning believes that the relevance of the national center has only risen within the past month due to the war in Eastern Europe. Photo: Jacob Jepsen
    Carsten Orth Gaarn-Larsen, Executive Vice President at the Technical University of Denmark. Photo: Jacob Jepsen
    Environment Minister Lea Wermelin could tell on Monday that the Folketing in the light of the war in Ukraine will decide what can be done to speed up the green transition and make Danish companies and energy meter less dependent on Russian gas.

Title: Den specielle bornholmske livsånd vil forsvinde med energiøen
Content:
Dear Bornholmers, sit down and think of Bornholm, writes Birgitte Tolstrup from Sydbornholm.

Torben Westh Jensen has had an excellent post in the Journal Monday, March 21, regarding Energiø Bornholm.

He is one of the few who has expressed his attitude towards the project, and he calls for a debate among us Bornholmers.

He is very critical of the project and feels alone with his attitude. He has tried to contact politicians, both locally and in Christiansborg, but does not feel heard.

But you are not alone with your attitude, Torben - I totally agree with you.

I also live in Sydbornholm and have among other things. a. For that reason, been particularly interested in the project. And I am quite sure that many other Bornholmers would also be concerned if they dealt a bit with the project "Energiø".

The reason why it can be difficult to relate to is, as Torben Westh Jensen writes, that the scale of this is so great that people do not understand it.

Dear Bornholmers! Sit down and think of Bornholm. Go for a walk just now and think of Bornholm. Make it clear what it is about Bornholm that just loves. Why do so many Bornholmers live on their island? Why do many young families move back as soon as the shadow of a job emerges? Why do many retirees move to the island? What makes the shoulders fall down and make the breathing easier when you get home from a turbulent weekend over? Why do tourists pay exorbitant prices to have the opportunity to live here for a short period of time? What makes Bornholm special and particularly attractive? When you reach what you love at Bornholm, consider carefully what will happen when Bornholm is changed to "the world's first energy island". Imagine the very specific changes.

Bornholm is a small island. It is a unique island with a unique beautiful scenery.

We are extremely pampered with beauty, wherever we turn our eyes, we are privileged with starry sky, with a wonderful animal and bird life, with small roads, without stressful and stressful traffic, no factory industry, which is noisy around the clock. We live our lives at a pace and in a calm that is human. Here is a spirit of life that is not found in many places in Denmark and soon not at all.

We are a small, slightly old -fashioned community that has been given the dubious honor of having to supply maybe three million households with electricity. It won't "just" be a forest of wind turbines 350 meters high, 15 kilometers out - it won't "just" be the construction of roads, heavy traffic, excavation of fields - it will not "just" be light, turmoil and activity around the clock around. No, I think we will lose the Bornholm that we know. The special Bornholm life spirit will be forever.

We must have power, but less must be able to do so. Three gigawatts are crushing.

Let's think about us! Let's take the debate! Let's find a reasonable compromise.

Title: Ét søkabel har været for lidt: ' Det siger næsten sig selv, at der skal ske noget med det kabel'
Content:
It does not come as a shock to retired civil engineer Paul-Frederik Bach, that the submarine cable has been broken over several laps and that Bornholm has been without power. - It's a calculated risk, he calls it.

It does not come as a shock to Paul-Frederik Bach that every five years Bornholm suffers from power failure when the submarine cable breaks.

He is now a retired civil engineer, and for 40 years he has been working on planning and production of electricity grids. He has worked most of the time in Jutland with the region's electricity network.

Paul-Frederik Bach by one thing or two more about search cables and supply than most, and therefore he is fully involved in the Bornholm supply situation.

A supply he seen from the outside has wondered.

- What has wondered me is that you live with one cable. It almost goes without saying that something has to happen to that cable.

- Of course, it is a matter of money that you do not have an extra. Search cables are exposed, if nothing else for anchor injuries. So if the cable is interrupted every five years, it is fine with the statistics, says Paul-Frederik Bach.


A power failure

Since he has not been sitting at the table when the supply to Bornholm was to be built, he dares not say exactly how it went when Bornholm got his submarine cable. Technically, there are three cables in the Baltic Sea at half a kilometer intervals, but they act as a total unit and only if all cables work.

However, Paul-Frederik Bach is safe in his case when he says that in his time one must have expected that a submarine cable will fail sooner or later.

And since there is no other submarine cable to take over the supply, it has been included that the power plant on Bornholm must take over the supply of the electricity grid. In this case, the Beof is the power plant.

- It is a choice you have made, that you have to live without power for a few hours and that a power plant must take over. It is a calculated risk, it is completely safe. I can understand that it is not cheap to put a cable extra in the short term, but power plants do not live forever, so if you choose the strategy that we leave a power plant backup, then that solution has an expiry date, says Paul- Frederik Bach.

Director at Beof, Claus Andersen, is also not sure how to come up with the solution with a single submarine cable.

But he suspects, like Paul-Frederik Bach, that a power plant has been weighed on Bornholm over an extra submarine cable.

- A general philosophy in this is that you always have to have a reserve for the largest unit.

You must have a certainty that if the largest unit falls away, you can still operate.

They have found that in a way it was cheaper with the power plant on the island that can be the safety of the submarine cable, says Claus Andersen.


More cables

With his many years of experience in planning electricity networks around Denmark, Paul-Frederik Bach had done things differently.

It was expected that the submarine cable would break sooner or later and that the power is smoking on Bornholm.

- At Bornholm you have made the choice with open eyes at that time. From the front, if I had to think so, I would have preferred that there was more than one cable. As our thinking was, we would not let a supply hang on a cable, says Paul-Frederik Bach.

If there is an energy island, then there will be the possibility that Bornholm will be connected to two other cables. That is, the destruction of a cable will not mean anything to the electricity grid on Bornholm. If it happens that Bornholm will get new connections with submarine cables in connection with the energy island, it will be a gift for the island, says Paul-Frederik Bach.

Title: Havvindmøllepark får opbakning til placering ud for Rønne
Content:

The Initiative Group Bornholm Havvind, which wants to build a privately owned offshore wind farm with seven mills off Bornholm, held a citizen meeting on Monday evening at Campus Bornholm and presented four possible locations for the future - small - offshore wind farm.

And of the areas off the castle sling, off the Northern Forest, off Rønne and off Nexø there was clear support for one: Rønne. This is stated by Helle Munk Ravnborg, a person in Bornholm's offshore wind.

- The message was that the best idea is to put the wind turbines up on the inside of the mills to the energy island. If there is a whole lot of wind turbines in advance, it does not make the big difference that there are seven privately owned offshore wind turbines in front, says Helle Munk Ravnborg.

There was no 100 percent agreement, points out Helle Munk Ravnborg, but a predominant support.

There were also critical voices among the more than 100 attendees at Monday's Citizens' Meeting. Among other things, it was suggested to rent an area by Poland and put up offshore wind turbines there instead, but in general Helle Munk Ravnborg believes that there was a mood for Bornholm to take responsibility himself and have offshore wind turbines off the coast.

Price: 1.3 billion The kroner process is now to initiate a dialogue with the Minister of Climate and the Minister of Business to see if you can reserve the area that you end up getting stuck on. In this connection, Helle Munk Ravnborg emphasizes that no final decision has been made on the location of the offshore wind farm and that the other three possible locations are not peeled off the table.

For this purpose, an actual offshore wind turbine must be created, which Bornholm's offshore wind hopes to get DKK 800,000 via the municipality's green grant pool.

The announcement is there, but the money has not yet been released.

If - or when - they come, the offshore wind turbine can be created and you can start figuring out how to sell the 480,000 shares that the offshore wind farm must be split up.

The 480,000 shares each cost DKK 2,700, which means that DKK 1.3 billion must be raised, which is expected to be the cost of setting up and 30 years of operation of the offshore wind farm.

If it all slides and everything goes according to plan, Bornholm's offshore wind is aiming for a privately owned offshore wind farm off the Bornholm coast by December 31, 2026, Helle Munk Ravnborg says.


Close to the coast

The strip of seven offshore wind turbines is located relatively close to the coast in Bornholm's offshore wind turbines - all the way to about five kilometers off the Northern Forest.

And there is a reason why the offshore wind turbines should close to the coast, explains Helle Munk Ravnborg. You would like to enter a sea depth below 40 meters due to the cost of the monopiles of steel that must be knocked far down the seabed.

Title: Krydstogtskibe vil bruge landstrøm: Havn vil have mere end en hensigtserklæring
Content:
19 Cruise Councils have signed a declaration of intent to use Landstrøm in ports in the Baltic Sea. At Rønne Harbor you are aiming to offer green fuel than Landstrøm.

The four largest cruise lines in the world, along with 15 other shipping companies, have signed a declaration of intent on the use of Landstrøm in the Baltic Sea as soon as possible and by 2024. Their intention to use Landstrøm when they are located in ports that have a rural power plant. This is stated in a press release from Wonderful Copenhagen.

Such a facility does not have such a plant at this time, and more than a declaration of intent from the shipping companies is needed to change this. Several things will be decisive for whether the port will establish land power for cruise ships, says CEO Thomas Bendtsen.

- Right now, the business model is not present, as we as a port can never get our investment back. But the important thing is also about standards. There must be a standard for shore power that can fit all ships, otherwise it just makes the financial problems even bigger, says the port director.


Green gas station

Rønne Harbor is constantly investigating the market for Landstrøm, but according to Thomas Bendtsen is also very aware that many of the upcoming cruise ships are sailing on green fuels.

- Therefore, our investments and activities are primarily focused on being able to help to be a port that offers refueling of the fuels, he says.

The harbor is part of a large consortium that will work on getting the harbor ready to be a green gas station by 2025.

- We see this as a significant task that needs to be solved, so the cruise ships are also green when they sail from port to port, says Thomas Bendtsen.


Less role

At Rønne Harbor you almost never feel that cruise ships are demanding land, says the port director, and according to him, access to Landstrøm plays a minor role when the shipping companies choose which ports to call.

- But in the long term it can have a meaning, he says.

Whether the upcoming Energiø will play a role in relation to the opportunity to offer land power, Thomas Bendtsen cannot say at this time. His assessment, however, is that the energy island will play a minor role.

- The energy island will make a huge amount of power produced just outside Bornholm, but what it should be used for, and not least how it should be linked to Bornholm, is still uncertain, he says.

    19 Cruise Councils have signed that they are intended to use land power in the Baltic Sea by 2024 when the ports offer there. The Port of Rønne does not, and the shipping companies' declaration does not immediately change, says Port Director Thomas Bendtsen

Title: Ny melding fra Energistyrelsen kan gøre energiøen betragteligt større
Content:
In the preliminary planning work for Energiø Bornholm, the Danish Energy Agency has adjusted the material, so that it will be possible for an energy company to set up offshore wind turbines south and west of Bornholm with a total capacity of up to 3.8 gigawatts.

On Monday, the Danish Energy Agency started a new consultation on Energiø Bornholm. The consultation is necessary to carry out because the state government proposes to allow significantly more offshore wind turbines than previously planned.

3.8 gigawatts is the maximum capacity that the energy company, which will win the order, can choose to erect.

The increase is related to the fact that the Danish Energy Agency will allow the mills to be able to produce more electricity than the collective electricity grid has the capacity to receive.

With the expected cable connections from the energy island. Such an overcapacity is referred to as "overplanting" in professional language. The Danish Energy Agency has assessed that "it is appropriate to keep a door open for a later stage to make a political decision on possible over -planting for the offshore wind," the board said.


Compensation for loss

"Overplanting does not mean that more power is delivered to the collective network than the production permit indicates. But overplanting can compensate for the loss of power (net loss) that can occur between mills and connectivity, and compensate for the fact that there are usually wind turbines out of operation due to service, etc.

It is not known how offshore technology develops until 2030, but if it is assumed that each mill will have an effect of 15 megawatts, more than 250 mills in the waters of 3.8 gigawatts should be set up in the waters of 3.8 gigawatt West of Bornholm.


Increased density

The extra mills will have to be placed closer to each other than the energy authorities have so far been based on.

“Overplanting occurs within the area that is already set aside for the establishment of offshore wind turbines, ie a maximum of up to 15 km from the coast.

In order to carry out overplanting in practice, the offshore wind developer must therefore choose to set the offshore wind turbines closer than what has been assumed when designating the area for the establishment of offshore wind turbines, "the Danish Energy Agency notes.


Only to gw is adopted

In 2020, the Folketing decided that the energy island will be built offshore wind farms with a capacity of two gigawatts. Last year, the government decided to expand the area where preliminary investigations are being carried out to enable three gigawatts to be performed. It was linked to the increasing need for green energy and uncertainty as to whether it would be possible to build a planned offshore wind farm near Hesselø in Kattegat. If the energy island is to end up getting a capacity of more than two gigawatts, it will require a new political decision.

The consultation phase prior to the environmental assessment runs until 9 May.

"If the environmental assessment shows that the plan can be implemented without significant influences when establishing 3.8 GW it will then be left to the offshore wind developer to choose the financially optimal capacity within a span of 3.2-3.8 GW," the Danish Energy Agency writes in The Consultation Letter.

In parallel with the supplementary state consultation, Bornholm's regional municipality conducts the first consultation round on the land facility in Sydbornholm. It is possible to submit ideas and proposals to the municipality until May 9.


Influences of environment and people

In the consultation material, the Danish Energy Agency lists the potential environmental impact that more mills with greater density could result in: greater impact on the seabed and animal and plant life. More sediment deposits, which can lead to increased release of nutrients and environmentally harmful substances.

Greater risk of collision with birds and bats in greater mill density.

Greater impact of marine mammals and fish during the construction phase because more mill foundations need to be set up.

Larger artificial reefs around wind turbine foundations, which in some cases can be favorable for more animal and plant species greater visual impact from land intensifying noise impact during the construction phase. The total plant period is expected unchanged as the wind parks regardless of size are expected to be operated by 2030.

Increased sailing risk.

Increased radar impact as more wind turbines within the same area can cause extra radar disorder.

Source: The Danish Energy Agency, additional consultation on overplanting.

    The possible offshore wind areas in the Baltic Sea have gradually changed design over the past few years. In the new consultation material, the western part of the energy island is as new divided into two separate areas. Among other things, it is the need for sailing safety that has reduced the area. The environmental studies are based on the fact that the mills can stand up to 15 kilometers from the coast

Title: Flere vindmøller til energiø var et ønske fra vindbranchen
Content:
The Danish Energy Agency is planning to enable the energy company that wins the supply of Energiø Bornholm, to set up more offshore wind turbines and place them closer to each other. By listening to the wind industry's desire to allow overplanting and incorporating it into the work on the environmental assessment, it will be faster to create the framework for more green electricity production. This benefit weighed Wind Denmark in the answer from December.

"By getting stuck on 3 GW, theoretically, theoretically cuts off the possibility of 1,476 MW (NL)- 8.190 MW (BE) ADDITIONAL SUBLE WINNING CAPACITY AND THE RISK OF DIFFERENTS IN AN AMACHED TEMPLIC As it will require the preparation of an SME supplement (strategic environmental assessment, ed.) ".

    So far, it has been a prerequisite that the offshore wind farms for the energy island must have a mill density of 4.55 megawatts per square kilometer. Title: Vrede miner ved borgermøde: Energiøens bagmænd mødte frustrerede naboer
Content:
The presentations during the Citizens' Meeting in Aakirkebyhallen contained no big news. In the hall, there was frustration that the critical voices could not be aired in plenary, as the municipality had prioritized that the well over a hundred participants could talk directly to the representatives of the Energinet, the Danish Energy Agency and the regional municipality.

The future neighbors of the high -voltage station south of Aakirkeby on Tuesday received air for their frustrations over the view of the construction of up to 25 meters high buildings in the open agricultural land.

Compared to the first civic meeting held in November in Rønne, the dissatisfaction with the plans had risen.

Meanwhile, Energinet has also narrowed the plan area to a 260 -hectare area south of Aakirkeby and west of Læså, and many affected residents or landowners had stepped up in the Aakirkebyhallerne to hear about the plans and make their opinion known.

The Citizens' Meeting was divided into two stages; Presentation from the stage and a conversation café. To the clear dissatisfaction of several people present, there was no questionnaire in plenary, so the critical comments had to wait.


Proud and humble mayor

With a defective microphone in his hand, Mayor Jacob Consolation (K) welcomed welcoming "Another Citizens' Meeting".

"When I say" another, "it is with equal parts pride and humility, he said.

Pride of Bornholm's status as the world's first energy island and humility over the municipality's impending task of hearing citizens whose existence can be influenced by the huge construction project.

- It's you who know the areas best. So thank you for coming, the mayor said.

This afternoon's host was Søren Møller Christensen, head of development and plan. He explained that the next phase is about getting stuck in the final area where the land plant is to be built.

- Our primary purpose of the meeting today is to dress you up to submit good consultation responses.

The important thing in this context is to get your input in relation to the location.

That is our greatest interest, said Søren Møller Christensen.

- Many people have asked us what it will look like with the landscape around the land facility. You are also very welcome to write about, but you will also have the opportunity to influence later in the process, he added.

Leading employees from the Danish Energy Agency and Energinet then got the floor for ten minutes, but they did not bring much new to Torvs.

The Deputy Director of the Danish Energy Agency, who, along with the municipality, is currently conducting a consultation on closer mill setup, emphasized the green transition in the large perspective.

"It is a European ambition we are working to fulfill," said Mogens Hagelskær, mentioning that in Europe today about 30 gigawatts of offshore wind has been installed.

The war in Ukraine has raised the targets considerably, and the European Commission presented an ambition to add 420 Gigawatt solar energy and 480 gigawatts from wind turbines by 2030, of which much is expected to be installed at sea. The energy island on Bornholm is expected to contribute somewhere between 2 and 3.8 gigawatts. The maximum limit has moved because the Danish Energy Agency has opened to allow so -called overplanting, which means that the wind farms are given a capacity that exceeds how much power can be transported in the cables. Neither the Danish Energy Agency nor Energinet had brought new visualizations where the wind turbines nor the land plant were located in the Baltic or the South Bornholm Landscape.

The speaker from Energinet, who becomes the builder on land, did not try to tone down the dimensions of the construction project.

- The station must use an area of ​​between 70 and 90 hectares. It actually corresponds to three times the area of ​​Christiansø, said Energinet's chief project manager Kim Søgaard Mikkelsen.

Pedagogically, he tried to explain what feature the large halls and outdoor installations get.

- The red bricks are converters who turn alternating current into DC - large phone chargers can be said, he explained, before drawing attention to the coils under the open sky.

- We use our outdoor facilities to raise the voltage of the system. At the same time, there are some dip ditees built in so that we can turn off the power, in case something happens at the station, explained Kim Søgaard Mikkelsen.

He drew a picture of the other possibilities that can lead to Bornholm to become an electric hub across countries in the Baltic Sea.

- At the same time, we have a great desire that we would like to connect large consumers and producers.

It could be for power-to-x and the production of fuel for ships and aircraft.

At the same time, it will be possible to connect a large solar cell park to the energy island, he said.


Target is minimal consequences

Before the traveling guests were given the opportunity to talk to the locals, Helle Munk Ravnborg (EL) took over as a person for the Nature, Environment and Planning Committee Microphone.

She tried to appeal to the fight to minimize global warming.

- If we want the green transition for Denmark and Europe, we must also look in the eyes that it has a price for our landscape.

She understood that the ambition of the municipality is that the construction "has minimal consequences for the landscape and minimal consequences for the citizens who have their homes in the area that is now looking at". At the same time, she reminded the people of the rows of chairs that offshore wind turbines and transformer stations in one place will redeem power plants and other buildings that do not adorn the landscape.

She got that point out by showing overview pictures of the ports in Rønne and Copenhagen with chimneys and oil silos.

- The fact that you can see your energy production and energy plant is nothing new. It is certainly not a architectural gems we can see in the picture, but maybe we can say goodbye to some of them when we get the energy island, said Helle Munk Ravnborg, who finished the speech.

The representatives from the municipality, the Danish Energy Agency and Energinet then spread around the tables in the other part of the hall.

There was the greatest interest from the closest residents for Energinet's table, where consultant Claus Arnfeldt Andersen was repeatedly asked to explain what Energinet will emphasize when the final location is to be found.

- I can't stand a formula, but we have to have everything up on the table in principle, he explained.

When all problems - it could be water holes that need to be looped, or acquisition of properties - are known, Energinet and the municipality will find the area to be covered by a new local plan and a supplement to the municipal plan.

- There's a sea of ​​things. We can't just say that one thing will weigh heavier than anything else, said Claus Arnfeldt Andersen, who received advice from farmers with land in the zone.

- It may be that you have to let some of the production professional things weigh a little higher than the larvae, said a landowner.


Billion bill at sea

Energinet's representative explained that the 260 hectares between Søndre Landevej and Vasegårdsvej have been selected on the basis of an overall consideration of what was already found by properties, geological interests and natural areas - in combination with the vicinity of the coast and suitable corridors for the approximately 25 cables that must be led ashore from the offshore wind turbines.

Some neighbors presented alternative locations outside the 260 hectare zone. The most alternative is the construction of a high -voltage station at sea. Both Energinet and the Danish Energy Agency were asked what it would cost. The Danish Energy Agency's Deputy Director of Energy Islands, Mogens Hagelskær, could tell that the calculations have never been made, but that the construction of the artificial island for the Energiø twin project in the North Sea amounts to six to ten percent of the total cost of DKK 210 billion. In other words, with a very rough calculation one could expect it to cost DKK 12-20 billion to spare Bornholm for the land plant, Mogens Hagelskær and Tidende sent himself together.

Back at Energinet's table, neighbors came up with several suggestions on how to best hide the high -voltage station if buildings come to protrude 25 meters over the fields. The proposal to build a ten -meter -high soil planted with trees was brought up as an idea that judged on the consultant's reaction seemed difficult to realize in practice.


Challenges with water

The fact that the land plant must be placed in a low -lying area will also make a deep burial, which several have otherwise expressed their wishes, it sounded around the table.

- We face major challenges with surface water, noted Claus Arnfeldt Andersen.

He was asked what would cause the energy to give up the gross area. The answer was that if the local polarists had to refuse to make a local plan after the hearing, then Energinet would have to find another place on Bornholm.

A resident with a house close to the gross area advised Helle Munk Ravnborg, who had found himself at Energinet's table, to soon get stuck in the final location.

"You should be obliged to choose the place quickly so that you can start planting right away," said the man who had brought his son to the Citizens' Meeting.

Around the table, accusations of a "shooting process" and the municipal council's unwillingness to receive critical questions at the Citizens' Meeting. The atmosphere caused Helle Munk Ravnborg, who himself is engaged in a local citizen group's plans to build a smaller, folk -owned offshore wind farm to let a remark fall against a municipal employee: - People are angry, overheard the Tidende to say her.

The ongoing consultation phase runs until May 9th. More citizen meetings and consultation periods await in the coming year. The municipality is aiming for the local planning basis to be adopted in June 2023, and Energinet aims to start construction in the fall of 2025.


Two hearings about Energiø

There are two currently two hearings in progress on Energiø Bornholm.

Bornholm's regional municipality calls for ideas and suggestions regarding the location of the land facility. The consultation must lead up to the preparation of a local plan and a supplement to the municipal plan.

The hearing runs until May 9th. Submission of consultation form can be done on the municipality's website, as an email to Plan@brk.dk or by mail to Ullasvej 23, 3700 Rønne, where the letter is felt "Energiø".

The Danish Energy Agency in parallel is consulted on an increase in the number of wind turbines for the Energiø project. The designated area has not changed, but with the additional consultation, it opens to place the mills closer to each other. This hearing also lasts until May 9th.

Title: Energiøen bør nedskaleres for at passe til Bornholm
Content:
Why can't an artificial island be built to the transformer station south of Bornholm, just as they do out for Jutland? Sounds one of the questions from Torben Westh Jensen.

It is currently. decided in the Folketing to establish 2 Gigawatt offshore wind farm south of Bornholm, which in my opinion is ample for Bornholm if we are to avoid destroying our nature and marine environment.

I and many others think Energiø Bornholm must be scaled down to fit Bornholm.

Isn't there a single Bornholm politician with courage enough to protect Bornholm's nature and marine environment? Or do they only have an opinion if it is a hut in a tree? I am still wondering that politicians, both locally and in the rest of the country, can only see the benefits of erecting offshore wind farms everywhere.

Energiø Bornholm's Hav and Land Anlæg will change the entire Bornholm minimum for the next 30 to 50 years, and therefore I believe that all Bornholm politicians have a duty to comment on this. I think they should be critical and that they also have a duty to make sure that there is a balance of things and not just taken into account our energy needs. The same goes for politicians in the rest of Denmark.

Is there not a single organization in Denmark as the Danish Nature Conservation Association with others who have an opinion on this, or are all citizens of Bornholm and in Denmark just happy that it should not be in their "back yard"? Speaking of "Back Yard" it is about to become so that if you, like me, live with a view of the sea, then one's opinions do not count at all because you only think of your sea view and property value.

We have to be neighbors of all this is not taken seriously at all.

Due to the war in Ukraine, the government will have established Energiø Bornholm even faster, and at the same time they will make it even bigger.

From the beginning, preparation has been done for 3 gigawatts, and now there is talk of 3.8 gigawatts.

That is, it is almost a doubling of the size of the plants, as they are currently. will do by over -planting offshore wind turbines so that they will stand too close, and with regard to the land plant, they will probably just take some more of our land.

Overplanting will surely prove to make the wind turbines ineffective because they stand too close and shade the wind.

I mean, it is a strange elastic in a meter -oriented way, to do things, and that we have in principle only relied on the consultations to 2 gigawatts.

How many hectares will be the land plant when making 3.8 gigawatts? Where should the PTX system be and how big it will be? There has been written about explosion hazard at the Transformer Station. If a mistake happens, then I hope the PTX ammonia system should be far away from the transformer station, because otherwise we risk it ending up as section 24 in "Christmas at Vesterbro"! How big does this whole giant industrial plant end up? Is there any limit? Why do you do hearings when everything is constantly changed? Is it legal to change everything at all after the case has been consulted? Should the consultations go all over? Why can't an artificial island be built to the transformer station south of Bornholm, just as they do out for Jutland? Are nature and people worth more in Jutland when they can spend 38 billion on an artificial island? - As we probably have to pay over the tax.

I would very much like to answer my questions from responsible politicians.

The process of consultations and dialogue with citizens is under all criticism.

The Danish Energy Agency repeatedly regrets that they will listen to us and in dialogue, but in reality there is nothing that could be more distant.

It all seems like a game for the gallery and something that just needs to be checked out like the different wildlife reports with MEDE.

It's all just something they are obliged to do according to a total outdated legislation, and then the excavators can get started.

It's sad, and it's all something we're going to regret when it turns out that a lot of wrong decisions have been made because our government imagines us that it is urgent. There are alternative solutions and we need to have other energy sources when it is not blowing! Unfortunately, this is not the first time our government with Mette Fredriksen at the forefront has made rushed, unbalanced decisions.

The rushed process of Energiø Bornholm ends up being a disaster for Bornholm and ultimately for all of Denmark, because there is no consideration for nature, marine environment and people. It's all about energy and money and politicians' own careers.

I am not against offshore wind turbines, but it has to be done wisely and nothing to the wind turbine industry must be taken into account.

The offshore wind turbines must at least 20 kilometers from land, and the entire coastal sea area must be peaceful for setting up offshore wind turbines throughout Denmark.

Laws must and must be adopted that limit the expansion of offshore wind farms with regard to nature.

    Energiø Bornholm's Hav and Land Anlæg will change the entire Bornholm minimum for the next 30 to 50 years, writes Torben Westh Jensen, among other things in this debate post.

Title: Naboer vil have alle bornholmere med i deres kamp for åbne vidder - men hvordan undgår man at sende aben videre?
Content:
The Journal followed when a group of residents at Sydbornholm on Friday founded an Energi-Citizen Association and discussed how they can best influence the plans to build a high-voltage station in their backyard.

On Friday, a new association was created in a circle at Pærgård. The meeting, which is considered a founding general meeting, takes place in the courtyard, where the afternoon sun draws 22 long shadows on the stones.

The attendees have in common that they risk living in the shadow of the future land facility for the energy island. Three days earlier, many went from table to table in Aakirkebyhallerne to gain more knowledge about the high -voltage station, cables, planting and so on.

- Actually, we thought it looked like a road party, because we were all there. We are not densely resident neighbors as in a residential neighborhood, but in this case I think we are close to each other, says host Lise Dandanell after an introductory round where most people present have presented themselves with first name, road name and farm name.

Together with Helle Krakau Holm, she has taken the initiative to gather the neighbors and establish the "Citizens' Association Energiø Bornholm".

Their intention is to gather the forces in the neighborhood rather than influence the plans as individuals, as it is their experience that it is not really battering.

- We have open spaces that we enjoy here every single day. It is a view of fields and sea - and we want to protect that, says Lise Dandanell.

Title: Trøst vil sige god for op til 253 havvindmøller
Content:
The state would like to open up to 253 mills later in the upcoming offshore wind farm off Bornholm. Mayor Jacob Trøst, in his response to the Danish Energy Agency, sets up to approve the possible extra wind turbines. Environmental impacts will only later be examined in depth. The mayor invites the state to expand the land facility with a visitor center.

No longer about 130 offshore wind turbines.

Also no longer 195, which the government opened in October. But up to 253 offshore wind turbines.

The Danish Energy Agency now wants to make it possible for the upcoming offshore wind farm off Bornholm to be at a later date. And Bornholm may well approve that, writes Mayor Jacob Trøst (K) in a preliminary consultation response to the state.

Consolation responds subject to the municipal council later this month approving the answer.

The consultation deadline for the possible even larger version of the offshore wind farm is so short that the mayor seizes his opportunity to respond for the time being when a case is both urgent and is "of a particularly principled or overall political nature", as stated in the municipal council's set of internal rules of play .

With his April play of up to 253 Bornholm offshore wind turbines, the Danish Energy Agency wants to "keep a door open for a political decision to be made at a later date on possible overplant for the offshore wind", the state's energy authority said in a note to the municipality.

Overplanting involves establishing more wind turbines with a larger production of electricity than the production that can be delivered to the collective network. Overplanting, on the other hand, will not lead to more power being delivered to the collective network than the permit allows the future manufacturers of wind energy to deliver.

Overplanting, on the other hand, can compensate for the loss of current that can occur between the offshore wind turbines and the connection point.

Overplanting can also compensate for some wind turbines to usually be out of service.

In this way, overplanting will be able to help the offshore wind farm more constantly produce the amount of energy it is intended to produce.

On the other hand, with the desire to open for overplanting of several offshore wind turbines, the Danish Energy Agency does not want to move the mills closer than the more than 15 kilometers from land on Bornholm, which is also planned for today. Neither will the park's land plant will be larger by virtue of overplanting.


Many possible environmental sequences

Bornholm may well approve that plan, says Mayor Jacob Solvet in the consultation response that the municipal council will have to decide on later this month. Bornholm also welcomes it to open for overplanting of the offshore wind farm.

“Bornholm regional municipality agrees that it is a good idea to enable overplanting.

In this way, with the upcoming project, you can have the opportunity to utilize the plan, the area and the capacity as optimally as possible, ”Jacob Trøst writes in his answer to the Danish Energy Agency.

"Bornholm regional municipality wants to continue to go constructively into the cooperation to establish Energiø Bornholm," the mayor also writes.

At the same time, the mayor and the municipality agree with the Danish Energy Agency that one must investigate the precise consequences for the environment if the offshore wind farm ends up being larger than first planned.

Among the follows, the Danish Energy Agency itself lists that up to 253 offshore wind turbines will of course appear from more than well and well half.

The risk of sailing in the area can also be greater and more ship radars can be disturbed.

More offshore wind turbines will also mean more noise during the construction work. More seabed can be lost, and more nutrients and environmental substances can be released to the water.

More fish and marine mammals than first assumed can also be displaced from the area if the offshore wind farm ends up being significantly larger.

For birds and bats, more offshore wind turbines will finally mean greater risk of flying into one of them.

Exactly how much the environment will be affected extra by a larger offshore wind farm, the Danish Energy Agency will set up the first to assess in depth if and when there is a concrete project to expand the offshore wind farm to the up to 253 mills that the Danish Energy Agency now wants to open the door for .

"Concrete and in -depth environmental assessments will first be carried out in connection with the environmental assessment of the plan and in connection with the specific project," states the note that the regional municipality has received from the Danish Energy Agency.


Something for something

At the same time, Jacob Trøsten takes the opportunity to try to get something again for Bornholm's yes to the Danish Energy Agency.

Even before the state began planning a large offshore wind farm off Bornholm, the association Bornholm's offshore wind was planning a significantly smaller, folk -owned offshore wind farm.

The capacity is intended to be 100 megawatts, just a fraction of the state's plan for now up to 3.8 Gigawatt offshore wind off Bornholm.

Jacob Trøst is now asking the Danish Energy Agency to lift the reservations in two sea areas that do not become part of the State's offshore wind farm, but may become possible places to place Bornholm's much smaller park.

The mayor also asks the State Energy Authority to consider establishing a visitor center together with the land facility that will be linked to the offshore wind farm.

"We would like to invite the Danish Energy Agency to a dialogue about the possibility of entering into a partnership on the establishment of a visitor center in connection with the facility, so that we and our many national as well as international visitors can get more information about the energy island and the future energy supply.

(...) A visitor center may be established together with a possible testing center associated with the land facility, "Jacob Trøst writes.
