Title: Energiø Bornholm er halve visioner og ødelæggende for miljøet
Content:
It is my conclusion that the environmental conditions in the area mean that the energy area proposed by Energinet is extremely unsuitable for the location of a land plant and a location on an artificial island is the only right.

Everyone knows that - Fossil fuels come to an end and we have to transition to renewable energy sources. The war in Ukraine promotes the need to become independent of Russian gas and make the transition to renewable energy sources, including wind turbines.

But even if the process is speeding up, the transition must be done in a way where our nature is not damaged. And I am afraid that the politicians have forgotten - or prioritized - to reach the goal with less emissions in the year 2030 - and that is not acceptable.

The current location of Energiø Bornholm is a clear example of this.

There should be no doubt that I am positive about the construction of wind turbines at sea.

Wind turbines will be able to contribute significantly to the country's energy consumption. But location close to the coast and the location of a land plant on Bornholm on according to illuminated between 70-90 hectares, is twice self-goals.

Why not do it properly and with respect for our common nature? In Jutland, a similar plant with wind turbines is established. Here, wind turbines are placed far out in the North Sea, just as it has been decided to place transformers etc. on a artificial island established for this purpose. That is, no "land facility" should be established inland - everything is being kept out of sea - far from the coast. Jutland is otherwise characterized by large nature with large open areas - that is, in principle plenty of space to place a land plant.

But when it comes to Bornholm, the "land plant" must be placed on land, that farms, houses where our fellow citizens have lived for many years, must be expropriated, demolished and other nearby houses become unsalvable due to low frequency noise around the clock 365 of the year. days.

It can't be right - what politicians can defend it - not to say - take responsibility for it? I have heard the argument that the plant in Jutland is larger, and therefore it is better to pay an artificial island in the North Sea.

After all, that argument no longer counts, as it is now being projected with an expansion of the number of wind turbines at Bornholm, so that the plant in the start -up phase becomes as large as the plant in Jutland. And then, with the half vision - the plant in Jutland is intended to be expanded over the years - but why not at the same time have a vision of expanding the wind turbine in the Baltic Sea similarly? Where is the foresight - the will to do the right thing for all of us? The location of a land plant on Bornholm will be devastating to our nature and the experience thereof. A land plant consisting of three to five buildings, every 25 meters high and 100 meters long will not be able to be hidden away. It will be a huge building that destroys our landscape and our wildlife to that extent. The area of ​​70-90 hectares will be fenced to a predominant, and in the dark hours of the day have been illuminated, possibly via sensors when something moves in the area.

Something more natural can you not imagine? The area proposed by Energinet on Sydbornholm between Sose and Limensgade is surrounded by roads, which means that the plant is visible from all four corners of the world.

An alternative location up to a forest had meant that the plant would be less visible.

The area is characterized by the groundwater being very high. Although the area is drained, water can stand in the fields in rainy periods. The water drainage takes place in materiality via Risebæk out in the Baltic Sea.

Agricultural land is among the better on Bornholm, but contains large quantities of the ferrous ocher.

In previous drainage and excavations of water drainage ditches, the protected Risebæk has been contaminated by ocher deposits, which have colored the river red/ orange and at times wiped out all wildlife. Everyone knows "the red waterfall". The ocher pollution has stretched all the way down to the river's outlet in the Baltic Sea.

Over the past 20 years, no new drainage has been established or elaborations of water drainage ditches and previous ocher contamination are no longer visible.

But when establishing a land plant consisting of large buildings, cable guidance etc., considerable excavation work will have to be done.

The excavation work will, without any doubt, cause huge emissions of ocher far exceeding past contamination of Risebæk. Although a plant is being established, which according to stated, should prevent ocher pollution, I am skeptical of this and also question whether Energinet has any knowledge of the scope of ocher in the area and thus the potential pollution risk? Incidentally, I see a significant problem in future handling of surface water.

Currently, it is so that surface water, which is led away via sinks and open ditches, is quietly led by the protected Risebæk and from there into the Baltic Sea. Establishing a land plant will result in the water from eg a built -up area incl. paved areas etc. On, for example, 10 hectares are led faster to Risebæk. Even a modest faster supply of water to Risebæk will cause considerable floods, as Risebæk and current plumbing on the way to the Baltic Sea will not be able to handle this. Floods in the river will destroy plants and wildlife and change the vegetation decisively. Comes there f.

Eg 30 mm of rain over a few days, it equates to three million liters of water.

In summary, it is thus my conclusion that the environmental conditions in the area mean that the energy area proposed by Energinet is extremely unsuitable for the location of a land plant, and a location on an artificial island is the only right. I have currently not related to the responsible conditions whose establishment of land facilities in the area causes ocher pollution or flooding.

I have, like so many other Bornholmers, participated in the meetings that the municipality and Energinet have invited. The meetings have been visited by many citizens, who have expressed dissatisfaction with both the size of the wind turbines and the short distance from the coast and not least the location of the land facility.

The meetings have mainly gone with representatives from Energinet and others. Has explained what opportunities Energiø Bornholm will provide, but there has been no information at all about the environmental consequences for Bornholm. It's like that topic does not exist or weights in the big game.

I really wonder that our local politicians, interest organizations such as our Nature Conservation Association and others. Not long ago has distanced himself from the current project. This project is Bornholm's largest and most devastating to our common nature ever, and no one dares to stand up and say that it must be changed. Why? Finally, I hope that our local politicians will address Christiansborg and get the whole project Energiø Bornholm reassessed.

Think of the future - let's establish an energy island out in the Baltic Sea with as many wind turbines as in Jutland - create a vision and execute it.

Title: Derfor må bornholmerne vente på at se realistiske visualiseringer af energiøen
Content:
As the size and final location of the land facility for Energiø Bornholm remains unknown, Energinet will not make visualizations of the high -voltage station in a Bornholm landscape. The New Citizens' Association believes that a visual presentation will be able to reduce local concerns, but the neighbors must probably wait until around the turn of the year for new illustrations.

Last week, the regional municipality decided to extend the consultation period on the energy island's land facility by 14 days. The Citizens' Association Energiø Bornholm, a newly formed group consisting of residents around the selected gross area at Sdr. Road, had requested an extension of the deadline.

One of the arguments behind the objection was that Energinet, who is the builder of the 70-90 hectare (0.7-0.9 square kilometers), has not made illustrations of what the high voltage station will look like in different places within the gross area, For which Energinet has asked the municipality to prepare a local plan for.

"They promised us at the meeting at the Green Solution House (November 29, 2021, ed.) That we would get a visualization, but we have not received that," said Lise Dandanell of the Citizens' Association's board of directors during the founding general meeting last Friday.

At both citizen meetings, Energinet has shown the same visualizations of the large land plant with several 25 meters high buildings deployed in a Danish farmland. At the first meeting it was said that the example came from Jutland, and detailed visualizations in Bornholmsk were promised at a later date - and Lise Dandanell has been told that the authorities in November talked about getting new visualizations ready for this spring.

However, residents have to wait a few more months for pictures of a land plant in the South Bornholm Environment, Energinet says. Chief project manager Kim Søgaard Mikkelsen expects illustrations around the turn of the year 2022/23.

- At that time the area has been concretized and we will have come closer to the technical solution, he says to the Journal.

Thus, the neighbors should not expect visualizations until the municipality and Energinet have settled in the area where the high voltage station is to be erected.

Kim Søgaard Mikkelsen explains that for several reasons Energinet finds it too early to make more accurate visualizations that, due to uncertain preconditions in Energinet's opinion, would give rise to more questions than answers.

- If we made a lifelike visualization in a very specific location in the field, it would not be able to avoid being misleading because neither the plant's precise dimensions nor the area's location is yet known. Therefore, such a visualization would at this time be more misleading than indicative, says the chief project manager.

He says that the size of the building will depend on, among other things, the park size and the choice of suppliers. Everything from three to seven buildings of alternating size is currently in play, the chief project manager said.

- We showed some typical pictures of what it might look like at the Citizens' Meeting. Later, when we know something more, we will make them, he states, says Kim Søgaard Mikkelsen.


Great interest in light at night

Also at sea, more advanced visualizations must be made further in the process.

At the Citizens' Meeting in Aakirkebyhallerne last week, the Danish Energy Agency participated, but it was not to present new illustrations.

"We haven't done that yet, but what we came up with was to inform that we are doing a supplementary consultation," the Deputy Director said of the now completed consultation phase on increased mill density.

The Danish Energy Agency is processing the more than 50 consultation responses that were submitted as citizens and organizations could come up with ideas and suggestions before working with an environmental assessment.

- And then we prepare for another consultation process that comes in the second half of 2022. In it we will try to make visible some of the concerns and points of attention that have been raised, including bird and fishing impacts, says Deputy Director Mogens Hagelskær.

He says that in the next phase, the Danish Energy Agency will also show how the light marking for the sake of aviation will look out from land - both during the day and night.

- It has been one of the major themes of the consultation, he says of the light effect at night.


Larger and closer to

In September 2020, the Danish Energy Agency made a report showing how the offshore wind farms in daylight will look like three places from the coast when the nearest mills are raised 20 kilometers from land. However, the visualizations are based on a total park size of 2 gigawatts and 15 MW turbines with a total height of 268 meters - that is, the distance up to the top of the wing tip in the vertical position.

Since these visualizations were made, the government has introduced an opportunity for the distance to be reduced to 15 kilometers, while the parks can get a capacity of up to 3.8 gigawatts with increased mill density. At the same time, it is very possible that the future of offshore wind turbines can become more powerful and larger. The Danish Energy Agency has itself described Møller with a total height of over 350 meters and an effect of more than 20 megawatts as a possible outcome.

The Deputy Director in charge of Energy Islands will not make an indication of what size Møller is most likely to see on the horizon of 2030.

- We have the assessment right now that we have used 15 megawatts. That is, about 130 mills for 2 gigawatts, and 200 mills to reach three gigawatts. But in the tendering process we will leave it up to those who offer.

If they want to make 20 megawatts instead of 15 megawatts, then let's get it in. But it is too premature for us to say whether it will be exactly 250, 270 or 300 meters, says Mogens Hagelskær.

At the Citizens' Association Energiø Bornholm, Lise Dandanell believes that Energinet and the Danish Energy Agency will meet less local skepticism if they get some visualizations and generally make sure to answer the Bornholm's questions.

- Many citizens are nervous about how affected they are of the project. I think that just more enlightenment and involvement could create a better mood so that it will not be that "they are them and we are us," says Lise Dandanell.

The Citizens' Association, which in two weeks has reached about 40 members, has continued to organize themselves. If you want to participate or sign up, the association can be contacted at Lise. dandanell@gmail.com.

    In November, Energinet presented several generic visualizations of the high voltage station. Here is a large version of the land plant surrounded by a strip of trees. The visualizations are based on the politically adopted decision on a capacity of two gigawatts, but it is possible that more than 3 gigawatts and thus significantly more mills should be set up, which will also make the land plant bigger.

Title: Under tidspres: Lokal havvindgruppe kæmper for at kunne opstille møller foran energiøen
Content:
Bornholm's offshore wind, after a vote at a civic meeting, prefers to set up offshore wind turbines 13 kilometers from Rønne, where the locally owned mills will eventually stand close to the energy island's large park. Right now, an area reservation for the Energy Island is preventing this location, and it can cause the initiative group to start a preliminary examination for the castle loop or balka.

Dan Jørgensen, Simon Kollerup and Rasmus Helveg Petersen could see their names tagged in a call from Bornholm's offshore wind on social media earlier this week.

The two ministers with responsibility for energy and business respectively, as well as the radical chairman of the Folketing's Climate, Energy, Supply Committee are some of the key people that the initiative group behind the locally-founded offshore wind turbine project is trying to influence.

"We hope that politicians cancel the state energy reservations to the coastal waters out to 15 km from the coasts of Denmark in connection with the ongoing revision of the sea plan," Bornholm's offshore wind wrote on Facebook.

The group highlights the proposal "Denmark can more II", where the government proposes to turn up investments in renewable energy and increase the speed to become independent of Russian gas and oil.

"Now that 'Denmark (hopefully) can do more II', not also politicians, authorities and industry professionals can agree that the state should not maintain land reservations that block the expansion of coastal offshore winds where the extension can let Say in respect of the marine environment and bird life, and where there is local support for it? ”, Bornholm's offshore wind wrote in the post.

The reservation, which Bornholm's offshore wind wants the state to give up, covers the sea west of Rønne. Two separate areas are set to get the status of "development areas for renewable energy and energy islands", but since the wind turbines for the future energy island must be placed at least 15 or 20 kilometers from shore, Bornholm's offshore wind believes that the areas closer to the coast can be used for the local initiative of An offshore wind farm of 100 megawatts.

These reservations block two of the four locations that Bornholm's offshore wind has identified in a screening and presented at a civic meeting in April.

A vote among those present at the Citizens' Meeting at the Green Solution House showed that the majority preferred to find space for the mills southwest of Rønne, about 13 kilometers from land.

The other candidates are located off Balka/ Snogebæk, Nordskoven/ Sorthat-Muleby and Slotslyngen/ Hammershus-all three places work at a distance of 5-6 kilometers from mills to the coast.


Not non-min-back garden

The fact that the Rønne area was preferred by the most, even though most of the attendees live in Rønne, caused the initiative group to conclude that "it seems that 'non-min-in-backyard' or 'it-may-other-other -The clear 'syndrome does not apply to Bornholm ” -or at least not among the specially energy -interested participants at the civic meeting.

Precisely the area southwest of Rønne, like the location off the Northern Forest, can be blocked by the state energy development zones.

- It is a political decision, and we try to tell about it around where it is now relevant, says Helle Munk Ravnborg from the initiative group Bornholm's offshore wind to the Journal.

One advantage of the Rønne area is that Bornholm's offshore winds, seen from land, will stand in front of the westernmost part of the energy island's offshore wind farms. The fact that the offshore wind turbines are concentrated in the same area perceived many at the civic meeting as a positive thing, says Helle Munk Ravnborg.

- The Danish Energy Agency is not going to be able to use that area, and there are mills in advance, so that the impact of the horizon becomes the least possible, she says.

If the area can be released to Bornholm's offshore wind, it is likely that the initiative group will focus attention on this area.

Impatient

Birds got in the way

The high voltage station, where the current in a strip of large buildings is to be converted to DC, will need an area of ​​70-90 hectares (0.7-0.9 square kilometers, and Energinet has selected a gross area at Søndre Landevej and Vasegårdsvej southwest of Aakirkeby as it best suitable place. Bornholmers to drop the plans on the land and copy the concept of the North Sea.

Therefore, clearly a no thanks to a facility on our lovely island, "Michael and Pia Jensen writes the newly created Citizens' Association Energiø Bornholm emphasizes" to limit the damage to Bornholm's Nature and Marine Environment "and proposes in their consultation response the same solution.

"The number and height of the offshore wind turbines must be minimized and their distance to the coast must be maximized and the land plant must be moved out on an artificial island," writes the association, whose founders all live near the designated gross area around Søndre Landevej.

"The Citizens 'Association basically does not agree that the planned transformer station should be built on Bornholm. Large distance differences

Last week, Tidende turned to the Danish Energy Agency to do an interview with the Deputy Director of Energy Islands, Mogens Hagelskær.

In a busy week of launching the big plans in the North Sea it was not possible. Instead, on Friday, the Danish Energy Agency sent a written explanation with four reasons why an artificial island has not been considered in the Baltic Sea.

- First, Bornholm's central location in the Baltic Sea makes the island function as the place where the current is collected from the offshore wind turbines, located 15-20 kilometers from the coast of Bornholm, Mogens Hagelskær is quoted in the written response.

- In the North Sea, the rationale for the artificial island is particularly rooted in the great distances.

There are 80-100 kilometers to the coast in Denmark and even further to other countries, which is why you have to make space at sea to establish high voltage and converter station and so on. If you consider the energy island as a collection point for offshore wind, Bornholm itself plays a fairly comparable role for the Baltic Sea, as the artificial island will do for the North Sea.

- Secondly, it must be pointed out that the establishment of an artificial island is a major investment.

The artificial island in the North Sea has an estimated cost of a double -digit billion, says Mogens Hagelskær - without, however, figuring out what the plant of a suspected less artificial island in the Baltic could be expected to cost.

Uncertainty about water quality also the environmental consequences of constructing an artificial island must be taken into consideration, emphasizes the Deputy Director of the Danish Energy Agency.

- Thirdly, it is important to note that a possible establishment of an artificial island in the oyster in Danish waters must be expected to have environmental consequences that our neighboring countries would have difficulty accepting.

This includes that an artificial island is likely to block the water flow, which can have an impact on the water quality in the Baltic Sea, and that area will be involved in an international nature protection area.

- Lastly, it is important to note that it is also necessary to establish a plant on land both in Zealand to receive the electricity from Bornholm and also in Jutland in connection with the energy island of the North Sea, where the latter will amount to approx. 40 hectares. If an artificial island was established at Bornholm, a somewhat smaller plant would also have to be established on Bornholm if you could connect Bornholm to the energy island, says the Deputy Director.


A premise

Title: Energiø: Stor beslutning for Bornholm er lige om hjørnet
Content:
According to Energinet, the land facility in Sydbornholm is prepared for two power-to-X plants to be linked to the high-voltage station, the Energinet Deputy Director during the panel debate at the National Assembly.

Should the energy island in the Baltic Sea have a capacity of 2 or 3 gigawatts? According to the Danish Energy Agency, that question will soon be resolved.

"Those decisions should be just around the corner," Deputy Director Mogens Hagelskær said during a debate Friday at the National Assembly.

The difference between 2 and 3 gigawatts will be 60-70 extra offshore wind turbines, just as the country facilities in Sydbornholm will require more space.

The event on the climate and energy stage was about the energy island of the North Sea and the Baltic Sea. In the North Sea, the project is growing tremendously, after the joint announcement from the Netherlands, Belgium, Germany and Denmark to reach 65 gigawatts in 2030. In the Baltic Sea so far only Germany and Denmark have joined the energy island of Bornholm. Sweden and Poland have not yet accepted the invitation to get a cable connection.

One of the audience asked why export connections and overproduction are needed abroad. Energinet's Deputy Director of Energy Islands, Hanne Storm Edlefsen, stated that the energy volumes are so large that they cannot be used by Danish electricity customers alone. She emphasized that the electricity system in Europe must be seen in a large perspective, and with several cable connections the power can be distributed as efficiently as possible.

"We need to balance the electricity system with water from Norway, wind from the middle of Europe and sun from the south," she said, stressing at the same time that the energy island would become too expensive if cables are not drawn abroad so that the power can be exported - we save Money by sharing the cables, said Hanne Storm Edlefsen.

She stated that Energinet, in collaboration with the German counterparty, is about to determine how the cable connection should be made in detail. Choosing technology and who has to pay for what is among the points, the countries' system operators must reach agreement on.

The technology to be used to gather the wind energy near the mills and convert it to DC's pioneering. Energinet expects the land system to receive great global attention.

- What we believe is that we can develop and test it in Bornholm as the first place in the world.

And that is mega exciting - especially for such an electric nerds like us.


Prepared for Power-to-X

During the debate, the participants mentioned the possibility of producing hydrogen on the energy island of the North Sea and brinking the brine pipe to land from the artificial island, which is 100 kilometers from the coast. -Our plant on Bornholm is prepared for you to connect two power-to-X plants if you want, explained Hanne Storm Edlefsen.

Title: Energiø-omkostninger skal reduceres med milliardbeløb
Content:
The Danish Energy Agency has given a commitment of DKK 27 million in support of a project to save the two energy islands from over 20 billion.

A project that will help reduce the construction costs of the two energy islands by more than DKK 20 billion has been awarded a large million in support.

Offshore Energy Hubs is the title of the project, which has just gained almost 27 million will develop a number of technologies and solutions for the Energy Islands, including in Power-to-X. Power-to-X is called it when using electricity for the production of hydrogen and other forms of energy. But as the technology is today, it is not ready to be used on a large scale. Almost DKK 27 million has been committed to support for the project, which is the largest amount of the 26 projects that were announced on Tuesday support from EUDP.

- The overall purpose of the project is to reduce the construction costs for the first two energy islands by over DKK 20 billion. At the same time, the solutions must secure an expansion of the Energiø concept internationally. The project will create a framework for Bornholm as a future large-scale Development and Test Center for Energiø technologies and thus strengthen the Danish industrial leadership position in the field, says Jacob Østergaard, a professor at DTU Vind and energy systems and is at the forefront of the project.

The description of the project also states that it creates both direct and indirect value, which is done through solutions that support stable and robust operation as well as increased profitability of the energy islands, the project description says.

The two energy islands are the first two of its kind in the world, one of which is placed on Bornholm. They are scheduled to be realized by 2030.

The press release from the Danish Energy Agency shows that the energy technology development and demonstration program (EUDP) supports a total of 26 different energy projects with DKK 194.5 million.

- The great interest in the program has given us the opportunity to support a wide range of energy projects - and we just have to invest in many technologies to achieve the goals of the energy policy goals, says Anne Grete Holmsgaard, chairman for the EUDP Board of Directors in the announcement.

Title: Rønne Havn i spidsen for undersøgelse af grønne brændstoffer
Content:
A study of power-to-X-production of green fuels at Bornholm receives support from the Danish Business Promotion Board. The study is expected to be completed over a year.

The Danish Business Promotion Board has chosen to support a study of the production of green fuels on Bornholm. The study will be led by Rønne Havn A/ S and will uncover the possibility of using renewable energy from the upcoming Energiø to make local power-to-x-production of green fuels on Bornholm.

This is stated in a press release from Rønne Harbor.

The idea is to examine a number of aspects of power-to-X production, including manufacturing, finances and opportunities for connecting electricity system and district heating systems on Bornholm and across the Baltic Sea. Production of Power-to-X-Fuel is a new type of industry that has not previously been on Bornholm. Therefore, part of the project will also investigate where on the island a plant and warehouse could be placed.

Power-to-X is about converting electricity (power) into something else (x), for example, hydrogen that can either be used directly or can be combined with other elements and refined to fuels or chemicals.

Rønne Harbor collaborates with a number of local and national partners such as Ørsted, Skovgaard Energy, Topsoe, Danfoss operated, Ramboll, DTU Management, DTU Wind and Energy Systems, Bornholm Energy & Forsyning, Bornholm Regional Municipality and Gate 21, it appears.


During a year

A year ago, Rønne Harbor initiated the consortium Bornholm Bunker Hub together with eight international partners.

The consortium works to make Bornholm a gas station of green fuels for ships sailing in the Baltic Sea.

According to the harbor, the Power-to-X study is a natural extension of the work with Bornholm Bunker Hub, and it will therefore also investigate how large quantities of green fuel can be sold on Bornholm, and whether some of the fuel can be set aside to heavy Land transport and industry on the island.

The study is expected to be conducted over a year and will result in a business case, which will describe, among other things, costs, potential benefits and any risks.

The press release states that the study is a follow -up to Growth Team Bornholm's recommendations from the spring of 2021, which included, among other things, that Bornholm must be the Baltic Sea Green Transport Hub, and the project is carried out as part of the commercial lighthouse tower to make Bornholm the Baltic Sea center for green energy.

It is not clear how much the Danish Business Promotion Board supports the study with. At national level, 14 projects are supported on the development of the green, innovative technologies of the future with DKK 225 million.

The projects all contribute to the development of power-to-x and hydrogen area in Denmark.

The Business Promotion Board has funds from EU structural funds and funds for decentralized business promotion, including tourism.


About the project

The purpose of the project is to conduct a feasibility study in the future large-scale Power-to-X (PTX) production of green e-Fuels on Bornholm in connection with the future energy island. The project is divided into six work packages, each uncovering an element of the study: 1) Examination of input for PTX production 2) Identification of the sizing and configuration of a PTX system 3) Focus on the market for the products and their revenue base 4) Examination of Integration to existing energy systems and associated revenue streams 5) Focus on the potential location of a PTX system and the possibility of export of Products from here 6) All of this information is collected in a Business Case PTX production is still subject to many uncertainties. Through this project, the partners will reduce the risks of establishing PTX production on Bornholm by creating a business case for PTX production, which includes sizing, revenue streams, costs of building and operation and a potential location.

    The possibility of using renewable energy from the energy island for local production of green fuels must be investigated. Rønne Havn A/ S leads the study.

Title: Kæmpe tech-virksomhed lægger vejen forbi Bornholm
Content:
The fact that one of the world's largest tech companies must have transported huge amounts of data from Sweden to Germany that the company Global Connect is now strengthening its fiber network on Bornholm. The energy island offers great opportunities, also for technology-heavy companies to choose to settle down, believes Global Connect.

The whole operation will go fast. Almost as quickly as when data is transported through fiber cables.

About 10 hours this Friday will take for fiber cable contractor Global Connect to bring a very strong fiber cable in Rønne. Here it will be rooted before the ship with the fiber cable continues to lay cable out a meter below the seabed all the way between Rønne and Sassnitz.

Global Connect constructs fiber cables for customers who must have transported large amounts of data, often over long distances.

Among customers are some of the world's largest companies.

The project of laying cable from Rønne to Sassnitz is only a small part of a much larger operation, which is about laying out fiber cable between northern Sweden and Germany. The work is commissioned by one of the so -called tech giants, where Google and Facebook are among the best known - there are some data centers that have extremely great need to move data.

We do not always know what to use so much fiber for, nor does it interest us, says Martin Højriis Kristensen, head of market and operations in Global Connect.

- I must not say who the customer in Northern Sweden is. But it is not a Swedish actor. It's one of the tech giants, he says.


Energy island provides opportunities

For the tech giants, Bornholm is currently becoming more and more interesting.

This is because the energy island is on the way with a promise of green energy. The tech giants are also giants on the consumption of electricity.

- That Energiø Bornholm is now coming can also make Bornholm interesting for large technology companies. Once the energy island has been realized, I think it gives some interesting perspectives.

But it requires that there is an infrastructure, both for electricity and for data, says Marin Højriis Kristensen.

- The energy island has been one of the assessments that we have had. But I also think we would have been here now if Bornholm had not become Energiø, he says.

The cable between Rønne and Sassnitz is also only the first of a total of three planned.

The first cable will connect Rønne and the German city of Sassnitz. This fall, another cable will go from Øland to Sandvig. A third cable will connect Simrishamn and Hasle - you want to build these connections where the power is green.

And it is easier to build the data cable where the power is than it is to move the flow up through Europe, explains Martin Højriiis Kristensen as to why a tech giant chooses to set a huge amount to be able to move data between Sweden and Germany.

- When you have to put fiber between Sweden and Germany, you can either go around Bornholm or you can walk across Bornholm. There we were in no doubt. Going over land on Bornholm offers a lot of opportunities in the long run, and it doesn't cost much to board the project here and now, he says.

The fact that Energiø Bornholm is now coming can also make Bornholm interesting for large technology companies.

Once the energy island has been realized, I think it gives some interesting perspectives.

Martin Højriis Kristensen, boss and market and operations in Global Connect.

    It looks like a cigar box or a piece of New Year's powder. But what Martin Højriis Kristensen here stands with is a fiber that can transport large quantities of that over long distances.

Title: Staten inviterer: Branchen kan påvirke udbuddet af energiøen
Content:
Through a so -called market dialogue, potential bidders have the opportunity to influence the supply of Energiø Bornholm.

The offshore wind farm at Energiø Born Holm will be completed by 2030. It will be the first Danish Energiø, and although it is eight years out in the future, is processed in full swing. Therefore, the Danish Energy Agency and Energinet invite potential bidders and the industry to so -called market dialogue at the end of August.

The purpose is to discuss the most important elements and frameworks for the upcoming tenders.

Thus, potential bidders and the wind turbine industry generally have the opportunity to influence the framework for the supply of Energiø Bornholm's offshore wind farm and other offshore wind farms. The idea is to optimize the tender material to eventually achieve as good bids as possible.

This is what the Danish Energy Agency says in a press release.

The dialogue will, as a starting point, focus on, among other things, the project on land and network connection, considerations of overplanting and power-to-x as well as environmental studies.


15 kilometers to the coast

It is still uncertain what exactly has to be sent out. It has been politically decided that Denmark should build two energy islands to secure green supply to the Danish and foreign electricity grid, but it has not yet been decided whether the installed capacity should be increased from two to three gigawatts or whether the wind turbines can be placed in to 15 kilometers distance to the coast.

Currently, the possibility of overplanting is being investigated, which means that the total capacity could rise to up to 3.8 gigawatts.

The possible extra capacity in the case of overplanting can be used for Power-to-X, among other things.

Overplanting means that it is allowed to set up more wind turbines with a larger production of electricity than the production that can be delivered by the collective net at the connection point. Power-to-X is about converting electricity (power) into something else (x), for example, hydrogen that can either be used directly or can be combined with other elements and refined to fuels or chemicals.

Title: Janie vil gøre lokale virksomheder grønne: ' De skal gøre sig synlige'
Content:
A newly hired project consultant at Business Center Bornholm must be a link between local businesses and the green transition.

There will be plenty of opportunities for Bornholm companies when the construction of the new Energiø hits in a few years. And here it is about being prepared, says Janie Dylsing, who has just taken up the position of project consultant at Business Center Bornholm, which is part of the National Center for Green Energy.

Janie Dylsing originally came from Zealand, but moved to Bornholm in 1989 with her then husband and lived on Bornholm until 2004, so she knows reasonably to the Bornholm conditions.

On February 1, she returned to Bornholm, especially because her daughter, son -in -law and two grandchildren still live on the island, but also to get back to the beautiful scenery and tranquility the island has. And then the job suddenly came.

- I feel tremendously privileged that I got this job, because it wasn't really my plan at all that I should have a job at Bornholm to start with. I commuted the first three months after I moved to Bornholm, but then the opportunity arose suddenly, and I thought that here I can make a difference as well.

Environment is a hugely important topic and something I would like to work with, says Janie Dylsing.

The new project consultant's main task is to get the right people to meet and help the Bornholm companies prepare and strengthen the innovation power of the island, including the newly started Residential College, where young DTU students come to Bornholm as a kind of satellite for the university.

- With Residential College we now get a knowledge bank on the island, which is really important that the Bornholm companies use. And it is one of my tasks to have contact communicated so that the young people's study tasks and research projects can be used for the benefit of our local communities and the Bornholm companies.


Investments in good time

When the energy island is to be established in a few years, there will be many tasks that can be solved by local businesses. But it requires them to get ready, Janie Dylsing emphasizes.

- There will be some great opportunities in getting different tasks for the island within the offshore and wind turbine industry, and it appeals to a really large collaboration between the Bornholm companies so that they can bid on some tasks together. And then it requires openness and curiosity about learning from other companies' experience as well as focusing on creating a collaboration on future projects, both on and off Bornholm, Janie Dylsing points out.

She also believes that, in addition to the most obvious, several other opportunities will arise for the Bornholm traders, as many people will come into contact with the big project.

For example, it can be overnight staff.

- It's about as a supplier to make yourself interesting and visible, because I think more companies will be subcontractors.

And there the Bornholm companies must see the opportunities and be ready to invest in them. The pitfall may be that you wait too long, because then the tasks are caught by others, says Janie Dylsing.

Therefore, it is important that companies stay really well informed about which tenders are coming. The National Center for Green Energy has just invited companies in a workshop 27 June to hear about their wishes for how to create a more detailed and clear overview of this.

We already have a lack of labor in many areas. How should the local businesses solve it? - It is a huge challenge today that there is a shortage of labor, both in Denmark and in many other countries. What I think we should use is the expertise that DTU students come up with. You can invite them into your business with their research projects and then look at recruitment options.

And then there is also something called international labor, and there are also opportunities.

In order to get the right skills for the tasks, competence development and targeted vocational education could also be thought of.

Janie Dylsing calls for companies that have doubts about how they can make themselves attractive and ready for the tasks, turn to the Business Center Bornholm, a partner in the National Center for Green Energy.

- We have several consultants who can work with the company and where you can talk about what thoughts you have to bid on the new tasks.

In collaboration with the National Center for Green Energi, we can dress them up so that they are good when the tenders come, says Janie Dylsing.

- Among other things, we encourage local companies to think in the ISO certifications that will be required and to be outreach and curious about what it takes to offer something.

And be aware of whether one's business lacks some skills to perform specific tasks and, if so, how to get the skills.

New to the energy area What is your own background for working with green energy? - It's actually brand new to me. I have worked in the financial sector at the start of my career. Then I have been a teacher at the Business School, and I have worked as a project manager and as general manager in employment and education for the past 20-25 years. So what I can do is create networks and see the opportunities and needs of the companies.

But the energy area itself is new to me, explains Janie Dylsing.

She therefore spends a lot of time and energy getting a broad understanding of the area.

- We all want to do something for the climate, but being part of a big project where we can actually make a difference is something I think is fantastic and it is something we do in collaboration. Where we can find the solutions together.

Janie Dylsing has previously worked with coaching and mentoring, where she helped smaller companies with, among other things, career development and how to get the working life that you want. And many of the instruments she thinks she can use in the job as a consultant at Bornholm.

- I mean, I have a good human understanding and a good understanding of seeing some potentials, and it is with both people and in relation to the development of a business. So today I really use what I've been working on for many years. And then my attitude is that there are always options if you grab them.

- For me it is important to focus on man when you have a business.

To ensure that you are in contact with yourself in relation to what you want with your business. That you can see yourself in your own business. That one can use one's intuition and your sense of something that works right for one yourself. You have to take ownership of your own business, concludes Janie Dylsing.

It requires openness and curiosity about learning from other companies' experiences.

Janie Dylsing Project Consultant.

    Janie Dylsing believes that there will be good opportunities for Bornholm companies to take part in the tasks when the new energy island is to be realized.

Title: Nu er der sat et prisskilt på en central del af energiøen
Content:
DKK 16.9 billion expects Energinet, it will cost to build the electricity infrastructure for Energiø Bornholm. However, there are several major uncertainties in the calculations, which include the construction of the land plant in South Bornholm and a similar transformer and high voltage station in Zealand as well as the cable connection in between.

In the state scenery, work is being done on the preparation of Energiø Bornholm. During the summer, a note for the Folketing's Climate, Energy and Supply Committee has emerged more new information. The state -owned system operator Energinet, who owns and operates the most crucial parts of the Danish electricity grid, sent an application to the ministry in the spring entitled "Energiø Bornholm Elinfrastructure" and a summary of the application has been shared with the Folketing Committee, which must have submitted projects , when the total budget exceeds a billion kroner. It makes the infrastructure the Bornholm Energiø to that extent: "The construction cost of the part of Energiø Bornholm's Elinfrastructure that Energinet will build is DKK 16.9 billion. The annual operating costs are estimated at DKK 121 million." The material from the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Supply.

The offshore wind farms themselves and cable connections abroad are not included in the price estimate. In comparison, in its time it cost 21.4 billion kroner (in 1988 prices) to build the Great Belt Bridge.


Uncertain preconditions

The state authorities believe that there are major risks in the project's finances. Energinet indicates uncertainty costs to be 20-25 percent higher than usual at Energinet's major construction projects.

"The Business Case for Energiø Bornholm's Elinfrastructure is based on more assumptions than usual, for example in relation to the number of GW offshore wind, final agreements with Germany about a foreign connection and a very ambitious schedule. This increases the overall risk pressure for the project's schedule, budget and technical solutions "The note says.

It is not yet politically decided whether the energy island should have a capacity of more than the 2 gigawatts (GW) already decided by the Parliament. Among other things, as a result of the increasing focus on green energy, it is in the cards that at least 1 GW will be added.

The note also emphasizes that "the socio -economic gains when establishing 3 GW offshore winds will be greater than when establishing 2 GW", as both the connection to Zealand and Germany "will achieve a better degree of utilization if 3 GW of offshore winds are built. rather than 2 gw ”.

The feasibility studies are designed in a way that the wind turbines at sea can get a capacity of up to 3.8 gigawatts. The application from Energinet states that the electricity connections together are expected to reach 3.2 gigawatts. The largest portion of the current, 2 GW, must be transported to Germany, while 1.2 GW will access the Zealand electricity grid. In Energinet's calculations of the costs, the cable is not included in Germany and the station plant on German soil, as the German pendant to Energinet, 50Hertz, will have financial responsibility for this part of the project.


Six-ni cables in land

Bornholm soil must be dug when the cables are to be laid, and in the memo you can read that Energinet expects six-nine transmission cables to land from the offshore wind farms and that they must be connected to the transformer station at Sydbornholm, where the power is converted to DC. .

"Energinet has designed the station on Bornholm so that it can be expanded in the long term and a total of three foreign connections can be connected in addition to the connection to Zealand," the note states.

Poland and Sweden are the obvious opportunities, but cooperation with these countries has a different time perspective than with Germany.


The small and big net

The note also mentions the desire to connect it - in an energy island - small Bornholm electricity network together with the energy island. The extra costs for a interconnection are not included in the application.

"Work is being done on a technical solution that can connect the Bornholm electricity grid to the station for Energiø Bornholm. This connection is not covered by Energinet's application, but the new station on Bornholm is expected to be built so that it is prepared to be linked to Bornholm's local network with a 60 kv connection. ” 60 kilovolts are the maximum voltage in the Bornholm electricity grid, while the high voltage network is otherwise 400 kilovolts, which also becomes the voltage level in the cable connection to Zealand. On the outskirts of Greater Copenhagen, more specifically at the area of ​​Solhøj in near Ishøj and Taastrup, the electricity from the mills in the Baltic Sea must be linked to the existing high voltage network. A new 209 kilometer long cable connection, like the station plant in Zealand, is included in Energinet's construction estimate of DKK 16.9 billion.


Where does the bill end?

Danish electricity consumers pay to Energinet through a tariff on the bills, but the idea is not that the huge Energiø infrastructure projects must be financed by consumers.

On the other hand, the companies/ investors behind the offshore wind farms must contribute, according to the note.

"It is a prerequisite for Energinet's final investment decision that a decision is made on how the cost of the project should be distributed. The cost is expected to be distributed to offshore winds (so -called 'overwhelming' at offshore wind) rather than for Energinet's tariff," Klima writes, Klima writes -, the Ministry of Energy and Supply, where one does not surprisingly look positively on the entire Energiø Bornholm project.

"Overall, on the basis of Energinet's application and the business case, it has been assessed that the project is needed," the ministry concludes: "The assessment has taken into account the project's socio -economic consequences.

Against this background, the Minister of Climate, Energy and Supply is positively related to the need for the project and will finalize the application when the project has been submitted to the Climate, Energy and Supply Committee ".

On June 22, the case was submitted to the Climate, Energy and Supply Committee.


Facts about the electric infrastructure for Energiø Bornholm

The project applied for Energinet's electricity infrastructure in connection with Energiø Bornholm consists of :? The establishment of two new 400 kV stations with associated converter plants at Solhøj in Zealand and Bornholm respectively? Establishment of 209 km of electricity connection between the station at Solhøj in Zealand and the station on Bornholm with a transfer capacity of the 2 x 600 MW project consists of an electricity connection between Bornholm and Zealand and two new stations on Bornholm and Zealand respectively. The construction project is scheduled to be implemented in the period 2024-2029, so that the new offshore wind can be put into operation by 2030.

Source: Climate, Energy and Supply Ministry/ Energinet.

Title: To placeringer er i spil til havvindmøller fem-seks kilometer fra kysten
Content:
Bornholm's offshore wind is close to writing off the preferred location off Rønne, where the mills could stand in front of the energy island's wind park. Instead, the initiative group expects it to be investigated whether the locally owned offshore wind turbine project can be placed off the Northern Forest or Nexø/ Balka.

When the initiative group behind Bornholm's offshore wind held a civic meeting in April, the participants voted on where they preferred the coastal offshore wind turbines to be placed.

Four options were presented and the favorite was the location farthest from the coast - about 13 kilometers from Rønne near the area where one of the offshore wind farms for Energiø Bornholm is expected to be erected at the end of the decade.

However, the Rønne location becomes difficult with the time horizon that the initiators prefer. This is because the state area reservation does not appear to be lifted until you know more precisely where the cables for Energiø Bornholm will be laid, and the clarification is expected to only be available in a few years, Bornholm's offshore wind writes in a newsletter.

"Although we will of course continue to push for the land reservation on the area on the 'inside' of Energiø Bornholm Møller, it is our assessment that the (most) realistic path rather than Bornholm's offshore wind is to clarify which of the other two other two other Location - Nordskoven and Nexø - We have to move on with, as a further waiting period of 2-3 years makes very little sense compared to ensuring a green and sustainable Energy supply for Bornholm for the benefit of both climate and the local economy ”.


Other foundations in the east

Since the Citizens' Meeting, several doubts regarding the areas off the Northern Forest and Nexø have been clarified. The seabed off Nexø/ Balka is of such a nature that the mills would have to be set up on gravitational foundations, ie some large concrete blocks, rather than monopiles that can be used elsewhere.

The experts, with whom Bornholm's offshore wind have allied, have previously been in doubt as to whether a project of 100 megawatts (equivalent to about seven mills) will be possible with gravitational foundations.

It indicates that it is possible, and therefore the Nexø location, which was the second most popular in the voting rounds, remains in play.

“The good news, however, is that because there is now much greater interest in setting up offshore winds around our immediate area, there are now several projects that are being projected with gravitational foundations.

Therefore, it is now more likely that we would be able to place an order on such foundations, we should want it than it was in April, ”Bornholm's offshore wind writes in the newsletter.

The next step is the feasibility study The area off the Northern Forest - preferred by the third most at the Citizens' Meeting - is currently limited by an area reservation that Bornholm's offshore wind expects will be abolished in the autumn in connection with a political meeting on the climate and energy plan "Denmark can more II".

Whether the local offshore wind project ends with a bet on Nexø or the Northern Forest will be clarified soon. An EU grant has made it possible to hire a team of experts for the project, and they are intended for a crucial role when making the decision.

"Fortunately, we have about half of the money back, which means that we can now ask our team of experts to proceed to prepare an application for preliminary examination that we can submit to the Danish Energy Agency, and in this context assist us in clarification of whether we should submit the application for the area off Nexø or off the Northern Forest, ”says the newsletter.

"Finally, we can tell that there is still great interest in our actions. We have thus been contacted by the organizers behind the climate meeting, which will be launched in early September 2022, to present our initiative there. We have also been contacted by one Group Nordic researchers at Nordregio, who would like to have Bornholm's offshore wind as a case in a research project on the importance of local ownership in energy conversion. Yes to ”.

The people behind Bornholm's offshore wind began their work three years ago. The first years they were aiming to raise the mills on Rønnebakke south of Arnager, but this area had to be abandoned due to a new large nature protection area, which will also wedge between the Energy Island's offshore wind farms.

It was the consideration of bird life that forced Bornholm's offshore wind to change plans.

The goal is that the wind farm can be put into operation in 2025 or 2026.


Voting on four locations

At the Citizens' Meeting in April, the 75 attended voted on which (s) of the four potential places they preferred.

The location next to Rønne received the greatest support with 45 statements, followed by Nexø/ Balka with 33 statements, the Northern Forest with 24 statements and the Castle Ling with 15 statements. Each of the attendees could point to up to two locations.

The Rønne area is 13 kilometers from land, while the distance from the coast to the nearest mill is 5-6 kilometers in the other three locations.

In the latest presentation, the initiative group assumes that seven wind turbines of 15 MW have to be set up, which have a total height of just under 270 meters.

The most popular area southwest of Rønne will hardly be available in the coming two to three years, according to Bornholm's offshore wind, which therefore concentrates on the proposals west of the Northern Forest and southeast of Nexø. Title: Tysk ambassadør besøger Bornholm
Content:
On Wednesday and Thursday this week, German ambassador Pascal Hector will be a trip to Bornholm on an official accession visit.

Here he will, among other things, look at the plans for Energiø Bornholm, which Mayor Jacob Trøst will show off, and he will also meet representatives of Bornholm's tourism and business. Among other things, a visit to the Bornholm Museum and Rønne Harbor is on the program, according to a press release from the German Embassy.

- The People's Meeting in Allinge was already a great experience and gave me a first impression of unique Bornholm.

Now I am very much looking forward to getting to know the sunshine lake even better, says Ambassador Pascal Hector.

He believes that Bornholm can do much more than be a tourist island, and therefore he wants to gain greater insight into the entire region.

- With its fantastic nature, unique location and rich cultural life, Bornholm is much more than a magnet for tourists. Bornholm and its business community play an important role in the successful green transition of the future, not only for Denmark, but also for Germany and the entire Baltic Sea region. All this I look forward to getting an insight into, he says.

During his stay, the ambassador is accompanied by Germany's honorary consul on Bornholm, Peter Vesløv. eel.

Title: Medarbejdere slår alarm: " Vi har aldrig før sendt så intenst et nødsignal"
Content:
Bornholm's entry times do not lead to the entrance among the municipality's natural, environmental and plan people. The cases, on the contrary, accumulate, the requirements of the law become harder and difficult to fulfill, the working environment becomes worse and the errors more. 10 man -years missing

Bornholm's upcoming status as an energy island alone will bring a large number of new tasks.

We make several mistakes, and despite the best intentions from managers and employees about structured follow -up and coordination, the pace is so blasting that we only succeed for us, ”writes the cooperation committee to the municipal council.

"The mental well -being is affected. The criticism of our work is increasing in the Bornholm community - especially because of the processing time, which in several areas can come up in several years - and the confidence in the authority and thus the municipality and its political leadership are negatively affected", It is also called.


Case pressure provides long wait

No coordinated climate effort

But, but: "In order to exploit this potential, the area is needed to be prioritized. (...) "No resources have been set aside for a general and continuous coordination of climate action."

Title: Statsministeren vært for EU-topmøde på Bornholm
Content:
Mette Frederiksen and several other European leaders will come to Bornholm next week, where the wind potential and an energy cooperation in the Baltic Sea are on the wallpaper.

Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen (S) invites seven of his EU colleagues and the EU Commission President to Bornholm.

The program includes the wind potential of the Baltic Sea and the establishment of an energy cooperation.

That's what the Altinget writes Tuesday.

It is not yet known who is attending the meeting, but political tips from Finland, Sweden, Germany, Poland and the Baltic States are invited.

In addition, it has been confirmed that the European Commission's chairman Ursula von der Leyen and the Commission's Energy Commissioner Kadri Simson will participate.

The meeting at Bornholm, which is called Baltic Energy Security Summit, is the second in the large European wind initiative, after the North Service Summit in Esbjerg was handed out on a rapid expansion of the wind power in the North Sea.

The European Commission has estimated that there is also a great potential in the Baltic Sea that can supply over 100 million households with green power, which is why the leaders are now meeting here on the island.

Kristian Jensen, director of Green Power Denmark and former Foreign Minister, believes that the meeting at Bornholm will come at a good time.

- In the midst of the conflict with Russia, there is a risk that some will prioritize the short -term conversion back to more coal and diesel. This summit can help cement that renewable energy and cooperation in the region must be prioritized, says Kristian Jensen according to the Altinget.

The hope is that at Bornholm you can lay the foundation for a larger regional cooperation with a starting point in Bornholm Energiø.

The European summit is set to take place on Tuesday, August 30.

Title: Museets direktør glæder sig over relevante spørgsmål til ministre
Content:
Director Jacob Bjerring-Hansen at the Bornholm Museum appreciates that MP Peter Juel-Jensen questions ministers about the archaeological work in connection with the energy island.

Both Minister of Culture Ane Halsboe-Jørgensen and Education and Research Minister Jesper Petersen will relate to the archaeological task that awaits the Bornholm Museum in connection with Energiø Bornholm. MP Peter Juel-Jensen (V) has asked them questions indicating that the local museum does not have the necessary resources. And it fits, says museum director Jacob Bjerring-Hansen.

- It is very relevant that questions are asked, because it is a huge task and something that requires time and planning, so that we can solve it satisfactorily, he says.

Peter Juel-Jensen wants to be informed how many new resources Bornholm Museum can expect to be added in connection with the assignment and whether there is the opportunity to include archaeology students in the work. According to Jacob Bjerring-Hansen, the problem is even greater, and it all starts with the basic grant that the Bornholm Museum receives from the state.

- As I see it, it is a big problem that we have so much bad conditions on the basic grant from the state to operate archaeology on the island in relation to how good and fine archeology we have. That is, at that time we will come from a very unsatisfactory and underfunded situation where we do not have enough people in the archaeological department to suddenly have a huge number of people, and that can be very difficult. It also makes it a very relevant question, says the museum director.


It's hard with students

Formally, the developer enters the energy island's land facility at Sydbornholm with Bornholm Museum to do a large preliminary study and then a large main study. According to Jacob Bjerring-Hansen, on such large construction tasks, there are some special rules that allow the museum to handle it a little better. But the foundation must be in order.

- We have to go from zero to 100 in no time and do it in several stages. It's not that once you get started, you can just stay on. First there is a preliminary study, then there is a break, then there is a main study and so on. There are breaks in what work, so people have to go over here, they have to work intensively, be sent home again and maybe over here again. It is a tremendously demanding task resources, and it is something that needs to be carefully thought out and where it is extremely important whether we as a museum have part of the resources internally in the house or not, because then you can better prepare in good Time before, and thus the pressure on those coming from outside will be less, says Jacob Bjerring-Hansen.

In relation to the involvement of archaeology students, he does not think it is an obvious solution, as this type of tasks typically does not are very good in relation to their studies.

He thinks it will be more relevant to start looking for labor outside the country if there are not enough Danish archaeologists.

- We have had good partners in Poland and so on in recent years, so we can see if we could get any help from the universities that have been on the island and dig for the last few years and see if they could have some fully educated or help in other ways.

But it is absolutely relevant to look for what extra resources are, he says.


Need for a schedule

Another basic prerequisite is a schedule and the museum will soon want to see a sketch with itself in, and a final designation of the area is also needed.

- Right now there is a gross area of ​​about 130 hectares as far as I remember, but we have to go down to about 90 hectares, which is what we need to excavate. Of course, it is of great importance for the area to be designated and a schedule must be added, and then we can start looking at the preliminary investigations, and when they are done, we can put in a real plan for the great work, namely the main study of it , We find, says Jacob Bjerring-Hansen.

In his eyes, the questions from Peter Juel-Jensen are closely linked to an inquiry that the museum and the regional municipality sent to the Ministry of Culture this summer with a request for a fair grant to the Bornholm Museum.

- It was precisely with the problem that the fundamental operation of archaeology at the Bornholm Museum is critically resource, and that is before the energy island has come to mind at all, says Jacob Bjerring-Hansen.


The questions

MP Peter Juel-Jensen (V) has asked the following questions: Minister of Culture Ane Halsboe-Jørgensen (S), the minister will state how many new resources Bornholm Museum can expect to be added in connection with their significant efforts in the establishment of Energiø Bornholm, which will benefit the whole country? To the Minister of Education and Research, Jesper Petersen (S) will, in the Minister's opinion, make sense to involve archaeology students in the work of establishing Energiø Bornholm, so that, for example, students were offered to follow the work/ participate in the work or/ and place parts of the education at Bornholm, while the investigations are in progress, and thinks the minister will make sense to spread this type of education to our neighboring countries, as they are also largely facing large investments in renewable energy, that basically does the same archaeological attention require? To the Minister of Education and Research, Jesper Petersen (S) is the minister in dialogue with his colleague, the Minister of Culture, about the possibility of involving archaeology students in the work of establishing Energiø Bornholm, so that, for example, students were offered to follow the work/ participate in the work or/ And placed parts of the education on Bornholm while the studies are going on?.

Title: Nyt brev til naboer viser i detaljer, hvor Energinet vil trække kabler i land
Content:
Neighbors to the field of study doubt that it is possible for the locals to force changes to the plans at Sydbornholm, after it has emerged which cable corridors need to be investigated in the autumn. The Citizens' Association Energiø Bornholm still hopes that the land plant can be made smaller or moved out to sea.

On Tuesday, heads of state, EU spikes and energy deficiencies come from afar to attend a short summit on energy and security policy in the Baltic Sea area. The presence of the top one afternoon fades in relation to the elongated preparation work that is in progress as a prelude to the construction of Energiø Bornholm.

The developer Energinet has set biologists, geologists and other experts to investigate the conditions to the south and west of the shore and west of the South Bornholm area, which the state authorities find most suitable to place the large high -voltage.

The affected residents of the area around Sdr.

Road between the stalls and Sose last week received mail from Energinet. The letter informs that the geotechnical and geophysical studies will be initiated in September.

On page 2 there is a map that shows the area where the underground is to be examined further. The majority of the shaded area is on the north side of Sdr. Road and extends from the middle of Arnager Bay, where the road runs closest to the sea, to the stalls in the east. In the middle is the gross area where the land plant is expected to be erected.


Biologists in the hills

In addition, five corridors down to the sea, where it is to be investigated whether the cables from the offshore wind farms can be carried ashore. One of the places where a belt from the coast and into the country needs to be examined is in the fields in the fields opposite Pæregård. Here, the Citizens' Association Energiø Bornholm was formed in April at a general meeting in the courtyard for a good dozen neighbors. The couple at Pærgård, Lise Dandanell and Fridrik Adamsson, were among the initiators, and they are not surprised that they will soon be digging near their homes. In fact, they have become accustomed to the sight of the people doing the preliminary studies.

- They have been hiking in the hills and around around. For months we have been able to see more ships from our windows. And now they have announced the beginning of the geophysical studies, says Fridrik Adamsson.

The Citizens' Association consists primarily of residents from the area around Søndre Landevej, Limensgaden and Vasegårdsvej. In the letter, the landowners are told that the next round of feasibility surveys will take 1-2 days on each property. In some places, however, Energinet needs to return to the wells several times.

"On some properties we need to make bores to map the soil layers in depth. The bores will be up to 35 meters deep. in the ground with a spear that sends a slight stream in the soil so we can measure what types of soil layers are on site, ”Energinet writes in the letter.


The sea as best alternative

The gross area, which the 70-90 hectare land plant can be placed inside, constitutes 260 hectares. In the spring consultation rounds, several citizens have submitted proposals for alternative locations to the Danish Energy Agency and Bornholm Regional Municipality, which is responsible for making a new local plan. Areas to the east and west have been brought into play by citizens.

The Citizens' Association Energiø Bornholm has not assigned anywhere else to the land plant if Haller is expected to be 25 meters high.

- What we have a common attitude to is that we would like to have it out to be at sea, says Lise Dandanell, who demands calculations of what an artificial island would cost.


Agreement with mayor

At a board meeting last week, members discussed how their case can be spread out to more Bornholmers. They believe that Bornholmers, regardless of address, should support their fight, as the wind farms and the high-voltage facilities, which they fear can grow into an industrial complex with power-to-X systems, data centers and other related industrial buildings, will be so large that they will influence the southern half of the island.

On the Citizens' Association's agenda are concerns about the noise and electromagnetic impact from the transformer station as well as the consequences for the groundwater and the local environment in the area. Also, the possibilities of getting compensation for loss of property value and expropriation conditions fill something among the members, the couple says. The association has an agreement with Jacob Consolation that he will attend one of the fall meetings, as well as plans to invite neighbors to a Jutland high -voltage facility to Bornholm to gain insight into their fight and good advice.


Difficult decision to change

Fridrik Adamsson doubts whether the effort has a realistic chance of bearing fruit if the final goal is a new location of the landing.

- Compared to the major costs for feasibility studies, there is probably over 90 percent likelihood that the decision on the location of the land plant has already been made.

It's just a matter of details, he says, and draws attention to the local planning process that he doesn't have much confidence in.

- Just as it seems to have been decided by the regional municipality, without ever being debated by the municipal council, says Fridrik Adamsson, who as a member of the Unity List was otherwise convened for the municipal council meeting last week as an alternate.

The upcoming geophysical studies "will form the basis for the design of the plants and the environmental assessment of the project, which is expected to begin in the fall of 2022," Energinet said in the letter.

Most of the area is located on a well over seven kilometers long on the north side of Sdr. Road.
