Title: Peter Juel: Større fragtkapacitet er et spørgsmål om et land i balance
Content:
The Left and the Danish People's Party wanted to increase the total subsidy for the Bornholm ferry operation due to the pressed shipping capacity.

At the beginning of the summer holidays, the regional municipality and Jacob Solvet were told that the Ministry of Transport turned the thumbs down to the proposal to set aside new money so that Povl Anker could be deployed as a freight ferry twice a week between weeks 34 and 43.

The letter stated that the ministry "has investigated the possibilities of obtaining extra financing for the deployment of additional shipping capacity to Bornholm in the summer/ autumn of 2022. This has not been possible." MP from left Peter Juel-Jensen is disappointed that it has not succeeded.

The Left is part of the ferry settlement, and in the settlement circle the party has called on Transport Minister Trine Bramsen to raise extra financing for the Bornholm ferries to improve freight capacity.

- It can be a little difficult to find money for the time being, but we can't help but invest in what we have to live by in the future, says Peter Juel-Jensen to the Journal.

He is disappointed that it has not been possible, because he believes that the time should have come to relate to what the development in recent years has meant to the ferries and capacity. He points out that the much -needed mid -term evaluation has been delayed, and therefore the government and the other parties in the settlement circle should have responded to the inquiries from the Traffic Contact Council by granting extra money for freight transport.

- When we made the ferry settlement, we enrolled that a mid -term evaluation should be made, which is now put into a Bornholmer analysis of the transport. I do not think it makes sense that one is not willing to add new money when there was a common understanding that it could be necessary to pill it midway.

The prices of ferry tickets were lowered considerably four years ago, and the grant to operate the Bornholm Line is about a million dollars a day. How can one justify increasing that amount? - Infrastructure costs money. If we want a country in some balance, we need to control the infrastructure that allows you to both settle and operate on our islands. Otherwise, it will be a pure deficit business, says Peter Juel-Jensen and elaborates his point.

- We have been in for a few years when it is my claim that Bornholm has contributed positively to the social economy, and we must maintain that development. So this is not an expense, but an investment in a common future for Bornholm and the entire Kingdom.

According to Bornholm Tidende's information, there were two parties in the conciliation circle who agreed to allocate more money for the ferry operation.

The Danish People's Party also supports the idea.

"We support increasing the grant. It is important to ensure an optimal infrastructure for our islands, and this also includes good shipping capacity for Bornholm," writes the Danish People's Party's transport mayor, Alex Ahrendtsen in an email to the Journal.


Ten ministerial issues

In the wake of Tidende's articles on the shipping capacity and the alternative proposal to finance the extrature with Povl Anker by canceling overpowering with the fast ferry Peter Juel-Jensen has asked ten questions to Transport Minister Trine Bramsen (S).

"Does the Minister agree that if the number of ferry departures is cut out of season, it makes it all the great work of making Bornholm attractive all year round, and it becomes difficult to secure year -round workplaces?" Peter Juel-Jensen asks, among other things.

He also asks the ministry to obtain various facts about the coating on the estate ferries and also asks what large projects such as Energiø's land facility and Rønne Harbor's wind turbine tasks mean for the freight capacity.

- We cannot live with the need for goods for the establishment of an energy island, the goods that usually keep the island running, says Peter Juel-Jensen.

He says he expects that the municipal council "sharpen the tone quite significantly", and he urges local politicians to link the capacity problem on the ferry with the energy island.

- I actually think Bornholm gives so plenty again when we look at the big wind turbine projects in the Baltic Sea. After all, it's not just a plus to Bornholm, because we're going to fight with some nuisance, so in the big cities you can get electricity. You do not make energy plants of this size because there is a lack of electricity on the islands.

In the letter to the regional municipality, the Ministry of Transport asked the Traffic Contact Council a final decision on the proposal to exchange departures with the fast ferries for extra shipping departures within the overall financial framework.

The Traffic Contact Council Chairman Jacob Trøst (K) informs the Journal that the members of the Council will discuss the matter and finally decide at the meeting in September.

Bornholm Tidende has tried to get an interview with Transport Minister Trine Bramsen since Wednesday - or at least get written answers to questions about why the Ministry of Transport refused to increase the grant in June and what she will do to ensure increased shipping capacity in the coming years the coming years . It has not succeeded yet.

Title: Større havvindmøllepark kan give Bornholm omkring 300 job
Content:
Just servicing the upcoming large offshore wind turbines can mean 300 jobs if you can end from the experience of Grimsby in England. After a visit to the city, business manager Christa Lodahl is optimistic. For Bornholm companies, it's still about getting ready.

It is good for Bornholm and for the Bornholm business community that the offshore wind farm is now getting bigger, coming faster and being financed and constructed with Germany.

This is what Business Manager Christa Lodahl says after Monday's agreement on the offshore wind farm, which brings the Germans directly into the gigantic project.

- I have no doubt that it is good for us that there is now more pushing on the offshore wind turbines, she says.

- The more activity that comes out there on the water, the more wind turbines must also be serviced.

I assume that the offshore wind turbines need to be serviced from Bornholm, so it should have a positive meaning that there are now 3 gigawatts instead of 2 gigawatts of offshore winds, says Christa Lodahl.

- Whether it's 3 or 2 gigawatts, it's all about putting Bornholm companies into play for the tasks that come.

Because if our companies are not ready, we will not get the full benefit that we could have gained.


Good experiences in England

Together with a colleague, Christa Lodahl has just visited the English town of Grimsby, which for the past ten years has served a large offshore wind farm with a capacity of 5 gigawatts from wind turbines.

- In Grimsby, they have created a service center that handles all the service and maintenance of wind turbines and all the shipping of goods. The service center employs just about 500 employees, says Christa Lodahl.

- Most of the 500 employees lived at most one hour drive away from the service center, so in Grimsby, the offshore wind turbines had a strong contagious effect locally. At least it was exciting for us to see what has emerged around what is currently the world's largest area of ​​offshore wind, she says.

It is still too early to say whether one can transfer Grimsby's experience with the number of jobs directly to Bornholm. But Christa Lodahl doesn't think it will be completely next door.

- Bornholm becomes a service island. But I do not know if you can end precisely from the fact that 5 gigawatts had given 500 jobs in Grimsby to 3 gigawatts on Bornholm giving 300 jobs here, she says.

- But it could well be a landmark without it being completely fixed. In Grimsby, the number also comes up to 500 because you have chosen to put some tasks from London out to Grimsby.

- Here we do not yet know if the upcoming operator of Energiø Bornholm will choose to do the same. In fact, we don't even know who the operator will be, says Christa Lodahl.


The leg work is in progress

However many new jobs will come up with the energy island, it is for the Bornholm companies to get ready for the chances that are coming. Many are already in progress.

- At least I have no doubt that there will be many opportunities for us. We also just have to be good at grabbing them, and fortunately I think that our companies have gone really well, says Christa Lodahl.

- For many companies at Bornholm, it's about doing some things right now, so you make it so professional that you can live up to the requirements to be able to bid on the tasks here, she says.

Tasks of many different kinds all require certificates.

- It can be about everything from the working environment to technical skills, and very often it requires some very specific certificates. We also saw that in Grimsby: If you just have to run a bus with their employees, it also requires some the right certificates, says Christa Lodahl.

- So it still depends on us playing our cards right and getting ready for the opportunities that come. Fortunately, I also think that our companies are really good at that. They change and take these opportunities on a spirit that impresses me a lot.

The more activity that comes out there on the water, the more wind turbines must also be serviced. I assume that the offshore wind turbines need to be serviced from Bornholm, so it should have a positive meaning that there are now 3 gigawatts instead of 2 gigawatt offshore winds.

Title: Ny fond: Enestående, at kunne samles om et så stort projekt
Content:

It is difficult to get your arms down for the Bornholm players in the brand new fund that will pave the way for a new and bigger way of producing green energy.

On Monday, it was clear that Ørsted, Siemens-Gamesa, DTU and Energinet are joining forces with Bornholm Regional Municipality, Bornholm Energi & Forsyning and Rønne Havn to establish the partnership Baltic Energy Island in Bornholm.

The goal is to create a global hub for innovation, testing and business development in green energy, and this gets Klaus Vesløv from Bornholm's Energy and Supply to clap your hands.

- It is unique that it has succeeded in bringing together this construction of large business funds, state and municipal organizations for such a large project on Bornholm, and then it is the idea that many others can also join, he explains.

However, establishing the cooperation is only the initial training for the big task the fund has ahead of it.

He compares the impending task of the establishment of the energy island of running a marathon, because it is a huge task that will take a long time to find your way.

- There are a lot of questions and they have some very complex answers. It's something brand new we need to do that no one has ever tried before, he explains.

He emphasizes that it is not only a huge thing for Bornholm's energy and supply, but also for the whole of Bornholm.

- It's going to make Bornholm more attractive to students, and it will mean that we get more students for a longer period of time.

The partnership Baltic Energy Island is formed on the basis of the project 'National Center for Green Energy', which was established with the support of the Danish Business Promotion Agency, the European Social Fund and the European Fund for Regional Development in 2021.

The first place in the world when the energy islands are currently being established is to support the security of supply and ensure the transition to sustainable energy forms. Bornholm will be the first place in the world where an energy island is established that can form the basis for the future development of energy islands globally. It is the idea that Bornholm should take the lead in the development of the Energy Islands and help ensure independence from Russian gas.

Bornholm's Energi & Forsyning had invited to a press conference in the old power plant in Rønne on Monday on just Baltic Energy Island. Here, Mayor Jacob Consolation and Environment Minister Lea Wermelin were present, as well as representatives from Ørsted and DTU respectively.

It is an opportunity to become the center of offshore wind in the Baltic Sea and an opportunity to develop Bornholm into a gas station for green transport on ships.

And then there is the fact that we can have new technologies tested, says Carsten Orth Gaarn-Larsen, Executive Vice President of DTU.

At Ørsted they are also excited about the partnership.

- We are extremely proud to see how far you can get when good forces merge, and we think the energy island on Bornholm is a really good example of, says Peter Obling, sales manager for Ørsted's commercial activities in continental Europe.

- There is a new technology that needs to mature. Title: Tillykke med millionerne, Bornholm

Really good work - we look forward to telling news of your plans.

"With formidable wind conditions and low water depths, the Baltic Sea area has a substantial potential for offshore wind," says in return.

Before the head of state goes on the podium in front of sun -drenched Marienborg, the satisfaction of the officials, who have been involved in the preparation for months.

The other key points are that countries will phase out black Russian fuels, collaborate on imports of fuels such as floating natural gas (LNG) and liquid biogas by sea, strengthen cooperation at the political level in energy security and explore the possibility of making more renewable energy projects across of borders.

In addition to the Danish-German agreement on a cable connection to Energiø Bornholm, Latvia and Estonia have also recently agreed to make a common offshore wind farm with support from the EU. Defeated pipelines

Today, the offshore wind capacity in the Baltic Sea region is 2.8 GW.

Denmark, Sweden, Poland, Finland, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania and Germany have agreed on a common ambition 19.6 GW by 2030.

Title: Politikerne accepterer dundrende milliardunderskud på Energiøen

Title: Mulige nye havvindmølleparker kan gøre landanlægget større
Content:
The company behind the plan for two new offshore wind farms off Dueodde and Svaneke is planning to end the parks to Energiø Bornholm's upcoming transformer station south of Aakirkeby. It is likely to make a larger land plant necessary. The municipality's consultation response gives green light to a preliminary study but at the same time asks for more information about, among other things, the land plant.

Energiø Bornholm's upcoming land facility south of Aakirkeby is planned to fill 70 hectares and become 25 meters high.

But maybe it gets even bigger.

For now, the investment company Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners (CIP) would like to build two offshore wind farms more beyond the two that the state is planning. And CIP operates by ending the power from its possible offshore wind farms 41 kilometers off Svaneke and 25 kilometers off Dueodde to the same land plant that the state will erect.

With a total intended capacity of three gigawatts, CIP's two possible offshore wind farms are to be as large as the two parks that the state will build as Energiø Bornholm.

The municipal office expects a larger land plant to be necessary if CIP is allowed to erect the two offshore wind farms and end the power to the energy island's transformer station.

Initially, CIP has applied to have to conduct preliminary studies. It is the first of a total of three steps that are needed against CIP expecting the two offshore wind farms east of Bornholm to start producing energy in 2028 or 2029.

In its consultation response to the Danish Energy Agency, the regional municipality approves that CIP can start preliminary investigations. At the same time, Mayor Jacob is asking comfort (K) on behalf of the municipal council's behalf for more information.

The Business Committee approved the mayor's proposal for the municipality's consultation response on Monday.

Out of a total of three possible disadvantages of yet another offshore wind farm, the size of the land plant is referred to as the first.

"It is proposed that the offshore wind farms must be connected to Energiø Bornholm's transformer station on land south of Aakirkeby. This could mean that increased area must be used for additional plants.


Energinet cannot answer

CIP will have to clarify it with Energinet if the power from CIP's two possible wind farms must also be brought ashore in the energy island's transformer station. Therefore, the municipality has asked Energinet what consequences it will have for the size of the energy island's land plant if CIP must have fulfilled its wish.

However, Energinet has not been able to answer. For the Danish Energy Agency has not asked Energinet to incorporate CIP's desire to also use Energiø Bornholm's land plant in its plans for the Energy Island.

Instead, the regional municipality is now trying with its consultation response to get CIP to unveil its more accurate thoughts on how large a land plant the investment company sees need.

"What is the applicant's plans here, when will be clarified with Energinet, and how will the applicant ensure that these areas are searched and arranged with the least possible negative effect in the local area?" Jacob asks comfort in the municipality's consultation response.

The municipality's two other concerns are that two offshore wind farms will also make more sea cables necessary - and that two extra offshore wind farms east of Bornholm can play negatively on fishing because CIP is planning to ban fishing with bottom trawl in the mill area.

"It is proposed that cable wiring be landed on the south coast of Bornholm, where increased area for cables must be used in relation to what Energinet will use.

What is the applicant's plans here, when are clarified with Energinet, and how will the applicant ensure that these areas are searched and arranged with the least possible negative effect in the local area? ”, It will therefore also sound in the municipality's consultation response that finally turns to the fishermen's conditions .

"It is suggested that there is no bottom trawl at the mill areas. This can have consequences for local fishermen. If the applicant goes into dialogue with the remaining Bornholm fishermen in relation to clarifying possible consequences.

What possible mitigation measures can the applicant imagine? ”.

The consultation phase ends on September 29.

Thereafter, climate, energy and supply minister Dan Jørgensen (S) will decide whether CIP should start a preliminary study.

If the minister gives green light and if CIP chooses to move on with the project after the feasibility study, the investment company will later have to apply to build the two offshore wind farms. If CIP is allowed to do so too, the company will finally have to apply to utilize the energy from the two offshore wind farms.

If CIP chooses to go all the way with its plan, the regional municipality will also be a consultation party in the next two consultation phases.

Title: Bornholm søger udbytte fra mulige nye havvindmølleparker
Content:
Offshore wind turbines Bornholm Bornholm should be part of the profits if two new offshore wind farms come east of the island, the municipality believes. Up to a fifth of the wind turbines may be Bornholm owned. The company behind the planned offshore wind turbines is also invited to put collaborations with Bornholm's business community in system.

If the investment company Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners (CIP) is to be allowed to build two wind farms off Svaneke and Dueodde, Bornholm should also get part in CIP's later profits to sell electricity from the wind turbines.

This is what Mayor Jacob Trøst (K) writes on behalf of the municipal council in the regional municipality's consultation response on the project, which the Business Committee approved on Monday. In practice, it should be the municipality that receives the money, the answer states.

"We believe that the project developer should be required to support the local area (Bornholm Regional Municipality) with a proceeds from electricity sales to local initiatives that support the municipal council's vision for Bornholm," Jacob Trøst writes.

At the same time, the mayor is seeking help in the work of getting money for Bornholm out of CIP.

"Can the Danish Energy Agency secure this?", The consultation response continues.

One -fifth of the two planned offshore wind farms may be Bornholm owned. For a start, however, it will depend on what status the Danish Energy Agency will give the planned wind farms off Østbornholm.

The fifth of an offshore wind farm must be offered locally when the wind turbines are built under the so-called open door arrangement.

However, this does not apply when it comes to experimental facilities, and here it can play a role in the fact that CIP plans to erect the wind farm either in whole or in part as floating wind turbines, a new technology.

"The administration has requested the Danish Energy Agency whether this will mean that the entire plant can thus be counted as an experimental plant and await answers to this," the Business Committee was informed before Monday's meeting.

"There may be the possibility of 20 percent local co -ownership of the parks. When is this clarified and how is it implemented?", The regional municipality asks in its consultation response.

Also elsewhere in the municipality's consultation response, Bornholm searches the opportunity to tie CIP up on committed collaborations at Bornholm.

This applies to Rønne Harbor's role as a first shipping port in a possible construction phase - and as a service port, when the wind turbines may have come into operation. But will CIP also take steps to secure local labor, housing for employees involved and opportunities for Bornholm business? the municipality asks in the consultation response.

"What will the applicant specifically do to promote these options, including any contributions to increasing the qualification and ensuring good housing opportunities? Will the applicant be aware of what tasks can be broken down in subcontracting so that more small contractors can bid on the tasks and will apply to contribute contribution To make visible these continuously in a common tender overview with Energiø Bornholm? ”, Jacob asks on behalf of The municipal council.

Getting more electricity led ashore can also strengthen the economy of placing a so-called power-to-x plant on Bornholm. The plant can transform electricity into hydrogen and other green fuel and will significantly strengthen Bornholm's ambitions to become a center for first and foremost ships to refuel green fuel. But it is still unclear whether Bornholm will get Power-to-X, or whether the energy island's power-to-X plant will be placed somewhere else.

"What specific plans do the applicant have in relation to the use and distribution of the large amounts of power?" Therefore, the regional municipality also asks CIP in the consultation response.

The municipality also asks CIP when the company decides whether the possible offshore wind turbines off Østbornholm should be floating mills or not. Floating Mills can, according to the consultation response, be "interesting" for the partnership Baltic Energy Island, which the regional municipality in August joined together with, among others, Ørsted, Siemens-Gamesa, DTU, Energinet, Rønne Harbor and Bornholm Energi & Forsyning. The goal is to create a global hub for innovation, testing and business development in green energy.

"When is it clarified which mill types are chosen? Will the applicant be prepared to enter into a collaboration with Baltic Energy Island?" Therefore, the municipality also asks CIP.

We believe that the project developer should be required to support the local area (Bornholm Regional Municipality) with a proceeds from electricity sales to local initiatives that support the municipal council's vision for Bornholm Jacob Trøst (K) shipped on behalf of the municipal council in the regional municipality.

Title: Almeborg og Koefoed slår alarm: Nyt budget vil gøre stor skade
Content:
The municipal budget Bornholm Bornholm will miss out on big money if the three parties behind the municipal budget stick to saving employees away in plan and development, warns Dansk Industri. Employees and management support the concern with specific figures.

It can and will probably cost many, a lot of money for the whole of Bornholm if the Unity List, the Left and the Social Democracy hold on to the budget agreement to remove two full -time equivalents in the municipality's departments for plan and development.

This is the opinion of Dansk Industri (DI) on Bornholm, which according to its consultation response on the budget looks "with great concern" on saving DKK 1.3 million by cutting the number of development and plan employees. The senders are director Michael Almeborg as chairman of DI Bornholm and contractor Jens Koefoed as chairman of DI Construction on Bornholm.

"DI finds the proposal extremely unfortunate, as plan and development lift a central and important task for the entire Bornholm Society's forward growth and development," they write.

Saving two man -years away in plan and development will mean "a significant deterioration of both the case processing time on local plans and municipal plant supplements as well as the support of major development projects that are important for both business and the entire Bornholm society", they also write.

If the three budget parties hold on to the plan, according to DI Bornholm's consultation response "will be largely inhibitory to growth and private investment". Just as it will hit "larger development projects that are central to the future of the island".

As an example, Michael Almeborg and Jens Koefoed cite the upcoming National Center for Green Energy, which "as a hub of knowledge of green technology, innovation and green business development has great perspectives and extraordinary growth opportunities for the whole of Bornholm." "It is crucial that plan and development have the necessary resources to support the fact that Bornholm harvests the potential of this and other major development projects that can make a positive difference to the island's development," writes DI Bornholm, who calls the area "decisive for The economic growth and development of Bornholm ”.

DI fears that the savings proposal "will have a negative impact on the entire Bornholm community" and believes that more money is needed to add more money instead of saving.

"Instead, plan and development in line with Byg should be ensured financing to continue to create the big, positive difference for Bornholm, which is necessary for a healthy society," writes Dansk Industri Bornholm.


Money from the outside will disappear

Dansk Industri is not alone with the concern.

The employees and the management of plan and development in their consultation response express much of the same.

"With the savings, development will no longer have resources to enter into the start of complex and strategically important projects that often have a major impact on business, social development and redemption of the regional municipality's vision of becoming 42,000 citizens," writes the Cooperation Committee in the Municipality Center for Regional Development , IT and Secretariat in its consultation response on the budget.

The municipality's development people have been behind several projects that are today considered Bornholm flagships or in other ways raise big money and open up new opportunities for Bornholm.

Almost 10 years ago, it was the meeting, and in September it was the new marching courts of the Rønne Harbor, where the municipality received a commitment of DKK 25 million in support in September. Going forward, this applies, among other things, Energiø Bornholm and the Center for Green Energy, which has received DKK 27.2 million in outside support.

"There are no resources anywhere else in the organization to lift these projects," writes the Cooperation Committee, which Development belongs.

At the same time, saving development will mean that the municipality will have to say no thanks to money from outside. However, the Development Unit has not had the opportunity to disclose in advance: Because the idea of ​​saving plan and development came from the left, not from a savings catalog, the positions to be saved away, without development even having the opportunity to describe the consequences of a minor development unit.

"In most cases, savings on projects will have financial consequences that should be described prior to political decisions, as most projects have an external financing from either the EU, state or foundations of typically 60-85 percent," the Cooperation Committee also states in its consultation response .


Legal requirements are not met

According to the Cooperation Committee, getting rid of local planners can also not pay for the municipality.

"It is estimated that a local planner who completes 2-4 local plans per year enables private investments of between DKK 10 and 200 million. In the case of Energiø Bornholm and Rønne Harbor, the amounts are significantly higher. The socio-economic reasonable in a saving on local planning is therefore Doubtful, ”the consultation response states.

The municipality currently has six local planners, which currently have a total of 24 cases in progress. In addition, they are in dialogue about another 20 local plans. Thus, each local planner has more than seven current cases in progress.

According to the consultation response, the local planners work in comparable municipalities between one and three cases at a time. At Bornholm, local planners may not always comply with the requirements of the law on how long it must take to deal with a case of a local plan.

"A priority of local planning cases has already been introduced because the large case pressure means that the legal requirement for a maximum of one year's case processing time (on cases where no new municipal planning framework) cannot be complied with," the consultation response states.

"Priority means that there are currently 2-3 years of case processing time on recreational facilities and businesses including cottage cases. Infrastructure and housing cases are currently being dealt with within one year, because these cases are considered vital in relation to the redemption of the regional municipality's vision of 42,000 citizens .

Title: Boderne ligner en boreplatform: Kabler skal trækkes den bedste og billigste vej
Content:
The feasibility studies for the new country plant with associated cables for the wind farm are in full swing. The first application has already been submitted and it is expected that the construction can start at the end of 2024.

It is rare that feasibility studies are being carried out for such a massive construction project as is currently doing in the stalls.

And that it happens under blue sky and with a solid sea view - there are certainly none of the working in flourcing orange clothes that complain about.

A large crane -like machinery goes far into the air - and far down into the ground. In these days, it is dot in the arable land, to find out what the Earth looks like below the surface.

- There is a very complicated geology here at Bornholm - especially compared to the soft Jutland mold, says Mads Robenhagen Mølgaard from the consulting firm Geo.

In the area here, cables will probably be established that can pull the power from the offshore wind turbines up to the land plant, but exactly where the cables should be pulled has not yet been decided. Therefore, a number of detailed feasibility studies are now underway.

- We know about what it looks like in general in the area here, but now we need to know the details, so that's why we make some core drilling.

That is drilled deep into the ground. From here, a sample of one and a half meters is pulled up, which is subsequently sent to Jutland, where they examine it at the bottom.

The studies must minimize the risk of unexpected disturbances during construction work.

- The soil should preferably be soft, but here on Bornholm there is a very varied geology, so the most important thing we can find out is how we can build and dig down without accident or unforeseen things. It can be if we encounter something that is very difficult to get through, explains Bent Sømod, who is the project manager at the preliminary investigations.


Will build in 2024

The work of examining the underground must clarify where the cables can be most easily and best pulled, where the land plant should be located exactly and what it should look like. Right now, work is being worked in a gross area that has been marked for the purpose.

So the whole thing is still just being investigated, and no more concrete locations can be reported - other than that 260 hectares of gross area have been allocated to the land facility just north of Søndre Landevej, and then the cables have to be drawn up there.

- We are over that it could be at Dueodde or something like that. It will be here in the area, says Bent Sømod.

The first applications for the project itself in the approximate area have been sent off.

He expects the application to hit the first public phase before the New Year, after which it will be consulted and then it should be more specific.

- We are preparing a proposal on how big it should be and what it should look like, and here we ask people to come up with ideas and suggestions, because here we have some flexibility. It goes into a kind of idea hearing, after which it becomes more specific and then we expect to hit another public phase on the specific project at the beginning of 2024, he explains.

- We first know where we will exactly build in the second half of 2024, when we get our permission to build this country plant.

At that time we have analyzed and examined it all, and found the best solution, says Bent Sømod.

After that you have four weeks to complain if you are still not satisfied. At Energinet you are not blind to the fact that few people dream of an energy island in the backyard.

- We find that people are generally interested and we do what we can to behave nicely. We have made some good appointments with the landowners and we find that there is a good mood. But it is no secret that most people would rather be free, says Bent Sømod.

He hopes that the feasibility studies can help make the construction work as quickly and smoothly for the peasants as possible.

- It's about risk -lying construction work so that there are no delays and so it all sticks to the plan. But it is not something that is going to affect citizens - or you can say that it is impossible to completely avoid being a nuisance. But we try to find the best solution so that there are no problems with crops, sinks and the like. We want to bother as little as possible, he says.

When the cables are buried to at least one and a half meters depth, you will not be able to see it at all, he assures. The farmer can again cultivate his land as he usually does - or at least almost.

- For the farmers who are going to set aside some of their land for cable excavation, a permanent compensation awaits.

There are going to be some crops they must not have, and then they must not plant forest - at least not trees with deep roots, and it is a significant restriction on the soil you own. That's why you get a replacement, he says.

In addition, compensation is also provided for the time and damage that occurs on the ground from now on while drilling.


Magnet on toboggan

Next to the big one lives toads an ATV around at a leisurely pace.

It provides associations for winter in the countryside, where a toboggan is tightened at the back of an off -road vehicle so that the youngest of the house can have a toboggan ride.

Here it is just a large electromagnetic object that gets a turn instead of a toboggan.

The object can paint a colorful picture of how the soil is composed in the top five to seven meters. It can feel how the soil responds to the magnet, and here the clay, mud, sand and lime respond in different ways.

- In fact, sand and lime answer in the same way, so that is why we also just need to pull samples up the ground, says Johanne Jensen from WSP, who is at the forefront of the geophysical studies.

- When we do both, we get a very accurate picture of how the soil layers are composed.

Work started three weeks ago and they're going to be in the area for a small month yet.

Title: Dan Jørgensen nåede at godkende plan for energiøen
Content:
The Danish share of the costs of constructing the electric infrastructure for Energiø Bornholm is expected to be DKK 3 billion lower than previously assumed, because Denmark and Germany this summer signed a political agreement on the large -scale energy project.

Climate, Energy and Supply Minister Dan Jørgensen (S) have approved Energinet's application for the electricity infrastructure to Energiø Bornholm. This happened on Tuesday before the election, according to an orientation to the Folketing's Climate, Energy and Supply Committee.

"The project must be implemented in accordance with the descriptions of the material that has been submitted for use in the case, including the choice of technical solution and other prerequisites set out in Energinet's Business Case for the project," Dan Jørgensen writes to the committee.

He states that it is a prerequisite that Energinet enters into an agreement with German 50Hertz on the distribution of ownership, costs and revenue.

"There are continued negotiations between Energinet and 50Hertz about this," the minister writes.

This summer it emerged that Energinet operated with a construction budget of DKK 16.9 billion for the land plants on Bornholm and Zealand as well as the cables to be used for Energiø Bornholm. Since then, Denmark and Germany have entered into a political agreement on German connection to the energy island.

This agreement has rocked the prerequisites behind Energinet's calculations, and the Danish share of the construction budget has therefore been reduced from 16.9 to 13.9 billion excluding risk costs, Dan Jørgensen announces. In addition, Energinet's derived operating costs are expected to be reduced from DKK 121 to 114 million a year.

The total price for Energiø Bornholm, when the construction of the offshore wind farms and the construction of the cables to the coast, is expected to be around DKK 70 billion, Dan Jørgensen announced in a response to Peter Juel-Jensen (V).

Acceptance from the municipal council Energiø Bornholm is scheduled to be completed by 2030. At the end of August it was formally decided to increase the size of the project from 2 to 3 gigawatts. The offshore wind farms will be erected south and southwest of Bornholm at least 15 kilometers from land, while the land plant is expected to be located within a selected gross area of ​​260 hectares on South Bornholm at Sdr. Road, Limensgaden and Vasegårdsvej.

In September, the municipal council approved the location that Energinet prefers after several Bornholmers in consultation responses had pointed to alternative areas that in their opinion would be better. The next step will be to prepare a supplement to the municipal plan and a new local plan for the area.

The land plant requires an area of ​​70-90 hectares (0.7-0.9 square kilometers). It must contain a converter system and high voltage equipment so that the green power can be transported to Zealand and Germany as DC with a voltage of 400 kilovolts.

The transformation from alternating-to direct current is complicated and requires some large buildings that are expected to get a height of about 25 meters. The developer Energinet has not yet announced what the land plant will look like, just as no visualizations have been made, where the large building is shown in the flat South Bornholm Landscape.

Title: Kristendemokraterne var det parti, jeg var mindst uenig med

Bjarne Hartung Kirkegaard has been in politics for many years, and now he is - again - standing up to the Folketing.

It was in the 1970s that I became a very passive member of the party's youth department. I was also a member of the Christian Listening Association, which was an unpolitical association where I was active, and so I had to be a passive party political.

But later I switched to and became a passive member of the Listening Association and active in the party. I was a member of the Leisure Board in Allinge-Gudhjem Municipality, elected for KFUM and K and sat as an alternate for one from the diving club Calypso, but he traveled after two years and then I took over. For example, we convened the Finance Committee to meet about the ball courts at Allinge Stadium, and I found out that with politics was a bit exciting.

- They then asked me in the party if I would like to stand up, and I did that to the municipal council in 1981. I became first alternate for our husband in Allinge-Gudhjem, but never came into operation. In 1985 I then lined up for the county council and was elected in 1986. I experienced that I belonged to the Christian People's Party because it was the party I had least disagreed with.

You have set up sometimes to the Parliament? - Yes, at least in 2011 I lined up, and at that time I was a candidate in Zealand. We then had some other candidates at Bornholm, and I was the national chairman in the years 2008-11, and when a candidate in Zealand was missing, I raised my hand and said, "It's me". If you give them money to the electricity bill or something else, there will be some others sitting and holding your breath because they are afraid of inflation getting a proper bang upwards. Unfortunately, I don't think anyone dares to put the election campaign on stand by for a few days to find such a solution, but it could have been fine, because there is really someone squeezing around.

Maybe also help to hire some people for it, because some bottlenecks are coming. In addition to the energy island, there is also the company Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners, CIP, which will build wind turbines east of Bornholm. They have thought that the wind turbines should spin as early as 2027, and should it happen, must very much fall into place, including the case processing in the regional municipality.

Title: Fra havvind til brint: CIP lægger op til et storstilet bornholmsk power-to-X-anlæg
Content:
The company behind the idea of ​​erecting two offshore wind farms east of Bornholm has been to Bornholm to meet the local actors. Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners is prepared for their offshore wind turbines not necessarily to be connected to the electricity grid. On the other hand, the power must first and foremost be converted into hydrogen or other fuels at a Bornholm electrolysis plant.

M own has been said and written and written about the wind turbine project Energiø Bornholm, which is expected to be ready to produce electricity from hundreds of offshore wind turbines by 2030. Therefore, it seems incredible if the state mega project really was to be overtaken by an offshore wind- Project of the same size on the other side of Bornholm. But that is the ambition of Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners - often just called CIP. In June, the company submitted applications to the Danish Energy Agency to build two offshore wind farms on every 1.5 gigawatts - one with floating wind turbines - east of Bornholm, and the goal is to be finished faster with the construction than the actors winning the state's tender. This is stated by Cip Magnus Brogaard, as the Tidende makes his way past the powerful company's headquarters in Copenhagen's Nordhavn.

- What is unique about these projects is that we are able to deliver them early and prior to the state tenders at Rønne Banke, which is expected to be ready by 2030. We expect to be able to deliver these projects in 2027 And thus help to start it all up.

So far, CIP is a step behind the energy island.

The first four -week consultation round is over. The application, which the Journal mentioned when the consultation started, is now at the Danish Energy Agency. The upcoming climate, energy and supply minister must, after an election, decide whether CIP should be allowed to do preliminary investigations. At the end of the year, CIP hopes to get permission to move forward with the preliminary investigations at sea.


Green hydrogen

How can one overtake a state -owned offshore wind turbine project that depends on cables for Zealand and Germany? Does CIP do not need the same connections, and will land and cables not have to expand to have room for the extra electricity? You could believe that, but in CIP's plan, the primary output is not power to the electricity grid in the Baltic Sea countries. On the contrary, it is green fuels, first and foremost hydrogen produced using electrolysis at a Powerto-X plant that CIP wants to erect on Bornholm.

- We do not expect to have full access to the collective electricity grid in connection with the two proposed projects. Energinet's connection to Germany and Zealand and the plant we expect is dimensioned to Energiø Bornholm.

That is why we expect our power-to-X project to be the absolutely primary customer, says Magnus Brogaard.

-We are pretty sure that we have both the skills and the means to create such a power-to-X system.

So the output from the offshore wind farms is actually largely power-to-x, ie different green fuels? - Yes.

What kinds of green fuels do you have to choose from on Bornholm? Can you tell you about your considerations? - The first and primary product is green hydrogen. In the electrolysis process you split water and get hydrogen, and it thinks we can be carried via pipes to Germany and used in their hydrogen network.

One of the things we want to look at are the ambitions of supplying green fuels to shipping traffic, and here I immediately think of ammonia, says Magnus Brogaard, who met in September with Rønne Harbor during the visit to Bornholm.

Rønne Harbor is in collaboration with, among others, Ørsted, Molslinjen and Topsøe in a consortium that works with plans to produce green ship fuel on Bornholm and popularly establish a gas station for vessels in the Baltic Sea. In CIP, you may well be an active participant, but the decisive decisions about what the large amounts of current from Eastern offshore wind farms must be converted to, will only be made later.

- So the question of how much we can possibly think our project into the plans that Rønne Harbor has for green fuels for ships? How much can be thought of in a decrease in Germany, where a pipe should be put. Now it is generally much cheaper to move energy via pipes than with electric transmission, so there can be a case. Working on the plans is waiting for us to get started with the preliminary investigations, says Magnus Brogaard.

It may also be a matter of supplying electricity to the electricity grid, says the CIP director-either through a link to the Bornholm electricity grid or via Energinet's future transformer plant in Sydbornholm and from there on to Zealand and Germany through the Energiø cables.

- It may be over two stages - first with an access to the Bornholm network and later you can look at whether you can be connected to the energy island's new plant and get some capacity from 2030. But we think it will be a relatively limited amount, So one has to imagine that the offshore wind turbines are delivering production into a power to X system, which of course we have to find out where it should be - and how much it is going to fill.

I can't answer you yet, says Magnus Brogaard.


Buried Power-to-X

He explains that CIP will seriously initiate the work of placing and dimensioning a power-to-X system and cable connections on land when/ if the company gets green light to take up the feasibility studies.

- We do not have a detailed description of exactly what the plants should look like and how big they become. But that will be what we will focus on getting on place as soon as we have a permit to start collecting data. We have worked in CIP a lot with the visual expression on the Power-to-X section, among other things in connection with our islands in the North Sea.

Can you dig them down? We mean that you can - at least partly. Can you integrate them into nature? We mean that too. There are some initial thoughts on how to get them integrated into the surroundings.

As one can sense of the answers, CIP's considerations about how the energy from offshore wind farms are specifically used are still in an initial phase. The final size of the offshore wind farms is also uncertain, and the two applications must be perceived as gross applications, says the director.

Should it be understood that your two projects each have a size of "up to" 1.5 gigawatts? - Yes. But it is clear that we would like some scale and a certain size in them. They are made to achieve economies of scale.

It is also the reason why we have moved the projects so far off the coast, says Magnus Brogaard.

He has a hard time answering how large the offshore wind farms at Bornholm have to be at least to make sense to realize the project, but he emphasizes several times that "scale" is a key word.

-You must also have a sizing that fits both the power-to-X production you want and the infrastructure and the decrease you need further from there. It's hard to answer exactly how much is needed. But 1 gigawatt I would say that you have to go up.

The final design of CIP's project will depend on preliminary studies and many other things that have not yet been clarified.

- It's a very early stage, says Magnus Brogaard.

- The applications define a gross area where the projects can be located - 41 and 25 kilometers east and south respectively.

The mills do not come outside those areas, but we now have a high degree of flexibility to customize the projects-both according to what we find on the seabed, what use is otherwise of the sea and how our power-to-X plant should be dimensioned , says Magnus Brogaard and highlights a couple of central unresolved questions: - What is there in Bornholm in relation to land facilities? And what is the use of the energy? How long have you really had a look at these wind areas? - We started in the spring, says Magnus Brogaard, emphasizing that the significant political announcements of renewable energy expansion have played into the CIP's decision to start work.

- We have been through all the data that has been available on marine plans, maritime traffic, Natura 2000 areas and so on - and of course also looked at which areas have been reserved for state tenders.

And then we have with great interest looked at the whole area around Bornholm - also based on the visions that are for Bornholm as a central place for the green transition.

And the role of energy hub in the Baltic Sea, says Magnus Brogaard.


Starting on local involvement

A small CIP delegation visited Bornholm in September. The program included meetings with, among others, Rønne Harbor, Bornholm Energi and Supply, the Regional Municipality and Nexø Harbor, which with the location can have an important role in the operation and maintenance of the offshore wind farms. CIP would very much like to be behind projects that are thought of in local interests and Bornholm's role as an energy hub, explains Magnus Brogaard - We believe we can help put things going and help set some standards for sea ​​and biodiversity - and set some standards for what the dialogue with the locals will look like. Our trip last week was the start, says Magnus Brogaard and at the same time promises that the Bornholmers will soon get more material about the parks.

- We have made some visualizations that we would like to showcase locally. They show that you are virtually unable to see them.

I think many Bornholmers would like to know more about what is going on on land.

When do you start interesting in that part of the project? - I think we will start with that at the beginning of next year. The expectation is that we will have the permission to initiate feasibility studies at the end of this year. In 2023, we will embark on both thoughts and dialogue about the country in parallel with the feasibility study in the sea.

The CIP and the wind turbine industry - like the climate and energy consumers in general - have an interest in the expansion of offshore wind over the next handful of years.

- All the state tenders are to be delivered in 2030, Hesselø maybe in 2029. It will create a huge pressure on the supplier chain.

Other European countries - the Netherlands, Germany, Belgium, England, Norway - will have their projects delivered exactly there because the political objectives were set by 2030. It means that if we can just get in with those projects a few years before, there will be a great opportunity - both to get the value chain going, also to avoid being caught in a bottleneck. So this is our interest commercial, but also the suppliers' interest in getting started, says Magnus Brogaard and summarizes the conversation.

- For the next two years we will become wiser on the project.

We are dedicated to delivering some scalable projects that also bring coexistence into the picture.

A few hours after the visit to CIP, a text message from one of the Bornholm representatives with whom CIP met at Bornholm.

"Hi Jakob, if one day you encountered images and dimensions of a 1.5 GW electrolysis system, I am very interested in seeing and hearing". The message of the power-to-X visions has thus arrived.

Title: Med lov skal man land(anlæg) bygge
Content:
The properties and houses that are very close to the land facility are impossible to sell at normal price.

Re Egesing, the Folketing and thus the State is the reason and is responsible for a loss of value of several million kroner for the people who become neighbors of the huge transformer and cable system and the power-to-X factory, which is planned in connection with Energiø Bornholm.

The huge country facility will be almost 100 hectares (about 150 football fields) and perhaps even bigger if even more offshore wind turbines are to be built at Bornholm, which is very likely. This means that the property value for the neighbors drops drastically.

The properties and houses that are very close to the plant are impossible to sell at normal price. If these properties are to be sold, it becomes a fraction of the value they had before the energy island project and the location of it was published.

We estimate that properties up to three kilometers from the land plant will lose significantly in value.

We encourage the Bornholmers and the Bornholm politicians to find another place on Bornholm to build the PTX plant. The whole of Bornholm has to help carry the energy island and not just us south of Aakirkeby.

The energy island projects are part of the green transition to save the climate, and the war in Ukraine has meant that we now have an energy crisis and thus the green transition is urgently urgent, and we can expect the projects to be implemented at maximum speed and little opportunity for to avoid errors.

Thus, it seems that the energy island projects are being implemented quickly and that there is broad support in the population and in the Folketing. We have democracy in Denmark, and therefore we must accept when it is decided that the energy island projects should be realized, even if we live in the area and become neighbors to the land plant, which is well built on land expropriated by the state.

However, we who are neighbors of the upcoming plant cannot accept that we lose a large part of our property value. Since the publication of the location of the land facility, we have not been able to sell houses in the area. Any buyers wait until the land plant is built before buying houses in the area, which means the problem will continue for many years.

When the Danish population and thus the state have initiated the energy island projects, the large majority of Denmark's population is causing a small minority that the neighbors of the land plant are, a large financial loss in the form of greatly reduced property value.

We can't accept that! When the majority in Denmark has decided that Energiø Bornholm should be realized, the same majority must help pay the costs, so that Energiø Bornholm and other energy islands do not ruin the people who are so unlucky to become neighbors to the land plant. There are disadvantages enough beyond the financial! Therefore, we demand that laws be prepared that make the neighbors to the land facility be damaged free. This may be possible by expanding the value loss scheme to include large transformer stations and cable systems, which can easily be compared to photovoltaic systems and wind turbines that are already covered. The legislative changes must apply from the time Energiø Bornholm was published.

The state is going to make money selling green power abroad for the next 50 years, and the inhabitants of the rest of Denmark will be able to get green electricity from Energiø Bornholm, but if the neighbors for the land plant do not get compensation, we will do everything to keep Combat Energiø Bornholm.

If all citizens in Denmark halved their property value due to the green transition, then I think the support would be extremely limited. Play with the thought! We have heard several times from Energinet and Bornholm Regional Municipality that they think it is very important with dialogue and that they would like to listen to us, but then they must see to get started with that dialogue. Dialogue means the exchange of views, especially between warring parties to reach mutual agreement FPR example as opposed to an armed conflict.

We have made a citizen proposal for the Folketing, and we urge all politicians to take this seriously and do the necessary work to change the law.

We would like to attend work if anyone wants to listen! If Denmark does not want even greater resistance to the green transition, then our politicians have to take us seriously and not only listen, but also act - now!.

Title: Den grønne omstilling kræver, at vi tager nogle trælse valg
Content:
Julie Pauch Nymark, who is running for the Folketing for the Left, will be an alternative to Lea Wermelin, and one young voters can reflect.

Why are you running for the Parliament? - I do this because I think there should be a female candidate the young people can reflect on. In politics you often talk about voters having no one to reflect on, and they have it now.

And then it was also a fun personal challenge for me to take an alternative to Lea Wermelin. So it is a good mix of that I would like to challenge myself and that I think a young liberal alternative in the election campaign is missing.

What do you see as the overall most important theme of the election? - It's hard, because it's hard to choose.

But climate and green transition must be the most important overall themes. Then comes energy, inflation and economy. And the whole thing is connected.

What do you see as the most important theme of the election for Bornholm? - I think the most important theme on Bornholm is the elements needed to ensure the island's development in ten years. The fact that we embrace the green energy island and address the opportunities for investments, because Bornholm has very good opportunities. Right now there are good opportunities for climate and education, and to be able to attract more labor and to be able to fire the island. We have to seize that.

With the Energy Island, we can in the future get a whole new segment of people working with the green transition, and it can again contribute a lot to families with children and more skilled workers coming.

- But we have to dare to make the choices it requires, even if everyone does not think it is so decorative with a transformer station. It requires us to make some tricky choices in order for us to develop Bornholm and be able to maintain the development of the green agenda.

How can we embrace it? Can you put more words on? - I think we should look at ourselves and acknowledge that even if it is a slave that it stands with me, it must stand somewhere. We, as Danes, are very good at saying yes to things as long as it does not go beyond ourselves as long as it is not just in my backyard, and as long as it is not me to eat less meat. It is at the level we need to start, because we never get beyond the steppes if we only look at restrictions and do not look at opportunities.

Does it also apply to ourselves as private? - Yes, if you have the opportunity and desire, then I think you have to make choices that help us in the right direction, but it is not individuals who are the greatest actor.

It is the big community and governments that need to change that. But you definitely have to sweep for your own door first, and if we want the green transaction, then we also have to say yes to some wind turbines that destroy our views over the water.

How much time do you spend on the election campaign? - It fills something for me every day. But I have some physical limitation, because I have a term in a month and a half. But in a week's time, I am much more on Bornholm in the campaign we have planned specifically targeting the young voters. And I'm really looking forward to it.

How many of your own money are you using? - I don't have an overview of it yet, but I've bought posters and stickers and different things for distribution, so I guess a good handful of thousands of dollars.

Why do you set up when your chance of being selected is so small? - That's because I think there should be some candidates the young people can reflect on, maybe some who are future parents who think that I can mirror me. It is extremely important with diversity on the electoral lists.

So even though I am not elected, I still hope to have some influence afterwards.

I think it all counts.

What is the most important new thing you have learned by running for the Parliament? - It has dawned on me how much to get into when you stand for the Folketing.

I have always had great respect for candidates and those who do volunteer work, but how much it is filling and how much time it takes to get into a lot of things, I did not have insight into before. There really is a lot of internship and bureaucracy in becoming voting and how to submit forms to the National Board of Appeal and everything. So I have gained even more respect for now.


Facts:

Julie Pauch Nymark is 27 years old.

She lives at Amager with her husband, Kristian Nørgaard.

Julie has his entire family on Bornholm and has a cottage in Sømarken himself.

She is currently waiting for the couple's first child.

She works daily as a clerk at the National Board of Digitization, where she has helped to make the Coronapas app.

Title: Jeg ville være en god suppleant for Lea
