Lars Goldscmidt stands for the Social Democracy without having the high hopes of being elected. But he thinks he would be a good alternate for Lea Wermelin if she needed a break.

Why are you running for the Parliament? - I do this because I think politics is important and it is important to engage politically.

So I set up to support our top candidate, Lea Wermelin, and because I think I would be a good bid for an alternate for her and would be good if I came to the parliament.

What do you see as the overall most important theme of the election? - There are several that are really important, but from my own interest, there is the climate agenda and a broad security agenda, which is about security, financial security and security in old age. These are the two main questions, but I am also quite interested in education at all.

What do you see as the most important theme of the election for Bornholm? - There is Energiø and the energy theme important.

And then to find out how we handle that there are too few hands in almost every area. It is a labor theme, but also a matter of organizing the workplaces so that they can solve the tasks with the people there are there.

How much time do you spend on the election campaign? - I'm going to use what's good button and nap equals a full -time job. My work depends a lot on what others are doing, so when others keep free, there are also no meetings on boards or anything else, so in that way the autumn holidays are a good time. You could say that last week of October is very busy with something else, but the other weeks have been very good compared to being able to lead the election campaign.

How many of your own money are you using? - I'm going to spend in the order of 10,000 kroner. But I use them together with the party.

Which means? - That we don't even go out and buy ads for ourselves. We do it with the party box so that we do not stand out in the way that if I had a lot of money, I could spend a lot of people on myself personally.

This is not how we do.

This is the third time in a row you are running for the Parliament, which you also did in 2015 and 2019 - do you think you will be elected? - The first time I actually thought I could be chosen, but no, I don't think so.

Why are you standing up if you don't think the chance is so great? - Well, success for me is that the Social Democracy on Bornholm gets a good choice and that Lea gets a good choice. I would very much like to be the first alternate, so if she needs a break, I can step into the Folketing immediately, because I think I have the experience for that.

When and how did you find that you are a Social Democrat? - I did that in the late nineties.

At that time I was organized in SF, but then I disagreed with the party line, especially in relation to the EU, and together with Christine Antorini I went from SF to the Social Democracy.

What is the most important new thing you have learned by running for the Parliament? - It is in fact what an election campaign consists of. I have done political work for many years as interest in Danish industry, but to experience having to sell not just a stand, but also himself as a convincing person and Meeting voters is different from what I've tried before. I've learned a lot from it - also that I'm not as good at what I really thought I was.

What lies in it? - That being a politician is also a craft, and in relation to the craft of getting out and being convincing in the streets and alleys I really have to make every effort.

But it is really very healthy to deal with something you can't just in advance.

Title: Ny virksomhed med gamle rødder: Direktøren er selv en bekymret el-kunde
Content:
Bornholms Energi & Forsynings direktør Claus Andersen får selv energi af at arbejde sammen med andre. Og der har været nok at se til, siden han trådte til som direktør for små to år siden, inden energikrisen brød ud.

Energikrisen gav allerede både politikere og ikke mindst bekymrede forbrugere hovedpine, inden Østersøen med komikeren Jonatan Spangs ord kom til at ligne en stor opløst Treo, efter der blev sprængt hul på både Nordstream 1 og 2. For selvom de to gasrør ikke forsyner Bornholm, er energipriserne - ikke mindst elpriserne - mildt sagt eksploderet de seneste måneder, hvor det er blevet klart for alle, at verden hænger sammen, så en energikrig med Rusland alligevel får indflydelse på bornholmske energipriser.

Og der går næppe en dag uden emnet fylder både i valgkampen og i medierne, men da Claus Andersen for knap to år siden trådte til som ny direktør for Bornholms Energi & Forsyning fra en stilling i Kolding som divisionsdirektør og en del af landeledelsen i det store internationale ingeniørfirma Sweco troede nogle af hans venner, at det nok ville blive halvkedeligt for ham at flytte til Bornholm. Men intet kunne være mere forkert.

- Jeg landede 1. januar sidste år. Så jeg er rimelig ny på både Bornholm og i den her branche, som nogen sagde var støvet og andre sagde var lavinteresse. Men de seneste måneder er energiområdet jo bare eksploderet i interesse. Og for os har det givet mange store udfordringer og krævet nytænkning, som det har været spændende at være en del af, siger Claus M. Andersen, som ikke har manglet spænding, siden han satte sig i direktørstolen og senest forrige mandag fik travlt, da strømmen pludselig forsvandt på hele øen - denne gang dog på grund af en lokal fejl og ikke på grund af et brud på søkablet til Sverige. Men da Bornholms Tidende besøger ham inden, er der også nok at se til.

- Hver dag er vi nødt til at sikre, at der er både drift og udvikling i selskabet. Vi skal selvfølgelig sørge for, at der er vand i vandhanen, varme i radiatoren og strøm i stikkontakten.

Så en stor del af virksomheden er beskæftiget med at lave sikker stabil drift.

Samtidig sker der alle de her vilde ting med krig i Europa og energipriser på himmelflugt og kæmpestore anlæg, der kommer til Bornholm og kommer til at påvirke Bornholm og vores virksomhed enormt meget.

Derfor er vi også nødt til at tilpasse os den udvikling og den nye virkelighed. Og balancen mellem driften i maskinrummet og det meget nysgerrige udadvendte, synes jeg er vildt interessant. Derfor er det også fedt, at jeg har overtaget virksomheden på et tidspunkt, hvor vi både har de finansielle muskler og kompetencer til at gøre andet og mere end bare at fokusere indad, men også har mulighed for at hjælpe Bornholm ved at gribe nogle af de muligheder, der opstår i tiden, siger han.


FÅR ENERGI AF ANDRE

Bornholms Energi & Forsyning (Beof) beskæftiger godt 120 medarbejdere og omsætter for omkring en halv milliard kroner.

- På den måde er det også en spændende størrelse virksomhed, fordi den er stor nok til at kunne noget, men samtidig er lille nok til, at jeg næsten kan alles fornavne. Og det har en særskilt værdi for mig, at alle kender alle i vores skønsomme blanding af smede, maskinmestre, elektrikere, andre håndværkere og en masse administrativt personale lige fra ingeniører til økonomimedarbejdere, byggeledere og anlægsfolk, så vi har virkelig mange forskellige kompetencer. Min egen filosofi er, at dygtige mennesker kan man aldrig få nok af. Og vi har virkelig mulighed for at bruge folks talenter, uanset om de er dygtige til et fag eller en bestemt akademisk gren.

Hvad giver dig selv energi som leder? - Det gør andre mennesker, smiler direktøren varmt.

- Jeg befinder mig enormt godt i samspillet med andre, så derfor var min første tid som direktør her midt under coronakrisen en hård tid som leder, hvor jeg skulle sidde derhjemme bag skrivebordet. Hjemmearbejde giver mig ikke særlig meget energi, men det giver mig energi at være sammen med andre mennesker, og det gør ikke noget, at der er noget at rive i. Jeg har det klart bedst, når der også er en smule travlt. Og der er vi i den lykkelige omstændighed, at der er nok at tage fat på. Der ligger masser i bunken, så vi kommer ikke til at kede os på den korte bane. Og så giver det mig også energi, når vi lykkes, og jeg møder en glad kunde, der er tilfreds med den behandling, vedkommende har fået. Man kunne også se vores teamspirit, da søkablet blev revet over i februar, og folk strømmede herned til kraftværket for at hjælpe i virksomheden.

Mange troede jo også, at det var Putin dengang? - Ja, det var en pudsig timing, men det viste sig jo bare at være et dansk tankskib, der havde sit anker hængende efter skibet, og det er søkablet jo ikke designet til. Så de har simpelthen ikke opdaget på skibet, at de havde et anker ude. Søkablet er ellers forsøgt spulet ned i havbunden, men det bevæger sig jo lidt, og vi har brug for det, indtil vi selv bliver selvforsynende med grøn energi.


ENERGIØER KAN GAVNE BORNHOLM

Det er især, når det er overskyet og vindstille på øen, at vi bliver nødt til at købe strøm fra svenskerne, så en af fremtidens opgaver bliver også at lære at lagre den energi, der kan skabes, forklarer han. Men Beof er selv med sine varmeværker og vindmøller hovedleverandør af den varme og el, der skal bruges på øen.

- Vi har også al spildevandet og cirka en tredjedel af vandet, og på varmeområdet producerer vi langt hovedparten af varmen, bortset fra det Bofa og Bigadan (biogasanlægget i Aakirkeby) laver. På elområdet står vi måske for halvdelen. Vi har et meget fint kort, som viser hele energisystemet på Bornholm.

Langt hovedparten af forsyningen står vi for, siger direktøren og rejser sig fornøjet op for at tegne og fortælle ved en tavle på sit kontor.

- Og næsten al øens energi er grøn, siger han smilende.

- Vi siger, at omkring 99 procent af energien er grøn, fordi den er produceret på vedvarende energi som vind eller på biomasse, der kan bestå af flis, halm eller træpiller.

Men vi bruger næsten ingen træpiller og næsten kun flis, som jo er bæredygtigt, fordi det er affaldstræ, så 99 procent af vores energi er bæredygtig. Grunden til, at det ikke er 100 procent, er, at vi jo skal have noget reserveenergi til strøm, hvis søkablet ryger. Og en gang i mellem er vi også nødt til at teste, om vores beredskab virker. Man kan ellers sige, at søkablet er vores livline til Sverige, så det el, vi ikke selv producerer, kan komme fra Sverige. Vores elforbrug på Bornholm ligger på omkring 250 gigawatttimer om året. Og af dem laver vi omkring 155 gigawatttimer her på øen, mens vi får resten fra Sverige. For når vinden ikke blæser, så har vi ikke nok el selv, men når vinden blæser, har vi faktisk mere, end vi selv bruger, så vi kan eksportere den til Sverige via søkablet. Og hvis vi får mere sol-og vindenergi, som planen er, så bliver vi også mere selvforsynende. Og der er planer for at sætte flere vindmøller op.

Fra Beofs kontorer kan man se de store vindmølledele, der ligger på havnen. Men dem får bornholmske forbrugere ikke gavn af foreløbig.

- Det, du kan se, er tårnene til vindmøller, som er ved at blive skibet ud fra Rønne Havn til et tysk projekt. Men der er jo også planer om det, man kalder Energiø Bornholm, sydvest for Bornholm. Jeg er ikke så god til at tegne, siger han undskyldende og sætter yderligere ringe ud fra sin tegning af øen på tavlen.

- Det er planer om to kæmpeparker herude cirka 20 kilometer fra kysten, og det skal landføres til den sydlige del af Bornholm, og så skal der lægges et kabel til Sjælland og et kabel til Tyskland. De to parker tilsammen giver tre gigawatt. Der er også nogle, som har planer om at opsætte vindmøller længere væk fra kysten øst for Bornholm med yderligere tre gigawatt. Det ene projekt skal efter planen op at køre i 2027 og det andet i 2030.

Selvom det er andre, der står for de store anlægsprojekter i Østersøen, vil det betyde en hel masse for Beof af afledte effekter, fordi de to nye energiøer både vil kunne forsyne øen med energi og måske give flere arbejdspladser til øen i form af for eksempel datacentre. Og med to ekstra kabelforbindelser til henholdsvis Sjælland og Tyskland, ville øen heller ikke være så afhængig af søkablet til Sverige og af at have sort energi i reserve, men så skal der altså til gengæld arbejdes på at blive bedre til at lagre energien, så der er masser af spændende projekter i fremtiden, forklarer han.


EN RIGTIG BESLUTNING

Beof er selv en ny virksomhed med gamle rødder. For øens første spildevandsanlæg blev skabt for over 100 år siden, og før i tiden var det øens forskellige kommuner, der stod for øens varmeforsyning, inden det hele blev samlet i Bornholms Forsyning.

- Hernede på havnen har vi ligget siden 1940' erne, hvor man byggede værket hernede, da Østkraft rykkede herned fra Lille Madsegade, hvor der havde været nogle generatorer, dengang Rønne blev elektrificeret.

Så det her har ligget her siden 1940' erne? - Ja, og det nuværende selskab Bornholms Energi & Forsyning blev dannet ved en fusion i 2016 mellem Bornholms Forsyning og Østkraft. Så på en måde har vi både en kort og ret lang historik. Men i 2016 besluttede man også at ombygge blok 6 heromme bagved fra kul og olie til flis, så flis blev vores hovedbrændsel. Det blev idriftssat i 2017. Det var også den beslutning, som hele konflikten med Rønne Vand og Varme udspringer af, siger han med henvisning til den juriske armlægning om varmeprisen, som parterne ser meget forskelligt på. Men beslutningen var alligevel rigtig, mener Claus Andersen.

- Når vi ser tilbage på beslutningen, var det med til at gøre vores produktion grøn baseret på bæredygtige kilder og samtidig har det vist sig at være betydeligt mere prisstabilt, end vi desværre ser priserne på gas, olie og el er, så det er også pt. den billigste produktionsform. Men den største udfordring for os er stadig, at energipriserne er eksploderet.

Men er det ikke også jer, der fastsætter dem? - Nej, det er markedet. Når vi producerer energi, så sælger vi det ud til en energibørs, men så har vi et andet selskab, som vores kunder køber energi fra, og det selskab er ude på samme børs og købe strømmen og sælge det videre til kunderne. Det er det, man mærker som kunde, men prisen bliver fastsat af børsen eller markedet, og det er præget af udbud og efterspørgsel. Og det vi ser nu er, at priserne er gået amok - dels på grund af krigen i Ukraine, og at Rusland har lukket ned for forsyningen til Europa. Det er så koblet med, at man har rekordlav vandstand i Norge, så vandkraftværkerne ikke kan producere det, de plejer deroppe.

Og der er tørke i Europa, som betyder, at flere af kraftværkerne i Europa simpelthen ikke har kunnet få kølevand nok fra floderne, og så har der heller ikke været særlig meget vind. De faktorer har tilsammen gjort, at prisen er blevet virkelig høj.


KOMPLICERET PRISSYSTEM

Så det er ikke korrekt forstået, at I energiselskaber i samme periode har tjent styrtende med penge? - Jo, på den ene side tjener vi mere på at sælge energi til energibørsen. Men systemet skaber altså samtidig en meget uheldig mekanisme, der betyder, at prisen bliver højere, når vi så skal ud at købe el, selvom vores egne omkostninger til vores vindmøller jo ikke er steget. Det vil sige, at vores omkostninger ikke er steget, men at vi lige pludselig får tre gange så meget som vi gjorde sidste år, fordi man får og betaler det samme som for gas. Det virker jo helt uretfærdigt.

Men det er hele markedsdesignet på elmarkedet, som er en europæisk konstruktion.

Det er ekstremt kompliceret, og hvis man begynder at pille ved det, kan det få store konsekvenser. Men Eurokommissionen arbejder på at skille prisen på gas og vedvarende energi ad.

Men når I tjener mere, kan I så ikke også stadig sænke prisen til forbrugerne? Ellers kan I jo virke som nogle grådige kapitalister - Nej, nej, griner han og tilføjer: - Til alle, der gider høre på det, vil jeg heller ikke forsvare den elmarkedsmodel, vi har i øjeblikket, for det er totalt ulogisk, at man pludselig skal have tre eller fire gange så meget for noget, der ikke er blevet dyrere at producere, så der er en fejl på den måde, markedet er strikket sammen på. Det har fungeret rigtig godt de sidste tyve år, siden elmarkedet blev liberaliseret. Det gør det bare ikke nu, hvor prisen på gas er eksploderet, og selvom vi tjener mere, skal vi jo netop også betale mere for den energi, der købes til kunderne. Det går desværre også udover de bornholmske kunder, fordi hele Europa er bundet sammen på energiområdet.

Det er som sagt kompliceret at pille ved, og det, der er den politiske frygt, er jo, at man stadig gerne vil have, at der er strøm nok og incitament til at investere i mere vedvarende energi. Så man skal sikre, at man både sikrer forsyningssikkerhed, den grønne omstilling og en lavere pris.


PÅ JAGT EFTER ENERGITYVE

Claus Andersen forstår godt de bornholmske kunder, der er bekymrede.

- Jeg er selv kæmpebekymret. Jeg har en elbil og jordvarme, og jeg skal ikke pive, for jeg er heldigere stillet end så mange andre.

Men prisstigningerne rammer alle husholdninger.

Og jeg forstår 100 procent, at man som forbruger synes, at det her er voldsomt. Vi skal vel 50 år tilbage for at have været i en lignende energikrise. Man kan vende det om og sige, at det er fedt, at vi nu har haft 50 år, hvor der faktisk har været relativ stabilitet på energimarkedet. Men jeg kan sagtens forstå, at forbrugerne nu er bekymrede, for det rammer alle husholdninger.

Og vi gør, hvad vi kan for at hjælpe de trængte kunder. Vi kan ikke sætte priserne ned lige nu, men vi kan for eksempel hjælpe med afdragsordninger. For når vores kunder lider, så lider vi også. Derfor kæmper vi også for at få ændret markedsdesignet, så vi får en så fair prissætning som muligt.

Hvad er så dit bedste råd til at komme helskindet gennem krisen? - Den bedste energi er jo den, vi ikke bruger.

Så den allerbedste måde at spare penge på er at bruge mindre. Derfor er der rigtig meget fokus på de her spareråd om at skifte til sparepærer, skrue ned for varmen osv. På vores hjemmeside har vi 20 konkrete spareråd.

Vi har også været ude med vores blå campingvogn for at møde de bornholmske forbrugere med sparetips.

I medierne har der været talt meget om, at folk nærmest må stå op om natten for at vaske tøj, men de fleste kunder på Bornholm har faktisk en fastprisaftale, så strømmen koster det samme døgnet rundt, bortset fra i tidsrummet 17-20, hvor strømmer koster mere i transport i vinterhalvåret.

Men for nogle - især med elbil - kan det betale sig at skifte til en ordning, hvor man kan lade op, når strømmen er billigst, og det rådgiver Beof også gerne med, hvis man ringer ind til dem, forklarer direktøren og tilføjer: - Men uanset hvilken model man er på, giver det en kæmpeforskel, om man bruger sparepærer og husker at slukke for sine standby-forbrug, så sluk for tingene, når du går i seng.

Hvad gør I selv for at spare på energien? - Det er godt spørgsmål, for vi bruger også meget strøm her i virksomheden, og der har vi igangsat tiltag for at finde energityvene, så vi prøver også at gribe nogle af de lavthængende frugter ved at slukke for den strøm, vi ikke bruger, og begrænse udslippene fra trykpumperne osv.

GRØN OMSTILLING KAN REDDE PRISER Direktøren tøver, før han svarer på, hvor lang tid energikrisen vil vare.

- Det er svært at svare på. Markedets forventning er desværre, at der vil ske en yderligere stigning, det er derfor, at regeringen vil give en mulighed for at skubbe en del af sin energiregning, nedsætte elafgiften og give en større børnecheck til børnefamilierne i det nye år, hvor forventningen også er, at priserne vil stige i første kvartal. Så tror jeg, at priserne vil stabilisere sig til et nyt normalniveau, der nok desværre er noget højere, end det vi tidligere har været vant til. For halvandet år siden var den rå elpris cirka 35 øre pr kilowatttime, og i 4.

kvartal er den rå elpris over 3,5 kroner, så det er faktisk en tidobling. Og jeg tror desværre, at der vil gå lang tid, før vi kommer ned på 35 øre pr. kilowatttime igen, siger han med et lille suk.

- Jeg tror, at gaskrisen vil være langvarig.

For jeg tror ikke, at den konflikt vil blive løst med det samme, så det er vildt, hvilke konsekvenser Putins beslutninger har haft. Det viser på godt og ondt, hvor meget verden hænger sammen. Og det vi skal være fokuserede på de kommende år er at blive så uafhængige af Putins gas som muligt. Er der andre muligheder for at få gas, så skal vi finde de produktionsmetoder, og der er heller ingen tvivl om, at krisen sætter tempo på den grønne omstilling. Det er der jo stort politisk fokus på lige nu.

Det vil vel også gøre det billigere på sigt? - Ja, det vil det gøre, siger han og lyser op i et smil.

- På sigt vil vi komme tilbage til noget, som vi kender historisk. Jeg tror bare personligt, at det vil tage noget tid, så vi i mellemtiden får en ny balance, hvor gas stadig er en del af ligningen, men vil fylde mindre.

Og det bliver måske et niveau mellem det, vi kender, og det vi kommer til at opleve i vinter, og på den lange bane vil de initiativer med massiv udbygning af vedvarende energi nok være med til at drive prisen ned, men det tager pt. syv-otte år, fra man sætter i gang med en vindmøllepark, til man kan tage den i brug, og samtidig bruger vi også alle sammen mere strøm med flere elbiler osv.

Men de næste år skal vi vænne os til at bruge flere penge på el og varme? - Ja, vi skal vænne os til at bruge flere penge på især el, og de steder, hvor man har gas, også varme, men jeg tror, at vi finder et nyt normal, hvor det ikke er plus 3,5 krone, men måske plus halvanden krone i forhold til, hvad vi er vant til og kendte til for halvandet år siden.


ÅBENHED SOM VÆRDI

Som direktør for Beof har han samtidig forsøgt at åbne virksomheden mere mod samfundet og forbrugerne.

- Åbenhed og transparens er personligt vigtigt for mig, og det er også noget af det, jeg gerne vil påvirke selskabet til. Så jeg synes, at der er en fin rød tråd i min ledelsesstil og det, jeg gerne vil med virksomheden.

Jeg tror, at vi har haft en historik, hvor vi i hvert fald for nogens vedkommende er blevet set på, som om vi lukker os lidt omkring os selv, men jeg vil rigtig gerne have, at vi åbner os ud mod vores omverden, kunder og omkringliggende samfund. Jeg tror meget på, at åbenhed og dialog er vejen frem, og så handler det dybest set om at give folk ansvar og mulighed for at påvirke deres egen hverdag. Det tror jeg grundlæggende, at vi er rigtig mange, der trives med.

Hvad er højdepunkterne i din egen tid i virksomheden? - Det var også et svært spørgsmål. Jeg synes, at der var et højdepunkt i salget af Elnet-Øst, som vi fik gennemført sidste år.

Nogen vil synes, at det ikke var et højdepunkt, fordi vi sagde farvel til en del af virksomheden, som var en stor del af vores identitet og havde været på bornholmske hænder i mange år, men grunden til, at jeg synes, at det er en succes er, at jeg synes, at de 18 medarbejdere, som vi sagde farvel til der, er kommet over i et fagligt fællesskab, så de simpelthen har fået nogle flere kollegaer at sparre med rent teknisk. Og det bornholmske elnet har fået nogle investorer, der har mulighed for at investere i det elnet, som vi som selskab ikke ville have haft muligheden for. Det kan man bare se på deres udbygningsplan for 1,3 milliarder kroner indenfor de næste ti år. Det ville vi ikke haft mulighed for at løfte, så det er også godt for Bornholm. Og så har det givet Beof muligheden for at afvikle en rigtig træls gæld, vi slæbte rundt på siden et udbyttelån i 2008, så vi fik en ny økonomisk mulighed for at kunne investere i fremtiden og skabe vækst og udvikling for Bornholm, siger han og smiler igen.

- Jeg synes virkelig, at det har været en win-win-win, der også markerede et vendepunkt for virksomheden, så vi kunne gå fra at rydde op i økonomien måned for måned til rent faktisk at udvikle og skabe. Og på ryggen af det har vi også fået en ny 2030-strategi, som vi fik vedtaget i december sidste år, og det synes jeg har været en superfed proces med både medarbejdere og bestyrelse, så det har også givet virksomheden en retning og nogle visioner for fremtiden, så vi kan være med til at forklare os selv og vores omverden, hvor vi gerne vil hen.

Hvor vil I så gerne hen? - Vi vil gerne skabe så billig, grøn og driftssikker energi som muligt. Et af hovedfokuspointerne er derfor fortsat at bidrage til den grønne omstilling, mens vi fortsat balancerer det med hensynet til økonomi og driftssikkerhed. Vi har fem forsyningsarter vand, spildevand, varme, elproduktion og elhandel, så der er selvfølgelig en strategi for, hvordan vi vil udvikle de fem områder, men så er der også et koncernspor om, hvad det er, vi kan mere end det. Fællestrækket er, at vi gerne vil fortsætte ad den grønne omstilling og få det understøttet mest muligt i alle vores forsyningsarter. Vi vil også gerne have mere åbenhed, som jeg talte om før. Og vi vil gerne blive set som dem, der leverer svarene på energi-og forsyningsområdet, så vi kan facilitere vores kunders grønne valg.

Det vil vi gerne have en mere aktiv rolle i, så vi kan hjælpe kunderne til at træffe grønne valg. Vi vil gerne skabe vækst og udvikling på Bornholm, så vi vil gerne være med til at skabe synergier på Bornholm, så vi netop via samarbejder kan gribe flere muligheder.

Hvad er det sværeste for jer lige nu? - At bibeholde fokusset på den grønne omstilling og alt det gode, vi vil der, samtidig med, at der er noget, der brænder lige her og nu. Man er nødt til at få slukket ildebranden, men man er også nødt til at komme videre med den grønne omstilling.

Fordi den også er med til at slukke ildebranden? - Præcis. På den lange bane. Så der er nogle greb vi skal tage på den lange bane samtidig med, at der er noget, vi skal have løst nu og her.

Jeg landede 1. januar sidste år. Så jeg er rimelig ny på både Bornholm og i den her branche, som nogen sagde var støvet og andre sagde var lavinteresse.

Claus Andersen Direktør for Bornholms Energi & Forsyning Jeg er selv kæmpebekymret.

Jeg har en elbil og jordvarme, og jeg skal ikke pive, for jeg er heldigere stillet end så mange andre.

Claus Andersen Direktør for Bornholms Energi & Forsyning .

Title: Bornholmernes valgkamp er blevet mere lokal: ' Der er sket en stor forandring'
Content:
The election campaign at Bornholm has this time been marked by much of the local challenges and concerns. Also more than experienced in previous parliamentary elections, believes the two Bornholm MPs, Lea Wermelin (S) and Peter Juel-Jensen (V).

The local challenges and themes are filling more and more in the Bornholm election campaign.

Compared to previous parliamentary elections, this time there is greater interest and concern about the things that directly affect Bornholm. At least if you ask Bornholm's two current MPs, Lea Wermelin and Peter Juel-Jensen about how they have experienced their election campaign going in the final phase.

- I think there is a great focus on the Bornholm themes. Energy island, defense and inflation are very much filling. Of course, the usual things are filling up, but if I think back to the other times I have been set up, then I actually think the local topics are filling more this time, says Left's top candidate Peter Juel-Jensen to the Journal.

The same experience has the Ditto of Social Democracy, Lea Wermelin, who believes that many of the national issues that are being discussed on the political scene also become local politics very quickly.

- Of course, people take out exit in their own everyday life, which is local, but it is also related to the national framework that is. This can be seen, among other things, with the defense policy, where tensions have increased with the war in Ukraine and most recently with the blasts in the Baltic Sea. When that happens, strengthening the defense compared to the Baltic Sea also becomes a local question, says Lea Wermelin.

She notices a significant change since she first lined up in 2015, where there is far more focus on the fact that national responsibility, which consists of providing a Denmark in balance.

- There is a huge difference between that time and until now. I find that all parties relate to a Denmark in better balance. Then you may think the answers are more or less good, but I think there has been a big change there, says the Social Democracy's top candidate.


Greater crisis awareness on Bornholm

With the current energy crisis and the financial consequences that come with the crisis, there is a much greater nervousness and concern for the individual citizen, the two members of parliament believe.

This is also very much true on Bornholm, where you have previously experienced how a crisis can hit harder locally than it may be in the larger cities.

- At Bornholm we realize that when we look into something that looks like a black hole, and it hits, it takes significantly longer before we get out on the other side. You could also see that with the financial crisis.

You have a greater opportunity to maintain your way of life in the larger cities, where you live a little closer together, says Peter Juel-Jensen.

He believes that there is a greater crisis awareness in Bornholm than there are many other places.

- It is a Bornholm experience and also a general experience in rural areas that when the crisis first hits, it bites harder out there. Some of the things that were a little easier for us before are getting harder now, and I think the Bornholmers are aware of, says Left's top candidate.

It is also one of the reasons why inflation and the general social economy fill a lot in the election campaign and in general in the Bornholm consciousness, explains Lea Wermelin.

- Part of my criticism, after the financial crisis, was that the bill was geographically skewed. There were several at Bornholm who lost their work during the financial crisis and subsequently had a harder time getting a job again. Therefore, it is important to me that we on top of the corona crisis and the current energy crisis say very clearly that we must help those who are most squeezed and that we must continue to have a Denmark that is connected, she says.

Politics rather than letter combinations The upcoming parliamentary elections is one of the more unforeseen of its kind, where there are more parties and prime ministerial candidates than has been seen in the previous elections.

And while first and foremost one would like to discuss local issues, there is ultimately a government to form and a prime minister to be appointed. But the questioning of who one or the other party points to as prime minister and whether a government can be formed at all does not fill up as much with the voters that Lea Wermelin has spoken to his election campaign.

- There are many who would like to speak politics, and I think it is primarily about what we are going for election on and you are less concerned with this with letter combinations and what happens if one or the other. I find that many voters say they do not bother that it will be shouting and the scream in the election campaign, but that they actually want to listen to politics. And I think we succeeded very well on Bornholm, says Lea Wermelin.

Peter Juel-Jensen, according to his own statement, has not given it a thought at all how a future government may look. And it is also not his feeling that the Bornholm voters focus solely on how the solitude goes up.

- I haven't hit so much into that person gallery, where it's about one or the other becoming prime minister. People would rather talk about the Bornholm solutions and challenges, he says and continues: - I think the Bornholmers are most concerned that no matter how the voices fall out, we have an opportunity to get some attention going forward.

And that's important because we still have some issues we have to address, says Peter Juel-Jensen.

Inflation and the general social economy fill a lot in the election campaign and in general in the Bornholm consciousness Lea Wermelin I think there is a great focus on the Bornholm themes.

Energy island, defense and inflation are very much filling.

Title: Den vigtige grønne omstilling
Content:
It must be made particularly attractive to install renewable energy solutions for existing households and in small energy pools between neighbors.

The green transition is a reality that everyone is going to arrange. However, the question of when and how is left. I think it is our responsibility to take hold now and even control it, instead of ending up in a situation where we are forced to act urgently, and maybe even too late.

The war in Ukraine has shown us the weaknesses of the addiction of the fossil forms of energy, and put light on the persistent that can make a big difference to us already in our immediate future.

It must be clear to most people that the time has come to make the shift in the way in which society, locally and globally, is arranged.


A sustainable society

I will fight for a Denmark where we recycle resources to a much greater extent, and do not build walls to protect what we very romantically know so well. For many years, through my work as a refrigeration technician in the country's supermarkets, I have seen how easy it is, with all due respect, to utilize, for example, the surplus heat in established installations in the company. It is an example of simple and easily accessible solutions already exist. And now that it is possible to do just that, without high taxes, we must make sure to pick the low -hanging fruits.

Here at Bornholm, and in the rest of the country, it must be made particularly attractive to install renewable energy solutions for existing households and in small energy pools between neighbors.

We are knowledgeable people and can easily make sure to use the energy when nature delivers it. There are timers built into many of our household products and heat sources, and thus we can make sure to use the energy when available.

And with a rapid development in storage, we can have enough available energy at the times when nature cannot deliver it.

Sustainable and renewable energy solutions must be set for key and renewable energy solutions when we build.

There must be a change and development of our agriculture, where plant -based products and ecology replaces conventional animal production with a better public health.

Solutions must be found to the excessive private motoring through a better public transport sector and sharing carism.

And the Danes must, big and small, understand the need for our consumption to be cut down.


Energiø Bornholm

Not everyone has the opportunity to install renewable energy in their homes or in a smaller company - therefore we must also work together on the task. There are the already concluded agreements on energy islands, the right way to go for new wide solutions.

In addition, the exciting power-to-technology, which in the long term can replace gas, oil and coal and supplement the renewable energy from sun and wind.

From a Bornholm perspective, it is especially important to utilize the financial framework for the project, to provide a boost of the service level on Bornholm.

In the election debates, there is a great deal of agreement between the parties that the energy island is a gift for Bornholm. So it is now that the Lands and municipal politicians have to smack their sleeves and together stand for the necessary improvements in eg. a. The Bornholm housing situation, which may be the basis for utilizing the upcoming billion -dollar investment.

It is also imperative to close the gaps in the legislation so that we can secure the residents who will be affected by the location of the work as soon as possible, and with a compensation that respects the victim they are required.

It will place great demands on the state and the citizens to create the changes, but together we can find the courage and the will.

And remember that a voice on me and the alternative is the voice that makes all other parties a little greener.

Title: Nexø gør klar til vindeventyr
Content:
Nexø Harbor's management has met with Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners, and the harbor may be intended for a key role as a service port if the wind farms east of Bornholm come true.

If offshore wind farms are to be erected east of Bornholm, it will probably create activity at Nexø Harbor. This view has also been given this view, Nexø Harbor Chairman of the Board, Bjarne Hartung Kirkegaard, after he met in September with Copenhagen Infrastructrue Partners (CIP), who has now entered into a partnership with Ørsted on the two proposed wind parks east and southeast of Bornholm.

-I have to say it was an eye-opener to have a visit from the people from CIP, and when I talk to professionals, they also say that it is interesting, says the chairman with reference to CIP's plans for floating offshore wind turbines and power-to-x- Production on Bornholm soil.

When the Journal visited CIP's headquarters in Copenhagen a few weeks ago, CEO Magnus Brogaard Larsen mentioned that CIP is in dialogue with Nexø Harbor about operational and maintenance activities with a 35-year perspective.

The port's management would like to enter into a collaboration and make areas or buildings available to the energy companies in the southern part of the port area. CIP has plans to build a new service building, says Bjarne Hartung Kirkegaard.

- At the meeting they said, "We need to spend so and so big an area," and then I look at the director.

"We can do that". Then they say that it may be, it gets bigger. Fine, we can do that too, says the chairman.

He emphasizes that the southern part of the harbor has a good mix around the lift and shipyard facilities.

- There are a few areas we can use to make a service building for them, and there are quay areas and sufficient depth for their boats to go in. We are ready to welcome the service boats, and we think we can offer it on land they need, says the port chairman, who feels that the CIP delegation was happy about what they heard in Nexø.

- They nodded, and then they had a checkbox more about some of that is a prerequisite for them to do what they want to go out on the water.

Bjarne Hartung Kirkegaard emphasizes that Nexø Harbor will not have the same function as Rønne Harbor, where the shipping of wind turbine parts to many of the projects in the Baltic Sea takes place from.

- We cannot, like Rønne Harbor, have the big mill towers and the kind of lying around. Not at all. But as a service port, it will fit perfectly.

We also have a lift, so if the boats need to be inspired and serviced, it can also be done.

The function as a service port is attractive to local employment, as these are enduring workplaces. The Kriegers Flak Park, which with 0.6 Gigawatt is somewhat smaller than the proposed offshore wind farms of 2 x 1.5 Gigawatt east of Bornholm, are served, for example, from Klintholm Harbor on Møn. Workplaces have been established for about 50 people in Klintholm, Vattenfall's service manager said last year when many Bornholmers sailed out with Povl Anker to see Kriegers Flak from the nearest team.

Allan Funch Kofod from Jobcenter Bornholm's Business Service lists in an article written for the project "Ready for Energiø Bornholm" The commercial opportunities that arise if Bornholm ports can attract service and operational tasks.

- In the long term, hopefully, we will also look into the fact that Bornholm will be service island on the operation of the wind farms, and many different professional groups may be needed, such as electricians, wind turbine technicians, mechanics, plumbing, blacksmiths, shipmates, ship assistants, warehouse personnel, administration With more, says Allan Funch Kofod.

These perspectives arouse joy in Nexø, where the chairman of the Business Association Østbornholm, Carsten Aalling, has high hopes.

- Rønne Harbor has fantastic areas for shipping, but Nexø Harbor can handle the service part with maintenance and the daily operation of these giant parks. I hope that the board of Nexø Harbor is working hard to make himself interesting, says Carsten Aalling to the Journal.

The President of the Port emphasizes that he sees very positively on the wind turbine plans from CIP and Ørsted.

- The other day there was someone who would build homes in Nexø Harbor out on the water. There is no room for that, so we had to say nicely no thanks.

Many people are interested in Nexø Harbor, but one of the things that will really give development is CIP, says Bjarne Hartung Kirkegaard - before it became clear that Ørsted had joined the projects.

He also mentions that Bornholm's offshore wind is also considering putting a somewhat smaller wind farm of 100 megawatts up near Nexø.

- The local offshore wind farm will also be able to use Nexø Harbor. So we see for us that Nexø Harbor will play a role with what will happen to wind energy in the Baltic Sea in the future, says Bjarne Hartung Kirkegaard, who also looks positively at the possibility that the offshore wind farms can supply energy to a Bornholm bunker Hub project on green ship fuel that Rønne Harbor is heavily involved in at the meeting with the CIP representatives Did he not get a clear view of where at Bornholm CIP is considering building a possible electrolysis plant. It has not been the case that such a power-to-X plant that can use large quantities of wind power to produce hydrogen must be at the harbor, says the chairman. He points out that it remains unclear how the wind farms should be connected to the electricity grid and how the energy is moving out into the world. During the meeting in Nexø, CIP aired thoughts of utilizing existing pipelines in the Baltic Sea to transport hydrogen or fuels to Germany, but it was before that some blasted holes in the Nordstream tubes. These considerations of cable or pipe connections to transport the energy away from Bornholm do not initially relate to the Bornholm politicians, according to Bjarne Hartung Kirkegaard, who sits on the municipal council and stands for the parliamentary elections for the Christian Democrats.

- It's something that those who have the money investing must think about. It is not something we at Bornholm can decide, but we can rejoice that Bornholm is a place where we can become part of that development.

Both for Nexø Harbor and Bornholm the wind is fantastic. There is a lot more of it coming and we will need it all.

Title: Der blæser nye vinde over Bornholm
Content:
Ørsted and Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners have a project that can create activity in the ports in both Nexø and Rønne.

It seems that Ørsted has thrown his love on Bornholm.

It was the big energy company that was first out with the idea of ​​making Bornholm an energy island, and it is now also the ones who together with the Copenhagen investment company Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners will take the Baltic Sea wind energy to new heights.

From the inside, the most recently published visions are extremely exciting, and as something new, they seriously link the Nexø edge of the dreams of the offshore wind of the Baltic.

After the collapse of fishing, Nexø has for years had to fight a bit with creating life around the harbor, but lately entrepreneurs have taken the clock and shown that the city is on its way to a new era.

The creator urge lives at its best, and that in the future Nexø Harbor may also become a service island of not just one but two offshore wind farms off the coast, it is exciting new for the area.

The harbor has met with Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners, and Chairman of the Board Bjarne Hartung Kirkegaard (KD) could yesterday tell the Journal that the meeting was an eye opener.

- At the meeting they said, "We need to spend so and so big an area," and then I look at the director. "We can do that". Then they say that it may be, it gets bigger. Fine, we can do that too.

The director at Nexø Harbor is called Carsten Andersen, and he is thus completely ready for the work that can lie and wait around the corner, one must understand.

The fact that there are certain restrictions in the area available to the port is a matter of course, but there is Rønne Harbor and the expansion that the port has long been underway into the picture.

Rønne Harbor has become experts in the offshore industry in record time and of course are also ready to go if the two offshore wind farms east of Bornholm are also ready.

In other words, Ørsted and Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners are a partnership that can be of great importance to Bornholm's two largest ports, and it can thus be the continuation of an adventure that is already well underway.

It seems that Ørsted has thrown his love on Bornholm.

Title: Kommunalbestyrelsen tøvede med at støtte CIP og Ørsteds fulde plan om power-to-X
Content:
In a new consultation response, the municipal council emphasizes that by supporting energy companies' desire to explore the possibility of two large offshore wind farms, they do not decide on Powerto-X systems. René Danielsson (DF) thinks it was wrong to make this reservation, which according to the Unity List's Helle Munk Ravnborg is about a chemical industry with large water consumption, which should be thoroughly debated in the local community.

This week Ørsted jumped on Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners' (CIP) Two wind turbine projects east of Bornholm.

In total, the wind turbines, half of which in the visions must stand on floating foundations, can reach the same capacity as Energiø Bornholm, if the plans for two parks of 1.5 gigawatts are realized. The purpose of the huge energy projects is largely - as CIP told in the Journal last week - to produce hydrogen and the green fuels of the future. That vision shares Ørsted, the press release said, which was released on the collaboration on Tuesday morning.

- Denmark has been a pioneer in the offshore wind industry and is a leader in the green transition. The four major open door projects can help cement Denmark's continued leadership position and create the foundation for kickstarting the next phase of a Danish business adventure in the production of green hydrogen and green fuels, said regional director Rasmus Errboe from Ørsted.

However, the ambitions of power-to-X production at a Bornholm electrolysis plant within five to six years are not received exclusively with enthusiasm in the municipal council. The Unity List's Helle Munk Ravnborg sat as a person for the Nature, Environment and Plan Committee on the board when representatives from CIP attended meeting with Mayor Jacob Trøst (K) in September. It was at this meeting that it became clear to the politicians that hydrogen or fuel production is so central to the wind turbine project.

In CIP's application to the Danish Energy Agency, on the other hand, there was not much focus on the form of electricity when it has to leave Bornholm.

- We cannot read much about what is going to happen to the power in the application, and I asked that. I am surprised that with such competent people you are presented with a material that is so silent about what the power is to be used for, says Helle Munk Ravnborg to the Journal of the meeting with CIP.


Narrow position

Based on the information, the Unity List suggested to add a section to the consultation response to which the municipality's administration had made a presentation. The section states that "with this consultation response only has been decided on the two outlined offshore wind turbine projects - and not to any derived options of this, such as land -based establishment of PTX plants or other".

There were several reasons to add this reservation, says Helle Munk Ravnborg. An electrolysis system will require large amounts of water which can be split by means of electrolysis to achieve hydrogen.

- You have to get ready what type of water to use. It cannot be groundwater, because it will empty our reserves.

So either seawater or wastewater must be used, says Helle Munk Ravnborg.

She points out that the Bornholmers and the local businesses in the coming years will endeavor to emit less water into the wastewater plants and instead withhold more surface and drainage water in the open country.

- It will hopefully reduce the total amount of wastewater. Today, it is true that the wastewater plants receive about twice as much water as what is delivered from the Bornholm waterworks, says Helle Munk Ravnborg.

This water situation should be in mind when considering power-to-X-production on Bornholm soil, the Unity List believes.

- Whether seawater or wastewater will be used, a cost of purification or desalination will probably have to be expected, says Helle Munk Ravnborg emphasizes that if there is a disposal of seawater, this process is also energy -intensive.

For the Unity List, there is also the question of whether Bornholm is the right place to produce hydrogen, ammonia or other fuels of the future, which will go to a green conversion of the transport sector.

- At some point we have to decide whether we would like to develop such a chemical industry on Bornholm? What are the advantages and disadvantages of it. Both environmentally and in relation to other business opportunities - both existing and new professions.

Here you are thinking of tourism in particular, or what? - Yes, I think about the tourist industry. To some extent, one could also imagine a competition with agriculture on the consumption of water, which is a very scarce resource on Bornholm.

There are also many business benefits.

Local production of Power-to-X can play with the plans for a bunker hub at Rønne Harbor? - That's right. And there we are waiting, among other things, to see the results of the work that Rønne Harbor is currently doing, says Helle Munk Ravnborg, who points out that "ammonia is something toxic city".


DF-Wand over electricity

At the municipal council meeting, the changed consultation response was adopted by a broad majority. The Danish People's Party and the Christian Democrats voted against, and DF's opposition to the wording is due to the reservations against Power-to-X on Bornholm soil, says René Danielsson (DF).

- Should we be green or not to be green? Every time it comes to something, the Unity List has all sorts of objections, says the DF and emphasizes his own party's line.

-We have no problem with Power-to-X. We basically think it is a really good idea and we would like to think that Nexø could become an important city in the green development.

When the four DFs in the municipal council did not want to signal skepticism to the same extent as the majority, it was about both the green transition and Bornholm's future development opportunities.

- For us, it's also about the business part. We we all like the island to grow so we can get more jobs and become some more people - and now the opportunity is there, says René Danielsson, who finds it striking that the consultation responses about the energy island did not contain sentences with the same kind of reservations.

Helle Munk Ravnborg emphasizes that a similar phrase not to decide on Power-to-X plants was part of the consultation response when the municipal council in May gave support to the Danish Energy Agency's plans for increased mill density to Energiø Bornholm.


Requires extra power

The unit list's pending attitude towards the green fuels is also linked to the significant energy loss associated with the production of hydrogen by electrolysis and the next steps that refine hydrogen to methanol, ammonia or something third. The alternative is to use the power directly and prioritize the development of batteries and the electrification of the transport where it is technically possible.

- On the larger socio -economic level, I think it is important to look at energy efficiency and where we get the most money. It will then be silly to have to set up three times as many mills to service a hydrogen -based fuel industry.

If we can get the same movement in our society with a third of the mills and direct electrification, says Helle Munk Ravnborg.

Title: Peter Juel om energiø: Kommunalpolitikere har været for passive

At the same time, Christiansborg can have an influence on other energy projects in the Baltic Sea, which can utilize Bornholm's geographical location and new role as an electric hub.

An example is CIP and Ørsted's proposed wind parks east of Bornholm and the idea of ​​using the flow from there to produce hydrogen and green fuels-perhaps at a Bornholm Power-to-X plant.

Five km closer to without resistance

If the municipal council had a fixed position with requirements, would you then get a better position to influence the Left's line? - Bornholm always comes the longest when we talk to one vote, says the Left candidate.

- I do not have a mandate to stepped down the brake and also do not have the opportunity, because I am only one in 179.

Threat to tourism

This means increasing municipal costs, because of course we have to help those who have a need, says Peter Juel-Jensen.

That is why I am talking about education, research and committed communities with Bornholm companies - but also about the whole Bornholm community having a carrot in it.

As examples of possible carrots, he mentions guarantees of more educational places and binding cooperation with knowledge institutions. It could also be a promise of traveling archaeologists, so the Bornholm Museum does not have to send all men to Sydbornholm for months, thereby missing people for tasks at the rest of Bornholm, which Peter Juel-Jensen fears can slow down other construction projects.

He also suggests that Energinet must invest in a building that fits into the surroundings and is hidden in the landscape, "so that the land plant on South Bornholm becomes not as large an eye bay" as he puts it. Fund and Home Aid

Title: Energiøen er præget af hastværk
Content:
Dear Peter Juel-Jensen, Thank you for your remarks in Bornholm's Journal the other day, where you objected that Bornholm gets too little out of providing valuable land and resources to one of Denmark's historically largest construction projects. I share your concern.

As we know, the citizens and the municipal council have had a number of meetings with the Energy Network, the Danish Energy Agency and other government agencies, prior to the adoption of the energy island and the decision to build land facilities south of Aakirkeby.

My short summary of the experience is that we experience it to some extent as a process that is controlled and determined by technocrats from the top.

We local politicians and officials are probably somewhat benevolent on the size of the project and the prospect of workplaces so that we do not receive sufficient consideration or assistance for planning and requirements for design.

Thus, the message from Energinet is that the municipality must carry out planning work, hearings, mayor meetings, within the municipality's own budget. As you know, our economy is already terribly pressured. In answers to proposed savings catalog, our technical department writes as follows: Energiø Bornholm opens up a wide range of fantastic opportunities for the island's future energy and heat supply. In order to exploit this potential, the area is needed. With the government's proposal "Denmark, more II" from April 2022 can be expected a number of large on extensive tasks in energy and heat planning in the years 2022 to 2028. There are very few resources allocated for planning and case management in the area of ​​heat, which becomes completely inadequate in it upcoming complex and extensive work in the field. There are no management information available for this area, but it is estimated that, on the basis of the upcoming tasks, half a year is needed further in the field.

With the prospect of the construction of even greater scope and complexity, the challenge of our administration's technical department will only increase. In other words, there is a need for the state to allocate funds to extra man -years, which can be dedicated to the energy island's many planning tasks.

Likewise, Energinet announces that there are no state funds or time to hold an international architectural competition for the design of the large technical facility, which may fill more than 90 hectares. In this connection, it can be mentioned that the Academy Council has continuously called on both the Ministry of Culture and the Ministry of Culture and the Ministry of Supply to take greater responsibility for the aesthetic and cultural protection and the exploitation of the open country. Just as the Unity List Søren Egge has asked the Minister of Energy to allocate resources to plan a proper architectural quality for the technical facilities. Apparently without effect.

Regarding the National Center for Renewable Energy, I also find that there is a very strong focus on technocratic projects. And I call for a social science element in the research projects.

One should examine the rollout and implementation of a "green" project's effect on the local community, and involve sociologists, anthropologists and other humanistic research fields in the center's pallet.

What does a project of this size mean for citizens' ownership and self -understanding, experience of democratic co -influence and how does one avoid a not in my backyard situation that leads to reluctance and opposition? It would be an advantage for the national center if, for example, you could include researchers or students from KU, SDU or RUC in the research composition, and this insight could be marketed internationally.

On the whole, the process so far is characterized by great haste and lack of reflection.

The rushed export of the project and a headless establishment of a large technical facility, which together with the expansion of Rønne Harbor, connection of various followers, and large technical areas at sea, will potentially have fatal and irreparable effects on the entire southern Bornholm coast.

Title: Vigtigt at du stemmer til Ewiis repræsentantskab

The establishment of Energiø Bornholm provides both challenges and opportunities for us. We must be active participants in the development of the energy island and utilize the direct benefits that the energy island gives us in the form of security of supply and access to green power.

Title: Energinet vil høre dine ideer til energiøen
Content:
The Danish Environmental Protection Agency has initiated an environmental assessment of Energiø Bornholm's upcoming converter station and electric cables. A civic meeting will also be held.

If you have an attitude about what a report on the environmental consequences of Energiø Bornholm's plant should contain, you now have the chance to speak. The Danish Environmental Protection Agency has embarked on an initial consultation phase and encourages all interested parties to come up with ideas and suggestions for the content of the environmental impact report for the project. This is stated on the Board's website.

Up to December 5, Bornholmers and other interested parties can send consultation responses to the facilities to Energiø Bornholm. Here on the island it includes the upcoming converter station south of Aakirkeby and the electricity cables, which will connect the station to the Zealand electricity grid.

- We are pleased that the Danish Environmental Protection Agency is now beginning the environmental impact assessment of the electricity plants on Bornholm and Zealand and the cable between the two stations. It is the first important step towards the environmental permit that is the prerequisite for the project. We hope that all interested parties will use the consultation period to send their ideas and suggestions to the Danish Environmental Protection Agency, so that we get the best possible basis for the environmental impact assessment, says Deputy Director Marian Kaagh in Energinet on the regional municipality's website.

It is Energinet who wants to establish the plant and has therefore asked the Danish Environmental Protection Agency to initiate an environmental assessment process for the project.


Citizens' Meeting

As part of the initial consultation, Energinet also holds a civic meeting where all interested parties can hear more about the project, the plans for the station and the cables as well as the environmental impact assessment itself.

There will also be the opportunity to ask questions and talk to employees from the Danish Environmental Protection Agency, the Danish Energy Agency, the regional municipality and the Energinet about everything from nature and the environment to agreements and compensation.

- We know that we come with a large plant that will fill the landscape. Therefore, it is important that all suggestions and comments from the citizens come up so that we can make the best possible plant. We are still early in the process and many things are not yet clarified, but we are very much looking forward to meeting the Bornholmers and talking about our plans for the project and the station at Bornholm, says Marian Kaagh.

She adds that it is important for Energinet to dress people up so that they can help influence the project with consultation responses to the environmental impact assessment.

- So we hope to see many Bornholmers for the Citizens' Meeting, says Energinet's Deputy Director.

The Citizens' Meeting will take place in the Aakirkebyhallerne on November 22 at 6.30 pm. It is open to everyone and there is no registration.

Work on the environmental impact report is expected to be completed by the beginning of 2024, after which it and a draft environmental permit are sent for consultation. After eight weeks of consultation, the consultation responses are processed before the Danish Environmental Protection Agency is scheduled to issue an environmental permit for the project in mid -2024.

Title: Kæmpe EU-støtte: Fremtiden rykker ind på kraftværk i Rønne
Content:
Bornholm's Energi & Forsyning is part of a project for DKK 100 million, which will show how to store green energy from sun and wind for later use in the electric and district heating dishes.

Andersen in Beof - Bornholm Energi & Forsyning, which adds buildings for the project.

Andersen in the press release.


Project should answer questions

The idea behind Second Life for Powerplants is to reuse the original technology of the power plants and build on the employees' competencies.

The project will develop a concept that dresses the power plant in order to be able to supply electricity and district heating to the Bornholm consumers and balance the electricity grid solely on sun and wind.

The work is given a salt storage, used electric car batteries and a high-tech flywheel battery, there are three different technologies that should make it possible to store green energy for later.

- The supply of the future must be robust, sustainable and to pay.

DKK 60 million from the EU BEOF director believes that the project will provide invaluable knowledge of how to handle and save sun and wind in the future, and how to effectively ensure balance in the electricity system.

We will have clear indications of what it takes of investment so that we can finally say goodbye to the oil and defeat the tile, says Claus M. Andersen.

The project is finally awaiting formal approval from the European Commission, but the expectation is that it can begin before the New Year. It is expected to last for three and a half years. There is a total budget of DKK 100 million, of which DKK 60 million comes the EU.

BEOF has also invested in the project.

There is no doubt to me that Second Life for Powerplants will be one of the most important stepping stones on the way to the supply of the future If we are to harvest the fruits of the new amounts of sun and wind, we need to answer a wide range of questions.

Second Life for Powerplants will give us a wide range of the answers we need.


The three technologies

By base the energy storage at Rønne Harbor on three different technologies, costs are reduced and the system becomes flexible and robust.

? The salmon reactor is cheap, compact, scalable and works with a higher energy density than other salts. The temperature can reach 700 degrees. The active ingredient of the salt reactor of the caustic soda.

? A FlyWheel is a magnetic flywheel that many may know from mopeds, motorcycles and cars. The flywheel turns around, creates magnetic tension and makes power. The technology comes from the airline industry. The specific flywheel hovers, has no shafts and works completely without friction. It gives very high speeds and the higher the speed, the more power can be stored. The technology promises long life, get operating expenses and stable operation. FlyWheel is the most expensive part of the energy storage, but necessary when storing large amounts of power quickly or when the electricity grid needs to be supplied with large amounts of power.

Title: Trøst imødegår kritik: Vi vil gerne fortælle om det, vi ved skal ske

Jacob Consolation and the person of the Nature, Environment and Planning Committee, Helle Munk Ravnborg (EL), represent Bornholm's regional municipality at the Citizens' Meeting. Works for complete openness

"Thus, both I and our planning department have had meetings/ dialogue in recent times with representatives from the Association Energiø Bornholm and other citizens".

The Citizens' Meeting will be held on Tuesday in Aakirkebyhallerne and starts at 6.30 pm. Expected end time at 9pm.


Energiø Bornholm and Environmental Impact Survey

Energiø Bornholm must be able to receive up to 3 GW offshore winds from new offshore wind farms. The mills will be placed 15-45 km south of Bornholm, and the parks will be able to supply 3.3 million households with electricity.

But in the end, it is Energinet's own architects who make the final decisions.

- Yes, that's it. And it would be an obvious thing to hold an architectural competition, but I am also aware that it would risk expanding the project by many millions of dollars, says Jacob Consolation.

A small cluster of the audience BUhede when he said in his welcome to the civic meeting that it was an honor for Bornholm to lay ground for the world's first energy island. Later, however, he harvested claps from significantly more spectators as he spent a few minutes listing all the benefits. Throughout the evening, which was completed around stands where you could ask questions to professionals from Energinet, the Danish Energy Agency and the Danish Environmental Protection Agency, he talked to several citizens.

What do you take with you from the Citizens' Meeting? - I take with me that some citizens are still worried about what it will mean to our nature. The neighbors also have some concerns, and I can understand that because one's home is one's hell. Title: Klart ønske til energiøen: Tag hensyn til naturen
Content:
The municipality is working on a consultation response to the Danish Environmental Protection Agency. Basically, Bornholm wants to be taken into account as much consideration as possible in connection with the establishment of Energiø Bornholm and the land plant.

Bornholm wants as few negatives nuisance and as many derived positive effects as possible by Energiø Bornholm. It is one of the messages in the consultation response that the regional municipality is preparing to the Danish Environmental Protection Agency prior to the initial studies. The consultation response is on its way through the political system and must be finally approved at the municipal council's meeting on Thursday.

In addition to the general wishes and expectations of the project, the municipality with Mayor Jacob Consolation, which sends in particular emphasis on the establishment of the land facility at Sose must be done with as much respect for the landscape, nature and the environment as possible. This applies, for example, to streams, groundwater and the coast.

This means, among other things, that the cable connections are established so that coastal nature and landscape are preserved as best as possible, that the land plant is fitted with the landscape as best as possible, and that ancient monuments and cultural heritage are best respected. In this connection, the municipality wants to make sketches and precise visualizations of the land facility's stringent effect and remote effect early.

During the construction phase, the regional municipality expects increased traffic congestion on Søndre Landevej, and it points out the Danish Environmental Protection Agency that it both wants an elaborate environmental assessment of the construction and construction phase and that it expects project owner or builders to take the necessary measures to ensure secure traffic. , especially for soft road users.

Protected nature in the draft consultation response makes the municipality the Danish Environmental Protection Agency aware that there may be more protected nature in the area than is evident from the registration available.

Registration of protected nature in accordance with section 3 of the Nature Conservation Act is thus indicative.

“Some areas have been registered along the coastline as protected overgrazing.

But since the registration is indicative, it cannot be completely excluded that more areas along the coast may be covered by the protection or that some of the boundary of the registered areas should be adjusted, "the municipality writes in the draft that the municipal council must decide before it is sent to be sent off.

At the same time, the municipality offers to enter into a dialogue about the protection status of the areas, and this points out that there are several different types of nature protection.

Effects on the seabed as regards streams in the area, the municipality sees a need for an assessment of the total transmission plant's environmental impact in relation to increased discharge of roof and surface water, potential discharge of oily compounds from transformer stations and discharge from the high -voltage system to streams with registered trout ups.

“We have a special attention to the watercourses as to whether the project involves lowering the groundwater and what solutions and consequences it will have.

Another aspect is the need for increased drainage of the area, how it can be solved and what consequences it will have for the environment, including the streams and the adjacent coastal waters, ”the mayor writes in the draft.

From the Bornholm side, there is also a desire for an answer to what effect wind turbines and submarine cables on the seabed have on fauna and flora as well as on the ocean currents and fish movements in the marine environment.

Finally, the municipality makes the Danish Environmental Protection Agency aware that its own solutions must be established for wastewater in the area, as no sewerage and that a permit must be sought for the handling of roof and surface water, ordinary house wastewater and industrial wastewater.


About the consultation response

The regional municipality hopes Energiø Bornholm can contribute positively to securing? The vision of 42,000 Bornholmers in 2028, including in particular the goals of creating 1,000 new job openings by 2028, and that Bornholm will be the attractive option for newcomers, tourists and companies.

? Effects for green transition on Bornholm, according to the target of Bornholm as fossil -free island in 2040.

? That good care is taken on nature and its diversity.

    The establishment of Energiø Bornholm's land facility at Sose should be done with as much consideration for nature and the surroundings as possible, believes the regional municipality. This is stated in the draft of a consultation response to the Danish Environmental Protection Agency, which the municipal council must decide on Thursday. Visualization: Energinet

Title: Energiø i naturen

Title: Anerkendt arkitektfirma skal tegne energiøens højspændingsanlæg
Content:
Architectural course about the land facility for Energiø Bornholm will start Wednesday with an open house and a workshop at Bornholm University College.

When the Bornholmers on Wednesday at a workshop at Bornholm College get the chance to influence the construction of the huge high -voltage station, it becomes architects from the well -known architectural firm Arkitema, who must try to convince.

Arkitema is known for, among other things, with Christoffer Harlang to stand behind Hammershus Visitor Center, for which the Architect Team has gained great professional recognition.

Bornholm Regional Municipality writes that "Arkitema must design the land facility", and the developer Energinet describes in the invitation to Wednesday's workshop Arkitema as "Energinets Architects at the Station Building".

Communications consultant at Energinet Sune Juul-Sørensen tells Tidende that Arkitema will be responsible for the overall expression and the buildings' interaction with the landscape.

It is natural that the election has fallen on Arkitema, as the architectural firm is owned by COWI, which Energinet has associated as an external advisor to the construction project.

"Arkitema will present at the two workshops a number of inspiring examples from other similar buildings, where work has been done with, among other things, facades, fitting in the landscape and planting," the invitation says.

In Energinet, it is hoped that many Bornholmers will show up and make their opinion known, as it is "the locals who know the area best".

- Of course, we are bound by the fact that we have to build a large electrical engineering plant with a number of restrictions. But there are also opportunities to work with, among other things, the landscape, facades and planting, so that the station is fit in the best possible way in the landscape, says Marian Kaagh, Deputy Director of Energinet.

Without competition, the regional municipality has sought a stronger involvement of architects, but the local desire to get Energinet to hold a decided architectural competition was rejected by the state -owned company responsible for operating and developing the high -voltage network.

"The administration works for the plant to be fitted with the landscape in the best possible way and has asked Energinet about the possibility of an architectural competition. Energinet denies that there is time to hold an architectural competition, but in turn offers a special process in connection with the design of the plant, which partly ensures that more architects are given the opportunity to provide input, and partly to include the public in the design at an early phase before there a proposal for a local plan is presented, ”wrote the municipality's administration on the case in September.

In addition to Arkitema, two external architects will follow the work. Rikke Juul Gram and Michael Krarup are appointed by Energinet and the regional municipality to act as external consultants. Both have "competencies and experience in landscape and infrastructure", the municipality writes about the two architects.

The actual workshop at Bornholm College will take place on Wednesday evening at 7 pm.

In the afternoon, between 13 and 16 there will be an open house at the college, where without prior registration you can come by and see the hosts' exhibited materials and have a chat with Arkitema and Energinet.

The architectural process continues February 2 with another workshop, and March 20, 2023, Energinet and Arkitema plan to present a comprehensive presentation at an event at the Electric Works in Rønne.

The crew at Arkitema's design studio makes their mark on Bornholm these years. Also the people behind the housing project at Østre School and the Art Pavilion on Kjærenæsgrunden in Allinge make use of architects from Arkitema.

    At the Citizens' Meeting in November you could meet the architects who will participate in the work with the land facility. Here, municipal councilor Mikael Benzon (th), who was upset about the absence of an international architectural competition, talking to the municipality's responsible director, Lillian Rasch Madsen (in the middle). She is in the picture flanked by the two independent architects, Rikke Juul Gram and Michael Krarup, which Energinet has made available to the regional municipality. Photo: Jakob Nørmark
