But the task becomes another in Sydbornholm's open spaces, where there are 25 meters high halls that need to be found. Stock Photo: Berit Hvassum

Title: Højspændingsstation skjules næppe under jorden: ' Strøm og vand er ikke en god kombination'
Content:
If the tall buildings for the energy island's land plant cannot be dug a few meters into the ground, reader asks. The selected area is poorly suited, says Energinet, who suggests to hide the 25 -meter -high buildings in other ways.

After engineers and technical specialists on Energinet's inner lines have worked on the technical design of the high -voltage system for Energiø Bornholm, the time has now come to bring architects with a sense of the aesthetic details into play. Arkitema will be at the forefront of two workshops at Bornholm College in the coming months, and the main question, which is to be answered, is how the up to 25 meter high buildings avoid becoming some clumsy boxes that damage the landscape in South Bornholm.

In the wake of the last civic meeting, the Journal has been given a question of whether one of the - in theory - most effective ways of hiding a building can come up: "In the whole debate on land facilities, you know if anyone has asked Whether the height of the building can be reduced by digging the building as far down as possible, ”asks a reader from Hasle.

This option has tried to get the Energinet several times to relate to. Each time it has been clear that a digging project is not included in the plans.

And there are good reasons for that, explained chief project manager Kim Søgaard Mikkelsen earlier this year - the big challenge is that electricity and water are not a good combination. The converter solutions we need are very delicate to moisture and water, and the risk of damaging the electrical system is something we need to avoid, says Kim Søgaard Mikkelsen, who has not heard of buried high-voltage plants elsewhere.

- Don't know me. Then we rather go the other way and look at what we can do visually to shield it. This is one of the things we would like to have input from the citizens, said chief project manager Kim Søgaard Mikkelsen, while the feasibility studies were still underway in the spring.

Water and electricity During the June Folk Meeting Interviewed the Journal Hanne Storm Edlefsen, director of the two Energiø projects, about the possibility of hiding the buildings: Is it a technical opportunity to dig the buildings just a few meters down? - I don't actually know yet. It's too early to say. In general, it is difficult to dig down such a plant.

Are you willing to that? - We look at what types of stations you can set up, ie whether you can set up some less. And we look at it a lot with it with fit in the area. But I can't say yet if you can do something with the height. I agree that the 25 meters of course sound like a lot, said Hanne Storm Edlefsen, before eliminating the problems of a burial.

- There is water in the area and there are cuts elsewhere. It sets some restrictions.

Water in combination with electricity is by nature not the best solution. And there are some groundwater reasons elsewhere. Among other things, we use the feasibility studies of nature to look at these things and thus find the best solution. So it's not because I exclude anything. We just haven't finished the feasibility studies yet. This is also why we cannot say where the plant is going to be and what it will look like, it sounded from the director during the National Assembly.

Subsequently, Energinet has stated that they are adding up to a station design with a few outdoor systems, which means that a larger part of the high -voltage components must be placed in gas -insulated buildings.

However, lowering of groundwater does not indicate that the feasibility studies have given Energinet the desire to try forces with a burial. Tuesday Tuesday asked Energinet about a status on the feasibility studies that are over. A majority in the municipal council decided in September to await the results of Energinet's investigations before the municipality will start the work on making a local plan and a supplement to the municipal plan. It is the bee of the water in the low -lying area that caused the municipal council to stepped soft on the brake.

"These are the conditions of the environmental consequences of a lowering of the groundwater level and the need for increased drainage that, according to the consultation responses, must be expected to cause a need to adjust the location of the high -voltage system," says the text that the Unity List wanted to add, and which was supported by S, V and Kd.

At the Citizens 'Meeting, Jørgen Hammer from Bornholm Citizens' Association's Collaboration recommended to plant a 300-meter-wide belt trees to Søndre Landevej as soon as possible, after Energinet announced by the beginning of 2023, exactly where the 70-90 hectare high-voltage station is to be placed within the gross area .

- We will appeal that you start to think about afforestation down there very early in the planning phase. And the forest that is being raised, one could very well call the "Elmindingen", Jørgen Hammer suggested.

Title: Energiø for enhver pris?
Content:
Does the Bornholm population want our small island patched in with giant buildings, where Nature Bornholm will look like a lego block?

There are - and must be made - major decisions about different initiatives here on the island. Here among Energiø Bornholm and Rønne Harbor with its extensions as some of the largest.

One can wonder about the decision -making processes that happen in these cases with such far -reaching consequences for all of us.

The goal that underlies the decisions is green energy. In addition, more jobs and economic growth, which has in fact proved not to be true. In total, it causes major concerns. And where is the influence of citizens? The people who are spokespersons for the above are politicians and officials in senior positions. So people by force. Power used and also abused regardless of whether it is a desire from us that resides on Bornholm. It almost leads the thoughts towards ancient communist conditions where the interests of the population are neglected. Big decisions are decided centrally. Then there may be consultation processes - but it does not change the original decision.

The population is assured that they are part of a democratic process - but are they in reality? Does the Bornholm population want our small island patched in with giant buildings, where Nature Bornholm will look like a lego block? Noisy transformers, repeated port extensions of Rønne Harbor, which are eating more and more nature and coastline. An otherwise unspoilt sea view that will in future be broken by giant offshore wind turbines. There must be respect for nature and aesthetic values.

Is that really what we want with our island? Lose great natural values ​​that never come back? When the values ​​are so restricted that it turns into tunnel vision, other values ​​gain less priority or no significance at all; For example, the human, aesthetic and environmental values, to name a few of the essentials.

The few who shout up are often set by the power elite in booths as not thinking about the island's best with more and with statements that green transition is needed, more cruise ships, space for more wind turbine elements etc.

There are solutions that are more adapted to the island and its size. As the development seems to be going now, the fear is that the island will end up as a regular industrial island.

For more draws more.

Energiø has been decided centrally parliamentally.

But that's why the island's political men and women don't have to play nods anyway. In other parts of the country, there have been more visionary thinking people with influence who have weighted the alternative values ​​higher. Guess the politicians and officials here could learn from these people who dare to think differently around the island with greater weighting of nature and environmental considerations - an island with the tranquility and harmony that everyone who lives here weighs and future newcomers opt for the island.

Title: Energinet om landanlæg: Vi vil opfylde alle støjkrav
Content:

Title: Bekymringen er status quo

At the workshop, which was the first of two, the second taking place on February 2, 2023, there was, among other things, the opportunity to enter into a dialogue with the architectural firm Arkitema, which will be responsible for the design of the facility north of Søndre Landevej at Sose, and the developer Energinet.

Arkitema is simply responsible for the overall expression of the plant and the interaction of the buildings with the landscape. The buildings themselves will probably be 25 meters high.

Fridrik Adamsson, who together with his wife lives relatively close to the area where the plant is to be located, is one of the founders of the Facebook group The Citizens' Association Energiø Bornholm, which brings together opponents of the large land facility, and the two were of course attended to the workshop, which he however Also find that not so terrible many other neighbors were.

The two were present at the college at the workshop itself in the evening, but also in the afternoon, where there was an open house with the opportunity to see the hosts' exhibited materials and have a chat with both Arkitema and Energinet.

- In the afternoon we had a really nice talk with some of the architects and those from Energinet, he says.

- And there was the opportunity to give some suggestions on what one thinks of materials and their suggestions for the location within the designated area, where it is located in the middle. We also expressed our usual concern in terms of noise.

You are both concerned with noise nuisance and in relation to the purely visual at the plant? - Yes, that's primarily it, because it's going to be a real eye. Not just for us who live here. My wife and I are not the most vulnerable, it gets worse for those who live even closer. They will experience it as a gigantic colossus that is going to noise around the clock.

Vikingeborg How many are it that is going to live so close? - I don't know exactly, but there are a lot of people and properties, says Fridrik Adamsson.

- It will be the world's largest transformer station, which you know is going to be a lot. Especially in humid weather, the plant will hum.

And that applies no matter how it is designed? - Yes, it does.

Are you more or less concerned after yesterday? - It is the status quo, says Fridrik Adamsson, noting that there was no very large attendance of neighbors, but in return a large part of the politicians present as well as employees of Arkitema and Energinet were.

- I don't know why the neighbors were gone, maybe they feel it is a fight that is of no use, says Fridrik Adamsson.

He himself had proposals for the design of the plant: - I suggested that it be designed as a ring castle from the Viking Age with high ramparts all the way around, which is planted to shield it as much as possible. It might be both interesting and beautiful.

What was the reaction to the proposal from the architectural firm? - Nothing special, but they thanked and said they would include the proposal.

Title: Arkitekten: Vi skal arbejde med en arkitektur, som kan tåle at blive set
Content:
At the next workshop on February 2, Arkitema will present specific proposals to Energiø Bornholm's land facility.

Like Energinet, the builder at the land facility in connection with Energiø Bornholm, John Strandfelt, who is a partner and business area manager at the architectural firm Arkitema, who will be responsible for the design, is well pleased with the course of the workshop on Wednesday at Bornholm University College.

It is also Arkitema who has designed the visitor center at Hammershus.

At the college, interested parties could meet up and provide input to the construction on the 260 -hectare area of ​​SOSE.

- I think it went really well, says the architect.

- There was a very great commitment on the part of the citizens with a great questionnaire. After all, we had brought a number of posters and models that you could give direct comments on post-it banknotes. In this way we got both comments and various notes home. A lot came up that we have taken back with, and it was the primary purpose of the day to both contribute information and to ensure a good dialogue.

It took place, so we're super happy for that.

Kim Søgaard Mikkelsen from Energinet points out that one can either try as far as possible to save the plant away or also try to make the buildings sufficiently interesting that they can withstand being free, what is your attitude about it? - I think what he thinks is that there are a two extremes, but I would say that you will always work with a certain degree of adaptation to the landscape, where plantings will come in the foreground of the expression. The other way around you can say that the buildings will also get a size so that they cannot be hidden completely, it cannot be done.

So we will use both elements, ie both fit, where we hide something in the landscape and make it less dominant and at the same time work with an architecture that can withstand being seen.


Concrete proposals

And now you have to look at the different inputs you have received and find out if you can use them more specifically? - Just exactly. Towards the next workshop on February 2nd, we will specify the basis we had on Wednesday, and which was more of a kind of registration and introduction to where we are in the process and what character traits the landscape has and which we have to work with. So at the next workshop we will talk to the citizens about some more concrete solutions.

Will you definitely present something that shows more about how you imagine the design becomes? - Yes. We will present some proposals that are in different directions and that can form the basis for a renewed discussion which is an extension of the discussions on Wednesday. But on a more concrete basis.

I know a citizen suggested building a round Viking castle with ramparts around, what do you think of such a proposal? - Yes, I know from my colleagues that the proposal has been noted, says John Strandfelt.

- But as I also said to several at the workshop, I do not think anything right now. We would very much like to take in all the inputs and see them in a context.

There were a lot of good suggestions yesterday, so rather than now, to start saying that some are good and others less good, I'd rather say that we start a system where we look into everyone and look at , what can you do on site and what can be done in relation to the purely technical.

Title: Fremtidens brintmotorvej fra Norden til Tyskland passerer tæt forbi Bornholm
Content:
Four Nordic energy companies are planning to bring a pipeline to hydrogen down through the Baltic Sea. It is a matter of linking Bornholm with the energy connection, and this can create a basis for establishing power-to-X plants on Bornholm soil. CIP, which is behind plans for offshore wind farms east of Bornholm, is part of the project.

In Finland and Sweden, a new pipeline for hydrogen is on the drawing board. The plan consists of connecting Sweden and Finland with the German energy market, and the pipeline can also get a detour to Bornholm, the partners behind the project announced last week.

One of the companies behind "Baltic Sea Hydrogen Collector", as the pipeline is called, is capital -strong Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners (CIP), which together with Ørsted also plans to erect two offshore wind farms east of Bornholm.

In the project of a hydrogen pipe down through the Baltic Sea, CIP has teamed up with the energy company OX2 as well as Nordion Energy and Gasgrid Finland, which owns and operates part of the gas network in Sweden and Finland respectively.

"The goal of the Baltic Sea Hydrogen Collector is to free up the significant offshore wind potential of the Botnic Bay and the Baltic Sea region, create a thriving hydrogen market and connect supply and demand," the companies write about the new connection.

On the map of the proposed route you can see that the hydrogen line is intended to go southeast around Bornholm on the way to the Greifswald area south of Rügen, where the Nord Stream tubes from Russia are also led ashore. A connection has been placed on the map to Bornholm.

"The offshore project can also be connected to other energy islands in the region such as Gotland and Bornholm in Sweden and Denmark," says the news that Gasgrid Finland released last Friday.

The pipeline in the Baltic Sea is part of a unified European ambition to create a bulky hydrogen network across the countries.

"European Hydrogen Backbone" is called the plans that involve 31 European gas infrastructure companies, including Danish Energinet. A main goal is to create connections from windy areas in the North Sea and the Baltic Sea to the population -dense industrial centers in the middle of the continent.


Electrolysis plant on land

Hydrogen can be produced through electrolysis using large amounts of electricity (a process often called Power-to-X). When moving really large amounts of energy over long distances, it can be cheaper to transport the energy as hydrogen rather than as power, as the total cost of pipelines is lower than for high voltage cables.

This can mean that electrolysis plants must be established near the offshore wind farms, and this also applies at Bornholm.

This particular opportunity told CIP about in an interview with Tidende earlier this fall.

- The first and primary product is green hydrogen. In the electrolysis process you split water and get hydrogen, and it thinks we can be led via pipes to Germany and used in their hydrogen network, Director Magnus Brogaard said of CIP's considerations.

He suggested that hydrogen from a Bornholm Power-to-X plant could be refined to ammonia and set aside for the Bunkerhub project at Rønne Harbor. Together with several large companies, the harbor has a vision of establishing a green gas station off Rønne for future ship traffic in the Baltic Sea.

Before the summer holidays, CIP applied for the Danish Energy Agency to get a permit to initiate feasibility studies for the two offshore wind farms called Bornholm Bassin East and Bornholm Basin Syd. Since then Ørsted has joined. The companies operate with a total capacity of three gigawatts, which is the same size as Energiø Bornholm Parks South and Southwest of Bornholm are expected to get.

In the interview, the CIP director emphasized that the offshore wind farms need to be on a large scale in order for the investment to be relevant to make. As Energinet does not plan to put more and larger cables so that the energy from eastern offshore wind farms can be carried away as power, Power-to-X is decisive to be crucial for CIP's offshore wind turbine plans to be implemented.

- So the question of how much we can possibly think our project into the plans that Rønne Harbor has for green fuels for ships? How much can be thought of in a decrease in Germany, where a pipe should be put. Now it is generally much cheaper to move energy via pipes than with electric transmission, so there can be a case. Work on those plans are waiting for us to get started with the preliminary investigations, Magnus Brogaard told the Journal in September.

On Tuesday, it was not possible for the Journal to do an interview with CIP about what significance a hydrogen connection from Finland and Sweden to Germany can get for the offshore wind turbine plans on Bornholm.


Independent of Russia

The four companies behind the new gas pipeline in the Baltic Sea aim to establish the new hydrogen infrastructure by 2030, they say.

Along with the pipeline at sea from Finland and Sweden via the Åland Islands to Germany, work is being made to make a network of brine pipelines on land from Finland via Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania to Poland and Germany, which will help make countries less dependent on Russian gas and oil.

"It creates the opportunity to make offshore wind energy in the region a safe and flexible source of energy, which improves the system's resilience, energy dependence and security of supply. It will also support the decarbonization of sectors that are difficult to change (from fossil fuels, ed.), and green industrialization in the Nordic countries, the Baltic and Central Europe, ”the press release states the pipelines.

After all, the first and primary product is green hydrogen. In the electrolysis process you split water and get hydrogen, and it thinks we can be led via pipes to Germany and used in their hydrogen network Magnus Brogaard director.

Title: Lea rykker igen frem i geledderne: ' Jeg har masser af kilometer i benene'
Content:
Lea Wermelin has become part of the Social Democratic group management and is now also the party's climate, energy and supply mayor.

It goes up and it goes down in politics. The Bornholm MP for Social Democracy Lea Wermelin was a member of the Environment, became Minister of the Environment in the latest government - but got no ministerial post in the new SVM government consisting of the Social Democracy, the Left and the Moderates.

Now, however, she is again moving closer to the center of power, after a group meeting in the Social Democracy on Thursday she can state that she has been incorporated into the party's group management.

Who the group management consists of, the new member has a good control: - It is the group chairman, the political rapporteur, a group secretary who, among other things, keeps track of voting, there are some group masters and some group members - so we are probably all in the area of 10, she says.

And what do you need to deal with in your new role more precisely? - In the group management we will meet once a week to talk about everything we need to talk about in the Social Democracy. Although we are part of a unified government consisting of three parties, we have a party where we meet partly at the group meetings, but where we also have a group management, which I look forward to being a part of. I also become the party's climate, energy and supply mayor, and I myself have wanted to be allowed to throw myself over that task, so I am really happy about that too.

- I know, among other things, from everything I have been dealing with in recent years as a minister that the climate case is the greatest challenge of our generation. It is crucial to Denmark and the rest of the world, but to a great extent also for Bornholm with our upcoming energy island.

50 members When you meet once a week in the group management, will it be about current things and issues? - I haven't been in the group management before, so it's hard to wise me exactly how the meetings will work, also because we are part of a common government. But it is clear that it will be important for us partly to ensure that the new government can implement its ambitious government base, which the Social Democratic group must contribute to, but partly also make sure that we are in the middle of it strong as a party with The important markers and cases people know us for. The collaboration must slip and we have to handle current cases, so I expect it to be a bit of it all.

Including overall strategies? - Yes, we need to turn the most important cases that are.

When did you know that you would be invited inside the heat? - There has been a big job in progress, because we are 50 members of the Social Democratic group, and it is nice that we got such a good choice and are so many, but it also means that there are a lot of people who Must have something exciting to do. There we have been able to report what we could think of ourselves, but of course there has also been a great job underway from group chairman Niels Lahn's and others' side in terms of getting the cabal to go up the best possible.

- It has been spoken back and forth, and it all officially landed on Thursday morning at 8.30am, where we met in the group. But I had heard about the bid to me already on Wednesday night, which is why I was just looking forward to the meeting. Now we know what 2023 will offer the different ones, and I am looking forward to my own sake to delve more into the climate area. There are lots of things I need to become wiser about, and there are many major tasks in our government basis in relation to the climate change.

Patch on the wound when you were told that you now became part of the Social Democracy group management, you should just wipe the sweat off my forehead and think "I just thought I was going on Christmas holidays, but now I have to go home and read up on The cases ”? - Haha, I think I have lots of miles in my legs, and I really want to help make a difference, both when it comes to being the Social Democracy representative to the outside and in relation to all the cases we are talking about on Bornholm . I have already pricked our new Minister of Transport on the shoulder and had the opportunity to say that there is something important to us. In this way, the work has already started, and we have also been looking forward to this during the really long government talks.

But there will also be time for a Christmas holiday with the family, we have had the last polls in the parliamentary hall on Thursday, and it is also nice.

I suppose it was a disappointment not to have to continue as a minister, is this a good solid patch on the wound? - Yes, that's it. Obviously, it is a huge privilege to be a minister, and I have also been incredibly pleased with the significant imprints on the nature and environmental field that we managed to implement - and some of which will stand for many years to come. I am very grateful for that and take the experience of that work with me.

Now I am even allowed to continue the work as rapporteur in the field. After all, we do not have a Social Democratic minister in the field now, and that means I have to get up early and be ready to lift the big task - I am happy about that, says Lea Wermelin.

Title: Hvordan skal Bornholm udvikles?
Content:
Which island would we like to live on, us who have the pleasure today? What we have on Bornholm is becoming more and more unique, and I am incredibly happy to live here where the pace is not too high and where nature, agriculture and scattered buildings are in between.

The energy island is becoming a reality.

In this connection, a transformer system will be built, which will include 90 hectares of SOSE.

The plans have of course sparked debate, but it is clear that the transformer system has been decided and will be clear in about eight years.

Some actors believe we should use the land plant as a catalyst for industrial development of Bornholm. It has been talked about using the huge amount of power produced to produce hydrogen or ammonia that can be used for fuel. This is popularly called Power-to-X. In the beginning, words like 'test island' were prevalent.

But now it is as if efforts are being made to put out a much larger area in SOSE for industrial development than they already allocated 90 hectares.

I am concerned about the development myself, and this is how I think more and more Bornholmers have it. The visions behind it will change Bornholm tremendously. Both on good and evil. But it is a difficult debate, because it is about the future.

No one knows what's going to happen.

Of course, employment will come for a shorter period of two to four years when the land plant is to be built.

There will also be derivative employment if we are to have more plants in the future. We can see to Lolland, where the Fehmarnbelt project has created declining unemployment in one of Denmark's poorest areas.

It's positive. But in many places in outskirts you see a 'grasshopper effect' when industries are established.

I can imagine that the transformer plants are being built by European labor, who lives in barracks right up the construction site and traveling again when the plant is finished.

When the plant is in operation, there is a risk that key people and technical staff can sit in different places in the world and manage facilities on Bornholm and elsewhere. We can get extensive industrial plants that do not create much permanent employment. It says everything that there are plans for an artificial energy island in the North Sea with a transformer plant that is far from land and must be run by very few people.

On the other hand, an industrial development of Bornholm can contribute positively to the island. We can get more high -tech companies where some of the employees settle on Bornholm. Perhaps the population decline can be reversed, and a larger industrial area in Sose may be what makes us attract families and well -educated labor to Bornholm.

The debate is about how we create life and development on Bornholm.

Why do families choose Bornholm for? Is it nature or the good jobs? And which island would we like to live on, us who have the pleasure today? What we have on Bornholm is becoming more and more unique, and I am incredibly happy to live here where the pace is not too high and where nature, agriculture and scattered buildings are in between.

The land plant is coming. But I don't think we need to change local plans to make room for a large industrial area in SOSE. Let's see what companies will be here and let's find out what they can offer Bornholm. It's hard. We should not be afraid of what is coming, but we must say no thanks if business projects do not contribute to making Bornholm a better society.

Although lobbyists and wind turbine companies are pushing, we are in no hurry.

Title: Her er Tidendes ønsker for 2023
Content:
2023 stands at the door, and the wish list from the Journal is long.

It's time to start on a fresh one. Shaking the horrible experiences of recent years and dreaming of new, good initiatives for Bornholm in the year ahead of us. 2023 can offer many. On the Journal we have listed a number of them.

Immigration and population growth are still the Bornholm miracle cure that will pour more gold into the municipal treasury and ensure a better social economy. We have broken the curve and the many energy projects will, no matter what, attract labor and help us along the way. The optimism at Bornholm will be able to draw more to the island in 2023, just as the many buildings around hopefully will be able to help with good housing offers for the fresh labor.

One of the most urgent problems in 2023 on Bornholm - besides the municipality's economy - is the freight ferry. Hammerhus is too small and too slow to be able to deliver all the necessary goods to and from Bornholm every day. Either we need to have a ferry more, or we have to think of shipping route to Ystad instead so that more goods can get back and forth every day. Business has hit the ceiling over the capacity and understandably complains. The prerequisite for growing and creating value on an island is that you can move goods to and from it. If the ferry is filled up, business speeds are blocked.

Another area that can be of great importance to Bornholm in 2023 is defense and security. Denmark must spend significantly more money on the defense and partly to live up to NATO membership and partly to secure against the growing threat in the east. Bornholm and Ertholmene are Denmark's easternmost outpost. This could mean increased the protection of the island with more jobs and more activity from the defense - with aircraft, surveillance and defensive defense. It can provide more security and more economic activity on Bornholm.

The first step is probably the already promised and planned expansion of Almegårds Barracks, but even more jobs are welcome at Bornholm The wild growing energy island will continue its entry on Bornholm in 2023. In 2022 we got both the island and double up with another 3 gw floating offshore wind farms From Cip Ørsted. With so much green energy on Bornholm - six million household electricity consumption per year - we will have to transform half the power into hydrogen or other green fuels to get rid of the flow.

It will throw off incomprehensible amounts of heat that we can use in new professions such as manufacturing processes, horticulture and more. In 2023, we move closer to this scenario and hopefully help business get started in a timely manner.

The political climate of the municipal council also holds room for improvement. In 2023, it will again be possible for the mayor to bring together the municipal council for a broad budget settlement to ensure Bornholm's poor economy and difficult situation in the field of children in particular.

Much more well will hopefully happen in 2023. The traffic corridor through Sweden is still missing, DAT lacks help to introduce green aircraft, and our wooden ship cultural heritage in Sydhavnen stands in front of its fate just to name a few things.

Tidende follows the development and brings the latest news to Bornholm about the cases in the coming and potentially lucrative year.

Title: Trøst: Kun fantasien sætter grænser for energiøs muligheder
Content:
Cheap district heating, large horticulture, energy from the wastewater - or maybe a water park? Or maybe it all at once? The large amount of green energy from the upcoming energy island can be used in countless ways, says Mayor Jacob Consolation after new inspiration taken in Esbjerg.

If Bornholm grabs the chance fully, with the upcoming Energiø will come so huge amounts of green energy to Bornholm that only the imagination limits what it will be possible to use it for.

That's what Mayor Jacob Trøst (K) says, after he participated in the Bornholm delegation from Tuesday to Thursday, who visited Esbjerg to take a closer look at what has been gained from the role of the center of green energy.

- Esbjerg is in the process of connecting the surplus heat to their district heating network, and it will also be the most obvious opportunity for us. Horticulture will also be very obvious, so we can get Bornholm vegetables all year round, he says.

- If we can change our wastewater treatment plants and use the wastewater to create green fuels, we can release space and create a new recreational area at Rønne Harbor.

- You could also make a water park. It will also be obvious, because there will be a lot of hot water to do with. But really, it is only the imagination that limits what one can do.

Because it's energy that comes in, says Jacob Consolation.

Esbjerg is in the process of unfolding some of the many options.

- You can at least see that Esbjerg has a strong development in attracting new businesses and that they also have a major focus on green transition, says Jacob Trøst.

- I can see that there are great opportunities to pull up Bornholm and create a new big income base.

It could help to withdraw the dependence on seeking money from pools from the state, he says.

- First of all, we talk about many jobs.

Grabbing this opportunity will attract some new professions that also require some education other than those we have today. It will add great resources to Bornholm, both in the establishment phase, but also in the subsequent operating phase.

Like Linda Kofoed Persson (DF), Jacob Consol sees a clear choice ahead of Bornholm.

- First and foremost, we have to decide whether we want that development on Bornholm. Will we add area to the type of business that we will be able to get? Will we see how we can best use the large amount of green energy that will come in? Or we just have a land facility and not more? he says.

Title: Linda: Bornholm skal turde for at vinde stort på energiø
Content:
The energy island opens up unanimous large opportunities for Bornholm. But it requires a yes without hesitation or wobble, says Linda Kofoed Persson (DF), who has just seen how Esbjerg grabbed the same chance.

Bornholm faces a huge choice. Between saying full -tone yes to the upcoming energy island and starting to act then - or only to say half -heartedly yes.

The difference must be measured in lots of new jobs, new housing, many newcomers, growth for business and a municipality that can get back on foot. To say full -tone yes or half -hearted yes is also the difference between whether all they and many other options come to Bornholm or not.

This is stated by Linda Kofoed Persson (DF), chairman of the Business, Housing and Employment Committee, which together with 30 others from Bornholm visited Esbjerg from Tuesday to Thursday this week. To hear about the roaring growth that Esbjerg is experiencing with offshore wind turbines, energy island and power-to-x-and how the city has handled to get the opportunity Bornholm now also gets.

- We can get jobs in a different caliber than those that we are known for today. And we can get a development of not only workplaces, but also housing and education that we have not seen before, says Linda Kofoed Persson.

- We can get that if we politicians dare to take responsibility for launching a development where we give some new forms of companies the opportunity to develop on Bornholm.

- We must also dare to say that yes, we must be 42,000 on Bornholm. But it is of no use if it is only to be retirees or people in some professions that they can only live just about, says Linda Kofoed Persson.

- We will be able to attract people who pay taxes on the big scale. It's crazy what we will be able to get out of this, she says.

But: - These big, big players on the other side of the water do not bother to come to Bornholm if we sit with crossed arms.

If, on the other hand, we say "come" and have arranged us so that it becomes possible and attractive for them to come here, there will be a completely different will.

Growth requires space Bornholm must be prepared to set space, says Linda Kofoed Persson. In practice, the municipal council must take steps to create a planning basis for more industry.

- It requires us to lay out much more commercial area. Some are so scared that it will ruin Bornholm, and I hear them well too. But we do not get ruined the glory value of Bornholm by laying out 250 hectares for business purposes, she says.

- We should dare to do that. Some would say that industrial buildings are ugly, but it will be to carry if we do it with one shovel one place. You will not be able to see the land facility for forest, says Linda Kofoed Persson, who is making a clear choice for Bornholm.

- Esbjerg has evolved from a fishing village to a center for green energy. We have gone from being a fishing society to being on constant poverty relief from the state. But now we can become self -sufficient again so that we do not have to seek these pools for difficult municipalities, she says.

- But we have to dare. If we do not get started now, we can get what we fear, namely a land facility without connection to Bornholm, where a service man comes and mows grass once in a while, says Linda Kofoed Persson.

- I believe that we are going to get started now. The train is roaring and it drives past us if we don't jump on.

Power-to-X is necessary to get the full benefit of the energy island, Linda Kofoed Persson believes that Bornholm should also be prepared to land for Power-to-X: The plants that can convert excess energy into green fuel.

-We must also dare to say yes to Power-to-X.

There are some afraid of, and yes, there was a risk to it once. But there is no longer there.

With modern power-to-x plants, I heard in Esbjerg that there will be a serious incident once for every million years, she says.

-Without Power-to-X, we won't get the jobs or the possibility that scientists want to settle on Bornholm to research the closed energy system that we can get here.

-Without Power-to-X we just get a land plant, and then there is no reason for the state to spend so much money to join the power supply from the energy island. The state will not spend that much money on it if we only want to use the power for our coffee machines, says Linda Kofoed Persson.

It is still unclear whether Bornholm gets Power-to-X. In Esbjerg, two plants are being built just outside the city. Also at Bornholm it will require politicians who will put room for, and not everyone is just ready.

-I think the Unity List has very clearly said several times that we should not have Power-to-X, at least not on land. But Power-to-X on the water is much, much more expensive, says Linda Kofoed Persson.

-Power-to-X on the sea requires you to build an island. And you never get anyone to put it eight-double of what it will cost on land. Then they just find somewhere else. Therefore, Power-to-X at sea is not a real option.

If we want it out on the sea, it won't come, she says.

Title: Det koster 50-70 millioner kroner: Sådan vil man indrette elværket
Content:

There are big plans for Rønne's old power plant.

The distinctive building complex must be the meeting point for the National Center for Green Energy and later Baltic Energy Island, the meeting place for companies, researchers, students, citizens and decision makers, satellite for education at the Technical University DTU and exhibition venue.

All that must be done in buildings that have been protected since 2015 and are in disrepair.

In the Business, Housing and Employment Committee's agenda you can read how to plan to set up the former power plant from 1910-12 and the extensions of 1925 and 1938. is due to a level that means that the regional municipality that owns the owner of the conservation. The ambition is to get a national fund to pay for the renovation, which is expected to amount to between DKK 50 and 70 million.

The large halls the complex consists of both the former power plant with two large halls, a director's residence and a bathing facility, and the halls are an obvious dilemma, especially in the light of the restrictions the conservation dictates. You cannot make offices in the two halls, and the task is therefore to find supporting features that fit in the large spaces.

Currently, we are working towards using the largest of the two halls as a simple auditorium for teaching larger assemblies. The hall will also be used for larger seminars and workshops. In the transition between the two halls you work on a larger space sharing element that will act as a seating furniture for lectures.

The smaller of the two halls is disposed of to a dissemination and visitor center for the entire green transition of the energy based on Energiø Bornholm. For current use the large halls have some side buildings that are suitable for more introverted activities.

For example, it may be offices, meeting rooms, secretariat. This also applies to the former bathing facility and a director's residence, which is designated for offices, while the side buildings for the halls are suitable for group rooms.

Both the former bathing facility and the managerial residence have been updated for current use, but not according to the requirements the conservation authorities will make now that the building is protected.

During the first half of 2023, the municipality will work on a final report for the vision of the power plant. The report will include an architectural vision and an operating model.

College in Museum The old power plant will house facilities for teaching students from DTU, but there will also be a need for dormitory and guest apartments for the students, teachers and researchers. It is not obvious to establish in the power plant itself, but not so far from there lies a building that soon loses its current function and which can therefore pave the way for a possible college.

A situation plan thus states that the current Bornholm Museum on the corner of Sankt Mortens Gade and Lille Madsegade is in play. But nothing is determined and the need for dorm rooms and guest apartments must be investigated independently.

Campus Bornholm and DTU are at the forefront of the dialogue on accommodation facilities, including the municipality, Bornholm Hospital and Bornholm Museum.

The idea is to explore the possibilities of establishing something that will lift as many Bornholm actors' needs as possible, while at the same time adding educational institutions with seats at the power plant are ensured suitable accommodation facilities.

In connection with the establishment of Denmark's first two energy islands, COWI has published a Desk Study Report focusing on the business potential in Energiø Bornholm.

The report was published by the end of 2022 and it will be opened with four specific recommendations to Bornholm.

Among other things, it is recommended that you make visible the local skills and capacity.

A task that Business Center Bornholm is already in full swing with. Here, Business Manager Christa Lodahl told 22.

November that more Bornholm companies were on their way to being upgraded.

- Right now we are working on 10 companies that are on their way to being certified, and we have a project that runs only with offshore and a man dedicated to it, Christa Lodahl told the Journal at the time.

In the COWI report, they recommend that the initiative be taken to create relationships between the contractor/ operator and the local businesses to align expectations in terms of quality, documentation and task solution.

They propose a digital market platform or an active business network, and this also applies to companies in industries other than just offshore.


Accommodation and infrastructure

It is also recommended that the Bornholm Regional Municipality prepare a long -term plan and strategy for how the municipality is best equipped for the elongated project. This applies to both logistics and infrastructure, as well as access to labor. This allows barriers and delays to be avoided, and future needs and opportunities are made visible and planned, the report states.

It is also recommended that accommodation capacity be planned and prioritized.

It is given that in the high season there will be capacity challenges when both tourists and manpower have to find accommodation.

And that is what Linda Kofoed Persson (DF), who is chairman of the municipality's Business, Housing and Employment Committee eagerly.

She told the Journal when she recently returned enthusiastically from a study trip to Esbjerg to see how they handle the virus on the energy islands.

Here, among other things, she expressed an eagerness to see new permanent homes on Bornholm.

- The difference must be measured in lots of new jobs, new housing, many newcomers, growth for business and a municipality that can get back on foot, Linda Kofoed Persson said earlier in January.


More vocational educated

The fourth and final recommendation is in many ways also an old trot. It is recommended that Bornholm support that more people complete a vocational education.

And here it says in the report that if the increased labor demand is to be able to be met with local labor residing on Bornholm, it requires a long-term labor market and educational efforts, which supports more people completing a vocational education.

- We need to have the number up. It is inconvenient that the young people -and their parents -not more aware of all the opportunities one has as a skilled worker, stated the president of the Danish Industry at Bornholm in a press release in February 2022, where he clearly supports the recommendation.

Title: Trøst og følge på 25 henter grønne ideer i Skive

Title: ' Vi vil have Bornholm tilbage i Østersøen'
Content:
Mads Randbøll Wolffev was chairman when Baltic Bridge resurrected. He will work to restore connection to Saaremaa and bring Bornholm back on the Baltic Sea Map.


Why is the time ripe for Baltic Bridge Version 2?

- There are three reasons for that. Saaremaa Cultural Festival with 100 participants in September during the Culture Week reminded us of the good things that happened when you had a collaboration.

They also told us that Estonia and Saaremaa are at a completely different level today. We are equal. The second is that we live in a time when conversation between people is more important than ever. With war and dissatisfaction so close, we have to meet with other people and hold on to friendships and relationships. The third reason is that it is time for Bornholm to return to the Baltic Sea map. It's been small in recent years, I think. Bornholm is part of the Baltic Sea, and I also think that it is part of the reason why people are interested in having a Baltic bridge.

We want Bornholm back in the Baltic Sea.

Where does your own interest in Baltic cooperation come from? - I became a student in 1990 and I went to high school with many of those who helped start Baltic Bridge in his time. I wasn't even with, but I remember those years of the fall of the Wall and all the things that happened. There was a huge curiosity about what it was for some people. Although I was not in Baltic Bridge at that time, it also meant a lot to me to see that world opened up. I lived in Estonia when I was a student and was practicing at the Danish embassy and have traveled a lot and worked throughout the Baltic Sea region, so it's something I've had under the skin for more than 30 years.


How do you see the collaboration and Baltic bridge develop in the coming years?

- That's the exciting question: What can we get support for? I think one of the first things we need to do is get a re -visit to Saaremaa in the foreseeable future, so we get to revitalize all the relationships, get some new ones created and look at what it is we can and will cooperate on. It applies to business, culture, education, leisure and at all just meeting other people.

That's one of the big things. Then I also think we will help create a little more debate on Bornholm about Bornholm's role and Bornholm in the Baltic Sea.

Should bridge be built to other places in the Baltic Sea? - It can be answered from two perspectives.

One is what the Baltic Bridge Association should. It needs what we as members have energy for. The other thing is what Bornholm should do. Should you look at the B7 cooperation, the cooperation of the Seven Baltic Islands? I think that personally, but I'm not sure it's a task for the association. I have been to most of the Baltic islands and have seen how there are a lot of similarities. There are a lot of things you can relate to together. In some cases, there are greater similarities between the islands in the Baltic Sea than there is between what is going on on Bornholm and in Jutland, because there are some common conditions that apply.

Why did you just become you who became chairman? - There was a desire for some new people to go in. It was especially the former chairman who wanted it. He is still a member of the board and a great asset to the association.

Then I was there. I wasn't the only new one, but it was me they pointed to.

That wasn't the plan. I thought it might be interesting to be part of the board, but then they asked if I would be chairman too.

What tasks do you get as chairman? - I am about to find out, because I was taken a little on the bed. I hadn't prepared myself on how to approach it. I am about to find out what it means and entails of tasks. The first two things I would like to spend time looking at the possibilities of making a re -visit to Saaremaa, so we get a large group of Bornholmers for Saaremaa, and some who have been with in the past, but also some new ones. There is the opportunity to revitalize and create some brand new relationships.

The second is to find out how we can contribute to the discussion of how we get Bornholm firmly in the Baltic Sea again. These are the two things I have told the board that I would like to look at.

What are you doing in your working life? - I have a past as an official of the Ministry of Food and the Nordic Council of Ministers, but I have been an independent advisor in recent years. I have a job that is a little hard to explain, because I don't have an 8-16 work and I don't have a feature somewhere. In short, I work to create a link between the global challenges and the local solution. I bring people together and find solutions to the challenges there are.


And in your free time?

- I live a working life that makes me not have a fixed framework. Most recently, I was in Canada for 10 days and in Egypt 14 days on tasks, so it's hard to be able to arrange something and have hobbies as such. It's something about going for walks, reading a book, being with friends, and then I do some volunteer work.

Among other things, I am a member of the Danish UNESCO National Commission. I was a member of Rønne Roklub in my young days, and once in a while I dream of getting out again if there was just peace of mind.

What relationship do you have to Bornholm today? - My parents are dead, but I still come regularly on Bornholm. I've just been over there and going over there again in a few weeks. I have come a lot on Bornholm, especially as an independent where I have been able to work from Bornholm when I feel like it. My relationship has begun to become more engaging. I am not only a guest, but will also be part of what is happening on Bornholm and helped to influence it. I love coming to Bornholm and think it is great with the energy that the National Assembly has brought with it and now Energiø Bornholm, a lot of good things happen, and I would like to be a bigger part of that.

Title: Venstre stærkt skeptisk over for at bygge energiøen ud
Content:
Søren Schow does not share the optimism about the upcoming energy island as the basis for a huge recovery on Bornholm and a status as the center of green energy in eastern Denmark. Therefore, the Left is just now leaning against voting no to plan for both Power-to-X and other large plants associated with the energy island.

For two laps, members of the municipal council have recently returned enthusiastically from a visit to Skive.

Here they have visited the Green Business Park Green Lab Skive, where companies within green transition are located side by side, create energy on their own energy sources, store and share energy - and utilize each other's surplus products for new production. Most recently, Mayor Jacob Trøst (K), nine others from the municipal council and another 16 from Bornholm visited the Green Business Park on Monday.

Group chairman Søren Schow (V) should also have participated. However, he had to cancel because he was called in to sail Povl Anker. Furthermore, he had constantly thought if it was not a waste of money to send Bornholm politicians to visit the same place twice.

In the back of his head, Søren Schow had all the time that he is far from feeling sure that the upcoming energy island will be some good business for Bornholm. And that he is inclined to believe that it is a bad idea to make the energy island's land-firm part even bigger with a power-to-X plant and a green business park as in Skive.

- It makes sense with such a business park, but if we hardly have time to do the plan work that is linked to the ordinary business community, I do not see how it is related to plan work for an energy island, as we Not to know what turns into, says Søren Schow.

- I have to say that I am critical of it.

The transformer station alone will fill about 40 hectares. It will be huge.

So if you say that now we have to make it even bigger with Power-to-X and a business park, I just want to know what we get out of it, he says.

The role of the municipal council consists of saying yes or no to local and municipal planning for a power-to-X plant, a green business park and whatever else may encounter.

The facilities can only come if the municipal council wants to start the planning processes for them.

V: The winnings are unclear The Bornholm delegations have been traveled home from both Skive and (last week) Esbjerg after seeing Green Change breeds more green transition: Companies are looking for the places where there is a lot of green energy. When the companies come, more people are coming along quickly. And all the time, jobs are created in a whole new sector for green energy that just grows and grows.

But Søren Schow doesn't think it lasts. Therefore, he is debating whether Bornholm should set aside large areas for a Powerto-X plant, a green business park and whatever the green transition could bring.

-We must first see what a power-to-X system will fill physically. And who is going to make it and what it should be used for. I am also nervous that Bornholm and especially Beof say they should be involved in a power-to-X system.

We have to let that private, he says.

- If it's a good business for Bornholm, then yes. But how does Bornholm benefit if a power-to-X plant is established on Bornholm? If it is as good an idea as some think, one must also be able to say why it is a good idea and what is more accurate in it.

For example, the Danish People's Party looks at it that a power-to-X plant is a very important prerequisite for companies and jobs and research and education to Bornholm with Energiøen. Do you share that view of things? - No, I don't really. There is a positive story about all the good that will follow. But if you go further into it, it is difficult to know where the gain is in it for Bornholm, says Søren Schow.

Fear of nature at the same time, Søren Schow fears what large industrial plants will do at Bornholm's Nature and Bornholm's opportunities as a tourist destination.

- I know how big it is in Esbjerg.

It takes half an hour to drive past all the plants that have come and it is not pretty.

On the contrary, we have Bornholm as a tourist island, and we have a very attractive nature, he says.

- There are Balka and Dueodde and Snogebæk that many tourists are increasing. But if people now have to drive through a 40 to 80 hectare business park to get there, I'm not sure it will give the best picture of Bornholm.

Have you settled on your attitude in the Left, or can you be moved? - We can easily, but it depends on the content. I just want to be allowed to ask some critical questions, and I think we are missing that at the moment, says Søren Schow.

Fishing about again? In the 1980s, Søren Schow saw as a young man in Nexø how the city's port was expanded. Also at that time on the dream of business adventures.

But it went wrong, and now he sees similarities when people talk about the energy island as the new adventure on Bornholm.

- The ports of Nexø and Hasle were converted into big cod fishing, and what happened? Then fishing died, and you stood with some very large ports that barely managed to be used for the purpose they were intended for, says Søren Schow.

Title: Sidestil elnettet med motorvejsnettet
Content:

Recent days atrocities in terms of bureaucratic hassle when one or the other unit in society will set up solar cells is only the last of countless absurd situations that arise for a simple reason: that someone has to pay to transport electricity and we have to Know who it is because there is someone to make a profit on it - read, for example, TREFOR. But this model is a big misconception.

What if the transport equated with the motorway network would in principle be free? Well, it is not in fact free to use the motorways, all the while we all pay for it through the tax, but we can use it as needed, according to the solid model where you do not have to explain how often you use it, And how many kilometers you drive. The motorway network is there and is maintained as needed, via work contracts from the public to the private profession. And the only bureaucratic side of it is the technically focused person who is tasked with making sure it works.

The newly hatched Climate, Energy and Supply Minister Lars Aagård with a past in Energinet, where he has also not contributed particularly to renewed thinking, today still does not seem to be able to think out of the box. And it is unkind that his conclusion is that the municipalities will just be free to pay tax. It is perhaps most important about Mr Aagård's way of thinking about the big problem that most people can eventually see - even if one does your utmost from an official team to give such complicated and foggy explanations that no one can follow them is that We work with a business model that has been overtaken by the development.

One can only think in the usual circles where the citizens' initiatives are in principle punished, and the desire to be constructive is totally stripped, while in our neighboring countries you have no problem with both citizen involvement and profit sharing (the Netherlands: Citizens are co -owners of local wind turbines and profits Going back to the local community to improve, for example, local institutions and facilities), or local producers with large solar cells can sell to the neighbors (Germany and Austria).

It is totally grotesque and fiercely provocative that in this country, on the one hand, it is screamed that 'we are leaders in the world with regard to green transition' while being hopelessly old -fashioned thinking and banging any contributed initiative to this transition from the citizens.

And finally in relation to Trefors's self-justification of violent tariff increases: How logically is it from now to completely separate the new energy island from the existing electricity network? Maybe someone can explain it, and also why Trefor does not even mention that aspect in any place ..

Danes are pragmatic - perhaps more pragmatic than most - but pragmatism is killed at the public level of box office thinking in the sacred name of tax and taxes - always.

If you make the amazing decision to make the electricity grid a part of the state's infrastructure, you have seriously released the green transition and opened to the broad creativity and renewal urge that exists in the market. Then the market will seriously come into its own, and the commendable in investing privately in DKK 100,000-200,000 in solar cells on the roof would again become meaningful.

Title: Bornholm bliver kun bygget af aktive politikere
Content:

Title: Beof: Vi er nysgerrige på mulighederne ved power-to-x - men ikke som investorer
Content:
Bornholm Energi and Supply will not invest in electrolysis plants, states communications manager Klaus Vesløv. But should Power-to-X be established on Bornholm, it can be of great importance for the future district heating system and wastewater handling.

If Bornholm is to be made hydrogen, ammonia, methanol or other fuels using the future of the abundance of electricity from offshore wind turbines, it will be without Bornholm's energy and supply (BEOF) participation.

-I would like to disprove that Beof has some plans to invest in a power-to-X system, says communications manager Klaus Vesløv.

The reason to establish Beof's strategy is a statement from the Left Group Chairman of the Municipal Council, Søren Schow. In Friday's edition of the Journal, he aired his skepticism towards Power-to-X on Bornholm soil.

-We must first see what a power-to-X system will fill physically. And who is going to make it and what it should be used for. I am also nervous that Bornholm and especially Beof say they should be involved in a power-to-X system.

We have to let that private, said Søren Schow.

When asked by Tidende about Beof's Power toxplanes, Klaus Vesløv explains that the municipal-owned energy and supply group does not have power-to-X skills, and that, among other things, it is why other companies must take the initiative.

- It will be some completely different actors who need to invest. But if there is Power-to-X, we need to be curious about what we as a utility company can get out of it.

If large quantities of surplus heat can help the Bornholmers to get very cheap green heat in the future, then we think we are obliged to explore those opportunities, says Klaus Vesløv.

Heat in excess There is a large waste of heat in the energy -intensive processes where water molecules (H2O) are cleaved into oxygen and hydrogen, and this heat will be with the Beof would like to take over and utilize for district heating.

Both Rønne Water and Heat and Beof already have a desire to receive surplus heat from the large transformer station to Energiø Bornholm. However, the amount of heat that can be harvested from Energinet's giant plant in Sydbornholm does not mean to be large enough to supply most of Bornholm with district heating, Klaus Vesløv reports.

But with Power-to-X production as part of the energy system, reality can become another.

Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners and Ørsted are aiming to use the energy from their proposed offshore wind farms east of Bornholm for hydrogen production. Should the two energy masters decide to establish an electrolysis plant on land - and get the companies the necessary permits from all authorities - it can also affect the BEOF in another supply area. Namely, large amounts of clean and cleaned fresh water must be used for Power-to-X, and an obvious option is to use wastewater as groundwater is a scarce resource.

- This could mean that the wastewater needs to be cleaned 100 percent. We treat five to six million cubic meters a year. It would be excellent if it could become a resource for Bornholm, says Klaus Vesløv.

If the wastewater is to be used for electrolysis, it will require a more thorough cleaning than is the case today, where there are still small quantities in phosphorus in the water emitted into the sea.

Developments in Power-to-X can thus characterize Beof's long-term planning.

For example, the amount of waste heat available will have an impact on the extent to which the separated district heating areas on Bornholm can be bound together. In addition, more waste heat will cause the biomass in the form of straw and wood chips, which today are used on the heat plants can be phased out faster. Many have criticized Denmark for the great use of biomass at the power plants. Tile, wood pellets and straw have the status of CO2-neutral fuels, although CO2 is discharged when the biomass is burned off. In reality, wood is only CO2 neutral if as much new forest is planted as felled, and this is not always the case.

- If there are some options like surplus heat, of course, we think it is quite obvious to utilize it as part of the future heating system, says Klaus Vesløv.

- This could mean that the wastewater needs to be cleaned 100 percent.

We treat five to six million cubic meters a year. It would be excellent if it could become a resource for Bornholm.

Klaus Vesløv Communications Manager Bornholm Energy and Supply.

Title: Find en fælles retning for Bornholms skyld
Content:
Bornholm can also be at the forefront if we dare to formulate a strong, common vision and are clear with what we want to achieve with Energiø Bornholm.

Dear Municipal Council - It is time for you to find common direction for Bornholm's sake.

Thank you to Bornholm Region Municipality for the invitation to participate in a study trip to Green Lab Skive with politicians and officials.

Here we gained insight into Skive's development of a green business park with a focus on synergies and symbiosis between companies around the use of energy and other resources. It is impressive and very inspiring what they have achieved in Skive in a relatively short time. An important factor is that the right timing has had a strong vision, started in and by Skive Municipality, where a unified city council supports the vision. A vision focusing on innovative collaboration. For us, this trip was a wakeup call.

Bornholm can also be at the forefront if we dare to formulate a strong, common vision and are clear with what we want to achieve with Energiø Bornholm and the upcoming business opportunities and not least if we together - municipality, business and workers - work persistently with the possibilities. There should not be much sling in the roller until the chance is missed.

Bornholm gets an energy island, it is facts and not for discussion. In addition to the energy island, there are big plans for the expansion of offshore winds in the Baltic Sea, and here Bornholm is really good at the center of many activities.

The perspectives are therefore enormous, and with such great perspectives there are both potentials and threats that need to be handled. The return on our communities in the form of jobs, more inhabitants, green transition and tax revenue as a result of Energiø Bornholm depends entirely on how we approach it. Overall, you can choose two approaches to these perspectives. You can see it and let the development go without actively taking a stand or running the process. This is probably the approach that we as a business community fear most.

We owe ourselves - the Bornholm society - to take a stand and have an attitude on how to accept the big changes that we are facing. How do we get the most out of the possibilities and what threats should we protect ourselves? What requirements and wishes can we, as a island, to make for the big players who everyone look curiously and interested against Bornholm? Of course, a demand must be made to contribute to Bornholm when, such as Energinet, Ørsted or other large actor, you want to use Bornholm to solve global climate and supply problems.

These requirements and wishes must be formulated.

We must also ensure that the existing companies on Bornholm become part of the future and that we get the most green transition to Bornholm, and then we have to make it attractive for new companies to establish themselves on Bornholm.

There is an exciting job and we find that many talented people are involved. But we also need our politicians to put turbo on their part of the work.

A vision must be prepared for Bornholm, and we must be clear about what we as a island want to get out of the energy island and the expansion of offshore wind in the Baltic Sea. It is a great responsibility our politicians stand with, it requires foresight, courage and above all one common direction that a unified municipal council can persistently support.

It is not time to nurture special interests or make political legs that have characterized the political landscape since the last election.

That's the case too important for.

Our call to the municipal council is therefore: "Take responsibility on you". On the other hand, we, the profession, would very much like to contribute and cooperate in a common direction. If we are many who pull the same way, then we stand stronger!.

Title: Beboere på Sydbornholm retter fokus mod power-to-x: ' Byg anlægget et andet sted'
Content:
