However, at neighbors of the upcoming transformer station, it causes great concern if the mega project is to be expanded with hydrogen production and a green business park. This particular scenario is warning of the latest consultation.

Last week was a Bornholm delegation in Skive to visit the Green-Lab business park, which houses a cluster of companies working on the development of sustainable energy. A similar business and development center could be imagined around the energy island and the future offshore wind farms on Bornholm, and the inspiration from Skive has aroused hopes that it can be possible to attract companies to a green energy park on Bornholm.

- We will get a lot of green power in the energy island. If we can translate it into jobs, it will be good for Bornholm, Jacob said after the visit.

An obvious bid for a location for such a business park is the fields around the transformer station, which is supposed to be erected in Sose north of Sdr. Road. Here, however, the neighbors believe that the transformer station with a fenced area of ​​about 52 hectares and 25 meters high buildings is already more than ample.

In the consultation responses to the Danish Environmental Protection Agency, which the Journal has obtained access to, members of the Citizens' Association warn against the allowing construction of Power-to-X systems, data centers or other energy-heavy companies alongside the transformer station.

"We are pleased to do something to make a nice transformer system, and therefore it will be completely wrong to build a PTX system next to a lot of pipes and tanks as well as smoking chimneys," writes Torben Westh Jensen.

The Citizens' Association Energiø Bornholm, founded by residents in the area last spring, gives a consultation response to frustrations over the development and lack of transparency in the decision -making process.

"We want to be informed by whom and how is Bornholm's population and the interests of the local citizens in this case, where the state takes over such a large area of ​​an island that will be radically changed? Bornholm will go from being a one Ø, which is traditionally based on agriculture, fishing, tourism, food production and light industry to also be the center of production of wind energy and green fuel for Denmark and the European continent ”.

The Citizens' Association requires insight into what arguments and decisions have led to the area southwest of Aakirkeby being selected by Energinet.

- We do not believe that we have been given a proper explanation of why this way has been gone, says Fridrik Adamsson.

Happy of political skepticism In the wake of the visit to Skive, Left group chairman Søren Schow, who was not among the participants, has spoken skeptical about the energy island, power-to-x and the possibilities of creating a local growth adventure on a foundation of green energy.

- If it's a good business for Bornholm, then yes. But how does Bornholm benefit if a power-to-X plant is established on Bornholm? If it is such a good idea as some think, one must also be able to say why it is a good idea and what is more accurate in it, Schow said in the Journal Friday.

At the Citizens' Association Energiø Bornholm, it is delighted that a leading municipal politician is critical of the Energiø visions.

- It is only here lately that it has been discussed by the municipal council.

It is surprising that there has been no political debate in the past, but it seems to be coming now, says Fridrik Adamsson with address to Søren Schow's skeptical statements in the Journal Friday.

Alternatives or not in the consultation response to the Danish Environmental Protection Agency you can read that the Citizens' Association has provided Energinet, that on the stretch from Rønne to Dueodde there is "many areas of the same size, where the approach from the sea to a transmission station is lighter, less harmful to nature and not in Carambola with protected prehistoric defense facilities and the shipwrecks in Sose Bay ". On the Citizens' Association's questions about why Energinet has come to the conclusion that there are no alternatives to the designated gross area, Deputy Director Marian Kaagh replies that “Energinet has assessed areas where it is possible to carry the cables ashore thoroughly, and it is Energy's assessment that there are no useful alternatives to the cables' landing outside the area shown in the consultation material ”.

- I don't give much to that, says Fridrik Adamsson.

He wonders why Energinet does not lead the cables from the offshore wind farms ashore further east, where there are not as steep coastal slopes as in Sose Bay. A conceivable explanation may be that it would increase the total cable length, as the energy island's offshore wind farms are further west.

Unwanted Power-to-X Although the consultation at the Danish Environmental Protection Agency is specifically about the transmission plant and the cable connection to Zealand, the neighbors in the consultation responses emphasize the possibility of establishing Power-to-X plants in connection with the high voltage station.

It can become reality if Ørsted and Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners (CIP) realize the plans for two offshore wind farms east of Bornholm and hydrogen production.

-It would be a disaster if the area is to be further expanded at the CIP's request and a power-to-X plant is placed in extension of this, says Fridrik Adamsson.

Experience from Esbjerg shows that a power-to-X plant does not necessarily have to be erected clutched up the transformer station.

Two weeks ago, Energinet announced that an agreement had been made with CIP and H2Energy to build two new high -voltage connections from Energinet's transformer station in Endrup to an industrial area on the outskirts of Esbjerg about 15 kilometers away, where companies plan to produce ammonia and hydrogen respectively. The Power-to-X supply will make it necessary to expand the existing high-voltage station in Endrup by two areas of about 100 x 250 meters, Energinet reports.

The Citizens' Association has recently asked Energinet whether surplus energy should be made to hydrogen on Bornholm, whether it should be done in the same area that the land plant should be built.

"This question should be accessed by the Danish Energy Agency," replies Deputy Director Marian Kaagh, you can read in the consultation material.

Energinet has previously stated that the high voltage station on Bornholm is prepared for two power-to-X plants if companies are interested in it.

In the consultation response to the Danish Environmental Protection Agency, the local civic association calls for the authorities to make an independent environmental assessment of power-to-x if it becomes relevant.

"The environmental impact report should not allow for the construction of PTX or PTX testing center, as the large amount of chemical substances should not be covered by the upcoming report.

In our local civic association there is great uncertainty and concern about the expansion of the area to include the production of PTX ".

'A Blankocheck' Torben Westh Jensen, who sits on the Citizens' Association's board of directors, demands in a separate consultation response more knowledge of the probability of building electrolysis facilities near the transformer station.

"It is very popular to use abbreviations such as PTX and the like, and when you call it green energy, everything can be done and we forget that there are very dangerous chemical substances and complicated processes with many mistakes. is that we do not know what we say yes to if we do not object and we are writing a blank check to the state where we destroy large natural areas on land and in The sea, and in return we get a lot of nuisance in the form of broken views, noise, light, magnetic fields, danger of explosion, hazard of poisoning etc. Jensen to the Danish Environmental Protection Agency.

He has attached an open letter addressed to Mayor Jacob Solvet, and in which the neighbors' uncertainty is outlined: “It is very stressful for us in and around the area south of Aakirkeby, and we are all challenged with the prospect of significant loss of property value and The joy of life. Must invest more in our houses with this uncertainty, and therefore time is a bit quiet south of Aakirkeby.

We are, as I said, under intense pressure due to the transformer station, and we cannot handle more industrial plants south of Aakirkeby if we are to have any nature back, ”Torben Westh Jensen writes to the mayor.

The two have previously met for a talk about the transformer station. Next week, the Citizens' Association Energiø Bornholm has been invited for the first time to meet with representatives from Bornholm's Regional Community Administration.

Here, the concerns raised in the five -page consultation response will be on the agenda, says Fridrik Adamsson.

We do not believe that we have been given a proper explanation of why this way Fridrik Adamsson has gone.

Title: Turistdirektør: Energiø kan positionere Bornholm som bæredygtig ø - bare husk beplantningen
Content:

Title: Hele området, som giver vand til Risebækken, bør fredes
Content:
The current conservation of Risebækken does not make sense if the area north of Søndre Landevej is transformed into a huge industrial area with large buildings and mast forests as it will destroy Risebækken forever.

Å Bent letter regarding the rescue of Risebækken to Environment Minister Magnus Heunicke, Climate-Energi and Supply Minister Lars Aagaard and Mayor Jacob Consolation.

Dear Magnus, Lars and Jacob.

The members of the Citizens' Association Energiø Bornholm are very concerned about the future of Risebækken in connection with the location of the land plant to Energiø Bornholm.

Risebækken is a stream on Sydbornholm, which with a fantastic beautiful waterfall has its outlet near Risegaard.

Risebækken is quite unique Bornholm nature, and there are currently. Predicted 11 hectares around Risebækken south of Søndre Landevej.

But Risebækken is more than the watercourse and the area south of Søndre Landevej.

The water in Risebækken comes from a large area north of Søndre Landevej, which was called the Duegårdsbeds, which extends from Store Hallegård to Soldiersgård and Duegård and south towards Søndre Landevej.

The Duegårdsbeds are located in the middle of the large gross area, which is designated by Energinet to place the transformer station to Energiø Bornholm.

The Citizens' Association Energiø Bornholm believes that the whole area, which gives water to Risebækken, must be peaceful and either remain agricultural land or be returned, as it was before the plumbing to a large meadow area.

The Danish Society for Nature Conservation has stated that it is 'just' agricultural land, but the good thing about it 'just' is agricultural land is that it can be relatively easily traced back to open streams with meadow area around, which will provide good conditions for biodiversity, such as This is done in several places in Denmark.

The current conservation of Risebækken does not make sense if the area north of Søndre Landevej is transformed into a huge industrial area with large buildings and mast forests as it will destroy Risebækken forever.

Bornholm Regional Municipality writes in its consultation response to the land plant that it is important that nature is taken into account when placing the land plant, and this case shows what what immediately seems to 'just' is to be agricultural land is very much. More below the surface and is linked to nature in the surrounding area all the way down to the sea.

The northeastern corner of the gross area is located very close to Vasegård, where many finds have been made of ancient monuments, and we can expect to find many new ancient finds if it is dug in this area. Likewise, it will be bad for nature to place the transformer station all the way up the Læsåen.

We believe that a new gross area should be appointed, and we have in previous consultation responses made suggestions for better placements of the transformer station.

PTX plants and other industry believe we should be placed in an industrial area near Rønne.

The whole process of designating a large gross area and then letting citizens discuss the final location of the land plant with the famous yellow square, which may or may not be square, we believe is flawed.

The final location of the land plant and thus the yellow square is necessary to announce, and then we believe that Energinet should expropriate or offer to expropriated all houses and properties in a radius of at least two kilometers from the land facility area.

We also believe that legislation should be made, which gives neighbors up to four kilometers from critical infrastructure such as large transformer stations, PTX plants and the like, compensation for lost property value.

This legislation believes we should be made as soon as possible and apply to the energy islands and similar projects.

The Citizens' Association Energiø Bornholm would like to participate and help with the work resulting from Energiø Bornholm, and we think it will be able to improve the entire project if we work together.

Title: Dobbelt op: Kæmpe skævhed i elpriser
Content:
DR has asked the Minister of Energy why electricity prices are almost twice as high on Bornholm compared to the rest of the country. Maybe the solution is a form of compensation or equalization scheme, says Associate Professor of Energy Planning at Aalborg University.

Why should we be punished because we live on a rocky island? This is the headline of an article that dr.dk posted online on Saturday.

Journalist Marie-Louise Rafn from DR Bornholm has in the article set out to investigate why there are such large fluctuations in the Danish electricity market, and in this connection asks the newly appointed climate, energy and supply minister to answer why electricity prices are Almost twice as high on Bornholm compared to the rest of the country and whether it is a matter he would like to go in.

However, it became a cool rejection from the moderate minister: "It is complicated to dig down electric cables and operate an electricity grid on a rocky island like Bornholm (...) I think it is healthy to hold on to the principle that those as a consumer Electricity also pays the costs it entails, ”said Lars Aagaard, among others.

WERMELIN: Deeply frustrating Lea Wermelin (S) is the climate, energy and supply rapporteur in the new SVM government, and Bornholm's Journal therefore asked the local representative at Tinge for a comment on the bias in the price of electricity. She returned on Sunday morning with a principled answer: - It is the perfect storm with inflation, rising energy prices and a bigger difference between prices over the day that have hit Bornholm, she says.

- I can understand that it is deeply frustrating for many Bornholmers who can really feel it in everyday life. Politically, we have lowered the electricity tax here in the first half of 2023 and also made a freezing scheme. And then in total, in Denmark we save about DKK 20 billion in investments in the electricity grid if we get better at using electricity around the clock, so the electric car, for example, is charged at night.

But making spaghetti with meat sauce for dinner can of course not be moved at a completely different time, says Lea Wermelin.

While citizens in the Triangle area in Jutland, for example, pay 1.57 kroner per kilowatt-time in Nettarif in the most expensive hours of the day, a citizen of Bornholm pays DKK 2.9 per kilowatt hour. So almost twice as much.

The new price system has been adopted in the Folketing.

From January 1, lack of electricity companies began to divide the day into three pricing zones - low loads, high loads and peak loads, where the peak load is the most expensive hours. Often, the companies spend the expensive hours between 5 pm and 9 pm. This means that an average Bornholm family with an annual consumption of 4,000 kilowatts has to pay DKK 4,360 in tax and subscription, while a similar family in Kolding pays DKK 2,460.

So a difference of DKK 1,900.

- It may not be true that there is that difference, says Ryan Andersen to DR. He lives in Melsted and is at the forefront of a Facebook group where the Bornholmers can be gathered in protest of the Nettariffs. At the time of writing, the group has over 1,000 members.

Compensation or equalization 45 percent of TREFOR's additional costs by operating the Bornholm electricity grid is due to the net loss, ie the surplus production that is lost to ensure a smooth power supply. And net loss is significantly larger in areas like Bornholm than it is for Trefors customers in the Triangle area.

TREFOR states to DR that a reduction in the power tax on Bornholm would require customers to subside twice as much power or that there should be twice as many customers connected to the network.

Peter Sorknæs, associate professor of energy planning at Aalborg University, compares the electricity supply network with the road network and believes that one can talk about an inequality in the system.

According to DR, he believes that politicians will be able to make some form of compensation or equalization scheme, provided such a scheme complies with EU rules.

Huge potential in the energy island In the end, it is up to the Folketing to decide whether it should be more expensive to settle on Bornholm than elsewhere, and Lea Wermelin has already been in contact with the Ministry of Climate to hear about the high power prices on Bornholm.

- I have asked about the very high tariffs in the Ministry of Climate, and the tariff increases are especially about covering the net loss, which becomes more expensive when the price of energy is more expensive.

The ministry follows that development and is in dialogue with the industry about it, says Lea Wermelin to Bornholm's Journal.

She does not believe that the high prices will be deterrent to people who are considering moving to Bornholm.

- Our task is also to ensure that energy prices are again lower. They are historically high right now. My expectation is that Bornholm will play a very important role in the green transition as an energy island and that we have a huge potential here. There is a need for both the municipality and us parliamentary members to throw in a lot of effort, so that we get the most benefit from the energy island locally.

Title: Skal der gå en sprækkedal mellem bygningerne eller plantes en masse træer?
Content:
Architects from Arkitema on Thursday presented several concepts for how the land facility to Energiø Bornholm can be adapted to the landscape. The king's idea is to make a design that reinforces the existing landscape traits.

Bornholm University College housed a workshop on Thursday evening on the design of the future large high -voltage facility in Sydbornholm.

A team of architects from Arkitema as well as two external advisers have been hired by Energinet to come up with their suggestions on how to fit the distinctive land facility to Energiø Bornholm in the existing arable landscape.

Participants were presented with several architectural concepts, including the "El-Mindingen", "The Big mark" and "The Crack Valley", located in different places within the gross area that Energinet works north of Søndre Landevej.

The idea of ​​the "electricity mind" involves a comprehensive planting around the plant, which must be placed "discreetly in the landscape behind the forest and lake", as stated on the presentation.

The fields in the area have been drained for decades, and the architects' preliminary drawings show that work is being done to utilize the water as an asset. The crevice valley concept contains a stream (the upper part of the Risebækken), which flows between the technical plants, which are divided into two halves. The last idea, "The Big mark", is referred to as "an exposed plant, framed by the landscape", and here too the water from the creek gets an aesthetic and recreational function.

On the three roll-ups, the buildings are different. On one illustration, the corners are rounded, on another pours the walls, while the halls on the last drawings are completely square.

The concepts have been developed on the basis of the comments from the workshop that took place at the college in December, explains architect Christian Platz from Arkitema.

- They are all about taking some of the landscape traits that exist in advance and reinforcing them, he says of the three ideas presented by the architects on Thursday night.

The technical plant of the high -voltage system, which is to be placed behind fences, has an area of ​​about 52 hectares, and some of the buildings are expected to protrude 25 meters above the fields.

The evening's workshop was the second and last in the series. March 20, Energinet and Arkitema will present a comprehensive presentation at an event at the Electricity Work in Rønne. Energinet promises that the presentation "will form the basis for the design of Energinet's high voltage station and the subsequent local planning process".

Most of the workshop took place after the newspaper's deadline. Read a longer report on Journal.dk Friday.

Title: Landanlægget kan overraske os positivt
Content:
It draws astonishingly beautiful with the upcoming land plant for the energy island -so should it.

On Thursday evening, Energinet presented its architectural and engineering work on the design of the giant land plant to the huge offshore wind farm, which we call Energiø Bornholm. Fortunately, it is far more promising than most of us expected.

Normally, one will fear an industrial concrete system with hard edges and cold surfaces fenced in pigeon wire fencing that sends thoughts against unpleasant prison camps. But that's not how it looks when the engineers and architects show off their sketches. On the contrary.

The architects' dream sketches show buildings packed in Hasleklinke-like tiles and muted earth colors. This makes the plant less alienating and industrial. There are also boldly inserted round corners and sloping walls that again make the construction more organic and are somewhat reminiscent of Viking castles or Asian temples. On top of the warm colors and round and sloping forms, there are still thoughts of packing the building green with the electric forest, so that nature will dampen the brutal construction, which also contributes to the experience that the building is not so human.

With its existence, the land plant is a gigantic tribute to our nature because it receives and transforms huge quantities is revolutionary green energy to transform our society and preserve our globe. But basically it is not a beautiful construction. Therefore, the new grips, which have very much come from the last civic meeting, strong and good initiatives.

But the most successful idea presented at the Citizens' Meeting on Thursday is the idea of ​​leading Risebækken in between the large buildings and building a public promenade close to the buildings.

By letting the pelvis ripple between the green energy mastodont and allow ordinary citizens to get very close to the incomprehensible forces, we open the green energy project and make it a common experience to feel the great forces packed in earth colors and forest. The land plant will be able to compare with Hammerhus and bison oxen as an excursion destination.

The next task is now that the municipality insists that Energinet does not throw the savings card and yet build a discount building with steel, concrete and barbed wire.

Earth colors and soft edges The architects also present three suggestions on how the large buildings can be designed.

On the drawings, the buildings have a reddish brown shade and work has been done on patterns on the facades.

Arkitema has gathered some bids on the building materials on a table. The color choice is a result of the Bornholmers' remarks during the December workshop.

Excursion destinations in front of the "crack valley" more people are captivated by the opportunity to get close to the high -voltage buildings and have an experience.

- The easiest thing for me would be to gather the buildings in a square block here, he explains a guest and at the same time mentions that Energinet's people will take on the architects' ideas as a challenge.

- And then we have to try to draw the engineering profession afterwards.

Requirements for the high barre idea of ​​the path is that it must connect Naturbornholm and Klintebakken in the north with Risebækken and the south coast. The idea of ​​creating a passage down between the energy island with an element of nature restoration of the pelvis, which today lies in cordy trenches along the fields, appeals to Bjarne Westerdahl, who as Chairman of the Board of Naturbornholm is involved in nature dissemination. He does not belong to the circle that is concerned with hiding the high voltage system as much as possible.

- We need to be able to tell our guests that it is in there we have the energy island, he says.

- I think there will be a lot of attention to it during the construction process and for a while to come. We, who come here often, will see it for a year and a half, and then do not notice it, he says, comparing it to traffic signs you pass every day.

He hopes that the municipality will be steeply on some requirements for the architectural design - it is now that we set the bar, says Bjarne Westerdahl.

Uncertainty until April with outdoor areas for rainwater pools and landscape camouflage such as earth and planting, the station is expected to get an area of ​​70-90 hectares. Energinet works from a gross area of ​​just over 250 hectares (2.5 square kilometers), which are bounded by Sdr. Road in the south and Limensgaden in the east. Around the hall, there are people who most of all want answers to exactly where Energinet ends up placing the approximately 55 hectares of fence.

One of them is Benny Hansen, who lives with his wife and two children on Hallegårdsvejen in the northwestern part of the gross area. He then makes them aware that one of the farms on the edge of the gross area has long been uninhabited and that you will touch a few people if you place the land facility in the northwestern part of the area and can avoid affecting housing along Sdr. Road.

At 21.15, Energinet's chief project manager rounded off and thanked the interest, after which the organizers of the workshop peeled the colored notes with comments down from the stands. Title: Energinet: Idéen om sprækkedal rummer flere usikkerheder

It is something we work on ourselves, because we have not shared a plant in such a way before. So whether it is practically possible to do so, we are working hard to find out. It's not something we dare say today.

Can you say that it is the architects' imagination that the engineers of you now have to try? - Yes, and we really make every effort to find solutions to the suggestions. These are two things that run in parallel and we have to find out how it lands.

The economic realities are also a parameter for you. Do you have a ceiling to keep in? - It's there, and it's also a parameter.

But I know we have not looked at the financial consequences (of the architectural process, ed.) Yet.

A presentation must be presented March 20.

Title: Vi kan stadig tabe det hele på gulvet
Content:
We must see the possibilities and not the limitations of Bornholm's energy adventure, writes Left's Peter Juel-Jensen.

B Ornholm will be the world's first energy island and huge amounts of electricity from wind turbines located south of the island will produce so much electricity by 2030 that it will cover the energy consumption of over three million Danish households. But not only that. The two Danish companies Ørsted and Copenhagen Infastructure Partners have also noticed Bornholm, and together they have ambitious plans for the establishment of two large wind farms east of Bornholm, which will be ready before the energy island.

The many plans for Danish wind farms follow the proud tradition we have in Denmark to focus on wind power and renewable energy. For decades we have been a pioneer in Denmark in the work of yielding wind power.

And at Bornholm we are already well in the process of becoming part of the wind adventure.

For the past few years, the port of Rønne has placed itself as the most attractive shipping port for offshore wind in the Baltic Sea.

And several Bornholm companies through the network collaboration Offshore Center Bornholm also get part in assignments on subcontracting.

Vestas, which is a world's largest producers of wind turbines, recently announced that throughout the Baltic Sea region there is only one port that can now handle Vesta's new mills - namely Rønne Harbor. So the harbor in Rønne shows the way for what is waiting ahead. Bornholm can become a green energy center in the Baltic Sea. The challenge is to bring the whole island.

The plans for the green development are large, and we need to play as a island and society to that extent.

We have already spent far too long waiting and disagreeing locally. It is high time that local politicians and the local business community work together to ensure that we are also together in the work to ensure local development and growth.

A number of business organizations on Bornholm came the other day with a singing in Bornholm's Tidende that we can be at the forefront if we dare to formulate a strong, common vision and are clear with what we want to achieve with Energiø Bornholm.

I can't agree more. With the ambitious energy plans, Bornholm also has great opportunities to create growth and development not only for Bornholmers, but for all Danes.

But right now there is a great risk that the possibilities are lost on the floor if we do not take together as Bornholmers and start focusing on the possibilities, we can help create and not least what we as an island can get out of that join.

At Bornholm we have a tradition of living off money coming over. We are Danish champion in grants and eminent to get support for local projects. The energy plans, on the other hand, give us Bornholmers an opportunity for us to live off our own money and develop projects that create growth on Bornholm.

The energy island is much more than the wind turbines at sea, right now, the US, China and Europe are vying to become home to the green transition - Americans are launching a giant aid package of DKK 2,500 billion, and also invites European companies to join - China has their very own way of getting technology, but also has strong economic muscles. The energy island provides opportunities to develop the morning's technological solutions, but it takes courage to commit to the future and see the possibilities, and make demands so that we at Bornholm also get other than cables and mills. The harbor and a number of companies have bet, and it has borne fruit - it would be a mistake to run the other way, as the energy island would like to be one of the things we have to live in in the future.

But if we are to succeed, it requires that we succeed in seeing the possibilities and not the limitations of Bornholm's energy adventure. As politicians, we should work together and we should listen to the local business community when they make us aware that there is a need to stand together.

As a island, we need to demand that we get Bornholm to become part of the opportunities that are created. There are a number of obvious opportunities in giving us so much renewable energy just outside our window.

Why do we not require that we have, for example, the surplus energy that comes out of the projects. And why are we not starting to work on creating projects that can ensure that we as a society on Bornholm become part of the adventure.

I seriously fear that we will not succeed in seeing the possibilities, but only the limitations of Bornholm's energy adventure.

It will be a shame for both Bornholm and Denmark.

Title: Energiøen - muligheder og omkostninger
Content:
Energiø Bornholm is a unique and historical opportunity for the island, writes Mayor Jacob Trøst (K). COMMENT.

E Nergiøen on Bornholm is moving closer, and it is increasingly filling the consciousness of many of us. We probably ask the questions: What does it mean for Bornholm, and what opportunities do it entail? I have therefore started the planning of an open civic meeting where everyone can come and become wiser on the whole project and the opportunities for Bornholm.

I have spent much of my first year as mayor to put myself into just those questions, because it is a historically big decision, and no matter how we choose to approach it, it will have an impact on the entire future of Bornholm .

Last year we were to set a budget for 2023 in Bornholm's regional municipality, where we looked into some massive savings because we have too low tax revenue compared to our expenses. We simply lack revenue.

We need them when we have to ensure that our children have a good framework in their upbringing, and our elderly get a safe and human care when they need it, as well as all the other municipal tasks we have to solve.

The budget for 2024 is getting even worse I can already reveal now, and I also think we all agree that we would like to make ourselves independent of the pool for particularly difficult municipalities that have provided relief in the form of million grants to our operations in the latest year. And if we are to maintain the current level of service in the regional municipality in the future, then it requires us to become 42,000 inhabitants to pay.

I also think most of us have come to the realization that we must hand over a sustainable society to our children and grandchildren.

That we need to do what we can to look after nature and climate, and maybe even deliver it in better condition than we even received it. But the green transition costs.

Not just money, but also views and area.

Some will claim that we can just build nuclear power.

Poland is planning a work on the other side of the Baltic Sea. It will be significantly larger than the land facility we are looking for at Sydbornholm, but will produce roughly the same amount of energy, and at a more expensive price per year. Megawatt. The director of Seaborg, which is developing a new form of nuclear power, Troels Schönfeldt, stated last year that Denmark does not have time to wait for their (Seaborg's) new technology, but should continue to invest in sun and wind energy. So we do.

Energiø Bornholm consists of an offshore wind farm and a land plant, and during the construction phase, which probably lasts about five years, up to 600 men (m/ k) must be used for the establishment. When the wind turbines are in operation, the experience of other similar plants says that about 50 men are needed per year. Gigawatt, ie In this case, 150-200 men, for servicing the wind turbines; So people who sail out to the mills and maintain them. It can be electricians, blacksmiths and other people with a relevant education.

If CIP/ Ørsted's plans for offshore wind 40 km from Bornholm's east coast are realized, we can times the above numbers with two.

All the people must also eat, transport, have clothes and houses to live in and buy in, and here it is expected that a similar number will be engaged in the derived professions.

Both Rønne and Tejn, but especially Nexø are also obvious as ports of the ships to service the wind turbines. It will create a whole new life on the ports and in the cities around, and attract the professions that can provide goods and assistance to the work.

The land plant itself does not provide many jobs in operations, but the large amounts of electricity that are produced can be used for many purposes, and this is where even more options arise.

Today you often see wind turbines standing still, although the wind is blowing. This is mainly due to the fact that we cannot subside or store all the current being produced.

In large offshore wind projects, you are of course interested in utilizing the wind energy all the time, and therefore there is great interest in using excess wind energy to produce green fuels (Power-to-X or PTX), such as hydrogen, so there is also there is energy to when the wind does not blow or the sun does not shine. Or to propel aircraft where batteries are not an option because they are too heavy.

DAT has announced that they are working to fly on hydrogen as early as 2025.

The Gotland Cola, which sails between Sweden and Gotland, has announced that they will introduce a hydrogen -powered fast ferry by 2030. So it is not only "birds on the roof", although the development is of course in its early start.

PTX can also cause other green fuels such as e-ammonia and e-metanol; Each fuel has its advantages and disadvantages, and among other things the ship industry is clarifying which is the best.

In the production of green fuels, a lot of water and a lot of power must be used. Esbjerg plans to use the area's wastewater for this production. In the process, both oxygen and a lot of heat are emitted, which are surplus products.

The heat can be used for district heating and oxygen can be used for more effective degradation of the sludge from the wastewater. However, there will be such large amounts of surplus heat that it also allows for alternative use, such as horticulture in the style of those seen in Iceland, where hot springs enable the production of vegetables all year round.

The Technical University of Denmark (DTU) has for a number of years been very active on Bornholm, as we are close to being an ideal "test society" where it is easy to measure output in relation to input when new technology is to be tested and new engineers need to Educated. We are isolated in the Baltic Sea and results can be easily scaled up so that it can be counted on how it can be introduced into the rest of the country or elsewhere in the world.

For the same reason, DTU is an important partner when we try to get the old beautiful and protected power plant in Rønne transformed into the home of our commercial lighthouse Baltic Energy Island, which will include a residential college.

Right now, unique negotiations between municipalities, ministries, private actors and educational institutions are taking place to succeed. It will attract new skills, new knowledge and data to Bornholm and it will help to strengthen our companies' competitiveness and accelerate the green transition.

A residential college can also benefit both campus, the hospital, the Bornholm Museum and others who may need temporary housing for students.

We are concerned about our unique nature.

The land plant will fill 70-90 hectares, and although it is "only" 0.15 % of Bornholm's area, it will of course with buildings up to 25 meters high, of course fill in the landscape. Fortunately, a great deal of work is being done to get it fit into the landscape, so that it creates the least possible nuisance for nature and neighbors. And should we get there that we want more space for green companies, then it is obvious to demand that part of the areas be laid out for biodiversity.

Others are concerned about tourism on Bornholm overlooking wind turbines and land facilities. By comparison, tourism on Fanø is not affected by all guests having to drive through Esbjerg first. At Bornholm, on the other hand, we have received more visits from abroad, precisely because we are far ahead with the green transition.

There are many who would like to see with their own eyes, and maybe even take inspiration with their homeland.

Energiø Bornholm is a unique and historical opportunity for the island. An opportunity to create development and workplaces, attract new businesses and education, and ultimately make Bornholm 100 percent sustainable and self -sufficient as one of the first places in the world. But it also has costs, and we have to talk about that in an open dialogue.

Are we seeing the Citizens' Meeting?.

Today's debate quote both Rønne and Tejn, but especially Nexø is also obvious as ports of the ships to service the wind turbines.

It will create a whole new life on the ports and in the cities around, and attract the professions that can provide goods and assistance to the work.

Title: Havvindmølleprojekt må vente: ' Det er drønærgerligt'
Content:
You can get permission to set up offshore wind turbines in two ways. The case processing for one of them is now put on hold, which also pauses Bornholm's offshore wind. ENERGY.

D is now pressed for what could potentially have been many more Danish offshore wind turbines. The case processing of offshore wind turbine projects and other wind energy projects under the so-called open door scheme is now on hold. The Danish Energy Agency stated in a press release on Monday. The open door scheme is one of the two ways that in Denmark can be allowed to establish an offshore wind farm. Here, a project developer sends an unsolicited application. The other option is by a tender where the state offers a project, as is the case, for example, at Energiø Bornholm, and it annoys the person for Bornholm's offshore wind, Helle Munk Ravnborg, that it will not be possible to send applications in the open door right now -The scheme.

- This means that if we submit our application now, they will not be able to start the processing of it, and of course it is daring. But don't think they think so too, so you do everything to find out quickly. I would think that, says Helle Munk Ravnborg.

Application paused on the Bornholm Sea Wind Association wants to set up a locally owned offshore wind farm with a capacity of 100 megawatts, and you were finally ready to send the first part of the application, under the current closed open door scheme, to the Danish Energy Agency, says the person.

- We had warned the Danish Energy Agency that we would submit our application in two parts, because we have to gather the financing of people, but the technical part we have more or less in place where only the last investigations are missing. We expect to get in place within the next few weeks, and we are almost ready to send that part of the application, but it does not make much sense when it is not to be treated now, she says and continues: - We know very little so far, but I assume that you do not pause it with such short notice without a very good reason for it. It will be interesting to find out what it is.

Farewell to the low electricity bill The Danish Energy Agency states in the press release that the case processing under the open door scheme has been put on hold, as the allocation of permits under the scheme may be contrary to EU law.

Therefore, the case processing of all ongoing cases has been put on hold until the case has been investigated, it is stated.

This is what Ulrich Bang, the market manager for climate, energy and the environment in the Danish Business, wonders.

He points out that the scheme has existed since 1999.

- I'm a bit shocked. It seems absurd that the treatment is now put on hold on the basis of something that may be state -ridiculous that has been around for 24 years, he says, according to Ritzau.

He points out that there are currently existing applications of 13 gigawatts. Dansk Erhverv has calculated what significance it can have for the Danes.

- If we take the six gigawatts that Ørsted and CIP have talked about alone, it could reduce the electricity bill for the Danes by ten billion kroner. The fact is that if it does not come through, the Danes can bid farewell to the low electricity bill they would otherwise have hoped for, says Ulrich Bang.

The project Melem Ørsted and CIP, mentioned, are the two offshore wind farms that Ørsted has entered into an agreement to try to get built in collaboration with the investment company CIP SYD and East of Bornholm.

You must have a number of permits from the Danish Energy Agency in order to set up offshore wind turbines.

First, one must have permission to do studies at sea and how it affects nature in the area. Then you can get an establishment approval and then permission to utilize the energy. Along the way, the application is also submitted for consultation. So far, Bornholm's offshore wind must be armed with patience.

- We can't do much more than wait and see, and then we can instead send our application together when hopefully soon it will be opened up again, says Helle Munk Ravnborg.

Title: Peter Juel er ' meget bestyrtet' over statens pauseknap
Content:
Completely strange if the state administration puts the stumbling thread in for more offshore wind, which Brede Christiansborg majority has been working on establishing for several years, says the Bornholm MP, who will initially move on with the SAG internally in the Left.

It comes to the back of MP Peter Juel-Jensen (V) to read that officials in the Ministry of Energy and Climate Last summer were already looking for opportunities to reject new offshore wind turbines under the open door scheme that was officially paused on Monday.

Documents provided in an access to Zetland show that the officials had several possible justifications up to the turn, and that a consideration of the state's economy in the upcoming state energy islands weighed heavily in the office's quest for reasons for rejecting privately funded offshore wind turbines according to the open door scheme.

- It's very new to me. I do not hope that the information about the Ministry's behavior is in line with the truth, says Peter Juel-Jensen.

After finding Zetland's article, the Bornholm MP states that he will talk about the case with Left's political spokesman Morten Dahlin and climate mayor Linnea Søgaard-Lidell.

- Over the past two years we have spent a lot of energy at establishing more offshore winds at Christiansborg, because it is one of the cheapest ways to get more green energy for Denmark. Then it seems completely strange that other places in the state administration try to put the stumbling thread for the same projects, says Peter Juel-Jensen.

The Left man also wonders that neither the European Commission nor the Commissioner Margrethe Vestager knew of a possible conflict between the open door scheme and EU law before the government on Monday paused 33 planned offshore wind turbine projects, justified by the possible conflict.

-It seems strange that just here for 11 hours you become aware that the offshore wind turbines can be in conflict with EU law after the open door scheme, he says.

Peter Juel-Jensen finds the case directly relevant on Bornholm, because Ørsted and CIP have applications for two new offshore wind farms near Bornholm among the 33 who were put on hold on Monday.

- I am very stunned, also on behalf of the Bornholm community. We are in the process of taking a very difficult talk about the upcoming energy island. Then it's bad if it's all just something we play, he says.

- The energy island should be a good cause, because it points in one direction out of the slightly pessimistic suppedas that we are in on Bornholm. Now we stand with something that can bring us out of the suppedas in a way that points forward, too, for the rest of the country. This is why it can make me the wing-band if it turns out that someone in the state administration has not had pure flour in the bag, says Peter Juel-Jensen.

The fact that the regional municipality managed to get the energy of the idea of ​​an architectural course with workshops where the Bornholmers have been able to influence the design, Jacob sees comfort as proof that the collaborative strategy has made sense.

- Some say we have a hidden agenda, but we put it up as we know. There are still many uncertain factors. For example, we do not know what the land plant will look like, and whether Bornholm is attractive to the companies that want to make Power-to-XS-or whether Bornholm Elnet will be linked to the energy island, Jacob lists comfort.

Title: CRT gør vejen kortere fra Christiansborg til Christianshøj
Content:
I Hasle sidder en gruppe forskere, der ikke alene studerer de regionale udviklingsmuligheder her på øen, men overalt i de danske landdistrikter.

Vil man kende fremtidens muligheder og udfordringer for Bornholm, er det en god idé at køre en tur til Hasle. Her sidder en gruppe forskere, der ikke alene studerer de regionale udviklingsmuligheder her på øen, men overalt i de danske landdistrikter.

Men med hovedsæde i Hasle.

Center for Regional-og Turismeforskning (CRT) har også en underafdeling i København, hvor halvdelen af centrets 15 medarbejdere blandt andet er beskæftiget med at (videre) udvikle en økonomisk model, som Finansministeriet bruger. Men her i Hasle bliver der forsket på livet løs i, hvordan man bedst får udviklet landets landdistrikter, forklarer centrets leder Anne Thomas smilende.

Direktøren hælder kaffe op, mens hun forklarer, at det var interessen for regional udvikling, der både fik hende til at gå ind i politik og senere forlade sin politiske post som viceborgmester på Bornholm for Alternativet, da muligheden bød sig til at blive leder af CRT.

- Jeg har egentlig en baggrund som eksportingeniør.

Men jeg sad i bestyrelsen for CRT, fordi jeg interesserede mig meget for regional udvikling. Og da posten som leder blev ledig, blev jeg opfordret til at søge den.

Anne Thomas fik jobbet på betingelse af, at hun forlod politik, så det gjorde hun. For selvom viceborgmesterposten var både givende og krævende, var kommunalbestyrelsesarbejdet trods alt kun en fritidsbeskæftigelse.

Og stillingen her var et drømmejob, der sjældent bliver ledigt.

- Jeg er jo også stadig engageret i øens udvikling.

Det er bare en anden vinkel, jeg har på det nu.

Anne Thomas tiltrådte stillingen i 2019 - få måneder inden coronakrisen gjorde hende til en chef, der næsten udelukkende kunne tale med sine medarbejdere på computerskærmen.

- Så jeg føler næsten lige, at jeg er landet.

Men siden jeg kom til, har vi også flyttet kontor, forklarer hun.

DISKUTERER ØENS FREMTID Den bornholmske del af forskningscentret lå tidligere i de historiske rammer i Nexø på Stenbrudsgården, hvor renoveringen var foretaget af genbrugsmaterialer, der pegede tilbage i tiden. Nogle af håndtagene var endda fra 1600-tallet. Det var derfor også rent arkitektonisk en forandring, da centret sidste år flyttede fra Nexø ind i helt moderne lokaler i Hasle. Indenfor har Gudhjem-kunstneren til gengæld skabt fire store vægmalerier af de fire årstider, der sætter farve på de billigere lokaler, som på flere planer peger ind i en bæredygtig fremtid.

- Vi tog en budgetgennemgang i forbindelse med coronanedlukningen og fandt ud af, at vi før betalte over 60.000 kroner per skrivebordsplads, så det var meget billigere her, men vi har faktisk været rigtig glade for at skifte, fordi det gav et behageligere indeklima at være her end i den ellers besjælede gamle bygning. Men her har vi også fået det her meget lyse, åbne lokale, hvor vi har haft vores videnscafeer, siger hun og nikker mod det åbne lokale.

- Før var det mest tænkt til at fortælle om vores arbejde, men nu er det også tænkt som en slags netværkscafeer for især øens beslutningstagere, så vi giver plads til, at de kan diskutere, hvor Bornholm skal hen. og hvordan arbejder man med regional udvikling.

Sidst vi havde videnscafe var folketingspolitikeren Peter Juel-Jensen, borgmester Jacob Trøst og hospitalschefen blandt andre med, forklarer hun.

- Frem for vi bare alene står og siger, hvad vi har fundet ud af, ville vi gerne skabe et forum, hvor man også i en bredere kreds kan få drøftet nogle af de her ting, der er afgørende for øens udvikling. Skal vi have en energiø? Og hvordan får vi kompetencerne til det? Skal der være en uddannelse til den? Alt det, som vi sidder og forsker i, er jo dybt relevant for Bornholm, siger hun med et smil.


OPSTOD MIDT SI KRISE

Da Anne Thomas tiltrådte sin stilling i - i 2019 - havde centret 25 års-jubilæum.

- Det startede med, at der var nogle forskere på Bornholm. Jeg tror, det startede med et EU-projekt, der så blev gjort permanent, selvom forskningscentre normalt skal være tilknyttet et universitet eller være et såkaldt GTS-institut som meteorologisk institut eller teknologisk institut, men vores center fik en særstatus. På det tidspunkt havde der været en stor krise på Bornholm i 1990' erne. Det var virkelig tungt, så man havde besluttet sig for at lave en bornholmerpakke, og så kom vi på finansloven.

I alt arbejder der i dag 15 medarbejdere på centret. Men det er ikke alle, der sidder på Bornholm.

Center for Regional-og Turismeforskning (CRT) har også en underafdeling i København, hvor halvdelen af centrets 15 medarbejdere blandt andet er beskæftiget med at (videre) udvikle den eneste regionaløkonomiske model i Danmark. Men centrets hovedsæde ligger altså i Hasle. Og her bliver der forsket i, hvordan man bedst får udviklet landets landdistrikter.

- I dag er der meget stille, siger Anne Thomas nærmest undskyldende, mens hun viser rundt.

- Her sidder normalt Marianne fra administrationen.

Derinde sidder et it-firma, som også er vores it-supporter. Her har vi seks forskere siddende, men vi har også forskere ansat i København. Men det her er Jesper Manneke, siger hun og nikker mod en smilende mand.

- Han sidder især med erhvervsforskning og med forskellen på, hvordan man laver innovation i små lokale virksomheder i forhold til, hvordan man driver innovation i nogle af de højteknologiske eksportvirksomheder.

Men du forsker også i cirkulær økonomi, ikke? - Jo, det er jo et lille sted, så du skal vide lidt om det hele, svarer han.

I øjeblikket arbejder han blandt andet selv med flere projekter i forbindelse med Bornholm som energiø og problemstillingen med mangel på arbejdskraft, forklarer han.

- Jeg arbejder en del med statistik og meget store registerdata i vores model, der kan fremskrive tendenserne på arbejdsmarkedet.

På den måde kan man forudse, hvad man kommer til at mangle af forskellige typer arbejdskraft i år det og det i den og den landsdel, siger Jesper Manneke.


KLÆDER POLITIKERE PÅ

Forskningen bruges af forskellige landdistriktsaktører både nationalt og decentralt rundt omkring i landet. Her på øen er forskningen fra CRT for eksempel med til at klæde kommunalbestyrelsen på til at træffe beslutninger, men helt generelt er forskningen både rettet mod borgerne, de forskellige aktører i landdistrikterne og politikerne på Christiansborg, som har til opgave at udvikle en egn som Bornholm, forklarer Anne Thomas.

- Vi forsker i arbejdsmarkedet, turisme, kommunale forskelle og i det hele taget erhvervsfremme, siger Anne Thomas, der selv er involveret i flere af centrets projekter, men helst undgår for meget fagforskning, så der også er tid til ledelse.

- Min dagligdag er jo delt lidt mellem København og Bornholm. Jeg er i hvert fald gennemsnitlig minimum en dag om ugen i København. Det kan så være to dage nogle gange. Nogle gange starter min dag derfor med at tage til København. Som direktør er min opgave selvfølgelig, at der er en retning på, så vi som center får en fælles fortælling, som folk kan følge med i.

Det handler kort sagt om at gøre vejen kortere fra Christiansborg til både Christianshøj og Christiansfeld.

- Når man sidder i København og arbejder på Christiansborg, så er det nogle gange svært at se den virkelighed, der foregår i de her meget forskellige 98 kommuner, vi har.

Så det er vores opgave at sikre os, at beslutningstagerne kender de meget nuancerede virkeligheder, de meget nuancerede forskelle, der er på, hvad det vil sige at være en dansker.

Fordi hvis man ikke forstår nuancerne, så kommer man nogle gange til at lave nogle beslutninger, som man ikke har gennemtænkt.

Og for os er det ikke afgørende, om de tager den ene eller den anden beslutning.

For os er det afgørende, at de ved, hvad de gør, når de tager beslutningen.

Så det er det, der er vores opgave, det er at sørge for, at beslutningstagerne kender nuancerne i deres valg.

Så I arbejder også for politikerne på Christiansborg? - Ja, det gør vi. Det er en del af min hverdag også at være til møder i forskellige ministerier eller udvalg på Christiansborg, der har med landdistrikterne at gøre.

Kan du give et eksempel på, hvordan der er forskelle på at være dansker afhængig af, hvor du bor? - Turismechefers job afhænger for eksempel meget af, hvor de bor. I Esbjerg handler det groft sagt om at sælge sommerhus til tyskere, og i København handler det lige så firkantet sagt om at sælge hoteller til kinesere.

Og det ene sted vil kunderne have natur, mens de det andet sted vil have kultur og indkøb. På samme vis er det også, hvis man er en virksomhed i københavnsområdet, så arbejder man måske med finansiering, og man har 100 ansatte, hvoraf de 90 har en videregående uddannelse.

- Hvis man er en virksomhed på Bornholm, så har man måske fire ansatte, og chefen er også faglært. Og der er ikke tid til at lave de store strategier og rekrutteringsplaner og innovationsprojekter. Det er bare en helt anden virkelighed.

KOMPLICEREDE REGNESTYKKER Den virkelighed skal man som politiker forstå, når der skal afsættes penge til udviklingen rundt omkring i landet.

- I landdistrikterne starter virksomhederne tit i det små med en hobby, der vokser sig større. Så hvis man laver en lov, hvor man bare tænker, at virkeligheden består af højteknologiske virksomheder, der kan arbejde sammen med universiteter, så har man altså glemt en meget stor del af Danmarks erhvervsliv.

Så det er sådan nogle ting, vi skal huske, og det peger vores forskning også på, siger Anne Thomas og forklarer, at kravene til grøn omstilling for eksempel også rammer skævt i landet. I Danmark er det blot 14 brancher, der står for 90 procent af CO2-udledningen.

Og når man beder virksomhederne om at reducere deres CO2-udslip med 70 procent, rammer det derfor især bestemte brancher.

- I København bliver erhvervslivet stort set ikke ramt. Men på Bornholm er det 15 procent af vores arbejdsmarked, der arbejder i en klima-eksponeret branche, som - Vi har ikke lavet en opskrift på Bornholms sjæl. Men vi arbejder for eksempel med at undersøge, hvad betyder, når der bliver man kalder det. Det gælder ikke mindst landbruget. Hvis de skal leve op til CO2-kravene, så skal de rykke sig rigtig meget, ellers så bliver det bare svært at være landmand, siger hun.

CRT's forskere har blandt andre også interviewet en del landmænd om arbejdsmarkedets udfordringer, mens et andet stort forskningsprojekt handler om at undersøge, hvilke tilflyttere der kommer til øen.

- Vi undersøger, hvor mange af dem, der får hjælp på Business Center Bornholm, og hvad er det for nogle typer, der kommer ind den vej med tilflytterguiden Rune Holm, og hvem der kommer bare af sig selv. Og det kan godt blive nogle komplicerede regnestykker, siger hun og griner.

- Vi har mange, mange datatråde, for vi har direkte adgang til Danmarks Statistiks data, siger Anne Thomas og tilføjer, at centret endda også samarbejder på tværs af landegrænser for at forske i landdistrikterne, herunder Bornholm. For sommetider kan det være godt at kigge ud i verden for at blive klogere på sig selv, som hun siger.

Hvad er den største udfordring for at udvikle det bornholmske samfund? - At få arbejdsmarkedet til at fungere, svarer hun straks.

- Det er en høne og ægget-ting for Bornholm, for vi kan faktisk se en nøje sammenhæng mellem indbyggertallet og hvor mange job, der har været. Med den grønne omstilling er det jo nogle andre typer job, der kommer til at være fremover. Det bliver overhovedet ikke nemt. Det er ikke umuligt, men det bliver overhovedet ikke nemt at sørge for, at de rette personer bor på Bornholm til et eksisterende job.

Kommer der flere akademiske jobtyper med den grønne omstilling? - Når vi kigger på fremtiden, så kommer der generelt flere akademikere. Der kommer mange flere nye akademiske job, end der kommer faglærte job.

- Men, siger hun med styrket stemme.

- Vi uddanner endnu flere akademikere, så er der faktisk rigeligt af dem i nogle erhverv.

- Der kommer ikke nær så mange nye faglærte jobs, men vi uddanner heller ikke så mange faglærte, så der kommer til at være større mangel på nogle typer faglærte.

- Der kan dog også komme efterspørgsel på visse typer akademikere, understreger hun.

- Hvis vi får en energiø, har vi for eksempel ingen kemiingeniører, der kan arbejde med power-to-x, ligesom der kan komme en større efterspørgsel efter smede i forbindelse med energiøen. Vi har jo i forvejen nogle virksomheder her på Bornholm, som er rigtig glade for deres smede.

Og hvis vi så får flere ekstra smede og folk, der kan noget med kemi, så er vi jo også nødt til at have nogle flere sygeplejersker og pædagoger. Og så skal de også have noget at bo i. Der mangler boliger. Specielt hvis man skal nå politikernes mål om at nå 42.000 indbyggere.

Grunden til, at man siger, at der skal være 42.000 på Bornholm, er, at der så er nok til at tjene penge til at betale skat til at kunne betale pleje af ældre og vores børn.

- Men hvis der skal være 42.000, så skal der være flere job. På den måde interesserer det os også, at erhvervslivet skaber vækst.

Ikke for vækstens egen skyld, men fordi vi går op i at få flere arbejdspladser til øen, så vi også kan bevare vores identitet på øen.

Hvem er det, vi er som samfund? Det interesserer os også. Hvad vil det sige at være Bornholm? Bornholm er noget særligt, som rækker ud over, at der er nok arbejdspladser og 42.000 indbyggere. Så vi skal jo bevare Bornholms sjæl.

Og hvad er det så? opkøbt gårde eller landbrug. Betyder det så noget, om det er en anden landmand, der køber en gård, eller om det er en kapitalfond fra Holland, der køber en gård. Hvad betyder det, om man gør noget for lokalmiljøet? Så det er nogle ting, vi kigger på.

Hvor går det allerbedst i forhold til udviklingen på Bornholm? - Det har været en god tid for turismen de seneste år, og det er restauranter og hoteller, der er de helt store jobskabere i den seneste tid. Det er dem, der sammen med sundhedsområdet har skabt mange job. Det, der kan være bekymringen, er selvfølgelig, hvordan reagerer man nu på en økonomisk krise.

Det, der er kendetegnet ved den tid, vi er i lige nu, det er den omstillingsfase. Det er ikke kun en miljømæssig omstilling, det er også en økonomisk omstilling. Så der er rigtig mange forandringer på vej.

Selv er CRT også i rivende udvikling.

- De seneste tre år har vi også forsøgt at være bedre til at få fortalt historien. Medierne har i højere grad trukket os ind og brugt os som eksperter, og vi er dem, der bliver inviteret med til at skulle holde oplæg for folketinget osv. Der er vi slet ikke nået i mål endnu, men der er flere, der forstår, hvad vi laver. Og det kræver, at vi også selv kender retningen, så vi skal ikke løbe rundt efter projekter, så vi også har noget at lave næste år. Vi er nødt til også at sige nej, så vi ikke trækker fokus fra det, som egentlig er det samlede formål.

Selvom virksomheden også har haft sin del af sygemeldinger og stressramte medarbejdere, beskriver hun den generelle sociale trivsel som høj. Hver anden uge mødes medarbejderne på Bornholm også til fælles morgenmad om onsdagen, mens hun normalt mødes med de københavnske medarbejdere om torsdagen. Og i juletiden er det en tradition, at alle møder hinanden hjemme hos en eller tager ud at spise sammen.

Hvad synes du, er det sværeste ved at være leder? - Jeg synes, det sværeste er, når man kun har én leder. Hvis der er én virksomhed her på Bornholm, hvor lederen har rigtig mange kloge hoveder omkring sig, så er det her, men ved dagens slutning er det jo mig, der skal tage beslutningen. I et ægtepar er man jo to om at tage beslutningen, så der kan man altid give den anden skyld, griner hun.

- Men det sværeste her er, hvis jeg er usikker på, om det er den rette beslutning, så ender det jo med, at jeg tager den beslutning, som jeg stoler på, men her går jeg i en vis forstand alene med usikkerheden op til beslutningen er taget, og jeg har ingen chef at brokke mig til, hvis jeg så tager fejl, siger hun og bløder op i et smil.

- Men jeg kan omvendt godt lide at finde retningen for virksomheden, og jeg bliver begejstret over at se muligheder og få dem skabt. Det begejstrer mig at se CRT, og hvad det kan blive, og tage ansvar for at få det bragt derhen. Det synes jeg er spændende.

Når man sidder i København og arbejder på Christiansborg, så er det nogle gange svært at se den virkelighed, der foregår i de her meget forskellige 98 kommuner, vi har. Så det er vores opgave at sikre os, at beslutningstagerne kender de meget nuancerede virkeligheder Anne Thomas Hvis der er én virksomhed her på Bornholm, hvor lederen har rigtig mange kloge hoveder omkring sig, så er det her Anne Thomas.

Title: Fremtidens kilde til vækst? Overskudsvarme fra foreslået elektrolyseanlæg kan dække Bornholms fjernvarmeforbrug fire-ti gange
Content:
The huge quantities of waste heat from a power-to-x plant linked to CIP and Ørsted's offshore wind farms, which were put on hold a week ago by the Danish Energy Agency, will be able to form the basis for horticulture, aquaculture and other heat-swinging professions within a few years at Bornholm. Last week, Business Center Bornholm focused on the possibilities of an innovation workshop.

It's been no more than half a year ago the public first heard about Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners' (CIP) vision of erecting two offshore wind farms east of Bornholm on the same large scale as the State Energy Island project off the south coast.

In the autumn, the energy company Ørsted joined the CIP's project, which, unlike Energiø Bornholm, is not about driving power away from Bornholm in copper cables, but about converting the energy into hydrogen in electrolysis plants, which should be placed on Bornholm soil.

It creates a potential for jobs and growth that the energy island's high voltage station does not hold. In addition to the actual operation of a power-to-x plant, there are local business opportunities if you can refine parts of the hydrogen for ammonia, which can supply ship traffic in the Baltic with non-fossil fuel. In addition, the surplus heat, which can create the basis for brand new industries on Bornholm. The potential quantities are so large that the Business Center Bornholm in collaboration with Baltic Energy Island last week held a theme day around surplus heat.

- What is really interesting is how we get value out of the surplus heat, says business manager Christa Lodahl to the Journal.

The title of the innovation workshop was "What to do with surplus heat when it can't get in the district heating network?" With the title, one must understand that there will be huge amounts of heat left over, even if you supply the entire Bornholm district heating network from a power-to-X system of the size of it.

- We need to expand the district heating network, but we get a lot more heat than that, says Christa Lodahl.

She says the message from the theme day was that the plant is expected to generate between 1-3 terawatt-hours heat a year-that is, 1-3 billion kilowatt hours.

The amount corresponds to four to ten times the need in the Bornholm district heating network. In comparison, the energy island's high voltage station is expected to create surplus heat enough to cover one -third of district heating consumption.

However, pipes to Germany a series of uncertainties surround the giant project, not least the Danish Energy Agency's decision from last week to put the open door scheme and the case handling. It is not known where the energy companies would prefer to build an electrolysis plant, just as it is to a certain extent in the uncertain how the regional municipality as a local planning authority or the state energy authorities relate to the idea. CIP has stated that they want to put the energy system into operation as early as 2027. In an interview with the Journal in October, CIP Director Magnus Brogaard Larsen mentioned a hydrogen connection to Germany as a possible outlets channel from a Bornholm power-to-X plant, and Since then, CIP has joined a project about a pipeline to be brought down through the Baltic Sea - from the Botnic Bay between Sweden and Finland in the north to Germany. On the cards, a possible detour has been placed to Bornholm from the pipeline passing east of land.

Horticulture and aquaculture One of the presenters at the workshop was a senior analyst from CIP's development company Copenhagen Offshore Partners. He introduced the 27 participants into the plans for the PTX system and told about why it will deliver so much surplus heat.

Along the way, there were also presentations from DTU, Skovgaard Energy and a consultant from HortiAdvice who provides advice to gardeners and fruit growers. Exactly horticulture is one of the heat -intensive industries that can be attractive within a few years to place on Bornholm.

The same can apply to aquaculture and so-called aquaponi systems, combining the cultivation of plants in water with fish farming, says Christa Lodahl. The surplus heat may also be used for industrial processes. Some of the questions that were discussed at the workshop are the quality of the heat.

For example, how stable will the delivery be and what temperatures are involved.

In local planning, it is crucial to know the possibilities of transporting the heat from an electrolysis plant around.

One can imagine that it will make sense to lay a single tube and lead the heat across the island. On the other hand, it will be cumbersome and hardly financially viable to spread the heat in many directions.

Possible cooperation Another important question is the price of surplus heat.

It will hardly be free, says the business manager. She emphasizes that a key concept is "binding cooperation", where part of the payment to the hydrogen producer is a guarantee of stable delivery to local businesses so that the greenhouses are not cooled if the wind turbines stand still for a few days.

The quite initial meeting on the surplus heat took place on Tuesday, the day after the open door scheme and thus the first part of the long process that the energy companies have to go through before a power-to-X-created business adventure on Bornholm can come true.

At the Green Solution House, the participants did not let the news out of the news, and at the Business Center Bornholm Christa Lodahl relies on the fact that for the sake of the green transition a sensible solution will soon be found.

- It's a pity that it's so. But I also assume that it is something they work hard to get resolved - one way or another. That's what's our starting point, she says.

Should the "door" remain closed, it is conceivable that the state will instead put the sea areas, which CIP and Ørsted to everyone's surprise saw the possibilities in tender.

- In that case, it will just take longer.

But that is why it will still be relevant for us to decide on the possibilities of surplus heat, says the business manager.

- There are some issues and potentials that we would like to investigate further.

Now we have become a little sharper on what can be worked on.


Facts about the hydrogen and wind project

Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners applied for permission in June for permission to erect two offshore wind farms of 1.5 gigawatts east of Bornholm. This capacity will require about 85 mills in each of the two areas.

In the applications, the parks are called "Bornholm Bassin Syd" and "Bornholm Basin East", CIP describes in the material that they expect to make use of "the latest wind turbine types, which are currently expected to be 17.5 -20 MW Møller with a rotor diameter of 270 -350 m ".

The total height from sea to wing tip will, with these mill types, be between 290 and 370 meters, you can read in the application material.

The south of the two parks is located in an area of ​​350 square kilometers.

The mills closest to the west will get a distance of 25 kilometers to the coast.

The eastern park has a water depth of 85-100 meters in the feasibility area, and the CIP's plan is therefore to make use of floating foundations. "Bornholm Basin East is expected to be developed as Denmark's first floating offshore wind farm, where innovative technologies and elements are brought into play," CIP writes in the application.

In the applications, CIP does not go into detail about the hydrogen infrastructure, but it has since emerged that CIP and Ørsted's plans are about using the power to produce hydrogen using hydrogen that can be processed into other fuels such as ammonia and methanol.

Title: Erhvervsudvikling på Bornholm -ja tak -men hvilken?
Content:
We are on the threshold of a green revolution. We have to radically change our lifestyle within a number of years. The way we produce our food, our industry, our tourism, our transport and so on.

The climate and biodiversity challenges -Husk that these two crises are inextricably linked -now have grown so large that a revolution is needed.

So the green of the kind. We have known it for a long time, at least for a minimum of 50 years. We are all part of the problem and thus must all be part of the solution. The climate and biodiversity crisis can only be resolved in time if we do it together! Fortunately, we have good cards on hand here at Bornholm. The undersigned recently had the pleasure of participating in the Bornholm tour of both Esbjerg and Skive.

Always interesting and exciting to be allowed to see what others have done and what they intend to do in the future. The most uplifting, however, was undoubtedly sharing the trip with people from the Bornholm business community, BRK, Beof, CRT, Campus Bornholm, Rønne Harbor, BCB, Off Shore Bornholm and several others. Then hold up where we have many super -competent and engaged people on the island. They all have projects for Bornholm and our common good.

Big thanks to all of them.

What can we expect from the business development on the island in connection with Energiø Bornholm, and not least what do we want as Bornholmers. In the Unity List we are positive about the energy island, but will, however, ask questions about what Bornholm as a society gets out of it, and not least what might "follow" so to speak. With the energy island we get wind turbines at sea, cables must be drawn, an even very large building -which is hopefully "wrapped nicely" and some surplus heat, which may be utilized in our district heating system. When the mills spin, we will undoubtedly also get some good jobs in servicing these.

Maybe we also get power to Bornholm, it is not quite clear yet.

During the actual construction, we also get a great deal of activity, which of course can and must benefit Bornholm. But we also get four to six years of violent "logistics - and building root". This very large project must in no way go beyond our current business community. Industry, agriculture and tourism will still be important elements of business development on Bornholm. Therefore, would it not be very reasonable that we as a society jointly made a "License to Operate" - ie a "something for something" agreement with the state? We do not just want to end up as "a big outlet" for the rest of Denmark/ Europe. This could, for example, be in the form of cheap electricity for the Bornholmers, permanent housing, upgrade and maintenance of road networks, extra capacity on the ferry, green education or something completely seventh? In Esbjerg and Skive we saw some of what might "follow" when you have large amounts of power. You can imagine so much, but the case is that virtually all the flow from the energy island will be driven outside. So not so much extra on that front, maybe with the exception of some small testing facilities around the island where it now has to make sense. Bornholm As Testø we have tried before, and in fact we are pretty good at it. So we will look at this in the Unity List as a starting point. Then we have CIP, who wants to erect two wind farms east of Bornholm. According to what to understand, CIP wants to use all the power for a PTX system where they will produce hydrogen, which may be sold from Rønne Harbor or transported away from the island in another way? If CIP was to succeed with their project, it will mean another large plant -may 20-30 hectares -on the island. When producing hydrogen, use water -very water -Circa 6 million cubic meters a year.

Using our precious groundwater is completely excluded. That descending seawater is problematic and expensive. A positive gain for Bornholm might then be to purify all our wastewater 100 percent clean. In that case, it would require major restructuring and investments, but could after all be a good thing for Bornholm.

Another positive area could be cheap heat. Such a PTX system produces a lot of heat in the process. Enough to heat all our homes up to several times. If so, of course, it should benefit us all. There would be heat enough for, for example, the heating of large greenhouses.

If necessary, this would be very positive for agriculture's absolutely necessary conversion to several plant proteins, and it would be high value products that could be exported in great style. There we could certainly learn from the Dutch, who are able to export agricultural products for about 700 billion a year against our currently about 100 billion. In addition, we could undoubtedly also raise our self -sufficiency rate on Bornholm, which is currently at a mad about 6 percent and quite unsustainable in length. Just think of if the ferry could no longer sail Bornholm. In maybe just a week, all the shelves in our supermarkets would be empty! There is a long way to go for CIP and their wind farms/ PTX systems. Many investigations, many permissions from the state, and in terms of PTX, not least a commitment from the municipal council and Bornholm that we find this a good idea.

And then of course, just the detail of finding investors for this many and even billions of big project.

In Esbjerg and Skive we saw several other projects realized and on the way. However, many questions and great uncertainty prevail everywhere. In the Unity List, we are far from sure that the various private investors should find it interesting and relevant to bring most of these projects to Bornholm, and do we want this at all? On the other hand, we believe a lot in the small scale - and the Testø concept. And then we must not forget our own "small" common wind farm - Bornholm's offshore wind.

In the current municipal council, we are now more than a year after we joined - for several reasons - unfortunately not yet succeeded in making a vision plan for Bornholm. It is high time this happens, not least in light of project Energiø. It was also a reviewed theme on the trips to Jutland. All the participants missed a direction - read vision plan - from the island's politicians.

Hereby another call to the mayor and our other colleagues in the municipal council to ensure that we will soon beg this important work for us all at Bornholm.

Biggest decision ever Social Democracy goes to the rest of the municipal council and out to the whole of Bornholm with its play for the reason that the party considers the energy island a chance - and considers Bornholm's response to Energiøen as Bornholm's most crucial and far -reaching decision perhaps ever.
