"We need to take the political leadership in establishing a clear political vision on Bornholm about what we want, where and how. Takes the political management of the development, ”states the Social Democracy presentation.

"The municipal council must set up a task force, which is pace in direction and cooperation with all relevant actors," the Social Democracy also notes.

"If that doesn't happen, there is a risk that Bornholm will forfeit the historical opportunities because we do not have a clear plan in advance in time where we have clarified what we want, where and how." "Every time something new emerges, it is submitted to a decision, and it will probably give a lot of debate every time, and the Bornholmers will be left with the impression that now the municipal council is coming back with a new project that they have to accept, But as they cannot see the overall drawing of the development on Bornholm, and how important this development is for the financing of the future welfare of Bornholm and the attraction of labor and inhabitants, ”writes Social democracy in the play of its view of the cautious approach.

As the second option, the Social Democracy describes an offensive, proactive approach aimed at seizing as much chances as possible for the most growth at Bornholm.

To achieve it, Social Demkrati will set aside a lot of area at once. Also more area than the land plant will need. To also have space for businesses, research and education, which has come to the other places in the country shortly after a new green energy center has been created.

"We are not going to tumble around on a case -by -case basis. It also risks that those who want to invest in Bornholm will be tired of slowness and doubts about the possibilities. Bornholm is one of the municipalities that have not laid out land for business in advance , and there is also a certain sluggishness in the residential area, "the S-play states.

"We need to change that and take the big debate once and for all about the overall vision of Bornholm's development perspectives. If you can see where we are going, then it is easier to get support for this." "Social Democracy recommends this path." S will create a large area in southern Bornholm, the Social Democracy will not only give up area to the energy island's land facility. Immediately up to the land plant, the party will simultaneously place space of companies that have not been named yet, but which are supposed to search for Bornholm.

"The area must be large enough to attract new green businesses. This means that a total plan for areas for the transformer station must be adopted for Power to X-Plants and other types of companies that we do not yet know, but which we have to able to attract, ”states the play.

"It is proposed that this area be placed in South Bornholm in connection with the Transformer Station and also gradually adapted to the landscape. Also as soon as possible, the Social Democracy will establish a secretariat of employees in the municipality, who work exclusively with the energy island and the overall plan that S wants for it.

"It is urgent," notes the Social Democracy, which will therefore spend two million kroner from the municipal treasury to create the Energe Secretariat already.

The Social Democracy proposes that the municipal council adopt a comprehensive plan for Bornholm's development, where the goal is that so many of the parties support this so that Bornholm can act inwardly acting and outwardly speaking with a convincing voice in relation to the government, the Folketing, Energinet and businesses. In a risk assessment, it is estimated that a interconnection can have a "catastrophic consequence" for the overall project economy if the energy's preferred technical solution turns out not to be possible.

Since Energinet announced in January 2022 that it is "likely to be possible" to connect the Bornholm electricity grid to the energy island's land plant, there has been relatively quiet around the interconnection.

Repeatedly, Bornholm politicians have emphasized that it will be an appropriate payment by the state to provide a link, so that Bornholm's only electricity connection to the outside world should not long be one fragile submarine cable to Sweden.

Thomas Thors (S) arranged in his mayor's time in 2021 to put the case on the agenda, and for his successor, Jacob Trøst (K), it remains a priority to get the two parts of the electricity grid.

- It is primarily a matter of security of supply, he says to the Journal.

Some Bornholmers have demanded financial benefits if many hectares are to be added to the state's electrrastructure, but a link will hardly result in lower electricity prices for the Bornholmers or other private economic benefits, points out.

However, there are other potential benefits. On the regional municipality's website about Energiø Bornholm, some green pluses are highlighted by a connection.

"You will be expected to do without the backup of fossil power plant that today is ready for use when the Swedish creator is out of operation due to, for example, damage. So the security of supply will become more green, no matter what. Bennholm benefits by a clutch is In addition, far better opportunities for both import and export of green power. " Today, the submarine cable with limited capacity for Sweden is a bottleneck that will eventually make it less attractive to invest in electricity-producing plants on Bornholm. One week after the civic meeting, Energinet unveiled some of the outstanding questions about the social economy of the giant project, which through a converter station at Sydbornholm connects the two upcoming offshore wind farms with the electricity networks in Zealand and in Germany.

In Energinet's Business Case report, a link to the Bornholm network is highlighted as one of the most serious risks of the overall project. In a diagram, "interconnection with the Bornholm electricity system" is drawn as a risk in the highest risk category, where the potential consequence of the project economy is described as "catastrophic". According to the diagram, the interconnection can have financial consequences that exceed DKK 500 million and it is stated that there is between 10 and 20 percent risk of this.

It is explained in another section of the Business Case that the possible financial consequences are "relatively high, as it must be invested in new plants for repairing technical problems if the challenges cannot be solved with the expected concept".

The business case was written in March 2022, but only made publicly available eight months later. And to find the best solution, you try to take into account how to expect electricity consumption to develop in Bornholm in the future, says Kim Søgaard Mikkelsen.

He explains that the security of supply on Bornholm is an important part of the work. The Danish electricity network is driven on the basis of a principle that the current in the contacts should not be interrupted if a single cable line or transformer station is hit by a mistake.

Title: Trøst vil have firmaer med i grøn erhvervspark
Content:
Can Bornholm get one or more companies to find out where a green business park around the energy island should be, how big it should be and what companies to aim for? Mayor Jacob Consolation is counting on this, and therefore the opportunity is now being investigated.

The upcoming Energiø will be larger and more than just the land plant that the state will place. In any case, five of the municipal council's seven parties make up a majority of at least 16 mandates to also open up new jobs and new growth from follow-up: Power-to-X, Green Business Park, Education and Research.

But where the activities must be, how much area they have to seize and whether the expected followers are to be assembled in one place or more places is still completely unclear.

To get started on the questions, both the municipality and Baltic Energy Island (in the former power plant in Rønne) are now creating what Mayor Jacob Trøst (K) calls an area development company.

The idea is to get one or more companies involved in developing the area and making it clear what activities the area or areas should be used for - and only on that basis decide where it should be and how big it should be.

Jacob Trøst sees the area development company as a newly formed company that must be formed to first find answers to the yet unclear key questions, and which must then play a driving role in building the energy island with a follow -up business. He has developed the idea together with Søren Møller Christenen, director of Baltic Energy Island.

- Last fall I talked to Søren Møller Christensen about how we can create a construction that opens up for business around the energy island, but without pulling all the money for it out of the municipal treasury, so that we instead get private players financing, instead, That an area is laid out, he says.

- The idea is found in several different places in several different versions. There are some constructions where the municipality plays the biggest role and there are some constructions where private actors do. But I think we need a private company that can see an advantage in playing with and can contribute with skills and input on how to lay the area. For example, how large the area should be and where it should be in relation to other business areas.

- Right now we are in a phase where we are investigating and analyzing the possibilities. At the same time, an area development company is only one stick out of a lot of people who have to do with the energy island, says Jacob Consolation.

Skive shows one way the inspiration is, among other things, taken in Skive.

Here, 15 years ago, the local municipality acquired a 60 -hectare area to create a business park for green energy companies.

Under the name Greenlab Skive, the Park's companies today have their own energy sources, and in several cases they use each other's surplus products.

Last year, the energy company Norlys invested DKK 250 million in Greenlab Skive and thus became a major shareholder in the green business park.

Last week, Norly's invested another 30 million kroner in Greenlab Skive.

That money will be used to establish an innovation center that will be ready in two years. The plan is to let some of the world's most talented researchers work with private companies to solve the energy challenges of the future.

- Norlys' commitment to GreenLab Skive is just one construction. Realdania is part of another construction. There are a number of different ways to do it, so we are looking at what opportunities there are and what will best fit Bornholm. Baltic Energy Island also works with it, says Jacob Trøst.

- We must, among other things, look at whether the municipality should buy land and rent parts of it out to green companies. Or whether private investors should buy land, possibly with the municipality. It is too early to say yet when we do not yet know how large the area should be and what the need will be, he says.

Both comfort and a large part of the municipal council have this year visited GreenLab Skive. Here, the mayor also noted that the ski bonites' choice of establishing a large area for green companies at once now makes it quick and easy to move to interested companies.

- In Skive we could see that a Norwegian company had chosen to place itself in Greenlab Skive, because a very large part of the plan and government work had already been done, so that the plan work for the Norwegian company could be done in a month, says Jacob Consolation.

First, however, choosing companies still lack the answers to the questions that absorb most: How much area should be used? Where should it be? And should it take place in one place or more places? - It depends a lot on what type of business could benefit from it and what requirements it makes. For example, one type of business may need a lot of power or much or a particular type of infrastructure, says Jacob Consolation.

- That is why we must first find out what type of business we would like to attract. What our options are will also depend on what actors we can get hold of. From that I think there will be a picture of what is best for Bornholm and what we can reach political agreement on how many Places do you see for you to follow the energy island? - Whether it should be one or two places is not clear either, because it will also depend on the needs of the company (s) that comes in. But I think it is important that we take a political position on where we want this type of activity and that we say that "it must be here" so that we do not get knob shooting, how individual companies establish many different places.

All the specific questions are unresolved right now. Will this be something that we will hear more about? - Yes. I'm pretty sure there will be specific answers to these things when we have an overview of what we have of opportunities, says Jacob Consolation.

I think we need a private company that can see an advantage in playing with and that can contribute with skills and input on how to lay the area. For example, how large the area should be and where it should be in relation to other business areas.

Jacob Consolation (K), Mayor.

Title: S bakker op om at involvere firmaer i grøn erhvervspark
Content:

Title: Power-to-x-anlæg vil ændre Bornholm på en negativ måde
Content:

In Bornholm's Journal, we were able to read about the Social Democracy's proposal for a comprehensive plan for Energiøen Bornholm on Tuesday, February 14. It is gratifying that some of our politicians in the municipal council finally officially announce what visions they have and notions they make.

It appears that the Social Democracy wants the "whole package". They want a business park and they want Power-to-X. They see a risk of losing the historical opportunities for Bornholm if they do not act now. They outline two possible approaches to the energy island - a defensive approach and an offensive, proactive.

The Social Democracy will the latter.

A business development is necessary for Bornholm as a starting point. You can only agree with that. But how far to go, what is the cost, what is possible and what does the Bornholmers want? When we hear politicians and commercial focus on the possibilities of energy island, it is only in positive terms.

We get population growth, better economy, our welfare is secured, all the work we want, exciting educational opportunities, cheap district heating, new professions that can export new products, etc. But no one mentions costs and negative consequences.

All actions will have positive and negative consequences! But especially a power-to-x system will change our small island totally-and in a really dull way.

Politicians link their notions of business parks and business opportunities up on a power-to-X system.

We will have to produce hydrogen using electrolysis and further process it for fuel for aircraft and ships at Bornholm. Possibly also export hydrogen.

A power-to-x factory of such a category is supposed to be completely out of proportions one's size taken into account! As: Power-to-X requires clean water and we have had drought problems on Bornholm over the past few years.

How much water does one expect to be used? And where should it come from? Groundwater? Salted seawater? Wastewater cleaning? Where should the factory and warehouse lie? A power-to-x factory gives off a colossal amount of heat, which is partly due to compressors under high pressure pushing gases into pipes and tanks. Again: Is there knowledge of numbers on the amount of heat to be removed/ used? On the whole: Is there anyone at all who has an overview of how large amounts of hydrogen and hence power-to-X chemicals to be produced? Has security taken into account? At Power-to-X, these are extremely reactive and toxic chemicals. How to secure such a chemical factory - both against accident and against terror. Keep in mind that we are very close to Russia and very far away from external help if the disaster one day hits.

What is the actual target, what quantities should be produced? Immediately, it seems that it is dreams of a municipal council that - without thorough care - simply wants to promote the financial foundation of Bornholm. It must also be promoted, but not using Power-to-X. It is too monstrous and dangerous.

Title: Naboer frygter udvidelse: Det kommer til at stinke, larme og dominere landskabet
Content:
The plans to expand Bigadan's biogas plant at Aakirkeby so that in the future it can receive more than four times as much biomass in the form of slurry, is evoking concern among the neighbors.

Two years ago, Ben Woodhams and Tina Lund moved from Vestermarie and into Villa Granly on Vestermarievej 84. Here there is a view of the biogas plant from the terrace, but in the future the plant will fill significantly more for the view and it has made them troubled.

- Before, I didn't think much about a plant over it, but as planning the expansion came out, I think about it all the time. I'm very worried, says Ben Woodhams.

According to plan, the capacity of the biogas plant will in future be able to receive up to 600,000 tonnes of biomass a year, where today it can receive 135,000 tonnes. In order for it to be possible, it is necessary to expand the plant to spread over an area of ​​more than six hectares. Here, among other things, 35 meters high chimneys and six reactor towers of 27 meters will be built. In comparison, the three current reactors are 17 meters high.

Ben Woodhams has made 3D visualizations of the plans to get a sense of how much the expansion of the plant is actually going to fill, and it has not reassured him.

- It's very scary. It will be far greater than any other plant seen here at Bornholm, and it will greatly dominate the landscape from Lobbæk to Aakirkeby and can be seen from Vestermarie, Almindingen and Klintebakken, he says.


Smell and noise

Especially Ben Woodhams and Tina Lund are hit by the expansion because they are the closest neighbors to the facility. But there are also others in the area who are concerned, and there are several reasons for that.

For the past 15 years there has been a neighboring group of about 10 households, which has fought against the smell of the plant because most of the biomass consists of slurry from pig and milk producers. And the fear is that when there is more than four times as much manure to the plant, the stench will also rise.

- Before I bought the house, I talked to neighbors about the smell and they said it has gotten much better now than ten years ago. I remember that when you drove past the plant back then, a disgusting smell really came, but right now it is not that big a problem.

But we fear it can be again when there is so much more slurry to the area than now, says Ben Woodhams.

In addition, the neighboring group fears the noise of the many trucks that will drive the many tons of manure to the plant.

- It's going to sound much more than it does now, because there is plenty of traffic. It will ruin the quality of life and I do not know if it will be possible to live here, he says.


Calls for compensation

Ben Woodhams points out that it may be necessary to plant some trees around the ground so that the trees can grow large and block the view of the large building.

- But I think it is really bad that there is no legislation in relation to compensation, just as there is when large wind turbines are set up. A private company can just build a huge facility next to our land without paying compensation to the locals who are affected by it. I think that's totally crazy.

Why did you choose to buy a house right next to the biogas plant? - When I bought the house, I didn't know that a huge expansion would come right against our grounds. And right now, the existing plant is hidden behind trees, but they have to be felled due to the expansion.

- But it is clear that the closer to one's own house, the more it pain. I'm sure if the plant was in Klemensker, then I wouldn't have spent that much time reading about biogas, Ben Woodhams honestly says.


Citizens' Meeting Monday night

Bornholm Regional Municipality has invited to a civic meeting on Monday night at Kanns Hotel in Aakirkeby from 19-21, and here Ben Woodhams and the rest of the neighboring group hope that a lot will emerge that will share their concerns about the expansion of the biogas plant.

Until April 13, it is also possible to submit consultation responses to the plans, and this is something that the neighboring group of 10 households intends to do, and the hope is that others will do the same.

- The ambition is that it will not happen. That's what we are fighting for. But we are just really afraid that this consultation process is running under the radar and that the ordinary Bornholmer is not aware of how big the plant really will be. That's why I've been driving around and handing in posters with visualizations to every single house in this area, so they're aware of it, says Ben Woodhams, who at all thinks that biogas is the wrong way to go for Bornholm when it is going to cover our energy needs.

- We believe this is Green Washing of an old and ineffective technology that is prioritized in order to continue a climate -damaging livestock production and give agriculture and politicians a way in which they seem to reach the green goals. It is incredible that you can build such a plant and fill with 6,000,000 tons of slurry every year and then call it a green solution. The green solution had been not to have 600,000 tonnes of slurry on Bornholm.

- I understand that we as a society will have to accept that changes are coming and looking at more wind turbines on the horizon, but this is something else entirely. It's really a wrong way to solve the problem.

Director understands the concerns the concerns of the neighbors meet understanding at Bornholm Agriculture & Food, which has helped to prepare the new biogas plan.

Director Thomas Bay Jensen tells the Journal that there will be no doubt that it will have an effect on the surroundings when expanding biogas production on Bornholm, as it will be a larger plant than today and thus will fill more.

At the same time, he admits that the expansion will mean more trucks on the roads, and it will not only be on Vestermarievej, but also in the rest of the Bornholm community, as in the future one will have to pick up slurry from 60-70 farmers, where today it is only at 20.

- I can understand those concerns. No doubt about it. But I imagine that Bigadan, in collaboration with the regional municipality, will do everything one can to minimize the genes on both noise and smell. For example, it may be by setting up noise valves or trees to shield the area as best as possible, says Thomas Bay Jensen.

- This is also why it is really sensible and good to make a civic meeting so that you can talk about the concerns you have, he says, pointing out that this method has been useful in the concerns of the high -voltage station in South Bornholm , which will receive the flow from the new energy island.

At the same time, the director rejects that biogas is Green Washing, so agriculture has an excuse to maintain its current stock of pigs and cows.

- It is factually wrong that it is Green Washing, because biogas has a positive effect on CO2 emissions.

In Denmark we have more hehov for biogas, and biogas is green energy, he states.

At the same time, he does not hide the fact that it is the wish of the Bornholm agriculture to maintain the livestock production that is today.

- Our task is to maintain our current production of pigs and cows, and this requires, among other things, that we produce more biogas and reduced CO2 emissions, says Thomas Bay Jensen.

The Biogas Plan has been prepared by BLF in collaboration with Beof, Bornholm Regional Municipality, Business Center Bornholm, Rønne Harbor, National Center for Green Energy, Biomasse-Vendoresforeningen, Halm-Liver Services Association and Bigadan.

We are just really scared that this consultation process is running under the radar and that the ordinary Bornholmer is not aware of how big the plant really becomes Ben Woodham's neighbor to the biogas plant.

Title: Klimaminister til Bornholm for at drøfte grønne planer
Content:
Climate, Energy and Supply Minister Lars Aagaard will meet with Bornholm politicians on Monday.

Offshore wind turbines, electricity supply, Energiø and the possibilities for Bornholm are on the agenda when Climate, Energy and Supply Minister Lars Aagaard (M) comes to Bornholm on Monday.

Here Aagaard meets with the Bornholm MPs, Lea Wermelin (S) and Peter Juel-Jensen (V), Mayor Jacob Trøst (K), the group chairmen of the municipal council and the partnership Baltic Energy Island.

This is stated by the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Supply in a press release.

- We are right on the threshold of the next big leap in the expansion of Danish offshore wind, when we are scheduled to start the supply of nine GW offshore winds this year, which will be spin by 2030. , amounting to about a third of the new green current. I would like to acknowledge that, and it is important for me to have a good dialogue with the local politicians, stakeholders and citizens of Bornholm to ensure that they experience gains knowing that they become a central green hub. That's why I visit Bornholm, says Lars Aagaard in the press release.

Strengthens supply security with the green plans follow opportunities for business development, education and jobs locally at Bornholm, and here the minister welcomes the partnership Baltic Energy Island.

- When private and public actors cooperate, it has something good. Therefore, I am pleased that some of the major energy companies, together with the researchers from DTU and Energinet, have joined a partnership with the local players on Bornholm to use the island's strategically important location to create a global hub for green energy technology. It is an important contribution to the green transition and Bornholm's development, says Lars Aagaard.

Energinet also works to connect the Bornholm electricity grid to the energy island, which will ensure large quantities of green power and increased security of supply to the Bornholmers.


An important visit

Former Minister of Environment, now climate, energy and supply spokesman for the Social Democracy, Lea Wermelin, calls it important in the press release that the minister comes to Bornholm: - For us Bornholmers, the energy island is not only about the development of offshore wind and green power in the future, but also about creating Brand new opportunities for growth and jobs locally, she says.

MF for the Left, Peter Juel -Jensen, follows up: - If we do this right, we create both a national and an international hub for the production of green energy. It is important that Bornholm can follow this process.

Therefore, dialogue and collaboration are a prerequisite for us to fully utilize both locally and nationally.

Content:
It is Mayor Jacob Trøst (K) who has invited Climate, Energy and Supply Minister Lars Aagaard (M), Bornholm Regional Municipality said in a press release on the ministerial visit on Monday 13 March.

Title: Energinet arbejder på separat priszone for Bornholm: Det vil give en smule billigere strøm
Content:
Bornholm can get a separate electric spot price when the energy island is built. The new zone is expected to mean that Bornholm consumers can get a little cheaper power, but the price difference will be limited, says the assessment from Energinet. However, the new price zone for the energy island will only cover Bornholm itself if it is decided to connect the Bornholm electricity grid to the energy island's high voltage plant.

During the energy crisis, many Danes have discovered that the country is divided into two price zones for electricity, east (DK2) and west (DK1). When the energy island has been completed around 2030, a third price zone is likely to be added, which will only include Bornholm.

The new price zone - or buddy, as it is also called - will mean that the pure electricity price on Bornholm may be different from the rest of Eastern Denmark, which Bornholm today belongs to.

- The price is expected to be a little lower than in the East Danish zone, Veronika Fischer, project manager at Energinet, tells the Journal.

However, a little cheaper access to electricity will only be relevant if Bornholm's electricity grid is connected to the energy island, so that the power from the future large offshore wind farms can be inserted directly into the local electricity grid. If it is decided that a interconnection is too complicated or expensive to perform in practice, Bornholm will remain in the East Danish Price Zone. In this case, Energinet will create an offshore buddy that includes exclusively the offshore wind farms and the energy island's land plants, says Veronika Fischer, who works with the market track in the Energiø program.

A no to a link will mean that the submarine cable to Sweden will continue to constitute Bornholm's only electricity connection to the outside world.


Following the cheapest neighbor

The reason Energinet will introduce a new price zone are the large amounts of energy from the offshore wind farms and the capacity of the cables.

The cables between Bornholm and Zealand will be able to transport 1.2 gigawatts, while the connection to Germany can accommodate 2 gigawatts.

- The market will not be able to see that only 1.2 gigawatts can be moved from Bornholm to Zealand, if the energy island becomes part of the existing bid zone, DK2, explains Veronika Fischer.

This means that the entire production from the mills south of Bornholm can be traded in Zealand, although it is not possible to transport as much power in the cables.

Energinet will have to sell the amount of power for which the cables do not have capacity.

- To counteract to get in balance would be extremely expensive for Energinet - and thus Danish society. By making a bid zone, the capacity restriction becomes visible to the market, says the project manager.

The new Energiø Price Zone will limit up to Eastern Denmark (DK2) and Germany. Why will a new zone make the power a little cheaper on Bornholm? The explanation is that the spot price due to the market mechanisms in the European power market is formed based on the prices in the cheapest of the neighboring areas, where there is free trading capacity.

- In the vast majority of cases, Bornholm will get the lowest adjoining price, says Veronika Fischer.

How much cheaper can the power become for the Bornholmers - if the interconnection becomes a reality? - I dare not put percentages on, the project manager replies.

The politicians informed about the effect The money question for the Bornholm consumers has also been interested in the municipal council. At a closed theme meeting last year, the politicians were presented a note from Energinet that dampened expectations.

This is perhaps why cheaper power is not used as a strong argument in the local debate about the energy island.

"Limited effect for consumers," says a headline on a note section.

"The price of Bornholm will depend on how the wind blows as well as on the price of the neighboring price areas, ie Zealand and Germany.

"The German price is most often expected to be higher than the Zealand price, which is why the connection to Germany will be fully utilized. Bornholm and Zealand will have the same lower price -end Germany during those periods.

Conversely, in the periods when the German price is lower than the Zealand, Bornholm will also most often have the same price as in Germany. Therefore, the electricity price on Bornholm is expected to be marginally lower than in Zealand on average with an independent price zone, ”ENERGINET estimates.

- When we say a "low" and "high" price, it's not because they are significantly different, says Veronika Fischer about the expectations of the future price differences between Germany and Eastern Denmark.


Crucial bottlenecks

Looking at the last month's spot prices, there has not been a single day when electricity prices in Eastern Denmark have been higher than in Germany, which is covered by one national zone.

With such a distribution, Bornholm in a new price zone will not have any financial advantage compared to people in Zealand and Lolland-Falster.

To the Journal, project manager Veronika Fischer states that in rare cases there may be hours when the electricity price on Bornholm will be the same as in the highest of the two neighboring areas. This can be the case if there is not much blowing, so the production from the offshore wind turbines is low, while the cable for the energy island is fully utilized from Zealand to Bornholm, while there is free capacity on the cable to Germany. In that case, the German (and higher) price will set the spot price on Bornholm.

But in the big picture it will be the exception, and therefore the expectation is that Bornholm can enjoy a small financial benefit of a new price zone.

Exceptionally, it may also happen that the spot price on Bornholm will be lower than in both Germany and Eastern Denmark. This will require the electricity generation from the offshore wind farms to exceed the capacity of the cables.

- If Bornholm is to have its own price, it must be because there are bottlenecks on both connections, which means that more power is produced than can be exported together on the connections, explains Veronika Fischer and elaborates: - The cables are dimensioned, So all production as a starting point can always be exported. However, there may be cases where there is no full capacity of the cables, for example if planned maintenance is carried out, which results in reduction in capacity, anchor damage and other. For example, if 3 gigawatts winds are produced, but the cable for DK2 is not available and thus only 2 GW capacity is available from Bornholm, the new Budzone will get its own price.

It is the most expensive necessary unit that sets the price of the electricity market. Since the energy island's wind turbines will have lower marginal costs than the plants (for example, power plants) that dictate the spot price in other price zones, such a situation will thus make the current in a Bornholm price zone cheaper.


Not greater impact

Energinet emphasizes in the note to the municipal council that the spot price usually amounts to just under a quarter of the total consumer, while the rest is made up of net tariffs, taxes and VAT.

"Therefore, marginal changes in the wholesale price will not affect consumers to Bornholm to a greater extent," Energinet concludes.

During the energy crisis, however, the pure electricity price has been a somewhat larger part of the total price, and it is also worth remembering that the high net tariffs for TREFOR EL-NET East are affected by the spot price of electricity, because the net loss in the wires must be settled at market price. So slightly lower spot prices in general will break through several places on the electricity bill, especially when the current is expensive.

In the note, Energinet points out that the price of Bornholm will also depend on how the energy island develops over time.

If several offshore wind farms are connected, the local electricity price may fall, while large power-to-X systems in the price zone can make the power more expensive.

The new price zone will only take effect when the energy island's offshore wind farms are ready to be put into operation. Although it is expected to take six to seven years, Energinet is in full swing with the preparations, as the market model and the new price zones for the two Danish energy islands must be fixed before the offshore wind farms are sent out. During the process, among other things, the European Commission must approve Energinet's plan.


Price zones in Europe

When Denmark and the rest of Europe are divided into pricing zones (also called buddy zones), it is because there are geographical areas where more electricity can be produced than the connections between the areas can transport back and forth. Thus, situations with high production and low prices can arise in a price zone, and high demand and higher prices in the neighboring price zone.

The entire electricity market -and also the price zones -are regulated by common EU rules to ensure that countries do not make special rules and protectionism, but that as much power as possible can be traded back and forth so that consumers get the cheapest possible prices.

Today, Denmark consists of two pricing zones separated by the Great Belt, where a DC compound has been built that can transport limited current quantities.

Germany today is not divided into bid zones. There is a common European bid zone study in progress that can form the basis for Germany to be divided into several bid zones. The time horizon for a final clarification is still unknown, and there is still no agreement on where any new bid zone boundaries would have to be.

Title: Energinet giver opdatering på afgørende beslutning
Content:

As a follow -up to an article on the interconnection of the two electricity grids (brought on 18 February), Tidende has tried to get more detailed information from Energinet about what the status is at work, which will be crucial to Bornholm's future electricity infrastructure and which will also affect others Energy projects and companies.

Which technical solution is working on today? And what uncertainties are still current? Will there eg.

be used AC-DC conversion for the power to access Bornholm? And Error Failure does not turn over in the Bornholm Electricity grid and create problems here. Conversion of the current from AC (AC) to DC (DC) and return to AC, which is used in all underlying electricity grids, has been mentioned as a possible technical solution, but Energinet thus strives to avoid this. Instead, the connection must be made in the part of the land plant where the power from the wind turbines is transformed up to 400 kV (ie the high voltage level that must be used in the cables for Germany and Zealand).

It is worth noting that it is the risk of errors proposing the Bornholm electricity grid that Energinet emphasizes in the description of the challenges.

Journal: "What implications get a link with the preferred technical solution for: a) Search cable to Sweden (future use, new investments, etc.) b) the power plant at Rønne Havn c) the electricity grid on Bornholm (Trefor El-Net East) d) Other future solar cells and wind farms on Bornholm. opposite path (to the transformer station and on to Zealand/ Germany in the DC cables)? ” Energinet: "At present, Energinet is working to investigate different connection points and scenarios, and it is therefore not possible to provide updated construction estimates. These alternatives are evaluated based on a wide range of criteria, which include, for example, the consequence on the electricity grid in collaboration with Trefor East, supply security (affects the Rønne plant and the submarine cable) and the possibility of connecting VE systems (WE means renewable energy, ed.) At Bornholm.

Energinet has previously stated that the question of a connection must be clarified before the construction of the high -voltage plant is offered. Whether the interconnection can be done will ultimately also depend on whether the suppliers of components to the land plant consider that the technical solution is realistic and the dialogue with potential suppliers is underway.


Documentation

This is what Energinet writes in note to the municipal council "The price of Bornholm will depend on how the wind blows as well as the price in the neighboring price areas, ie Zealand and Germany.

The German price is most often expected to be higher than the Zealand price, which is why the connection to Germany will be fully utilized. Bornholm and Zealand will have the same lower price -end Germany during those periods.

Conversely, in the periods when the German price is lower than the Zealand, Bornholm will also most often have the same price as in Germany. Therefore, the electricity price on Bornholm is expected to be marginally lower than in Zealand on average with an independent price zone.

The electricity price, the wholesale price, amounts to approx. 23% of the total price that consumers pay, the rest are taxes and tariffs. Only the wholesale price is affected if Bornholm becomes part of a new price zone. Therefore, marginal changes in the wholesale price will not affect consumers to Bornholm to a greater extent.

The above conclusion is based on Energinet's market simulations and calculations in connection with the first phase of Energiø Bornholm with the establishment of 3 GW offshore winds and a connection to Germany. If large consumption units are connected, such as electrolysis systems for hydrogen production or additional electricity connections are established to several foreign islands from the energy island, it will also have an impact on price formation and thus on the conclusion above. All else being equal, increased consumption in the form of, for example, PTX could lead to an average of higher price, while increased production, for example in the form of extra supplied offshore wind capacity in the price zone, will lead to lower price. "

Title: Trefor: Staten bør dække alle udgifter til en tilkobling
Content:
Today, the Bornholm electricity network south of Aakirkeby is not strong enough to receive current quantities that can cover the entire island's consumption. But it should not be TREFOR and Bornholm electricity customers who have to pay for new cables that will make it possible to connect the electricity grid to the energy island's land facility, Trefor EL-NET East chairman, Charles Nielsen.

If the Bornholm electricity grid is to be linked to the energy island's land plant so that the far -reaching offshore wind farms south of the coast can supply the island with electricity, it will require the existing electricity grid to be reinforced.

This is stated by Charles Nielsen, the director of infrastructure in Trefor, which owns and operates the local electricity grid.

- It is not Bornholm that has to pay to be ended. It should not cost Bornholm money, says Charles Nielsen to the Journal.

The thing is that the electricity grid is only two places equipped to handle as large quantities of electricity as it requires to supply the entire Bornholm. It is around the power plant in Rønne and in Hasle, where the search cable from Sweden is led ashore. Thus, new cables will have to be invested if the future main entrance to the electricity grid is to go via the high voltage system in SOSE. The bill, Charles Nielsen believes, should not end up with Trefor EL -NET EAST - and thus the Bornholmers, who pay for investments in the electricity grid via the Nettariffs, which is already higher on Bornholm than anywhere else in Denmark.

The TREFOR director points out that the financing of the expenses should go via larger pool from the state or Energinet if operations are financed by payments from all Danish electricity consumers.

- When new production enters the electricity grid, producers have to pay to get on. In principle, this also applies to Energinet, says Charles Nielsen and elaborates: - It should be a political price to pay for Danish society to be allowed to put a lot of hardware over here. Those who want the energy island must help pay for the Bornholm network to be upgraded, so that you can connect the electricity grid over here with the energy island. It makes sense in my head, says Charles Nielsen, who is also chairman of the board of Trefor El-Net East.

What will a connection to the energy island specifically require of the Bornholm electricity grid? - I can't say that, because I don't know enough about it yet.

- There is a price that someone has to pay for us to get an energy island. Bornholm has to land to a net station for a large energy island, so we can supply electricity to Germany and Denmark, maybe Sweden and Poland at some point. We can't have such a big energy island out there as we have to land, without Bornholm getting it happy. And the price for the Bornholmers to benefit from it, the Bornholmers do not necessarily have to pay twice - by both landing and upgrading the net to handle it.

- Those who need the right to build a station must also have to pay a price to deliver power to Bornholm in exactly the same way as if the power comes in with a cable from Sweden to Hasle, says Charles Nielsen.

Is it TREFOR's wish that the interconnection of the two networks be implemented? - We basically just have the net around Bornholm, and whether the stream comes from the Swedish -catered, the work in Rønne or from an energy island, there are some others who have to decide. We are fundamentally indifferent to whether it is one, second or third. It is Energinet who has the universal service obligation on Bornholm. It is Energinet that pays for it when the work is to be started and has to pay to renovate the submarine cable - and they are the ones who sit with the business case for what it will cost to connect Bornholm on the Energy Island rather than replace the Swedish Cabinet .

What is the latest message you got from Energinet? - It's that they work on it. They are fully aware that they have a challenge if they do not get Bornholm connected to the energy island.

Because then everything must be as it is today - and there will also be a large offshore wind farm, while Bornholm is just transit without enjoying it.

Title: Trøst vil slå Bornholm fast i udvikling af energiø
Content:

In contacting the Climate, Energy and Supply Committee, the mayor writes that Bornholm needs a dialogue at the political level to ensure local gains and local support for Bornholm's contribution to Denmark's green transition.

- It is to tell what it is that characterizes Bornholm and what special considerations we think you have to think about when you do this, he says.

Backing from the citizens seen from Jacob Trøst's mayor's chair is not only Bornholm who can benefit from the proposed representative of the Folketing's climate-energy and supply committee.

It will also benefit the state, he believes.

At the same time, he thinks it is important that the energy rapporteurs know the local conditions in the area they have to make decisions about.

In contacting the committee, he writes: "As the tender is the first of its kind in Denmark, it is important for Bornholm to have a dialogue about the supply, so that we ensure the greatest possible winnings and considerations of the local community and the backing of the local community. We also want a dialogue about the number of tenders and whether the state is planning a total tender or individual tenders and what the pace is. ” Actors from the business community In the first place, Jacob Trøst has asked for representations and meetings in Copenhagen, and a digital meeting has also been agreed with an energy mayor, but it may also be relevant to invite the committee and rapporteurs to Bornholm, as well as climate- , Energy and Supply Minister Lars Aagaard.

I hope to be able to explain them the Bornholm angle: What is it that we have of concerns on Bornholm and wishes in relation to the energy island and the derived things that could come from it.

Title: Minister: Danmark skal give noget tilbage til Bornholm
Content:
Bornholm can become a master in his own house with the opportunities that the energy island brings, said Energy Minister Lars Aagaard at his visit. Denmark must also give something back, and in the first place work is being done strongly to connect Bornholm to the energy island's electricity generation, he said.

The upcoming Energiø can make Bornholm self -sufficient and without the need to seek extra money in pools from the state to make the municipality's economy interconnected.

This was stated by Climate, Energy and Supply Minister Lars Aagaard (M) on Monday morning in the old power plant in Rønne, which today houses the consortium National Center for Green Energy, of which Rønne Harbor and Beof are part of.

Lars Aagaard spent about four hours on Bornholm. Here he first saw the place where the energy island's land plant is to be located. In Rønne both he and Mayor Jacob Trøst (K) then held a presentation on the energy island, and partly for top people from the Danish Energy Agency, Energinet, Ørsted, DTU, Rønne Harbor and Beof, and partly for Bornholm's two members of the parliament and the group chairmen of the parties in the municipal council.

- I think the energy island and what we stand with here can be Kim for a fundamental strengthening of business development on Bornholm.

We can develop new professions so that the proud Bornholm people again become master of their own house, Lars Aagaard told the approximately 25 assembled key figures in the power plant.

"When Bornholm gives something to Danish society, Denmark must also give something back to Bornholm," the minister said.


Great effort for connection

Mayor Jacob Trøst (K) met Lars Aagaard with seven concrete wishes from Bornholm around the energy island. Both Aagaard himself and several participants say that it was not the day of the specific promises, because Lars Aagaard is still in a phase where he listens and collects inspiration.

But the minister would like the Bornholm electricity network to be connected to the flow from the energy island's land plant, he said. He is also very open to the fact that the Bornholmers can get cheap heat out of the surplus heat that the land plant will produce.

- I think it sounds like a real thought that the Bornholm electricity grid should be linked to the energy island's land plant. We also need to investigate whether the surplus heat from the land plant can give the Bornholmers a lower heating bill, said Lars Aagaard.

Among the other participants of the visit, several people were adhered to by Lars Aagaard's clear support to get the Bornholm electricity network connected with the energy island.

- Work is really being done on the Bornholm electricity grid being connected. I see that as very positive, because being connected is a deal breaker for Bornholm. In relation to the Bornholmers, it is important that we do not put land to the energy island without even getting cheap electricity and maybe surplus heat out of it, says parliamentary member Lea Wermelin (S).

- The Minister told us that "We are working Max" to connect Bornholm. There are no two lines under anything, but there was a very powerful signal that we are doing everything we can to connect Bornholm, she says.

Title: Energiøens amatørarbejde
Content:
The government is planning Energiø for 100 billion, but cannot secure the seven closest neighbors a decent solution.

On Monday, Energinet presented its plans for Energiøen's land facility at a civic meeting in Nexø. South Bornholm must be decorated with a 25 meter high and 100 meter long buildings with a round hand. There are a bit of trees and some soil walls around and a stream down between the monumental buildings to be lined with burnt clay. It should give the Bornholmers the experience of having been in the process, could go for a walk in the area and have influenced the work after two workshops where many citizens have given their best and wild ideas.

But the meeting was not characterized by the architects' almost predictably boring solution to the design of the transformer plant.

No. The presentation of the land facility in the probably DKK 100 billion expensive project to secure our future energy needs in a climate -friendly way was instead characterized by seven bothered neighbors who now get the buzzing 25 -meter -high industrial buildings as neighbors in their backyard.

Right now, the seven affected homeowners cannot be allowed to sell their housing to the Danish Energy Agency. They get no compensation for the large building, and they find it extremely difficult to sell their homes at ordinary price, now that the state is building large in their backyard. The affected neighbors characterized the debate in Nexø, where several claps were against the project and its location.

Had the project be a rural park or solar park, the neighbors would have been compensated for their losses. But because the Folketing has not yet done proper legislative work in this area for the country's first energy island, the neighbors have to settle for understanding conversations with Energinet and a long nose for their losses.

Mayor Consolation told the hall that he spends almost all his waking hours affecting the parliament and government so that the law of law can be put in place. Unfortunately, our two government -supporting members of Bornholm were not present in the hall.

But they promise in today's Journal to fight to get control of the situation.

It is a waste of good popular support for the climate -friendly and 100 billion expensive construction not to be able to deal with paying the few citizens the relatively few million kroner in compensation. In addition, it is a waste of our mayor's time that he has to spend all his waking hours helping the squeezed neighbors. Bornholm has lots of other challenges that our mayor has to work with.

Lea and Peter: Lift the burden of our mayor and tormented homeowners' shoulders and resolve the case as soon as possible. We cannot be served with the situation as it is now.

Title: Gigantisk landanlæg begynder at tage form
Content:
On Monday evening, Energinet presented the design of the energy island's gigantic land plant, which will be established south of Aakirkeby.

On Monday evening, Energinet at the Furniture Factory in Nexø presented its bid for the design and location of the upcoming converter station to be built south of Aakirkeby as part of Energiø Bornholm.

It was the third time Energinet opened its doors to an open meeting on Energiø Bornholm, where the citizens could meet and give their concern - this time to present the presentation of what the station should look like.

The presentation was the culmination of a process that since December has included the Bornholmers in working to design and fit the large station that becomes the heart of Energiø Bornholm, and even before the evening's meeting Kim Søgaard Mikkelsen, who is the main project manager at Energinet for Energiø Bornholm, had Stated: - We look forward to showing our proposal to an upcoming station rather than the Bornholmers.

We have had really good participation in the process and gained a lot of good input and ideas for the work, so I am excited about how our presentation is received.

The first workshop with citizen involvement took place in December, the second at the beginning of February, and now it was time to present the proposal for the design and fitting of the station, which will also form the basis for Energinet's application for a local plan for the construction.

Both Kim Søgaard Mikkelsen and John Strandfelt, who are partner and business area manager at the architectural firm Arkitema, explained some of the thoughts behind the construction of the facility, as well as Mayor Jacob Trøst (K) initially gave a speech in which he explained, among other things, that he understands well. , that the plant is a big mouthful to swallow too many Bornholmers, but that the municipality has chosen to go constructively into the case, which also after all is about workplaces and finances.

The facades of the large buildings will be characteristic, as they will be as gigantic stones with sloping surfaces in matte and natural color material, and although it will be clear that it is a man -made landscape, it will also be sought to be sought , that there will be the greatest possible biodiversity.

Content:
On top of Monday's presentation on Energiø's land facility, there was also the opportunity on Tuesday to ask questions, now in a quieter environment.

On Monday, more than 100 people showed up at the furniture factory for Energinet's presentation of the land plant's design.

But on Tuesday, a lot was slowed down when Energinet armed with coffee, pastry and Energiø material had invited to an open house in Aakirkebyhallernes Cafeteria, where even more questions had to be answered in a slightly more intimate room than the assembly at the furniture factory allowed.

- The purpose is to give people who could not find peace yesterday, an opportunity to ask questions and to follow up on what was presented, says sub -project manager Bent Sømod, who, together with two colleagues, was ready to welcome they Citizens who may emerge.

- And we have an expectation that it is those with something special at stake that would show up, he says, adding that they expect 10-20 citizens during the afternoon.

Because there is a lot at stake when it comes to the plant. It could be felt on Monday's presentation, which according to Bent Sømod was constructive and with emotions at stake.

- And we fully understand that and we will do what we can to treat people as best as possible, he says.

And even if you can't solve your problems by showing up in Aakirkeby on Tuesday afternoon, you can come and make your views applicable.

They steal money from us One of those who have emerged to make his views applicable is Michael Ellermann.

He has lived on Limensgaden close to Søndre Landevej for 25 years and will live about 140 meters from the land plant.

His land should not be acquired otherwise expropriated, just as some other affected reasons must, and his very large appeal is that the legislation is not adapted to a large energy project such as the energy island.

- There is some legislation that is not in place. My neighbors and I are not covered by value loss legislation, as if it had been solar cells or wind turbines to be erected. If I have to apply for compensation, it can only be when the land plant is in operation and there I am almost retired, he says.

- Maybe it was reasonable to change the law.

As it is now, we must search for what is called neighboring tolerance limit.

In addition to the noise nuisance and the extra traffic that the construction of the land plant will result in, Michael Ellermann also estimates that a land plant so close to the property will make the house difficult to sell and that at least it will result in a loss of value.

- I am a supporter of the green transition, but I am frustrated by the prospect of not being able to sell your house. They steal money from us in the sense that our property is rattling down in value, he says, adding that he has put a lot of money into his house to make it more energy friendly.

He feels failed by the country politicians and hopes that local politicians can do something for him and the neighbors and that the legislation will be changed.

For the energy island of Bornholm, probably is not the last major energy project being established.

Title: Her er de næste skridt mod energiøen
Content:
After a meeting on Monday, Energinet has presented the next steps in the establishment of the energy island.

For a meeting at the Furniture Factory in Nexø on Monday evening, Energinet presented its latest bid for the appearance and fitting of the upcoming converter station, which will be built south of Aakirkeby as part of the establishment of the energy island.

According to Energinet, the location is chosen for several reasons, and in a press release is told, among other things: - The eastern location provides plenty of room for landscape fit of the station, including a wide belt of trees. At the same time, the eastern location is closely related to the chosen architectural solution, which has been called the crack valley.

Here the station is divided into two parts, which together form a wedge with buildings on each side. At the same time, Risebæk is restored in a naturally thrown course between the two parts of the station, to form a recreational wetland together. The buildings are designed with sloping walls with a facade cladding in natural colors that emphasize the crevice valley.

Local plan must be submitted to the principles for the design of the station, according to Energinet, will form the basis for the application for a local plan, which in the near future will be sent to Bornholm's regional municipality. Thereafter, the application must be processed both administratively and politically, and a public consultation is held before the local plan can be adopted - probably until June next year, Energinet reports.

- It is Bornholm Region Municipality that sets the framework for how the station should be designed and fit into the landscape.

I think we, together with them, and the Bornholmers who have participated, have made a good basis for the further work. And then it is important to say that the station is not finished yet, so that details and layout can be changed. It finally comes into place when we have offered the task and found our supplier to build the station, says Kim Søgaard Mikkelsen, head project manager for Energiø Bornholm in Energinet.

Prior to the publication, Energinet has been in contact with the landowners who may lay land to the station.

Energinet has also contacted the neighbors who may live closest to the station.


TIMETABLE

March 2023: Application for a local plan for Bornholm Regional Municipality Initiation of local plan Preparation of plan proposals and environmental report Spring 2024: Approval of plan proposals and environmental reports Spring 2024: Public consultation June 2024: Finally adoption of plans and publication.
