Title: Her er spørgerunden, som borgmesteren ikke gav dig
Content:
It was not possible to get answers to its questions as the municipality held a civic meeting on the energy island last week. We rush to with a queue round.

Last week, the municipality and Mayor Jacob Trøst (K) had convened a large -scale citizen meeting on the energy island, where Bornholm's citizens were invited to Søndermarkshallen, where we could get answers to our questions about the huge project that soon strikes us.

The state has decided that we must be energy island, so we will be with offshore wind turbines, land facilities and whatever else.

The aim is now to have the greatest possible influence on the design so that we can all be fairly happy and satisfied.

Citizens' meetings are a good idea in this regard. Then you can step up with your dissatisfaction and questions and get some of the wise heads to speak - and maybe get answers to the uncertainties that had to fill your head.

But unfortunately, some of the criticism in the wake of last week's session in Søndermarkshallen has been that the possibility of getting answers was not present sufficiently. For where was the opportunity to ask questions? Several of the Citizens' Meeting's participants came to the Journal and asked if it could now be true that there was no questionnaire in plenary as an actual program point, and yes, unfortunately there was the case.

Exactly a year ago - in April 2022 - there was actually a civic meeting on the energy island. It was in Aakirkeby with the participation of, among other things, angry neighbors. And guess what was one of the criticisms after the meeting: Lack of questionnaire in plenary.

In other words, the municipality has not learned much about holding a civic meeting on the year that has passed, and therefore we have decided on the Journal that we will try to get answers to some of the questions that it right now As a private citizen at Bornholm is difficult to find answers to.

Therefore: If you are missing answers to questions related to the large project Energiø Bornholm, do not hesitate to ask Tidende in an email to redaktion@idende.dk. Then, through the relevant authorities, we will seek the answers that it was unfortunately not possible to find in the Søndermarkshallen.

And until then we would like to give the municipality our best advice when planning the next citizen meeting on the energy island: Remember a questionnaire now.

Title: Formand med klar besked til erhvervslivet: Alle vil få gavn af energiø
Content:
As chairman of the Business Center Bornholm Board of Directors, Karen Bladt urges everyone to be curious about the opportunities that Energiø Bornholm offers.

It depends on the eyes that see whether to be excited or worried about Energiø Bornholm. In Business Center Bornholm you have no doubt. The energy island is a huge opportunity if the Bornholm community and the island's businesses are curious about the possibilities and embrace the changes.

It is one of the messages in the annual report from Chairman Karen Bladt.

- Bornholm stands an exciting place.

The energy island is on the way, hopefully together with several wind farms and follow -up industries.

It is a huge opportunity for our community and local businesses, it sounds from her.

The energy island is already filling up a part in the local business center, which is working to make the local businesses ready to bid on the tasks that come in connection with the big project. It is about dressing them up with certifications, knowledge and skills so that they can become an active part of the upcoming work, which with the President's eyes will also benefit others.

- Not all Bornholm companies become part of the energy island directly, but I am convinced that we will all benefit from the development that comes with the effort. With the energy island and the followers of the industry follows labor, which must live and live on the island, and thus many will be able to feel the side effect of the energy island. It will spread like rings in the water, says Karen Bladt in her annual report.

Business Center Bornholm Chairman is listening to the fact that there is some insecurity and concern when the talk falls on the energy island and what it will mean for Bornholm.

- I can easily understand that, but I would urge everyone to be curious about the opportunities that lie in the energy island and how the local business community can come into play. At Business Center Bornholm we are already well underway, she says.

As mentioned, Energiø Bornholm is already part of Business Center Bornholm's work, and it will fill a lot this year, Karen Bladt predicts.

- We must help ensure that both business and Bornholm get the most out of it, and that the companies and their employees become clear and adaptable that Bornholm becomes a Danish hub for future energy production. We need to embrace the changes, because more of them will be coming in the future.

But also remember that with change, new exciting opportunities often arise, she says.


Projects for just over 40 million kroner

Specifically, the business center's work with Energiø Bornholm takes place in the two projects National Center for Green Energy and Ready for Energiø Bornholm, which will make Bornholm respectively a hub for green energy and make local businesses and their employees ready for this.

The total budget for the two projects is DKK 42.4 million, and the Business Center Bornholm contributes with employee resources.

Under the auspices of the National Center for Green Energy, 10 individual business courses have been initiated with a focus on giving the Bornholm companies structure and overview of how they become an attractive partner and supplier, and ready for Energiø Bornholm, among other things, gives them insight into the culture of offshore -The industry, requirements for suppliers and framework conditions for the offshore industry.

Title: S vil placere boliger til energiøen i fire byer
Content:
Bornholm will start as soon as possible if the upcoming housing for the energy island's construction workers must be good, permanent housing instead of container villages, says the Social Democracy, which calls on the mayor to go into negotiations with the state.

The many people who will build the offshore wind turbines and the land facility for the upcoming energy island must not be accommodated in temporary container housing.

On the contrary, they must live in actual housing that can become part of the Bornholm housing stock when the construction is over.

At least that is the opinion of the Municipal Council's parties, and the wish was also presented to Climate, Energy and Supply Minister Lars Aagaard (M) when he visited Bornholm on 13.

March.

But even though the minister here was asked to think permanent housing into Bornholm's overall development plan or compensation for landing the energy island, Bornholm must also very quickly start making their own housing and that they are both designed And located that Bornholm wants.

Therefore, at the upcoming meeting of the municipal council, the Social Democracy will suggest that the work will start as soon as possible.

The Social Democracy has four cities in the binoculars and wants the upcoming homes erected in extension of Rønne, Nexø, Aakirkeby and Pedersker. This is stated by group chairman Claus Larsen-Jensen (S).

- Aakirkeby is close to the land facility.

Rønne is a shipping port for offshore wind turbines in the Baltic Sea and will also be a service port for the offshore wind turbines. Nexø is also expected to become a shipping port for offshore wind turbines, he says.

-Placing the homes in South and Midtbornholm therefore makes good sense in relation to future workplaces, the integration of the homes in these cities and a support of the trade and cultural life in the cities, says Claus Larsen-Jensen.

In addition, Energinet can act even the Social Democracy will start now, because the party fears that greater forces will take the matter into their own hands.

- If that work does not get started, the risk is that Energinet and the companies to establish the offshore wind turbines and build the land plant has to find alternative and temporary solutions, and then the Bornholm's chance to get the homes as permanent housing, says Claus Larsen-Jensen.

Therefore, the Social Democracy will give Mayor Jacob Trøst (K) mandate to immediately start negotiating with the government, Energinet and the parties behind the tenders at Energiøen's facility.

The Social Demkratia will also order the mayor to negotiate with a goal that the state pays the partial financing of new public housing that the municipalities are usually committed to laying.

- You can establish a development company that aims to establish housing so that they can become general rental housing afterwards.

It should be proposed that the state, for example, goes in with the proportion that the municipality usually has to pay as part of a general building, or that in another way the economy is provided to build these homes, says Claus Larsen-Jensen.

With its proposal, the Social Democracy will also order the municipality's administration to start considering specific areas as soon as possible and preparing building permits, "so that there are no delays in the process".

Title: Vi skal selv sætte retningen
Content:
Jo mere samarbejde over Østersøen jo bedre, skriver Knud Andersen, der er tidligere amtsborgmester for Venstre.

Bornholms Tidende har stillet spørgsmålet om, hvor vi drømmer os hen, når vi taler om Bornholms placering i Østersøen. I henvendelsen fra avisen spørger chefredaktøren yderligere, om vi skal sætte retning på udviklingen eller lade os blæse med vinden.

De nærmere overvejelser på avisen kan jeg naturligvis ikke vide noget om, men ser vi på de seneste års udvikling på Bornholm, er det på høje tid, at vi selv begynder at sætte retning på udviklingen. Vi har i den grad ladet os flyve rundt, som vinden blæser. Vi har i dag en politisk ledelse af Bornholm, som er usynlig, venlig, men usynlig. Venlighed kan måske række til et genvalg, men ikke til at udstikke de veje, som Bornholm skal gå.

Hvis man anskuer de seneste tendenser i kommunalbestyrelsen, så er der næsten kun et parti, som fastholder den politiske linje, nemlig Enhedslisten.

Derfor er mit første ønske for Bornholm, at alle partier i kommunalbestyrelsen sætter Bornholms ve og vel foran egne politiske interesser, sådan at Bornholm får orden i eget hus, inden vi tilbyder andre samarbejde.

Lad mig nævne et par eksempler på beslutninger, der ikke underbygger en sikker angivelse af retningen. Regionskommunen har siden sin etablering svækket erhvervslivets stemme ved at ændre det tidligere erhvervsråds status fra at være erhvervslivet stemme i debatten til de facto at være en afart af en kommunal institution uden væsentlig betydning i diskussionen om erhvervslivets vilkår på Bornholm, se blot listen over kommuners erhvervsvenlighed.

Samtidig har man føjet turisterhvervets ønsker. Vel vidende at antallet af turister ikke er et brugbart mål for, hvor meget lokalsamfundet vinder på et øget antal besøgende.

Senest ses sagen om flexboliger i et helårsområde.

Derfor er mit andet ønske, at kommunalbestyrelsen beslutter, at delfinansiere et nyt erhvervsråd med en stemme lige så stærk som turismens stemme.

Som tredje eksempel har socialdemokratiske borgmestre siden Regionskommunens start nedtrappet vore internationale kontakter, sådan at der i dag kun er Euroregion Baltic tilbage. (Samarbejde mellem Bornholm og regioner fra Sverige, Polen og Litauen) Derfor kan Bornholms politiske placering i Østersøen ikke tage udgangspunkt i samarbejder, der blev skabt i 90' erne. Situationen dengang var tre baltiske lande, Polen, tidligere Østtyskland og Rusland, som alle var interesserede i og havde behov for at se, hvordan frie lande fungerede.

Tilsvarende var der på Bornholm et stort ønske om at lære vore naboer at kende.

Vi havde helt grundlæggende den opfattelse, at små samfund (Bornholm) skal have store ører og store øjne for at lære noget af andre. På den baggrund havde amt og kommuner i 90-erne samarbejdsog uddannelsesaftaler med 12-15 byer og regioner omkring Østersøen. Vi kunne lære noget af hinanden.

I dag er situationen anderledes. Et samlet Tyskland, Polen, Litauen, Letland og Estland er nu foran Bornholm i udvikling, og hvis disse lande på det erhvervsmæssige område ønsker bistand, spørger man i Bruxelles og ikke på Bornholm. Rusland er et kapitel for sig. Som situationen er nu, er samarbejde med Kaliningrad og St. Petersburg ikke aktuelt.

Tilbage er der kulturelle samarbejder og sociale kontakter. På disse områder er der til gengæld et stort behov for udvikling og nye aktiviteter. Ved besøg i de baltiske lande og Polen bliver man hurtigt klar over, at frygten for den store nabo mod øst er meget mere udbredt og reel end hos os. Godt nok er landene medlem af EU og Nato, men man bliver ofte mindet om, at to gange tidligere er landene blevet ladt i stikken af vestlige lande -trods garantier. Derfor tror mange ikke på at den sikkerhed, som Nato skulle give.

I det billede har Bornholm noget at gøre.

Jo mere samarbejde over Østersøen jo bedre.

Det vil øge tilliden til, at garantier holdes, hvis det skulle blive nødvendigt. Samtidig lærer vi lidt om, hvad vi selv kan gøre for at man i grænselandene mod øst føler, at man ikke er alene med truslen fra den store nabo.

Derfor skal foreninger af alle slags på Bornholm aktiveres med henblik på at undersøge, om netop de har noget at tilbyde og selv kan have glæde af kontakter i et eller flere lande om Østersøen. Det være sig kulturelle, sports, religiøse foreninger og andre.

Vi har set et nyetableret Baltisk Bro som et godt tegn på, at interessen er til stede på begge sider af Østersøen.

Samarbejder rundt Østersøen kommer ikke af sig selv. Der kræves finansiering af fælles aktiviteter. Derfor er mit tredje ønske, at regionskommunen stiller midler til rådighed for foreninger, som vil indgå i samarbejder med tilsvarende foreninger i et eller flere lande omkring Østersøen.

Til en begyndelse kan regionskommunen invitere relevante personer fra de forskellige landene til en konference på Bornholm med henblik på at konkretisere et øget kulturelt samarbejde.

Bornholm har tidligere været initiativtager til oprettelse af EU programmer, der omfattede aktiviteter i Østersøområdet. Tiden er inde til at genoprette den status i EU, som Bornholm havde inden kommunen lukkede ned for de internationale aktiviteter. Der skal arbejdes for, at der etableres et EU-program, der støtter og udvikler det kulturelle samarbejde over Østersøen med henblik på at knytte befolkningerne tættere sammen. Et er, at Nato-landene har soldater placeret i de baltiske lande og Polen, noget andet er at skabe bred forståelse for situationens alvor.

Derfor er mit fjerde ønske, at regionskommunen genopliver det internationale politiske engagement.

I Østersø-sammenhænge er energiøen det store dyr for tiden. Lytter man til kommunalbestyrelsen, så vil etableringen løse mange af Bornholms problemer. Der høres synspunkter om, at det vil blive lige så stort som fiskeriet var tidligere, cirka 3.000 arbejdspladser, at power-to-x-udviklingen og produktion vil foregå her, at Bornholm vil blive tilknyttet elnettet (det ejer vi ikke mere).

At Bornholm kan blive midtpunktet i en energiudvikling i Østersølandene og lignende synspunkter. Dem er jeg noget skeptisk overfor. Virkeligheden var vel også, at ingen andre steder i Danmark ville have anlægget placeret på land. Derfor var det nemt for politikerne at få det placeret her uden kendskab til de reelle konsekvenser, hverken hvad angår beskæftigelse eller miljøpåvirkning.

Miljøpåvirkning på flere felter, hensynet til naturen og konsekvenser ved arbejdet med power-x, hvis det skulle blive aktuelt.

Mit fjerde ønske for Bornholm er, at ansvarlige politikere trin for trin vurderer, om fordelen ved at placere et anlæg af den størrelse overhovedet er interessant for andre end dem, der skal modtage strømmen. Heri ligger naturligvis noget Østersørelateret, da det er lande omkring Østersøen, der skal modtage den strøm der produceres.

For at svare på Bornholms Tidendes spørgsmål om hvor jeg drømmer mig hen: 1. At alle partier i kommunalbestyrelsen sætter Bornholms ve og vel foran egne politiske interesser.

2. At kommunalbestyrelsen beslutter at etablere og delfinansiere et nyt uafhængigt erhvervsråd.

3. At regionskommunen stiller midler til rådighed for foreninger, som vil indgå i samarbejder med tilsvarende foreninger i et eller flere lande omkring Østersøen.

5. At ansvarlige politikere trin for trin vurderer, om fordelen ved at placere et anlæg (EnergiØ) af den størrelse overhovedet er interessant for andre end dem, der skal modtage strømmen.

Nogle af disse penge kan bruges til at finansiere mine andre ønsker.


KNUD ANDERSEN

Knud Andersen er gårdejer og politisk kommentator. Han er tidligere borgmester og amtsborgmester for Venstre på Bornholm.

Jo mere samarbejde over Østersøen jo bedre, skriver Knud Andersen, der er tidligere amtsborgmester for Venstre.

Bornholms Tidende har stillet spørgsmålet om, hvor vi drømmer os hen, når vi taler om Bornholms placering i Østersøen. I henvendelsen fra avisen spørger chefredaktøren yderligere, om vi skal sætte retning på udviklingen eller lade os blæse med vinden.

De nærmere overvejelser på avisen kan jeg naturligvis ikke vide noget om, men ser vi på de seneste års udvikling på Bornholm, er det på høje tid, at vi selv begynder at sætte retning på udviklingen. Vi har i den grad ladet os flyve rundt, som vinden blæser. Vi har i dag en politisk ledelse af Bornholm, som er usynlig, venlig, men usynlig. Venlighed kan måske række til et genvalg, men ikke til at udstikke de veje, som Bornholm skal gå.

Hvis man anskuer de seneste tendenser i kommunalbestyrelsen, så er der næsten kun et parti, som fastholder den politiske linje, nemlig Enhedslisten.

Derfor er mit første ønske for Bornholm, at alle partier i kommunalbestyrelsen sætter Bornholms ve og vel foran egne politiske interesser, sådan at Bornholm får orden i eget hus, inden vi tilbyder andre samarbejde.

Lad mig nævne et par eksempler på beslutninger, der ikke underbygger en sikker angivelse af retningen. Regionskommunen har siden sin etablering svækket erhvervslivets stemme ved at ændre det tidligere erhvervsråds status fra at være erhvervslivet stemme i debatten til de facto at være en afart af en kommunal institution uden væsentlig betydning i diskussionen om erhvervslivets vilkår på Bornholm, se blot listen over kommuners erhvervsvenlighed.

Samtidig har man føjet turisterhvervets ønsker. Vel vidende at antallet af turister ikke er et brugbart mål for, hvor meget lokalsamfundet vinder på et øget antal besøgende.

Senest ses sagen om flexboliger i et helårsområde.

Derfor er mit andet ønske, at kommunalbestyrelsen beslutter, at delfinansiere et nyt erhvervsråd med en stemme lige så stærk som turismens stemme.

Som tredje eksempel har socialdemokratiske borgmestre siden Regionskommunens start nedtrappet vore internationale kontakter, sådan at der i dag kun er Euroregion Baltic tilbage. (Samarbejde mellem Bornholm og regioner fra Sverige, Polen og Litauen) Derfor kan Bornholms politiske placering i Østersøen ikke tage udgangspunkt i samarbejder, der blev skabt i 90' erne. Situationen dengang var tre baltiske lande, Polen, tidligere Østtyskland og Rusland, som alle var interesserede i og havde behov for at se, hvordan frie lande fungerede.

Tilsvarende var der på Bornholm et stort ønske om at lære vore naboer at kende.

Vi havde helt grundlæggende den opfattelse, at små samfund (Bornholm) skal have store ører og store øjne for at lære noget af andre. På den baggrund havde amt og kommuner i 90-erne samarbejdsog uddannelsesaftaler med 12-15 byer og regioner omkring Østersøen. Vi kunne lære noget af hinanden.

I dag er situationen anderledes. Et samlet Tyskland, Polen, Litauen, Letland og Estland er nu foran Bornholm i udvikling, og hvis disse lande på det erhvervsmæssige område ønsker bistand, spørger man i Bruxelles og ikke på Bornholm. Rusland er et kapitel for sig. Som situationen er nu, er samarbejde med Kaliningrad og St. Petersburg ikke aktuelt.

Tilbage er der kulturelle samarbejder og sociale kontakter. På disse områder er der til gengæld et stort behov for udvikling og nye aktiviteter. Ved besøg i de baltiske lande og Polen bliver man hurtigt klar over, at frygten for den store nabo mod øst er meget mere udbredt og reel end hos os. Godt nok er landene medlem af EU og Nato, men man bliver ofte mindet om, at to gange tidligere er landene blevet ladt i stikken af vestlige lande -trods garantier. Derfor tror mange ikke på at den sikkerhed, som Nato skulle give.

I det billede har Bornholm noget at gøre.

Jo mere samarbejde over Østersøen jo bedre.

Det vil øge tilliden til, at garantier holdes, hvis det skulle blive nødvendigt. Samtidig lærer vi lidt om, hvad vi selv kan gøre for at man i grænselandene mod øst føler, at man ikke er alene med truslen fra den store nabo.

Derfor skal foreninger af alle slags på Bornholm aktiveres med henblik på at undersøge, om netop de har noget at tilbyde og selv kan have glæde af kontakter i et eller flere lande om Østersøen. Det være sig kulturelle, sports, religiøse foreninger og andre.

Vi har set et nyetableret Baltisk Bro som et godt tegn på, at interessen er til stede på begge sider af Østersøen.

Samarbejder rundt Østersøen kommer ikke af sig selv. Der kræves finansiering af fælles aktiviteter. Derfor er mit tredje ønske, at regionskommunen stiller midler til rådighed for foreninger, som vil indgå i samarbejder med tilsvarende foreninger i et eller flere lande omkring Østersøen.

Til en begyndelse kan regionskommunen invitere relevante personer fra de forskellige landene til en konference på Bornholm med henblik på at konkretisere et øget kulturelt samarbejde.

Bornholm har tidligere været initiativtager til oprettelse af EU programmer, der omfattede aktiviteter i Østersøområdet. Tiden er inde til at genoprette den status i EU, som Bornholm havde inden kommunen lukkede ned for de internationale aktiviteter. Der skal arbejdes for, at der etableres et EU-program, der støtter og udvikler det kulturelle samarbejde over Østersøen med henblik på at knytte befolkningerne tættere sammen. Et er, at Nato-landene har soldater placeret i de baltiske lande og Polen, noget andet er at skabe bred forståelse for situationens alvor.

Derfor er mit fjerde ønske, at regionskommunen genopliver det internationale politiske engagement.

I Østersø-sammenhænge er energiøen det store dyr for tiden. Lytter man til kommunalbestyrelsen, så vil etableringen løse mange af Bornholms problemer. Der høres synspunkter om, at det vil blive lige så stort som fiskeriet var tidligere, cirka 3.000 arbejdspladser, at power-to-x-udviklingen og produktion vil foregå her, at Bornholm vil blive tilknyttet elnettet (det ejer vi ikke mere).

At Bornholm kan blive midtpunktet i en energiudvikling i Østersølandene og lignende synspunkter. Dem er jeg noget skeptisk overfor. Virkeligheden var vel også, at ingen andre steder i Danmark ville have anlægget placeret på land. Derfor var det nemt for politikerne at få det placeret her uden kendskab til de reelle konsekvenser, hverken hvad angår beskæftigelse eller miljøpåvirkning.

Miljøpåvirkning på flere felter, hensynet til naturen og konsekvenser ved arbejdet med power-x, hvis det skulle blive aktuelt.

Mit fjerde ønske for Bornholm er, at ansvarlige politikere trin for trin vurderer, om fordelen ved at placere et anlæg af den størrelse overhovedet er interessant for andre end dem, der skal modtage strømmen. Heri ligger naturligvis noget Østersørelateret, da det er lande omkring Østersøen, der skal modtage den strøm der produceres.

Mit fjerde ønske for Bornholm er, at ansvarlige politikere trin for trin vurderer, om fordelen ved at placere et anlæg af den størrelse overhovedet er interessant for andre end dem, der skal modtage strømmen. 4. At regionskommunen genopliver det internationale politiske engagement.

5. At ansvarlige politikere trin for trin vurderer, om fordelen ved at placere et anlæg (EnergiØ) af den størrelse overhovedet er interessant for andre end dem, der skal modtage strømmen.

Title: Bornholm som potentielt østersøisk Saudiarabien i energimæssig forstand
Content:
What should we learn from the past to commit ourselves in the Baltic Sea of ​​the future? Where are we going to dream ourselves in the future?

My childhood TV newspapers often had a feature from Bornholm, where fishermen in blue boiler suits and fur hat with serious faces talked about quotas and catch days.

The word 'Konkors' pronounced on broad Bornholm appeared regularly. I myself lived 'over' from 1980 to 2003. My family moved over when I was five years old, but I had a slight memory of how much fishing had filled and how many cutters were in the ports.

When I returned to Bornholm, the harbor basins were deserted. And when I was rolling a stroller around Nexø, when I was holding paternity leave, the trip went past Nordfilet, where my little boy with big eyes admired the burial cow, who tore the industrial building down. It was clear that an era was over. But still, it didn't seem like there was the great sadness about it. I met some of the seamen who had had to sign the old cutters.

I commuted to Copenhagen and some of them I met in the airplane to Copenhagen. There was Esvagt or DanPilot on the work clothes. As good sailors, they had taken cutlery of the situation and relieved anchor and headed for new and more profitable waters. In Esbjerg, fishing had also suddenly disappeared, but instead the old fishermen now sailed for the offshore industry. Bornholmers were also needed. Others sailed tour boats in the Port of Copenhagen, and then of course there were those who stayed in the fishing, but now just sailed further away to the North Atlantic. The greatest luck had Ocean Prawns in Nexø, which hit a financial golden vein in the Greenland shrimp fishing.

I have often thought of my encounter with the generation of sailors when I have worked with Bornholm's history in a broader perspective.

For the willingness to find a path that I saw with them, I find again historical precedent. When there was a decline in fishing in the Baltic Sea in the mid-1800s, Bornholm ships sailed instead to Jan Mayen and Spitzbergen, where the slaughtered seals in large numbers.

The seals were cooked to Tran, which gave light to the Copenhagen street lamps. Bornholm was also an energy island at that time.

Those left on Bornholm also invented other than filleting fish. Rye biscuits were baked and distilled snaps and brewed beer, which you could rinse your Bornholm pasta. Cheese from Klemensker and mustard from Nexø moved into the Danes' refrigerators. And it wasn't just the stomachs that needed to be filled - there was something to the head too.

There was room for culture, spirit and politics with the People's Meeting in Allinge and the festival with Denmark's most cracked name, Wonder all that I mention here is in contrast to the downfall that you can sometimes meet among Bornholmers. When things do not go the right way, one complains, and shows back to how the "Copenhageners" also failed in 1945 and in 1658. This is how we all use the story as a mirror when we discuss our time. The story is our everyone's and it is a good place to pick up arguments.

But even though the Bornholmers can sometimes feel that they are bounded and live in a periphery, I now think I see the opposite.

The Bornholmers are to a much greater extent than other regions extremely well -integrated with their capital. It is especially when the connection to Copenhagen is challenged that the Bornholmers complain most loudly. In fact, we expect that we can get to Copenhagen easily, quickly and conveniently. It is not an expectation one has in Skagen or Thorsminde. This relationship with the capital and state power goes far back.

In 1658 it was also not much whether Bornholm's capital was called Copenhagen or Stockholm.

The story of the fishing on Bornholm is in fact a transitional narrative rather than a downfall narrative. Of course, there were examples of people who were hit hard by the circumstances as fishing collapsed.

But the general picture of Bornholm in the years after the collapse is surprisingly positive. Bornholm has never become part of the 'rotten banana'. And if you want to see villages with empty houses and boards for the closed shop windows, then you have to go to West Zealand or Lolland - not to Bornholm.

This does not mean that there are no social and financial problems on Bornholm. But the scope is smaller than one might have expected.

Now Bornholm is facing a new transition.

Climate change and security policy suddenly make Bornholm a really central place on the European map. When I open my app to see what the weather is like, I get a picture that shows where it blows her.

Often large parts of Europe are colored completely blue, which means that there is almost wind, but around Bornholm there is often yellow or orange. Here it mostly blows. That makes Bornholm interesting as a potential Baltic Sea Saudi Arabia in the energy sense.

In any case, billion investments in wind energy will in any case mean that the Bornholmers will once again get used to new industries and new neighbors. There will be a migration to a degree we have not seen for generations.

The new plants will characterize the landscape and partly as well as damn it. But seen with the glasses of the historian and the archaeologist, it is just another phase in a wide range of landscape changes. We have long since waved goodbye to the phone poles that characterized my childhood Bornholm. And in a hundred years, I also dare to predict that wind turbines and land facilities have again disappeared in favor of something else that I do not have the imagination today.

As the wind turbines rise on the horizon on the sea, you will need to sail out and service them. It is not inconceivable that the fisherman who embarked on a trawler in Nexø in 1985 and who is forced by the collapse of fishing in 1990 turned his nose to Esbjerg, now at a mature age can return to Bornholm and sail his last years for the energy island.

Title: Viden, fællesskab og samarbejde
Content:
I dream that we have a society where we focus on each other, writes Maria Hach.

In recent times, Bornholm's Journal has focused on Bornholm's future and what future we dream of for Bornholm. It has been debated in the newspaper and a number of debate salons are scheduled to start today's meeting on Bornholm's role in the Baltic Sea.

It has been interesting to follow the different views and dreams of where Bornholm is going, and I can easily understand many of the perspectives that are presented. I do not think there is any doubt that most citizens of Bornholm know about the challenges the war in Ukraine has brought with them, increasing prices of energy, food, wear parts for production and transport. We also experience the threat at regular intervals when the Danish Jægerfly marks the territory at Bornholm, and every time I hear them, I think they are there, but if it came to the piece, we probably did not have the big chance. We would need help and collaboration with others.

We are, as Ivar Nielsen also writes, part of a larger context, part of a country with a government, a European community and a world where everything has an impact on each other. Of course, we could spend time tired of that, but does it help at all? Here I mean that instead of complaining about what someone is doing or not doing, or waiting for someone to do something for us, then we have to tighten the waistband, put on the work gloves, and find out what we want. Focus on the things we are good at, build on them and find a direction for where we want to go. We must create the society we want with the opportunities we have.

Where do I dream of Bornholm? Yes, I dream that we have a society where we focus on each other where we can accommodate each other's differences.

A society where we jointly lift our children, create good family life, good institutions and schools. A society where all the municipal employees are valued, including those with the icy hands behind the computer and not just up to the election campaign. I want a society where we dare make mistakes, try new ways of doing things off, and acknowledge if it doesn't work. The fact that we create housing that provides a framework for us to help across generations and interests, and I could continue my dream, my vision for Bornholm into the infinite.

To get you in advance of where the money will come from, I will immediately say that they have to come from two things. First, we must do as I mentioned before. We need to tighten the waistband, put on the work gloves and know where we want to go. Secondly, we need to find the opportunities we have.

So what opportunities do we have and what role are we wanting to have in the Baltic Sea? We do not get around it, but we have a huge opportunity in connection with Energiø Bornholm and the whole way in which our joint energy company BEOF works to gather new knowledge within the future energy systems.

Here I see that we have more opportunities to take advantage of.

1. We get the Bornholm network connected to the land plant, which will mean that we at Bornholm are guaranteed a stable supply of electricity, whether or not a cable to Sweden should be smoked.

2. It creates knowledge and can provide revenue for Bornholm 3. When we have access to large amounts of energy, in addition to being able to pass the power on to other countries, we will also be able to generate an income to Denmark. We will be able to attract companies that work to test energy storage or to transform electricity into other forms of energy. The processes provide a surplus heat which, if we shop for it, can use in our common district heating network and over time provide cheaper district heating and district heating where wood chips are not the primary source.

I could come up with many more examples of how Energiø Bornholm is a huge opportunity that we at Bornholm in the future can play a central role in the Baltic Sea. We must be those who create the collaboration and the community around the Baltic Sea.

Those who ensure that we keep getting new knowledge about what technologies can work in the real world and what directions we should go into in the green transition.

We need to focus on creating good relationships with our neighboring countries and finding the areas where we can create new collaborations for the benefit of Bornholm.

No, the energy island is not the solution to all our challenges, but it is a huge opportunity to think long -term and think ahead, and create some economy to pay for all our dreams. I am aware that there are more citizens who are severely affected by the development that the energy island brings, it is not just something we need to know and acknowledge, it is something we as a society have to act on. We need to make sure that those affected can move on properly, create a new life, because that is what the community does in my view.

Title: Debat om energiøen - i bred forstand - blæses i gang
Content:
The time has come for the Bornholm society to have a thorough discussion about what opportunities one will seize when Bornholm achieves a position as a hub for electricity and perhaps hydrogen in the Baltic Sea in a few years, says Søren Møller Christensen from Baltic Energy Island. Today, Tidende starts the second theme in the debate series "Where do we dream".

Tidende's series of debate "Where do we dream" today are embarking on a new theme that will run until the end of May.

The energy island is the focal point of the debate.

After six weeks of a wide range of posts and views on the Tidende debate pages, many of the debaters gather for a debate salon, which is scheduled to take place 23.

May at the Electric Works in Rønne.

With the energy of the future as the subject, the power plant is an obvious place to meet. The protected building contained until the 1950s the generators, which supplied electricity to the citizens of Rønne, and lately the power plant has become home to Baltic Energy Island, which is the organization previously called the National Center for Green Energy.

The idea of ​​a "National Center for Green Energy" was first aired in the public during the municipal election campaign in 2021, when Thomas Thors (S) talked about the vision, which had gathered the first participants.

- It is a huge chance for Bornholm that you can make this center, where prominent professions will go in as partners, and now we have announcements from two major partners, DTU and Energinet, the then mayor said.

Along the way, among other things, energy autodonts such as Ørsted and Siemens-Gamesa have joined the partnership.

In 2022, support of DKK 27.2 million succeeded from the Danish Business Promotion Board, which communicates millions from the EU's structural and regional funds for business projects in the regions.

Outwardly, the project has changed its name along the way to the more internationally oriented "Baltic Energy Island". In August, the main forces said the partnership in 2023 will be expanded with a fund.

The fact that the support schemes for regional lighthouse projects were introduced, at about the same time as the birth of the Energiø project and the extensive investment in offshore winds around Bornholm, is hugely fortunate for the region, points out Søren Møller Christensen, constituted director of Baltic Energy Island.

- It lands at the same time as the biggest business opportunity since fishing collapsed on Bornholm, he states when the Journal visits the Power Plant, where the small staff in Baltic Energy Island has their offices in a heated side building.

A mecca in a broad sense for citizen meetings about the energy island, Søren Møller Christensen has participated several times. Initially as head of "Development and Plan" in the regional municipality, and lately in his new position as constituted director of Baltic Energy Island. At the mayor's recent civic meeting in Søndermarkshallen in March, he had 10 minutes to keep the presentation "The Energy Island: A Green Mecca for Development".

In isolation, Energiø Bornholm is a single very large wind turbine project that the Danish state has taken the initiative - with associated high -voltage station and cable connections to Germany and Zealand.

But when the "energy island" is described as a development mecca, the word is understood in a broader sense. Søren Møller Christensen reminded the audience that three offshore wind turbine projects are currently being worked on around Bornholm.

The locally anchored Bornholm's offshore wind (0.1 gigawatts) off Snogebæk and Nexø, Energiø Bornholm South and Southwest of the Coast (3.2-3.8 GW) and Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners (CIP) and Ørsted's joint power-to-X-X- Based project (3.0 GW) that is currently surrounded by uncertainty because the Danish Energy Agency has suspended the open door scheme that the energy companies have applied for.

The overall capacity of the three projects is very similar to the capacity of all wind turbines that are today erected in Denmark - on land and water together. Overall, the parks - if they all realized - could supply electricity to seven million households, Søren Møller Christensen told the civic meeting.

"The total investment is up to DKK 150 billion for all three projects," he said.

In the two offshore wind farms that CIP/ Ørsted wants to place east of Bornholm, the nearest mills must stand 25 and 42 kilometers respectively. Energy Island Møller gets a distance from the coast of 15 kilometers, where they are closest, while Bornholm's offshore wind is a coastal project with nine mills, where the nearest is scheduled to be 5.5 kilometers from the coast.

At the same time, CIP is involved in a project with a new Baltic Brint connection to go from Sweden and Finland to Germany and pass east around Bornholm. In his presentation, Søren Møller Christensen presented German and Danish maps of future hydrogen and electricity compounds, where Bornholm was clearly marked and had a central location.

- Suddenly Bornholm has a completely different geography. On the cards we are not misplaced in a corner of the Kattegat, but are the Center for Energy Production, he said.

This location offers plenty of options, but to get an overview it makes sense to distinguish between the forms of energy.

Energiø Bornholm is about electricity generation, and the wind turbine power must be led in cables from Bornholm to Germany and Zealand. It is a pioneer project because it has never been built high -voltage plants with several direct current connections and the technique that Energinet adds up. Therefore, there are high hopes that Bornholm will be interesting for researchers and companies who will keep up with the development. Included in the dream are the creation of a test center at the land facility and a residential college with classrooms and study places at the Electricity Works as well as college housing for visiting researchers and students in Rønne.

The construction phase for Energiø Bornholm will require many men, but the hopes of the large business adventure with new businesses and many hundreds of extra jobs are rather linked to Power-to-X (PTX) and the production of hydrogen or green fuels at a local electrolysis plant.

However, the big dreams are not only related to the Power-to-X production itself, but at least as much the followers that can make use of waste products from the process.

These are especially surplus heat, but also oxygen that occurs when splitting the water molecules to make hydrogen. The quantities of heat that are left over are colossal.

It is estimated that the waste heat from an electrolysis plant on the scale that CIP/ Ørsted could need will be six-nine times larger than Bornholm's current district heating consumption. In addition to giving Bornholmers and businesses on the island cheaper heat and better framework conditions, such large amounts of energy can attract new professions.

Horticulture, aquaculture and a tropical water park have been mentioned as opportunities. The large quantities of power that are led to land can form the basis for establishing electricity -consuming plants as data centers. Experience from other places has shown that data center will not lead to the creation of many permanent jobs.

Debate about priorities The synergy from the energy - yes, it sounds a bit like a biscuit metaphor - thus holds many opportunities, and this is where the establishment of a business park comes into the picture. The recommendation from Søren Møller Christensen is that the municipality quickly starts an analysis of what you want to bet on.

- The most important thing is that we decide what wants out of the energy island. What do we want to seize and what do we not want to seize? he said at the Citizens' Meeting.

In that debate, politicians must also decide where a business park should be placed. Elsewhere in the country, Power-to-X plants are built a dozen kilometers from large transformer stations.

However, there are immediately technical and financial benefits of gathering everything close to each other near the vicinity of the high -voltage facility in SOSE, but whether a location on the South Bornholm is ultimately the right one must be investigated and debated so that a decision can be made on an informed basis, says Søren Møller Christensen.

-If we are to have Power-to-X, how do we get Bornholnmsk Job creation out of it? What is the benefit of placing the PTX close to the transformer station and how crucial is it for the derived occupations to be close to the PTX production? Mention Søren Møller Christensen as examples of questionnaire, he believes should be examined and discussed.

- An overall assessment of what makes sense is needed. For Bornholm, it is important to find a setup that results in the creation of lasting jobs, he says with pressure on the word "lasting".

"To wait and see the time" and take cutlery of business interest in connecting to the energy island will be a mistake for the Bornholm community, says Søren Møller Christensen.

He advocates that one creates an ambitious narrative and some framework that can strengthen Bornholm's position as a crucial hub with technology that has never been tested before.

- We need a vision. It takes more than a good Excel sheet and a business case. It is a huge chance for us that we are a first place to build an energy island. That is why big companies are so eager to join, says Søren Møller Christensen.

He believes that the next time will be spent on gathering information and keeping advantages and disadvantages against each other, so that the debate on the local strategy can be taken on an enlightened basis - and it is important to take the discussion now so that we can attract new businesses - And also innovation and research.

Tidende has joined forces with Baltic Bridge, Lag-Bornholm, CRT and the Bornholm Citizens' Association's Collaboration to run a number of theme batters, which over the next year will be brought into the columns with attitudes, opinions and not least dreams of Bornholm's challenges and opportunities.

The first theme was Bornholm's role in the Baltic Sea, and today the second theme is launched: Energy Island.

Title: Vision for et særligt sted
Content:
We look forward to presenting a preliminary bid for housing to Residential College Bornholm.

We go into a new era when Bornholm becomes the center of the green transition in the Baltic Sea region. The plan is for green power to be produced equivalent to three million icons of Danish household's electricity consumption.

But the adventure doesn't stop here. Among other things, there will be a sea of ​​opportunities to develop and test new technologies to translate and store the energy from the wind turbines.

Bornholm becomes the center of a project of dimensions, which is called a Marsmission for the Danish energy system.

However, the energy island is not a distant planet. A picture of a project is beginning to draw a major impact on the island. Seen here from Campus Bornholm, there are some opportunities that we have previously only dared to dream of.

The reality of the island's educational institutions is that the group of young people between the ages of 15 and 24 over the past 10 years has been reduced by 21 percent. It has presented challenges in ensuring a good study environment and in getting the schools' finances connected. For the Bornholm companies, the reality is an increasing shortage of qualified labor in both the public and the private sectors. In addition, a large part of the current workforce is approaching the retirement age.

One thing is sure: Energy Island will result in more jobs - but which and how many? The Center for Regional and Tourism Research in Hasle (CRT) has investigated this, and they will be publishing a coverage of competence needs later this month in connection with the energy island. It is obvious that construction and operational tasks will cause a significant expansion of the workforce, but people are also needed for many other industries when more people come to the island and more need to be serviced with everything from groceries to dental treatment.

We have a unique chance to get on the map both as Energiø and Education Island, but it does not happen by itself. We need to start creating a good framework as soon as possible to attract students and students from home and abroad, so that the energy island also becomes a catalyst for a boost of the overall educational environment on Bornholm. It will also make us more equal as a partner for other educational institutions.

It is not the story of a lack of that should attract people. It is the story of Bornholm as the center of the green transition, the story of the test island, where new technologies are developed in interaction between companies, researchers, students and users.

The story of a living laboratory with high ceilings, where professional groups meet across borders, subjects and experience. The story of an island in transformation that can attract companies and universities with resources and interest in investing and taking part in the green adventure.

We now have good experiences in making things succeed in spite of the island's modest population and despite small adolescents.

The programs collaborate for each other's best, and so do our partners in Baltic Energy Island (BEI), which invites broad cooperation from their new base in Rønne's old power plant.

The power plant will form the framework for a sustainable knowledge and learning environment for green energy aimed at students, researchers, apprentices and other guests. It will be a strong professional environment that campus will benefit from and vice versa.

The hope is that we will create an educational environment that attracts young people from other parts of the country as a necessary supplement to the island's own young people. In addition to ensuring a high professional level, it is necessary that we create a place where students, apprentices, researchers, etc. can live.

Now we have a historical opportunity to create a place where students, apprentices, researchers and others. can live for shorter or longer periods.

We work closely with Bei and DTU on this, and as DTU describes their activities on Bornholm under the hat Residential College Bornholm, the working title for our vision so far is housing for Residential College Bornholm.


Housing for Residential College Bornholm

The island's educational institutions, DTU, companies and more people agree that we need housing for Residential College Bornholm. That is why we have initiated a partnership with the participation of BEI, Bornholm Regional Municipality, DTU, Bornholm Hospital, Bornholm Museum, Campus Bornholm, Bornholm Health and Nursing School, Copenhagen Professional College and Copenhagen Business Academy.

Together, for almost a year and a half, we have been working on a vision of creating an attractive and synergy -creating educational environment, which both attracts young people from other parts of the country and thus strengthens our existing youth environment on Bornholm. The place must be closely linked to Bornholm as Energiø, to Baltic Energy Island and to the island's educational institutions.

We think in wise square meters, and the facilities we together have in the form of sports facilities, canteen and other things must be included in the overall solution.

It is hoped that the residents of the site, who are only here for a limited period, will become aware of the island and its business opportunities, and that it will give some desire to return and establish themselves here. For that is badly needed.

We have set up a working group with representatives of the various actors. Thanks to financial support from Sparekassen Bornholm Foundation and Bornholm Fire Insurance, we have been able to buy both architectural assistance and advice on how to organize and finance the place.

Until June we are working to describe the project in a so -called space program. We are not going to Mars, but we need to describe the needs of the coming users as accurately as possible.

It is crucial that we create a place that fits users' needs and their financial ability. Therefore, we must also ensure that the space is utilized as best as possible all year round. Upcoming user groups and other stakeholders are involved in the project through interviews that our advisers help to complete. We work on several possible scenarios and including possible locations and several possible ownership.

We look forward to presenting a preliminary bid for housing to Residential College Bornholm and looking forward to presenting the idea and material to foundations, investors, authorities and others who can also see the utility of the place.


Inge Prip

Director of Campus Bornholm and chairman of the steering committee for housing for Residential College Bornholm.

Title: Demokratisk underskud i vigtige energibeslutninger
Content:
It must be a common interest and ambition that large and important decisions that determine our energy infrastructure for the next several decades should not be listed by the back door, but made on a free, prior and informed basis.

Out in the world, one operates with the principle that when, for example, a state will carry out a large infrastructure project in an area that belongs to an original population, then there must be a 'free, prior and informed consent' from this group. Thus, it is not enough to obtain consent if it does not rest on a free decision -making process; If it is only sought after the important decisions have been made; Or if it does not rest on an enlightened basis.

In many ways, there are some quite well -known and healthy principles, such as the many state and municipal consultation processes that are carried out every year - when you want to build a new residential area, expand a company or build an energy island.

Or at least should rest on. Because when it comes to the many decisions that are made in these years in connection with the transformation of energy production away from fossil fuels and the construction of a new energy infrastructure, something indicates that these basic democratic principles are actually not complied with.

Last year at this time - on April 11, 2022 - the Danish Energy Agency called for a supplementary consultation in connection with Energiø Bornholm with a note on 'overplant', ie to increase the number of mills in the same place beyond what one would normally do . Here, the public was invited in a broad sense and also Bornholm's regional municipality to submit attitudes and suggestions on what conditions wanted to be elucidated, in relation to deciding whether an opportunity for increased mill density should be opened in relation to the impending supply of Energiø Bornholm .

The six -page note from the Danish Energy Agency lists a number of topics that could be considered to be examined to assess the environmental significance of such a 'overplanting'. What the memo does not say anything about, however, is the reason why the idea of ​​'overplanting' suddenly appeared and necessitated a supplementary consultation process.

All the Danish Energy Agency says in the memo is that in connection with the work with Energiø Bornholm it has assessed 'that it is appropriate to keep a door open for the fact that a political decision can be made at a later date on any' overplanting 'for the offshore wind. ' PTX in off the back road? What the Danish Energy Agency here desires is that this assessment is based on a so-called mini-market dialogue performed by the Danish Energy Agency in March 2022, ie prior to the broadcast of the note, with so-called market players, ie the companies that might be interested in having an interest in that offer the construction of the offshore wind farms south of Bornholm.

The conclusions of this mini-market dialogue can be read about if you dig a little deeper on the Danish Energy Agency's website. Here it appears that 'there is agreement among the market players that overplanting will make supply more attractive and that most market players mentioned the possibility of PTX production in connection with overplanting.' If we return to the principles of 'free, prior and informed consent', then consent to overplanting obtained on the basis of the Danish Energy Agency's consultation note would probably be characterized as free. On the other hand, it will be far more questionable whether a consent obtained on the basis of the Danish Energy Agency's consultation note can be characterized as neither 'prior' nor 'informed'.

For if the reason for enabling 'overplanting' is that potential bidders on the erection of offshore wind turbines south of Bornholm, would be able to expect to be able to establish PTX production on Bornholm, was that not what the public should be asked? And is it at all reasonable to make an offshore wind that allows for overplanting, and thus give the so-called 'market players' an expectation that they will be able to establish PTX production in connection with the installation of offshore wind farms if one has not secured a' prior 'and' informed 'basis for a decision on the desirable in and the consequences of a possible PTX production? Unfortunately, it is not only the Danish Energy Agency that, with the consultation note, fails the basic democratic principles of prior and informed consent. The public energy debate initiated by Bornholm Regional Municipality, most recently with the Citizens' Meeting in Rønne on March 30, 2023, leaves a lot to be desired when it comes to creating a free, prior and informed basis for discussions on the large energy investments, We are facing these years. Whatever one might think of PTX, it must be a common interest and ambition that large and important decisions that determine our energy infrastructure for the next several decades should not be listed by the back door, but be made on a free, prior and informed basis . It is basically what characterizes a democracy. We do not dare or dare it, Bornholm, to now use Jakob Seerup's image from an article brought in the Journal last week, not just becoming a potential Baltic Saudi Arabia in the energy sense, but also in the democratic sense.

Title: CRT: Power-to-x er nøglen til tilflytning
Content:
With two large offshore wind turbine projects around Bornholm and an associated electrolysis plant on a large scale on land, Bornholm's population will be able to grow by over 1,600 people in 2030, the Center for Regional and Tourism Research in a new study on the energy island's lasting job creation and settlement effect estimates. The target of 42,000 inhabitants will be within easy reach if new follow-up business is emerging that can utilize the waste heat, but without local power-to-X production, population growth does not come to that level, CRT states.

H vordan will the energy island affect the size of the Bornholm population? That question has the Center for Regional and Tourism Research (CRT) with a qualified look in the crystal ball tried to answer.

Let's start with the main conclusion: CRT's bid is that an energy island with both the state and CIP/ Ørsted's offshore wind farms as well as a power-to-x plant on Bornholm soil will be able to lift the population with 1,650 people in 2030. From 39,600 to over 41,200-ie Two -thirds of the road towards the 42,000 inhabitants that the municipal council has declared targets.

The prerequisite for this lasting employment effect is that the wind farms must be established with Rønne Harbor as a installation port and serviced from Bornholm ports and that an electrolysis plant of 3 GW is being built, writes CRT.

The study is built on three scenarios for the energy island. 1. Bornholm as Service Port, 2nd Bornholm as Service Port and Installation Harbor and 3rd Service Port, Installation Harbor and Power-to-X production.

The operation of the land facility is also included in the figures, but the two most important functions from an employment perspective are service port and power-to-x.

A service port for the state offshore wind farm will create 190 new man -years. In these figures, CIP/ Ørsted's proposed offshore wind farms of 3 gigawatts east of Bornholm are not recognized, but CRT estimates that the employment effect will be twice as large if these parks are realized with service from Bornholm, probably from Nexø. A Powerto-X system will provide 150 man-years when it is in operation, but such a large electrolysis system will depend on CIP/ Ørsted's idea of ​​several huge offshore wind farms.

The focal point of the study is the politicians' dream of reaching the 42,000 inhabitants who are believed to make the local community more economically sustainable, and the municipality's future significantly brighter.

CRT asks himself, in a press release, whether the energy projects can bring the population near the 42,000 by 2030.

"The short answer is according to the analysis: Yes, Energiø Bornholm has the potential to bring the number of Bornholmers up near 42,000, but it requires a power-to-X system," writes CRT.

The calculations do not contain offers for new businesses and workplaces that can be founded due to the innovative technology, the large amounts of current or the surplus heat that can potentially be utilized from an electrolysis plant or transformer station at Sydbornholm.

“It is impossible on the current basis to say how many companies and jobs could realistically lie in these green business opportunities.

Conversely, it would be unrealistic to imagine that no new energy -related companies will come to the island as a result of the energy island investments, ”writes CRT.

The figures and conclusions of the study are based on the assumption that all the lasting jobs must be occupied by newcomers, as there is already "approximately full employment" in the industries that are affected most by the energy investment that CRT writes. In addition, CRT assumes that each new workplace on the energy island will both provide employment with a partner and result in a derived effect on employment among subcontractors and in the industries that are otherwise benefiting from the rising economic activity on Bornholm. Finally, CRT assumes that the migrants for the energy island will have the same family profile as the newcomers in recent years, and in this way it can be calculated how many extra children are brought to Bornholm.

These assumptions, for example, mean that when 150 men are hired to operate a power-to-X system, the increased employment ends up 255 people, while the population grows by 301 according to CRT's figures.

The figures above include the many employees who will be temporarily accommodated on Bornholm during the construction period. The construction of the offshore wind farms, the high-voltage station, a possible power-to-x plant and the entire electrrastructure will bring a lot of people to the island. CRT estimates that temporary accommodation of up to 1,900 full-time equivalents will be needed when the construction activity is at its peak in 2028. Located employees will put a total consumption of DKK 662 million.


Become living after construction

It has previously been promoted that Energinet needs less than a handful of employees to operate the automated high -voltage station in Sydbornholm. Nevertheless, CRT estimates that the construction of the land plant will result in a direct employment increase of 40 people - and 75 when the derived effects are included.

Director Anne Thomas explains that because the construction process lasts several years, CRT assumes that a certain amount of people who take jobs at Bornholm to help build the high voltage station or an electrolysis plant ends up staying on the island .

- When a newcomer has moved here and has been here for a period of time, we expect him to be part of the Bornholm labor market.

That is why we are talking about lasting employment.

The CRT's proposal for the population of 2030 is thus based on the expectation that some of the traveling employees will remain in the local craftsmanship when the complexes of the energy island are completed.

The same mechanism applies to the installation of the offshore wind farms to Energiø Bornholm. Here, CRT assumes that lasting employment will increase by 60 people, as more than 500 people will stay at Bornholm when the wind farm south of land is to be established.

Because at Bornholm there is a shortage of skilled labor, and many employees retire in the coming years, CRT assumes that an increase in employment will require a similar number of people to the municipality - even if the tasks for the energy island's projects go to local Businesses, it is newcomers who have to take them because we have a saturated labor market, says Anne Thomas.

At a so -called Knowledge Café on Tuesday, the CRT presented the results of the study, and in May a more detailed report is reported, which must be presumed to include an overview of references and sources that are so far absent in the 12 -page note "Bornholm's Road to Growth", As the research institution based in Hasle presented Tuesday. CRT's study is financially supported by the National Center for Green Energy, which is funded by Social and Regional Funds from the EU.

Title: Uden brint blegner energiøens vækstpotentiale
Content:
The effect of the major energy projects on the relocation and employment becomes almost three times greater if CIP and Ørsted's plans for hydrogen production on a large scale on Bornholm soil can be realized. If the project falls to the ground, a service port with a few hundred employed will become the energy island's primary source of jobs.

C Enter for Regional and Tourism Research (CRT) in a new study estimates that by 2030 the population of Bornholm can reach approximately 41,200 people whose Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners (CIP) and Ørsted will be given green light to realize their hydrogen project on Bornholm. The idea, which has been known since August, includes the construction of two offshore wind farms totaling three gigawatts in the easternmost part of Danish waters.

The parks must convert the energy into hydrogen into an electrolysis plant on Bornholm soil.

According to CRT's data, the CIP/ Ørsted project will increase local employment with 900 people in lasting jobs and help the population grow by 1,070 people. When the Energiø project is laid on top, the population is placed 1,650 people - and in these figures are included not to feel the business opportunities that the colossal amounts of surplus heat from PTX bring with it.

Without the CIP/ Ørsted turbines and Power-to-X, the energy adventure "just" 578 ​​has extra inhabitants and 490 employed when all derived effects are counted. The most tangible jobs for Energiø Bornholm are the approximately 190 positions that are created around a service port.

According to CRT's model, the overall job creation effect of Power-to-X will be about 480 lasting employed, of which 150 will include the operation of an electrolysis plant of three GW. The rest are derived jobs.

In addition, approximately 500 are employed as a result of the eastern offshore wind farms that require service from land to the same extent as the energy island of the energy island south of the coast.

Whether this potential can ever be triggered will depend on both national and local political decisions.

After Wednesday's energy summit, Green Marienborg Meeting, which the prime minister is at the forefront, according to the information of the Tidende, news can emerge that sheds new light on the possibilities of establishing a power-to-x plant on a large scale on Bornholm. The government's decision in February to suspend the open door scheme cast doubt on the wind turbine projects that CIP applied last summer for permission to erect via the scheme.

After CRT, the study on Wednesday contacted the Journal of CIP to get a status. Before the Marienborg meeting on Wednesday, CIP does not want to tell more about how far they have come to develop the Bornholm project idea. The labor force for the installation of the offshore wind farms for Energiø Bornholm (only the state project, not CIP and Ørsteds) counts 550 full -time equivalents in a single year.

According to CRT's director Anne Thomas, the PTX information in the study stems mainly directly from CIP/ Ørsted, and the researchers have tried to keep the figures up against the experience of the few places where the large electrolysis systems were early in the process of building large electrolysis systems.

At Bornholm there are critical voices of the idea of ​​PTX. The consumption of water to the process is one of the problems that, among other members from the Unity List, have pointed out.

These environmental and resource considerations are not mentioned in CRT's study, and these are good reasons for, says Anne Thomas.

-We do not look at whether it is a good idea with Power-to-X, but solely on whether it will bring us close to 42,000 inhabitants, explains the director.

NB: The last figure is uncertain as CIP and Ørsted's proposed offshore wind farms are not included directly in CRT's study, where it is estimated that it will require about as many hands to build the eastern offshore wind farms as the parks for Energiø Bornholm.

Title: Metal forudser en folkevandring af faglærte
Content:
Chairman Klaus Holm in Metal Bornholm believes that Energiø Bornholm will lead to a positive business development with the need for a lot of skilled labor.

B Ornholm stands on the threshold of a new era as a pioneer lake for green transition, with what it entails of development, and at Metal Bornholm, chairman Klaus Holm believes in a good business development for the benefit of the citizens. He is excited about the coming years and expects that all ports and unemployed areas will be used by new businesses that will come here and become part of the development. He said this in the chairman's report to Metal Bornholm's General Assembly.

- We are going to see a migration of skilled workers who will help build the energy island and all the following industries that grow up as small underground companies, the metal chairman said.

With Energiøen, Bornholm advances several lengths in relation to employment and growth, and the professional organizations look into an exciting and challenging future.

- Bornholm has proud traditions of being well organized. Therefore, future labor will meet a strong trade union movement that allows them to be organized in a rock -solid work movement, Klaus Holm said.

He sees Metal Bornholm and the other trade union movement as the strong foundation that ensures good working conditions, so that Bornholm does not become a Klondike where Bornholmers subsequently stand and look for the train when it is run.


Without skilled workers it will be at the talk

According to Klaus Holm, access to skilled labor is a prerequisite if Denmark as a society is to be achieved with the green transition. There simply have to be skilled enough to make it all a reality.

- The lack of skilled workers becomes the great societal challenge of our time. We can only get rid of the high energy prices and gas imports from dictatorship states if we have the right hands and wise heads. It is skilled workers who have to build, operate and develop the green transition.

These are skilled hands and heads to produce the wind turbines, heat pumps and all the other products and machines that together form the green transition.

In short: If Denmark does not get many more skilled workers, the green transition will be the talk.

- In the industry alone, we will be missing hundreds of thousands of skilled workers in 2030 if Denmark is to reduce its CO2 emissions by 70 percent, Klaus Holm said.


Proper terms a prerequisite

In Metal Bornholm you do not let it be at the talk when it comes to the need for skilled labor, and you do not content to organize parts of it. You are also a link to gather the industry in a joint marketing to attract labor.

- A common platform allows us to show the world around us that Bornholm is an industry island - and not as in everyday speech a holiday island. We see all too often that our newcomers do not know what is going on here on the island and who it is that is based over here, Klaus Holm said.

He sees it as a sign that Bornholm stands together that virtually all companies are part of the joint marketing.

- I want to go so far as to say that this is what makes Bornholm unique.

The metal chairman believes that proper conditions are a prerequisite for grabbing the necessary labor. Therefore, this spring, Metal Bornholm will focus on agreements and visit the few companies that are not covered.

- If we are to attract labor from the from from, we must have the basic substance in order and be able to offer proper conditions to the employee, it said.

Title: Fond indstiller sig på energiøen
Content:
Bornholm Business Fund provided a commitment for a total of DKK 17.5 million last year.

In 2022, 18 companies received a total of DKK 17.5 million from Bornholm Business Fund for investment projects. Most of the appropriations went to tourism, food and delicacies as well as agriculture. At the end of the year, the total loan and commitment amounted to a total of DKK 66.1 million, which works to create growth and development in 91 Bornholm companies, the fund said in a press release.

- We see ourselves as a catalyst for many Bornholm companies' desire for new establishment, extensions and change of ownership. In recent years we have been able to enjoy having helped not least tourism on Bornholm well, and we also especially support food production on the island, says chairman Charlotte Rønhof in the press release.

Two applications were rejected in 2022.

In the future, the fund also hopes to help companies get business out of the vision of Bornholm as Energiø.

For many years, Hans-Henrik Thiesen has been the fund's administrator and contact person for the companies.

He will soon be 68 years old and has decided to retire this fall.

- Fortunately, it gives us time to find a good replacement for him, says Charlotte Rønhof, who is calling on potentially interested parties to approach the fund.

The position will be looked up before the summer holidays.

Title: Bornholms vej til vækst
Content:
How close to 42,000 citizens do we come with the energy island?

I was even present when the goal of the 42,000 citizens was born. It happened at a vision meeting in Ystad, while the snow overturned outside the meeting room, where the fully elected municipal council in 2018 gathered for the first time - to set the direction for the upcoming term.

It was not such that one discussed back and forth whether the most realistic bid for a goal was now called 39,999 or 50,000. 42,000 citizens were the result of a math that was presented to us: This goal we had to achieve if Bornholm ever had to dream of a sustainable economy.

Intuitively, it is not hard to imagine that there is a limit to how small a society you can be with your own hospital, airport and high school. After all, we can see that there are limits to how many medical beds you can keep open if there is a shortage of nurses. There must be enough children in a school district if the school is not to close. Enough must be bought in locally if the utility is to be open. SKAT must also be paid enough for us to pay home help.

Since 2018, CRT has seen several times skeptical of how good the chances were for Bornholm to actually achieve the municipal council's goals, and we are probably not the only ones.

Sometimes it is not enough to want and should.

A goal does not have to be realistic just because it is necessary. And while there have been positive winds for the past five years, it is hard to imagine that the natural development alone, even with a very large figure of Rune Holm, should have a flat or slightly rising curve to suddenly look like a hockey stake. .

In 2020, the government then decided that billions should be invested in Energiø Bornholm.

And not long after, Russia's invasion of Ukraine made European leaders agreed to set very high targets for investments in wind energy throughout the Baltic Sea. There are such large sums that one can badly dream of other and larger oranges in the turban in the foreseeable future.

The natural question we asked in CRT was therefore: How close to 42,000 citizens can we come up with Energiø Bornholm? .


The math

Before we look at the math, let's just look at what we already know:? We know which industries are most affected by the energy island investment, it tells us experience.

? At Bornholm there is already today in these industries almost full employment.

This means that they already have challenges today.

? By 2030 we also know that a relatively large part of the Bornholm workforce will retire.

? Even without an Energy Island investment, Bornholm can expect a great lack of especially skilled labor.

? When we look back in time, we can see that there is a pretty close connection between the number of jobs and the population. Bornholm is a popular place to live if you can find a job.

? We have experience with how many newcomers come alone and who brings family.

We must therefore expect that the local employment on Bornholm to be used for Energiø Bornholm can and must be attracted from the rest of the country and from abroad.

We must also expect the traveling labor to bring the same number of partners and children as all other normal newcomers.

So let's return to the math.

And let's focus on what we can be reasonably sure of: 1. First, most of us eventually believe that Bornholm gets a land plant and becomes a service port for the offshore wind farm when it is built.

2. Next, local companies can hope that Bornholm will also become a installation port when the offshore wind farm is to be established.

3. Finally, there is all the talk about a Powerto-X system. It can share the population a little.

But if it comes, then it will probably be of a certain size to be able to earn itself home. We've used an example of 3 gigawatts. It is a very large plant compared to those you know today. But the interest in alternative fuels for aircraft and ferry as well as the need to be able to use large amounts of energy when the wind blows, points out that the size plant will be an option.

Now CRT's task was to grab the bone and ask various experts and the industry to share their experiences and business secrets: How many hands do you need locally, in the three parts of the math.

Green hydrogen and fuels will give a huge boost to employment at Bornholm and the ambition to reach the goal of 42,000 inhabitants. The concluded Center for Regional and Tourism Research in a study whose main conclusions were published on Wednesday.

Others will travel away

Democratic deficit A third objection from the association towards CIP and Ørsted's idea is that the plans for power-to-x have so far been "without any discussion with Bornholm authorities and locals," writes Bomef in the EU hearing: "There are already heated discussions in the process of establishing the land plant for a 2-3 GW offshore wind farm on South Bornholm.

The task of promoting the electrification of society is also involved in via the citizen -driven offshore wind turbine project Bornholm's offshore wind.
