Bornholm's Environment and Energy Association has about 50 members, says Peter Haag.


300,000 tonnes of hydrogen per year from electrolysis plant

In the EU Commission's energy program "Projects of Common Interest" (in Danish: Projects of Common Interest), CIP and Ørsted's offshore wind farms and power-to-X systems are included in the list of upcoming projects that can better connect the EU energy system. Through the EU program, it is possible to apply for co-financing for energy projects that cross borders.

The plans for Bornholm are thus presented in the consultation material, where it is mentioned that the project has a link to a bunker hub at Rønne Harbor that can supply the shipping traffic with green fuels: “Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners (CIP) has applied for permission to develop two offshore wind turbine projects, Bornholm Basin East (1.5 GW) and Bornholm Basin Syd (1.5 GW), under the Danish open door scheme with the expectation of being able to deliver the first power in 2028. on Bornholm, which is in the priority corridor Bemi -Hydrogen "(which focuses on increasing security of supply and making the Baltic countries independent of Russian energy, ed.).

"In addition to delivering up to 300,000 tonnes of hydrogen annually, corresponding to 2 percent of the Repowereu target of 20 megaton, the project can meet the demand from the local hydrogen market on Bornholm and support the island's vision of becoming the Baltic Sea Bunkerhub for green fuel and Bornholm's energy policy objective of that be climate neutral in 2040 ".

In the description of the project you can also read that CIP and Ørsted intend to connect the offshore wind farms directly to an electrolysis plant on land. Title: Tanker om vejen mod Rønne Havn som grøn tankstation
Content:
At Rønne Harbor we have a vision that Bornholm can become the Baltic Sea's green gas station for some of the 60,000 ships that pass close to the island every year.

Ship traffic transports about 90 percent of all goods in the world. Unless we change our consumption, we cannot do without that transport and replace it.

Ship transport is an industry that accounts for about three percent of the world's global CO2 emissions, and since most ships cannot use batteries and electricity, it is also one of the most difficult industries. Therefore, we do not get over the fact that we have to have some green fuel.

The new green fuels contain only half as much energy as the fossil fuels used today. This means that the ships either have to have a bigger thought on board or that they have to refuel more often.

Usually we are at Bornholm far away from all things, but maybe we are in fact right in the middle of it all when it comes to supplying green fuels for ships. And the geographical position in the middle of the Baltic Sea we can take advantage of when we dream of becoming the new gas station for ships.

Every year, 60,000 ships sail close past Bornholm, and the future forecasts predict that figure will rise.

In addition to offering fuels at a good price, it is also important that visitors ships have the opportunity to get other services. Exactly as it applies to any other gas station. When you think your car, it is also often that you fill sprinkler fluid or buy some food.

For example, it could be that ships in the future can get rid of their garbage or get fresh supplies on board. Maybe there is something to be repaired or some of the staff that needs to be replaced. And here there are extra opportunities for the Bornholm companies, which already have extensive experience in serving the maritime industry and the offshore projects installed out of Rønne Harbor.

The dream is, as I said, that Bornholm must be the Baltic Sea's green gas station for ships, but there is still a long way to go before that dream can be made a reality.

First, there must be ships that can and will sail on the green fuels.

There are not yet many who can, but there are more on the way due to requirements for the new ships.

But there must also be someone who produces the fuels. It can happen through the so-called Power-to-X technology.

The technology is already available, and quietly there are more and more plants that can produce the green fuels.

In Fredericia there is a plant that is already making hydrogen, and by 2023 European Energy will build a plant in Aabenraa, which can make methanol for Maersk's first green container ship.

However, shipping uses very large quantities of fuel, which is why many more power-to-x plants are needed to produce the green fuels before we can seriously make a transformation of the shipping.

Finally, we must have created the entire value chain between the production of fuel and for refueling the ships to use it.

If we are to put a picture of what it is for a journey that we are doing, then we should think seven to eight years back in time. Back then, there were some visionary people on Bornholm who dared to think big and dream that one day Bornholm could become the center of the Baltic Sea, where offshore wind turbines could be sent out of Rønne Harbor, and it could create new jobs and activity in the Bornholm community .

The dream of offshore wind has come to fruition, with more projects completed and even more on the way.

If Bornholm Bunker Hub is to be a similar success, many decisions and initiatives are waiting.

But the dream lives and becomes more realistic every day.


Where do we dream?

The other is with the theme of Energiø Bornholm and is about the opportunities and challenges that we face in the work towards the huge energy project.

Title: Energiøen skal også være en bornholmsk succes

There is a great responsibility on the government when the work of making Bornholm an energy island starts. Denmark is in dire need of more renewable energy, and it is crucial for future green projects that Energiø Bornholm will be a success at all levels.

In particular, it is important to take the municipality and locals on board. We are facing a time when both offshore wind turbine projects should and should be implemented throughout the country. Therefore, it is important that the already agreed project on Bornholm will also be a local success.

But how do you secure it? Yes, we did firstly what we could do when we negotiated. Now comes the execution of the agreement, and here it is about the government knocking out the listening steaks and taking into account the local interests in the project.

They can advantageously start by orienting themselves in the wish list that Mayor Jacob Trøst presented the other day.

For the mayor, it is important, among other things, that the local environment is taken into account and that the energy island leads to more jobs and more initiatives for the benefit of nature on the island. Good input if you ask me. Of course, there must also be local winnings when we expand the green energy in Denmark.

Of course, it benefits everyone in Denmark that we get our energy sources transformed into sustainable by the kind, but it is clear that the communities that are particularly close to offshore wind turbine projects are affected in a different way.

Therefore, it is certainly necessary to consider local gains that Jacob Trøst proposes, both on Bornholm, but also in other municipalities and cities, which in the future will be in the same situation.

For more similar situations will occur.

Both the climate crisis and the war in Ukraine make it imperative that we get the green transition in a hurry.

And if that process is to go as smoothly as possible, then it is important that Bornholm and other communities are involved, and in no way feel run over when the projects are to be realized. Because we need everyone to get along if we are to reach the goal - and we should.

Title: Giganter med brintrør vil styrke energiøen: Projekterne understøtter hinanden
Content:
Energy CIP and Ørsted try to convince MPs that they must prioritize the huge Bornholm hydrogen project. One of the arguments is that a power-to-x plant will make it profitable to invest in pipelines, which also Energiø Bornholm can enjoy if the politicians want to put even more offshore wind turbines around Bornholm.

A future of production of hydrogen and ammonia on huge scale on Bornholm soil and two offshore wind farms east of the coast has the potential to radically change the municipality's economy and nature on land and water. However, Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners (CIP) and Ørsted, ready to make double -digit billion investments, have been reluctant to tell about their Bornholm project in recent months, after it began to be clear that the government and energy authorities would not easily give a green light and issue a permit for feasibility studies. On Thursday, representatives from the two companies opened up their thoughts as they attended a hearing on the open door scheme in the Folketing's Climate, Energy and Supply Committee.

Since the beginning of February, the open door scheme has been put on hold. It was this scheme that CIP in June applied for in the hope of - without payment - to have areas with a total area of ​​over 800 square kilometers east of Bornholm available for two offshore wind farms. Also, three places in the Kattegat and the North Sea try to access large marine areas, but due to the many open door applications and concerns about the EU's state aid rules, the scheme was put on hold.

On Wednesday, the government announced that it is prepared to adjust the scheme. This will mean that the sea areas must be exposed to competition and that the ministry is investigating which projects can be worked on.

- We have followed the announcements from Marienborg yesterday (Wednesday, ed.) And are of course very interested in the upcoming process, now that it seems that the partially closed door is opening again, said Magnus Brogaard Larsen, associate partner in Cip at the consultation.


Nine Great Belt Bridges

Together with Ørsteds Søren Scherfig, he gave a status on CIP's plans at Esbjerg (Ammonia for Agriculture), Hanstholm (Hydrogen), Læsø/Aalborg (Airline Fuel) and the two parks on Bornholm.

- We identified these five projects, which we sent applications into in May and June, which make up just over 6 GW. We speak an investment of the order of DKK 180 billion, which is equivalent to nine big belt bridges-with Power-to-X, said Magnus Brogaard Larsen.

Of their descriptions of the projects, the impression was that a few of the other power-to-X projects that the large offshore wind farms must supply with electricity is further ahead than the Bornholm. Nevertheless, the energy companies are striving to be ready with hydrogen production at Bornholm in five to six years.

-We see the Bornholm projects be a precursor to create a power-to-X-infrastructure on Bornholm, said Magnus Brogaard Larsen.

- We have already submitted an application for a pipe down to Germany. We have looked at areas at Bornholm and how to make pipes for a PTX infrastructure.

He elaborated that CIP will invest in pipelines as part of the plan so that hydrogen can be transported away from Bornholm. In January, CIP and the German system operator for Gastransmission Gascade announced that they are planning to build a brine tube from Bornholm to Lubmin. The pipeline, which must be an important part of the supply of a new German hydrogen network, will extend over 140 kilometers and get a capacity of up to 10 gigawatts.

CIP is also involved in Baltic Sea pipes that will connect Sweden and Finland with Germany, and which can go via Bornholm.

With 3 gigawatts, the offshore wind farms are expected to become almost as large as the energy island, and it is the idea that the power should be converted directly to hydrogen. Denmark has a strategy that by 2030 4-6 Gigawatt Power-to-X (hydrogen or different fuels such as ammonia or methanol), and can CIP and Ørsted's plans be implemented, a significant proportion will be manufactured on Bornholm .

If the Bornholm Open Door Seawind wind farms meet support in Christiansborg and at the ministerial offices, it will create an advantage for Energiø Bornholm, the two energy lobbyists from CIP and Ørsted pointed out. Their point is that a green light for their projects will form the basis for expanding the energy island with more within the same area (also called overplanting), as the current being produced under good wind conditions can be converted into hydrogen. With increased mill density, power will be left over if it is not decided to invest several billion in cable connections away from the energy island.

- We look into a fairly strong connection with the plans that the Danish Energy Agency has outlined for Energiø Bornholm. It will positively affect the overplanting option that is introduced by the energy island, said Magnus Brogaard Larsen, who at the same time described his own projects as "whole instrumental" for the development of hydrogen infrastructure.

A question of both and Ørsted's responsible for the development of new wind parks and power-to-x plants in Denmark, Søren Scherfig, saw doubt as to whether Energiø Bornholm can be expanded if you reject CIP and Ørsted's open door project.

- The extra mills you can set up to make hydrogen from them may not be enough to support infrastructure out of Bornholm. If hydrogen tubes are to be built, we should have more electrolysis and hydrogen production. Therefore, the projects support each other. Title: Ministeriet slår fast: Møllerne kommer ikke tættere på land
Content:
Energiø Bornholm can get more wind turbines if it is decided politically to place the mills closer to each other. It will also make the production of green hydrogen on Bornholm more likely. However, the area of ​​the parks will not be expanded, says the climate, energy and the Ministry of Supply.

Last week, Tidende mentioned a new message from the government that Energiø Bornholm's offshore wind farms can be greater when the state tender is to be prepared.

The Journal has approached the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Supply to elaborate on this phrase: "The government will also work on preparing the supply of Energiø Bornholm, which can further increase capacity".

The Ministry states in a written response that there is no work on finding new sea areas for the already large project.

"The aforementioned capacity increase is the possibility of over -planting of 0.8 GW. It is the maximum capacity that is part of the strategic environmental assessment," the ministry writes to the Journal.

Overplanting means that the mills are placed closer to each other. The concept also includes installing a higher capacity than the cables can transport when the wind conditions are best. On the other hand, the cables can be utilized more optimally, even when the wind conditions are inferior.

The opportunity to increase the total capacity 3.8 Gigawatt (GW) was known when the Danish Environmental Protection Agency had the proposal for the environmental assessment in consultation last year. Tidende asked the ministry if there were plans to make the mills even closer, but that does not seem to be the case.

"The framework for overall planning, ie the possible capacity of upcoming offshore wind farms, depends on the political agreements. The political agreement is that a minimum of three GW offshore winds must be set up. Based on the size of the area and an overall assessment of the possible mill density, the Danish Energy Agency has Chosen to environmentally assess the possibility of establishing offshore wind turbines up to 3.8 GW. Overplanting than the 0.8 GW, ”the answer reads.


PTX on private initiative

Overplanting will also make it more likely that the winner of the state tender will be interested in establishing an electrolysis plant on Bornholm.

"Possibility of overplanting is currently being investigated, which means that the total capacity could rise up to 3.8 GW. -x (PTX) ", wrote the Danish Energy Agency last year about Energiø Bornholm.

A dialogue round conducted by the Danish Energy Agency last year with potential participants in the tender round showed that the energy companies have an interest in thinking of Energiø Bornholm together with an electrolysis system for the production of hydrogen or ammonia. Such a power-to-X system will have to be placed on Bornholm, as there will be a lack of capacity in the cables to transport the extra power away from the energy island.

"Among the market players, there is a consensus that overplanting will make supply more attractive, and most of the market players mention the possibility of PTX production in connection with overplanting," the board writes in a summary.


Minimum 15 kilometers

In the answer to the Journal of the Ministry's office, it is also stated that Minister Lars Aagaard (M) has no plans to spread the wind turbines over a larger area.

"The green transition must go hand in hand with the environment and nature, business and local support, among others. Local support and to reduce any visual genes, one has chosen not to move the set -up area closer than 15 km from the coast, ”the ministry writes.

The size of the parks is also limited by the cable connections, and there is also no new to report on that front.

"There are no concrete plans for connections to other countries or additional capacity to Germany in addition to the planned connection of 2 GW, but Energiø Bornholm is being prepared to be able to connect more connections, which may become relevant at a later date."

In addition to the export connection of 2 GW to Germany, cables with a capacity of 1.2 GW must be driven from the high voltage station on Bornholm to Zealand.

Title: Medie: Energiøens projektøkonomi er forværret yderligere
Content:
A new assessment of Energiø Bornholm's project economy shows, according to the Engineer, that the construction of the wind farms and the electricity infrastructure, in the most likely of the ministry's scenarios, will provide a deficit of DKK 12 billion.

"It is a condition of the projects that they are profitable". This is what a sentence sounds like in the historic political climate agreement, which was concluded in August 2020 and put the two energy islands in the North Sea and the Baltic Sea on rails.

An updated analysis of the long -term economy for Energiø Bornholm shows that the large -scale energy project will require state aid to run around. It writes the trade media The Engineer, which has come into possession of the Climate, Energy and the Ministry of Supply's latest assessment of profitability.

The analysis consists of several scenarios, and in what the ministry considers to be the most likely, Energiø Bornholm will end up with a project economic deficit of DKK 12 billion, which according to the Engineer must be covered with state aid.

It will require DKK 1.6 billion annually for 20 years - a total of DKK 31.5 billion.

The deficit has become two billion kroner larger than when a similar financial assessment was designed in the fall of 2022, the Engineer writes. It is not clear from the article what has deteriorated the project economy. Last fall, the applications from Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners and Ørsted about the construction of two large offshore wind farms east of Bornholm via the open door scheme prompted the ministry to downgrade expectations for the energy island's project economy.

Last summer, the parties behind the climate agreement chose to expand Energiø Bornholm from 2 to at least 3 gigawatts, although expectations for profitability were not the same as two years earlier. The fact that the politicians, despite the changed economic views backed up on Energiø Bornholm, were linked to the question of security of supply, the Left's then climate and energy mayor, Carsten Kissmeyer, had understood.

"The situation is critical right now, and when we look into the future, it is necessary to ensure that we have enough energy," he told the Engineer, where he recalled that the economy will ultimately depend on the tender rounds and the future of the future Electricity prices.

- If we get a level of electricity prices that are a little higher than we originally expected, then I would guess that we can see that this can be profitable.

Historically, offshore wind farms have required state aid, but in recent years offshore wind turbines have become so efficient that projects can avoid becoming a net expense for the state. The Park Thor, who is under construction in the North Sea, is the first example of a project that does not depend on state aid.

The agreement circle notes that the Climate and Energy Agreement of June 2020 overall does not entail costly for citizens and businesses and emphasizes that the agreement supports lower energy prices.

Title: Energiøen kan løse vores mangel på arbejdskraft
Content:
Overall, an increase in population will strengthen the total labor supply on Bornholm and thus also benefit the island's public and private companies.

'The future depends on what we do in the present,' Gandhi said, and although the proverb belongs to another time, it frames quite well that we at Bornholm actually have an influence on how we best exploit the many potentials such as Energiø- Investments bring with it. It is undeniable that there will be many temporary jobs to the island, which will also require the establishment of many new temporary housing. For us Bornholmers, it should be an independent goal that many families want to settle on our island and thus become a lasting contribution to our communities. Therefore, we must already think wisely and make sure that some of the temporary housing also gets a permanent aim.

Most Bornholmers are probably both excited, but also a little worried about what it really will mean for our everyday lives that Bornholm will be one of the cornerstones of Denmark's green transition in the coming years. The idea of ​​new jobs and relocation arouses enthusiasm, whereas there is concern about the unique nature of the island and of whether the energy island sucks all the local labor away from the island's current companies.

The challenges of obtaining qualified labor are far from a new problem.

At DI Bornholm, we have long pointed out that lack of labor is slowing down corporate growth, which in turn stretches legs to attract new Bornholmers and thus increased tax revenue that can finance our welfare. The Energiø investments certainly do not make these challenges smaller, but in return we now get a burning platform that can put turbo on long-term solutions. And this begins, among other things, with the fact that we can also offer a permanent housing offer to the people and families who will soon arrive from other parts of the country.

Brand new figures from CRT (Center for Regionalog Tourism Research) state that even in the 'minimum scenario', where only land plants and service port are established, we must already be able to offer housing for lodging labor equivalent to 340 man-years, which Estimated gives a relocation equal to a minimum of 460 people. Bornholm becomes an additional center of the installation port and power-to-x plants, so that more than these figures are increased and the population will increase by 1,060 until 2030.

Overall, an increase in population will strengthen the total labor supply on Bornholm and thus also benefit the island's public and private companies. Therefore, it will be too short -term if we are currently focusing only on the construction phase when establishing housing for labor from the outside, for example by establishing a large 'sheds city' on a bar field. We simply miss the great opportunities if we do not think long -term from the start - that is, also establishes housing with a more permanent perspective.

Mayor Jacob Trøst has proposed that Energinet in the upcoming supply of the land facility will consider housing solutions, which both solve the temporary need, but at the same time designed in a way that can be converted into lasting homes for new families in the long term.

We support the idea, which expresses both common sense and responsible use of scarce resources.

Such a model probably involves a number of tendering legs, but it must not discourage us from trying to make things wise. The energy project will draw large exchanges on the entire Bornholm community, where the road to success also takes place through the local support. Therefore, right now we must recall Gandhi's wisdom that the decisions we make today will have a specific impact on the future.

Title: Teknisk svær opgave at slutte lille forbrugsområde til stor produktionsenhed
Content:
Bornholm Tidende has asked Energinet two questions that have filled a lot in the debate on the energy island: Does Bornholm's Elnet be connected? And does the energy island mean cheaper electricity for consumers on Bornholm? Director of Energy Islands in Energinet, Hanne Storm Eldlefsen, gives her answers here.

A few years ago, supply security and electricity price were topics that very few Danes thought of. We turned on the power when we needed it, without giving it a thought where the power was produced and what it cost. Cheap power in the socket was a matter of course. Today, many have an app on their phone, where you follow the electricity prices hour by hour. We are thinking about our consumption now, for example we turn on the dishwasher and let the electric car at night when the power is cheapest.

Bornholm has always been in a special situation when it comes to electricity due to its location in the Baltic Sea. The current through the Swedish -created has at times been unstable and led to several power cuts, for example because it has been torn over by a ship. At the same time, Bornholm has some of the highest electricity prices in Denmark. This is because there are few consumers on the island, which causes a relatively large loss in the island's electricity grid.

Therefore, it is quite obvious that the Bornholmers are looking at the upcoming Energiø on Bornholm as an opportunity to solve some of the problems. With a local consumption of about 50 MW and a production from the energy island of 3,000 MW - the equivalent of about three million household electricity consumption - it immediately sounds straightforward to supply Bornholm with green power.

Understandably, the desire for the connection of Bornholm Elnet has been made to "The Great Energy Island" from the start filled a lot with the Bornholmers. In January last year, Energinet announced that the initial analysis is likely to make a connection of the Bornholm electricity grid to the Energy Island - well to mark without compromising the stability of the grid and security of supply. We have worked on this solution with the site.

It may sound like a banal task to pull a cable from the local transformer station and connect it to the energy island so that the power can flow when the wind turbines spin. But it is actually a difficult technical task to connect so small a consumption area to such a large production unit. When we look around the world, it's not done before either. Therefore, we must have developed a whole new technical model that ensures that we can constantly operate the system without overloading the components or risking no power in the outlet. Specifically, Bornholm will receive electricity from the wind turbines when the wind blows and they produce, while when it is quiet, the supply will come from either Zealand or Germany via the new cables to the energy island.

Therefore, Energinet has triggered the preparation of a decision basis for the connection of Bornholm Elnet to Energiøen. The basis for decision must elucidate all aspects of the connection. This applies, for example, to the different technical possibilities for the connection, the impact of security of supply and of course the financial consequences of different solutions.

Energinet is, as a state -owned company, subject to a wide range of requirements for initiating new projects that the connection will be. One of the requirements when we need to initiate a connection to the electricity transmission network is that we have to choose the most socio -economic solution - that is, a connection with the same functionality cannot be made cheaper than the set solution. Here, savings in the operation of alternative solutions will contribute positively to the social economy.

An important gain will be the opportunity to replace the current fossil reserve solution, which is on Bornholm now in the form of diesel and oil -fired power plant blocks. It is good for both the environment and the economy. There is a significant possible saving on the current costs of fossil reserves, that is, the cost of keeping a power plant ready to produce power in the event of a failure or breach of the cable between Bornholm and Sweden. Our initial analysis shows that over 40 years the savings will amount to around DKK 670 million - converted to present value. In addition, the energy island will allow for exporting more green power from Bornholm, which can contribute even more to the socio -economic gain.

Overall, our various analyzes will form the decision basis for a final decision to connect the Bornholm electricity grid to the energy island. We are working purposefully on the case, and expect to make a decision by the end of 2024.

Cheap power? Another question that has filled the debate on the energy island is the electricity prize. Naturally, the high electricity prices in general have generally in the past year and locally on Bornholm made many people ask the obvious question - becomes the power cheaper if we are connected to the energy island? The short answer is that the energy island will only mean lower prices to a very limited extent. To find an explanation, we need to delve into how the price of electricity is composed.

Today, Denmark is divided into two prize zones, where Bornholm to the east of the Great Belt, also called DK2. This means that Bornholm has the same wholesale price of electricity as Zealand. The energy island becomes a new independent price zone, and if the Bornholm electricity grid is connected to the energy island, the local consumption will be part of the new price zone. In practice, this will not mean the major changes for consumers at Bornholm.

The price in the new price zone will depend on how the wind blows as well as on the price in the neighboring price areas where the energy island is connected, ie Zealand and Germany. Generally, there are no major differences in prices across our neighboring price areas.

The German price is most often expected to be higher than the Zealand price, which is why the connection to Germany will be fully utilized, understood in the way that much of the power will be sold to Germany. Bornholm and Zealand will have the same price - slightly lower than Germany during those periods.

During the periods when the German price will be lower than the Zealand, Bornholm will also most often have the same price as in Germany. Therefore, the electricity price on Bornholm is expected in the future (with an independent price zone) on average to be marginally lower than in Zealand.

The wholesale price for electricity is about 23 percent of the total price that consumers pay to the electricity dealer. The rest are charges and tariffs. Only the wholesale price is affected if Bornholm becomes part of a new price zone. Therefore, small changes in the wholesale price will only affect the price you pay as a consumer quite a bit.

Despite the fact that a connection does not give cheaper electricity, there is still good reason in connecting the Bornholm electricity grid to the energy island. We believe that we can create a stable and secure supply to the Bornholmers, abolish fossil reserve solutions, make a gain for society and give Bornholmers access to green power in the outlet with Energiø Bornholm.

Title: Energiø er spild af penge
Content:
By attaching to electricity everywhere, you end up with black transition.

Now it also emerges that Energiø Bornholm will cost far more than first assumed, and thus the project can only be referred to as an employment project, but only while building, because when you are done, everything will be old and the many Money has to be in again, and therefore you will sell the power at the market price here on the island as well.

Therefore, it will not create so many more jobs.

There will also be a huge loss at the long distances that you have to deliver the power over, you can just ask Trefor about, they know a lot about it.

When producing alternative energy, it will always be an advantage that you only create the quantity that can be used in the area, then you should also not build such large "bricks" to convey the energy, and in this connection is a giant " Battery ”, which you want to build in Hasle, also a waste of space, because if you had built a hydrogen production instead of electricity, you could store the profits much easier and in less space.

It is also wrong to use electricity as the only propellant in cars and buses as well as trucks instead, for example, hydrogen, for example, because there is a large loss of energy especially in winter, and you cannot get the same power out as you can with an internal combustion engine , without shortening the range so much that it is not appropriate.

In addition, batteries have a limited service life and it is a major damage to the environment when producing batteries that need to be thrown away afterwards.

The whole green transition is inconsiderate, because you create new problems when you do not want to use the combustion of, for example, waste and other necessary processes to get rid of our surplus products, including the conversion of plastic into oil, which must then be burned.

If you wanted to make the trucks more environmentally friendly, they could just run on old plastic, and if you wanted a good business out of making green transition, you could make small plants where you need the energy so you can use The surplus heat to energy -intensive companies and avoid the large losses on the long transport of energy.

Green change should have been thought to be completely differently, namely that you looked at all your problems, and then from them solved them in a new and better way. By attaching to electricity everywhere, you end up with black transition.

Title: 100 kroner per familie kan sikre vores strøm
Content:
Without timely care, according to analysis, Denmark can potentially lack power when we bet more on sun and wind. But it can be fixed relatively cheap.

It is extremely rare that there is no power in the Danish sockets. But already by 2030 we may be missing large quantities some years.

Cars and factories must, in the name of the climate, be away from fossil fuels, and instead large amounts of power from solar cells and wind turbines must be used.

The problem is that they are dependent on something very unreliable - the weather.

If there is no actual acting, there is a risk of major power cuts, the Climate Council, which advises the government, states in a new analysis.

According to President Peter Møllgaard, the good news is that we can secure our electricity supply security and that it does not have to be expensive.

Gasturbines can step in in the hours when production is low and be backup at a price of DKK 2.9 billion annually.

- To insure us from being interrupted costs about DKK 100 per family a year, says Peter Møllgaard, who is also dean at the University of Southern Denmark.

- We believe that is an affordable insurance sum to avoid this going violently beyond our electricity supply security.

The adjustable electricity capacity is one of several solutions to future -proof electricity supply security that the Climate Council has looked at.

But if you want to completely ward off current shortage also during the most extreme periods, it is essential.

According to Green Power Denmark, representing parts of the energy sector, the new report and the debate it raises is extremely important.

However, Head of Department Martin Dam Wied wonders that new fossil gas turbines are recommended instead of using the capacity that is already.

He considers power plants that use sustainable biomass as an indispensable piece. But the Council believes that the electricity supply should be secured without a high consumption of biomass.

- They will remove an important tool in the toolbox that can really deliver a lot. I think that is problematic.

- And if it is to replace it with fossil gas, we can't really see the point, says Martin Dam Wied.

According to the Climate Council, however, the turbines must be used rarely, so even if they use natural gas, the climate impact will be small.

Biomass is debated in climate context. It must be regarded as climate neutral, as the burnt wood can be replaced by new forest, which occupies CO2.

But there are several problems - for example, it takes many years for the new trees to occupy as much as the old ones.

The Climate Council has also looked at electricity storage, where power is stored when the weather is for it, while the consumption, in turn, is moved away from periods when the power is missing.

The Council estimates that a combination of the two, adjustable electricity capacity as well as exchanging power with abroad, can be the socio -economically cheapest way to secure.

However, it requires political focus to ensure the security of electricity supply. That requires planning and that the decision is made well in advance.

- If we are to use gas turbines, for example, it requires examining with the EU whether there are state aid rules to be handled.

- We feel that there is, and these are such things that might as well be started now, says chairman Peter Møllgaard.

It has not been possible to get a comment from the Minister of Climate, Energy and Supply Lars Aagaard (M).

But climate, energy and supply spokesman Lea Wermelin (S) says in a written comment that the Social Democracy is listening to the Climate Council's recommendations.

- For us, it is crucial that we ensure a continued high security of supply when we will produce far more green power from both wind turbines and solar cells in the future.

- We've already done a lot. Right now, for example, we are negotiating about Energiø Bornholm, which will, among other things, ensure the establishment of a new foreign connection, says Lea Wermelin.


Many solar cells and wind turbines are on the way

The total electricity generation from renewable energy on land - wind turbines and solar cells - must quadrupled by 2030. This must be done, among other things, by finding 10-15 areas that can be used for energy parks with both.

There are also plans to expand massively at sea, where the government will reserve 30 percent of the space for wind turbines. Internationally, Denmark and eight other countries will double the amount of electricity from offshore wind in the North Sea.

In the Baltic Sea, where there are far fewer mills, Denmark and the other countries - except Russia - will seven double the amount of electricity.

Title: Ministre står ved energiøen trods tvivl om dens økonomi

Title: Dialog er afgørende for Energinet og Energiø Bornholm
Content:
We are very aware that our plans for such a large building are a violent message that can hit the individual family hard and influence plans and dreams for the future.

In the Saturday edition of Bornholm Tidende, Jørn Sonne writes about the energy island and the upcoming land facility on Bornholm. He is one of the nine landowners whose property is affected by the upcoming land facility south of Aakirkeby.

It is a major intervention in the individual's life when Energinet comes up with plans to build a high -voltage station. But unfortunately, it is not possible to find space for such a large plant without affecting anyone. We try to minimize the number of landowners and neighbors who will be affected by the plant directly or indirectly. Among other things, we have done this by finding a location relatively close to the water, so that the length of the cables is as short as possible.

The consideration of landowners and neighbors of a facility weighs heavily. At the same time, nature, wildlife, past memories and many other common interests that are protected by the applicable laws must also be taken into account. Overall, we have found that selected location is the best possible - or the least little if you want. For it is going to fill the landscape. It is a necessary evil in order for us to implement the green transition of Denmark and secure green electricity to millions of consumers.

Jørn Sonne refers to the location of the land facility as illegal. It is important for me to emphasize that our proposal for location is not illegal - the project has been decided by the Folketing, and Energinet naturally catches up with all the necessary permits to realize it. We have sought Bornholm's regional municipality to initiate the treatment of a local plan that includes an area of ​​a total of 107 hectares, which in addition to the technical high -voltage plant also allows for land for planting and processing of the landscape. The latter must help reduce the visual impact on the technical plant.

The process of preparing the plan basis has, as I said, initiated at Bornholm Regional Municipality, and the plan basis must ultimately be adopted by the municipal council. Only when the planning basis has been adopted and when the Danish Environmental Protection Agency has granted an environmental permit to the project can the construction work begin. At the same time, we must have made an agreement on the acquisition of the areas we need.

I am sorry to hear that Jørn Sonne has a bad perception of the dialogue he has had with us. We are very aware that our plans for such a large building are a violent message that can hit the individual family hard and influence plans and dreams for the future. Energinet's message is by no means that "it's just a pity". We go into having a proper and respectful dialogue with those who are affected.

We would very much like to make an agreement on acquisition that is in the best possible way of the individual landowner. Jørn Sonne and the other landowners who have to deliver their property or land will be replaced for their losses. We know well that it is only a financial replacement and that it cannot compensate for plans and dreams that may be destroyed. Therefore, it is extra important for us to have a good dialogue with those who are affected by the energy island. We also know that many neighbors to the upcoming station feel squeezed and want compensation. The current legislation does not allow us to provide compensation to the neighbors to the station. Among other things, this is the reason why we do everything to try to minimize the genes from the station as much as possible by wrapping the station in green areas, among other things.

Although it may seem like Energiø Bornholm has been underway for a long time, there are still many things that have not yet been clarified. All the technical details are not in place, the local plan is under preparation and the environmental assessment of the project is in full swing. Therefore, we cannot answer all questions yet. But we always want to answer the questions we can. Therefore, we hope that landowners, neighbors and the rest of Bornholm will continue the dialogue - both face to face and here in Bornholm's Journal.

The two utilities that have been in conflict for heat supplies for years have buried the battle ax when it comes to receiving surplus heat from the energy island's high voltage station.

Although it is expected to take six to seven years before Energiø Bornholm is ready, the district heating companies are well in the process of planning how they can utilize the excess heat from the huge high-voltage plant in Sydbornholm.

The transformer station is expected to generate enough surplus heat to supply one -third of the island's district heating customers, and in addition, electrolysis systems for hydrogen production can be established, the surplus heat from this can cover the total heat consumption several times.

At Rønne Water and Heat General Assembly on Tuesday evening, the company told about the plans for the waste heat. It is RVV's wish to establish a shopping company together with Bornholm Energi and Forsyning, which operates the district heating dishes on the rest of Bornholm (with the exception of Pedersker).

- We pretty much agree with BEOF about it. Both with Helle Munk Ravnborg and Claus Andersen we have had a good dialogue, says RVV director Erik Steen Andersen to the Journal of the Purchasing Company.

The proposal from RVV is that the jointly owned company must buy waste heat to resell it to Bornholm's heat (BV) and Rønne Heating (RV). The costs must be divided into the same quantity ratio as the heat is removed.

Title: Museet tager hul på gigantisk opgave
Content:
Now the archaeological feasibility studies start in connection with Energiø Bornholm, and they extend into the fall of 2025.

On Monday, May 22, the Bornholm Museum puts the spade in the ground for the first archaeological preliminary investigations at Vasegårdsvej in connection with Energiø Bornholm, the museum said in a press release.

In the first phase, preliminary studies are carried out where so -called search trenches are made with excavators to search the entire area for possible finds. In the second phase, the areas where findings have been made.

The studies are carried out in the areas where the transformer station for Energiø Bornholm is to be built - a 107 hectare area as well as adjacent areas that can potentially be used as work and storage areas during the construction work. In the first vein, an area of ​​60 hectares is examined. Later, feasibility studies are also carried out in the areas where cables are to be buried.

There are well -known finds in the area, and the Bornholm Museum has a clear expectation that interesting finds will be made along the way.

Due to the large area to be investigated, the Bornholm Museum and Energinet expect the preliminary investigations to take place from May 2023 to the fall of 2025. It is Energinet as the builder who finances the archaeological investigations.

Bornholm Museum and Energinet expect to invite the Bornholmers inside when the investigations have started, the press release states.

In September last year, Museum Director Jacob Bjerring-Hansen in Bornholm Tidende pointed out that it is a bigger task to do large archaeological investigations on Bornholm than elsewhere in the country, where the necessary resources can easily be obtained from surrounding museums. Already in May of that year, he said, among other things: - It will be by far the largest archaeological project in the history of Bornholm Museum, and at that time he even considered that the relevant area was "only" 90 hectares.

Title: Landskab og natur må ikke blive taber
Content:
In the Danish Nature Conservation Association on Bornholm, we believe in a good solution for the energy island's land facility, but places great demands.

Opining from climate -impacting to climate neutral energy sources is full of challenges.

One of them is the size of the facilities, and here we have ended up at Bornholm in the middle of a dilemma because of our geographical location in the middle of a sea area that has become central to the supply of renewable energy to the entire Northern Europe.

In addition to a questionable economy in the major projects underway, there are of course major concerns about how the giant plants will affect Bornholm's nature and landscape. Nature and the landscape are load -bearing and crucial values ​​for our island - it is simply the main reason for Bornholm's great popularity, and it must not be overridden.

The Danish Nature Conservation Association Bornholm has as its main purpose to protect and improve nature, environment and landscape, and overall we participate with everything we can, in the green transition to a society that does not pollute, destabilize the climate, displace nature or destroy the landscape.

We could choose a strategy where we were against all development and just said no to wind turbines, solar cells and other large plants that fill the landscape violently. But if we are to promote a development where nature and the landscape have the highest priority, environmentally friendly solutions are crucial. After all, it is no use looking after nature if you do not take care of pollution and threatening global warming at the same time.

Therefore, we have chosen an approach where we place very high demands on the giant land plants that are underway and we will not compromise. It will be the largest building on Bornholm, and although in the area it fills only about a per thousand of the island, it can be seen in a significant area due to its height. Therefore, it is important that it is placed in a place where it goes as little as possible beyond nature and landscape, and that it is arranged with architecture, planting and ramparts so that it is harmonious in the surroundings.

If there is to be such a large land plant on Bornholm, we have difficulty seeing a different location than the one found. Nowhere is trouble -free, but this is the case of agricultural land without high natural values ​​and a flat and fairly low -lying landscape at a skilled distance from the beautiful south coast. The location north of Søndre Landevej will go beyond agricultural land and buildings, but nature can be improved with different grips in connection with the plant.

In the proposal that is at play, there are areas with low vegetation, shrubs and trees between the buildings and trees around it all, and a small stream is exposed through the area.

All in all, it means that the nature content will undoubtedly become richer than the current one.

But landscape we miss in the Danish Nature Conservation Association that ramparts of varying heights of raw land are constructed around the plant, in order to make the huge buildings less dominant in the landscape and partly to form good conditions for nature. Ramps with slopes create great variation in temperature and moisture conditions, so that a rich and varied plant and wildlife can also be immigrated, and the ramparts will also be used for hiking trails where you can enjoy both the view and the close nature.

Nature and landscape must not be loser. There is a lot at stake, and it should end with a solution that is not only good for Bornholm, but also nationally and internationally can serve as an example of how to reconcile green transition to renewable energy with regard to nature and landscape. That is the challenge and we will fight for and believe that it will succeed.

Title: Power-to-x på Bornholm - hvorfor det?
Content:
What can Bornholm get out of Power-to-X? In addition to the obvious, which are the jobs that will be linked directly to the production, Søren Møller Christensen sees three topics that are interesting: district heating, new green businesses and green workplaces as well as innovation, research and education.

G Rønne fuels and especially hydrogen produced on the basis of sun and wind energy fill a lot in the discussions about the green energy system of the future.

This is also the case at Bornholm, where Power-to-X and hydrogen production are both an opportunity in connection with Energiø Bornholm and the main idea in CIP and Ørsted's project east of Bornholm.

In this article I will try to explain why Power-to-X and especially hydrogen is getting so much attention, which is why it can make sense to have power-to-x-production on Bornholm and what Bornholm can get out of it in shape of, for example, workplaces.


Why at all Power-to-X?

To handle the climate crisis, we must have transformed all parts of our energy consumption into renewable energy as soon as possible.

In many contexts, the most optimal solution will be to replace coal, oil and other fossil fuels with electricity.

The electricity we use in our home must come from renewable energy sources such as wind and solar energy instead of coal and oil, and the driving force in our cars must be electricity from sun and wind stored on batteries instead of gasoline and diesel produced by oil . This direct use of electricity is the most effective solution because almost 100 percent of the electricity stored in a car battery be converted into driving force in the car.

In some contexts, however, it is not possible to electrify. This is the case, for example, with most of the shipping and air traffic. This is because what is called the energy density is low for batteries, while it is more than 25 times greater for the fuels that can be produced through Power-to-X-for example, hydrogen, ammonia, methanol and jetfuel. Energy density is an expression of how much energy a particular source of energy has in relation to weight. Specifically, this means that the batteries for a long -range aircraft would weigh several times the aircraft's own weight if it were to bring the energy needed to bring the aircraft forward and a container ship would not have room for containers with goods because the ship would be Filled with batteries. In those contexts, other forms of energy are needed if we are to get rid of the fossil fuels, and this is where Power-to-X is a solution.

How effectively is Power-to-X and green fuels? However, the higher energy density in, for example, hydrogen also comes with a price, as parts of the energy are lost in the production of the green fuels. If we look at the production of hydrogen, it is done by the fact that water in an electrolysis process is split into hydrogen and oxygen respectively. In that process, part of the energy is lost. The process is becoming increasingly efficient and the developers of electrolysis technology are now talking about the energy loss in the production of hydrogen will soon be down to 15-20 percent. Funny enough, however, it is precisely in the energy loss that we find the opportunities for development on Bornholm, because the lost energy is transformed into heat, which can be used in district heating and in new types of businesses that can utilize the heat and thereby create jobs.

Why make hydrogen and green fuels on Bornholm? I have been asked several times how it can make sense to produce Power-to-X on Bornholm. Does it not make much better sense to transport electricity to Copenhagen or Berlin and transform it into, for example, Jetfuels where there is at the same time a large city with a large district heating network that can subside the large quantities of heat? It's a logical question. The problem, however, is that it is expensive to transport electricity in cables, while it is cheaper to transport hydrogen in pipelines. In other words, from an economic perspective, it makes the best sense to produce hydrogen as close to the energy source as possible. It also expresses the fact that the wind turbine manufacturers are working to develop mills, which in the future will produce hydrogen right inside the mill or on platforms close to the mills. In those mills, most of the heat will be lost, but it is expected that the mills are cost -effective because electricity is transformed into hydrogen all close to the energy source. However, this type of mills does not come into play to Energiø Bornholm, because the main focus is on the production of electricity and because the new mill type is not expected to be ready until the 2030s.

In relation to the question of why it is relevant to produce hydrogen on Bornholm, it is also worth noting that Bornholm is not the only community to find out what Power-to-X means to them. Green fuels and especially hydrogen are included in the ideas in most places where there are plans for larger extensions with wind and solar energy - and often in smaller communities it is far away from the big cities. This is also the case on the other two energy islands in the Baltic Sea, Gotland and Åland, where especially Åland is far ahead in the plans to produce hydrogen based on the 4-6 GW offshore winds, which can be developed in the sea around the archipelago.

Is there economics in power-to-x? I have often also been asked if Power-to-X makes sense purely financially.

The think tank Kraka has, among other things. a. Published a report arguing that the construction of a power-to-x industry in Denmark will require significant financial support because green fuels today are more expensive than black fuels. Both the question and the argument are logical, but they do not change the fact that Power-to-X is an indispensable part of the solution to the climate crisis and that there is political awareness of the fact that roads must be found that enable commercial production of green fuels . This can be done through the support of the Danish state or the EU, which is already happening today, and this will also be expected in the future to also be done through additional taxes based on the amount of CO2 a particular type of production emits, which will make CO2-neutral fuels more competitive Compared to eg. a. Coal and oil. Whether power-to-X is helped by support or indirectly supported through taxes on CO2, the expectation in the energy industry is that Power-to-X will be crucial to the green transition in the future, and at Christiansborg there is a great deal of attention to , that Power-to-X must be a new Danish business position.

What does Bornholm get out of it? What can Bornholm get out of Power-to-X? In addition to the obvious, which are the jobs that will be linked directly to production, I see three topics that are interesting.

The most obvious item is district heating.

Can we remodel our district heating system so that it can be based on surplus heat from green energy production? And at what price can it be done? It is one of the exciting topics to be examined by Bornholm Energi & Supply together with Rønne Water and Heat. If it succeeds, it is expected to lead to lower heating prices and thus make it cheaper to be a Bornholm and Bornholm company.

The next topic is new green businesses and green workplaces. If Power-to-X production is established on Bornholm, there is expected to be more surplus heat than we can utilize in the district heating network.

There will also be a lot of oxygen, as oxygen is another surplus product that occurs when water is split. The question is therefore what kinds of business we can build up around what can be called Bornholm's two new raw materials: heat and oxygen.

It can be food in greenhouses, production of protein, water park, fish farming, industrial processes that require hot and probably many other options that will arise as we gain more experience. From the fall of 2023, Baltic Energy Island, together with a large number of partners such as Business Center Bornholm, DTU, Energy Cluster Denmark, Danfoss, CIP and Gate21 will focus on this topic and include both Bornholm and outside companies in developing possible solutions to what we can use heat and oxygen for.

The last topic is about innovation, research and education. As can be seen, all the solutions do not exist today. It may well give a sense of uncertainty, because what is we saying yes to, and is it going to happen at all? Conversely, it is an opportunity for Bornholm because it is the innovation that today runs universities such as DTU, AAU and SDU to participate in activities at Bornholm, and it is the innovation that causes large companies like Ørsted and Siemens Gamesa to engage in Baltic Energy Island.

For Bornholm, it is an opportunity to attract research, students and innovation projects, which are of crucial importance for Bornholm both now and especially in the long run.

From other smaller communities and cities such as Gotland and Luleå we know that establishing university education and innovation houses supports the establishment of new businesses and develops existing companies to become more competitive.

Is it a good idea? As described, it is very much that suggests that Power-to-X can become a future profession on Bornholm, which can both directly and through derived businesses to strengthen the island economy. However, the road there requires both innovation and dialogue if it is to be successful. At Baltic Energy Island, we are both ready to enter into the dialogue about Power-to-X on Bornholm, and we are ready to help find the solutions needed to fulfill the potential.

Title: Energiøer kan godt ligge på land
Content:
It is our great ambition that Greenlab should not only be a sunbeam story for the Skive area, but serve as a work drawing for a number of other rural areas.

WHEN DISC IN NORTH JULY lies the Green Industrial Park GreenLab, which works to produce, store and share energy in new ways, thus creating a more coherent energy system. Here it has been shown that green change is not only for the benefit of the climate, but also has great potential to create local growth and development.

CEO of Greenlab, Christopher Sorensen, talks about Greenlab and the great vision for the future.

I have recently had the pleasure of several visits to Bornholm and conversations with Bornholmers, where we have had the joy and curiosity of the green opportunities of the future in common. I have learned that Bornholm is rich in competencies, natural resources and commitment. It is an island with independent opinions, and one thinks when others step in the door with a lot of good ideas. It is right now that all the possibilities need to be considered, and you have to make sure that you make the choices that give the best results.

For almost a year and a half, the Danes have had to deal with new times in the energy market.

Supply security is not something that you take for granted, energy prices have risen, and in a short time we have become very aware of when we turn on the washing machine and maybe not so tempted by dishes that require a lit oven for hours. The new attention to domestic energy consumption is important, but it may surprise many Danes that it is in industrial processes that are most energy lost. In fact, about half of the energy used in the industry is lost - for example, in the form of heat energy that is shut out it is free without being used for anything.

An energy island on land This is, among other things, the loss of energy we try to stop in the green industrial park GreenLab at Skive. Here we are working to create future energy systems where energy can be used circularly and where we do not think of energy as something that belongs to different silos - electricity, heat, gas etc. - but find ways in which we can transform one type of energy to another type of energy, so we utilize the potential of energy to a much greater extent - that's what you call sector coupling. You could say that we have created a large springboard for the Energy Islands on land, where we work with four core areas, which I will go here here.

1. We are testing Power-to-X as the first we are right now by building a large-scale test system for Power-to-X, which gets its energy from our solar and wind park via a direct clutch. It is quite unique and can only be done because we have been given the status of regulatory test zone. In a regulatory test zone, selected innovative energy and supply solutions can be granted a temporary exemption from rules that would otherwise prevent the project's implementation. With our status as a regulatory test zone, we have the opportunity to try the technologies that will help to drive the green transition.

And just as important - try how they work in context. It is an important lever for the upscaling and sector coupling that is needed prior to the establishment of the planned energy islands.

2. The companies in the park are running on green power and sharing their energy When the Power-to-X system is up and running, it will mean that the industrial companies that lie in our industrial park and who all work with technologies within it Green transition is connected to the green energy sources, so they run at 100 percent green power. But it doesn't stop there.

The companies in the industrial park also share their excess energy with each other through our unique symbiosis network? that allows one company's surplus energy to become another company's resource.

Symbiosisnet is the energy's answer to the cooperative community, where the joint effort gives a common gain. For example, one of the companies' surplus heat is channeled to another company, where it acts as a supplementary energy source that displaces natural gas.

Thus, an industrial symbiosis such as GreenLab can, even with energy -intensive consumption, ensure efficient use of renewable energy and relieve the electricity grid when it is severely stressed by utilizing new storage options. Then the wind turbines can continue to spin and exploit the full potential of renewable energy, without bottlenecks.

3. Research with soil under the nails GreenLab works closely with the technical universities in Denmark and acts as a test site when theories are to be tried in practice. There are currently 10 research projects underway in the park with interdisciplinary professional content and targeted scaling of promising energy systems and technologies. The green transition requires experiments with new forms of energy and research that are tried in practice and on a large scale, so that we can quickly find out what can be worked on and what is not working.

4. Local anchoring and local change is part of the foundation GreenLab has been created as a public-private partnership, where Skive Municipality and local private actors took on the initial risk. This means that we are strongly locally rooted, and it is crucial to us that our work helps to create local green growth on the Skiveegnen.

From we started on a bar field in 2019, about 100 new full -time jobs have been created, over 180,000 hours of additional work for local companies, DKK 489 million in capital investments and over DKK 2.6 billion in new investments in the development and operation of the matric.

We are proud of that, and we hope we can serve as inspiration for the green industrial parks of the future.

We dream of being copy/ pasted It is our great ambition that Greenlab should not only be a sunbeam story for the Skive area, but serve as a work drawing for a number of other rural areas where sun and wind are abundant and where the potential for the potential of Take advantage of it's great. Our hope is that the learning we have done since its inception can become the foundation of a number of new industrial clusters - both in Denmark and abroad - so that coherent energy systems are reduced that reduce the industry's energy waste as many places as possible.

I have just returned from the United States, where we entered into an agreement with a major infrastructure company in Nevada to learn from us so that the United States can also get one or more Greenlabs. And there is also a need for front runners in Denmark. I hope therefore that Bornholm is the next location that would like to use some of Greenlab's experience to create their own version of green growth with a view to what citizens want. We are ready for the collaboration when you need it.

Title: Wermelin håber på brintrør til Tyskland - men hvad bliver statens rolle?
Content:
The possibility of hydrogen production is part of the negotiations on Energiø Bornholm, says Social Democracy Energy Mayor Lea Wermelin, who at last week's conference on the energy island expressed support for Power-to-X on Bornholm soil. Energy/ politics.

For Lea Wermelin last week was largely in the sign of energy island. In the Folketing she is in the middle of the negotiations on how Energiø Bornholm should be structured and financed, and on Tuesday the Social Democratic energy mayor could just squeeze a visit at home on Bornholm to Baltic Energy Island Summit. Here she talked positively about the establishment of a hydrogen infrastructure in the Baltic Sea, which will create a basis for producing hydrogen or other green fuels on Bornholm.

- In addition to being the Social Democracy's energy and climate mayor, I am also from Bornholm.

It has become one of my children, if you can say that we have to exploit the full potential of the energy island, Lea Wermelin said at the conference.

On the back of the summit, she states to the Journal that the Social Democracy hopes that it will somehow be possible to establish hydrogen infrastructure in the Baltic Sea.

- Yes, settled. If we are to make our hopes for the industry to be changed, I think hydrogen will be the answer there, says Wermelin.

She believes it is obvious that some of the wind resources in the Baltic Sea are transformed into hydrogen.

- We need to create a good framework for some of the benefits to be harvested, says the former Environment Minister.


Private or state

While a Danish-German hydrogen connection in Jutland has been under planning for several years, the political ambitions in the Baltic Sea are newer and less familiar. Lea Wermelin points out that hydrogen infrastructure in the Baltic Sea can become both a state and a private matter.

- There must also be opportunities for the right framework for private initiatives.

Have you written off in advance that the state can actively enter into the establishment of hydrogen tube in the Baltic Sea? - It is not yet decided how we will do it exactly, so it is probably a postage too early to answer, says Lea Wermelin, who emphasizes that she will not reveal anything from the negotiating table.

She mentions in the same breath that the day after the summit came out in the newspaper Børsen, the Danish government has gone into the negotiations on Energiø Bornholm with a starting point that 25 percent of offshore wind farms must be owned by the state, which industry organization Green Power Denmark immediately warned against.

When it comes to hydrogen tube, ownership conditions also occupy the energy companies, you could see on Baltic Energy Island Summit. 'Hopefully soon'

It is Lars Ewald Jensen, who thus defines the ranking of spades, and as project manager for archeology at Energinet, he has quite good control of such spades that Bornholm's Journal has met to attend - namely what begins the first archaeological preliminary studies in connection with With Energiø Bornholm.

That is why we are also freely out under a glorious summery sun at a plow field, where the preliminary maneuvers are made to what director at the Bornholm Museum Jacob Bjerring-Hansen has been designed as "without comparison the largest archaeological project in Bornholm Museum History ".

The invitation to the press stated that it was just about meeting at 10am, then the Bornholm Museum would put the shovel in the ground for the first archaeological feasibility studies in connection with Energiø Bornholm. "It is possible to get pictures of the first shovel and the initial excavation work," the invitation lured, but alas, it must have been in transferred meaning, for Lars Ewald Jensen explains unsentimental: - First shovel was taken just over 8 o'clock, a contractor is waiting Not just like the press.

The application deadline now, in the name of efficiency, we avoid a set picture of a shovel, but fortunately can continue this engraving journalistic article to find that also among other Jens Berthold, who is a newly appointed chief archaeologist at the Bornholm Museum, is of course present.

He can explain that yes, quite a few archaeologists must be used for this gigantic task, but: - Not right now. The trick is to ensure that the archaeologists and construction workers do not get on the same square meters at the same time. So we archaeologists start much earlier, and it is only at the end of 2025 that something really has to happen here purely in terms of building. Now we are starting to make search trenches using the excavator, which is in the process, so we can see if there is anything to come after purely archaeological.

In fact, we have exactly today (Monday, ed.) Application deadline on three job postings we have made and where we are looking for archaeologists.

Does Bornholm Museum have advice to just hire three new archaeologists? Here Lars Ewald Jensen steps in and explains: - The Museum Act is screwed together so that a builder must finance the archaeological excavations, and that is, what is going on out here is financed by Energinet.

The museum has an archaeological responsibility that it should solve, but we are well aware that when we come up with a 107 hectare station and dump this plus the cables to be pulled, it is a huge task. Probably Bornholm's biggest to date, when it comes to archeology, but even at national level it must be described as big, and therefore we go in and help the museum both logistically and otherwise so that it can lift that task.

And also in relation to the financing of the extra archaeologists? - Yes, we always do. It follows from the Museum Act.

The cultural heritage is all of us, but the builder is required to pay for it, and the possible finds come to a large part to end up at the Bornholm Museum.

A little sad one must assume that the 20 archaeologists who can come up will only get a temporary employment? - Yes, says Jens Berthold.

- They should not be here until the retirement age, but maybe for a few years. It is difficult to determine precisely in advance.

Lars Ewald Jensen: - These are the conditions of Danish Archeology. It is financed that way, and I personally think it is a little sad for some of our younger archaeologists that they have to commute the country around.

Nor exactly when the three archaeologists found through the three current posts have to start, Jens Berthold can say, because it depends on various things.

- But if they are not on other contracts and are ready to get started, it must be in a month's time, he says.

- That would be good.

Lars Ewald Jensen: - As an old museum man I can say that you also want to get hold of some archaeologists who are good, and then you would like to wait for them to come.

Work on the first 60 hectares, which are now being investigated, should be able to be done until October this year, then the work is waiting up to the 107 hectares, which is the station area itself, but also an additional area will probably be withdrawn from the landowner's land , says Lars Ewald Jensen.

He says that, among other things, once in the 19th century a truly unique gold treasure was found here in the area - you do not know exactly where - with 36 Roman coins, which today are exhibited at the National Museum, and which could suggest that there is more here To come by, possibly a settlement.
