Title: Ejerskab til energiproduktion giver ikke blot forsyningssikkerhed, men også økonomisk sikkerhed
Content:
Fortunately, it seems that one has noticed that it will be silly to repeat the mistakes of the past, where the right to utilize common resources - namely the North Sea's oil and gas fields - were only given away in Denmark, while in Norway in Norway Far higher managed to manage such resources in common financial benefit.

It is hardly behind anyone that many rural municipalities in these years good sugar after an economic salt water injection, so that the cities' trade and cultural life can be started, and so that families can feel reassured that there will also be good deals for Them when the children need to be looked after and to school when you get hurt and need to be re -trained, or when you get older and need an extra hand in the home.

Therefore - and to be part of the solution to the galloping climate crisis - many rural municipalities have offered when project developers for sun and wind projects have been looking for locations for new energy projects.

This applies not least to many Jutland municipalities, where large sun and wind parks have been built in recent years. But now something new has started to happen. The desire to play actively in the green transition has not diminished, but some municipalities have begun to become aware that it can happen in several ways. Instead of just welcoming the project developers inside, municipalities such as Ringkøbing -Skjern, Varde, Lemvig, Esbjerg and Tønder have begun to look at whether the projects cannot be developed in a different way - and not least in another ownership - so that the local economy Gains are getting bigger.

And the Rural Joint Council has just published a proposal for a green overall plan for Danish rural areas, which have 'committed local return from energy plants' as its first benchmark - something that is proposed, among other things, through local ownership and thus a better distribution between burdens and gains. In these efforts, municipalities, rural areas and communities are helped well by the legislation adopted in Denmark a few years ago, which made it possible to create renewable energy communities - local energy communities and citizen energy communities - also with municipal participation.

Some years ago, Karl Sperling and Brian Vad Mathiesen from Aalborg University published a report that examined the importance of local ownership of energy production. They were based on a 52 MW Landvindmøllepark in Billund Municipality with an estimated construction budget of DKK 24 million at that time. and examined various distributions of ownership, including a distribution where full ownership was outside the municipality, and a distribution where ownership was fully locally rooted within the municipal boundary, distributed by 50 percent to a local project developer and 50 percent to local citizens . The results are thoughtful. In the model, where all ownership was outside the municipality, the annual local economic effect in the operational phase was estimated to be DKK 500,000 per year.

year. Of these, about half were revenue for the municipal treasury in the form of contributions from project owner to the green pool (then green scheme), while the other half linked to the extra local employment that the operation and maintenance of the wind turbines threw off. In comparison, the local economic effects at 100 percent local ownership were almost three times higher, ie almost 1.5 million. kr. year! This was not only a contribution to the municipal treasury, but also about citizens and businesses that were part of the profits from the sale of electricity, and all the dynamic effects this gives to the turnover of the local trade, culture and business. And with such local winnings, investments can quickly earn home.

This is the picture that a number of Jutland municipalities and also the Rural Joint Council have now begun to spot and therefore has begun to demand local ownership. Many have also started to create energy communities, some with municipal participation.

Why let the majority of the financial gain by laying land and prospect of renewable energy plants countries outside the municipality if, through another distribution of ownership, it could land within the municipal boundary and benefit both the private and municipal economy? And here in the eleventh hour it now also seems that from a political point of view in Christiansborg, we have now woken up when it comes to the exploitation of Denmark's common offshore wind resource. Fortunately, it seems that one has noticed that it will be stupid to repeat the mistakes of the past, where the right to utilize common resources - namely the North Sea's Oil and Gas Fields - in Denmark were simply given away while in Norway in Norway Far higher managed to manage such resources in common financial benefit (that in Norway, also contributed tremendously to the destruction of the climate, is another, and quite sad case). Therefore, it is now considered to require 25 percent state ownership of the state offshore wind projects that will soon be offered, including Bornholm. This look at ownership of ensuring benefits for the community in the green transition of our energy supply - whether in the municipalities or at national level - is completely fundamental. For precisely because energy production and supply are so central to our society, ownership does not just provide greater security of supply; It also provides greater financial security. And then ownership becomes tremendously important, not only for the support of the green transition, but also the social and economic cohesion of our society, in the municipalities as well as between country and city, now and many years to come.

Title: Jeg drømmer småt
Content:
I dream that my Bornholm should not be destroyed so that we can become an energy producer for distant own. Like an Arab oil state, just without the revenue and without determining what is going to happen to our country.

I dream of a Bornholm where the future is in line with the special values ​​I have experienced at Bornholm and appreciated for 45 years here. After growing up in the Copenhagen area and moving here as a 24-year-old.

The especially Bornholm values ​​for me are a society that is clear, varied and composed of many small elements. This applies to both business and culture. The foundation of all this is nature. Within a sharply limited area, here is an ease of variation. The sea around us makes it a little difficult to get here. That's good. Then we can fully feel the tranquility falling on us and lowering our shoulders upon arrival.

This is what Bornholm - the country Bornholm - which I almost fell in love with. I therefore do not share editor -in -chief of Gravgaards and many others' views when he writes (in the leader 19.

May) that "it's time to dream big on the climate and Bornholm's behalf".

That he wants to dream big and good for the climate, I join in. But I think the "big dreams" for Bornholm, who are increasingly unfolding from people with influence (local and country politicians, Energinet, public and private interests in the energy sector, Rønne Harbor) looks like a nightmare for the Bornholm that I hold of. It must then be supplemented with a new and longer quay so that even larger cruise ships can call Rønne. It is not my dream of future tourism for Bornholm. Neither for the climate (CO2 and air pollution) nor for the environment for tourists and Bornholmers when for a few hours several thousand people come to our rather small urban communities.

Now a number of gigantic industrial buildings are dreamed further because central (elected officials!) Governors believe that Bornholm should add land and water to energy plants to supply Denmark and Germany. Wind turbines, transformer stations, fuel factories of unknown dimensions on Lille Bornholm.

It's not my dream either.

The Center for Regional and Tourism Research has not figured out how many emigrants will mean in the long run with this change of Bornholm's DNA.

I'd rather dream small. It fits me better and my Bornholm.

I will dream of many small businesses, entrepreneurs, IT companies and the development of the large industries we already have. I dream that people will continue to visit Bornholm as a holiday island and want to move here because of the special calm, nature and variation in the culture and business we have. I dream that my Bornholm should not be destroyed so that we can become an energy producer for distant own. Like an Arab oil state, just without the revenue and without determining what is going to happen to our country.

Of course, we have to work for a green transition, but in a way that is balanced in relation to Bornholm's environment and values. And more decentralized in its construction to create greater security in the case of sabotage - and proximity to users in Denmark and Germany.

There is plenty to think about. Russia's attack on Ukraine and threats to infrastructure are crucial factors that have not been thought out in the dreams of the energy island. It can be disastrous. Therefore: Stop the expansion of Rønne Harbor now. Stop the energy island on Bornholm now.

Title: Power-to-x og natur: Debatsalon om energiøen
Content:

The debate salon is part of the debate project "Where do we dream?", Which is a collaboration between Baltic Bridge, Center for Regional and Tourism Research, Lag-Bornholm, Citizens' Association Cooperation and Bornholm Tidende trying to promote the debate on Bornholm distributed over various themes .

And in the past month, a large part of Tidende's debate pages have been earmarked debate about the energy island, where stakeholders have debated attitudes and perspectives on the energy island and its challenges, opportunities, gains, limitations and consequences - and there are many of them.

Come to become wiser It is the old power plant in Lille Madsegade in Rønne, which forms the framework for the debate salon.

In the large, raw hall, Baltic Energy Island has exhibited various interactive videos and elements that will make terbs and hears wiser about the visions, and that exhibition also constitutes the quiet and unofficial warming of today's debate.

"Green Energy is a shared responsibility," reads the conclusion of a video to the approximately 30-40 talers who have emerged. One of them is Jeppe Poulsen, who as a private person has come to today's debate salon to become wiser.

- I'm interested in what we can get out of it. What I as a inhabitant get out of it, he says of the energy island.

And whether he is getting smarter must be up to today's panelists who are armed with words such as power-to-x, surplus heat, electrolysis plant, business park, biodiversity and transport costs will each give their concerns and perspectives on the upcoming energy island.

And provided with soda and draft beer takes the associated space, while today's chairman, Tidende Energy Reporter Jakob Nørmark, introduces the seven panelists who are onto teams on stage and summarize their pointers. In common to them is that they have all written debate in the Journal about the energy island, but they represent different Bornholm interests, including business, economy, tourism, locals, nature and energy.

The seven are Anne Thomas from the Center for Regional and Tourism Research, Klaus Vesløv from Bornholm's Energy & Supply, Lars Nordahl Lemvigh from Rønne Harbor, Christa Lodahl from Business Center Bornholm, Jørgen Hammer from the Citizens' Association's Collaboration, Søren Møller Christensen from Baltic Energy Island and Michael Stoltze from the Danish Nature Conservation Association Bornholm.


The landscape and nature must play together

Michael Stoltze and Jørgen Hammer, who represent nature and communities respectively, are called on stage, and the chairman Jakob Nørmark first addresses Michael Stoltze: - You explained in your debate posts for your basic points of view that nature and green setting should be able to go hand in hand. What does the Danish Society for Nature Conservation (DNF) look at the large model of the energy island? What are the thoughts? - We have related to the specific transformer system where there is a model, replies Michael Stoltze and puts some figures on the plans that are for the land system for the energy island: - Bornholm is just over 600 square kilometers.

If we say there is an area of ​​600 hectares, then we are at one percent. 300 hectares, then we're up to half a percent. These are not some large areas that way, and if we compare with a few large pig farms, it is no longer anymore. These are large buildings that are dominating on Bornholm, he says.

Specifically, DNF dreams of a sustainable island and a sustainable society where the energy island must play with the landscape and nature.

Title: Hvor stor kan energiøen blive? Det største bud lyder på 600 hektar
Content:
If Bornholm's role as an energy hub leads to the creation of factories for the manufacture of hydrogen and green fuels as well as a business park with companies that can utilize surplus heat, the energy island may end up absorbing about one percent of the island's area. It assessed the panel in Tuesday's debate salon. Although there will be benefits to establishing a concentrated cluster, everyone does not necessarily have to be gathered on Sydbornholm.

The word "if" was included in many sentences and was often pronounced with pressure as energy-interested readers on Tuesday afternoon gathered in Rønne's old power plant for a debate about the energy island. It happened as part of the debate series "Where do we dream", which Bornholm Tidende takes part in.

In particular, the panel deltas used if the possibility of the possibility of production of hydrogen and green fuels on Bornholm. When talking about local opportunities for new professions, lasting jobs and relocation, Power-to-X is decisive for how great the potential can be.

The uncertainty of what the future brings was the Journal prepared for, and therefore we had brought a framed Bornholm map to the debate salon to make one of the debate's main questions more concrete: "How big can it be?". And by extension, "Where should it all lie?" We asked the questions, while the panel consisted of Søren Møller Christensen from Baltic Energy Island, Anne Thomas from the Center for Regional and Tourism Research and Klaus Vesløv from Bornholm Energi and Supply (BEOF).

Søren Møller Christensen estimated that if the energy island is also going to consist of offshore wind farms east of Bornholm, an electrolysis plant on a large scale and a larger business park, where companies that can utilize the surplus products - heat and oxygen - or proximity to the advanced electricity plant, then the total area can reach about 600 hectares, ie six square kilometers.

At the same time, 300-400 hectares mentioned as another scenario, which may be the case of planning if the different plants do not get the same size. With less energy and surplus heat available, the area requirement will also be reduced.

The most secure piece is the land plant, which belongs to Energiø Bornholm itself. Here, according to Energinet, the technical plant to be fitted will fill about 52 hectares. The total land plant including planting, access roads, rainwater lakes and more becomes 107 hectares. With an area requirement of 600 hectares, there will be a six -fold.


Overall or divided?

If the energy island can be made a reality in the max edition, it does not necessarily have to be gathered up the land plant in Sydbornholm, the panel emphasized.

However, several things are suggesting that an electrolysis system is placed nearby, as it will make the most sense financially and technically, as you will save costs for electric cables or heat pipes.

Such a large coherent area south of Aakirkeby and Lobbæk will in many ways settle for traditional planning, where cities are gradually growing outward, and businesses gather in clusters on the outskirts. Thus, it will also be an opportunity to put a business park in, for example, Nexø, Aakirkeby or Rønne, said Søren Møller Christensen, who was formerly the leader of development and plan in Bornholm Regional Municipality. At the same time, he pointed out that they are planning to place the large energy parks with solar parks, onshore wind turbines and factories for the production of hydrogen and green fuels, which are under planning elsewhere in Denmark, out in the countryside in total clusters to create distance from the cities. For example, the production of ammonia will require large security distances which will make it difficult to place in ordinary business districts.

The most concrete project proposal on Power-to-X on Bornholm soil comes from Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners (CIP), which together Ørsted wants to build offshore wind farms east of land, a hydrogen system, and at the same time invest in hydrogen infrastructure for Germany. CIP was invited to participate in the debate salon but chose to refuse the offer. Instead, we asked Anne Thomas and Søren Møller Christensen, who through their work have been in dialogue with CIP, about where CIP wants to build a power-to-X plant if they get green light for the project from the authorities. To this, Anne Thomas replied that it should not necessarily be on Bornholm and that the geographical location does not have to be crucial to CIP on the slightly longer run. In the long term, hydrogen can be produced at sea, either directly in the mills or on platforms.

In time, you probably have to go well into the 2030s before sea -based hydrogen in large style can be done in practice, so that the hydrogen investors' interest in Bornholm area is real enough, the panel pointed out.

Wastewater in, District Heating out Klaus Vesløv described the implications of the large version of the energy island from a supply perspective.

BEOF will both be able to stand as a supplier and buyer if electrolysis is to be carried out on Bornholm. Water in large quantities must be used in the process, and Klaus Vesløv immediately made it clear that the drinking water could be removed from the equation. Water from the Baltic Sea, which, as you know, is not the most salty sea area, can be used, but the desalination of the seawater will require extra investment.

Instead, one can use the Bornholm wastewater, which according to Beof will be an obvious resource to lead to Sydbornholm, or where a power-to-X plant may be located.

When the water molecules are to be split, a considerable amount of energy goes to waste in the form of heat. With a project of the size that CIP and Ørsted have presented, the total Bornholm district heating needs can be covered many times - up to a nine or doubling can be involved. So much extra heat has caused the BEOF to consider the possibility of tying the five separate district heating networks with new pipes.

When something becomes "left over," it is supposed to be cheap to buy, Klaus told Vesløv, who for that reason expects the Bornholm's heating price to be significantly reduced.

How much cheaper one can expect that the district heating in eight to ten years may be, he could not give a more concrete answer to.

After all, there were too many if's.

To some extent, the debate on the energy island - and not least Power -to -X - takes place on rocking grounds. But if everything was already nail -resistant, there would be less to debate.

One of the possibilities is that a total cluster is established around Energinet's high -voltage station south of Aakirkeby. Title: Peter Juel-Jensen: ' Jeg forventer ro på bagsmækken'
Content:
If there is no tranquility internally in the party, it is impossible to navigate as politically elected, says parliamentary member Peter Juel-Jensen (V).

Peter Juel-Jensen (V) woke up on Thursday morning to the news that his local chairman Michael Hendriksen has resigned from his post and leaves the party because a majority in the board does not want him. It read the member of the parliament in an email to the members of the Left, and his immediate reaction was the annoyance that the board has not been able to make the cooperation work.

- There is a little hassle in the board, it seems. It is not good for a party when those who lead the local organization cannot agree that I must understand on the mail that they cannot, says Peter Juel-Jensen to the Journal.

What is the basis of the disagreement and thus Michael Hendriksen's decision does not quite know.

- I have talked quite briefly with Michael Hendriksen this morning and can understand that he thinks things are stuck. I have known Michael Hendriksen for many years and am on good terms with him, and of course I am sorry that you have not been able to make it work internally. I don't quite know what is the reason, and it's not something I spend a lot of energy on either, says Peter Juel-Jensen.

As a member of parliament, Peter Juel-Jensen is largely the left of the Left.

It is he who is at the forefront when the party goes out and argues for its attitudes and views in election campaigns, and the board of directors is his closest political partner at Bornholm at all times.

- I expect there is peace of mind, because otherwise it will be completely impossible to navigate as politically elected. Whether it is one or the other, I have no opportunity to assess that, says Peter Juel-Jensen.

Hard to comment on the bottom when there are cures on the thread, and things don't really run in oil, then it's something that sits all the way down an organization, says Peter Juel-Jensen, because it will be difficult to set aside the necessary time , if you just have to sit and disagree.

- If an organization or party is to work, then there must be peace of mind. Of course, you may disagree, but you have to disagree at such a level that you can look each other in the eyes and make things work, says Peter Juel-Jensen.

Seen with his eyes, politics internally in a party is about bending against each other and meeting about something everyone can back up.

- But I think it's hard to comment on the bottom when I don't know what has gone before. It is also not my job to screw me down, because I have another task, and I spend it all my waking hours solving, he says.


Plenty of tasks with political content

Personally, Peter Juel-Jensen had hoped that the internal fights in the Left on Bornholm had been arranged a long time ago, because internal strife suggests that there is also doubt about the political direction, and there is not, he states. He is fire excess that the Left now again gets a ride in the Bornholm press for something he does not think the party deserves - both the organization and the board are significantly better than the image that is drawn when we do not agree, he says .

Isn't it because you deliver plenty of shoots yourself? - There is no doubt about that, but I would rather have the board of directors in the press for something good, for a membership campaign, a membership growth or some good dialogue meetings where you try to come to Bornholm interests and the Bornholm business community and have created created some common platform. We stand in a place where we need a very strong organization, both with the prospect of an energy island and a new defense settlement and a completely different security policy situation on Bornholm. There are plenty of political content tasks to address. This is where I want to put my weight and not on internal fights about something that can be very difficult to understand for outsiders, says Peter Juel-Jensen.

Title: Her er kommunens lobbyindsats: En millionbetaling for " noget af det dyrebareste, vi har" og seks konkrete idéer til udbud
Content:
A larger community contribution, prioritization of permanent housing rather than scabs and financial support to operate the power plant are some of the wishes that Jacob Trøst has to the tender conditions for Energiø Bornholm, which the parties' energy rapporteurs and the government are currently negotiating. If no money is falling directly to the municipality, it will be "huge pressed" in the coming years, the mayor warns.

In mid -March, Mayor Jacob Trøst (K) sent a letter to the Folketing's energy mayors. Here the Bornholm views and wishes are formulated in a short mail and an attached document on just over two A4 pages. In the letter, which comfort has shared with the Journal, it can be read that the mayor is calling on the Folketing to compensate Bornholm for laying land and views of Energiø Bornholm's land facility and offshore wind farms.

"Bornholm is going to give some of the most precious we have - area on and around Bornholm - to an upcoming state offshore wind farm. Therefore, Bornholm and the other parts of the country that contribute to expensive area to the community and the green transition in Denmark, must have something again, ”Jacob Consolidation states in the first paragraph.

"The upcoming offshore wind project Energiø Bornholm is expected to make a profit to the state. It is important that there is a distribution of the profit to the state, municipality and communities, so that it also just as a social contribution to the area that paid a high price, ”says the argument from the regional municipality's political leader.


Green pool without a win

He reminds the politicians that Bornholm is not able to receive any subsidy from the Green Pool, which others in the event ensure that resorts of renewable energy plants such as solar cells, wind turbines on land or closer to the coast have to pay a contribution to the local community.

"The purpose is to promote local support for setting up VE (renewable energy, ed.) And support the green transition of the local communities. Had Energiø Bornholm been covered by Green Pool, Bornholm Regional Municipality would have received about DKK 500 million. A similar scheme should be considered In connection with Energiø Bornholm, and this should also be the case when the extension of the offshore wind turbine fields covered of the open-door scheme, is initiated, ”Jacob Solves writes.

The amount of half a billion kroner comes from calculations of what the municipality's revenue would have been if all the mills for the state's wind turbine project were to be set up 0-15 kilometers from land. The grant from the Green Pool is only triggered to coastal projects that are within 15 kilometers of distance to the coast, and the current political agreement states that the mills do not get closer to the south coast than just 15 kilometers. Neither is the high voltage station in SOSE covered by the pool, and Jacob Trøst thinks that should be different.

- So we get a land plant of just over 50 hectares, and the whole area, which is reserved for Energinet, is over 100 hectares, says Jacob Trøst, who in the letter provides examples of what new revenue for the regional municipality will create of opportunities.

He suggests that the community contribution "targets investments that make it possible to lift the great opportunities that Energiø Bornholm provides for business development on Bornholm - and thus to make Bornholm financially self -supporting".

Consolation's three concrete suggestions are :? “Investments in a business park for green companies that take advantage of the opportunities that the energy island offers for business development.

? Investments in vocational education at Bornholm within "Green Skills" (green skills, ed.)? Investments in the development of municipal core welfare to support the development in the form of day care institutions, schools, but also the necessary government treatment. " - We will be extremely pressed for resources if there is nothing extra in it for us, says Jacob Consolation to the Journal before listing some of the many municipal tasks that the energy island brings.

Everything from new daycare centers and schools due to relocation to the work on local plans, building permits and laying out of new business and residential areas will provide an extra burden in the administration if the energy island does not trigger a direct economic injection to the regional municipality.

- I think we will need some help, because we do not have a cash balance of several billion kroner as in the City of Copenhagen, says Jacob Trøst.

Uncertainty during negotiations in the letter also presents the conservative mayor's six concrete proposals for the tender documents. The points (see the illustration) will be in different ways in Bornholm's interest.

Jacob Trøst points out that the six proposals for, among other things, permanent housing, apprentices and biodiversity are not merely about the fact that the Bornholm region must have more out of the giant project. The idea of ​​enrolling requirements that the bidders must contribute financially to a technology platform, a test site and dissemination activities in the power plant in Rønne will benefit Danish business opportunities in a broad sense, the mayor believes.

- The project can help lift all of Denmark's technological innovation.

Of course, it will also benefit locally at the same time, he says.

These days and weeks, the recipients of the letter negotiate on Energiø Bornholm and the conditions in the tender. How the energy rapporteurs use the local wishes in the negotiations, Jacob Consolation can only guess.

- I have a very hard time assessing that, because I am not locked into the engine room, he says.

- But at least I know that they have got a clear impression of what wishes we have at Bornholm. That's what been the focus for me.

Jacob Trøst says that his party partner at Christiansborg, energy mayor Mona Juul, has said that the timing for lobbying in the early spring up to the negotiations has been good.


Neighbors in mind

In addition to the desire to make additions to the tender material and channel a social contribution to the municipal treasury, Jacob Consolation in the Follow Mail to the energy rapporteurs makes it aware that future neighbors of large energy plants as the land plant should be made better. He proposes to spread the possibility of financial compensation, as well as the state's ability to buy properties near a high -voltage station should be able to increase.

"Today, the legislation provides the possibility of acquiring properties by planning railways and highway under certain conditions. A similar option when planning a larger WE plant could ensure better popular support for this," writes comfort in the follow-up email, where he suggests that he suggests that he A large transformer and transformer station such as Energinets is equated with energy-producing plants such as solar parks and wind turbines.

"One possibility could be that - as with onshore wind turbines - you were compensated according to the size and proximity of a WE system of a certain size," says the at the bottom of the mayor's mail.


Technological innovation

There should also be a requirement for contributions to technological innovation in the tender. Baltic Energy Island is building a platform for technological innovation under the auspices of energy islands in the partnership with the state of commercial fire tower Bornholm. Baltic Energy Island's Technological Roadmap and Test Site are obvious areas to ensure a close link and financing.


Nature and Environment - On Lands and To Water

The tenderer must ensure that the project is a gain for nature, the environment and biodiversity for both land facilities and offshore wind turbines. Therefore, requirements for nature restoration and efforts must be introduced to create increased biodiversity around the plants.


Apprentices

Apprentices are used through all the phases of the project, so that a geographical distribution of the effect is ensured the construction building has for qualification. The tenderer must also contribute to competence development and education in Green Skills both during the construction period and during the operational phase.


Dissemination efforts

It is important for Bornholm that the winners of the offering are obliged to disseminate their project and enter into dialogue with the locals. This will contribute to a constructive dialogue about the establishment of the offshore wind farm and the upcoming open-door offerings. There is also a need for anchoring among education seekers and guests. An exhibition facility has already been planned to be run by the commercial fund Baltic Energy Island. It is a Bornholm wish that the tenderers are obliged to be part of the activities around Rønne Elværk and the dissemination activities. A bid for resources for the operation of dissemination efforts could be DKK 2-3 million. DKK annually over the construction period.


Overplanting

In connection with the subject of business park, the Bornholmers are concerned with what we have called "overplanting", where more energy is produced around Bornholm than can be transmitted in the state's network. The main interest is to create the framework for using the migration energy locally. It will benefit the possibilities of the production of green fuels, the opportunity to utilize surplus heat in a possible business park. A business park will create jobs and needs for qualified labor and thus education. And with more Bornholmers, it requires investment in community development.


Distribution of proceeds is a unique opportunity to lift Bornholm

Energiø Bornholm is expected to deliver a proceeds to the state. It is important that there is a distribution of the profits to the state, municipality and communities, so that it also justly accrues as a social contribution to the area that has paid a high price. In other contexts, a larger community contribution is accrued in the form of the so-called green pool under the Loven Act, where the sets of VE have to pay a contribution to the local development when wind and sun set up. The purpose is to promote the local support for setting up WE and supporting the green transition of the local communities.

Had Energiø Bornholm been covered by the Green Pool, Bornholm Regional Municipality would have received about DKK 500 million. A similar scheme should be considered in connection with Energiø Bornholm, and this should also be the case when the expansion of the offshore wind turbine fields covered by the open-door scheme is initiated.

Title: Trøst får ministerens kolde skulder: Et naturligt svar
Content:
Last week, the Minister of Energy stated that special local considerations in a tender are basically contrary to EU law. Bornholm Regional Municipality has just wanted to challenge the law with a proposal that the winners of the supply to Energiø Bornholm should prioritize permanent housing for the traveling workers instead of temporary scabs, Jacob says.

For the past few months, the mayor and the regional municipality have tried to influence the parliamentary politicians in relation to Energiø Bornholm. A small delegation with Jacob Trøst (K) at the forefront presented in April a number of local wishes and views for the climate, energy and supply committee, and a few weeks earlier there was the opportunity to convince Lars Aagaard during the Minister of Energy's visit to Bornholm.

Last week, the minister commented on the committee's request the regional municipality's proposal, which was mentioned in detail in the Journal Friday. In the written response, Lars Aagaard was noted that the project will, overall, "involve investments on a larger double -digit billion" and therefore benefit Bornholm.

"The large investments can have a number of significant, positive derivative consequences for business at Bornholm-for example in relation to the construction of the land facility, for derivative service industries and in relation to the demand of labor locally for the project," wrote Climate, Energy and Supply Minister Lars Aagaard.

At the same time, the minister - without informing specifically, what wishes he refers to - distanced distance from some of the proposals. He wrote that it is "essential to keep in mind that the procurement rules mean that it is basically contrary to EU law to take special local considerations when designing the requirements of the tender.

At the same time, the introduction of distinctive requirements can be expected to expand the project. "At the same time, he pointed to the risk of setting a precedent.

This semi -cold shoulder chooses Jacob Consolation not to put so much in.

- He has to draw attention to that.

He can't promise anything, because he sits in the negotiations, so I see it as a very natural answer, says the mayor of the Journal.

The regional municipality, which has formulated six specific wishes for the upcoming tender, has proposed to oblige the winners of the offering of offshore wind farms to enter into partnerships to accommodate the construction work in permanent housing rather than temporary scabs. Jacob Consolation recognizes that it is a different idea and that the municipality is deliberately trying to "challenge the law", as he says.

- We are aware that the requirement for permanent housing is not something that has been done before, says Jacob Trøst, who hopes that in Christiansborg they will look seriously at the idea.

Lars Aagaard pointed out in his response to the Parliamentary Committee that local interests have already been taken into account. He cites three examples: The architectural course around the land facility, the establishment of the commercial fire tower Baltic Energy Island and the efforts to connect the Bornholm electricity network directly to the energy island's new transformer station, whereby Bornholm will have a more secure electricity connection to the outside world.

Jacob Trøst does not believe that these measures, along with the total size of investment, should be enough to affect all the Bornholm priorities. On the other hand, he encourages the government to go to the matter with a holistic perspective, so that other ministries are involved in the issue of Energiø Bornholm.

He points to the Ministry of Education and the Ministry of Business as examples.

- I agree that one may be inclined to focus on one's own ministry. My hope is that you can look wider and look beyond your own ministry, says Jacob Consolation.

Lobby work for hydrogen? Many at Bornholm have recently talked about the fact that the commercial potential of Energiø Bornholm itself is not as large as with the hydrogen project presented by Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners and Ørsted. It has shown a current study from the Center for Regional and Tourism Research. According to the researchers' figures, the total employment potential of the energy projects will increase by approximately an extra 900 positions, if the offshore wind farms east of Bornholm and an electrolysis plant on a large scale (3 GW) can also come true.

In addition, there are hopes that access to suspected cheap surplus heat and oxygen will create new business opportunities.

These figures could speak for the municipality to extend the lobbying effort to promote the hydrogen project as well. Among other things, a realization will require politicians to support the establishment of a pipeline for Germany and other hydrogen infrastructure.

According to Jacob Trøst, the municipality has not yet launched an attempt to convince politicians to look east when it comes to hydrogen.

- So far we have concentrated on the energy island itself, says Jacob Consolation.

Any effort to promote hydrogen infrastructure in the Baltic Sea will hardly throw itself over before the framework for Energiø Bornholm is firm, says the mayor.

- It's something we need to look at when the energy island finally falls into place.

Jacob Trøst estimates that much will depend on what commercial players such as CIP and Ørsted do. The CIP Foundation has recently been engaged in Baltic Energy Island, which Ørsted was already in from the beginning when the commercial lighthouse was born under the name National Center for Green Energy. Throughout this forum, Bornholm's regional municipality can keep up to date.

The two energy companies' application for permission to initiate preliminary studies for the two proposed offshore wind farms east of Bornholm is currently collecting dust from the Danish Energy Agency, which suspended the open door scheme early in the year.

- Right now, I think you are awaiting the legislation and decisions about the open door scheme, says Jacob Consolation about the case.

This week, a broad majority in the Folketing decided that state -owned Energinet and Evida, already responsible for the methane gas network, must own the majority of the hydrogen tubes and carry out operations. As an exception, direct, privately owned hydrogen lines that are not part of the coherent hydrogen system can be given. The agreement includes something about where in the country should be laid out hydrogen pipes.

However, a look at Energinet's website clearly shows that the focus is on Western Denmark. Energinet writes that it is especially in the southern part of Jutland, "where there is very specific interest in the export of hydrogen to Germany and access to hydrogen storage.

Energinet is already working closely with the German gas TSO Gasunie Deutschland on the preparations of a hydrogen connection between Denmark and Germany. "

Title: Bornholm mellem øst og vest - før og nu
Content:
No matter how it goes with the war in Ukraine, it will not change that Russia is a large and unreliable neighboring country that we will in future relate to.

When the Soviet ship Vladimir Polukhin on April 5, 1946 sailed out of Rønne Harbor with the last soldiers from Stalin's Red Army on board, the Bornholmers cheered on the dock. There was a mood of relief.

The Russians had freed Bornholm from German troops - but also insisted on maintaining a peacetime occupation for 11 months.

A feeling of uncertainty in relation to the great Soviet neighbor had spread. As time went on, it was clear that the Danish government had imposed on itself and Bornholm a very special condition to reassure the Soviet Union.

In the often mentioned "Note" from 1946, Denmark had written that in the future it was possible to protect the protection of Bornholm "without any participation of foreign troops". In the context, it was logically enough that it was believed that Soviet troops were no longer needed on Bornholm.

But in the decades thereafter, the note was "over -implemented" and interpreted in the way that there must be no foreign troops on Bornholm - nor soldiers from Denmark's NATO allies from F.

eg the US or UK. This was how Bornholm got the strangely unclear status in Danish security policy thinking, which has advised almost to this day.

The story of the note of 1946 culminated in 1983, when an American military horn orchestra was refused to perform on Bornholm, and the then Social Democratic Minister of Defense Poul Søgaard explained a BT journalist that "Bornholm is not a member of NATO", which caused much debate. The government Poul Schlüter with the flamboyant young Foreign Minister Uffe Ellemann-Jensen at the forefront made up the interpretation of the note when they took office, and in 1985 the disputed Horn orchestra came to the Hareløkkerne.

But it has now turned out that the Danish defense did not fully cope with the interpretation, and that the defense actually had a policy in the area until 2000 that kept foreign forces from here.

Since then, things and things have happened. Not least after Russia's unprovoked and illegal attack war against Ukraine, the security policy focus has changed in the Baltic Sea area. It has also had consequences for Bornholm. Until 1989, Bornholm lay as a lone Nato island in a sea dominated by the Soviet-led military alliance, the Warsaw Pact.

From Dueodde there were only 99 kilometers to the nearest WAPA beach in East Germany.

It was a position that was in many ways insecure, but which was also interesting to NATO. And even though NATO ships did not add in Rønne and Nexø, there were still advanced radar and listening equipment, which was partly set up in the radar head of the rider knee and partly in the "secret" listening tower, which knew at Dueodde's old guy and listened With on WAPA communication all the way to the Carpater Mountains.

Bornholm, of course, has not moved geographically, yet in 2023 we are now in a completely different place on the security policy map of the Baltic Sea. With Germany's reunification and Poland and the Baltic States' connection to NATO, the Bornholmers were in a much less contentious waters. At the same time, the relationship with Russia for a number of years was characterized by not only relaxation but also direct cooperation. The annual Baltops exercise, which in 1971 had begun as an American-led demonstrative NATO sailing into the Baltic Sea to show that it was not the Warsaw Pact in Sea that the Kremlin called for the "Sea of ​​Peace," continued after the fall of the Wall in OSCE NOW with the participation of Swedish, Finnish and Russian units. During the exercise in August 2008, the large Russian landing vessel "Kaliningrad" added to Rønne and landed Russian navy infantry, who practiced with the Danish soldiers on the shooting terrain at Raghammer.

If, from Russian, you had ever seriously thought that the note from 1946 meant that there were no foreign troops on Bornholm, then you would have finally settled with it - one would think. But since Russia's full-tone invasion of Ukraine on February 24, 2022, Russia's ambassador to Denmark, Vladimir Barbin, has been reminded on the "1946 Agreement" on several occasions.

He knows it does not hold in the district court, but by mentioning it, he tries to drive a wedge into the Danish security policy debate in a field of tension, where he knows well that there are still Danes who are in favor of a demilitarization of Bornholm. Barbin has talked directly about the fact that it will increase the level of tension in the Baltic Sea area if, for example, American soldiers come to Bornholm. Here one must point out that it is first and foremost Russia that has increased the level of tension by waging war in our immediate area.

On May 24, 2022, an American C17 Globemaster Transport Fly landed at the Airport in Arnager. Out, two so-called Himars (High Mobility Artillery Rocket System) rolled and demonstrated a simulated firing of less than ten minutes from the aircraft put the wheels on the runway.

Their rockets could theoretically hit Russian bases in Kaliningrad.

The exercise marked a tectonic shift in security policy thinking around Bornholm. From cautious talk about relaxation and endeavor to lower the level of conflict by partially demilitarizing Bornholm, the Danish defense was now active in collaboration with the US to use Bornholm in operations in the Baltic Sea. In time, the Himars Exercise coincided with the announcement that Denmark intended to enter into a bilateral military cooperation with the United States. Since Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen had not specified what the cooperation would mean, more people guessed that there might even be a US military base on Bornholm. It was then found that there was primarily the expansion of logistical support points in the large ports in Esbjerg and Frederikshavn - and thus no base on Bornholm. But the interesting thing was probably how difficult it was to spot some significant resistance in Denmark in general and Bornholm in particular. The Ukraine War has set a new agenda.

In September, the sabotage happened on the two Nordstream pipes east of Bornholm. The explosions took place immediately up to the inauguration of the new gas pipeline Baltic Pipe from Norway to Poland west of Bornholm. Although there is no final evidence yet, it is clear that the sabotage demanded explosives and equipment on such a large scale that it may have been only a state actor behind it. The most likely is that Russia itself was behind and that the attack on hybrid warms should signal that our critical infrastructure is vulnerable.

There has since been some debate about how in the future we should secure the critical infrastructure, such as the energy island west of Bornholm that will help not only secure the green transition, but also to make us independent of Russian gas . Here, Bornholm's geographical location will continue to be an important factor in the future. Should Danish or international strengths in the future protect the energy island based on Bornholm? One can imagine a lot.

No matter how it goes with the war in Ukraine, it will not change that Russia is a large and unreliable neighboring country that we will in future relate to. Although Finland's and soon also Sweden's admission to NATO means that Bornholm is now in a NATO in sea, it is on the basis that Russia continues to consider the crucial superpower in our part of the world.

Title: Energiøen er et bornholmsk mareridt
Content:
There is a need for a referendum on Bornholm so we can find out what the silent majority thinks.

I dream that hopefully I will soon wake up from the nightmare, which unfortunately is becoming reality and discovering that it was all just a dream.

For me, the development that is in the process of Energiø Bornholm is a nightmare that in the long term will destroy the Bornholm we know.

I realize that others see this development as a wet dream as for some, and at the same time is a source of income.

Energiø Bornholm will destroy nature both on sea and on land initially the area south of Aakirkeby, where I unfortunately live.

This project will continue to grow forever because it is driven by the green transition, which in turn is driven by the big capital.

It's not about climate, but about money.

Due to the best good of the public, with the help of the Danish state of the Danish state we own the land we own at a spot price and transform good agricultural land into a giant industrial area with transformers, mast forests and chemical factories, as far as the eye can see.

This area they will then call a crack valley and try to sell it all as better nature than it is now. It screams to the sky and is also helped well on the way by the Danish Nature Conservation Association. (It is also Denmark's and not Bornholm Nature Conservation Association) In the Energiø Nordsø project it is planned to build an artificial island 100 kilometers from country at a price of DKK 10,000 million. Conversely, in the Energiø Bornholm project, there is no advice to buy the land around the transformer station, which would cost around DKK 90 million.

At Bornholm, the Transformer Station is located close to about 20 houses and properties, which will be worthless, and the residents will probably get nuisance such as noise and light and more.

Move the land plant 200-300 meters to the northwest, so that the houses are taken into account along Søndre Landevej and Limensgaden, whether or not these neighbors receive compensation.

A large part of the project must be paid for by Germany, and I think it is incredible that one can use an argument as the public to expropriated land when this project is partly paid for by one or more foreign countries! When this can be done, I don't think the Constitution is worth anything anymore.

At least ownership is worth the right to own, and this development is a lawless Klondike, where huge companies and whole countries are drumming across the people who live here and 'own' the land.

Love that stands in the way of the green transition is called leg spans, and they are removed or dispensed with, and laws that are missing, as compensation to neighbors at giant transformer stations, the Folketing turns a blind eye to, all timed and organized by the government With Mette Fredriksen at the forefront.

Politicians at Bornholm have repeatedly claimed that the silent majority are supporters of the Energiø Bornholm project, but does it fit? There is a need for a referendum on Bornholm so we can find out what the silent majority thinks.

Vote yes to continue the Energiø project without restrictions that now vote no to stop the Energiø project and move the offshore wind turbines to the North Sea.

You will be able to see the difference between the offshore wind farm in the North Sea, whether there are 10,000 wind turbines as planned, or 10,250 wind turbines including them from Bornholm.

When I don't have a nightmare, I dream of like Jens Stubkjær wrote the other day! The big dreams that the yes side has for Bornholm like Energiø, have too high a price, and the fact that we cannot afford to say no is a nonsense.

Whether we get money from Denmark in the form of grants or as part of the power sale, it is Denmark that decides how much money we get and if the Energiø project is going to provide a large deficit, you can only guess , how it will affect the Bornholm economy.

When something sounds too good to be true it is because it is, and when we are promised a lot of new jobs, it can also become a problem for already existing companies that will be missing labor to an even greater extent than now.

If you, dear reader, are part of the silent majority, remember that the next transformer station or power-to-X system may be in your backyard, you live on an energy island.

Because you don't think the land plant in South Bornholm will be the last? One is tempted to dream of opting out of Denmark.

Title: Tilfreds Trøst ser flere løfter i havvindaftalen
Content:
The parties behind the new offshore wind agreement have committed to return to the questions of compensation to the municipality and to the neighbors to the energy island's land facility, says Mayor Jacob Trøst. If it was only empty words, they would not have been written into the deal, he says.

At first glance, there is some way between the new political agreement on offshore wind turbines, including Energiø Bornholm - and the wishes that Mayor Jacob Trøst (K) on behalf of Bornholm had played in at Christiansborg.

However, this is not how the mayor even looks at the broad deal that was landed on Tuesday night.

- I'm relieved and happy. We have succeeded in landing an agreement where I think there has also been some of the elements that we have come up with from Bornholm's side. The agreement is a big and important step. In relation to lobbying, I think the agreement shows that we put the right effort at the right time, says Jacob Solvet.

- It has been written into the agreement that you continue to work with local and municipal compensation in relation to the land plant.

There are also a number of other things that we have played in with, he says.

- There will be a social commitment to take apprentices, and nature is also taken into account with the Harbor Fund of DKK 500 million, which will strengthen our marine environment. And then it is also written in the agreement that work is being done on connecting Bornholm's electricity network on the energy island.

- The focus is also on the energy island of ensuring Denmark's position as a leader in green technology.

You can see that there is a major focus on the innovation and business part that DTU and Ørsted and other large companies have already started. Some new technologies need to be developed, and some of them have to be developed on Bornholm, says Jacob Trøst.

After the interview with Jacob Trøst, Bornholm Tidende has been clarified in the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Supply, that in the state's offering of the offshore wind turbines to Energiø Bornholm will not be the same requirement to restore nature and marine environment that the state will provide in its tenders offshore wind elsewhere.

"The parties have committed" Possible compensation to both the country's neighbors and to the regional municipality, where the energy island will soon provide a great need to build and invest, with the new agreement will be made part of an upcoming Christiansborg negotiation - to follow Up on the "Climate Agreement on Green Power and Heating 2022".

What would you say to those who read the agreement's wording about compensation to the municipality and the neighbors and about connecting Bornholm's electricity grid on the energy island as birds on the roof without any concrete promises? - If it was only that, the things wouldn't have been written into the deal. The fact that the parties write those things into the agreement also obliges them to work on them, says Jacob Consolation.

The agreement talks about "Possible compensation related to land facilities on Bornholm" and "Possible initiatives for local and municipal support". Surely it is not a guarantee that something is actually coming? - This is how it is with all projects. For me, the biggest and most important step is that it is written into the agreement that one undertakes to find a solution.

Why didn't that solution come yesterday? - I think in that case you would go down to a degree of details that there was no room for in the first place. The things that we are still missing belong to in phase 2 after the big frames came yesterday, says Jacob Consolation.

Uncertain economy filled a lot while the parties negotiated the agreement on the upcoming offshore wind turbines, new forecasts for the economy in Energiø Bornholm showed that the project will probably result in a potential up to DKK 60 billion over 20 years.

This meant that a large part of the negotiations on the Bornholm part of the offshore wind agreement was about just pushing a better economy into Energiø Bornholm. The parties of the agreement landed on the amount DKK 17.6 billion to cover the costs of the land plant and the cables to Zealand and Germany.

Jacob Trøsten expects the uncertain project economy to also mean less room to talk about the specific wishes that Bornholm had played into the negotiations.

- I am aware that the project economy in the energy island has been a focal point in the negotiations. And it is clear that you will remove the focus from some other things when you have a lot of focus on the project economy, he says.

So what will happen now and what is the municipality doing now? - From the municipality we continue to work on getting the local plan in place for the land facility. Around housing, it was not possible to include our desire for permanent housing in the agreement. So we continue our normal work in relation to housing on Bornholm.

Were you really nervous that the entire energy island could be taken off the table? - I won't say that. I was convinced that this project and the whole green transition was something you wanted, and you can't do that without Energiø Bornholm, says Jacob Trøst.

- The numbers here made me lift an eyebrow, but when I noticed in my stomach, I still thought it would succeed. When I noticed, I believed that the project economy was a stone on the road that we could well drive around.

I am relieved and happy.

We have succeeded in landing an agreement where I think there has also been some of the elements that we have come up with from Bornholm's side Jacob Trøst (K), mayor.

Title: Bornholmsk nøglespiller frygtede at energiøen ville blive skrottet
Content:
Energiø Bornholm had been taken off the table if the parties behind the offshore wind agreement had not found 17.6 billion to shoot in, says Baltic Energy Island's director, who stands by being nervous while the parties were negotiating.

- Energiø Bornholm is saved with the agreement here.

This is stated by Søren Møller Christensen, director of the Baltic Energy Island consortium, where Beof, Rønne Harbor and the municipality work with, among others, DTU and Ørsted to use the energy island to develop new solutions that can ultimately create a new energy system worldwide.

Do you look at it that the energy island has been truly threatened? - Yes. If the agreement here had not been landed, there would have been no finances in the project, and then Energiø Bornholm would not come.

So the good and the big thing in the agreement is that the parties have been together on an economic model that one expects to be able to secure Energiø Bornholm were you really nervous that the energy island would go to the floor? - I was nervous about two things: about the uncertainty that has been created about the project economy - and of whether there would be parties that stepped out of the deal. It is an agreement that extends over many years, so the more parties that are included, the safer the agreement, says Søren Møller Christensen.

- I would not say that I have been extremely nervous, but I have been nervous.

But I have also had a belief that there would still be a large majority behind the energy island, also because it is important for the 2030 goal, he says.

Important extra wind turbines in practice were doubted whether Energiø Bornholm would be realized or dropped created by the fact that new forecasts for the energy island's project economy during the negotiations showed likely large billion deficits.

- We have been waiting for how the parties will deal with the challenges that have proven to be with the project economy in Energiø Bornholm. The challenges have been solved with the agreement in a way that all the parties are still involved, says Søren Møller Christensen.

- It has also been written into the agreement that the parties recognize the need for local support around Energiø Bornholm, and that compensation must be negotiated for the neighbors. It is a great gift for the work that the municipality has done, he says.

Søren Møller Christensen sees it as very important for Bornholm that in addition to the energy island's planned 3 gigawatts, 800 megawatts are also offered extra capacity from additional offshore wind turbines off Bornholm.

The extra wind turbines go in offshore wind language under the name "Overplanting". With the new deal, the originally planned 600 megawatts grew in overplanting to 800 megawatts from offshore wind turbines, which will be set up by 2032.

The additional 800 megawatts are offered on purely commercial terms without state aid.

The 800 extra megawatts are being converted into hydrogen or other green fuels and thus become a new Bornholm based industry on a large scale.

-The extra 200 megawatts in overplanting increase the possibility of getting financially sustainable production of power-to-x, says Søren Møller Christensen.

- Whether the extra capacity must be connected to the hydrogen line to Germany or used as green fuel for ships in a bunker hub, the increased volume means a better opportunity to create a sustainable economy out of overplant. This is important because the wind turbines in the overplant must be set up without state aid, he says.

Also as a citizen of Bornholm, Søren Møller Christensen is pleased with the new agreement on offshore wind. Even though the agreement does not contain anything concrete about neither compensation for neighbors nor to the municipality - or any firm guarantee that the Bornholm electricity grid will be linked to the energy island.

- Work continues. You have been able to get something through with this agreement, and it has always been clear that we could get some things in the agreement on the supply of offshore wind, and that there would be some things that we can hope to get with in later agreements, says Søren Møller Christensen.

- If the project economy in the energy island had not been challenged, there would probably have been more focus on the other things that did not come up with. But there are also limits to how many political agendas you can travel at once.

If the agreement here had not been landed, there would have been no finances in the project, and then Energiø Bornholm would not come.

Søren Møller Christensen, director of Baltic Energy Island.

Title: Fond bag ny brintrapport har kæmpestore ambitioner på Bornholm
Content:
Electrolysis on Bornholm on a larger scale than previously mentioned is included in the CIP Foundation's new report on a future Danish hydrogen infrastructure.

The CIP Foundation comes in a detailed report with a bid for the brint infrastructure of the future. The biggest plans are in the North Sea, but Bornholm plays a larger supporting role in the mapping by 2045 that the Energy Fund Company has presented on Wednesday.

At the Bornholm, the CIP Foundation recommends that four gigawatts (GW) electrolysis be established and that the hydrogen is transported from here to Germany. About 6 GW of offshore wind must be used for an electrolysis system of 4 GW, the CIP Foundation writes in the report. Thus, it will require that around Bornholm be installed offshore wind farms that are twice as large as Energiø Bornholm's capacity if the hydrogen vision is to be realized.

In the overall plan, Power-to-X capacity on Bornholm is seven percent of the total Danish hydrogen production, of which 90 percent must be exported abroad-first and foremost to Germany, the Netherlands and Belgium.

Poland and parts of Sweden may also need an import Danish hydrogen, the CIP Foundation estimates.

Title: Er 17,6 milliarder nok? Statsstøtten er meget lavere end energiøens forventede projektunderskud
Content:
The Ministry of Climate, Energy and Supply estimates in a note from April that the need for state aid in most scenarios is over DKK 30 billion and that the installation of offshore wind turbines does not appear to be profitable. Despite the uncertainty, Green Power Denmark's Kristian Jensen and Lea Wermelin (S) believe that energy companies will be interested in offering the giant project.

17.6 billion kroner. This is the maximum amount that the state will provide over a 20-year period in support of the bidders of Energiø Bornholm's offshore wind farms. Although the support seems great, it is far from certain that the billions will be enough to secure the construction of the energy island.

The Ministry of Climate, Energy and Supply, assessed in a note from April 26, which the Journal has gained access to the fact that the need for support in the scenario on which the Ministry itself emphasizes will be DKK 31.5 billion.

Thus, there is almost DKK 14 billion in the difference between the assessment and the adopted state aid.

The deficit for the project economy in the main scenario is admittedly "just" DKK 16.3 billion. In the calculation, however, a premise has been included that the offenses of offshore winds must have a return of three to four percent a year, and when this is recognized with a discount, the support need increases to DKK 31.5 billion.

The Ministry has made four scenarios in the memo, and only in one of them is state aid needs lower than DKK 17.6 billion.

The big question that can probably only be answered when the tender round is over in 2024 is whether the energy companies are interested in offering Energiø Bornholm with these financial conditions.

The Journal has asked the question to Kristian Jensen, CEO of Green Power Denmark, which represents the energy industry.

-There is an opportunity, but no guarantee when the parties to the agreement have put a ceiling on the support, says the former Left Minister, who is today a top lobbyist.

Technological carrot he expects that despite the support ceiling, there will be interest in erecting the energy island.

- I believe that there will be companies that will bid with three gigawatts, says Kristian Jensen.

The energy island becomes the first of its kind.

Do you think that the opportunity to gain experience with new technology increases interest among energy companies to offer the task? - I think so clearly. One can see that the interest in energy islands is spreading to other countries.

Will it also make companies more willing to run a financial risk? - I think they would like to be risk -averse because they can gain some experience that will be able to increase their future earnings, says Kristian Jensen.

Total Energi's, which operates many Danish oil and gas fields in the North Sea and plans investment in green energy, has expressed an interest in the energy island and the other offshore winds.

- Immediately we are interested in the whole thing, but it is clear that Energiø Bornholm is in a category for itself, says Betina Jørgensen, director of renewable energy development, to the Exchange with reference to the energy island with the technological solution is an innovative project.

It is sufficient the parties behind the agreement have decided that "if there is no bid to establish offshore wind under the stipulated support ceiling, the project will not be realized". In that case, DKK 1.2 billion will have been wasted if the project falls to the ground.

LEA WERMELIN (S), like Kristian Jensen, believes that the support from the state is sufficient.

- My clear expectation is that with this agreement we will get both the energy island and up to 14 gigawatt offshore winds in total, says Energy and the climate rapporteur to the Journal.

She emphasizes the great uncertainty in the Ministry's figures.

- The calculations are not chopped in stone. There are a large number of assumptions behind, including the electricity price in 10, 20 and 30 years, says Wermelin.

State aid goes only to cover the bidders' expenses for infrastructure and sustainability measures, but not the actual set -up of the mills, emphasizes Lea Wermelin.

- We have placed as a premise that the offshore wind is support -free.

Never any doubt Tidende makes her aware that the Ministry of the Support Note has calculated that the cost of establishing and operating the parks is drawing to be less than the revenue from electricity sales - even before the expectation of a return is counted.

"The results indicate that the offshore wind is expected to generate a deficit," the note states.

Lea Wermelin has the hope that the next few years will show that this assessment does not scare potential bidders away. Among other things, the strong belief in the project she picks up in the many applications for new offshore wind projects that private companies sent to the Danish Energy Agency last year.

- The industry is tripping to build offshore wind farms on purely commercial conditions, says Lea Wermelin.

- And if we don't succeed, we have to meet and talk about it.

Was it during the negotiations to give up Energiø Bornholm completely? - For me and the Social Democracy, there was never any doubt that the energy island should turn into something, says Lea Wermelin about the party's position in the negotiations.

How did the other parties look at it? - You have to ask them.

The social economy Wider economic calculations of the project show that it is most likely that Energiø Bornholm will end up giving a negative social economy.

When the benefits are recognized - for example, cheaper electricity for consumers and earnings of approximately DKK 6 billion to energy in electricity - the socio -economic result is significantly better than the project economy with a range of minus DKK 16 billion to plus DKK 4 billion - with a deficit of seven billion kroner as the most likely outcome.

In the socio -economic figures, factors are lacking that are difficult to translate into figures but are important for the project. These include climate effects, environmental effects and security of supply, the ministry writes in the note.

- We must remember that although we can become independent of Russian gas, our security is not saved by it if the Germans are dependent.

Therefore, there is a greater perspective in this agreement than the narrow individual park's socio-economic gain, says Climate, Energy and Supply Minister Lars Aagaard (M) to the Exchange.


A greener Europe

The numerically hidden benefits also highlight both Lea Wermelin and Kristian Jensen when they speak for the energy island. Both point that the energy island with the foreign connection to Germany will be important for the efforts to create a greener Europe.

At the same time, Kristian Jensen emphasizes that an expansion of the electricity infrastructure between Zealand and Germany was in any case necessary, and this should be remembered in the assessment of Energiø Bornholm.

When asked by the Journal, Kristian Jensen says that he has the impression that during the negotiations it has been considered to drop Energiø Bornholm because of the financial uncertainty. However, he welcomes the fact that politicians did not choose to blow the plans.

- If you did not do a wind turbine project on Bornholm, you should still make an international connection between Zealand and Germany. This is also why it is a good idea to make Energiø Bornholm, says Green Power Denmark's director.

He does not find it worrying that the Bornholm project is not viable on purely commercial conditions, which one expects the other offshore wind farms from the tender agreement to be. Kristian Jensen compares it to if you also include expenses for all the gas stations along the road.

- There are simply more costs, he says of the Energiø project.

- I think they would like to be at risk because they can gain some experience that will be able to increase their future earnings Kristian Jensen CEO, Green Power Denmark, about energy companies' interest in Energiø Bornholm.


Profitability and state aid in numbers

The project economy depends on the development of the electricity market. If the electricity price becomes high, the support needs can be lower.
