Title: Her er fremtidens sikkerhed for Bornholm
Content:
Security has been significantly changed for Bornholm. We should not fear Russian invasion, but a whole new threat from Russia, says former Rear Admiral Nils Wang and director of Navalteam.

The Cold War is back and we should soon secure Bornholm militarily against a Russian invasion. This is how it regularly sounds from defense analysts and experts in the public security and defense policy debate. Such an invasion involves a not insignificant risk to the striker, so that the view assumes that Bornholm actually plays a central role for Russia in the military strategic geography that the country is now and for many years to come with in the Baltic Sea.

Although the confrontation between Russia and NATO can evoke memories of the Cold War that any of us can remember, today we are in a completely different situation. Therefore, the Cold War analogy can -at best unconsciously -to conclude to conclusions and military solutions that do not fit into the current operational reality.

Among other things, the war in Ukraine has provoked that Finland and soon Sweden have joined NATO, and that the countries around the Baltic Sea generally erupt violently at the same time as Russia dislikes its economic and military strength in Ukraine. This means that the military geography and the future strength of our region look significantly different than it did before February 24 last year. Of course, it also has an impact on the threat picture that NATO and the Danish kingdom are facing - also on Bornholm.

First of all, it is important to state that Russia's military ability to conquer and maintain large land territories distant from Russia's own borders at no time - nor before the invasion of Ukraine last year - has been close to the invasion threat, the former The Soviet Union constituted.

Reinforcements from the United States It has already taken off the cutlery, so the Russian military set -up on what is called 'NATO's East Flank', ie the border between Russia and the Baltic countries including Kaliningrad Oblast, primarily poses an immediate military threat to the Baltic Countries. Russia knows well that an invasion of these countries will trigger a war with NATO, which will, if necessary, create an immediate need for the alliance to quickly get reinforcements from the United States. These reinforcements must first be sailed across the North Atlantic, where they can become the target of the Russian northern fleet in the waters between East Greenland and Iceland as well as between Iceland, the Faroe Islands and the UK - the so -called 'Giuk -Gap' (abbreviation of Greenland, Iceland UK GAP) - and then they must be able to pass on via marching areas in Danish ports such as Esbjerg and Aarhus. The last part of the journey will for much part take place on ships from Denmark to the eastern part of the Baltic Sea.

And this is where the Russian missile arsenal in Kaliningrad Oblast comes into the equation.

As long as this missile threat is intact, it will be associated with a very high risk partly to set up the reinforcing forces in Danish ports and partly to transport soldiers and valuable material across the Baltic Sea. NATO will therefore be forced to fight for maneuver freedom at sea in that scenario, which in turn requires superiority in the airspace. In military terminology, the Russian set -up is called "A2/ AD", which stands for "Anti Access/ Area Denial". Together with Russia's military strength of strength along NATO's east flank, it sends a clear message to the ATO: that Russia, if it will, can conquer the Baltic countries in whole or in part, and that NATO will subsequently find it difficult to create the freedom of movement at sea that is a prerequisite for the military strength building that is needed to recapture the lost territory.


Deterrence and risk

NATO's response to the Russian threat has been under construction for some years and has been accelerated after Russia's invasion of Ukraine last year. Setting up troops in the Baltic countries from a number of NATO countries, including Denmark, must both reinforce the defense there and make it unequivocally that a Russian attack on one or more of the Baltic countries will be an attack on the entire alliance. At the same time, NATO increases the presence in both the Baltic Sea area and the North Atlantic through extensive exercise activities.

All in the effort to create a credible conventional military deterrence, which everyone of course hopes can prevent a war between Russia and NATO.

Whether the deterrence will actually be perceived as credible and thus will work as intended no one can know. But after the war in Ukraine, it will take some time before Russia establishes military and financial surplus to carry out an actual deliberate military attack on a NATO country. Therefore, it is far more likely that an actual military conflict between Russia and NATO is accidentally started.

It can happen as part of Russia's often very risky response to NATO's presence, for example when Russian fighter jets fly very close to NATO's aircraft and ships, or when Russian warships and aircraft deliberately violate Danish territory at Bornholm and have to be rejected.

What we, on the other hand, can be absolutely sure of is that in the years to come, Russia will continue the so -called hybrid warfare against NATO, which takes place in the gray zone between crisis and war, which targets our digital and physical infrastructure. The attack on the Nordstream gas lines in the Baltic Sea and the general systematic Russian mapping of our critical maritime infrastructure is merely illustrations that ". Formerly clear thresholds between peace, crisis and war have been replaced by blurred and overlapping transitions", as the Defense Intelligence Service expresses it in The latest risk assessment.

So what is Denmark's military role in the construction of this conventional military deterrence, and where does it leave Bornholm? The Arctis The government has publicly stated that the Arctic part of the Kingdom should be prioritized on the basis that the concentration of NATO forces is greatest in the Baltic Sea region. In other words, Denmark can play a relatively larger military role for the alliance and the United States in that part of NATO's area of ​​interest, including the part of Giuk-Gap located in the waters between the East Coast of Greenland and Iceland. This means, among other things, that Denmark must invest in ships, helicopters and drones that can find and harm the Russian nuclear underwater boats in this complicated waters with polar ice as well as extreme weather conditions with a high risk of icing. Today, there are no ice-reinforced anti-submarine frigates in NATO, so it will be quite natural for Denmark to provide this capacity when we still have to patrol this waters for sovereignty reasons. In addition, these ships with the right radar systems will also be able to create some of the long -range airspace surveillance that is today completely absent in the area.

Critical maritime infrastructure following the attacks on Nordstream I and II gas lines in the Baltic Sea close to Bornholm has also come to a considerable political awareness of how vulnerable we are if we leave our critical maritime infrastructure unattended and unprotected. It will require very large investments that can only be overcome in a collaboration between the defense, the defense industry and the industry that owns the infrastructure. The green transition will only increase the vulnerability in the coming years with a significant increase in offshore wind turbines and the establishment of energy islands for many billions. In these future plans, Bornholm also plays a significant role as an energy hub for offshore wind farms and as a natural energy island in the Baltic Sea that can transform electricity into green fuels.

The missile threat in the Baltic Sea Finland's and soon Sweden's entry into NATO, as mentioned, affects the strength of the strength in the Baltic Sea region of NATO's favor.

When it comes to the missile threat to Denmark, however, there is not much help to get here. A missile shot from the forests of Kaliningrad Oblast towards Copenhagen or Flyvestation Skrydstrup passes neither Sweden nor other allied nations. It, on the other hand, flies over water all the way, and the fastest of the kind travels the route to the capital or Skrydstrup in minutes.

So where neighboring countries like Poland and Germany can establish an effective geographically layered air defense on land, we need to place our advanced air defense on ships in the Baltic if we are to hope to fight the threat effectively. On the short horizon, we should take advantage of the fact that we already have three frigates that, with the right long -range missiles (which are not the ones we are currently equipping them with) and the right sensors will be able to solve this task.

However, these ships are also in demand for a number of other tasks outside the Baltic Sea, so that the more long -term solution is that the patrol vessels that are considered acquired is equipped for this task.

These ships must be at sea in the Danish waters around the clock, including monitoring the critical maritime infrastructure in the waters around Bornholm.

Therefore, it will be logical to equip them so that they can at the same time act as missile launch ramps for our national air surgery center as we get geographical depth in our national air defense.

However, air defense on ships and ashore is only the defensive component air defense of Denmark and in the battle for freedom of movement in the Baltic Sea. If the deterrence fails and NATO has to start recovering lost territory in the Baltic States, then it is important to destroy as many of the Russian missiles with associated command and control structure as soon as possible before leaving firing and depots. It requires offensive long-range precision weapons in the form of aircraft and ship-based kneeweapers, with which the US Tomahawk missile, which has a great bursting power and fits into the missile launchers that our frigates are already equipped with. This capacity is not found in the region today.

It will immediately be tempting to use Bornholm for these long -range offensive and defensive weapons, but partly the mobility and ability to solve other tasks will be greater with a ship -based solution, and partly a land -based solution will require disproportionate amount of resources for self -protection and finally it will In itself, increase the likelihood of missile attack against Bornholm in the initial stages of a possible. conflict.


The basic component of deterrence

Denmark must also be able to contribute to the basic component of the deterrence, namely the advanced NATO presence with land troops on NATO's east flank.

It assumes that we get the finished and manned 1. Here Bornholm will continue to play a significant role as a garrison for parts of the brigade and for the part of the Home Guard, which must, among other things, be able to solve guarding tasks, including those that arise as Bornholm develops as an energy hub.

The biggest potential risk of Bornholm in the new security policy situation in the Baltic Sea is that the island gets a central location in the green energy structure, which is under development in this part of the Baltic Sea. Thus, it must be foreseen that Bornholm and the surrounding waters be particularly exposed to the previously mentioned hybrid threat from Russia, which we have already seen in different contexts.

In relation to a decidedly military invasion threat, it is important to note that Bornholm in the new NATO geography is in a corridor consisting of NATO countries. Thus, it will be associated with a significant risk if Russia tries to conquer and keep a territory so far to the west. If so, it will be far more effective to challenge Denmark's and thus NATO's control over access to the Baltic Sea by offensive mining of the Danish streets from ships and/ or aircraft.

In other words, Bornholm does not face an immediate invasion threat, and the island's strategic significance is primarily related to the role of Bornholm in connection with the green transition.


Where do we dream?

Where do we dream? Under that headline, Tidende puts together with Baltic Bridge, Lag-Bornholm, CRT and the Bornholm Citizens' Association's Collaboration in a number of debates.

The third is with the theme of defense and is about Bornholm's future security. The theme ends with a debate salon on Tuesday, June 21 at 4.30 pm.

Title: CRT: Bornholm kan tjene stort på at blive et grønt laboratorie
Content:
The energy island opens up for everyone at Bornholm to participate in testing new green solutions. If Bornholm chooses to become a so -called Living Lab, it will bring companies, experts, the municipality and the citizens into a close and unprecedented cooperation that can bring Bornholm to the front worldwide, says a new report.

The upcoming Energiø will be built out with a business park of green energy companies.

There is a majority in the municipal council, and therefore Bornholm will now work that way.

But Bornholm can also go further.

Bornholm can also seek to become a leader worldwide by turning into "an open, living experiment on full social scale, where experts, professionals, businesses and citizens are included as active actors and partners in the development and commissioning of solutions for the sustainable community of the future." It tells the report "Testø Bornholm 2.0 - Possible Perspective for a further development of Bornholm as a test -and development environment for green energy and technology", which Bornholm -based Center for Regionalog Tourism Research (CRT) has just published.

"The foundation is the testing and demonstration of energy technology. But the activities are expanded and deals with development, testing and documentation of all sorts of green solutions on the basis of the opportunities that Energy Island provides, for example in agriculture and food, health care, transport system, tourism, construction and recycling of garbage, "CRT describes in the report the so -called scenario 3 about the whole of Bornholm as a living Laboratory.

Bornholm's framework is unique knowledge brought into Bornholm can be spread out worldwide, because Bornholm at the same time is a whole society with all functions - and a limited society with far to the nearest neighbor.

With huge amounts of green energy and surplus heat from the energy island available, Bornholm will be able to attract both companies and research institutions and become home to a test environment that is not found anywhere else. And there is both demand and need for the kind of test environment that Bornholm can go after to become, according to CRT's report.

"The case studies have clearly shown a great, continued need for testing and development environments in Denmark. They have also shown that the development of these environments is the only way to go if one wants to succeed in a real green transition, not least due to uncertainties linked For future energy forms and systems, "this is called.

"The need for test and demonstration activities is especially linked to technology companies' need to be able to document the usefulness and security of new technologies as part of export." "For Bornholm, it is therefore important to be on the wave both nationally, but also locally, where with the right approach there are good opportunities to develop as a pioneer example in other local communities' green transition," CRT also writes in the report.

If Bornholm chooses to go that way, part of the art of getting the new role as one big green laboratory will be naturally growing out of the existing Bornholm.

"At the same time, it is important that the development in the coming years is linked to the island's general place development, which is a very important and priority factor on Bornholm and among the island's population," CRT also writes.


Three main roads to go

Bornholm is test island already today. For the past 15 years, BEOF has worked closely with DTU, so that all of the Bornholm electricity consumption, for example, can be followed at any time on the DTU platform Powerlabdk. With funds from not least the EU in the back, DTU and BEOF have also launched other projects.

It has been done without many at Bornholm noticing it and thinking about it. The fact that the previous collaboration between DTU and BEOF continues largely unchanged in the CRT report called "Scenario 1". The energy island can enlarge the collaboration a bit, but not to an extent that makes the activities of testing energy technologies a new engine for growth.

In CRT's scenario 2, the energy island is built out with a business park, where green companies and institutions in research are located side by side and work closely together near the energy island's land plant.

This is the path that the municipal council has just laid out the first tracks - and will, according to CRT, require a "new, more targeted commercial organization". According to CRT, pursuing the possibilities of the business park will also require "political prioritization and financial initiative as well as a management and framework that is not yet found on Bornholm".

"The goal of the collaboration is to realize (possibly specified parts of) The technological potentials provided by the elements of the energy island, for example the development of a complete sustainable and circular energy and supply system on Bornholm," writes CRT about the Business Park scenario.

"The perspective is to develop and shape the future energy development on the island, but at the same time contributing to national and international development needs in the energy sector." In the scenario, the business park will be linked to the energy island's plants and systems. CRT expects the development to lead "new actors" to Bornholm "because of the special, advanced test environment".

Bornholm companies will also become more involved here, but the scenario with the Business Park will still be most attractive to "relatively few but technologically and business closely related actors".

According to CRT, Bornholm must choose scenario 3 and the living laboratory before the Bornholm business community can benefit from it in a broad sense. Only here can "not only companies in the energy field on Bornholm, but in principle all companies on the island with an interest in sustainable development are involved".

According to CRT, the three scenarios do not exclude each other, but overlap.

Bornholm can thus choose to pursue parts of the different scenarios.

Lasting growth requires will CRT director Anne Thomas announces that the energy island will first bring lasting and significant growth if Bornholm goes further and builds the living laboratory on beyond the green business park near the land plant.

A green business park will create new jobs.

But at the island level, Anne Thomas expects the number of new jobs to go big right up with the jobs that the green transition will cost.

- What really gives effect to Bornholm's business community is that Bornholm also goes into scenario 3 about the living laboratory.

This is where the really big opportunities are.

But it is also a slightly muddy way because no one has walked it before. But should I choose, I would start scenario 2 about the business park and then keep a close eye on scenario 3, says Anne Thomas.

The living laboratory has never been tried anywhere in the world. Is it over your head realistic? - Scenario 2 with the Business Park comes by itself. Scenario 3 with Living Lab comes only if we're enough that believe it.

If, on the other hand, one says "we do not believe it," it becomes a self -fulfilling prophecy.

- Not wanting to go for scenario 3 is a boring alternative, because the green transition comes no matter what. Green taxes are coming and it will be more expensive to drive a car. It's coming. So the sooner Bornholm takes scenario 3, the faster we will be on the development wave that will also come, says Anne Thomas.

How big is the potential for Bornholm? - We just did not count on it because the size of the potential is so uncertain.

But I will turn it around and say that with the energy island Bornholm can reach the 42,000 inhabitants.

- If we do not go for scenario 3 with Living Lab, we must expect some jobs to disappear because the new jobs that come will go straight up with the jobs that disappear in the climate -exposed professions, says Anne Thomas.

- We have calculated the jobs that there are 3,000 of on Bornholm, and some of the jobs will disappear. If we need more than just replace the jobs that disappear, we need to start scenario 3 and Living Lab.

Much becomes imperceptible CRT's director does not expect people at Bornholm to get an extra source of income from living in the living laboratory from Scenario 3.

- No, I don't think so. But I think we can expect the companies that will come to Bornholm will be high -productive, so that both wages and house prices will rise. The homeowners will be able to feel it. But we should not imagine that we will be paid to have a dipping down in our house, says Anne Thomas.

Being part of an island-wide green laboratory will not necessarily be noticeable, intrusive or something that you will think about.

About 2,000 Bornholmers have already had part of the experience as they made their heater available to researchers and practitioners in the so-called Ecogrid project.

- Some Bornholmers have already been part of the work with Ecogrid and had different fogs installed. We do not have to be aware of a large part of the test activities, says Anne Thomas.

- It may be mostly something that we notice when we are outside Bornholm.

We will notice the difference over because we will have started with some solutions that have not reached everyone yet. This is equivalent to the fact that people from the outside notice that we have not yet come as far as sorting our garbage as they are, she says.

Not only can the municipality can both the green business park in scenario 2 and not least the superstructure with the living laboratory in scenario 3 will require much of the municipality, which is already pressed and will soon look into another savings budget. - Yes, the municipality can do well. At least I am now experiencing a significantly greater agreement and a greater commitment. Some balls are already in play. The municipality is now starting to redefine the energy strategy, the planning strategy and the education strategy, says Anne Thomas.

- It requires an investment and it also requires a new way of thinking of business development. In order to get the full benefit, the Business Center Bornholm must work closely with clusters of companies that are not just single companies. And then one has to think about recruiting certain types of companies.

- But the municipality cannot stand alone with it. It requires the state to be behind as well. Now the state will be co -owner of the Energy Islands, and then there must also be some state commitment to the big extra tasks that the energy island brings with it for Bornholm.

- You can expect the municipality to be the task of adult. But it will be unreasonable to expect the municipality to lift the task alone, says Anne Thomas.

It also does not stop with neither the municipality nor the state. At the very different end, according to Anne Thomas, it is also up to the individual Bornholmer to fully fold the great potential.

- It requires many at Bornholm to ask themselves "Where am I myself in the green transition?", She says.

- There are lots of dreams in the local communities, we can also see. But it is struggling with the forces and means to lift those dreams.

Some of the forces and means can be added here.

What really gives effect to Bornholm's business community is that Bornholm also goes into scenario 3 about the living laboratory.

This is where the really big opportunities are.

But it is also a slightly muddy way because no one has walked it before. But should I choose, I would start scenario 2 about the business park and then keep a close eye on scenario 3.

Anne Thomas, director of CRT.

This week all the parties of the Folketing have entered into an agreement on Denmark's first sea plan. It has been a long time, but in 11 hours the total area, which is laid out as zones for renewable energy, doubles from 15 to 30 percent.

One of the new areas lies southeast of Bornholm and wraps around Dueodde at a good distance from the coast. To the west, the energy zone borders the easternmost part of Energiø Bornholm.

With the agreement, new areas are allocated in the Baltic Sea for wind farms at Bornholm and east of Falster. Also in the Kattegat and Skagerrak, the energy zones are expanded compared to previous proposals for the sea plan, but all these additions pale in comparison with the large triangle more than 100 kilometers out in the North Sea, which has also been included in the plan. Politicians emphasize that the energy of the future should preferably be set up far from land.

"Thus, planning is done for the future offshore wind, based on the sake of coastal nature, primarily outside the coastal areas," the parties wrote in the agreement.

The sea plan also sets the point for most of the open door projects that energy companies have wanted to establish without competition and payment to the state.

Title: Kommunen risikerer at svigte klimaplanen
Content:
Let's not be so blinded by the major energy projects that we forget to think the climate holistically.

Dear Municipal Council.

With great amazement and concern, we have followed the development of the approval of Bornholm's Climate Plan, which was dealt with in the Nature, Environment and Planning Committee on June 8.

With this letter, we want to direct a warning index finger against the municipal council and encourage you to ensure that the proposed climate plan not only becomes empty words, but is followed up by necessary financial resources and action.

Bornholm Regional Municipality has an obligation to approve the climate plan, which we have entered into as part of the cross -municipal cooperation "dk2020 climate plans for all". It is crucial that we as a municipality live up to our obligations and show our commitment to tackling the climate challenges. A approval of the climate plan is not only a symbolic step, but a concrete act that shows our willingness to act to create a Bright Green Island.

However, we are deeply troubled by the lack of mention of the climate plan and that the necessary funding is not at risk of being adequately met.

Without adequate funding, the climate plan will be doomed to fail and it will be a bankruptcy declaration for our municipality.

We live in a time when Bornholm is playing a key role in the development of large-scale offshore wind farms and the ambitious Energiø project. It is an impressive initiative that we as a municipality should be proud of. But let's not be so dazzled by these projects that we forget to think the climate holistically.

The climate is about more than just energy production; It also includes transport, food, circular economy and many other aspects that the climate plan just addresses.

We can't just focus on energy and forget about everything else. We must see the climate challenges in a wider context and take care of them in all areas of our society. The climate plan is precisely a tool that helps us do this. It guides us towards sustainable transport, promotes circular economy and supports the development of a more climate -friendly food system.

Therefore, we encourage the municipal council to give the climate plan the necessary priority and resources. We need to see action behind our words and ensure that Bornholm remains a luminous green island and an example of other communities.

Title: Energinets nye planer sendes i høring efter markante ændringer
Content:
The area for the land plant and cables on Bornholm has been narrowed, and at the same time Energinet has decided to collect two submarine cables for one and move the Zealand high -voltage station. Due to the major changes, the Danish Environmental Protection Agency sends the environmental assessment to Energiø Bornholm in consultation again.

Since Energiø Bornholm was most recently in public consultation in late 2022, Energinet has narrowed the areas on Sydbornholm, where it is a matter of laying cables and constructing the large land plant. Therefore, the Danish Environmental Protection Agency is now conducting a supplementary consultation before working on environmental assessment of the huge construction project.

Energinet suggests that five cable routes should be examined more closely. The three western routes are possible connections from the land facility to Zealand. The westernmost cable route is west of Sose Odde, while the other two are in Sose Bay. To the Journal, Energinet informs that cables will only be put in one of the three corridors, and the upcoming studies will be used to find the most suitable connection.

It was previously planned that two submarine cables should go from Energiø Bornholm to Zealand, but it has now been decided to collect the power in one cable system of 1.2 gigawatts. Thus, both on land and on the seabed, only one cable grave must be established.

"Energinet is in dialogue with the landowners who can get a cable buried on their land," Energinet writes.

Almost twice as much power must be transported to Germany as to Zealand. However, the cable routes from Bornholm to Germany are not included in the current consultation. The whole exercise will repeat itself when it is time to environmentally assess the German cable connection.

The two corridors farthest to the east - a little west of the stalls - are for the cables, which go from the offshore wind farms to the land plant. It is not Energinet, but the winners of the supply, which will be the builder of these cables. The final cable guide to the land plant may therefore end up following routes other than the two that are part of the environmental assessment. How many cables to be carried ashore have not yet been clarified, Energinet says.

Connecting to Bornholm Energinet has also since the first consultation reduced the area on land where the high voltage station is to be erected. After a workshop course with the participation of architects, Energinet requested in March that the regional municipality makes a local plan for the eastern part of the 260-hectare gross area, which was until then in play. It was decided to place the land facility on the eastern side of Vasegårdsvej.

Energinet writes that the station is expected to fill 103 hectares (1.03 square kilometers) when included, for example, shielding planting and basins for collecting rainwater. The technical plant itself is about 53 hectares. In the new floor plans, Energinet has found space for two additional transformer stations of 132 and 60 kilovolts. It is these stations that can make it possible to connect the Bornholm electricity grid to the energy island. Land facilities are moved in Zealand, Energinet has also made new plans. The location of the 50 hectare land plant, which has been a great debate in the local area, has been moved a few kilometers to the northwest to a new project area between Hedehusene and Taastrup. It is also clear that Energinet will lead the cable ashore at Karlstrup Strand in Køge Bay.

The hearing started on Thursday and runs until June 25.

Title: Energiø Bornholm bliver mål i hybridkrigen
Content:
Our Folketing has chosen an energy kitchen construction that means that billion -dollar investments of crucial importance for Bornholm and for electricity consumers in Denmark and Germany can be sabotaged by quite limited effort.

How should Bornholm's future, security and defense look, asks Bornholm's Journal.

The best defense of Bornholm is the prevention of attacks - also in the hybrid war.

The energy island on Bornholm poses a crucial threat to Bornholm's safety and future development of infrastructure associated with the energy island. This is due to the way the project is screwed together with huge wind turbine systems over a large area, all of which have to go through the transformer station in Sose before it reaches the customers. An attack here will therefore be able to put Energiø Bornholm, with all affiliated plants to the water and on land, out of function. These are boring considerations that apparently did not take into account in the project.

Governments should therefore take Energiø Bornholm to be considered due to the risk of sabotage with catastrophic consequences. The security of Bornholm will be anything but "future -proof" if the plans for the energy island are realized.

On the contrary, the energy island will, as Rear Admiral Nils Wang writes in the end of his thorough post in Bornholm's Journal on June 3, pose "the greatest potential risk of Bornholm in the new security policy situation in the Baltic Sea". Not by the Russians threatening to invade Bornholm, but knows, Wang points out, "the hybrid threat we have already seen in different contexts".

Our Folketing has chosen an energy kitchen construction that means that billion -dollar investments of crucial importance for Bornholm and for electricity consumers in Denmark and Germany can be sabotaged by quite limited effort. The many giant mills all have to supply power to the transformer station on Bornholm, from which the current is transmitted. If the reformation is destroyed, wind turbines are for x billions in the Baltic Sea useless. Has the government considered the security of this construction? Has it considered the consequences for Bornholm and for the customers of the electricity in Denmark and Germany, if it happens? Has it considered the consequences for the other production plants that may be linked to the energy island? Power-to-X, hydrogen production and other local industries? Has it consulted its own intelligence service? Has it considered billion -dollar compensation claims from the wind turbine investors if their mills can't get rid of the flow? Title: Medie: Statens støttemodel til energiøen kan komme i klemme
Content:
The state aid model for Energiø Bornholm with a ceiling on total expenses is at risk of not living up to future EU rules, EnergiWatch writes.

The government's analyzes of the project economy show that support in the billion class from the state will probably be necessary for Energiø Bornholm to be established.

Last week, ten parties in the Folketing agreed on a support model, which over a 20-year period can trigger up to DKK 17.6 billion to the winner of the offer to erect the planned offshore wind farm west of Bornholm.

The outcome of the supply will determine whether there will be a need to pay state aid or whether the state should receive a concession payment from the wind turbine manufacturer who provides best bids.

However, the selected model risks getting into carambol with EU rules, writes the media EnergiWatch. The EU has for a while worked on an electricity market reform that can set a standard for how states can support the production of electricity. The proposed principle is that the aid must ensure a minimum price for their electricity, while the state will, on the other hand, receive part of the profits if the electricity price becomes high and exceeds a certain level.

To Energiø Bornholm, however, the parties to the agreement are planning to use a fixed price supplement that increases the risk of wind turbine owners, as a fall in the market price is not covered by the state as in the proposed EU model.

Dansk Erhverv: Risky a fixed price supplement has the advantage of putting a ceiling on how much money the state risks having to pay. If the EU model is introduced as the sole support, one will increase the financial risk of the state, and the question is whether politicians will dare to continue with the Energiø projects if the expenditure risks increasing further.

Dansk Erhverv warns against introducing an electricity market reform with the state aid requirement, which according to the Head of Energy Esben Thietje Mortensen risks stopping the largest renewable energy projects in Danish history.

- The Commission risks with the requirement not only tightening legs for Energiø Bornholm but also to pull the blanket away during other WE projects across the EU that require state aid. After all, what applies to Energiø Bornholm will also apply to the energy island in the North Sea. And the expense risk is expected to be even higher here, says Esben Thietje Mortensen, Dansk Energi, to EnergiWatch.

The EU's new electricity market reform is scheduled to be finally adopted at the end of the year when the European Parliament and EU countries have over the negotiations.

Title: Danmark vil styrke maritim overvågning med andre lande for at undgå sabotage
Content:
Several countries around the Baltic Sea and the North Sea come together to strengthen cooperation to avoid sabotage against critical infrastructure.

It was agreed on Tuesday at a meeting of the British -led coalition Joint Expeditionary Force.

This is stated by acting Minister of Defense Troels Lund Poulsen (V) after the meeting in Amsterdam.

- Russia is apparently in the process of mapping critical infrastructure. Not just in Danish waters, but also with our allies.

It indicates that Russia may be prepared to perform sabotage at worst, says Troels Lund Poulsen.

At the meeting on Tuesday, the defense ministers from the ten countries in the coalition were present. In addition to Denmark and the UK, that is, Sweden, Norway, Finland, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, the Netherlands and Iceland.

Together they form a large part of the countries around the Baltic Sea and the North Sea.

The countries will specifically share intelligence on possible maritime threats. It should ensure a common updated image of possible threats.

The countries will also coordinate their presence in the waters. This is done in collaboration with NATO. NATO has also increased the collaboration.

- A war or conflict can start somewhere other than on the battlefield. It can start by shutting down some countries. It will be deeply serious.

It is in that context and in the light of Ukraine that we will have to have a closer collaboration, says Troels Lund Poulsen.

The decision should help prevent sabotage after the four explosions that blasted the gas pipeline Nord Stream on the bottom of the Baltic Sea.

However, according to Troels Lund Poulsen, the countries have not appointed special parts of critical infrastructure as most vulnerable. But from the Danish side, there is concern as to whether Russia could find to attack the renewable energy.

- We are faced with establishing an energy island off Bornholm. It will contribute green power to up to 14 million people. If it suddenly cannot function for a period of time, then it is not only Denmark that is affected.

- It is a new threat that we have not really related to before, says Troels Lund Poulsen.

Title: Minister om power-to-x: Bornholmerne bestemmer selv

Title: Bornholm ligger ikke ved Anholt
Content:
Bornholm has gained a new security policy and strategic significance, which is clear to all decision makers, and they know well now that Bornholm is not in the Kattegat.

Many of us can remember the old school atlas from our school hours, where Bornholm for space was in the middle of the Kattegat. But it has soon dawned on most Danes that Bornholm is the Baltic Sea and that our lovely island is not just a favorite holiday destination for many Danes.

When Russia invaded Ukraine on February 24 last year, a lot happened in our immediate area.

We have experienced breaches of the submarine cable, unexplained GPS outcome on the ferry, and outside the category, the breaches of the gas lines Nordstream 1 and 2 were well.

Some of it can be attributed to the current conflict, while otherwise may not. Either way, the many events exhibit our vulnerability and addiction.

Danish society is robust and extremely well -functioning, but above all very efficiently driven. The last thing is very good to say about, but there is also a vulnerability.

A vulnerability that is made clear when a submarine cable is torn over by an anchor or when the ferry cannot sail because the GPS does not work.

The special Bornholm spirit, where everyone helps everyone, seems far down the road, but as the security policy situation looks at the moment, there is probably an increased robustness.

Next year, the Home Guard will be 75 years old. Ever since its establishment in 1949, the purpose of the Home Guard has been to strengthen the defense of Denmark and to mobilize citizens in the event of crisis or war. Since its establishment, the Home Guard has continuously adapted to the changing security policy situations and solved societal and military challenges.

Denmark is not at war. But the Home Guard's ability to mobilize and defend the country's borders have been renewed after Putin's Russia invaded Ukraine.

On February 24, 2022, we woke up to a new reality, and this has made the Home Guard fill more in the consciousness of the Danes, but especially with many Bornholmers.

For the indomitable struggle for peace, democracy and freedom of the Ukrainians, has shown that the effect of an organized, equipped and trained popular defense cannot be underestimated.

The Home Guard is therefore more relevant as a voluntary military contingency organization in relation to Denmark's security than we have seen in many years. Since the start of the Ukrain War, we have seen an annual net growth of 10 percent to the Bornholm Home Guard.

Throughout Europe, we now see an extra focus on the security and defense policy agenda.

In Denmark, the war in Ukraine has meant that both politicians, the population and the media have intensified attention to the defense and the Home Guard.

Not least in light of the national compromise of investing in the defense to meet the future security policy challenges.

Does this mean that the Home Guard must change and be trained in order to support the defense in the tasks of the future? The Home Guard's core tasks have been a military guarding and securing strategically important areas since its creation. And precisely military guarding has been at the center and formed an important foundation in connection with the so -called host nation support tasks, where Allied forces need to transport military equipment and personnel safely through the country.

With its strategic location, Denmark is a hub in the Baltic Sea region, and therefore we should expect that tasks such as host nation support will only grow in the future.

The Home Guard's voluntary soldiers have already shown that they have the ability and capacity to plan, coordinate and perform the many tasks that the new security policy situation has brought.

For example, many of the Home Guard's volunteer soldiers have solved tasks with guarding during the spectacular Defender 22 exercise, where many heard about Himar's rocket launch platform for the first time. The Air Force's rejection broadcasting has been here for extended periods. There have been radars set up in the paradise trays. Guarding of Rønne Harbor during an exercise with the US Navy. All these tasks were solved by the Bornholm Home Guard.

It takes a great deal of flexibility and commitment of the volunteer soldiers to handle the task - especially when it comes to host nation support.

It is a task that is not limited to the weekend or after 4 pm. It therefore draws large exchanges, not only on the individual soldier, but also with relatives and employers.

If the current situation of war in Europe continues, the number of military tasks for the Home Guard will not be reduced.

It requires many more hands than we are today, as well as increased education and training.

But above all, it requires support and understanding. From the family, the employer and the community who will suffer deprivation, run stronger and show the recognition that motivates the volunteer.

So in the very close, the Home Guard fits us in everyday life.

Bornholm's special location in the Baltic Sea means that we are like a plug, which is why we have a strategically important location. In other words, Bornholm is crucial to securing entry to the Baltic Sea with reinforcement forces to the Baltic countries.

What it will mean in the upcoming defense conciliation negotiations, only the parliamentary politicians know. But judging by the new foreign and security policy strategy, there will be a focus on the Baltic Sea and the expansion of green energy.

The military perspective in the Baltic Sea is known, but the new is the safety of green energy. For example, Energiø Bornholm will in future be considered as part of security policy. A new situation that will certainly become part of the discussions before the new defense settlement.

Of course, we Danes and Bornholmers are not alone. Bornholm is part of Denmark and Denmark is part of NATO.

In a year, the Home Guard can celebrate the 75th anniversary, incidentally at the same time as NATO.

The development of society means that the retirement age for everyone, including the supporting structures in the community such as the Home Guard or NATO, is a violent path. Neither the Home Guard nor NATO can afford to retire.

These are new times. And behind the scenes, there are many changes that we can only see the contours of when the defense settlement is in place.

But the Bornholm Home Guard, all soldiers at Almegårds Barracks, the total Danish defense and NATO, are ready to look after all Bornholmers, so you can still sleep well.

Bornholm is like Anholt a lovely holiday island, but here the similarities hold up. Bornholm has gained a new security policy and strategic significance, which is clear to all decision makers, and they know well now that Bornholm is not in the Kattegat.

Title: Vindmølletopfolk: 'I kan få den grønneste produktion af tekstiler'

Energiø Bornholm can thus just turn out to be the start, expect the co -founder of CIP, which last year applied for permission to build two offshore wind farms east of Bornholm for the production of hydrogen, but initially has not received political support for the plans.

- Let me give two examples of the world being a little bigger than you just think. At CIP we work with a project to connect the Åland Islands, Gotland and Bornholm down to the German hydrogen market. We hope it ends up with a big interconnector. There are also some at Bornholm who can work on that project, said Jakob Baruël Poulsen, who also came up with what he described as a "slightly popped example" of the possibilities.

Packed lunches to the whole world - last year at the People's Meeting at Møn - which is a slightly smaller event than what we are on here - I met a man who provided lunches for service crew at Klintholm Harbor. Søren Scherfig, country manager for Denmark at Ørsted, called on the Bornholmers to seize the possibilities as a hub for the green transition in the Baltic Sea.

The Railway of the Railway Kristian Jensen from the industry organization Green Power Denmark emphasized that the green investments can lay the foundation for a boom for Bornholm entrepreneurship.

- 150 years ago it meant something in Denmark where the railway was. Here came the cities and business development. He expects Bornholm to have a competitive advantage when it comes to marketing, as the energy island will almost always supply Bornholm with renewable electricity.

- What you also get is a guarantee of almost a hundred percent for always getting green power. There is something interesting about that, said the former Left Minister, who last year became a top lobbyist for the energy sector.

- More and more consumers around the world want products with as low a CO2 footprint as possible. When you look around the world, you can see that some companies are starting to move their production - not where the labor force is cheapest, but where they can tell their customers that the goods are made with the lowest possible CO2 imprint. For example, Apple moves part of their production from China down to Vietnam because they are in this way very close to a place where power comes in, said Kristian Jensen, who failed to reserve a situation where it fails to make The interconnection between the energy island and the Bornholm electricity grid that Energinet is working on.

Only next year is it clear whether the interconnection can be done or not, but it will be promising, said Energinet's Director of Energy Islands during the National Assembly. If Bornholm gets a direct connection from Energiøens Møller, Bornholm will be interesting for a wide range of companies, "if you try to fire to have the greenest production at all because of the wind turbines that come in a little while," Kristian Jensen predicts.

- It's not just energy -related. It may also consist of making the greenest textile production or greenest production of things we use in our kitchens. Think out of the box, the call for the Bornholmers in the audience was at the Circus Square.

Greenest island in the world Deputy Director Anne Højer Simonsen from Dansk Industri shares the optimism for future production and innovation on Bornholm, which can be laid out in new ways to use technologies and the green hydrogen.

- It is a huge opportunity agenda for the island. It is an island that will be known for becoming the greenest in the world. When we stand here again in 15 years, you will run on green electricity, have green skills and a port that drives the development.

Kristian Jensen ended up calling for Mayor Jacob Trøst (K) and the rest of the municipal council to be proactive.

- Now the mayor is not here, but if he was, I would shoot back a little. For this will also require that they in the municipality are agile and flexible. There are crazy ideas and crooked opportunities that we do not think will arise. The municipality must be prepared to be able to move a little quickly when someone comes with the ideas and support them. Because if you do not have that agility, you can only plan, and I believe that your creativity is much greater than the one we have up here, Kristian Jensen told the Bornholmers.

What do the Bornholmers even think of Energiø Bornholm? That question tried to shed light on during the National Assembly with a simple vote.

"Is the energy island good for Bornholm?" The question read, which could be answered anonymously at Tidendes Plads at Kampeløkken Harbor.

Here's the result :? Yes: 61 (of them the 18 do not live on Bornholm).

CIP and Ørsted miss greater demands on sustainability

The energy people used the debate on the main scene in Allinge as an opportunity to criticize the supply of Energiø Bornholm and a number of other offshore wind farms with a total capacity of at least nine gigawatts. They would have liked to see that sustainability had become a competitive parameter, but politicians have designed the tenders in a way, so the price is the only criterion that the bidders are judged on when they have met certain sustainability requirements.

Only for two of the upcoming parks has a requirement for so -called "natural -inclusive design" have been added, which means that the erection of mills must lead to a positive impact on the marine environment and biodiversity in the area. "We would have liked to see that there had been that requirement for all nine gigawatts and that the requirements had been as high as possible," said Kristian Jensen.

- But I think my former friends in the Ministry of Finance were a little scared that too high environmental requirements would make the check to be paid to be allowed to set up offshore wind turbines would be too low. So some politicians prioritized the check on the nature requirements for the wind farms. We would have liked to see that they had prioritized the requirements higher and the check lower.

The heavy boys of the green transition supported the message that the energy companies would like to see greater environmental focus from the political side. Søren Scherfig from Ørsted estimated that minimum requirements will result in minimum solutions, while Jakob Baruël Poulsen from CIP explained why the industry has a financial interest in prioritizing the marine environment and life underwater.

- The fact that we become as good at what possible will be a competitive advantage in other countries, because other countries will also demand that things. So for Ørsted and CIP, I actually think it's an advantage that we get as good as possible on our domestic market.

Title: Tyskland og Danmark deler både udgifter og indtægter til energiø
Content:
The energy ministers from Denmark and Germany on Monday signed a decisive intergovernmental agreement on Energiø Bornholm.

In connection with a Ministerial Council meeting on Monday in Luxembourg, the Danish Climate, Energy and Supply Minister, Lars Aagaard (M), and Germany's economy and climate minister, Robert Habeck, have signed an agreement on Energiø Bornholm.

In a joint press release, the two countries' operators of the transmission network, Danske Energinet and German 50Hertz state that the parties have negotiated ownership conditions and the distribution of energy amounts.

“The agreement means that Energinet and 50Hertz incur every half of the infrastructure costs for the project, as well as sharing the ROOD shares that the project causes.

50Hertz and Energinet will also distribute the bottleneck revenue from the electricity connections between the countries equally, ”the press release states.

Thus, half of the cost of building the transformer station in Sydbornholm must be paid on from the German side, just as the financial benefits of trading in electricity will be divided, even if the land plant must be erected on Danish soil.

Most of the power is scheduled to be transported to Germany. A cable connection of 1.2 gigawatts will go from Bornholm to Zealand, while the capacity of the DC cable of 525 kilovolts to Germany becomes 2.0 gigawatts.

The cornerstone Energinet describes the signature of the ministers as "yet another important cornerstone". The agreement creates a "" firm basis for Energinet and 50Hertz to work closely together and distribute responsibility between themselves when the various tasks in the construction of the world's first and innovative energy island to be solved ", the companies write.

Stefan Kapfer, CEO of 50Hertz, emphasizes in the press release that the energy island will fundamentally change how the power from offshore wind turbines is brought ashore.

-Energiø Bornholm paves the way for a future where offshore winds will no longer only be linked to individual countries via point-to-point connections. In the future, part of the produced power from offshore wind will flow to where demand is greatest, via high-voltage equilibrium grid on sea.

- Energiø Bornholm will also result in another trade connection between the German and the Danish electricity market. It is financially feasible and will increase both countries' security of supply under new geopolitical circumstances, says Stefan Capifer.

Title: Energiøen er en ommer - en svær ommer
Content:
The decision to realize Energiø Bornholm should be reconsidered under the impression of the new threat picture and the renewed need for investments to address these threats.

Energiø Bornholm is an ommer. The decision to construct Energiø Bornholm and place it on Bornholm was made without considering the risk of sabotage and any consequences for the electricity supply and for the Bornholm community. The Minister of Defense has confirmed that.

The threats are actualized by the war against Ukraine, blasting of gas pipes and Russian espionage against infrastructure. Events that occurred after the energy island were decided and put in the lake, the Baltic Sea.

To Ritzau, acting Minister of Defense Troels Lund Poulsen (V) stated on June 14: - We are faced with establishing an energy island off Bornholm. It will contribute green power to up to 14 million people. If it suddenly cannot function for a period of time, then it is not only Denmark that is affected.

"It is a new threat that we have not really related to before," Troels Lund Poulsen told Ritzau.


Former NATO General Secretary

If you maintain the construction and location of Energiø Bornholm, it will require additional investments in security that are not shown in the plans from Energinet. It points out former prime minister and NATO General Secretary Anders Fogh Rasmussen.

Asked in TV2/ Bornholm about what significance Energiø Bornholm gets for security, said Anders Fogh Rasmussen on June 15: - This means that we now have to increase investments in what is called the defense of the critical infrastructure, and precisely the explosions After all, on Nord Stream's pipelines shows that now the critical infrastructure becomes part of the threat we are exposed to. Therefore, any new investment in energy islands must be accompanied by similar investments in increasing security.

It can be many things. It can be monitoring with modern radar systems.

It can be underwater monitoring with the help of underwater drones.

There are many options, Fogh told TV2/ Bornholm.

Should it be the operators who are responsible for making monitoring? But if you do monitoring, you also have to be able to respond, otherwise it doesn't make much sense if we know someone is on their way in and pills an installation.

What really needs is a social security strategy at national level and possibly as an independent ministerial area, Rasmus Dahlberg said in TV2/ Bornholm.

The Prime Minister The decision to realize Energiø Bornholm should therefore be reconsidered under the impression of the new threat picture and the renewed need for investments to address these threats. Title: Dårlig aftale om energiøen?
Content:
Bornholm adds sea area to the energy island, but is it free for Germany, asks Lave K. Broch.

I enjoy reading Bornholm's Journal and preferably the physical newspaper, but on the 21st.

June I had to read an article twice.

It had the headline "Germany and Denmark shares both expenses and revenue to Energiø". It sounds really good immediately, but on closer reflection it seems like a bad deal for Denmark - and not least for Bornholm.

I am not an expert on the energy island, but as I have understood it, the whole offshore wind farm must be located in Denmark/ Bornholm's financial zone, which in English is called EEZ. Bornholm thus adds sea area, but is it free for Germany? In addition, there is nothing about compensation for the Bornholmers whose homes are close to the land facility.

Should Denmark and Germany give them compensation together? For they get compensation? I do not hope that our government has entered into an agreement without ensuring that Germany pays "rent" to join the energy island and without our countries sharing compensation to affected Bornholmers. If this is not the case, I think the energy island should instead be in Germany's economic zone and that the land plant should be on Rügen.

However, I would add that I have been very positive about the energy island, but I had hoped that Bornholm would be compensated for it to be in the island's financial zone it should be. For example, it could be that we who live on Bornholm got cheaper electricity. It would have benefited both us citizens and business at Bornholm. Now I hope someone can assure me that the Danish government has not fooled.

- I have an ugly feeling of being powerless.

I really fear for cables and noise, says his wife, Vibeke.

The mayor immediately states that one of the municipality's main priorities is to change the legislation so that the neighbors can access the loss of value as soon as possible.

- The law is not geared for a project like this, he says.

And that is why we need to target our energy to change it, says Jacob Solvet, who, however, understands that the Folketing cannot handle the task in a few months.

- I know that under Corona you could change the law from day to day, but usually it is something that takes a long time.

Private interests Jacob Consolation emphasizes that from an early stage he has tried to speak the neighbors' case.

The lobbying work is intensified in the spring, where he met a few times with the Folketing's Climate and Energy Committee. When Jacob Trøst talks about his collaboration with Lea Wermelin and Peter Juel-Jensen, a few of the neighbors are on their noses because they do not have the big scam for the impact of the local parliamentary members.

- I can easily understand the frustration and anger, but we will have to focus on how we can find solutions, Jacob replies.

- It will be to take care of private interests, explains Anka Nordvig Sonne.

- Jacob often writes and close, and sometimes I think we have to take care not to get tired of us, says Lillian Rasch Madsen.


Fear of Landspland Directive

Title: Bornholm vil med i fællesskabet
Content:
Bornholm's mayor, Jacob Trøst, sees great advantages in the municipality joining the Rural Joint Council.

Bornholm's mayor, Jacob Trøst, sees great advantages for the municipality in being able to get support to speak Bornholm's case, among other things, in connection with becoming Energiø, while the chairman of the Rural Joint Council, Steffen Damsgaard, is pleased that Bornholm Regional Municipality wants to join in the community, which now includes 56 of the country's municipalities.

Bornholm Regional Municipality thus enters as a member of the Rural Joint Council, and Jacob Trøst looks forward to membership and finds it natural to enter the community that has a mission to create a Denmark in balance where it is attractive to live, live and work in all parts of the country.

Bornholm's regional municipality, like several other outer municipalities, is challenged on its demographics and is, like island, extra exposed, as there are no neighboring municipalities to lean upwards. The enrollment in the Joint Council must be seen as part of Bornholm's efforts to attract more newcomers and to build a more sustainable society in every way.

Mayor Jacob Trøst says: - The Rural Joint Council works politically to create development opportunities throughout the country. As a island and outer municipality, it is a strong community to step into. It is also of great importance to us that the Joint Council works on the basis of a green overall plan. The plan indicates that rural municipalities must be ensured compensations by laying soil for energy plants so that the value added that the energy plants will create also accrues to the local areas it will affect.

- It is super relevant for Bornholm, who is faced with having to add island to the energy island's land facility, he says, referring to the green play presented by the Joint Council earlier this year, Green New Deal.

Good dialogue with Bornholm as a new member rounds the Rural Council Municipality number 56. Steffen Damsgaard has since 2008 held the post of chairman of the overall rural organization.

- We have had good dialogue with Bornholm for several years and prioritized to participate actively at the People's Meeting at Bornholm every single year. Therefore, I am pleased to be able to welcome them in the community.

Bornholm is a fantastic island, but it is also clear that Bornholm, like many other island and outer municipalities, is challenged by the demographic development, he says, adding: - Now that Bornholm has to be Energiø and lay soil for large energy plants, it is Even more relevant for Bornholm to join. In the Rural Joint Council, we work actively to ensure that the rural municipalities not only carry the burden, but also reap the gains of the green transition. Getting it on the nationwide climate agenda is one of our important focus areas along with other rural policy agendas, which I am sure Bornholm can benefit from.

But a lot of conditions around the energy island are insecure, and if we are to secure Bornholm in the future, it is about not to build air castles, but instead bet on a more solid house. Estimates from CRT, based on interviews with some of the actors behind some of the planned power-to-X projects in Denmark, point out that the energy island can create 900 lasting jobs on Bornholm. About half will be created as a result of the world's largest power-to-X plant, which receives electricity not only from the energy island, but also two similar large wind farms east and south of Nexø, which again has great uncertainty. If the plant is to be smaller, so will the number of new jobs. Another but very relevant problem is that the positive climate effects of Power -To -X are questionable, and one must therefore wonder if it makes sense to fix green investments that way? At the same time, in recent months, the financial basis for the energy islands, which should have been expenditure neutral, has crumbled despite a new agreement that Energiø Bornholm must cost up to DKK 17.6 billion. Public kroner.

It cannot help but create uncertainty. Especially not when calculations assess the need for state grants to be almost twice as large.

Therefore, it is also not useful that our business strategy is unilaterally investing in, for example, a business park that is dependent on Power-to-X in connection with the energy island. On qualifying employees in green transition and on how to create business networks that can ensure that Bornholm companies are ready to bid on tasks related to a potential energy island and, for example, test island activities, as part of the development of future energy -and resource systems.

Title: Vi holder øje med dem, der bygger
Content:
Not everyone knows how to build on a rocky island, writes Jonna Nielsen.

The world is changing, and Bornholm as well.

The major transitions Our society is facing will to that extent materialize on Bornholm if Energiø is to be built. The green transition will be crucial to start and achieve in the coming years, and sustainability is more generally central, and here the construction plays a central role. Both when it comes to building energy islands, setting up solar cells, etc., but also when it comes to making our housing stock more energy efficient. We have to fire less for the gray sparrows, so to speak. It requires energy renovations.

All of these agendas 3F Bornholm would like to play an active role in shaping and making a reality. Because there is no doubt that if we are to reach the goal, then it requires all actors to cooperate.

There are many different elements that must go up into a higher unit if it is to succeed.

There is the question that in the coming years we are looking into a time when there will be a massive lack of skilled labor.

Employers are screaming for 'more labor', but we think we should ask the right ones - green transition requires the right skills, and it will be a task to make sure that our local labor has the necessary skills. We will help our members through qualification and continuing education in 3F Bornholm.

Here, our local businesses also play a key role as they have to prioritize getting their employees sent off on continuing education.

It is equivalent to the master and the individual, and not least for our local communities. It could be structures (Earth & Concrete Workers) that we know will play an important role in the green transition.

Green change is also about energy -efficient buildings but at the same time it is also about employees not being exposed to asbestos and other dangerous substances. It is about a social and just green transition, here can again be mentioned the importance of continuing education so that employees can go safely to work.

The apprentices' house is an example of renovating and respecting old construction, which we have a lot of here at Bornholm.

Many in the field of construction can advantageously be qualified from unskilled to skilled.

It will benefit both the individual and Bornholm - according to the AE Council, it potentially has a greater socio -economic gain to train 2,000 from unskilled to skilled than to abolish the top tax1. Ultimately, it's all about securing our labor market in the future.

Because it doesn't matter who is building the foundations and buildings that will stand for the next several years, nor for the energy island.

As we have seen in recent years, large foreign consortia have been heavily involved in some of the largest public buildings and infrastructure projects. Foreign companies without their own employees who hire subcontractors into long and opaque chains, where they use cheap foreign labor for the community's tax dollars. It should make the alarm bells ring.

These are, for example, the Metro Cityringen in Copenhagen, the new Storstrømsbro and New Odense University Hospital to name a few examples.

Where we initially saw bypass of the agreement with the underpayment of foreign colleagues in the construction industry, the development must be said to have deteriorated significantly. After all, you do not believe your own ears when you hear about the miserable conditions for which foreign labor is exposed. In addition to strategic circumvention of the agreement with underpayment, it is criminal activities that take place. We should not have that in the construction here at Bornholm. This is all from the fact that the foreign colleagues are exposed to violence and threats if they join the union, to money laundering and invoice cabinets, cheating with tax and social contributions such as pension, false signatures, to so -called return commission, where they are forced to to repay parts of their wages in cash.

Unfortunately, many of them are unskilled and know neither language nor their rights.

It is challenging in many ways - it is difficult to talk to them and make them understand their rights, but they also do not know about materials or construction processes.

One can only imagine whether this is why many large public buildings in these years are both very delayed and more expensive than expected, because the quality is poor.

This problem has not previously been a problem on Bornholm, but with the new large buildings that come to the Art Museum and not least the energy island, it will be a great priority for us in 3F Bornholm, which we will follow closely, so wages and working conditions are the same For everyone, large buildings such as the Almegårds Barracks and Bo42 have been won by local competitive construction companies with which we have a good and constructive collaboration.

We welcome foreign companies and foreign colleagues in the construction - but it must be on equal terms. Otherwise, it is completely undermining our local businesses, for the terms we have seen from the major construction projects, no Danish or Bornholm companies can compete for that matter.

On the other hand, we have good experiences in 3F which we would very much like to share how it is avoided that these conditions become realities here at Bornholm.

At Bornholm, the construction has traditionally always entered into agreements, unfortunately we have also experienced new lucky knights in the industry that will make some quick money, and do not care about the employees' well -being, here we have prioritized the battle for agreements in 3F Bornholm to secure. that our members are not exposed to odd terms.

It requires, among other things. a. Solid working clauses with requirements from the developer on collective pay and working conditions in the tender documents.

But it can't stand alone. The builder must also play a very active role in ensuring that the main contractor meets this requirement in the contract. This is done by effectively enforcing and sanctioning the clause. And it's about getting started as soon as possible if it needs to be done properly. We want to contribute to this process so that we ensure that it is done properly from the start.

In 3F Bornholm we will keep a close eye on those who build. We invite foreign colleagues into the community of the union, but we will also strike a blow to put the local labor into play. And here we think we should bet on wise qualified hands. Not everyone knows how to build on a rocky island.

Title: Vi har brug for visionær boligudvikling
Content:
We all have great opportunities to develop Bornholm. But it requires action here and now, says Ocean Prawn's director.

It is no secret that Bornholm is a relatively poor municipality that faces a challenging future.

The regional municipality is struggling every year to get the municipal budget connected, and our population composition is skewed and more and more elderly people are getting on the island. It is time that we take a strong stance to reverse the development and attract more working people to Bornholm. The regional municipality has also acknowledged that we need more citizens, more jobs and more economic growth, and has set an ambitious goal of achieving 42,000 inhabitants by 2028. To achieve this goal, a visionary housing development plays a crucial role.

As director of Ocean Prawns, one of the island's largest companies, and with a strong interest in Bornholm's future, I write this post to focus on the need for housing development on our island.

Bornholm is currently in an extremely favorable position with an incredibly positive reputation, and the island enjoys great interest and popularity, not least thanks to events such as the People's Meeting that attract many guests as well as tourists on the island throughout the year. We should fully utilize this headwind to fully realize the potential of the island. The projects around Rønne Harbor and the upcoming Energiø will open up a number of new opportunities and create more jobs.

It is crucial that we understand how to utilize this headwind and focus on creating a sustainable and forward -looking future for Bornholm.

In the profession, our biggest challenge is a lack of labor and competencies, as the workforce is too narrow in relation to demand.

To be attractive to potential newcomers, Bornholm must deliver on the whole package: Good job opportunities, a wide selection of housing, schools, care services and more. We need to make Bornholm a more attractive place to live, so people are willing to move up the tent poles and build a new life on the island.

The next big challenge is where to house the potential influx of labor and newcomers? Is our housing offer wide and varied enough to meet their wishes? I believe that the solution to the Gordian knot must be found in a visionary housing development that takes into account the needs and desires of the future, and finds a balance between conservation and renewal.

We are finally underway, as Ocean Prawns is involved in two upcoming housing projects: The Apple Leash in Rønne in collaboration with Bornholm Brand a. M. B. A. And Grynebakken in Svaneke under the auspices of Jens Møller Gudhjem. It is precisely these housing projects are our attempts to support the development of Bornholm, and we are experiencing great interest from potential residents.

Therefore, we wonder that the case is not prioritized higher. Housing buildings do not seem to have the necessary priority, which is very worrying, and I could dream that we were a little more at the forefront of the development, so that the municipality's goal of the 42,000 inhabitants can be realized.

For example, as investors, we have signed the agreement on the grounds for the apple lobe in Rønne Syd back in December 2021.

However, it seems that we can only begin the actual construction at the earliest in mid -2024, and it is expected that the finished construction will be ready in 2025. We have otherwise been eager to get started and have done ours to promote the project But unfortunately, construction seems to have ended up in an administrative bottleneck.

I hope that we are learning some of the process right now and that we are getting to the forefront of the development, so that Bornholm is ready to move on to the opportunities that arise when investors and companies knock on. I think it is important learning in relation to the upcoming energy island and what follows in this regard.

With our experience in construction on Bornholm, I would appeal that the regional municipality is already starting to build the possible areas that could become attractive in the future of companies and investors.

We need a smooth and effective case management that allows us to act quickly and effectively when investors and businesses show interest in our island.

Bornholm has in many ways headwind in these years, but we must not rest on the laurels.

Bornholm needs a visionary and forward -looking approach to housing development and building maturation to realize the full potential of the island. A sustainable plan for housing development must be drawn up, which not only meets the needs of the present, but also prepares us for the challenges and opportunities that await us in the future. In short, it is now to be invested in the future.

Ocean Prawns is ready to support the housing development of Bornholm, but we need political will and action now.
