Title: Planer for energiø vækker uro i Sverige
Content:
The Swedish authorities are concerned about what the cables for Energiø Bornholm will mean for the marine environment in the Baltic Sea. However, a decision to settle for one cable bundle to Zealand meets praise from Sweden.

A crucial part of the infrastructure for Energiø Bornholm is the search cable, which connects the high -voltage station at Sydbornholm to a station in Zealand. The cable, which gets an effect of 1.2 gigawatts, must be passed through Sweden's economic zone.

Before the summer holidays, the Danish authorities' updated plan was in consultation, and the comments on the environmental impact report shed light on some concern with the Swedish authorities, which are responsible for the Baltic Sea. It shows the consultation responses, which the Environmental Strain has given Bornholm's Journal of access to access.

Given the large number of planned infrastructure projects in the area, Sweden's Meteorological and Hydrological Institute (SMHI) finds "It is extremely important that the overall environmental impact becomes as small as possible" when the energy island is to be established.

Precisely for this reason, both SMHI and the Länsstyrelsen are pleased that since the first hearing it has been decided that only one cable connection should be added between Bornholm and Zealand. When the project was in consultation last winter, Energinet planned to put two cables of 0.6 gigawatts in two separate cable tombs.

Important for the entire Baltic Sea Smhi, in the consultation response, points out that the southern part of the Baltic Sea supplies the central, deeper part of the Baltic Sea with salty and oxygen -rich water flowing from the Sound and the Danish belts. "Thus, local impact on the southern part of the Baltic Sea can have an impact on the environment throughout the Baltic Sea," writes the institute, who sees several risks to the marine environment at the cable laying.

"On the stretches where the search cable is to be protected by stone settings, increased turbulence can cause the bottom -on stream to be mixed with water closer to the surface, reducing its quality and significance for the Baltic Sea's deepwater areas."

The Hydrological Institute repeats a wish that has been made in previous consultation rounds; That the Danish authorities make sure to investigate and put figures on how the wind turbines affect ocean currents, waves and the mixture of the surface water.

The Swedish authority in charge of the aquatic environment in the southern part of the Baltic Sea, the Vattenmydigheten Södra Östersjön, writes that with "the current information cannot comment on the impact of the cable laying on the coastal water areas" because the method is first described in detail later .

Warning against formal deterioration on the part of the EU requires that projects must not aggravate the current classification of the seawater, points out the Swedish water authority, which highlights two formulations from the Miljøstyrelsen report, which raises concerns.

-The Vattenmydigheten is therefore troubled by the fact that "the establishment of the search cable will -for the construction method -resulting in the spread of sediment to the water phase." As well as "the potential environmental impacts may have a cross -border nature in relation to Sweden, Poland and Germany", the consultation response says.

In advance, there is a risk that the surface water will not be able to achieve "good ecological status" in 5-15 years due to oversizing and the occurrence of environmental toxins such as zinc, the water authority writes.

The Swedish Agricultural Agency The Agricultural Agency emphasizes in its answer that it is important for the Danish authorities to consult with relevant actors in the fishing industry as early as possible, so that the work affects fishing as little as possible. In order to improve the coexistence of fishing and energy extraction and reduce the risk of accidents, the Agricultural Authority recommends that "all cables are buried or covered so that fishing equipment does not risk getting stuck." German reaction Three German answers have been received to the consultation.

Due to the distance from the Zealand cable to German waters, neither the German authorities for shipping and hydrography nor the local authorities in Mecklenburg/ Vorpommern have any comments on the Danish consultation.

Germany's army, Bundeswehr, reminds the Danish authorities that it is important to avoid the cable coming close to a NATO diving area for submarines. As they sent maps from the Danish Environmental Protection Agency show that the cable scales north of the military area, nor do Bundeswehr have any objections to the energy project.

In addition to the high -voltage plants on Danish soil, the current consultation is only about the cable between Bornholm and Zealand. A cable from Bornholm to Germany must also be kept, which will be the subject of an independent consultation process.

Title: Olieselskabers kæmpebud på tysk havvind øger optimisme om energiø
Content:
Surprising results of supply on German offshore wind farms in the Baltic Sea and the North Sea cause analysts to believe that the market price is higher than expected when the supply of Energiø Bornholm was prepared.

In July, the energy companies BP and TotalenEngies won the rights to build offshore wind farms in the German part of the North Sea and the Baltic Sea by offering a total of DKK 94 billion for a total capacity of seven gigawatts. The award is, according to Jan Behrendt Ibsø, director of renewable energy in the consultancy COWI, "Surprisingly High". He estimates that the market price, which has been demonstrated in Germany, increases the possibility of Energiø Bornholm becoming a good business for the Danish state.

- It should give the request to update the business case for the energy islands. Especially considering that the Danish wind conditions are better, says Jan Behrendt Ibsø to Finans.dk.

- It is clear that the bidders' assessment of the value of the green stream is significantly greater than the one the authorities have expected when assessing the economy of the Danish projects, says Karsten Capion of Concito in the same article.

Before the summer holidays, a majority in the Folketing agreed on the tender conditions for Energiø Bornholm, which with the agreement can be awarded up to DKK 17.6 billion in state aid.

Shortly thereafter, it was decided to slow down work on the energy island of the North Sea due to financial uncertainties in the mega project.

Minister hopes Climate and Energy Minister Lars Aagaard thinks it will be "fantastic" if the Danish state can achieve equally attractive bids. In that case, the support scheme for Energiø Bornholm does not have to come into use. He has asked the ministry civil service to analyze the German bids to become clearer whether the energy companies are willing to pay a higher price than expected when the state aid model for the energy island was designed.

- I hope that the market's willingness to pay is greater than what lies in the Ministry's models, because it means greater revenue for Danish society and fewer costs.

However, you just have to eat bread, because there may be a difference between the German and Danish tenders in the requirements for the environment and the cost of infrastructure, says Lars Aagaard to Finans.dk.

Several other offshore winds offered at the same time as Energiø Bornholm are not awarded state aid, but is expected to bring in the Danish state a billion surplus. It is the cost of electricity infrastructure, not least the long high-voltage cable from Bornholm to Zealand that has created uncertainty as to whether Energiø Bornholm can be built without support for the company that wins the supply.

French total energy, which pumps large quantities of oil and gas from the North Sea's underground, won the German supply in the Baltic Sea.

The wind farm is at 1 gigawatt (GW) and will be erected northeast of Rügen, just 20 kilometers from the area reserved for Energiø Bornholm. The other German offshore winds supply of a total of six gigawatts are in the North Sea, where total energy and British BP have settled on two and four gigawatts respectively.

Title: Mindre fragt med Hammershus
Content:
In the first seven months of the year, there has been a total decline in the number of trucks and loose trailers on the Rønne-Køge ferry route compared to last year. But more capacity is still needed in the future, says two Bornholm transport companies.

The Bornholm industry and more freight forwarders have long wanted more freight capacity on the ferry route between Rønne and Køge.

The case has even been on the agenda several times in the Contact Council for Traffic Service by Bornholm, and the Council President, Mayor Jacob Trøst, has decided that the challenges with capacity are being dealt with at Council meetings until a solution has been found.

But figures from the Bornholm Line's monthly reports show that in each of all the first seven months of the year there has been a decline in the number of both trucks and loose trailers on the route compared to the same months last year.

The only exception is the number of trucks in January, which increased by almost 21 percent.

The transport company BHS Logistics confirms the experience that there has been more space at Hammershus' car deck.

- There have immediately been challenges in getting the desired number of trailers in both ways, says department director Mikkel Lund Ørum to the Journal.

- There may have been a little in June around the National Assembly - I don't remember it exactly.

The need for the extra freight capacity has not been present in recent months this year.

Is it because you have optimized it, or what is the reason? - No. You could say the market for the goods flow has been different this year than in previous years. This has meant that the load has not been as large as we have experienced in the past.

What are some mechanisms that change it? - This is the question of how much time there is in the production companies all around, and how many we all spend each one buying for our private consumption.

Is it just a short -term fluctuation? - I hope so. I assume that, says Mikkel Lund Ørum.

Fall of 7.9 percent through July, the number of loose trailers has fallen by 7.9 percent and the number of trucks has fallen by 3.7 percent on Rønne-Køge.

A year ago, the BHS director advocated a year ago in the Journal that Bornholm needs a decided estate ferry and that the greatest pressure on the ferry is from the beginning of March until the beginning of the industrial holiday. However, the figures for the months from March to June this year show a decrease of just under nine percent for loose trailers and for trucks a fall of slightly more than five percent -in cut.

The director of Ole Holm Transport, Erik Jørgensen, also has a perception that this year it has been a bit easier to get shipping at Hammershus.

- If you ask if there is really bad space, then it has been worse, he says.

Should I understand that there has been a little recovery? - Yes, you can say that for us.

- Over the years it has gone up and down, however, he states at the same time.

Have you started sending trailers via Ystad? - No, we can't really. We send primarily to Køge. We can't really use Ystad for anything. This is not what they (the Bornholm Line, ed.) Wish, says Erik Jørgensen.

'Quick ferries and shipping is not a good combination' According to Bornholm Line's PR and communications manager Jesper Maack, capacity has increased with Express 1 and Express 5 on the route to Ystad. But sending trailers is not a viable solution.

- When the capacity is raised, there will be room for more trucks on the fast ferries.

We have said all the time: Fast Ferries and Shipping is not a good combination -it has never been. Therefore, it should not be a solution either.

- We take trucks to a certain extent.

But the fast ferries are not built to transport goods back and forth to Bornholm, and the route is built to bring people and cars, develop tourism and to give the residents a flexible and frequent alternative.

Both at BHS Logistics and Ole Holm Transport, however, expect, among other things, the construction work in connection with Energiø Bornholm will create a need for extra shipping capacity on the route between Rønne and Køge.

- Although the storm may be blown off now, one has to think ahead. You have to be ready for what Bornholm wants, says Erik Jørgensen, adding: - If all the many hundreds of millions of dollars to be invested in Bornholm must have goods, then there is not enough ferry capacity.

Content:

Title: Besparelser i byggesagsbehandlingen bliver meget dyrt for Bornholm
Content:

These are very unwise savings because these departments form the very foundation of the continued development of the entire Bornholm.

And here I think not only of business and tourism, but also of our common welfare, which depends on people being able to find a job and a home on Bornholm.

Therefore, we strongly warn against savings in this area and, on the contrary, dream that the area is being prioritized.

The case processing time for construction cases has long been in the firing line, and on behalf of the Bornholm companies I have expressed frustrations on lack of agility and long waiting times in the municipal case management. We also understand that BRK - completely in line with all other companies - must fight hard to attract qualified labor. We also fully acknowledge that BRK as an authority must be able to be on target for laws and regulations being complied with.

If we are to seriously create a more efficient construction case treatment, we see three focus areas: First, the construction case must be provided with all the necessary data, and the construction case must be ensured an effective "flow" through the various municipal departments. And finally, we do not avoid the fact that the necessary resources are being added to the entire case management chain.

Regardless of the fact that Bornholm's municipal economy is under pressure, it is now the task of the municipal council to make decisions that in the long term best benefit the Bornholmers. On the other hand, there is a need for extra resources that do not have to stand alone. There are many good opportunities for growth and value creation on Bornholm, and this is the whole prerequisite for us as a small community to continue to offer jobs and good welfare services, which in turn are crucial to being able to maintain and also attract new citizens to the island. Therefore, we call for the municipal council to act wisely and long -term when making decisions about the municipal economy.

Title: Wermelin: Folkeskolen og campus får noget ud af ny finanslov
Content:
The weakest pupils of the primary school need better conditions, and business schools must educate more and better skilled workers. Both will be felt on Bornholm, says Lea Wermelin (S). A billion kroner for renewable energy may help the municipality that will see a lot to look around the energy island.

More money for primary school's weakest students.

And for vocational education at Campus Bornholm - and possibly also to the municipality, because it may be able to share a billion kroner for renewable energy.

These are the most important gains that MP Lea Wermelin (S) can immediately see from the proposal for next year's Finance Act that the SVM government presented on Thursday.

In primary schools, the academically weakest students must have extra teaching in small teams.

There is a part of them on Bornholm, where the students are below the national average at the exam.

For those students, the government will set an extra DKK 350 million next year. And DKK 500 million a year in 2028.

- This is the first step where we add more money to primary school. We will later look at how we can give more freedom to primary schools so that they can spend less money on documentation and more money to teach, says Lea Wermelin.

- It is always dangerous to guess how large a proportion of Bornholm gets from something that is distributed across the country. But it is clear that Bornholm must have its part, and it will be good that the primary schools at Bornholm can get more means to teach the students smaller teams, she says.

Lea Wermelin assumes that the extra money of the Finance Act for the academically weakest pupils in primary school will be given directly to the municipality and that the money will be earmarked.

- It is the municipalities that are responsible for the primary schools, so I would think that the money comes out in the municipalities via a boost in the municipal block grants and that they will be earmarked to lift the weakest students.

More and better skilled Campus Bornholm can look forward to more money for his vocational education programs, which educates skilled workers. At national level, the government will add DKK 300 million more next year - and DKK 500 million from 2026.

- We need more skilled workers. If we are to have a good welfare society, then we need better business schools. That's a big priority, said Finance Minister Nicolai Wammen (S) as he presented the government's bid for next year's Finance Act.

- At Bornholm it is very much about campus, and I am really happy with this venture. We have prioritized business schools high for many years, but we have not reached the goal yet, says Lea Wermelin.

- It will give a boost to Campus Bornholm and a boost to the quality of teaching in vocational education.

Campus will experience an improved economy already next year.

- We need a lot of skilled workers, even when it is time for the operation of Energiø Bornholm and in relation to all the companies that will follow the energy island, says Lea Wermelin.

- When I was last past Campus Bornholm, we talked, among other things, about targeting education for the energy island. We have to talk about this with Campus about, she says.

Share in new billion? With its Finance Act, the government will also set a billion dollars under the heading "Renewable energy on land". According to Lea Wermelin, the government does not yet know in detail who and what kind of projects will be able to share in that sum. But she sees opportunities.

- Right now, an amount has just been allocated, but we have not quite agreed to how the money should be spent. But you can see Bornholm into part of what these money can go to. Since Bornholm becomes Energiø, Bornholm is at the forefront around laying area for the green transition, says Lea Wermelin.

- At the same time, one has to ask how a challenged municipality like Bornholm has to lift the huge plan task that comes around the energy island. Some of this money might be going to go to it, she says.

Already last week it was clear that the government will also raise an extra billion kroner to the municipalities and the regions. At Bornholm it will add extra four million kroner to the municipality's hard -pressed budget.

- The municipalities have a difficult task. But the Danish economy is going well and we can give an extra hand, but it does not solve everything, Nicolai Wammen said on Thursday.

Title: Kulturhistorien - et væsentligt aktiv
Content:
The culture helps to create debate and find common ground.

Culture is a broad concept and hardly to define as something concrete.

When I write about culture here, my starting point is cultural history.

I sit on the Art and Cultural History Council as a representative of cultural history and am in my daily work leader of Bornholm's island archive and educated historian.

So in this post it is from there my world goes.

We have a strong prehistory at Bornholm, both when we look back on archaeology and on the recent history. It is a prehistory that is very conscious of the island and which has increasingly been used in commercial connection.

It is a culture -bearing identity that many largely take on in the form of e.g.

Tattoos of Bornholm or posters in the living room.

But despite this, we find in the Council that cultural history is under -represented in the applications.

That is, although Bornholm has a great deal of importance and we take it on us as an identity, there are not so many initiatives with the breeding ground in the cultural history of the island that want help from the council.

For a number of years, in the cultural field, the focus has been on food culture and crafts.

There you have really managed to set an agenda and create a strong story that can be built on. It has required hard work from all sides to get to where you are today. Initiatives have been taken that have served as catalysts for new ideas and initiatives. Something has succeeded, others are not. But it has been in a broadly rooted collaboration that has opened up the possibilities and has shown that when we stand together, it is moving something.

Can we get inspiration from these initiatives? The building of a new cultural history museum and a new magazine, where we gather the Bornholm Museum and Bornholm's Ø-Archive collections and hopefully also gather the staff of the two institutions at the same address, help to create a breeding ground for new collaborations that can work as a A catalyst in the cultural -historical field? At least we live in the hope that it will give us new opportunities.

But maybe it's not that easy. We are not all rounded off the same, although we have Bornholm as our starting point.

So my story isn't necessarily your story.

Culture is often not something we think so much about in everyday life, even if it is a big part of our everyday lives - it is "just" until it is not there anymore.

Therefore, it is good sometimes to be reminded -what is our cultural history here on the island, what are we rounded off? What stories form our background and what stories would we like to pass on to the next on the island? Bornholm has over time been exposed to many changes that have influenced the island and our cultural identity.

At times, it has hit the island unforeseen, and it has taken some time to recover from the battle, turn the gun and find a new stand.

Now we are also affected by the winds of change, such as Energiø, but this time we know they are coming and we can actively choose to be a fellow player. There is no doubt that whether we want it or not, the island's self -understanding and our cultural identity will be affected.

We should not be so scared of the change.

But often, one has to know one's past to be able to build the future, and this is where I believe that our cultural history is an important player.

Cultural history can draw threads between past and present, but it is very much about what is happening right now and here.

One cannot say that there is "a" particularly strong Bornholm culture or history that we must develop. For who choose which story or which cultural topics are the most important? It's not just a story that creates the story of Bornholm. There are many stories that blend together and create a cultural identity on the island.

It is more important to create a framework in which the dissemination of the Bornholm cultural history can develop.

It can be a physical framework, and at Bornholm we have the unique framework that we are in a unified geographical area where we do not have to work across municipal boundaries and the like, which can provide restrictions elsewhere in the country. But it can also be a framework created by a collaboration between a wide range of actors -nineto can stand alone.

It is both the professional institutions, the volunteers who make a great effort around the island, and the municipality that will help to create cohesion in the culture.

One must see cultural history and its actors as an essential asset that can contribute to tourism as well as play a role in forming cultural identity for the island. The most important thing is that we talk together. Culture can contribute so much. We will not always agree on what is up and down, right or wrong. We are going to have each of our understanding and experience of things, but that is what culture can also - create debate and find common footing.

It is a waste of everyone's energy and economy on Bornholm.

Title: Ingen penge til ny klimaplan - Bornholm er på vej ud af national alliance
Content:
In fact, the new budget majority in the municipal council has announced Bornholm out of a nationwide Climate Initiative, because the budget majority will not invest in working with the climate plan that was adopted before the summer holidays. The unit list will prioritize differently and remove over a million dollars from the work on the energy island.

The municipal council adopted Bornholm's climate plan before the summer holidays, it happened with an accompanying recommendation to the politicians to devote money to hiring two employees who can continue to work with local CO2 reductions and climate adaptation. The five parties behind the budget agreement - the Social Democracy, Conservatives, the Danish People's Party, the Christian Democrats and the Bornholmer List - failed to finance the work.

The consequence seems to be that Bornholm Regional Municipality must opt ​​out of the broad cooperation of the climate alliance, which all the country's 98 municipalities and the five regions should participate in the support of the green think tank Concito and Realdania.

"If resources are not added to the work, the administration will not be able to lift the efforts in the climate transaction plan and in practice it will be to compile with an announcement of the climate alliance," the municipality's administration on the case wrote in June.

In the Unity List, it is believed that the downgrading of the climate plan will mean that Bornholm "de facto will resign from the climate alliance," says Helle Munk Ravnborg, person for the Nature, Environment and Planning Committee.

- I would not say it is a fear, because that is what is described in the case making, she says, elaborating on what consequences she expects a cancellation will have: - Now we do not know exactly what the climate alliance will deliver. But there is no doubt that there will be some exchange between municipalities and regions, and that there is the possibility of support of different kinds, both technical, professional and perhaps financially. It will be a shame to do without it. Conversely, we cannot pretend that we are with, without doing anything.

Partnerships and climate protection in danger Helle Munk Ravnborg points out that the municipality in the new climate plan is planning to engage in climate partnerships with agriculture, construction and the transport sector, so that these sectors can lower the CO2 imprint locally.

The plan is also about climate protection - both at the coasts, where the consequences of rising sea water must be mitigated, and inland, where rising rainfall and higher groundwater level risk creating flooding.

Storms, cloudbursts and droughts can lead to landslides, overloaded sewerage networks and broken buildings and port facilities, so the goal of the effort is to ensure that Bornholm can withstand climate change, the climate plan says.

Without hiring new employees working on these topics, this focus will be lost, the Unity List expects in an alternative budget proposal that the party announced on Tuesday, wants to allocate DKK 680,000 (equivalent to a man -year) to work with the climate plan.

- You can always discuss whether there should be one, two or three employees. I can't assess that at all. But if there is not at least one employee who has as his or her task to ensure that we think rising groundwater level and other climating in when new neighborhoods are being built or new districts, then it is difficult to see it is being done, says Helle Munk Ravnborg The Climate Plan also continues the ambitions of the Green Mobility Strategy, including a goal that 50 percent of the vehicles in public transport must be transferred to fossil -free Drive funds by 2025.

With the five budget parties' decision not to acquire ten new electric buses in 2024, but wait until 2025, 2026 and 2027 to lease five, ten and five emission -free buses respectively, this goal will not be met. The buses filled a lot in the budget negotiations, and the Unity List proposes in the new budget proposal to lease ten electric buses from December 2024 and twice twice five electric buses a year in 2025 and 2026.


Energy Island as distraction

At the same time, the Unity List is proposing to cut the municipality's new Energy Secretariat from three to one employee. According to the party, a downfall makes sense because the offshore winds and hydrogen project launched by the CIP and Ørsted will not be implemented for the time being. The unit list believes that attention to the energy island has become so large that the municipal council forgets the local efforts to reduce the emissions of greenhouse gases.

- You can say very well about the energy island, but it will not lower our climate imprint.

And that's what Bornholm's Climate Plan is all about.

After all, one can build the perspective that Bornholm, by adding area to the energy island, does extremely much to produce green energy and reduce global emissions, and that Bornholm can therefore afford not to invest in the green transition locally.

- Then this is the argument that one should unfold, instead of pretending, the energy island itself is doing something good about Bornholm's climate imprint.

I think you mix two tasks together, says Helle Munk Ravnborg, who voted for the climate plan despite dissatisfaction with the weighting of the energy island.

- You can see what is being emphasized in our own climate plan, and you can criticize that, I mean: That's all that is about Energiø and does not necessarily lead to lower CO2 imprints on Bornholm.

One of the two new positions in the Energy Secretariat that the Unity List wants to cancel is intended for the extra authority work with environmental screenings that Energiø Bornholm entails. The other energy worker must, among other things, work to secure permanent housing, new business opportunities at Bornholm, compensation for neighbors and low communication about the energy island.

Part of the money that can be saved will instead spend more knowledge about CO2 emissions when the municipality has to buy goods and services. Precisely CO2 accounts were crucial to the Unity List in the election campaign. On election night, where the party grew from two to seven mandates and became the municipal council's largest group, the Unity List provided the establishment of a new economy and climate committee. The unit list's attempts to gather a majority to implement CO2 accounts have since failed, and if the budget majority holds on to the decision not to dedicate a part-time employee to work for more climate-friendly purchases, Helle Munk Ravnborg believes that the committee could as well could as well renamed.

- If that doesn't happen, there's no reason why it is called an economy and climate committee.

Then it will just be an finance committee, she says.

As politicians outside the majority last week left the budget negotiations ahead of time, they indicated a lack of focus on the climate and green efforts as explanations. "As we interpret it, the green development will not () Until now the climate plan and biodiversity pool have been removed, because there are no employees to do it," said Søren Schow, after he and Heidi Burgedahl had traveled say from the negotiating table.

Stock Photo: William Sonne Kaalø.


Facts

Bornholm's Climate Plan Bornholm's Climate Plan "Bornholm as Testø and Role Model for Green Change" on 45 pages was adopted in June by the municipal council.

The plan's three main targets for CO2 emissions and climate efforts are: 2030: 70 percent reduction compared to 1990, equipped against climate change 2040: Fossil -free island and equipped against climate change 2050: Climate neutral and equipped against climate change in the plan, a vision has been formulated in four points: - Reduce CO2 emissions in all sectors to fulfill the target of climate neutrality Most recently by 2050.

- Conduct climate adaptation so that Bornholm is climate -robust now and in the future for the benefit of the citizen and business.

- Ensure ownership of the climate efforts of the citizens, associations, companies and other partners. Climate efforts must be relevant and express the economic, environmental and social gains associated with the transition.

- Develop and test new solutions that contribute to the solutions of the future and potentially the jobs of the future.

Title: Energiø Bornholm er ventetiden værd
Content:
Last Saturday, Bornholm's Journal brought the debate post "Energiø Bornholm - Waste of everyone's Energy", which speculates whether the government and Energinet are stepping on the brake and will not at all Energiø Bornholm.

It couldn't be further from the truth. In fact, on May 30 this year, the Folketing signed an additional agreement for offshore wind in Denmark, which initiates the supply of 3 Gigawatt offshore wind turbines and at the same time allocated funding of up to DKK 17.6 billion. DKK for the project.

In Energinet we work on high pressure to realize the Danish Parliament's decision. We have conducted feasibility studies at sea to map the underground, wave height, ocean currents and bird and wildlife.

We have done feasibility studies on land where nature and wildlife have been mapped. We have examined the Bornholm underground to map the area where we will build the land plant.

Over the winter we have held workshops on the location and design of the land facility. And before the summer holidays, we started the archaeological preliminary studies so that we can secure the Bornholm cultural heritage before we build.

All of the many studies also help to form the basis for the Danish Energy Agency's environmental assessment of the entire plan for Energiø Bornholm and the Environmental Protection Agency's environmental assessment of Energinet's land facilities and cables.

We fully understand that one can lose patience with the project, because it is urgent with the green transition.

But when it does not go as fast as one would wish, it is because we have to make sure that we do not unnecessarily affect the environment, that we find the best and cheapest suppliers and that we get to hear those who stay influenced by the project. It takes a long time, but it ensures that we get all the way around and eventually make the best possible project, which will bring green electricity to millions of households in Denmark and Europe. We hope you want patience with us - in return we promise that Energiø Bornholm will be worth the wait.

Title: Energiøen kan give os grønne brændstoffer
Content:
Is it possible to establish the production of hydrogen or green fuels on Bornholm? That question answers Rønne Harbor and the other actors in a large study "Yes" to. However, the calculations show that the price is drawing to be slightly higher than anywhere else in Europe, but there are many uncertainties in the figures, the partners behind the new Power-to-X report stated.

The first results of a so-called "feasibility study" about Power-to-X on Bornholm were presented at a press conference on Thursday. The main conclusion is that it will be possible to produce hydrogen and green fuels in connection with Energiø Bornholm.

There is sufficient power, the price of the power-to-X-fuel is not unrealistically high, there are potential customers, and there is sufficient wastewater on Bornholm to supply a plant with water.

- There are some options, but it does not mean that it will happen, summarizes Rønne Harbor's bulk manager, Maja Felicia Bendtsen, who was in the panel during the press conference at the old power plant in Rønne.

On the one hand, the Bornholmers and the municipal politicians must support the idea, and on the other, the companies must see an attractive business model for themselves, she points out. With the preliminary study, some results have been made that can be worked on and which - probably so important - do not bury the idea of ​​making hydrogen or green fuels on Bornholm.

Of course, the economy will be crucial, and the preliminary calculations show that the price of Bornholm hydrogen or ammonia is drawing to be slightly higher than with potential competitors.

- There are an incredible number of factors. We have been conservatives in the assumptions. It is not a prize that goes off, said Maja Felicia Bendtsen, who emphasized that there are opportunities to make the project more profitable.

- If you could make a supplement with solar cells, it would be quite interesting - also to get a slightly lower cost on production, she said.

Surplus heat for sale - costs may be at the slightly higher end of similar European projects, but that is before we recognize synergies, said Marie Münster, professor at DTU.

Sales of surplus heat or oxygen - the potential synergies - are not included in the figures.

Bornholm's Energy and Supply (BEOF) is, like District Heating and Wastewater Company, an obvious buyer - both of heat to the district heating network and oxygen, which can be used in the wastewater treatment plant.

BEOF has also participated in the work on the study, and the utility company's Deputy Director Klaus Vesløv noted that a large power-to-X plant in connection with the energy island will be able to cover the entire island's district heating needs if the separated district heating networks are tied together with new pipes.

"As we can figure out, we will be able to supply the entire district heating system with waste heat from a Powerto-X system with an overplanting setup," he said.

Access to water was one of the points that Maja Felicia Bendtsen emphasized in the presentation.

- There is plenty of wastewater available on Bornholm. It is important to me that we should not use drinking water, she said.

The wastewater from the Rønne area will be able to meet the need for a large power-to-X plant about twice. It will require a new treatment plant to manufacture water that can be used for electrolysis.

The Power-to-X study is based on surplus current from Energiø Bornholm and the possibility that the company that will own the wind farms wants to make use of the opportunity to set up more mills than there is capacity in the electric cables to Zealand and Germany - Called overplanting.

The supply of the Energy Island's offshore wind farms is screwed together in a way that the energy companies can choose to utilize an overcapacity of up to 0.8 gigawatts. The extra electricity capacity can be used for electrolysis.

In the first phase, by splitting water atoms (H2O) you can create hydrogen and oxygen. The hydrogen can then be refined to methanol or ammonia or other chemical compounds by adding an additional process where carbon or nitrogen is added respectively. These fuels can be used for shipping and fast ferries or supplying agricultural machinery and other heavy vehicles that cannot be immediately electrified. Another option is that the hydrogen is not processed but transported in pipelines to Germany.

The two main scenarios in the study are based on hydrogen production with transport to Germany and the production of ammonia on a large scale. The possibility of making methanol that require CO2 will be investigated in the coming months. The carbon for methanol can come from the Bornholm biogas plant, but due to CO2 button on Bornholm it will not be possible to produce methanol in close to the same quantities as ammonia or hydrogen.

The press conference ended with Maja Felicia Bendtsen handing over the first copy of the report to Søren Møller Christensen, who is the director of the partnership Baltic Energy Island, which at one point "will take over the task and run on with the ball".

He thanked for the new knowledge base.

- When making big decisions, knowledge is absolutely crucial. A large number of players have to make big decisions in the coming months and years, said Søren Møller Christensen, and mentioned a few examples:-There are developers who have to bid on the energy island and find out if they think of power-to-X . There is the utility company at Bornholm, which will find out if they want to be part of it, and the port should find out if they should make facilities available for shipping fuel.

And then there is the society Bornholm to find out what we do. What opportunities are there in it and how do we grab them? Work on mapping the Power-to-X potential runs out the year.


Facts

The Power-to-X shorting The project is supported with EU funds, which have been disseminated through the Danish Business Promotion Board.

Total EU support is DKK 6.4 million. DKK to a consortium with Rønne Harbor at the forefront. The work has also had the participation of eg. a. Ørsted, Skovgaard Energy, Topsoe, Danfoss operated, Ramboll, DTU Management, DTU Wind and Energy Systems, Bornholm Regional Municipality, Gate 21 and Bornholm Energi & Forsyning. In total, the consortium has invested an additional DKK 2.5 million.

DKK, so the total budget amounts to DKK 8.9 million. Kr.

Title: Vil power-to-X-anlæg være konkurrencedygtige? Det kræver måske bornholmsk betaling
Content:
If the Bornholm utilities are not interested in buying surplus heat and oxygen at a price that ensures extra revenue for a power-to-X company, it can be difficult to cope with international competition, DTU professor estimates. Other countries such as Morocco have with the combination of solar and wind energy better energy resources to PTX than in the Baltic Sea, but Bornholm has with the location close to a hydrogen-hungry industrial country like Germany other benefits.

At a press conference in Rønne on Thursday and in press releases that Port of Roenne A/ S published in both Danish and English, the partners presented the first conclusions from a long-awaited study on the possibilities of building power-to-X plants at Bornholm in connection with with the energy island.

The Journal, after the media, interviewed one of the DTU researchers who has helped to set up the models and count on the figures, professor of energy system analysis Marie Münster.

What speaks to the new knowledge that Power-to-X production at Bornholm can come true? - What is advocating - at least if we speak hydrogen or ammonia production, which we have focused on in the first place - is that resources are present in the form of wind and water, says Marie Münster.

She refers to the quantities of wastewater from the Rønne area and Energiø Bornholm's offshore wind farms, which with the opportunity to set up more mills on the same area, without the extra mills accessing the electricity grid (overplanting), can ensure enough power for the operation of a Large electrolysis plant.

The study focuses primarily on the production of hydrogen and ammonia on a large scale respectively, where the maximum number of mills is fully utilized. While hydrogen will probably have to be sent to Germany in pipes, ammonia in large quantities is primarily intended for the Baltic Sea shipping.

The report's financial calculations and comparisons with estimates of other European PTX projects show that Bornholm produced green fuels will not be unrealistically expensive.

- The prices are a bit at the high end, but you have to take that we have not calculated the income from possible sale of district heating or oxygen. It requires a little more details and negotiations with BEOF on what they might want to give to the heat and oxygen.

So there is a possible source of income that can get the price further down, says Marie Münster, who together with PH. D.- Student Endenicola's Campion has done a large part of the analysis work.

North African energy on the question of what speaks to the flourishing of a green fuel industry in Bornholm, Marie Münster points to the competitive situation.

- We often compare with Morocco who has really good sun and wind resources.

You get the cheapest fuel if you have a combination of the two things, says the DTU professor.

She explains that in Morocco there is plenty of room for solar parks, so if investors in North Africa can combine land wind turbines with solar cells, it will provide the cheapest possible power, which guarantees a high operating time on the power-to-X plants throughout the year.

However, a country like Morocco has a harder time improving the operating economy through the sale of oxygen and surplus heat, which in Denmark will be able to be sold to utilities or other companies.

- That is why it is so important to control these synergy potentials. If we do not get it, it can be quite difficult to compete with fuels produced elsewhere in the world.

A stable investment climate and access to qualified labor are other benefits that Denmark and Bornholm can utilize in their advantage in international competition, points out the DTU professor.

- If you have to borrow money, the price is different, depending on which country you want to place a plant in. In Denmark you have the advantage that you can get some cheap loans because it is a stable country with a good infrastructure and so on . By contrast, it costs more to borrow to build in, for example, Morocco.

Pipeline for German Industry If competition for green fuels makes it too expensive to produce ammonia on Bornholm, hydrogen may continue to be relevant.

- For the industry in Germany needs hydrogen, and a pipeline does not cost much to establish. As neighbors to Germany, we do not have to send the hydrogen through another country, and there are maybe some existing wires in Germany that can be converted.

Especially in relation to hydrogen, the location means a lot, says Marie Münster, who estimates that Bornholm has an advantageous geographical location.

- Bornholm is also pretty good if you were to supplement the Baltic countries with fuels, she adds.

For a fuel like ammonia, a short distance from the production site to consumers means less.

- It costs something to transport fuel from Morocco to the Baltic Sea, but not terribly much. For hydrogen, the location has a greater importance, says Marie Münster, before summarizing the possibilities.

- The good news is that it does not seem to be completely impossible to establish a plant that could become competitive on Bornholm, but we must be really good at utilizing the synergy potentials to make it competitive.

Title: Metanol i mindre skala kan laves med bornholmsk biogas
Content:
Ammonia or hydrogen will have to be produced in very large quantities, but liquid methanol is an alternative Powerto-X option that the local community can get easier by dealing with and applying.

The study of the possibility of realizing power-to-X production at Bornholm works with two main scenarios: 1) Hydrogen for export in Germany via pipes, and 2) ammonia production on a large scale in order to supply shipping.

But there are other options for what the X can stand for. Some of these need to be more thoroughly elucidated in the coming months.

- We have had a master student to start by looking at methanol and bio oil, and it also looks interesting. That's one of the things we want to look at a little more in the next phase of the project, says DTU professor Marie Münster.

Both hydrogen and ammonia are gases at ordinary air temperature and must therefore be compressed under pressure. This makes the substances more difficult to handle than methanol, which is on fluid form at room temperature.

- Hydrogen is a cumbersome fuel that has a low energy density. Ammonia also has a low energy density, and in addition it is toxic. Methanol is just easier to handle, and perhaps with methanol you can better meet a local need, and easier to imagine that more locally on Bornholm can quickly get started using that fuel.

Requires carbon ammonia requires nitrogen (nitrogen) which is not a scarce resource. If, on the other hand, you want to make methanol, CO2 must be added to the hydrogen, which is more expensive to produce. The most obvious CO2 source on Bornholm is biogas from Bigadan's facility at Aakirkeby, which can stand in front of a major expansion.

"Biogas contains about 40 percent CO2, which is why it is obvious to use CO2 from the biogas plant for any methanol production," the team behind the study in the presentation, which was presented at the press conference on Thursday.

Another bid for a carbon supplier is the power plant in Rønne, which uses wood chips as fuel and which in theory could be equipped with a system for CO2-catching. Since the cogeneration plant is likely to be phased out in the early 2030s when surplus heat from the energy island can be used in Rønnes District Heating, it is not an obvious CO2 source for methanol production.

A third option is to recover CO2 directly for the air, but this technology is currently far from ripe to delivering carbon in a realistic price range, says Marie Münster.

Can be better used locally If ammonia is to be produced, it is to achieve a competitive business model crucial that the plants become as large as possible.

In the calculation examples of hydrogen and ammonia, Energiø Bornholm's offshore wind farms are fully utilized, which means that the excess heat will exceed Bornholm's total district heating needs and may not be sold.

It will hardly be the case if methanol is to be produced.

- I do not think that the 0.8 gigawatts were completely utilized for a methanol system, because then the plant will be quite large and you will not have enough cheap carbon sources. So we imagine that if it becomes a methanol system, it will be somewhat smaller.

- Methanol systems do not necessarily have to be as big to have a good economy as the ammonia plants must be.

Therefore, you may be able to get a methanol system that fits the resources that are locally found and where you can utilize all the surplus heat.

The methanol potential may not be large enough to cover the Bornholm Line's fuel consumption.

If the ferries are to switch to green methanol, about 50,000 tonnes a year must be used, the study shows.

- In the small analysis we have done so far, where only CO2 is utilized from biogas production, we come up with covering 31 percent of fuel consumption on the Bornholm ferries.

With ammonia production on a large scale, on the other hand, we are up to covering something in the style of five percent of shipping traffic's overall needs throughout the Baltic Sea. It is ten times the consumption of Bornholm ferries, says Marie Münster, who notes that the potential of methanol can be increased if more of the possible CO2 sources can be exploited and counted.

Title: Anne Thomas vil være borgmester for Socialdemokratiet
Content:
After four years out of politics, former Deputy Mayor Anne Thomas has joined the Social Democracy and is now going to become mayoral candidate. Many at Bornholm have long encouraged her to return to politics, she says. But because she first joined the party in June, it will require an exemption before Anne Thomas can come into play for the role of top candidate.

Former Deputy Mayor Anne Thomas goes after becoming the next mayor of Bornholm. If so, for the Social Democracy, which she joined three months ago.

Thus, Maria Hach, one of the Social Democracy's two Bornholm Vice -Presidents, is no longer alone to go after the role of top candidate. In March next year, the members of the Social Democracy at Bornholm elect the party's number 1 for the municipal elections in November 2025.

- I have decided that I would like to join politics again. To recreate the confidence that everyone on Bornholm must have for the future, says Anne Thomas to Bornholm's Journal.

- I have found a new political position and joined the Social Democracy. Or in fact, I still have the same position: It was only a matter of what political family I could stand in with that position. It is the political scene that has moved. It's not me, she says.

Anne Thomas says that many people have long encouraged her to return to Bornholm politics, which she left with the title of Deputy Mayor in August 2019. This year it came to the fact that the Social Democracy also approached - and asked her to consider becoming mayoral candidate.

- I have been invited to stand to become the top candidate for the Social Democracy, and I have the courage to do that, she says.

There is still a "but". For the Social Democracy's statutes say that one must have been a member of the party for at least one year in order to become a candidate. And Anne Thomas first joined in June. Thus, she will only have nine months under the belt in the Social Democracy when S chooses the top candidate.

- So if I have to be a top candidate, the General Assembly in the Social Democracy must first give me an exemption to be able to stand. Next, I have to have enough votes to become a top candidate, says Anne Thomas.

Do you also set up for the Social Democracy at the next municipal elections if it does not become as a top candidate? - Yes. Whether it becomes as a top candidate or not, I am on the team for the Social Democracy at the next municipal elections.

Politicians must set direction to follow Bornholm politics from the outside was not difficult for Anne Thomas for the first two years. She had left politics on becoming director of the Center for Regional and Tourism Research (CRT) in Hasle, a position she still sits in.

Excited about her new job she did not want back.

It changed little by little after the last municipal elections.

- A lot has happened since I stepped out of politics. First, we have got a new municipal council that has no middle.

Some huge kinds have come, and a culture has come that is characterized by "I want" and by attributing to each other bad motives and talking badly about each other, says Anne Thomas.

- When I say that we must have restored confidence, I think of the municipal council.

But I also think of the confidence that must be between the municipality and the employees. I also think it is important to get back in place very quickly. For municipal employees, some are very important people.

- The desire to return to politics has first come in this election period. It has come more and more as the degree of trust has fallen.

The new unstable municipal council leads in Anne Thomas' eyes to the fact that quality is lost in political work - and for the municipal Bornholm lack of direction for where we are going.

- The municipal council has had a harder time talking together and finding out what it wants. Now we are two years into the election period and we still do not have a vision because the municipal council cannot agree on a vision. And when there is no vision, the politicians just sit down and pills down in the engine room.

I also know that many Bornholmers feel like I have it, she says.

- The turmoil also comes because we have politicians to sit down in the engine room and peel all the buttons. Politicians should not. The politicians must stand up on the bridge and stick out the direction.

- The municipal council is a board of directors and there are many ways to be a board of directors. But a golden rule is always that it is not the board that has to run daily operations, says Anne Thomas.

According to Anne Thomas, the frustration of what she saw in Bornholm politics has also been reflected in the fact that more and more people have encouraged her to line up again.

- In this election period, it has also happened more and more often that people have said "Can't we get you back?" And "It could have been you who was mayor". I have more and more met this "you should join," she says.

- There is a lack of seriousness about making the collaboration work. But I chose to go myself, so first I felt like I wouldn't say how I felt about how things are running now.

It's just gotten harder and harder, and I take the consequence of now by line up.

- Personally, I feel close to my political "opponents", but I can't see that culture in this municipal council, says Anne Thomas.

- There was not one that I could not join the municipal council that I was a part of. Nor can I point to one in the current municipal council that I cannot.

Children, jobs and Energiø In addition to wanting to lead a broad collaboration, Anne Thomas points out first and foremost in three places where she will put in if she first becomes mayoral candidate and then mayor.

It's the economy and budgets. These are the children's terms. And then it is to secure the welfare of the future on Bornholm by getting more people to move to and secure more labor. She sees a main road to it in the upcoming Energiø.

She also misses that Bornholm finds out what we want out.

- I want to emphasize that Bornholm will be a good place for children to grow up and thus also a good place to grow old. The key to making the elderly care work is that we make we make the children's area work. Because it's about finding a solution where we have enough hands. It requires new labor and many of the people have children, says Anne Thomas.

- With the new budget we have seen the Youth Council been very disappointed, and we have seen the families of children in Rønne be very disappointed that the two schools will be one district. We need to be careful about saving the children to transfer money to the elderly area. Because it only keeps the pants warm for a short time.

- If I become a top candidate, I will also work for a broad majority around that Bornholm gets the most out of the energy island. And that we first really set out to find out what we want out of the energy island, says Anne Thomas.

If Anne Thomas becomes the next mayor, it will be for a municipality with a significantly poorer economy than the one she left just over four years ago.

She will not comment in detail on the new municipal budget because she did not participate in the negotiations herself. But she finds overall next year's budget "financially responsible" and she welcomes that.

But if she becomes mayor herself, she will run the budget work in a different way.

- Some municipalities set very long -term budgets, and I think we will benefit from that too. And that we as politicians set some goals to get there and there in four years, says Anne Thomas.

- We have to say "This is what we would like to achieve with this budget". And then the municipality's administration must give some concrete suggestions on how it can be done. And then we as politicians have to say "it's too ambitious" or "it's not ambitious enough". But we need to have a political dialogue where the roles are clearly distributed.

I have decided that I would like to join politics again. To recreate the confidence that everyone on Bornholm must have for the future.

Anne Thomas (S), mayor.

Title: Trøst om Bornholms mulige udtræden af klimasamarbejde: ' Jeg ved det ikke'
Content:
Although no money was allocated in the budget agreement to work with Bornholm's new climate plan, climate efforts will not be completely stalled, Mayor Jacob assures comfort.

When Bornholm's Climate Plan - a 45 -page document with local CO2 reduction targets and concrete green focus areas and plans for climate adaptation - was adopted in June, the municipal council failed to put money into employees who can work on making the many words into climate action.

Neither did the budget agreement prioritize the political majority of the climate plan, although the municipality's administration had warned in advance that it would mean that Bornholm could not take part in a new national climate cooperation between municipalities and regions.

"If resources are not added to the work, the administration will not be able to lift the efforts in the climate transaction and in practice it will be to compile with an announcement of the climate alliance," the office wrote in June.

Mayor Jacob Trøst (K) cannot yet say whether the consequence of the budget agreement will be that Bornholm must leave the climate cooperation.

Do you expect BRK to remain in the climate alliance, now that the budget agreement was not allocated funds for new man -years to work with the climate plan? - I don't know. I will explore the possibilities within the framework we have, Jacob Solvet writes in a response to the Journal.

Title: Power-to-x: 'Vi har med vilje ikke sagt, hvor det kan ligge'
Content:
An electrolysis system will fill 20-30 hectares if the purpose of Power-to-X on Bornholm is to make hydrogen, while ammonia production will require at least as large area as the energy island's high voltage station. But where at Bornholm should such large industrial plants be built? That question slides the authors of the EU-funded Power-to-X report around.

- Then there is the hard - where should it be? We have not decided in any way.

This is how Rønne Harbor Maja Felicia Bendtsen said about the location of Power-to-X facility on Bornholm, as a report stated that it will be possible to make hydrogen or green fuels, was published on Thursday.

The report mentions no specific suggestions on where to build an electrolysis plant for hydrogen production or an even larger ammonia factory. But figures are set on how large areas of construction will require.

An electrolysis system will fill 20-30 hectares, depending on which technology is chosen. 30 hectares is twice as large as the area of ​​Rønne Harbor added with the port expansion in 2019. 30 hectares also correspond to 42 football fields, which you will have to find space for if the X in "Power-to-X" ends with to become hydrogen to be exported in pipes to Germany.

Ammonia production on a large scale requires approximately 70 hectares for the plant itself as well as an additional area for a safety zone, the scope of which according to the report will depend on a risk assessment. In total, the need for space will come in line with the energy island's high voltage station if ammonia is to be the end product.

In the elaborate, EU-supported report, it is assumed that the wind energy from Energiø Bornholm is fully utilized, and as a general rule, one must expect the capacity of the plant to be as large as possible to become profitable. While ammonia will require large-scale production, however, an initial, however, indicates that it may be possible to produce green methanol or bio oil on Bornholm in smaller quantities, DTU professor Marie Münster told the Tidende the other day.

If a company wants to make ammonia or methanol for shipping on Bornholm soil, in addition to the production plant, a warehouse will have to be built and the report is presented in the report three basic scenarios for how to place Powerto-X plants and a tank plant in relation to each other and a shipping port (see fact box).


DELIBERATELY

Back to where on Bornholm it can all lie it is not a matter of course that an electrolysis plant is produced next to the high voltage station on South Bornholm. The current can be carried in cables to another place, and elsewhere in the country.

The authors of the report merely outline what considerations to take. There are, among other things, maps of the local electricity grid, nature -protected areas, the district heating network, streams, coastal proximity zone and cultural -historical sites. A total of 16 different parameters can influence the location.

- We have not intentionally said where it can be. There are so many factors that need to be taken into account. That is why we will not point to anything, says Maja Felicia Bendtsen to the Journal.

Wasn't it intended that you should designate possible locations? This is what it looks like in the presentation for the study.

- No, we have not wanted to put precise addresses on.

Let's fix one thing: Can a Power-tox system be at Rønne Harbor? - Immediately my answer is no, because we need Rønne Harbor for other things.

What about fuel tanks at the harbor - is there room for them? - We can't answer that. If a hydrogen pipeline ends up to Germany, there should be no stock anywhere at all.

But if the product is to be green fuels for ship traffic or the ferries that you are planning with Bornholm Bunker Hub, should there be a warehouse somewhere? - Yes, says Maja Felicia Bendtsen, head of the bulk area at Rønne Harbor. Long approval process When you see your plan for the next stages of the port expansion, you can see no thought on the map.

- That's right, and it's because we don't know what's going to happen yet. We have an ambition about it and do different studies, but we don't know. And in the end, it is not our ambition that it is Rønne Harbor that should build such a tank plant, but the goal is to attract someone who will build it.

In the appearance, a tank plant for green fuels will be reminiscent of the existing oil tanks that Q8 and YX have standing on the part of the harbor closest to the residential quarters. It is in the cards that any tanks for ammonia or methanol will be erected further away from the city, says Maja Felicia Bendtsen. Getting a new tank plant approved by the authorities will take at least 18 months and the application must come from the company that will build a tank plant.

- It is a very long, cumbersome process, and that is why we cannot think of a card, because we cannot implement the process.

Is part of the port area so close to the city that today you will not be able to obtain permission? - I am glad that we have a tank plant at Rønne Harbor, so that we can supply Bornholm with gasoline and diesel. Should I be honest, I do not think that today you will be allowed to place similar tanks so close to buildings. But it was built in another time, and today you make some sharper demands on safety. On the other hand, I would say that the long process reassures me that it will not be dangerous, says Maja Felicia Bendtsen.

The EU-supported study emphasizes that placing tanks for ammonia or methanol at Rønne harbor can be difficult.

"Storage of e-fuel at the port of Rønne is a sensitive topic because of its proximity to a densely populated city. To address this concern, a comprehensive strategy involving the public is recommended. By engaging society in the decision-making process, potential Concerns and problems are solved proactively, promoting transparency and trust ”.


Location of PTX system and tanks

The study indicates three scenarios for the location of a power-to-x system and a storage system with fuel tanks. 1) The power-to-X system is placed inland while the tanks are erected at Rønne Harbor.

2) The Power-to-X plant and warehouse are together inland some distance from the export port.

3) Both the Power-to-X plant and the warehouse are built at a new port.

The last total solution, which, due to the construction of a new port, occurs at least realistic has several benefits as one does not have to carry the fuel in pipes or tankers across the island: “A location where PTX and the warehouse are close to the export site, would be the optimal scenario as you avoid transport, ”says the report on option 3.

Title: Store dele af Bornholm får udsigt til energiøens vindmøller
Content:
Far inland you will be able to see Energiø Bornholm's wind turbines, according to consultation material from the Danish Energy Agency.

Whether you stand at Ruts Church, at the Queen's Rock or at Dueodde, you will be able to see the wind turbines that rise as part of Energiø Bornholm. This is stated in documents that the Danish Energy Agency has submitted for consultation. How visible the mills become depends on which model you end up choosing, but visible they become.

The State Energinet works with four different scenarios, where the number of mills, the height of them and the size of the wings vary. For all of them, the mills will be visible from large parts of Bornholm, southern Sweden and German Rügen. So it is not only along the coast on the western side of the island that you will be able to see the wind turbines.

"From Bornholm there are large areas of the inland, from which the wind turbines can also be experienced," says the visibility analysis that is part of the current consultation material.

Red light at night The analysis is based on seven vantage points, five of which are located here on Bornholm: Galløkken, Boderne and Dueodde along the coast as well as Ruts Church and the Queen Rock inland. The five places have been selected in collaboration with Bornholm Region Municipality, which has also proposed other vantage points. Kaolinsøen, Tassevej, Klintebakken, Kadeau, Arnager and Slusegård have, however, been deselected and are not included in the visibility analysis.

There are several factors that determine how visible the wind turbines will be from land.

The color of the mills plays a role, and bright shades mean that the mills coincide with the surroundings to a greater extent.

The weather also has something to say, and the clearer it is, the more visible the mills are.

For the sake of aviation and maritime security, the wind turbines are probably equipped with light. Therefore, they will also be visible after dark, the light will at least.

Title: Lad os tage arven med i en grøn fremtid
Content:

Bornholm has long been known for its unique taste, from the smoked fish, the delicate cheeses and sour sea buckthorn berries for award -winning beer and the taste of local ingredients at our large selection of fantastic restaurants.

Our island is recognized as a gourmet destination and we are proud of our Bornholm foods. But how can we take our food heritage to the next level and at the same time contribute to green change and development at Bornholm? As Business Manager for Business Center Bornholm and with a background on the island, I have seen Bornholm undergo many changes over the years. We have gone from the greatness of fishing to a time of decline in the number of inhabitants and businesses - a reality that has fortunately begun to turn to the positive. That is why it is so important that we always think in development instead of settlement - it is and will be my mantra. Bornholm is an island with incredible potential and we have a unique opportunity to shape our own future. But in order for this to happen, it is important that companies, inhabitants and politicians support and are open to new opportunities and that we dare to put turbo together.

Bornholm is already known for its diverse food production, across smaller producers and experience food for slaughterhouse, agriculture and dairy, and these companies account for many jobs.

I think we can be proud of our versatile food industry from the farmer, ensuring food supply to the world market for the many niche products that ensure the local identity and food experience.

But we can't rest on the laurels. Green transition is the key to a sustainable future, and we are already on the right path. A good example is the production of plant proteins, such as lenses and peas, an important alternative protein source for meat that is already underway on the island. This shows our ability to adapt to a world of development and the demand of future consumers.

But there is room for more, much more.

Because there are many issues and potentials, and it is important that we take them seriously and act on them. A selection of the challenges and opportunities that I am concerned with are: · The changed consumer behavior due to climate change where local goods with a low CO2 imprint will only become more and more in demand. Can Bornholm make a strong network that makes it easy for the grocery store to choose locally for the shelves and which makes consumers aware of that choice? · New, protein -based groceries that meet consumer demand. It will be obvious to make located foods, not only the crops themselves, but also meat alternatives such as Seitan and Tofu. Can't Bornholm Gourmet stamp be used here? · We have many manufacturers who want to process raw materials, but they depend on the supply of high quality raw materials. How do we create the best possible collaborations that allow the manufacturers to get it locally, even if it is in small quantities? · We are going to see an ever -increasing focus on being self -sufficient in private and in small communities, both with green, eggs and meat. Should a better opportunity is created here to get slaughtered locally, without being a primary producer? And can private food communities be supported and helped to become associations that can collaborate across the sale of surplus production? · Climate change that we are already experiencing.

What crops can and should we grow and how do we secure ourselves as best as possible against drought and cloudburst? Should we look at Samsø and their use of water reservoirs or are there any other alternatives that can be made for business potentials? · Bornholm in Global Context. How can we help ensure food in a world where there is a bigger and greater shortage of them? The more we ourselves nationally and locally import, the less there are to others. So how do we make sure to take care of the majority of what we eat in a way where the manufacturer can still live off of it and the consumer can afford to buy it? How can we optimize food systems and increase coherence across the supply chain, based on big data? · Food, the upcoming Energiø Bornholm and Power-to-X technology can together have a positive meaning. Our future as Food Island and Innovation Center is closely linked to our ability to develop new products and business areas. The Energy Island and the Power-to-X process will give us new resources such as surplus heat and hydrogen. Bornholm should take advantage of these resources to create innovative food companies, in the business park that can be built in connection with the Energy Island.

In order for us to succeed in the green transition and the development of the food of the future, both in raw materials and production, we must also attract new businesses, innovation and research to Bornholm. We need to cherish our island and everything we are good at - but we must also receive help and knowledge where it strengthens us. And shouldn't that lead to both new inhabitants and more tax dollars? Through Bornholm's commercial lighthouse around the energy island and the consortium behind Baltic Energy Island, we are already working to attract education and innovation to Bornholm, and we are on the way to becoming a center for energy technology and green solutions.

We can also do this, with a focus on food and in a strong coupling, so we think the development of different areas in context and not in silos.

At Business Center Bornholm, it is very important for us to support the green transition and development, through sparring, guidance and workshops for the island's entrepreneurs and companies - and we constantly seek out opportunities for projects that can finance that we can be allowed to go Even more in depth with it. All companies and entrepreneurs with a good idea can book a meeting with BCB - we are ready to do everything we can to help develop and transform existing companies and attract new businesses.

But in order for us and the companies to succeed, everyone must contribute to the food of the future, both consumers and producers. We cannot create new and change the world - or just Bornholm, without even changing anything.

Together we can shape a green future for Bornholm, where our food heritage and sustainability go hand in hand.

Title: Folketingspolitiker: Episode med sejlbåd giver flashbacks til den kolde krig
Content:
