In the upcoming defense settlement, it must be taken into account that Bornholm is a front line to the east, the politician believes.

Peter Juel-Jensen gets flashbacks for the Cold War as the Journal asks for a comment on the story that one of the defense's patrol vessels back in September followed a Russian sailboat for five hours in the waters southwest of Bornholm.

- Now we do not know the sailing boat's intentions, but there are some flashbacks for the Cold War, where we have to pay close attention to what is happening in our territorial waters, says Bornholm MP Peter Juel-Jensen. He is the Vice -President of the Defense Committee and former defense mayor.

- I have been happy and relieved for many years after the wall fell, and we lived in a significantly more peaceful world. Now we are forced to look each other deep in the eyes and say: The security policy situation we have had since 1989, when the wall fell, no longer exists. Now we are forced to think our security and defense policy into everything we do.

As Peter Juel-Jensen himself mentions, we do not know the intentions of the sailboat. Tidende has asked the Russian Embassy in Denmark, but the embassy has not returned to our inquiry. Neither did the Defense Command have wanted to disclose why the sailboat was closely followed for five hours, other than that you follow the ship traffic.

However, the local parliamentary politician believes that the episode gives rise to an emphasis that Denmark should be aware that there are 'others' who are watching at -lo —ligsom that' we ', to the extent that we have the opportunity,' holding Eye with them '.

- You can be very indignant about that, but the fact that we always have insight into what each other is doing, I also see as some guarantee that you will not be taken on the bed with something . We are aware - we are watching each other, says Peter Juel -Jensen.


'We're Front Line'

Most of all, in the current security policy situation, he is afraid that the human factor may have major consequences in a given situation.

- I am a dog rose for some fighter pilot from Russia or a Russian inspection ship to start opening fire or making something strange that makes it a human factor that triggers some kind of crisis, he says, adding: - So the more we know about each other and each other's intentions, the better it is.

The government and the other parties are on the threshold to start negotiating a new defense settlement. Over the next 10 years, DKK 143 billion has been set aside for investments in the Danish defense, which according to Peter Juel-Jensen is 'immensely many billions'.

This is also why he has invited his party partner, Defense Minister Troels Lund Poulsen (V), to Bornholm on Tuesday.

- I can listen to at Christiansborg that there has been a perception that Denmark is a transition country. If and if the worst possible thing was to happen, then it is Denmark's role that we must be able to ensure that allied units get through Denmark as soon as possible and on to the Baltic States, says Peter Juel-Jensen, who does not completely agree with , to look at it so black and white.

- I just want to say that as a Bornholmer and as a Bornholm elected politician, my approach is a little different. I think I'm a front line. We are over here. So it may well be that we are a small country. We are a transit country, but we are spider -embroidered also front line, he says.

Episodes will have an impact on settlement. According to Juel-Jensen, we got to see in connection with Nord Stream. We see that with the mentioned episode with the Russian sailboat -but also with the other events below the surface recently found in the northern part of the Baltic Sea.

- It is becoming a weekly recurring event that there is something. We are front line. I would like to take this into account in an upcoming defense settlement - but also in the agreements we make with each other across the Baltic Sea, between us who want each other well. That is one of the things I would like to have the Minister of Defense to see with his own eyes before disposing the funds available in an upcoming defense settlement, says Peter Juel-Jensen.

Does the events have a bearing on the way to go into the defense conciliation negotiations do you think? - Far along the way, yes. We are forced to screw a defense settlement together so that it takes into account what is happening in the air, on the sea surface - but also what happens below sea level. We haven't had what happens under the surface on the radar for a long time. We need to have that now, says Peter Juel -Jensen, who further argues: - It must be seen in the context of being Energiø in the future. We will supply large parts of the energy supply to Zealand, but there is also a mains line to Germany. So there will be another infrastructure that we need to keep an eye on. I assume that is going to be able to be seen in an upcoming defense settlement.

Title: Kan man lære at designe fremtidens fødevaresystemer på Bornholm?
Content:
Each year, 15 research students visit Gaarden in Melsted to learn about what the place means for the way we set up our future sustainable food supply.

The fact that Bornholm has had its name engraved on the gastronomic scene is no news. For example, if you read the New York Times, Guardian, Sydsvenskan or Vogue, you will already be well informed about everything that Bornholm stands for culinary. But that Bornholm as a food island is also known in the research world that deals with something as long -haired as food systems -it is probably less well known.

But in fact, the universities in Lund and Copenhagen together with Gaarden and Gourmet Bornholm have for the past five years with great success held a so -called summer school, which has attracted research students from most of the world. It is true that when you have to be a researcher, the road goes through a so-called PhD study. It typically takes three years, has a well -defined topic, a lot of teaching and last but not least a number of courses. The annual summer school called Food, Place & Innovation is such a course offer.


Food systems for lunch?

Over the past decade, the entire food research has become more and more concerned with the idea of ​​the systemic and holistic perspective.

A sustainable food system is closely related to being able to think about circular food economy, waste sorting and, not least, energy and water supply in new and more sustainable ways. So the idea that "everything is connected".

Here Bornholm is obviously a really good example. Bornholm is not just a food island. It is also an energy island, it is an island that has a clear strategy for zero waste and it is a natural island. Bornholm is also a really good example, because networks and contacts in a very special way arise and maintained. It is exceptionally rich in a very special kind of capital - not the one we can put in the bank - but the one that scientists like to call it social capital. For example, it makes it much easier to arrange field visits, and it makes it much easier to exemplify and visualize the idea of ​​a coherent food system.

Another important reason why the summer school benefits from lying in a remote place like Bornholm at a time when the vacant auditoriums at both Lund and Copenhagen Universities are almost in line to be used, yes it is "the place". And the place is very important in our context because we use a particular form of learning that we call situated or place -based learning. We have good experience that if one has to learn to understand the whole complex concept that is called a food system and not least understand how the food system is closely integrated into an agricultural system, in an energy system and not least in a circular food perspective -Ja then is then is One simply has to combine lectures with field visits. You have to talk to practitioners and you have to see both feel, sense and feel. And in that regard, Bornholm is a really good framework that the students enjoy a great advantage and joy of.

As an important part of the summer school, the students must come up with suggestions for innovations that promote a green food change.

And here our set up is ideal because the students can use the many field visits to find the informants they have to use in their tasks.


Is there a special Bornholm food story?

And at the same time, holding the course at Bornholm provides a unique opportunity to understand how the identity of the Bornholm foods is created in an interaction between the particular biological and geographical conditions and the linguistic practices that are developed into narratives.

And that is why we are also well underway to parallel to collecting data for our research project Sunrise over Gudhjem - The Making of the Bornholmer Food Narrative.

And the last thing we have just been lucky to invite you to the conference that, under the title "Mapping Key Challenges to Sustainability on Islands", which with, among other things, the Baltic Selection in the back was carried out at Holmön in Sweden in the days from 12 to 14.

October this year.

On top of that, there is great interest and incredible openness when we go in search of new places for our field visits every year. We have a natural core of places that go again. But we also attach great importance to having some renewal and variation in the course This openness and interest we also find when it comes to the perspectives in Bornholm as an educational island. A fixed program point is therefore a full day at Campus Bornholm.

Another essential point is that Bornholm is not surrounded by "Denmark" but in the center of the Baltic area. That is, with an "Outlook" to both Scandinavia, Northern Europe and the Baltic States. In fact, it is of great importance in our international marketing, and of course it has a huge impact that Bornholm is not only innovative and develops oriented when it comes to food, but also when it comes to energy and waste management.

In terms of research, we see that there is great interest in new types of consumers, gastroturists, nature tourists, sustainability tourists, experience tourists a cetera. This means trying to understand destination development in relation to this new type of traveler.


Situated education - an opportunity for Bornholm

For us as an educational institution, it is particularly interesting to work with the boarding format.

It offers some extra opportunities when it comes to group work because we have the students 24/7. And it is extra interesting because we know that there is great interest in the idea of ​​Bornholm as an educational island and not least the idea of ​​situated education or Residential College Education, as it is called internationally. This means that in practice you will be able to take courses or shorter courses on Bornholm.

And it is not least interesting in the discussion about how future education should be screwed together. So what type of educational offerings would you, for example, be able to put on an island like Bornholm? Traditionally, but have thought that you are moving whole institutes or education from the major cities to the rural areas. But if you think instead courses or modules, you can technically imagine hybrids.

Bornholm will give Bornholm some very good opportunities for innovation by becoming strong to design modules, courses and tailor -made special courses.


See you this summer?

We are in full swing with the planning of version 2024 of the course - the sixth of the kind, and we expect it to end in a month.

Title: GENERATION GRØN
Content:
Young people show interest in education and career with a focus on green transition.

Green change has become an essential factor that affects the young people's educational choices and career paths. This is shown in a new study from the Danish Evaluation Institute (EVA). According to the study, 15% of all Danish students have made green transition a significant criterion for their educational choices, and almost a quarter of young people want to work in green transition after graduation.

It is especially in the technical education that the desire to contribute to green transition is clear, and in a mention of the study published at EVA. dk, says Andreas Pihl Kjærsgård, senior consultant: - It makes good sense that green transition is most important for those who choose technical education, because here you train many of the employees who have to work in sectors and with tasks to do moving our society towards the green transition.

However, this does not mean that green transition does not also have a role to play on other programs, he estimates. And it is Søren Møller Christensen, CEO of Baltic Energy Island, touching agrees. He says: - Although certain programs, such as the blacksmith and electrician programs, are important for the green transition, all education is relevant to the green transition .

He elaborates: - Green change is a challenge that touches on all aspects of society, and it is crucial that different perspectives are contributed.

Energy Island's Future Muligher The Green Interest among the Young Thus, is awakening enthusiasm at Søren Møller Christensen, who together with partners such as Campus Bornholm, DTU and Bornholm Regional Municipality is working to make Bornholm a center for green educational opportunities. He describes the concept as "Generation Energiø" and explains: - The term covers that we want to emphasize our common targeted efforts to offer attractive educational opportunities at Bornholm - including parts of university education and a strengthening of vocational education.

Educational choices are, of course, influenced by a large number of factors, and it is not only the ambition of helping to "save the world" that is a significant driving force for young people, Christensen acknowledges.

- My impression is that many young people are also aware of where the job opportunities are in the future. There are good future opportunities in helping to move society in a more sustainable direction, not just on Bornholm or in Denmark, but worldwide.

He adds that the career opportunities within the green transition are of course also aimed at the elderly who want to change career tracks or to be professionally qualified at all.

- In a time when climate change and CO2 emissions are global challenges, the focus on green transition is becoming more important. Whether you are already in business or are faced with stepping into it, it will be important to have knowledge of green transition. In the future, we expect to see a big shift from the jobs that have a significant CO2 emissions for those who are working to reduce it.

Even Baltic Energy Island is also actively working to promote green energy. Together with a large number of local and national partners, the fund is already working with local businesses, and they will also strengthen cooperation with schools and higher education, says Christensen: - We participate, among other things. a. At Bornholm's Education Mass (BUM) to make the different options visible, and my hope is that we together with, among other things. a. Bornholm regional municipality can introduce Generation Energiø with green teaching already in the small classes, so that you get the understanding of the green transition as early as possible.

Title: Trøst med opråb til Christiansborg: Bornholm bliver forbigået
Content:
More certainty is needed about and how Bornholm benefits directly from the upcoming energy island. This is what Mayor Jakob Consolation believes.

The potential for Bornholm is great, but there is a lack of clarity on exactly what Bornholm gets out of laying the sea and land for the upcoming energy island.

This is stated by Mayor Jacob Trøst (K) in a press release from the municipality.

- When it comes to the direct gains, Bornholm has so far been bypassed. This is now clear after the Danish Energy Agency Has rejected Bornholm Regional Municipality's desire for a community contribution from the winner of the offshore wind turbine offering. Therefore, there is a political answer to the question of compensation for the burdens the energy island will also cause.


Government must be on the field

Therefore, Jakob Consolation believes that the government must get on the field and make it clear how the energy island will directly benefit the island.

- It's about the Bornholm citizens being assured that it is worthwhile to take responsibility for the green transition. Otherwise, the state risks that the popular support is reduced, he says in the announcement.

According to Jakob Consolation, questions about compensation must be seen in the light of the fact that the municipality was entitled to DKK 500 million if it was an open door-offshore wind turbine project located 14.9 kilometers from the coast. This corresponds to DKK 165,000/MW, the press release states.

According to the mayor, the energy island falls between two chairs when it comes to local and municipal gains.

- On the one hand, Energiø Bornholm is not covered by the schemes intended to promote the local population's acceptance and commitment to the development of wind turbines and solar cells, and on the other hand the political agreement on the tender framework for Energiø Bornholm does not have the opportunity to demand a social contribution from the winner of the offering, the message to the press says.

A unilateral focus on the award in the political agreement prevents tendering parameters that can benefit the locals, incorporated into the tender material, continues the call to Christiansborg.


New play gives little optimism

In October, the government presented a play titled; 'Climate Action - Together on More Green Energy from Sol and Wind on land', which sets the framework for the extension of renewable energy on land with 12 concrete initiatives, including must ensure local support.

In this connection, it is planned that an analysis of possible gains and compensation schemes for neighbors for particularly large electricity transmission plants must be prepared. And after all, it pleases the mayor.

- The play indicates that the government has listened and that there is a political agreement that the local community must be compensated to ensure continued support for the green transition. But we are far from in goal yet. With the Danish Energy Agency's announcement in mind, it is now crucial that Christiansborg has a look for a political agreement to be made, which rewards both neighbors to the land facility and the wider Bornholm community, says Jacob Trøst.

Title: Vi drømmer ikke om en erhvervspark, men om et eventyr
Content:
Bornholm needs a green business adventure. Here are five suggestions to make it end happily.

Iet radio show recently expressed the mayor very properly that we citizens have many opportunities to get the municipal council into speech and that hearings are not the only way to make their opinion known. So here are my "five things to take with the next time you speak Energiø".


1. Our young people deserve opportunities

A friend hit the spot with me when she said the other day, "What interests me the most is whether there will be good jobs here in the future for my children. I want my grandchildren to grow up nearby and experience The childhood you can have here. All municipalities are screaming for more labor. But those who have the most companies actually have it easiest. As a newcomer, the job is crucial, but job opportunities in the majority are better.

Danes, and especially the young people have become very mobile. They often move in groups of friends. They choose places that can give them a good life with family, nature and development opportunities. Life must be meaningful and the job must be exciting.

Working with sustainable development is attractive because it is experienced as both meaningful and exciting.

We have many positions.

More are an advantage.


2. Business Park and Energiø

Do not let Bornholm like Energiø confine itself to a transformer station and a power-to-X system. For the ordinary Bornholmer, it is not the plants that are interesting, even with a view tower, more nature and hiking trails they can probably become difficult to love. No, it is the possibilities in the wake of these plants that may prove to be the orange in a turban. Surplus heat, new networks, new demand. Should we be bornholmers swallow a bitter pill, let the state give us some syrup to swallow it with. Give us the ticket for a green business adventure. Let a business park be part of Energiø investments.


3. Don't be afraid to think big

The image of a large transformer station not far from Sose Strand may one day become a postcard worthy. Right now it's not in my glossy picture. It does not mean that small is good. And not at all when we talk about business parks. A business park is basically just a line on a map, a piece of field with a lease agreement. A large business park is therefore no worse or better for us cycling to the beach next summer. However, the size of the area is crucial to how attractive it can be for new businesses to move here.

If many companies then settle down, then a big business park is no longer just a big pasture. Then it has turned into buildings full of something I and my friend today can only dream of: green jobs for our young people.

I have great respect for our local farming. But this is not where most young people dream of a career. The reality is probably that agriculture is not for all eternity to make up 60 percent of our area. We have 34,100 hectares of agricultural land on Bornholm. So don't think small, don't be afraid to draw a big line around the plans for the green business park. But put high demands on the companies that must then build there.


4. New knowledge and new networks

A profession does not just consist of many individual companies. It is a network of value chains. The raw material in the field that was plowed in the spring turns into a summer menu at the restaurant. A menu that was drawn by the local graphic artist while the farmer's tractor was in a workshop. Quietly, together we become more proficient and more dependent on each other.

The more interdependent we are, the harder it is just to think completely and basically new thoughts.

New businesses have new needs and come with new knowledge. It gives oxygen to the duck pond. And right now we have more than ever need to think new.

12 percent of our workplaces are found in industries that are defined by the Climate and Conversion Council as particularly "climate-exposed". If we do not reinvent ourselves, then we will really suffer from CO2 fees and harsh customer requirements.

It will be beneficial for Bornholm's total business, to renew the island's value chains, that we get greener companies - very much like someone who can inspire and present practical problems that need to be solved. We are pretty firm for that.


5. Odd children can play best

Several of our local businesses are world -class. They have strong craftsmanship, good development and healthy exports. But we do not have many highly educated, and are not at the forefront of the digitization wave.

The high -tech companies we can wait will settle here are in many ways quite the opposite.

The two types of companies can thus compliment each other. But they basically speak a very different language.

The Danish business promotion system is screwed together so that the local business service must primarily take care of business promotion at each company.

Getting development and collaboration to happen through a whole new value chain is something a little different.

Therefore, when you put the desire for a large business park in the Christmas sock, make a small extra wish with: Set the requirements for what the secretariat for this business park should be able to. Of course, they need to attract new businesses. Of course, they must support companies there in utilizing waste heat and contributing to research. But add the third thing that it is the secretariat's responsibility to increase cooperation with the local business community.

After all, we do not dream of a green business park in Sydbornholm, we need a business adventure on the whole island.

Title: Minister afviser at forholde sig til Trøsts opråb til Christiansborg
Content:
Despite political concerns about whether Bornholm is being compensated sufficiently for burdens at the upcoming energy island, the Minister of Energy will not relate to the matter.

On Tuesday, Mayor Jacob Trøst (K) came with a call to be all the way to Christiansborg.

The Danish Energy Agency's refusal of the municipality's desire for a community contribution from the winner of the offshore wind turbine offering raises concerns at Snorbakken. Specifically, the mayor is concerned about whether the government is aware that Bornholm is compensated "for the burdens that the Bornholmers are imposed by laying the country and horizon for 'a pioneering project within the green transition'.

Since Tuesday, Tuesday has tried to get an interview with the responsible minister, Lars Aagaard of the Moderates. On Thursday, his press service denies that he will line up. Otherwise, the Journal would have liked to have asked the minister about the following: What does the minister say to the mayor's concerns about the energy island? Does the government intend to ensure that the Bornholmers are compensated? If so how? How will the government ensure that Energiø Bornholm becomes an advantage for Bornholm, and secure popular support for the project from Bornholm's citizens? .


Refers to playing on energy parks on land

Instead of an interview with the minister, the message from the minister's press adviser Tino Rueskov Pedersen reads.

- The clarity that we can give is that in the government's play on energy parks, which is being negotiated right now, it is promised that an analysis of possible winning and compensation schemes for neighbors for particularly large electricity transmission plants must be prepared.

That's the clarity that is right now.

The mentioned play can be found on the Ministry's website. In the play, 32 possible places are raised for energy parks in different municipalities across the country - but not on Bornholm.

The play is not about setting up offshore wind turbines, as is the case for Energiø Bornholm. The play carries the title: Climate action: Together on more green energy from sun and wind on land. The play says on page 16: "The government will prepare an analysis of possible winning and compensation schemes for neighbors for particularly large electricity transmission plants." LEA WERMELIN: We are aware of Bornholm Climate and energy spokesman for the government's largest party Social Democracy, Lea Wermelin, would like to relate to Jacob Trøst's concern.

- It is the mayor's role to make sure to keep putting Bornholm on the map and tell partly how happy we are for the energy island, but also make sure we grab the potential that the energy island can bring not only for Denmark, but also For Bornholm, she says and elaborates: - It is about local development, jobs and educational opportunities.

So what the mayor here says very clearly to Christiansborg, is now remember to help us create the right framework, and I think that is quite fair.

However, Lea Wermelin does not believe that there is a real reason to be concerned about whether Bornholm will get enough of the upcoming energy island. Here she refers to a "Additional agreement on tender frames for 6GW offshore wind and Energiø Bornholm", which was entered into on 30 May.

- Because we have written into the political agreement from this summer, that the whole question of the large transmission system to look at how to make a model for local gains and compensation.

So it is a job that is underway, which is why the Danish Energy Agency in connection with the tender cannot say to Bornholm that the framework will be like this, because there is not a political agreement yet, it says.

Therefore, at this time it is also not possible to tell exactly how Bornholm will benefit from the project, and whether and how to compensate.

- As a climate and energy mayor, I can promise that I make sure that I have Bornholm with all the time in the negotiations that we have. So Bornholm is definitely on the radar, she says.

The political agreement states: "The parties to the agreement note in this connection that any compensation related to land facilities on Bornholm will be discussed as part of follow -up on climate agreement on green power and heating 2022 regarding possible measures for local and municipal support.".

Title: Sætter gang i aktiviteter for 30 millioner
Content:
Baltic Energy Island receives another eight million in appropriation.

The Danish Business Promotion Board has recently published this.

The new grant comes in addition to two appropriations from the spring, and the consortium now has the opportunity to initiate project activities for a total of DKK 30.6 million, of which the Danish Business Promotion Board contributes the 18.8 million.

- With the new grants, together with a strong partnership, we are ready to strengthen the work to ensure both local and national value of Energiø Bornholm, says Søren Møller Christensen, CEO of Baltic Energy Island in the press release.

- Locally, we are working to make the energy island a basis for strengthened education and growth in SMEs, while we are working nationally to make energy islands a new Danish position of strength, which cemented the Danish innovation lead in wind energy. We thank you for the trust and look forward to getting started with the work.

With the aforementioned appropriations, the consortium will, among other things, initiate innovation courses, continue Residential College Bornholm, strengthen Rønne Old Power Works as a showroom and provide handheld support for business development.

The activities are a collaboration between Baltic Energy Island, DTU, Bornholm Energi & Forsyning, Campus Bornholm, Business Center Bornholm, Energy Cluster Denmark, Odense Robotics, Destination Bornholm, Offshore Center Bornholm, Bornholm Regional Municipality, Gate 21, Technological Institute, Danfoss, Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners, Ørsted and Siemens Gamesa.

Title: Trøst går efter fire år mere for bordenden
Content:
Mayor Jacob Trøst (K) has decided to stand for the municipal elections in 2025 as a top candidate. He says this in an interview with the Journal, where he also talks about the first two years in office that has not been without challenges.

Mayor Jacob Trøst (K) was not just green of party color when he first entered the mayor's office on January 1, 2022. He was also green in the way that at the same time it was the first day of service as a local politician at Bornholm. Since then, the mayor has had a steep learning curve, as he has expressed it in many interviews with the local press. The constitution has not made the curve less steep, says Jacob Consolation in this interview with the Journal, where he also reveals that his ambition is to stand for the municipal elections in 2025 as the top candidate for the Conservative People's Party.

We are soon midway through your period as mayor.

Have you made some thoughts on the upcoming municipal elections? - Yes, I have. Two years can go quickly, and then there is choice again. This is also why we have started to put the team next time. It is always good to be prepared and to set a strategy. At the last election, we were all pretty much new and took some things as they came. Back then we probably weren't so strategic because we hadn't tried it before.

How could it have been more strategic? - For election night, next time we can prepare better for the question of what we think is important - for example in relation to committee items and what tasks should be on the committees, as well as what committees we will be represented in. Now we know a little more about what the different committees can do. We also know how a constitution is going on - we've never been to that before.

It came something behind you? - Yes, it did.

Did it matter to how it ended? - boats and. I would say that my strategy was to go after the mayor's post and a place in the Finance Committee and a place in the Children's and School Committee.

That was our overall goal. After all, they succeeded very well with the three things. But to make a text -so an agreement -in such a constitution I think is important, so you agree on what direction to in that constitution.

Are there any things you want to work for together for the next four years? The constitutional parties must agree on this. We did not have such a text, and afterwards I can see that the majority have changed on a case -by -case basis for the first two years. It has been difficult to find a red thread, and it is partly because we have not made a clear agreement on what the constitution includes.


The red thread is missing

- It brings me to the challenges I have had as mayor: that it is difficult to find the red thread in the political cases. When the cases come to the subject committees and in the municipal council, we must find the majority on a case -by -case basis. This is not how every time you can be sure of the majority. It is on a case -by -case basis. After all, it has made my job a little extra challenging. I have had a very steep learning curve and it has not become easier.

But that's how it will be in other municipalities where you are only three? - Yes, but there you will probably sit in a slightly safer constitution, where you have your constitution with you and thus a majority. Our constitution has not been shown to hold in quite a few cases because we are four very different parties. In some cases, at least there is far from the Danish People's Party to the Unity List.

Have you regretted the constitution? - No, I haven't. But there is no doubt that it has helped make life difficult for myself.

That you said yes to that? - Yes. So it has given some extra work.


Have tense the arch to the outermost

Now you say yourself that you have had a steep learning curve.

But everyone is people - then it has affected you personally that you have had so much to look at, if you can say it that way? - Yes, it has. I have to say there have been a few times where I have had tense the arch to the extreme, where I have moved on the edge of what I have been able to.

In relation to the workload or? - Yes. After all, there are a huge number of different agendas I have to work with every day.

It goes straight from Energiø to Night Guards in Elderly Nursing.

It ranges tremendously and there I have to get into a lot of things and move on sometimes I am not used to - for example at Christiansborg I have had to find out how to do it best when you like will have some results.

In what order should you contact whom? But also in the municipal, local cases. There are many unwritten rules on how to make an effort to succeed in the cases. So there I have to try too.

But what do you mean by having 'tense the arch'? - It's probably most at work. It is many hours a day a week for many weeks in a row. I want to do it as best I can.

I want to live up to the confidence I have gained from the people who have voted for me and made me mayor. That's why I've worked a lot - and at first I worked too much. At one point I found out that I had to just gear down a little if I had to take care of myself.

When you take all that into consideration, do you have the courage to line up again? - Yes, I have. I believe and hope that the first two years are the toughest. There are also several who have told me that this period has been extra hard politically. There has been more turmoil than it usually does. You can also look at the number of people who have gone from their party. Those who have been involved for many years say it has been the most troubled term for many years. After all, it comforts me a little to hear that there is a good chance that it will be easier.

But why do you really want to line up again if it's been so hard? - I also think it's exciting. I think it's great to come out and meet a lot of Bornholmers who are passionate about doing something good for Bornholm - a lot of volunteers and associations, all of which work to do something good for their communities and for other citizens. But also politically, when you succeed in getting some cases through and either getting started or completed some projects that are good for Bornholm and the Bornholmers, it is great to be part of that process and have an influence on things happening.


Will be re -elected as mayor

When you set up again, is it like the top candidate? - Yes, that's it. But I have to be chosen.

But you want to continue to be mayor? - Yes.

And can the party agree too? - Yes. I have to be formally chosen, so there must be a process - so I should not reject, there is someone who will also stand up, but I have not heard of it. But as my chairman said, "Jacob, it goes without saying that when we have a sitting mayor, this is of course our top candidate." When should it be decided? - We have a general meeting in January, but I think it will first be the next general meeting in a year. But it's not quite fixed yet.

But now you are halfway? - Yes. I would also say that there are some things that have become easier. Now is not the first time every time I have to try something. When it is the first time you do something, you spend a lot of energy figuring out how to do it. The second time it will be a little easier and the third time easier. Therefore, I can use my energy on some other things and things.

Title: Bornholm og Island skal samarbejde om fremtiden
Content:
Iceland and Bornholm can act as partners in the green transition. It is one of the conclusions of Thursday's visit from the Icelandic ambassador.

Can Iceland and Bornholm learn from each other and cooperate when it comes to the green transition? This could indicate that after Bornholm on Thursday visited by the Icelandic ambassador Árni Thór Sigurðsson.

The day started for the ambassador with a meeting with Mayor Jacob Trøst (K) and the Person Business, Housing and Employment Committee Linda Kofoed Persson (K).

After that, it went into battle with meetings.

First with director of Campus Bornholm, Inge Prip, then the director of Baltic Energy Island, Søren Møller Christensen and finally communications manager at Beof, Klaus Vesløv.


Future cooperation

Common to the meetings was that the focus was on the upcoming energy island and the needs and solutions that are needed in this regard.

It tells Consul Jørgen Hammer, who was also part of the Icelandic visit.

- It was clear after the visit that it is aimed at the fact that a delegation of key people in the green transition on Bornholm will visit Iceland this spring and that the embassy will assist in the organization of the visit's program. For the Bornholm delegation, the focus will be on how to use geothermal heat in Iceland, which can inspire Bornholm in the use of the significant process heat that will be one of the consequences of a possible Bornholm production of hydrogen by electrolysis (Power-to-X ), Jørgen Hammer tells Journal.

Conversely, the Icelandic society will focus on the development of new green fuels to replace the use of fossil fuels in diesel vehicles and fishing vessels.

- Here Iceland will be able to draw inspiration from Bornholm's previous experience in the establishment of the energy island. At the same time, with the background of the ambassador's visit to Campus Bornholm, visits to educational institutions outside Reykjavik will be planned, which is thought to be inspired by the Bornholm experiences with a campus that brings together more education under the same roof, says Jørgen Hammer.

The visit ended with a dinner for the participants involved on Thursday night before the Icelandic ambassador turned the muzzle towards Copenhagen again Friday morning

Title: En rund million skal trække verden til Bornholm
Content:
Søren Møller Christensen was extremely happy when he saw that a million has been allocated to Baltic Energy Island in the new Finance Act.

He has not known it for a long time, but he had heard that it was a possibility that an amount could be allocated in the Finance Act to create networks and profile Bornholm as a hub when it comes to energy islands in Northern Europe.

- I was extremely happy when I saw it, because I didn't know we got anything, he says when the Journal talks to him on Monday night.

He says that because it is so new with commercial fire tower, he believes that it is important that funds are set aside to initiate activities and make it sustainable in the long term, and that they have reached out several times when there has been the opportunity to get a helping hand purely financially.

With the money, another round of Baltic Energy Summit must be arranged, which is a knowledge sharing network for actors in energy islands throughout Northern Europe, which gather and discuss how energy islands can be successful.

- We have an ambition to make Bornholm a hub for all knowledge of energy islands and Energiø technology and with the power plant as a meeting place for Energiø players.

With the million, Baltic Energy Island will work for Bornholm to get something back in the form of attention, education, researchers and companies who know that this is exactly where you can get the best knowledge and experience about the energy islands.

- With all these actors we want to create an Energy Island Forum, where we can together break the code for how energy islands can become a key to the green transition, and every year we have the Baltic Energy Island Summit where you present the thoughts , developed in that forum, he explains.

Basically, it is about some very complex issues in relation to the energy islands that no professional groups can solve alone. Therefore, facilitators are needed so that the right people can be brought together to a common problem solving.

- We need to find out how we get the universities, businesses and authorities together to solve a number of the problems that the individuals cannot solve themselves. It's about finding out what technologies we need to bet on for energy islands to be safe, efficient and cheap enough for it to be possible.

- One actor can't figure out it himself, so a neutral platform is needed.

He explains that the focus on Energi Island Forum is largely about creating a job that extends beyond Bornholm and draws the world to this.

The million, which rolled into the budget today, comes as a strong complement to a double -digit million amount, which Baltic Energy Island received a commitment from the Danish Business Promotion, which will equip Bornholm to get something out of the energy island.

The two commitments will therefore go hand in hand and hopefully ensure that the energy islands can be made as well as possible and that Bornholm gets as much as possible out of it.

- It's a really good day in the office, concludes Søren Møller Christensen with smiles in his voice.

Title: Energinet møver sig frem i køen med ny manøvre
Content:
Turbo has been set up on the supply of tasks for Energiø Bornholm. We must be quick to ensure all necessary materials, says Deputy Director of Energinet.

The global appetite for electrical engineering equipment is so great that Energinet is now advancing several tenders on tasks for Energiø Bornholm. This is done to ensure that you can get the necessary materials and equipment, Energinet announces in a press release.

- You could say that we change our plans to keep our plans. There are a lot of people who need to build infrastructure for the green transition, so if we did not advance the supply, we would not be able to get the equipment we need when we need it, explains Hanne Storm Edlefsen, director of energy islands in Energy.

The advance will not change other processes such as environmental assessment, Energinet writes in the same vein.

Today, tenders are sent out on the electrical engineering equipment to the stations, as well as a supply of production and installation of the cable on the seabed between Bornholm and Zealand.

Later, the task of building the station buildings in wholly Denmark and Germany is offered, as well as the installation of the cables on land and study of unexploded ammunition at sea. Energinet expects to have completed the tenders in the second half of 2024.

Title: Kommunen stiller krav og kritiske spørgsmål til energiøen
Content:
Bornholm is still behind Energiø Bornholm, but a large number of very central questions must be answered in a way that Bornholm can see itself in the project, the municipality plans to tell the Danish Energy Agency.

Bornholm still agrees to give up area to the energy island. The municipality also asks critical questions, but not anyone who rocks the overall support for Energiø Bornholm.

The consultation response will be the municipality's official response to the plan "Plan for Energiø Bornholm", in which the Danish Energy Agency will set the overall framework for the huge Energiø project.

“The Bornholm climate goals originate from the desire to take responsibility for a sustainable future and at the same time create a local development based on the green transition.

The municipality has therefore gone constructively into the work of realizing Energiø Bornholm.

In continuation of this, we agree that it assumes, among other things, that Bornholm puts precious country to a large electricity transmission plant in Sose and Horizon to two extensive offshore wind farms south of the island, "says the draft continuing:" Bornholm's regional municipality therefore backs up About "Plan for Program Energiø Bornholm", but at the same time asks that Bornholm be taken into account in the work of realizing the plan so that Energiø Bornholm will put as much a positive impression on Bornholm as possible. Heidi Burgedahl (Loose) was absent so no one could gather a majority.

The state has to pay connection

"However, it is also a prerequisite for the municipality's support for the planned connection that the expenses associated with this are not passed on to the Bornholm consumers, but is handled nationally," the municipality's consultation response is likely to tell the state.

At the same time, the energy island has to attract investments and create lasting new jobs and permanent new homes. That it happens describes the consultation response as "central to Bornholm in the work with Energiøen".

Therefore, the regional municipality reminds that a majority in the municipal council this fall made a yes to both a green business park and hydrogen production at Power-to-X facilities for official Bornholm politics. Both probably near the energy island's land plant. That course, the municipality officially agreed with a supplement to its business strategy.

Therefore, according to the consultation response, it is necessary that both the cable order and the energy island's land plants be organized so that none of the parts are in the way of Bornholm to pursue its business strategy to build on the energy island.

“Energy Island's local business potential is closely linked to the possibility of building a business park with a Power to X plant as well as a test site in the immediate vicinity of the land facility.

It is therefore crucial that in connection with the establishment of wind farms as well as cable and land facilities on Bornholm, he is taken into account, so that the design of the plant supports the energy island's potentials locally. "


Focus on safety

The municipality is already in dialogue with the Danish Energy Agency and Energinet. The consultation response emphasizes four topics, which are, among other things, on the table in that dialogue: When the energy island is to be built, housing is needed for the construction work.

Bornholm wants permanent housing "of high quality". However, the consultation response does not make specific requirements for the state or propose the state to support housing construction as requirements for the winner of the upcoming tenders.

On the other hand, there are requirements that the winners of the tenders also need apprentices. The municipality will have this requirement into the state's tender material.

The municipality also calls on the winners of the offer to work with Campus Bornholm to create "attractive education and apprenticeships".

The municipality also "sees" like "that the energy island will affect nature and the number of species in nature positively. And that the state's tenders will demand that the energy island's plant be erected in a "nature-including" way that also plays a positive part in nature.

Fourth, the regional municipality will also have the state to ensure that the safety of the energy island's plants is in order.

For they can become terror targets, and although the municipality does not directly use that word, there is not much to be mistaken for: “The municipality wants the greatest possible attention to the safety and the emergency level around the cable and land facility.

It is crucial for Bornholm to take the necessary measures needed to ensure the energy supply and make the cable and land plant less exposed to events, ”says the consultation response.


Gain to be ready

The Bornholmers should not just have something out of the energy island. The Bornholmers must also find that it actually happens.

Otherwise, the support for the giant project can crumble. That call, Mayor Jacob Trøst (K) went out in November. In this connection, Bornholm must not simply be perceived as a resource from which the green energy is harvested and Shipped in the electricity market. for Denmark and Europe are appreciated. ” It is thus essential that the Bornholmers feel a local ownership of Energiø Bornholm, and that they can see some direct benefits by enabling a green pioneer project such as Energiø Bornholm. In other words, a fair distribution of gains and burdens is crucial to the success of the program. If no local ownership of the energy island is experienced, the state risks that the popular support for the green transition is crumbling. ”This can prevent the state by making the upcoming offshore wind turbines less visible - and by reducing the noise from both the wind turbines and the land facility.

And by compensating both the direct neighbors, the general population and the municipality, which with the energy island looks into a number of very large planning tasks.

Bornholm would be eligible for almost DKK 500 million in compensation if the energy island had been a very ordinary wind turbine project under the Green Pool scheme, the consultation response is reminiscent of.

But as the law is today, Bornholm is not entitled to anything, for large transmission plants are not mentioned in the law that forms the framework for compensation for energy projects. It is only wind farms and solar parks. At the same time, the Christiansborg Agreement on Energiø Bornholm does not open for the state to demand that the winner of the concession on the offshore wind turbines pay some form of social contribution to Bornholm.

"Energiø Bornholm is currently falling" between two chairs "as far as local compensation and the direct gains by taking responsibility for the green transition," the consultation response summarizes this part of the picture.

Finally, the municipality proposes that the offshore wind turbines be set up so that they are perpendicular to the coast. Instead of quitting them up in rows that go from north to south.

The difference will be that the wind turbines become less disturbing when you see them from land. From about half of Bornholm's area you will be able to see at least one offshore wind turbine with the plan that the Danish Energy Agency is currently working on.

Could this idea be better? One does not recognize a pattern." "You should look at a solution that seems more" simple "in connection with the set up. Visualization of this is desirable for comparison ”.

"Some mills experienced" for themselves "are unfortunate. There are different scenarios with either many smaller mills or with fewer larger mills.

It is considered to be most appropriate with fewer and larger mills. "

Bornholm's regional municipality wants to emphasize that it is imperative to secure local support if we as a society are to succeed with the green transition.

Title: Leas klimadagbog: Tør jeg være optimist?
Content:
Lea Wermelin sets course for the oil state of the United Arab Emirates and takes readers to the coming days of international climate negotiations.

Today, together with the Folketing's Climate and Energy Committee, I take off to participate in this year's climate negotiations at COP28. When I left on the historic COP21, where the Paris Agreement was concluded, I wrote every day a diary here to the newspaper so you could follow behind the backdrop. I will do that again this year.

To give an insight into what is going on behind the closed doors for a crucial meeting for our and our grandchildren's future - and where we Bornholmers will deliver to the global effort with our energy island from 2030. It is at COP ' One that the framework for the global climate effort is set. And this year's COP negotiations are the most important since the Paris Agreement back in 2015. Why? Because this year, for the first time since the Paris Agreement, we are making formal status on global climate efforts. It's going to be the starting point for new national climate goals in all countries.


We screw the time back

Before I head for the COP, it's probably worth just turning the time back to 2015. In Paris, all the countries of the world agreed to limit global warming to 1.5 degrees.

Unfortunately, the latest UN report shows that we are heading towards temperature increases of about 2.9 degrees. With climate change that can not only be felt in countries far from here.

Also at home, there are heat records that are beaten over and over again. And we see more severe weather, such as the storm surge recently, which meant major damage to Bornholm. Still, it is not wasted forces to meet globally. Without the Paris Agreement, the expected emissions would have increased by 16 percent by 2030 by comparison with the three percent increase, which is expected today. So politics makes a difference.

From the Danish side, of course, we leave with high ambitions again this year. And then there is plenty to be impatient -and sometimes frustrated -over when working with climate policy on a daily basis. It is not an easy exercise to have to reach an agreement across borders, but it is crucial that it happens.


Record of the Year

This year I might even dare be careful optimist.

Already the negotiations have been historic. For it is rare that agreements are already obtained on day one. But it has happened this year. With an agreement on a climate department to support and compensate the poorest countries for the damage caused by the climate crisis. It's no secret that it's the rich countries that emit the most. And unfortunately, often those countries that already have the least that pay the price with extreme drought or floods for the small east states. For me as a Social Democrat, for the same reason, it is clear that it is the rich countries that have to contribute and pay to the fund. From the Danish side we have given DKK 175 million, and we were the first to support the fund when it was decided last year. It is besides the billions of dollars that we give to climate assistance every year.


The Danish goals with the COP

Although the agreement on a climate department is both large and important, we are far from the goals of the negotiations.

When we are on our way to the COP, we have our eyes on a number of goals that we would like to have through.

On the Danish side, we work to get a global goal of completely phasing out coal, oil and gas. Right now, the fossil sector stands for 75 percent of our greenhouse emissions, so it is a crucial piece to get in place if we are to achieve our goals. At home, we have set a specific end date for when all oil and gas activity in the North Sea should stop. As the first oil -producing country in the world. We hope this example the rest of the countries will follow. But it is also important that we work globally for what is replaced by fossil fuels, namely renewable energy.

That is why we are working to ensure that by 2030, we must have tripled the renewable energy and double energy efficiency by 2030. Here our energy island is a good example of why other countries are inspired by Denmark. All wind turbines set up to date are designed according to Danish inspiration. We have a lot to offer from solutions to the major global emissions.


Read on in the coming days

As you can read, there is plenty to address. And one must not be the great comedian to make fun of the COP being held in the oil state of the United Arab Emirates. But also the oil -producing countries will be on the journey if we are to have a greener future.

I have jumped in my work clothes and I look forward to following the negotiations and having a sea of ​​meetings in the coming days. And then of course I'm looking forward to taking you on the trip.

Title: Bornholms Havvind bygger på andelstanken
Content:
Sometimes it may be good to refresh the story, and Benny Elmann-Larsen has, with his debate post (Bornholm's Journal on December 4, 2023) on the ideal and technical basis on which Bornholm's offshore wind rests, gave an opportunity to do just the.

So we grab it with a kissing hand. And because not only is asked about the idea, but also to the technical basis, it is here the development consortium Bornholm's offshore wind that answers. The development consortium consists of representatives from the citizen energy community Bornholm's offshore wind, Energi East and Nexø Harbor.

Bornholm's offshore wind is based on the cooperative idea - and it has many fathers and mothers It is quite correct that Bornholm's offshore wind in its essence is based on the share tank - a good and healthy thought that has many fathers and mothers.

When the first Danish utility association was founded just over 150 years ago, it happened to secure 'ordinary people proper goods at proper prices'. And one of the driving forces was the Bornholm priest Hans Christian Sonne.

For Bornholm's offshore wind, it is not butter and soap that is the focus, but rather 'proper green power at proper prices and on proper conditions' for Bornholm citizens and businesses.

So yes, the basic idea behind Bornholm's offshore wind has many years on the back and has been reinvented many times since then. And certainly also in energy production.

For example, think about how many of the Bornholm onshore windmills we see today come up, or on the Middelgrunden off Copenhagen. Bornholm's offshore wind is certainly not the first to think locally and popular ownership where everyone can join.

It is also quite correct that no party has a patent on neither the basic idea behind or on Bornholm's offshore wind as a project. And it is with well -being hu. When we set up the small 12-person initiative group for Bornholm's offshore wind farm in 2019, the idea was that it should tighten widely. Therefore, the group also spoke members with sympathies for different political parties across the political spectrum and from different parts of Bornholm, both geographically and in relation to business.

Common, however, was the desire to take responsibility for the green transition by quickly establishing a production of persistent green power to cover Bornholm's consumption now and in the future, and to do so in a way that would benefit the development of Bornholm. In addition to the safety of proper power at a proper price, it is a clear expectation that a coastal offshore wind farm off Bornholm will create extra activity in our ports and among the many who work to develop the energy system of the future. It is also the wishes and expectations that gather us today.

Therefore, it is also with a view of the government's desire for popular commitment to the climate agenda and the green transition also quite incomprehensible that the same government is stretching legs for the further development of our initiative. The fact that Bornholm's offshore wind is far from the only project that is affected by the government's policy for expansion (or lack of the same) of renewable energy in Denmark, it just makes it even more incomprehensible.

Enough for Bornholm and nothing more than the surplus can be exported with offshore wind, until a certain limit at least, it will be easier to achieve a good economy in a larger one than in a smaller project, simply because just it for example Having out to sea and doing the initial preliminary studies cost, the landing of the power costs and so on. At the same time, the cost of, for example, sailing out to the mills is all else just lower to coastal mills than to mills further out to sea. Therefore, when we started the initiative, we set out to make the project so large so that it could supply Bornholm with the amount of power that would be needed and at the same time not make it larger than the possible excess power could be exported away from Bornholm through the submarine cable or could be stored. We have been counted on this, now for different calendar years and both calculations show that with a capacity of 100 MW, we will be within this span of a 3-9% of the annual power generation that we - or others - must find a way to store.

What probably makes the difference to the considerations that were made in connection with the supply of coastal offshore wind in 2015-2016, which Benny Elmann-Larsen refers to is that today we see that the transition from fossil energy to sustained sustainable Power is in progress.

More and more people are getting electric cars, heat pumps and more, and that development will continue. Thus, demand for electricity is increasing. At the same time, the development of batteries and other technologies has also started to store electricity. Of course, this is also included in our considerations, and we are thus also in dialogue with relevant parties in the field. And then you should also not forget that you have built up a much greater experience in establishing offshore wind farms that fundamentally change the economy so that they no longer need public subsidies to be profitable.

The project economy and the future electricity price A prerequisite for being able to make an investment decision in a project such as Bornholm's offshore wind is, of course, that thorough preliminary studies of environmental and technical conditions are carried out, and that one has as high a level of information as possible about the future electricity price and interest rate development .

What Bornholm's offshore wind has applied for the Danish Energy Agency is precisely to get permission to carry out the necessary preliminary studies in the location where we want to set up the mills. It is only when these studies are done, and we can realistically start obtaining prices for mills, cables, etc. that we can prepare a final prospectus and thus make a final investment decision.

In relation to the introduction of the flow from Bornholm's offshore wind to the Bornholm electricity grid, we have recognized in the project estimate that the electricity grid at Nexø is not strong enough to receive the power, which is why a cost to lead the flow from Nexø to Rønne, where the power can then can then led into the Bornholm net.

In relation to expected power prices, the expectation is that they will change in line with the expansion of the cheap sun and wind energy production across Europe.

It is not only a condition for Bornholm's offshore wind, but also for projects such as Energiø Bornholm, because everyone sells into the same energy market. As you can read in our technical report, our project estimate is based on an average power price of 30 øre from 2030 onwards, whereas the Danish Energy Agency's expectation of the average power price is a piece above, namely 42 øre in 2030, falling to 36 øre in 2050. So a cautious estimate on the side of Bornholm.

In addition, as you can read in our technical report, we have done some initial sensitivity analyzes that estimate what the consequence will be if now the power price is 5 or 10 øre lower, 5 øre higher, etc. The result is that on At present, a sufficiently sensible project economy is seen to make it meaningful to continue the development of the project.

If we get the opportunity.

Open-door scheme and EU right in November 2022 made an assessment of the EU legal aspects of the open door scheme and found that the open door the scheme did not entail illegal state aid.

This is stated in a note that the Danish Energy Agency prepared in March this year and which can be found on the Danish Energy Agency's website. The same conclusion has also come up with several law offices, including Gorissen Federspiels, who published a so-called 'White Paper' on the subject in March 2023. Since then, from a political point of view, the European Commission has been in dialogue with the European Commission on the issue, but so far without That the result of this dialogue has come to the public's knowledge.

It is this insight that we - and a lot of politicians, not only from the Unity List but also from Conservatives - presses to gain. And of course we hope that it will succeed. Not just for Bornholm's offshore wind, but also in favor of the many other coastal and locally anchored offshore wind projects, which fortunately flourishes around Denmark.

Title: Lea Wermelin: Bornholm skal også have gavn af energiparkaftale
Content:
Bornholm does not immediately get part of DKK 2.5 billion in the compensation pool, but the deal benefits Bornholm anyway, says Lea Wermelin.

Bornholm is not immediately included in a new agreement on terms to realize a quadrupling of the total electricity generation from sun and wind on land until 2030.

But then anyway, says Bornholm MP Lea Wermelin (S), who has been involved in the negotiations: - This agreement is basically about setting up more renewable energy - ie solar and wind energy - on land. Since we get an energy island with three gigawatts of offshore winds, it is not really an appointment for us. But in the negotiations I have been very busy making sure that the good frameworks that are to establish energy parks will also be something Bornholm can benefit from. I am glad that we have joined the deal, says Lea Wermelin on the phone from the United Arab Emirates, where she is at the COP 28 climate summit.


Bornholm with the agreement

It was a broad majority in the Folketing, which on Tuesday presented a new agreement, which states, among other things, that the state, on the basis of ongoing application rounds, will be able to appoint specific areas for larger energy parks.

However, in order for projects not to be delayed due to restrictions on, for example, the environment, in the spring of 2024 a new law will be put forward, which will award energy parks special conditions.

The agreement states that the law must relax area protection and thus make it easier and faster to obtain permits and exemptions for the installation of renewable energy.

- I am glad that Bornholm has been drawn specifically into the agreement. There are a lot of elements in the agreement that would like to clear some stones out of the way when you want to establish an energy park, and of course we must also benefit from them, she says.


2.5 billion

The parties, which in addition to the government count SF, the Conservatives, the Unity List, the Radical Left and the Alternative, therefore agree on a significant increase in, among other things, the compensation scheme Green Pool.

Neighbors in Sose

Title: Hvorfor er der ikke flere bornholmere der kører i elbil?
Content:
Flexbornholmer wonders about the limited amount of electric cars on Bornholm.

As one of a few positive news compared to our CO2 emissions, sales of electric cars have finally begun to rise. Still, you can be pretty sure that if you meet another Danish car on the road between Malmö and Ystad it is a "tourist" on the way to Bornholm. The Bornholmers are among the Danes who have bought a percentage few electric cars over the past few years. Why really? Part of the explanation is probably Bornholmers' innate skepticism about everything that is new and everything that does not come from Bornholm.

It probably takes more to be accepted on Bornholm than anywhere else in the country, obviously also for electric cars.

Politicians and businesses on Bornholm have otherwise tried to set the tone with a green vision for mobility on Bornholm as part of Bright Green Island, "Bornholm drives green on land" (2008). But it does not help with the local skepticism about electric cars. Now you can say that green mobility is also more a declaration of intent than real politics on the part of the regional community. You can make sure of this by seeing all the white Toyotas from the regional municipality driving around the island, or by following the debate about whether it can now stand by the green mobility or whether you should just buy some new ones Disel buses. So the regional municipality does not go ahead with the good green example.

Of course, as a Bornholmer you do not buy your car "from over", so you also depend on what is negotiated by cars on the island. Here you have to look good for the electric cars. But they exist. We were even written up to buy an electric car from one of the Bornholm car dealers. It ended up demanding more patience and perseverance on our part than we were in possession of. It could be delivered 3/4 years after we had signed the contract, and when the 3/4 years had passed, it was only on our own inquiry that we could be informed that there were delivery problems and that they could not give anyone Final Date of Delivery. We had leased an electric car for a year and had been convinced that it was the car of the future. Since we could buy a only one year used electric car from a dealer in Hvidovre for 100,000 less than the one we had ordered, the decision was not so difficult. Used electric cars, strangely, there are no car dealers who have settled on Bornholm.

Range anxiety may be able to keep some from investing in an electric car. But that can hardly be the case for Bornholmers. The cheapest city electric cars should be called island cars. At least they reach plenty of driving needs on an island like Bornholm. And charging stands are so plenty on the island. I think Bornholm has the country's best charging coverage, and with the prospect of the energy surplus that becomes as part of Energiø Bornholm, there should also be no concern about future supply or prices.

Electric cars are now only slightly more expensive in acquisition than a similar petrol car, and a FDM study (September 2023), which must be described as reasonably impartial in this context, shows that with a driving need of about 100,000 km in five years, is There is at least DKK 1,000 to save per month on choosing electricity as a means of propulsion rather than gasoline.

In addition to skepticism towards everything new, I have been accused of being accused of being extremely price conscious. Therefore, of course I have chosen an electric car.

I am fully aware that an electric car is obviously not the greenest way of transporting. Of course, it's taking the bus. With or without electricity.

Title: Svenske eksperter advarer mod energiø
Content:
Swedish meteorologists warn in a consultation response to Energiø Bornholm's disruptive effect on the marine environment. This is especially true of the cable connection between Bornholm and Zealand.

SMHI, the Swedish response to the Meteorological Institute, has just undergone consultation responses and environmental assessment of Energiø Bornholm and shares a number of concerns about the park's expected environmental impact.

Specifically, this applies to the planned cable connection between Bornholm and Zealand.

The southern Baltic Sea area plays an important role in the renewal of central Baltic Seawood waters, where salt and absolute water flow from the Sound and the Baltic Sea towards deeper areas in the Baltic Sea. Thus, according to SMHI, local influence in the southern Baltic Sea can have an impact on the entire Baltic Sea environment.

"Given the large number of completed and planned infrastructure projects in the sensitive area of ​​the southern Baltic Sea, SMHI sees it as extremely important that the cumulative environmental impact becomes as small as possible," says the Swedish meteorological and hydrological institute.

SMHI therefore looks positively that only one cable connection should now be added instead of two between Bornholm and Zealand. When cables are closed down, there is an impact on the abiotic factors in the marine environment in the form of the erection of the water, an increased amount of nutrients, the spread of any toxins from the bottom material and several shipping transports.

Wind turbines affect the reading side The Meteorological Institute in Sweden remains concerned about the stretches where the submarine cable is to be protected by stone settings.

These can cause increased turbulence that causes the bottom -on power to mix with the surface water, which according to SMHI reduces the quality of the Baltic Sea's deep water. Since the cable laying will affect Swedish waters, SMHI believes that there is a need for Sweden to continue to participate in the environmental impact assessment.

The Swedish meteorologists also point out that wind farms affect the airflow on the reading side of the plant. This results in changes in power, waves and stirring in the surrounding sea surface layer.

SMHI believes this effect should be quantified.

The consultation response can be read in its entirety on the Nature Walls' website. The work is a board under the Swedish Environment Ministry.

Title: Klimadagbog: Vi har en aftale!
Content:
When I left for COP 28, I packed my suitcase with good news.

Today I unpack it with even better news. Because while I was on my way back to Denmark, the deal landed in Dubai to get us closer to the goal of limiting global warming. It required 24 hours of overtime. It is a good and a historic deal.


Away from oil, coal and gas

For the first time in more than 30 years, the countries of the world have agreed that we must change away from coal, oil and gas. It is groundbreaking in the global climate effort as it is the first time ever when fossil fuels are written directly into the text. It sends a clear signal to all the countries of the world to change away from fossil fuels. But now we do - on top of that in an oil state.

But I might as well be honest and say that the deal is not perfect.

As I wrote yesterday, we struggled with beak and claws to get the word phase -out into the agreement text. That part did not succeed.

Still, we landed well on our feet rather than with the stomach splashes I feared.

It makes a difference to our climate and our future.


Danish goals with in the agreement

From the Danish side we left with three overall and ambitious goals that we would make global. 1, phase -out of fossil fuels, 2, tripling renewable energy and 3, doubling energy efficiency. With the agreement, we have gained all the countries of the world on the goals of a tripling of renewable energy and a doubling of energy efficiency.

This means that we must now have accelerated the green technologies. And we must have set up many more wind turbines and photovoltaic systems around the world.

It's not just good news for the climate. It is also good news for Danish companies that supply green energy solutions. Of course, the ambition of the Danish side is also that the world's wind turbines will continue to be built according to the Danish model.

Just as it makes Bornholm a showcase with the world's first energy island and as a place where we are going ahead and are already in the process of delivering more offshore wind.


Climate Facing to the Most Vulnerable Countries

At the same time, the agreement also provides on climate financing.

A longtime Danish priority.

Already on the first day of COP 28, the countries of the world decided to establish a fund for losses and damage to the most vulnerable countries. Here, Denmark contributes DKK 175 million. and here we also have to go further.


What then?

As I wrote yesterday, things don't end at Cop. They start there. With the agreement text in place, it is now up to the individual countries to go home and make agreements and legislation that live up to the words of the agreement.

So it is now that we all have to show that we can translate words and promises into real action. Just a few years ago, it had been a utopia to imagine that we could stand with the deal we are in hand now. It is historical progress.

But it is also absolutely necessary if we are to succeed in limiting temperature rises to 1.5 degrees and thus living up to the Paris Agreement.

And in two years when we meet at COP 30 in Brazil, all countries must have updated their national climate goals. So they match the goals we have now set. Here, Denmark has played an important role in helping in that process. So even though the copen are over and my diary ends here, the work is far from over. Thank you for reading!.
