Title: I 2024 handler det om velfærd
Content:
In a few days, 2023 will run out and 2024 will be at the door. For many - including myself - the days up to the turn of the year often give time for reflection. It's needed, because politics is really going strong. The pace is high and one deal replaces the other. Finance Act. Agreements on Energiø and Salary Lift for public employees. And much, much more.

It can be difficult to follow. Even for us politicians who work with it every single day. Let me take you back and look at the year that has passed. What political agreements have we made during the year? And what are we looking forward to in the new years? In many ways it has been a special year in Danish politics.

When we went to election, it was with the ambition to form a broad government. As we presented a government over the middle before the turn of the year last year, we therefore fulfilled the first of the promises we went to election in the Social Democracy. The SVM government is the first broad government in over 40 years.

Therefore, it is also clear that sometimes there are camels that need to be swallowed. Compromises to be concluded. But it is not unique to a broad government. This is how the government is. No party has 90 seats. Salary promise now becomes reality

When I look back on the year, I see appointments that have come to stay. For the first time in 25 years, for example, we have made an agreement across the middle in the cash assistance area. With more simple rules and where single parents get more between their hands. I think so, says a little that our collaboration works.

But of course we should not only make compromises. We must also fulfill the Social Democratic promises we gave when we went to election. They must be brought to life and turn into real action. A little a month ago, we fulfilled one of our - for me to see - most important election promises. Namely, a payroll for employees in the close welfare. With almost 7 billion DKK per year.

This means that we can now finally provide a higher paycheck to people working in health and elderly care, educators, healthcare professionals and employees in our prisons. It is an important agreement that is of great importance to our common welfare.

In my eyes, we have one of the strongest welfare societies in the world. But there are places where it cracks. We also experience here at Bornholm - and for that matter in the rest of Denmark - how our health care and elderly care are under pressure. Therefore, in addition to the salary lift, we will invest massively in our welfare in 2024. It is money that will go to ease the pressure in hospitals. And to give the elderly a worthy care.

The climate high on the agenda 2023 has also been a year in which the climate has shown teeth. With massive heat waves. Forest fires. Extreme drought. And at home with storm surge, which brought great devastation here at Bornholm. It will be naive to think that this is the last time such natural phenomena occur on Danish soil.

Therefore, in the Finance Act, we have allocated money to help the severely needy municipalities with a storm surge pool. The weather phenomena have also been a reminder that we need to call every man on deck and act now. And it has been a look at what we are looking forward to if we do not put the brake in now.

That is why we have worked hard in the green area this year. And we have reached the goal of many good and important appointments. In May we wrote history when we entered into the largest offshore wind of Danish history. A deal that also means one of the world's first energy islands right here at Bornholm. We need to make the most of it locally in terms of creating development and local employment.

A few weeks ago we then entered into an agreement on the possibility of energy parks, where I have struggled to give Bornholm the same opportunities as in the rest of the country, even though their renewable energy comes from land and ours in the future comes from the energy island.

It succeeded, and in that way it goes hand in hand to represent our island and be the rapporteur for climate and energy. And only in the new year do I hope that we will decide how we take into account the neighbors and make it a local gain for the municipality to lay land to the energy island.

Although on the climate debate in the newspaper columns and the news broadcasts, we could think that we are very far from the climate goals, we have reached 98.7 percent of the road to the target in 2025, and we have made decisions that get us 3/4 out of the way to the goal by 2030. Next year we will move on.

Campus Bornholm, release of the elderly care and investment in health we again look forward, then the 2024 of the year will be the first steps to strengthen vocational education. An important investment.

Because we're going to have a massive lack of skilled workers if we don't invest now. And with the green transition of our society we are facing, we will need even more skilled workers in the future. To build our PTX system. Serve our wind turbines. And energy renovates our houses. For Bornholm with a new energy island on the drawing board, which will become a green power center, more skilled workers are also necessary for us to give our ambitions air under the wings.

The other major headlines will be the release of the elderly care, where the professionalism must return to the employees in the front line rather than that documentation requirements and bureaucracy must take time. And our common health care system must also be prioritized.

Very happy New Year on the personal level, my year has been different than 2022. I am back in the parliamentary group as a climate, energy and supply mayor after more than three years as environment minister. It has meant new exciting tasks.

And just as I am passionate about our environment, I also passion for our climate. As you know, the climate is our generation's biggest challenge. And the responsibility for solving the crisis rests on our shoulders. That is why I look forward to continuing work as I pull on the work clothes again in the new year. For Bornholm, Welfare and the Climate. I am very humble about the confidence I got last year upstairs the election and I wish you all a really happy new year.

Title: Lad os få stabil energi
Content:
It is a failure of dimensions if one maintains the resistance to nuclear power, says Jørgen Bondorff.

With the magnificent plans for Bornholm as Energiø it is clear that the debate that is going on must be about energy.

The source is planned to be large offshore wind turbines, but is it a question whether the concept of renewable energy should not rather be called variable energy? In this country, depending on the site, there is somewhere between 30 and 170 days a year, where it blows so little that wind turbines are not effective.

One likes to call wind energy "green energy". What the Green consists, remains uncertain.

The steel towers from which wind turbines are built are largely produced in China, where the steelworks are coal -fired. They are then sailed to Europe with diesel -powered ships, after which they are transported with diesel -powered trucks or ships to the place where they are to be erected.

A wind turbine has a lifetime of between 20 and 30 years. Then at least the wings have to be replaced. You still have trouble finding out a method of disposing of them.

During the life of the mill, it will have derived considerable amounts of microplastics that end up in the sea or later through the food in us.

It will have killed some birds and especially insects, and during the periods when the wind is inadequate, it will require backup in the form of biofuels or fossil fuel.

Denmark imports biomass annually from a forest area the size of Funen and Zealand together. It is burned off in Danish power plants such as backup for sun and wind.

The burning causes a CO2 emission that is fully in line with the burning of coal, but a Danish political adoption has been made that burning wood pellets should not count in the CO2 accounts, referring to the fact that it is planted New trees that will make the accounts balance for years.

Now I have not been at all on the resources it requires to make a wind turbine.

After all, fiberglass, "glue" (resin) is needed to build them, gravel and sand (which is already in short supply) to make concrete, concrete for base, steel for reinforcing the cement, copper and other metals for the electrical components, as well as hectoliters of paint to protect the construction.

So, all in all, wind turbines are not "green", they are not cheap and they are not stable energy suppliers. But there are far better, cheaper and more environmentally friendly alternatives in the form of nuclear power.

Thorium in Bornholm's Journal on December 22, Steffen Olsen warns against believing that nuclear power is harmless. As an example, the Fukushima accident and Chernobyl are mentioned. These are the same accidents that some Danish politicians always drive with the accident on Tremile Island in the United States.

All three accidents have happened with nuclear power plants of a generation that are outdated compared to the works that can be built -and build -day.

There are two groups of younger Danish researchers, Copenhagen Atomics and Seaborg Technologies that are developing small principals created with thorium as an energy source, and not with uranium used by conventional reactors.

Unfortunately, they have to work abroad, as politicians stubbornly stick to a 1985 parliamentary decision not to have nuclear power in Denmark.

Title: Politisk splittelse om millionaftale med staten

It will be to stab people in the eye to bet unilaterally on the energy island. The energy island is coming, but I do not feel convinced of the effects it can throw away.

René Danielsson (DF).

Title: Regeringen vil udvikle erhverv på Sydbornholm

Title: Den grønne fremtid kræver handling nu
Content:
The letter of minister to Bornholm is a good second step. Now Bornholm has to in work clothes to shape the future growth engine.

It is a significant milestone for Bornholm that the government, represented by four ministers, has focused its focus on the island in connection with the Energiø Bornholm project.

Mayor Jacob Consolation's good steps to demand counter -services for the island's role in Denmark's energy policy is drawing to bear fruit.

But now the true work begins.

Bornholm stands at a crossroads where the opportunities to attract 'green' companies near the land plant must be translated into concrete, investment -worthy projects. It's not just about creating jobs; It is about shaping a sustainable, future -oriented society with a pulse of growth from the wind of the sea in South Bornholm.

However, we must be realistic. Bornholm's geographical position and size means that the island is not immediately an obvious choice for any type of production. Therefore, it is essential that we select the right industries and businesses that can benefit from the large quantities of green surplus energy that could be in a green business park. The dream of a business park is both the dream of offering tax -free power almost without net losses, but also an interaction between companies in the park that can utilize each other's waste products and skills.

It doesn't happen by itself. But with the right municipality that both marketing the opportunities and ensures that companies are not suffocated in slow case management and silo thinking, we can accomplish green miracles.

Education and competence development become crucial in this context. To realize the potential of the upcoming green businesses, we must ensure that the Bornholm labor market is equipped with the necessary skills and knowledge.

We secure this best with living education on the island.

Bornholm's future lies in a balanced approach, where we both cherish our unique nature and at the same time welcome innovation and new industries. Our focus must be on creating a harmonious interaction between the environment, economy and social development.

The coming months and years will require determination, vision and not least collaboration across sectors and political divisions. Only through a joint effort can we ensure that Bornholm not only becomes a footnote in the green transition, but an active, leading participant in the creation of a sustainable future.

Let's seize this unique opportunity to put Bornholm on the world map as an example of how a small community can create major changes. For every decision we make now, we are shaping the island's way forward -towards a greener, stronger and more climate -friendly future.

Title: Medie: Udbud til energiøen bliver forsinket
Content:

The government postpones the largest supply of offshore wind of Danish history: 3 gigawatts from Energiø Bornholm and 6 gigawatts from offshore wind turbines elsewhere in the sea around Denmark.

It writes the trade magazine Engineer, quoting sources close to the government.

"The engineer finds that the ministry is postponing the supply to some point in the spring. The reason is that the negotiating partners have not yet reached an agreement on the framework for the 6 Gigawatt traditional offshore winds and 3 gigawatts from Energiø Bornholm," writes the Engineer.

The Danish Energy Agency informs the Engineer that it is expected to start the supply of the offshore wind turbines during the spring.

- I only think it's a little bump on the road. Also, the different parties may not be particularly far apart. There are just some things to clarify, says Søren Møller Christensen, director of the Consortium Baltic Energy Island, which works with Energiø Bornholm from premises in the former electricity plant in Rønne.

Søren Møller Christensen says that he has no sure knowledge of what the supply of offshore wind turbines is delayed. However, he has some ideas.

- I think it's about the preliminary dialogue with the actors shown that there are some doubts and challenges about the state's co -ownership of the 6 Gigawatts elsewhere than Bornholm. And about the sustainability, where it's also about thinking about the seabed, not just on the green transition, he says.

- I also think they negotiate how to settle the price for electricity from Energiø Bornholm if Bornholm becomes its own price zone in connection with the energy island, says Søren Møller Christensen.

He is not surprised that there are some doubts to clarify between the Danish Energy Agency and the energy companies that have shown interest in offering the offshore wind turbines.

- There are many questions that you have not had to decide before. And I actually think it's very good to clarify those questions before sending the 3 gigawatt offshore winds in tender, says Søren Møller Christensen.

- If you did not clarify these questions now before the tender, it could be that there were no bids at all. And if you have to choose between getting the supply delayed and not getting any bids at all, you have to take the delay, he says.

Title: Sidste udkald: Tunnelforening overvejer at nedlægge sig selv
Content:
The situation of the Bornholm Tunnel Association is reminiscent of a boxer who is beaten in the floor by the opponent.

The match leader is bent over the boxer and counts, and the secondary in the ring corner has the towel in his hand and is considering throwing it into the ring.

The question is whether the boxer manages to get up and fight on, or whether the match ends with a defeat to the beaten fighter. In a boxing match you know the answer within seconds, in the Bornholm Tunnel Association you know it on January 25.

That day, the Board of Directors has convened an extraordinary general meeting at Rønne Library. After many years of efforts for a permanent connection between Bornholm and Sweden, both Anne Margrethe Roesen and Karsten Brodersen want to stop the board. They do not have the energy to continue. Peter Hansen has, but he can't do it alone, and the question is whether someone will come to him and the association to the rescue so the fight can continue or whether the association has to throw the towel in the ring and give up.

Members have been notified directly that the Bornholm Tunnel Association is being spoken out. The same message is shown in a post on the association's Facebook page, and Peter Hansen repeats it as the Journal talks to him about the association's situation and the future.

- It's not so good. We hope we can continue, but we fear we will close, he says.

A little up and down with Anne Margrethe Roesen and Karsten Brodersen's decision to step out of the board, Peter Hansen is left alone, and that is not possible, he says, and he is not filled with optimism before the decisive and potentially fateful general meeting.

- I don't know how to evaluate the chance. I hope some are coming so we can continue, but it looks a little black, says Peter Hansen.

It is not that he - or the soon -to -be former board members - have lost faith in the idea. Not at all. It's just hard to find someone who will spend the necessary volunteer hours in the project and the association.

- The idea has gotten better and better, we think. In light of climate and war, I think it looks better than it did when it started, says Peter Hansen, who himself has been active in the association Bornholm Tunnel for eight years.

In those years it has gone up and down with the interest in and the belief in a permanent connection to Sweden.

- We have tried to do something, among other things by being at the People's Meeting and talking about a possible tunnel to Sweden. I think it has gone up and down a lot. That's how it is, says Peter Hansen.


Started with Pokémon

For Peter Hansen, the engagement in the Bornholm Tunnel Association began after a remark from his son while on their way to Halloween in Gudhjem.

- At that time he played a lot that Pokémon on the mobile, and he asked if we couldn't drive over to Grandma in Zealand, because there were many more Pokémons. It didn't work out, but it started the idea, he says.

It is eight years ago, and today the idea of ​​a tunnel makes even better sense than then, says Peter Hansen.

This is due to both the plans for Energiø Bornholm and the development of electrified vehicles.

- The green island and electric cars give more fuel for the project. It offers better opportunities for a tunnel, because electric cars do not emit CO2. As it is now, ventilation ducts need to be made, but it becomes less and less relevant with electric cars. We have also talked about electric train, says Peter Hansen.

If you have the courage to take up the fight with him, you are welcome to go or attend the extraordinary general meeting.

- The 25th is it bang or fall. There we find out if we are continuing or whether we do not continue, says Peter Hansen.

If you fail to find new forces to supplement Peter Hansen, the association will use the last of its fortune to put down itself. If there is still money left in the account, according to the articles of association, they must be transferred for a similar purpose.

- It is far along the way that has already been implemented. The young children's Bornholm is an investment in preventing. We have also already set aside the first funds to work with the energy island, and we have decided to reorganize the elderly care, he says.

Is the Development Agreement about the Ministry financing something that you have already decided? - Yes. The ministry needs to know that these are initiatives that we will aim for. But even though we have decided to reorganize the elderly care, it has only just started. The same with the energy island, where the effort has also just started with a few employees.

- Then there may well be a greater need for employees for the energy island later, and so will. This agreement does not put a number of employees on, but it puts figures on what we would like to develop and how we would like to fix our finances with the budgetary security that comes with such a development partnership, says Jacob Consolation.


Who should negotiate?

In relation to the pool of disadvantaged municipalities, the Executive Board and the CFO ask me how much an amount we should request the ministry. And even if we get a development partnership with the ministry, we will still have to seek money from the pool.

It does not rule out that you take over and negotiate with the ministry about the amount in an agreement? - No, it doesn't. And I would like to think that we will get the amount that corresponds to our imbalance on the municipal budget, says Jacob Trøst.

Are you ready to go and negotiate yourself? - Yes. I do what it takes and as the administration thinks will work best.

Title: Bornholms Grønne fremtid i fællesskab
Content:
Collaboration between the Baltic Sea Energy Islands strengthens growth and local inclusion.

Bornholm, Gotland and Åland's formal conclusion in direct cooperation as future energy islands in the Baltic Sea is an event that deserves great recognition and support.

This alliance, which is formalized in Mariehamn in Åland, represents not only a common vision of a green future, but also a promise of economic growth and new businesses where the local population plays a central role. The core of the collaboration is knowledge sharing and the development of new business areas, with a strong focus on local commitment. This approach is essential to ensure that the green changes we face will be inclusive and beneficial to everyone on Bornholm. By involving citizens directly in renewable energy projects, we ensure that the transformation is not only technological and economic, but also social and cultural.

It is noteworthy that cooperation will open doors to EU financing, which can accelerate the development and implementation of sustainable energy projects in the islands. This collaboration between Bornholm, Gotland and Åland is a luminous example of how small island communities can unite the forces and make a significant difference in the global green transition.

Our mayor, Jacob Consolation, rightly emphasizes that cooperation is the key to success. This alliance shows that even small islands can contribute significantly to the green transition and find a balance between natural, social and economic needs. This approach is not only visionary, but also pragmatic, taking into account the unique challenges and opportunities that come with being an island in the Baltic Sea.

It is also worth noting that the collaboration is non-exclusive, which means that the door is open to work with other partners. This flexibility is crucial to ensuring the best possible results and the widest possible impact on our efforts.

As part of this groundbreaking collaboration, Bornholm should be proud to play an active role in shaping the future of renewable energy in the Baltic Sea region. With this initiative, we take a big step forward towards a sustainable future, where our island can serve as a role model for green transition and local commitment. Collaboration and knowledge sharing are the key to progress, and with this agreement Bornholm is well on its way to realizing its potential as a leading green energy island.

Title: Ved de, hvor meget vand, der står ved Sose?
Content:
Does Energinet and Environmental Authorities really realize how much water stands at SOSE?

There is water in the area at Sose, where Energinet intends to place the land plant they will build as part of the Energiø Bornholm project. There is a lot of water! One of the explanations, of course, is that the fall of 2023 has been very wet and that 2024 has also started tremendously wet. But unfortunately, that's not the whole explanation. First, the area that Energinet has pointed out is as the preferred for the location of the land facility -s -proof due to the density of the coastal area characterized by freshwater formation. This is evidenced by the environmental assessment of the whole plan for Energiø Bornholm, which Ramboll has prepared and which has just been consulted. At the same time, the area is one of the places on Bornholm, which is expected to be at the greatest risk of groundwater rise as a result of the ongoing climate change, and to a degree, so that by 2050 it is expected that the groundwater level is not located below the soil surface, but on the contrary. Surface level. This is stated in a climate adaptation plan that Cowi made in 2022 for Bornholm. Thus, the area must be expected to be covered by water for much of the year within a short number of years.

Does the Energinet have considered what it means for the location of Energiø Bornholm's transformer station? And have you considered it in the municipal council for that matter? And have you considered what the environmental consequences will be when you have to do something to lower the groundwater level in the area? After all, the environmental assessment of the entire Energiø Bornholm plan, which has just been in consultation, told with all desirable clarity that if groundwater lowering is to be done. Establishing a high -voltage station, then it is considered to be able to result in deterioration of water quality and quantity in the area.

Not least, one must assume, because in the area, as you know, there is a significant natural occurrence of ocher that risks being released by drainage, groundwater lowering, etc. We have painfully experienced this in connection with previous drainage projects.

As a citizen of the area and as someone who wants to look after our nature, I hope that both Energinet, as the developer, and the Danish Environmental Protection Agency and Bornholm Regional Municipality as authorities, take their responsibility for the environment seriously in their eagerness to realize Energiø Bornholm project.

As stated earlier, a location further north in the totally designated area will be preferable, as the northern area is higher and will not be challenged to the same extent with the groundwater. At the same time, the southern area, where the plant could currently be proposed to be located instead, be a nature restoration area where former meadows with lots of wildlife etc. could be recreated. Furthermore, all our fellow citizens along Søndre Landevej, who are currently risking getting the land facility directly in their backyard -except any kind of compensation -will get it at a greater distance and shielded by a new nature restoration area.

I really have a hard time seeing that is not a much better solution.

Title: Energinet passer på grundvandet under energiøen
Content:
Energinet responds again. We are in control of nature at Sydbornholm.

In Thursday's edition of Bornholm's Journal Jens-Otto A. Sonne asks rhetorically if we know in Energinet how much water is in the area and whether the area for the same reason is now also well-chosen. It is a good and relevant question, especially in this very wet winter.

The choice of the area at Sose, south of Aakirkeby, has been selected after a long and laborious process. It has to live up to a wide range of criteria for being suitable. Placing a station of that size is not an easy task and it cannot be done without affecting anyone. Unfortunately, it affects a number of landowners whose properties we will have to take over, but also a number of neighbors who get the station in their local area. They are quite understandably concerned about how the station will affect them. That would be the case wherever we place the station on Bornholm - it is inevitable that a construction of that size will affect someone.

When the election has fallen in the field of SOSE, it is due to a number of factors that, overall, make the area the most suitable. It is located close to the sea, and thus the cables that will connect the station to the wind turbines and the Danish and German electricity grids will be shorter and bother fewer landowners.

The area consists primarily of agricultural land.

Therefore, there are relatively few protected nature interests. Energinet has spent over a year mapping plant and wildlife to get a precise picture of the entire area.

Jens-Otto A. Sonne also raises the concern about the occurrence of ocher in the underground in the area. Energinet has done geotechnical and geophysical studies of the whole area to get a good insight into how the underground is composed. It is important for us to plan the location of the station and the subsequent construction works.

Our studies confirm that the area contains slate, which contains the mineral pyrite - also known as sulfur kis. If pyrite is exposed to oxygen, for example if the soil is drained, it develops ocher that is harmful to the aquatic environment if it is discharged into streams. It is a well -known phenomenon in the area where the drainage and development of ocher has previously colored Risebækken Orangerød.

The risk of leaching of ocher is a well -known problem that can be handled by using certain techniques during work - for example, the groundwater is collected and cleaned before it is discharged. Together with groundwater, it is generally a topic that is thoroughly addressed in the environmental impact report, which is part of the Environmental Protection Agency's environmental assessment of the project itself. Here, there will be a number of requirements for the construction work so that groundwater and streams do not suffer damage.

We share in Energinet Jens-Otto A. Sonne's desire to look after nature on Bornholm. Once the station is established, there will be large areas for planting and recreational areas that will contribute to biodiversity in the area.

Hopefully it will be an area that can also be used by locals and guests and help tell the story of the energy island.

At the same time, the entire Energiø Bornholm project will contribute to the green transition of Denmark and Europe with green electricity to over 3 million households.

Title: Myndighederne tvivler: Energiøen taget ud af plan
Content:
It is not worthwhile to offer the task of Energiø Bornholm. This is what the authorities' current assessment sounds like, and the energy island's planned 3 gigawatt stream is therefore no longer included in the Ministry of Energy's climate writing. A natural process that does not make the alarm bells ring, says Søren Møller Christensen.

The energy island on Bornholm is not profitable.

At least not as it seems right now, says the Ministry of Energy's Department. In fact, the economic aspect is currently considered so unlikely that the 3 gigawatts from Energiø Bornholm have been written out of the central course of the upcoming climate writing from the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Supply. It writes the media EnergiWatch.

"The politically agreed support ceiling is below the estimated support need, which is why Energiø Bornholm, cf. the methodological consideration of economic profitability for developer, will not be included in the basic course of KF24," says the so -called sector prerequisite note for climate rewriting 2024, which is currently in consultation .


The alarm bells don't ring

But even though the announcement comes in the wake of the news that the supply to the energy island in January had to be postponed, the alarm bells do not call at Søren Møller Christensen, director of Baltic Energy Island, who works with Energiø Bornholm.

- No, they don't. It is recognized that the developers, Ørsted, Vattenfall, etc. have mentioned that there are some things in the way you settle the flow that they are worried about. You have to look at this before it becomes profitable for us to bid, says the developers. On the existing legislation, there are some challenges in relation to how to get the assurance of getting rid of the flow in Germany, says Søren Møller Christensen.

He adds that some of the same reasons have helped postpone the supply.

- It is related to the things that came into the market dialogue. And my attitude is that it is crucial to get control of those things so that someone also offers.

My alarm bells would ring if no one said that something should be done about these things. If you just drove on as if nothing had happened, you would end up in a situation where no one offers the task.


Political support

It is also important to emphasize that climate writing is not a political document, says Søren Møller Christensen.

- It is an official document where you look at it based on some objective criteria.

And if you went on tender now, with the existing prices of electricity and materials and the existing legislation, you believe that none of these projects are profitable, explains Søren Møller Christensen and continues: - But I am very confident that there is a large political majority that has said this will succeed. When you read the settlement that was made about Energiø Bornholm, the political parties have given each other hand that if more funds are needed in support, they will find it. It is an expression of the support for the project, says the director of Baltic Energy Island.

Rather, Søren Møller Christensen sees it quite natural that there are some challenges when working with an 'innovative project', which he calls the energy island.

- It is an innovation to settle electricity in that way and work is being done to find a safe way to sell electricity across countries.

Whether we look into a half or full year's delay is for me to see inferior. The most important thing is that you do the work properly.

In addition to Energiø Bornholm, the Ministry of Energy does not consider that several of the other projects are profitable. All in all, only 4 out of 13 GW of offshore winds from the upcoming tenders are counted in climate write -off, EnergiWatch writes.


Facts

Climate reimbursement (previous basic projection) is a technical, professional assessment of how greenhouse gas emissions and energy consumption and energy production will develop in the period until 2030, provided a so -called "frozen policy" scenario.

"Frozen Policy" means that the development is contingent on a "politically frozen" absence of new initiatives.

Title: Søren arbejder for at få Bornholm midt ind på dansegulvet som energiø
Content:
The Baltic Sea will lay the sea to three energy islands - Bornholm, Åland and Gotland. Recently, the three islands signed a cooperation agreement, which has been baptized Three Islands Initiative. And that will help to place Bornholm centrally in the region's energy initiatives, says the director of Baltic Energy Island, Søren Møller Christensen.

What is Baltic Energy Island for those who don't know you? - Baltic Energy Island is a Bornholm commercial lighthouse that aims to ensure that the energy island of Bornholm will create growth in companies and provide competences for students and labor at Bornholm, but also generally throughout Denmark. So we have both a local leg, which is about jobs and education on Bornholm, and then we have a national leg that is about making energy islands a new Danish position of strength so that Danish companies can live by building energy islands elsewhere in the world also.

- And together with the regional municipality and the consortium of companies behind us as an organization, we have worked to get the Cooperation Agreement Three Islands Initiative to stand, which is an agreement concluded between the three political sizes in the islands - Bornholm, Bornholm, Åland and Gotland.

Why does the cooperation agreement make sense? - Åland and Gotland are also working to become energy islands. These are just some different things you can on the three islands. The ambition now is to see what we have of experience now and then define new projects together so that we can draw some money to the islands and start the development that we need on all three islands.

- Åland and Gotland also look like Bornholm by being islands that are a little to themselves at sea. We know it at Bornholm, where we are a little far away from the rest of Denmark. There is not even room for us on some Denmark maps, where we are either moved to Læsø or Lolland. But with the things that will happen in the coming years, we are suddenly in the middle of it all when we talk about energy.

- If you use a dance metaphor, we have been out on the sidelines a little on the sidelines and looked at the fact that all the others have progressed - Helsinki, Stockholm, Copenhagen, they drive around on the dance floor - and all of a sudden the spotlight is directed at us. Then we suddenly stand in the middle of the dance floor. Because with the energy that our energy island can create, the party will come from us. And we don't just want to be the EU outlet. We will be a place that others will invest in so that we can attract jobs and education to Bornholm. They have the same dreams in Gotland and Åland, so now we have a new fate of destiny.

What does the agreement more specifically get to Bornholm? - One is the knowledge that already exists where the others can do something we cannot and the other. We can exchange that, and by the fact that we are three islands that go together, it is much easier to attract money to investments in the islands, whether from the EU, or it is energy companies that would like to invest around the Baltic Sea. In addition, everyone also has a relationship with the project The Baltic Sea Hydrogen Collector, which has achieved high investment status in the EU because it is important for European energy security in a green future. It will connect Finland, Sweden, Åland, Gotland and Bornholm with Germany with green energy. So it is a project that all three islands have to relate to and work with. And there it also makes us much stronger to be able to do it together.

What has been the biggest challenge of your time as director of Baltic Energy Island? - The biggest task is to build a new organization that plays all other good ones. After all, Baltic Energy Island is created to be a Bornholm commercial lighthouse that can lift us all, and I already think we have succeeded. But there is still much to reach before the energy island is scheduled to be ready by 2030 or 2031.

How many workplaces will it mean for the island, and are there any professional groups you need particularly? - It's a super interesting question.

Because if we did nothing, then maybe 150 jobs would come. But the whole ambition of what we work with is to have a lot of business built up around it, so the jobs that come become local jobs and not people who fly in and out and take advantage of the potential that comes with green power on Bornholm.

Title: Energiø Bornholm: Handling bag ordene, tak
Content:

With the Ministry of Energy Removal of the project's 3 gigawatts of power from the upcoming climate writing, serious questions arise about politicians' commitment and the project's reality.

It is worrying that a project of this caliber - apparently supported by a broad political majority - now seems to hang in a thin thread. For Bornholm's citizens and business, who have invested time, hope and resources in the vision of Energiø Bornholm, this development is not only disappointing, but also deeply problematic.

The key question is why we should invest our society and life in the realization of the energy island if the positive climate effects and economic sustainability are so uncertain that they are not even included in the ministry's own projection? This creates a sense of uncertainty and lack of confidence in the future of the project.

This uncertainty about Energiø Bornholm's future should manage for political action. It is crucial that politicians not only express support for the project, but also actively work to ensure its viability and realization. It involves a serious reassessment of financial models and an adjustment of the support frames.

The current situation around Energiø Bornholm illustrates a bigger problem in climate policy: big visions and promises that fall to the ground when the realities knock on the door. To achieve real sustainable development and climate improvements, beautiful words and appointments are not enough. We need concrete action, safe financing and transparent plans that can stand the distance even when challenges arise.

For Bornholm part, it is essential that Energiø Bornholm does not end up as a cold -sailed dream. The future of the island - financially, environmentally and socially - can be closely related to the success of this project. It is therefore crucial that politicians at all levels take responsibility and deal with the necessary seriousness and commitment needed to transform Energiø Bornholm's visions into reality.

As citizens and as part of a community that faces major climate and financial challenges, we expect our politicians to deal with the same degree of seriousness as they talk about climate change and sustainable development. Energiø Bornholm can and should be a lighthouse for green transition, but only if words are turned into action.

Title: Antropologistuderende ser på borgerinddragelse omkring Energiø Bornholm
Content:
Hannah Birch, an anthropology student, hopes together with his fellow students to create some awareness of Energiø Bornholm and not least the citizens' experience of the great project. For only through successful citizen involvement can one get citizens to engage in the green transition, she believes.

Yesterday you made a workshop at the Electric Works in Rønne together with your study group. What did it go about? - My study group and I read anthropology at the University of Copenhagen in the fourth semester, and we have been tasked with doing a fieldwork around democratic inclusion in green transition. I come from Bornholm myself, so we chose to do a project about how the citizens feel included around Energiø Bornholm. That was the workshop part of.

How have you worked with your fieldwork so far? - We have tried some different methods of and did many interviews for example with the Citizens' Association Energiø Bornholm, which is against Energiø Bornholm. Then we have also talked to the municipality about how Energiø Bornholm is to be performed and how the citizens are involved in it, just as we have also talked to Baltic Energy Island about how Bornholm should cooperate with Åland and Gotland as energy islands.

- We have also been to BOFA and heard about how, for example, they involve citizens by inviting schools to visit and take a Bofa bus out to the locals to talk to them one by one. And we have done that to see if there is any of what BOFA does, which Energiø Bornholm might learn a little from in relation to citizen involvement.

Why is it so important with citizen involvement?

- We believe that a community can motivate people to engage themselves in the green transition, and if there are some major authorities that take over such as the government, the municipality and so on, then we believe that if there is no some citizen involvement, then you lose citizens, and that means they do not engage in the green transition. But by reaching out to the citizens and talking to them one by one who believe that you can better hear them and meet them and engage them in the green communities and initiatives.

- For example, we visited Jørn Ole, who is part of the Bornholm Citizens' Association and is against Energiø Bornholm. He has been told that his Christmas tree plantation must close because there must be an energy -grinding plant as part of Energiø Bornholm. And then we asked him how he could have better been informed of Energiø Bornholm, and then his answer was that if it had been at the early stage and more people had come and had talked to him and told him the information, then He would probably feel a little more involved in Energiø Bornholm.

- We also talked to the Business Center Bornholm, which is positive about the project and tries to involve the young people on the island, to get them back to the island, because Energiø Bornholm will probably get more jobs in the long term on the island. The island is now a lot of tourism, and Energiø Bornholm sees the Business Center Bornholm as an opportunity to operate the island all year round, so it is not just in the summer.

Is it your impression that Energiø Bornholm has been too poor to involve the citizens of Bornholm? - It's not to conclude yet, as we've only been here three days. We are trying to find out how the decision -making process has progressed, and there we have been informed that there have been some citizen meetings where there were many who attended at first, but that there has been a little more dropout through the citizen meetings, they have had.

Does not drop off a little interest on the part of the citizens? - We have the impression that there is a lack of information about the project. When I even got the idea that my group and I should go to Bornholm, I thought what we were going to investigate was Bright Green Island, but was told by Bornholm Regional Municipality that it was something you went into a little more for four years ago, and now it is Energiø Bornholm that has taken over. So we have the idea that there is some information and dissemination to the citizens, so that they know that the energy island project at Bornholm exists.

What does you particularly occupy you as an anthropology student?

- The green transition takes up me a lot, but it also takes me a lot to hear groups that are usually not heard and try to understand their position, where they come from both in green transition, but also in cultural understanding. I very much believe that a collaboration works best when all parties are heard in a situation and in relation to Energiø Bornholm.

Do you find that there is a lot of resistance to the energy island among the citizens here on the island? - At least with several of those we have talked to so far. But the ones we have talked to have also been primarily from the resistance group.

But for the workshop we wanted to see people with slightly different backgrounds. It's not so much about being for and against, but about hearing all citizens.

How long do you stay on the island? - We are here on Friday, but our fieldwork lasts a month, so maybe we will come back or we will continue the fieldwork online.

What thus happens the information you get together through your fieldwork on the island? - We prepare this in a report that will be our exam, and we have promised a lot of parties here from the island that we will send them the report afterwards. Because if there are many parties who get the report, they might use our results for something.

Title: Elværkets vilde historier
Content:
The old power plant contains piles of stories, and in the future they become even more crucial to us. Here's a glance behind the beautiful and thick walls of Rønne.

If the walls of the old power plant could speak, they would be able to tell many stories from the more than 110 years of the power plant.

The walls and the whole building, which was built for Rønne Municipal Electricity Works and Hot Water Bathing Institute, were designed by the renowned Danish architect Anton Rosen and erected 1910-12 with later extensions in 1925 and in 1938. The buildings were preserved in 2015.

Unfortunately, walls can not speak. But fortunately, we are often visited by Bornholmers who have lived part of their lives in the buildings. It is fascinating, because the experiences range widely. Last year, an elderly lady from Nexø told me that she had grown up in the director's residence as a child of the last power plant manager. Others say that as children in the 1950s they got their weekly bath in the bathing facility. The bathing facility is a fascinating story in itself. If you walk past the power plant, you can see that there is a distinctive tower out towards Lille Madsegade. The tower is not only for decoration, because at the top there is a water tank of 20,000 liters of water, which was heated by surplus heat from the machines inside the large halls. In this way, the story repeats itself when we discuss today how we can utilize surplus heat from the land plant and a possible PTX production to supply ourselves with Bornholmers with district heating.

Surplus heat was hardly what occupied the young people who used the empty halls for underground raving parties in the years after the turn of the millennium. At least they were preoccupied with system -critical graffiti that adorned the walls when we moved in, and even though they are not quite as young when they talk about the parties today, they are still proud of their youthful daring.

There are also many memories from the time after electricity production, which in the 1950s moved down to Rønne Harbor. The buildings were taken over by a machine shop. had a visit by a former employee from Rønne Maskinfabrik. He handed over a larger material with pictures and descriptions from an exciting period where Was produced shrimp pills and where customers spoke a business like Novo.

Today, the power plant forms a framework for the Bornholm commercial lighthouse and the Baltic Energy Island Foundation. In the old director's residence, we gather all those who work for Energiø Bornholm to be the basis for growth and development on the island. Inside the old halls we, together with Energinet, have made an exhibition where you can become wiser on Energiø Bornholm, and where you can see, among other things, an example of a wing tip from the new type of wind turbines that can stand south of Bornholm.

It is our ambition to renovate the beautiful protected buildings and create a mini -university at Bornholm; A place where companies, researchers and students can meet and together create innovative solutions that can drive the green transition and at the same time create growth on Bornholm. Already today we often have visits from companies and not least students from DTU and other universities who come here to collaborate with Bornholm companies.

Do you fancy a look in behind the old walls? Then finally look past when we are open power plants next time on March 21 from 16-18 or when we open the halls one of the coming months. Follow the www.balticenergyisland.com.

In the future, Søren Møller Christensen will talk once a month about what is happening at the power plant and throughout the project behind in Lille Madsegade.

Content:
Last week, a chronicle breathed new life in the criticism of the energy island and especially the economy behind it. Locally and nationally, there are still shared opinions about the future of Energiø Bornholm.

D.

Rop the energy island and give the money to the municipalities.

Nuclear power plants could be a better solution. Scrap the plans if the price rises.

If you say Energiø out loud, there is always doomed debate. With shared opinions as a result. The above statements come from three different politicians and they have much more at heart.

Last week, three economists spoke against Energiø Bornholm. Peter Mogensen, director of the think tank Kraka, research leader and professor emeritus at VIVE, Jørgen Søndergaard and Peter Kjær Kruse-Andersen, Assistant Professor of Economics at the University of Copenhagen, jointly authored a chronicle with a simple and clear message: Energiø Bornholm is a waste of tax crowns .

To the Journal, Peter Mogensen elaborates his criticism.

- It is an old political hype that drives this loser project that the energy island is. Because you can get many other solutions much cheaper, says Peter Mogensen.

Forget water and seek land he thinks Bornholm should drop all thoughts of water and instead turn their eyes to land.

- Cut some wind turbines up in the middle of the island with you (Bornholm, ed.) Instead of in the water. It is not much soil that is needed. It only costs two-thirds of what it costs to build out in the water, and then it is much faster home, says Peter Mogensen and comes with an alternative if Bornholm does not want to put island to Møller.

- In West Jutland, for example, there is plenty of room to build mills. It is far cheaper and not least much faster to get listed if you want to accelerate the green transition.

Budgets seem to be sliding, and if they step much more, the Liberal Alliance steps from the deal. That is the message from the party's climate mayor, Steffen W. Frølund.

- We don't think further taxpayers should be put into it. If it can be run within the current framework, we are happy. If new money is needed, we are not involved, he says.

Steffen W. Frølund also has another fear.

- I don't think the environmental consequences are thoroughly illuminated. One of the things we can be afraid of is that the marine environment is damaging, he says.

Waste of tax dollars in the municipal council doubts René Danielsson (DF) that the one who Energiø is actually a good idea.

And if there is a choice before the plans for the energy island are finally adopted, Atlantis will be sentenced. - If we get a blue majority, we won't get any energy island, he states.

Basically, René Danielsson seems to be a waste of tax dollars.

- We have a hard time seeing the reason in throwing good money after bad money. I'd rather have had the money paid to the municipality so we could invest them in another way, he says and continues with a calculator at the table: - If Peter Mogensens and the other's chronicle comes true, I'd rather have the share in the 31, DKK 5 billion as a subsidy to the municipality than some uncertain, possible jobs on an energy island. If the original DKK 17.6 billion is distributed proportionally to the municipalities, Bornholm would get DKK 123 million.

Why don't we know the numbers? On the whole, he does not think there is enough light on what the energy island gives Bornholm of opportunities.

- Why can't we be allowed to see what the potential is for the island as a community and as a municipality, should it be such a good business? It's a lot of positive theses without us being allowed to see what's behind. They shoot with a shotgun. Now I have heard of this Energiø for three years, and no one can tell me how many jobs it can become, he says.

At the municipal council's conservative member Linda Kofoed Persson, the energy island must pass. But one should have considered another option.

- If we had been able to get started with the discussion earlier, I'd rather have had nuclear power. I have read some articles that it is not so dangerous anymore and that they have made some new solutions. It is not the same amount of radioactive waste to abolish any longer. It's not like Barsebäck. If it had been cheaper to produce electricity that way, I would clearly have preferred a nuclear power plant instead of an energy island. If you patched less of the sea with something other than the many offshore wind turbines, I would clearly go for it, she says.

However, supply security plays into the energy island must exist regardless of a possible budget overrun.

- Now you have come so far with this, so I think we should go out and continue so we can get some green transition. But with the other hand, one must also start looking at new solutions that could be the nuclear power of some kind. Because there is so much new exciting there, without having read me all the way down. But just with the articles I've read, I think it could be hugely exciting, says Linda Kofoed Persson.

In Christiansborg, both the Social Democracy and the Moderates are called for insanity. - There is nothing new in what they write in the chronicle. It is a point of view Kraka has had all the way and they overlook in my eyes an important thing. We have a huge interest in tying our energy system together across Europe with first Germany and later Poland. We must also create security of supply to Zealand with the cable that is being drawn in connection with the energy island, says former Environment Minister and current climate mayor Lea Wermelin (S).

The same wording is found in the moderates. - There are many things in the energy island besides the price. The security of supply from Germany to Bornholm and on to Zealand is also an important aspect. So to start concluding something before we have had it in tender, I think I do not make sense, says climate mayor Henrik Frandsen.

The next step towards the creation of the energy island is to find out which private companies should help to realize the project. Different tenders happen.

Title: Forening vil søge flere diskussioner om energi i Danmark og Europa
Content:
In the coming year, Bornholm's Environment and Energy Association will seek to participate in several information and discussion events that are about renewable energy in Denmark and Europe.

It is one of the results of the association's general meeting, which was held on Wednesday.

The association feels that there is an interest in the association's attitude towards large Bornholm energy projects. -Due to several consultation responses and debate posts, several board members have been contacted by both media and not least researchers who are interested in the association's attitude to both the content, but just as much the debate on relevant topics, especially in connection with Energiø Bornholm and Power-to-X projects, says chairman Peter Haag.

Although the association has previously had to shut down activities due to a lack of financial basis, the chairman estimates that it has continued to work for the association's purpose.

- In previous years we were able to use our remaining equity to provide deficit guarantees to eco -land Bornholm as well as to the initiative group for Bornholm's offshore wind.

- Bomef will continue to provide support for similar projects that can be of great importance to Bornholm's environmental and energy development, says Peter Haag, who, however, acknowledges that the association's activity level has been modest in the past year.

However, the members of the association continue to assert themselves in relevant debates, by board work in the local action group (LAG) and the citizen energy community Bornholm's offshore wind, as well as in the green dialogue forum

Title: Bornholm, Danmark og Europa bliver taberne
Content:
The opposition to the energy island must be rejected, says Social Democrat Claus Larsen-Jensen.

E

N Rules of economists have recently tried to cast doubt on the entire Energiø project. Some of them have always been opposed, and now the resistance to the project is again aired. And someone then combines their resistance with the fact that they would rather have nuclear power than wind power. But Denmark has rejected nuclear power and bet on wind and sun. The decision on the energy island is a consequence of the chosen strategy. The energy island will secure electricity for three million households in Denmark and Europe. It is therefore also part of the energy strategy in the EU, and Denmark is a crucial player in this. Bornholm is the center of this.

The resistance to the energy island must therefore be rejected. There is no major infrastructure project in Denmark, which is not exposed to the same resistance. There is financial criticism. There is criticism in relation to nature and the environment, etc. And of course, consideration must be taken. There was resistance to the Great Belt Bridge, the Øresund Bridge, Lynetteholmen, the Fehmarnbælt tunnel, and now the resistance to the energy island and the focus on wind power, where there is also an agenda that deals with nuclear power.

Is there a financial uncertainty with the energy island and the other major projects? Yes. This is always the case, because everything cannot be predicted by such large, new and groundbreaking projects. But the crucial thing is that if you have decided to want that development, then one must stand firm and complete the project. What is the alternative? Nothing? Or what else? Therefore, it is good that the government and the Folketing are held firmly in the Energiø project.

For Bornholm it is crucial. It is the largest infrastructure project and the largest investment in many decades at Bornholm.

It is not only the prerequisite for the energy island, but also for the establishment of a green fuel plant and a green business park on Bornholm. Everything that needs to attract labor, create new types of jobs, and increase the people of Bornholm. Everything it takes for Bornholm to get out of the financial clamp we are in now. It takes a few years before it is established and is in operation. But if you imagine that the energy island was dropped, then Bornholm says no to the possibility of this development boost.

The economists' proposal that the state instead of spending the money on the establishment of the energy island, spent them on grants to the municipalities is no alternative. Nor for Bornholm. It is hardly likely that the large billionth investment would instead go to BRK's operation. And that leaves the problem that Denmark and Europe cannot implement the Green Energy Option and ensure security of supply with electricity. It is also perspective -less that money that Should be used for investment therein to create development is spent on operation that does not lift the development.

Denmark and Europe will lose that. But the big loser would be Bornholm, because then we can forget about the development lift, which it together with Rønne Harbor with the shipping of wind turbines, gives Bornholm opportunities. It is important that we do not shake the hand at Bornholm, even if the development creates some changes. It constitutes a chance that must not be lost. And those who are politically opposed, the Bornholmers owe an explanation of what if the chance was lost. With the energy island, etc. Bornholm moves from being an outskirts in Denmark to being at the center of green energy production in Denmark and Europe. It offers new opportunities for Bornholm.

Title: Investeringer for mere end en halv milliard
Content:
You can provide input to the plan for the development of the Bornholm Electricity network applicable from 2025.

H.

If the electricity consumption in Bornholm develops in the same way that expectations are in the rest of Denmark, we can look forward to more than a doubling of consumption by 2030 on Bornholm. This is done as a result of the electrification of society, which especially breaks through the number of heat pumps for heating homes and on different modes of transport - both electric cars for private transport and for heavier transport needs.

We've got the first electric buses. At the same time, there are more and more private individuals on Bornholm investing in solar cells. Most of our electricity grid is built in a time when the world was different and electricity was used for supply lights, television, refrigerator, etc. But with the rising electrification, where electricity also has to cover heating and transport, our existing electricity grid must be expanded . At the five-year aim, the calculations show that about half a billion kroner's investments in electricity grids, IT systems and measuring equipment are needed to meet the increasing need. As the legislation is, all customers have the right to have their consumption covered. The investment plan must reflect that.

Openness about investment needs and calculations The electrification of society is evolving at a high pace in these years. Therefore, the legislation requires that the grid companies - on Bornholm Trefor EL -NET EAST - prepare and publish plans for investments for the next five to ten years. The plans must also state which warehouses the company will use to balance consumption so that investments can be limited. It is important that monopoly companies are open about the conditions in the company that affect consumers and prices.

Energinet's Board of Directors and thus the state has not yet decided whether and how Bornholm's Elnet should be linked to an upcoming Energiø and Transformer Station south of Aakirkeby. Therefore, the forecast in the development plan is based on the fact that Bornholm remains linked to the state network with the search cable from Hasle. In two years, when we have to make the next web development plan 2027, that question is probably clarified. It can be of great importance at that time.

Invitation to major consumers The proposal for a network development plan for TREFOR EL-NET EAST CARE CARE from 2025 is available from April 4 on the Supply Authority's website and in consultation until May 1, 2024.

It is our hope that especially the large energy consumers in Bornholm as a municipality, the municipal limited companies, the large state companies, the hospital and the largest private companies such as blacksmiths, dairy, slaughterhouse and others will take the time to respond to the consultation.

Each one has knowledge of special changes in their company's electricity consumption or investment plans that may affect the investment requirement in the electricity grid.

The same applies if private or fiery souls with special knowledge can contribute to the qualification of the forecasts for the development of electricity consumption at Bornholm.

Title: Bornholm i centrum - igen
Content:
Brint, atomkraft og pantsætning - det har været en alsidig uge på det gamle elværk.

Der er aldrig to uger, der er ens på kontoret her hos Baltic Energy Island.

Både gæsterne og emnerne spænder bredt, hvilket er meget sigende for arbejdet med energiøer. Lad mig tage jer med igennem en tilfældig uge, der viser bredden i arbejdet; uge 12.

Mandag morgen havde jeg besøg af en haslebo, Joachim Lind Koefoed, som nu bor ovre og arbejder som manager hos Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners - en global virksomhed, der satser massivt på grøn energi herunder havvind og energiøer. Selvom det er mange år siden, han er flyttet fra Bornholm, har han fortsat et godt øje for sin fødeø, og inden han satte kursen retur mod Sjælland, var han forbi til en kop morgenkaffe. Kaffen blev krydret med en god snak om østersøregionen og ikke mindst CIP"s fokus på de mange havvindmøller, virksomheden forventer at etablere i regionen, herunder i Baltikum, Sverige og Finland. For Bornholm er det særligt interessant, at CIP arbejder for at etablere et brintrør, der skal transportere brint fra Den Botniske Bugt i nord til Nordtyskland i syd. Det giver mulighed for tilkoblinger til energiøerne Bornholm, Gotland og Åland og dermed muliggøre afsætning af brint produceret via power-to-x på Bornholm og de to andre øer.

Fredag fik vi besøg af Morten Løkkegaard, der repræsenterer Venstre i Europa Parlamentet i Bruxelles. Dialogen med Morten kom særligt til at handle om atomkraft og Bornholms placering i Østersøen. Morten fortalte om, at atomkraft er kommet i fokus på den europæiske politiske scene, og at mange sætter deres lid til, at atomkraft kan løse den grønne omstilling. Jeg fortalte, at jeg er overbevist om, at atomkraft spiller en rolle i den grønne omstilling, men at det på den korte bane er vigtigt, at vi fokuserer på havvind, som er billigt og sikkert. Med den nuværende teknologi koster strøm fra atomkraft cirka det dobbelte af strøm fra havvind. Vi var enige om, at det er ikke et enten eller, men et både og, og at det bliver interessant at se, hvad den aktuelle udvikling af en ny generation af atomkraft kan føre til.

Morten Løkkegaard var også meget optaget af det samarbejde i Østersøen, som vi er ved at opbygge. Grøn energi og sikkerhed har stort fokus i EU, og vi drøftede vigtigheden af et endnu stærkere samarbejde mellem landene rundt om Østersøen, og at Bornholm har en vigtig rolle i den sammenhæng.

Samme emne var i fokus torsdag aften, hvor vi under overskriften Bornholm - fra udkant til centrum slog dørene op til vores månedlige arrangement Åbent Elværk. Efter et kig på udstillingen i hallerne samledes vi i workshoplokalet, hvor jeg fortalte om, hvordan Bornholm med energiøen så at sige flytter plads. Vi går fra at være en ø, der er klippet ud og sat ind i en firkant ud for Læsø, til at være i centrum - og hvor Sjælland og København i nogle sammenhænge bliver vores udkant.

Men, jeg er jo tilflytter - og heldigvis kunne en indfødt bornholmer, og antropolog, Lars Christian Kofoed Rømer gøre os meget klogere på, hvordan Bornholm, udover at været centrum for bornholmerne selv, flere gange gennem tiden har været genstand for stor værdi for andre end bornholmerne selv. Det vidner de rige arkæologiske fund og mange forsvarsværker om. Bornholm har været et sted, som man gerne ville have kontrol over og indflydelse på. Lars fortalte også om, at Bornholm flere gange er blevet fanget i dette spil. Blandt andet da Bornholm blev pantsat i de sidste 50 år af middelalderen til Hansestaden Lybæk, som betaling for Lybæks støtte til kong Fredrik den første i hans oprør mod Christian den anden. I et historisk perspektiv har Bornholm på den måde flere gange været en del af et spil, der er større end øen selv. Bornholm kan på én gang både være et værdifuldt center i Østersøen, samtidig med at øen er en dansk udkant, hvor man lokalt ønsker at have medindflydelse og gevinst, når - og hvis - Bornholms centrale placering skal bruges til at løse større internationale udfordringer og ikke blot overlades til en oplevelse af at være blevet pantsat for at imødekomme eksterne interesser.

Lars" fortælling var tankevækkende.

Der er ingen tvivl om, at Bornholm med energiøen igen står i en situation, hvor vi har stor værdi for mange andre end lige os, der bor her på øen. Hvordan sikrer vi, at energiøen for os bornholmere ikke bliver en oplevelse af igen at blive pantsat og sat uden for indflydelse? Mit bedste bud og min klare overbevisning er, at det er ved, at vi læner os ind i projektet, og gennem konkrete handlinger kæmper for den vision, som både kommunalbestyrelsen og vi i Baltic Energy Island har sat os for: Energiø Bornholm skal blive en løftestang for den bornholmske økonomi med nye arbejdspladser, bedre uddannelser og flere bornholmere. Det sker dog ikke at sig selv. Vi er nødt til at kæmpe for det, hvis vi vil have det til at ske.

DAGENS DEBAT-CITAT Jeg har overvejet at flytte til Svaneke, da jeg har hørt, at det er der, de interessante bor Den bekymrede

Title: Hård kritik: Energiø gør Bornholm til mål for russerne
Content:
The Bornholm Association will convince the Defense Committee of the risk of Russian attack.

H.

Enrik Espersen saw it with his own eyes as he sat in his sailboat. A large Russian military ship sailed around the Baltic Sea at exactly the place where the German electric cables run together.

Before long, a German helicopter came out and whipped the water up around the ship to make it pack and sail home.

And precisely because of episodes like this, Henrik Espersen fears the location of a transformer station on Bornholm.

- It will be a 10 -minute flight for a Russian missile shipped from Kaliningrad, he says.

It is precisely such a scenario that the Citizens' Association Energiø Bornholm will present when they are represented by the Defense Committee.

In addition to the attack on Bornholm and the accompanying devastation, Henrik Espersen outlines the possible consequences for the rest of northern Europe.

- The planned transformer station on Bornholm will, as I said, be an obvious target for a Russian attack. If a 3Gigawatt transformer station is bombed, it will put the electricity grid down in large parts of Europe. In this way, it will be very easy for the Russians to cause great damage with a little effort, he says.

At the same time, the Citizens' Association Energiø Bornholm thinks that the authorities are too poor to inform about the processes and the consequences.

- The neighbors of an upcoming transformer station feel overheard. Some are for, some are against. And some feel anxious about it all, explains Henrik Espersen.

It is not yet decided whether the homeowners close to the transformer station should be compensated financially, and it seems Henrik Espersen is deeply unreasonable.

Loss of power en route to Germany The reason why a transformer station should be built is that the power must be redone. The wind turbines produce alternating current. This is the type of power we use in Europe. The problem is that it is more effective to transport direct current; There is simply less loss and that is why you want to set up a transformer station. Then the power from the mills will be transformed into DC at the Transformer Station on Bornholm and back to AC when it is in Germany.

But Henrik Espersen thinks that is unnecessary.

He does not think that the power loss is in line with all the other genes that Bornholm is applied in connection with having a large transformer station erected on the island. - Why should you first carry the flow from the mills in the sea 20 kilometers to Bornholm and then send it to Germany. There are only 100 kilometers from the mills down to their facilities, he says.

The Citizens' Association Energiø Bornholm has already represented the climate, energy and supply committee to argue that the project is not profitable and will adversely affect Bornholm in many ways.

By requesting representing the Defense Committee, they hope to be able to raise awareness of the security issue for Bornholm and the general security of supply in Europe.

Title: Borgermøde om højspændingsstation
Content:
The municipality and Energinet inform and answer questions about the land plant. ENVIRONMENT.

B

The Ornholm Regional Municipality, together with Energinet, invites you to a civic meeting on the planning basis for the high -voltage station (the land plant) to Energiø Bornholm. The meeting will be held at Snorrebakken 66 in Knudsker on Tuesday, April 23 at 4.30 pm.

The meeting comes well midway through the current consultation period for the various plan proposals, which will pave the way for the establishment of the large land plant on Søndre Landevej near Sose. The municipal council approved the plan proposals for the high voltage station on March 19, after which the proposals were submitted for consultation for eight weeks. Consultation responses to the plan proposals must reach the municipality's plan department no later than 15 May.

At the Citizens' Meeting, the municipality and Energinet will inform about the content of the documents and the project as well as the further process, and you will have the opportunity to ask questions about the consultation. On the municipality's website you can find the consultation material. The establishment of a high voltage station requires both a municipal plant supplement and a local plan with associated environmental report.

The proposal for the local plan lays down detailed provisions for how the construction can be placed and what it should look like. The environmental report describes what environmental considerations have been taken and what environmental impacts the plans can lead to.

When the consultation is over, the municipal council must process the consultation responses received before the plans can be adopted with any adjustments. After that there will be a four -week complaint.

Title: Fra Samsø over Bornholm til Bruxelles
Content:
