In recent weeks I have been away from Bornholm twice - a trip to Samsø and a trip to Brussels. There are two very different places, but one thing ties the two places together with Bornholm: A common focus on following local value with when set up sun and wind.

Friday morning, April 19, I boarded the ferry to Samsø. Together with Lea Wermelin and Klaus Vesløv from BEOF, I had left to visit Samsø Energy Academy. We were on a common mission to focus on the possibilities the green transition provides island and rural society as Bornholm. When we started the dialogue, I was actually quite skeptical. I had doubts about how much Samsø has focused on citizen -driven initiatives and local self -sufficiency can be related to the situation we are facing at Bornholm, where Energiø Bornholm will produce up to 50 times Bornholm's own power consumption. However, my skepticism was put to shame. At Samsø, politicians have decided that they will at least produce twice their own power consumption, and they will use the green energy production as a basis for local value creation. At the same time, they find that the solar and wind projects that are planned on and in the sea around the island gradually become so large and expensive that local staff becomes difficult. They are therefore looking for other models to create a local value creation - in the same way as is the case with us at Bornholm.

If we take up the discussion in the helicopter and put it in perspective, we are talking about a development that can potentially elaborate on the gap that already exists between city and country. The green transition and upcoming charges on CO2 emissions will hit country and city differently. At Bornholm as in other rural areas we have a lot of agriculture, a lot of production and much transport. There are sectors that have high CO2 emissions and will be affected by CO2 taxes. At the same time, the same rural areas can look forward to putting fields and sea views for large sun and wind energy projects to secure green power to the big cities. This means that the green transition provides a local experience that the traditional business foundation is crumbling at the same time as the areas are socketed for the green transition of the urbanized urban areas. With a jerky expression, it can be seen as a losing losing situation for rural areas. When I was in Brussels a week before, I experienced in both parliamentary politicians and representatives of the Commission a deep concern that this contradiction between country and city is growing so deep that it stops the green transition.

Several have experienced that Brussels was blocked by protesting farmers who drove their tractors into the city and that the so -called yellow vests loudly showed their dissatisfaction with actions to ensure a green transition, but at the same time affect their lives in a negative direction . In response to this experience, Samsø and Bornholm will work together to show the way for a social vision for rural areas, where the billion-dollar investments in solar and wind energy are based on a development and transformation history that rests on local value creation. This does not mean that things will not change, but hopefully Lose-Lose can be turned into the experience of a transformation that pointed to a local positive development.

What is it that we are talking about? We zoom in on Bornholm, CRT prepared in 2023 an analysis of the local value creation in connection with Energiø Bornholm. It shows that between 390 and 900 new jobs will be created, while population growth in 2030 will be between 460 and 1,059 people.

The large span is defined by how large parts of the economic activities in relation to the energy island that Bornholm manages to attract. At least the scenario is Bornholm alone Service Port for the offshore wind turbines, in the second scenario Bornholm also manages the installation of the offshore wind turbines, while Bornholm in the third scenario also attracts Power-to-X. To this end, additional elements such as Green Energi-Erhvervspark and Residential College at Rønne Old Elværk, which are not included in the analysis, can be added because the activities were still under development when the analysis was prepared. A similar analysis is made at Åland, where they estimate that 150-300 lasting jobs will be created solely due to the service of the wind turbines, while up to 1,700 will be employed in the construction phase.

However, none of this comes by itself.

We need to develop new models for citizen involvement, business development, co-ownership, supply systems, innovation and education with ourselves in rural areas, where we are traditionally disconnected from the growth and innovation environments in the major urban centers. This is precisely what is the focus of the collaboration with Samsø. As two Living Labs, we will develop models that other communities in Denmark and Europe can be inspired by, so that the green transition not only succeeds but also succeeds in a way that is geographically fair.

Title: Drømme og fantasier om vejen til de 42.000 bornholmere

Title: En ødsel omstilling
Content:
The unit list is not against green transition, but against the power-to-x industry on Bornholm, Helle Munk Ravnborg points out in a response to a reader letter.

K

Honor Esben Ørberg, thanks for reading my post from the other day and also thanks for taking the time to comment on it.

Let me start by stating: For me - and for the Unity List Bornholm - an energy efficient and socially economically appropriate green transition is a very important goal, and that is the goal we are seeking to pursue.

Next: As you hopefully noticed, my post is not about Project Energiø Bornholm, ie the plans for 3 GW on offshore wind off Bornholm with associated land and cables for Germany and Zealand respectively.

The Unity List - and the Unity List Bornholm - has supported these plans, as part of the green transition and efforts to get more green power, not only to Denmark, but also to Europe, and to build the infrastructure to be built to, so that we can exchange green power across land borders in Europe, so that we can jointly get rid of fossil energy.

The original agreement on Energiø Bornholm stated that Energiø Bornholm should be for socio -economic gain.

This has been modified later, and now the political agreement states that it is willing to provide a state subsidy of up to DKK 17.6 billion from the Danish side to the project, and that Germany will also contribute to financing both cable wiring to Germany and of land facilities on Bornholm. This is the backdrop but not the subject of my post.

On the other hand, my speech is about the plans for Power-to-X on Bornholm, which is outlined in the supplement to Bornholm Regional Municipality's business strategy, which a majority in the municipal council on Bornholm adopted in late summer 2023 outside the Unity List Bornholm. The supplement bears the title Powerto growth and is focused on the desire to establish a business park on Bornholm with a view to establishing Energitung Industri on Bornholm in connection with, but not as part of Energiø Bornholm. After all, the fact that the PTX plans are not included as an integral part of Energiø Bornholm, is evident, among other things, from the fact that they are not included as part of the plan for Energiø Bornholm that the Danish Energy Agency has just published.

What motivates my post is that this power-to-growth supplement has now just suddenly gained a very prominent place in the draft planning and development strategy that is for political treatment this month. I wonder - and us in the Unity List - hurt. It is true that in the spring of 2023 in the municipal council we adopted what should be the benchmarks for the plan and development strategy that the municipal council has a duty to prepare and adopt. Here, "Energiø for the benefit of Bornholm" was one of the benchmarks, while the power-to-growth supplement did not include, all the while that it was neither prepared nor adopted.

The Unity List Bornholm has at no time backed up on a possible establishment of a PTX industry in Bornholm, because we do not believe it will benefit Bornholm and the green transition. There are several reasons for this. A very important reason is that we want an energy and socio-economically appropriate green transition in line with the energy strategy that an unanimous municipal council on Bornholm adopted in 2021.

PTX, ie electrolysis (= the cleavage of technical water to hydrogen and oxygen), is a technology under development, and at this time the energy loss, that is, the production of heat in the process is quite large, namely in the region of 40 percent. If the hydrogen is then processed into methanol or ammonia, there is a further loss of energy. The energy loss is in the form of heat, and the cleavage of water for hydrogen and oxygen occurs, and the further processing to methanol or ammonia, ie PTX, in the parts of Denmark where there is a large district heating network that can utilize this heat, then the energy loss can Possibly defended because the heat from the process can be utilized and replaced the burning of biomass and more. But in Bornholm, it will only be a very small part of the heat from PTX that can be recovered in a socio -economically appropriate way and therefore it will constitute an energy loss. This means that for every kilowatt-time current that will be brought into a PTX plant on Bornholm with the known technology, somewhere between 40 and 80 percent will be lost in the form of heat. This is something that we in the Unity List Bornholm have very difficult to connect with green transition. Rather, in our view, it sounds like a very resource -intensive and thus wasteful - both in resource and financial sense - transition, something we have difficulty supporting. And of course, of course, we cannot support a planning and development strategy that proposes the establishment of such a socially uneconomical and energy-efficient development that PTX on Bornholm in our view will constitute. The fact that it will also not create the basis for the population development we all dream of for Bornholm in no way makes the case better.

Title: Bornholm vil bevare støtteordning i EU

Title: Forsker vil hjælpe bornholmerne med spørgsmål om energiøen
Content:
Poor communication has created uncertainty in the population. It shows the first parts of Kristian Holst Kristiansen's research.

What exactly are you doing on Bornholm? -I first examine the public controversy about Energiø Bornholm and Power-to-X.

What kind of skepticism is there when you talk to the Bornholmers about the energy island? -It is very difficult to generalize, because resistance to energy island and power-to-x is rarely overall in relation to what I have experienced.

- There is a dissatisfaction with how citizen involvement has been so far. There have been some citizen meetings where people have come in suits who have handed over some information.

- At the same time, it has been limited what opportunities have been for dialogue and to get answers to some of the questions they have not been answered yet. - And then in relation to the hearings that have been, there are lack of response to the consultation responses.

So there has been a dissatisfaction and concern about how citizen involvement has so far taken place. Citizens also do not have a feeling of knowing how Energiø Bornholm is going to affect their lives.

Does the dissatisfaction make sense? - Yes, I think so. There has been an experience that those who have handed over the information have not had an insight into the local conditions and for those living in the area. There is a problem in relation to the compensation in connection with the energy island. Some citizens either become expropriated or receive compensation, but it has not yet been settled, and it helps to create dissatisfaction. There are also those who live just outside the area where the transformer station is to be placed. They do not receive any compensation, which also helps to create dissatisfaction.

What exactly is it that the affected citizens want to know? - They feel frustration at not knowing when the case will be settled and how much they can get in compensation. It is a question that fills a lot and helps to create the citizen resistance. Those affected are also concerned with what it means for the value of their houses. Others are concerned about Bornholm's identity; Whether it fits into the Bornholm community, what it means for tourism and the land idyll. It is spoiled by this and will have Bornholm more industry.

What other reservations are true among the skeptical? - Hydrogen must be produced in connection with the energy island, and the citizens ask where to place a large chemistry industry for the production of hydrogen and whether they should live near it. It's a risk company, but I'm sure you have the best experts on the matter. The question of the security factor also matters. Some are concerned about whether Bornholm can become a strategic target for Russia. If you take the sabotage of Nord Stream; It remains fresh in the memory of many people. They are afraid if the situation can be repeated if you build such a large plant. Especially the older generation that has experienced it themselves or has parents and grandparents who experienced it in relation to World War II and Russia's invasion of Bornholm.

How do the critical Bornholmers relate to the authorities? - Someone says they do not trust the municipality and the local politicians and that there is a lack of transparency in the decisions that are being made. What differences are there on the groups of the people you meet, in relation to who are skeptics and who are supporters? - There are some who do not mind the project as such and think it is certainly a very good idea and that we need the workplaces; We need the green transition.

- When I talk to the industrial side such as Rønne Harbor, it is primarily more positively voted; That we have a business opportunity and the opportunity to strengthen the economy with new jobs and newcomers. Then there are others who have the concerns I have told about.

What will be able to strengthen your research and who would you like to talk to? - First and foremost, I am interested in finding out what is of concern to the citizens and what is at stake.

- But I am also interested in finding ordinary people who are positive about the project, but I have a little trouble finding them.

- I am also interested in hearing the concerns of the industry and those that can see the benefits of the project. You need some water for this, and is possible in relation to wastewater. But also what opportunities and limitations for how to utilize the heat that becomes of profits from production. Here I also need to get hold of Beof.

Kristian Holst Kristiansen wants more Bornholmers to speak - this applies to both individuals and businesses. Everyone can contact him at khk@dbigroup.dk so if you have something at heart about the energy island and Power-T-X, he would love to hear from you.

His ambition to be able to use his Ph.D. in relation to being able to enter into a dialogue with the municipality and Rønne Harbor about what can be done better regarding citizen involvement. - We must have set up a ministry of social security. Here, a number of functions and units need to be gathered so that we get an authority that can provide the right emergency plans.

For example, we need to get things from the Defense Intelligence Service, the Emergency Management Agency and questions about cyber security in so that we can make a total threat assessment, then we can make plans for what we do if something is going to happen. If we had that ministry, it would have been obvious to assess all matters about the whole of Energiø Bornholm, he says.

It says in the government basis that one must analyze whether the need for that ministry is there. Now the ministerial pots with the proposal have simmered for a space of time, and both Christian Friis Bach and Carsten Bach agree that it is a good idea to get started.


New and unknown aspects

The Left's defense mayor, Peter Juel-Jensen, is pleased with the defense minister's response. But as he also says, Troels Lund Poulsen couldn't go further than he did.

- He can't answer anything else when his own intelligence service says there's no military threat. But I think he answers between the lines; That he is very aware that it is a piece of critical infrastructure that we need to take care of, and I actually think it's a good answer, says Peter Juel-Jensen.

At the same time, he also believes that the Citizens' Association Energiø Bornholm focused on some important areas.

- I think this deputation was pointed out some aspects that we had not heard before. There is no doubt that a municipal council that decides that the wind turbines can be moved to 15 kilometers from land opposite the 20 who were originally decided have also not relied on the security issue throughout the energy supply. Therefore, this deputation was very welcome, and I read and understand the minister's response as this is something that one will follow continuously.

The next step in the plan to realize Energiø Bornholm is to implement the supply of the two main elements of the project. The Danish Energy Agency manages the supply of the Mill Park itself. Energinet is responsible for the supply of the land plant and the accompanying cables to send the result of the wind's dance with the mill blades. It should be in place during the year so that it can be dug, weld, hammer and saw from 2025.

Title: Drømmen der blev til et mareridt
Content:
DF Bornholm has always had a certain amount of skepticism about the energy island, writes René Danielsson.

N

U has the worst hill choir laid on top of my party's decision to remove the support for the energy island.

Therefore, the time is perhaps mature for one to try to get a word that hopefully can make people think rationally rather than just come up with the standardized (and almost) religious outbreaks when some question the climate policy.

Some skepticism.

Let me emphasize that in DF-Bornholm we have always had a certain amount of skepticism locally, and that we have continuously had a really sensible dialogue with DF-Christiansborg before their announcement. But it is clear that the recent long -term realities i.f.t. Energy Island's economy, the (lack of) technical possibilities, and a completely unsustainable time perspective means that we do not believe that the municipal council must make additional service deterioration to finance something that may at best only be realized in 9-15 years (if all goes well ).

If you look at the financial aspect of the project, it is so relatively simple.

The more expensive the energy island becomes, the fewer funds we can invest in other things purely socially.

And we want to prioritize health care, elderly care and psychiatry more than we want to allow taxpayers to finance up to 58 billion. DKK (at low electricity price).

New trends.

Then there is the offer problem. So far, it has proved incredibly difficult to find some that find the project profitable. This can be compared to newer reports from Germany, where the great bourgeois party CDU/CSU will reopen their nuclear reactors. If this happens, the business case for Energiø Bornholm is almost non-existent, and since the EU has also recognized nuclear power as a renewable energy, demand and political pressure will mean that it can simply pay for the Germans to become one of the leaders in A-power in Europe. Of course, it is theses and speculation, but nonetheless it is not thought that we in the Danish People's Party stand alone with.

The dream for many of my colleagues in KB is that the following businesses will be able to create a financial boost for Bornholm. Only a guess has been made, made by the local wise people from CRT, who have collected some data, a large part of which is extremely uncertain as it depends on oral handed theses and interviews. Here we talk about an extra tax income when everything is built (and everything goes well) of around 25 million. DKK annually to the municipal treasury (both lasting and temporary effects) in 2029 (and it should probably be pushed 3-4 years to the right) and a population growth of just over 1000 inhabitants. These calculations do not take into account is an increased competition due to wage pressure, and then there are the real circumstances, such as the large model, the PTX project Høst, which is now scaling down significantly and the operation is postponed. This means that the positive effects and prerequisites in that analysis are at best exaggerated - at worst they are directly wrong. So whether the energy island succeeded in its fullest, it does not resolve the economic reality of a society like the Bornholm. On the contrary, the hunt for the energy island can strengthen the negative social spiral and increase the spending pressure in the welfare areas as the efforts are removed or deteriorated when the parties are to chase financing for the interest that the municipality has in the energy island.

Add to that the existing profession suffers from the process. Long case processing times and prioritization of those we live today inhibit the growth of our communities.

If you put it above that the municipal council does not have the finances to lift the Bornholmers socio -economically (which is what will help the economy the most), then the dream of the energy island becomes a socio -economic nightmare, which everything else will knock the bottom out of the box for the next several years.

Like green transition, but we prioritize the Bornholmers. BRK cannot afford both. That is why we prioritize the Bornholmers - and we do so clearly.

It is the only socially responsible. We want to green transition, but it must be done wisely and socially responsible. Other we are not asking for.

Title: Juel-Jensen: Forkert at opgive tanken om en fast forbindelse til Sverige
Content:
A tunnel between Sweden and Bornholm could be a good idea, says one of the island's elected officials. But the idea has to sprout in Bornholm mud, emphasizes Peter Juel-Jensen from the Left.

D.

A Folketing voted on the Øresund Bridge and the Great Belt Bridge, there were parties that voted against. "It's never going to happen," you said. The Great Belt Bridge opened in 1998 and the Øresund Bridge followed in 2000, two years after. Today, no one is talking about closing the two bridges, on the contrary, traffic grows year by year.

At Bornholm, many are also against a tunnel, at least among the municipal politicians who have the power. And the wish must come from a unified Bornholm.

This is stated by Peter Juel-Jensen, who is chosen to represent the Bornholmers on Tinge for the Left. As the party's transport mayor, he is eventually difficult to find reasons why a tunnel to Sweden should be a bad idea.

But if the Bornholmers say it is a bad idea, then it is not something he will work for in Christiansborg.

- It must be a Bornholm wish if it is to have time on earth. The municipal council must say to Christiansborg: Dear Friends, this we would like to investigate. The question of a tunnel is complex. It is about proportionality, visions and financing. A drilled tunnel for Sweden will cost 60 billion. This is the opinion of the engineering company Cowi in an estimate of Bornholm's Journal.

But where should that money come from? Who should love so much of Udkantsdanmark's outermost outpost that one would put energy into running such a project on the domestic policy priority list? 40,000 inhabitants do not weigh heavily in the Danish politicians' voting bags.

It is confirmed by the story. When the tunnel case was turned up in 2013, then the then Minister of Transport Hans Christian Schmidt also kicked the ball back to the Baltic Sea: The wish must come from the Bornholmers. Otherwise, we will not move on.

However, a brief look back in the Bornholm traffic history shows that the fear of the future can be a brake on the development.

Anne Margrethe Roesen, former chairman of the Tunnel Association, remembers that Winni Grosbøll (mayor of Bornholm 2010-2020, ed.) Was a fierce opponent of a tunnel to Sweden, possibly because she was guided by her predecessor at the mayor's post. The fear was groundless according to Anne Margrethe Roesen, Thomas Thor's tunnel opponent was because he did not think it would benefit the port of Rønne if the number of calls fell.

That fear has proven to be groundless, says Anne Margrethe Roesen.

- Today the harbor is somewhere else. The port no longer needs the Bornholm line to pay money. They need it for wind turbines, offshore projects and green energy. Things are developing all the time, she says.

Peter Juel-Jensen, like the Tunnel Association, believes that at least the case should be investigated. He has been in the Folketing for the Left since 2007. He has been elected to one of the two mandates on Bornholm and as a transport mayor has a close knowledge of the historical conditions, including the sailing of Bornholm and the many agreements and routes that have secured over time The connection between first Rønne and Copenhagen - the famous night ferry - and later the fast ferries, which started sailing in 2000, the same year that the bridge over the Sound opened.

In 2013, it was estimated that a feasibility study would cost between 10 and 25 million because it includes physical studies in the form of seismic measurements and geotechnical bores.

In May, COWI revised the old figures for the Journal, and the head of the tunnel department, Christian Boye, today recommends that you start the process with a strategic analysis.

According to Boye, it will cost between two and four million.

A matter of economy Peter Juel-Jensen is surprised that the price of tunnel today is estimated to be around 60 billion.

- It's a lot of money. But the state spends a small half billion a year securing the sailing of Bornholm. If you put them into a tunnel consortium a la Sund & Belt, then there may be some dynamic effects that make you have some more money to advise. I don't know what the math looks like. But there will also be revenue from the tunnel when it is done, he says, emphasizing that it is a high thinking - not a thoroughly analyzed math.

In addition, he says, in theory, there could be a lot of spin off effects at a tunnel.

- Now we talk Energiø, and we have those cables for Sweden which are occasionally torn over. We know that the cable needs to be renewed at some point, can you do it at the same time as the tunnel? Will it provide greater security and a better economy, asks Peter Juel Jensen, who was appointed in April as new defense spokesman in the Left.

The elected Bornholmer is optimistic in terms of getting the Swedes into the idea, although they will be paid well.

- I think the Swedes will say to Denmark: It sounds like a good idea. But as a payment for that, you must expand the road between the tunnel and Malmö. A black connection The climate question may in fact constitute the most tuning tunnel argument of them all. Quick ferries on diesel may be fun for a caricature, but creates deep brow wrinkles of the officials sitting and counting on how to achieve the climate goals. The climate emissions of the fast ferries and freight ferry are not included in the Bornholm CO2 rainfall, but if it did, it would look really bad for Bornholm.

Bornholm's ferry service emits 93,000 tonnes of CO2 annually. The 93,000 tonnes make up almost half of the entire island's other CO2 emissions of 217,000 tonnes. A ferry trip to Bornholm today emits about twice as much CO2 as a trip with the wing, and it is the fast ferry between Ystad to Rønne that pulls down the climate accounts.

Seen in that light, according to Peter Juel-Jensen, a tunnel will draw a different green picture.

Especially because the number of electric cars is progressing rapidly in these years. And you like that in Christiansborg.

- Half a billion in direct payment to something that is very CO2 emissions, it doesn't look good. Denmark has some pretty ambitious requirements for CO2 emissions, and it's hard to do anything about it, with the technology we know today. The mole line has become greener, but not green enough, says the leftist.

Finally, Peter Juel-Jensen is concerned about the population of the food island. It has been steadily declining since the 1950s, but has stagnated about 39,000-40,000 inhabitants in recent years.

- We cannot, with 39,000 inhabitants, have all the skills on Bornholm that we are deeply dependent on. Here I am especially thinking about our hospital and our healthcare system, but also all the other skills that we depend on in the Bornholm community. Environmental approvals, qualified labor.

We need to find some solutions so that we can continue to live with all the benefits that exist in the rest of the kingdom, despite the fact that we are on an island far out in the Baltic Sea. We need to be at the forefront, says Peter Juel-Jensen.

He thinks it will be wrong to give up the idea of ​​a permanent connection to Sweden. - And it may well be that a tunnel connection for nine out of ten occurs as a fantasy project, but it is fine to test it once in a while. Both to move on, but also to show that we are still alive and that there is a willingness to survive out here in the Baltic Sea.

Title: Fond sender millioner til lokale virksomheder
Content:
Bornholm Business Fund received fewer applications than usual in 2023. In total, the fund commited to DKK 9.5 million.

Since 1972, the Bornholm Business Fund has shot money in a wide range of projects that local companies are matering with. Last year, 11 projects received co -financing for a total of DKK 9.5 million. Especially companies in tourism and the food industry have received money.

In both industries there are four companies that have received money from the Business Fund.

The tourism companies have received a total of DKK 4.8 million, while the food companies have received DKK 3.4 million.

- We see ourselves as an important partner for the Bornholm companies and entrepreneurs when they have plans for expansions, ownership and generational change or by establishing a new company, says chairman Charlotte Rønhof in the Bornholm Business Fund in a press release.

According to her, 2023 was one year characterized by rising interest rates and events in the big world, and this was also noticed in the fund, which has received fewer loan applications than usual.

- It understandably causes more companies to await the situation and postpone investments, she says.


Support for Green Conversion

Therefore, it is important for the Business Fund that local businesses and their advisers know the fund's loan terms. One of the latest initiatives is that the fund also wants to lend to the green transition, such as investments in renewable energy, resource and energy saving measures and various activities to support the development in relation to the establishment of Energiø Bornholm.

- I hope that in the future we see an increase in the applications so that we can continue to help the Bornholm companies develop their business, says Charlotte Rønhof.

Title: Campus Bornholm ansætter ny direktør
Content:
The new director at Campus Bornholm was born and raised in Rønne and comes from a position as CEO of VUC Storstrøm.

The 15th. August starts the new director at Campus Bornholm.

The election has fallen on 51-year-old Martin Lasse Hansen Sieben, who comes from a position as CEO of VUC Storstrøm and has extensive experience both as a teacher, manager and director.

This is stated in a press release from Campus Bornholm.

It also states that the new director brings extensive experience and valuable insights in the education sector, and that he is ready to lead Campus Bornholm into a new and exciting future.

The appointment of the new director was unanimously approved by the school board on Thursday, and Chairman Charlotte Rønhof expresses his personal enthusiasm for having found the right candidate for the position of Campus Bornholm's new director:

- I am really pleased that today we can present Martin as our new director of Campus Bornholm. Martin has a heartfelt interest in Bornholm and is passionate about the strengthening of local anchors, where his strong strategic skills and solid background in top management in the education sector make him the perfect match for our organization. - We look forward to working with Martin and take advantage of his insight and leadership as we continue the work to strengthen the school and contribute to Bornholm's sustainable development, she says in the press release.

Child of Bornholm Martin Lasse Hansen Sieben himself comes from Bornholm, and he is very much looking forward to returning home and opening a new chapter of life for the whole family, which besides himself counts his wife Mette and six children together, of whom the two youngest of 13 and respectively. 14 years will move to Bornholm.

- It will be really good to return home and continue the fantastic work that has been done to ensure good educational opportunities at Bornholm and strengthen the cooperation relations throughout Denmark and beyond the borders of the country, he says.

He believes that there are many development potentials in, among other things, Energiø projects and the tourism area. In his opinion, this can contribute to the positive development of the school's educational programs for students, students and students. - I look forward to meeting the school and pulling on the work clothes for August, where I will endeavor to use all my experience and knowledge to strengthen the community and inspire the work to create the best educational opportunities at Bornholm.

Title: Åbent brev til Energinet og Trefor El Øst
Content:
Helle Munk Ravnborg sends an open letter with questions.

Dear Thomas Egebo, CEO, Energinet, and Per Sørensen, Electricity Supply Director, Trefor El Net East. Preparations for Energiø Bornholm are in full swing - including the investigations of whether and how it will be possible to connect the Bornholm electricity grid at the land plant to be established in connection with Energiø Bornholm, thus ensuring that Bornholm has access to part of The current that will be produced from the planned offshore wind farms south of Bornholm. Necessary investments

Although the final solution has not yet been presented, I seem to be able to understand the statements of Energinet that it will be technically possible. After all, it's gratifying.

Without in any way I have to invoke the technical insight into the technical solutions needed to enable the connection of the Bornholm electricity grid with the land plant, I imagine the connection will require investment - both on Energinets and on it Bornholm side of the land facility.

Today, the Bornholm electricity network is arranged in order to be able to receive and ship large quantities of power via the attachment to the search cable at Hasle. In order to enable connection to Energiø Bornholm, I suspect that the Bornholm electricity network will have to be prepared so that (also) can be received and shipped large quantities of electricity via Energiø Bornholm's land plant at Sose.

While I imagine that Energinet, and thus all the power consumers in Denmark, will have to raise the investments to be made within the land of the land plant to connect the Bornholm electricity grid to the land plant, I imagine the connection will also necessitate investments outside , i.e. On the "Bornholm" side of the fence.

These investments, I expect, will be up to the owner of the network, TREFOR EL-NET EAST, and thus the Bornholm power consumers.

Bornholm interests We have in various reports could read a little about the magnitude of the investments that Energinet must lift in order to connect the Bornholm electricity grid, but as far as I am informed, we have not yet heard any estimates on the order of the investments that will had to be lifted by TREFOR EL-NET East and thus by the Bornholm electricity consumers.

This - I think - is a question that will have many - if not most people - Bornholm Electricity consumers' interest - therefore this open letter, which is also shared with Bornholm's Tidende.

Thus, when I turn to you, it is to hear if the above -out understanding of the principles of distribution of investment responsibilities is correct and whether you have the opportunity to give an insight into the order of the investments that must be expected to be with TREFOR Electricity-net east, to enable a connection of the Bornholm electricity grid to the land plant as well as the expected depreciation period.

I look forward to hearing from you.

Title: Vi må ikke debattere
Content:
They want to make their opinion known, but no one will give a stage space to the Citizens' Association Energiø Bornholm.

No one will listen to us. This is how it is the Citizens' Association Energiø Bornholm. They are arge opponents of the energy island and have dreamed of getting talk time at the National Assembly to present their message. But they haven't been lucky with that.

- I have written to those who organize the debate on the climate and energy stage to hear if we could join a debate, but they never answered, says the association's chairman, Henrik Espersen.

The association has 112 members and a large part has stepped up at the National Assembly to get visibility and participate in debates. Without luck.

- We are 10 who walk around with signs and tell everyone about the problems with the energy island, says Lise Dandanell, a board member of the Citizens' Association Energiø Bornholm. They find that many people want to talk to them, but a microphone and a stage floor have not been able to get the cuts in.

Away from the camera in an attempt to get more visibility, Henrik Espersen took a sign up to a debate. It didn't go.

- A producer from TV2 Bornholm would take it out of my hand and said I didn't have to be there, he says. And it's good enough. This confirms the director of TV2 Bornholm, Jan Jørgensen.

- That's right. This is how TV2 and Denmark's Radio agree that one cannot demonstrate yourself on a live signal, he says. Henrik Espersen asked those responsible for the debate if he had to join.

Here was the answer no.

They are frustrated, the members of the association.

Frustrated at not being able to speak as a Bornholm Association for a Bornholm People's Meeting.

- There are plenty of people who lose a lot of money in their personal finances when their house cannot be sold because the energy island has to be there, says Fridrik Adamsson, who is also a member of the board.

But the rejections have not caused the members of the association to give up. They march on with their signs.

Title: En madkunstner, 6 kokkeelever og et ønske om at skabe forbindelse mellem Bornholm og verden derovre
Content:
The first thought that falls in when you say Energiø Bornholm is often wind turbines.

Therefore, the wing tip was in our exhibition at Rønne Gl. Power plants also part of the table covering when on May 6 we gathered 180 guests from 12 countries for our annual Summit. Here, the food artist Tine Galatius together with 6 chef students arranged green energy at the wing tip. While Tine Galatius comes from from from, they study 6 chef students on Campus Bornholm. The chef students were from the first cut of the vegetables that were transformed into giant flowers, asparagus garden, stone fence and a soil -filled vegetable garden - all edible, a great experience for the guests and a unique professional inspiration for the chef students.


Energy Island comes to us from from from but we make it local

The story above illustrates to me one of the most important values ​​in the task that we face with Energiø Bornholm.

The energy island changes Bornholm's position from being an outer area to being a European center of green energy. With the new position comes the attention of the outside world. Attention, which can be expressed as a large land facility, wind turbines out on the sea, publicity in national and international media, cooperation with Gotland, Åland and Saaremaa and visits from all over the world can seem overwhelming. At times, you can almost get the feeling that what is happening more concerns the rest of the world than Bornholm. However, we should not be overwhelmed. We need to receive attention and turn it to be the basis for local development, because the great attention comes with opportunities for local Bornholm development, as was the case with the 6 chef students, and as is the case with investments that can create jobs, Nature, environment and better framework for the local supply.

More jobs, more Bornholmers and a mini-university My focus is that the large investments must give a broad local effect. More inhabitants, greater workforce, investments in housing, the development of the local supply system, growth in local businesses and the attraction of new businesses are examples of possible effects - and illustrate the potential breadth of the value creation that we at Bornholm can enjoy.

The Center for Regional and Tourism Research in Hasle documented in a number of analyzes in 2023 that the lasting employment effect can be between 390 and 900 full -time full -time full -time, while population growth in 2030 may be between 460 and 1,059 people. The range from at least to the largest is defined by how large parts of the economic activities related to the energy island that we are able to attract. At least scenario, Bornholm alone is a service port for the offshore wind turbines, while the effect will be greater if we also manage to attract the installation of the offshore wind turbines and the production of PTX.

Title: Tusindvis af lastbiler til energiøen presser Køge-ruten
Content:
Energinet estimates that more than 10,000 trucks will take the trip from Køge to Rønne in connection with the establishment of the energy island's land facility.

The Cpacity of the route between Rønne and Køge is a source of still concern in the Bornholm business community, and this is a case that the Traffic Contact Council is closely following. The council is regularly informed of how it goes on the route, where there has been no room for all shipping at times. Currently, however, there has been a minor decline in the amount of goods, but this is changing the planned Energiø Bornholm.

How large the need for transport is when the construction of the land plant is underway is difficult to guess. Therefore, the Traffic Contact Council Secretariat has been in dialogue with Energinet about the expected transport needs. The message from Energinet is that during the establishment phase different types of material and materials of varying size must be shipped to Bornholm, and preliminary estimates show an expected load on ferry transport from Køge during that period. Based on experience from previous projects, the energy of the Energin is expected that by 2026-2030, when the need for transport is greatest, more than 10,000 trucks must be transported to Bornholm, according to the Traffic Contact Council's agenda.

Title: Havvind i sejlene for Bornholm
Content:
A small and well -deserved victory for local commitment and green energy.

It is nothing short of impressive to observe how Bornholm's offshore wind continues their struggle to realize the vision of a citizen -driven offshore wind project off the coast of Bornholm. In the midst of a time when the government's big investment on Energiø Bornholm is filling up a lot in the energy debate, and the economy challenges the project, Bornholm's offshore wind is fighting for local commitment and sustainability.

Bornholm's offshore wind represents a project that not only adds local value to local value through even greater financial support to the municipality, but also shows the way for how local energy projects can involve and benefit the local community directly. The recent decision by the Energy Complaints Board, which gives new hope for a positive re -processing of their application, is a shoulder blow to the team work and the endurance on which the project is built.

While the government continues its focus on the large state -driven projects, Bornholm's offshore winds show that there should also be room for and need for smaller, locally anchored initiatives that can supply both green energy and local anchoring. It seems paradoxical that while the Energiø project is struggling with financial and visionary challenges, a profit-making and municipal support initiative as Bornholm's offshore wind resistance.

This raises a significant question of balance and recognition of various energy solutions in Denmark. Are we really willing to put all our resources on individual, big projects and ignore the potential local successes? Bornholm's offshore wind deserves to be heard and supported in their efforts to contribute to the transition to renewable energy, which is so crucial to our common future.

This case should be an eye opener for politicians and decision makers about the need to reassess how we best support and utilize all types of energy projects - large and small. There is a need for a broader recognition that small, local initiatives such as Bornholm's offshore wind can play an important role in the energy sector.

We must not overlook the value of local commitment and the opportunities it brings. Bornholm's offshore wind demonstrates that citizen -driven projects are not only a dream, but a realizable reality that can complement the larger energy projects and ensure a more diversified and robust energy supply.

Take note of the positive development and make sure that Bornholm's offshore wind gets the support and recognition they deserve.

The more we are who backs up, the more attentive our voting politicians become. It is time to embrace both the big visions and the small, effective solutions that together can ensure a greener and more sustainable future for Bornholm and the rest of Denmark.

Title: Energinet svarer på Helle Ravnsborgs indlæg fra 11. juni
Content:
It is primarily about Bornholm's connection to the energy island.


COMMENT

Energinet has received a letter from the municipal councilor in Bornholm Regional Municipality Helle Munk Ravnborg on June 7, 2024. She asks how the investments that make it possible to connect the Bornholm electricity network to Energiø Bornholm's El infrastructure is distributed between Energinet and Trefor.

The letter has also been brought in Bornholm's Journal on June 11. We have answered Ravnborg in writing and held a meeting with her, where Trefor also participated.

Here we also answer in the newspaper.


Now and future

Today, Bornholm is primarily supplied with electricity via a cable from Sweden.

That cable must either be renewed within a number of years - or the local electricity grid can be connected to Energiø Bornholm's Elinfrastructure. The link between a local electricity grid and an energy island has not been done before, but since it has been a local political desire to be able to, then Energinet has investigated the opportunity.

Our preliminary analyzes show that it is technically possible and that it is a socio -economically good idea. In addition to a lot of green current, our analyzes also show that the Bornholmers get a better security of supply and relatively stable electricity prices if the local electricity grid is connected to the energy island.

Question: Is the outlined understanding of the principles of distribution of investment responsibility correctly understood? Energinet owns and operates transmission systems (such as Energiø Bornholm's stations and cables) and plants of 132 kV and above.

As mentioned above, it is possible to connect Bornholm's electricity grid on the energy island without compromising on the stability and security of the web. Technically, it is difficult to connect such a small consumption area to a large production unit as Energiø Bornholm.

We are therefore in the process of developing the technical solution to ensure that we do not overload components and continue to have power in the outlet.

Question: Can Energinet provide insight into the size of the investments that are to be expected to meet TREFOR EL-NET East to enable the connection of the Bornholm electricity grid to the land plant?

Energinet is preparing a decision basis for the connection. The basis for decision must elucidate all aspects, such as the different technical solutions, security of supply and economy. TREFOR ELNET-ESTIns contribute estimates on the cost of the connection on their side, and the estimates come together with Energinet's figures to be included in the socio-economic calculations for the project. The Minister of Climate, Energy and Supply must ultimately approve Energinet's decision-making basis for the connection. However, this decision can only be made when the settlement circle in the Folketing behind Energiø Bornholm has taken a renewed position on the big project.

The ministry expects this to happen around the turn of the year.


Socio -economic considerations

As a state -owned company, Energinet is subject to a number of requirements when we set new projects - which the connection is - in progress.

Among other things, we must point out the solution that is socially economically best. That is, a connection with the same functionality cannot be made cheaper than the solution we set. Since the connection can cause TREFOR EL-NET East to reinforce the local electricity grid, we work together to look at different solutions.

Question: Can Energinet provide an insight into the expected depreciation period? Energinet's connection for the connection is expected to be written off over 40 years.

Energinet will continuously inform TREFOR and Bornholm Regional Municipality about the work on the link of the Bornholm electricity grid to the energy island.

Title: Udligning af selskabsskat forringer kommunens økonomi
Content:
It is good when investing in Bornholm.

It creates jobs, meets the need for food, housing, experiences, energy and much more. At best, it can even contribute to a more sustainable society.

But it doesn't matter who invests. Or rather, it does not matter who the company that invests on Bornholm is jointly taxed and where this tax parent has its home.

Every time an investment in a company that creates its value on Bornholm is done through a company that is based and thus taxed outside Bornholm, Bornholm loses compared to a situation where the same investment was made through a company that also has a tax office on Bornholm.

WHY? This is due to the way the municipal equalization system works in relation to the municipalities' share of the corporate tax.

Overall, almost 15% of the corporate tax rate accrues to the municipalities, while the rest accrue to the state. However, the municipalities' total income from the corporate tax is offset against the total block grant.

An example If we imagine a slightly simplified example with three equal municipalities measured in population numbers, which have a total corporate tax revenue of DKK 60 million, then the total block grant for the three municipalities will be equivalent to DKK 60 million less compared to a situation without a municipal situation corporate tax revenue. If the corporate tax payment is equal in the three municipalities, then it will go straight up. If, on the other hand, there is a difference in corporate tax revenue between the municipalities, then a new compensation rule comes into force - namely, that the differences in municipal income from corporate tax per year. inhabitants are offset by 50%.

If, in the example of the three equal municipalities, we assume that corporate tax revenue is distributed so that one municipality has an income of DKK 20 million, while the other two municipalities have a corporate tax income respectively. DKK 10 and 30 million, this means that while they are all deducted DKK 20 million block grants, the municipality with the highest corporate tax revenue must hand over DKK 5 million to the equalization scheme to the municipality with the lowest corporate tax revenue.

Overall, this means that the municipality with the lowest corporate tax revenue will lose five million kroner, while the municipality with the highest corporate tax revenue wins five million kroner.

The real world - Bornholm has minus 34.8 million in the real world and calculated by the online media NB economy PBA. Figures from the Ministry of the Interior, however, the situation is that 20 of the 98 Danish municipalities in 2025 will win on the corporate tax equalization, while the remaining 78 municipalities, including Bornholm, will lose the scheme. Among the municipalities that win on the scheme is Gladsaxe, which houses, among other things. Novo Nordisk, Billund, who houses Lego, and Fredericia, which houses Ørsted. For Bornholm, the equalization scheme means a loss of DKK 34.8 million, compared to a situation without set -off and equalization of corporate tax.

Each time a Bornholm company - be it a production or agricultural business, a slaughterhouse, a hotel, a restaurant, a store or the like - is established or taken over by a company with a tax office in eg Gladsaxe, Randers, Fredericia, Copenhagen, Skanderborg, Gentofte or Rudersdal - and well noticeable, if that company pays tax - then it means Bornholm's economy is shrinking.

There simply will be less money to secure good roads and public transport that can bring employees and customers to the companies, when companies want to build new, for employment services, when companies need more employees, for business promotion, care and care and Schooling for children while parents are at work, etc.

What is business policy really? It is for me to look worth this to keep this in mind when we are pursuing business policy on Bornholm, especially in the current situation with the prospect of large investments as part of the plans for Energiø Bornholm.

For the more successful investments that they succeed in attracting to Bornholm, the more the Bornholm municipal economy will lose if these investments are taxed outside Bornholm. The fact that this is the case is due to the bottom-out-of-the-state municipal equalization system. But as long as this equalization system applies with the current rules for equalizing corporate tax, as long as it should be obvious that Bornholm's business policy should have a sharp focus on promoting Bornholm companies, which also have their homes on Bornholm in a tax office.

Title: Energiøen åbner nye muligheder for Bornholms turisme
Content:
Researcher at CRT in Hasle believes it is worth investigating how the energy island can become a plus for local tourism.

With the green transition, many questions follow and Energiø Bornholm is no exception. It is still unknown who will be tasked with building the offshore wind park to deliver the power, and there is also a lack of answers as to whether neighbors to the land facility in Sose can get some form of compensation.

In some circles, you even ask if the energy island is a good idea or whether the state should drop it. But there is also another question that is largely not talked about, and this has wondered tourism scientist Andreas Skriver Hansen at the Center for Regional and Tourism Research in Hasle.

- Until now, I do not think there is much talk about what it means for tourism or can mean for tourism, both positively and negative, he says to the Journal.

For many years, there has been a tendency for wind turbines and energy systems to be considered something negative for the tourist industry. It is also what fills the most in the professional literature written about the meeting between energy and tourism.

But that narrative does not actually vote, and the negative effect is far from as great as hitherto assumed. In addition, the green transition and the energy island can actually become a lever for the tourist industry if the parties have a good dialogue about both opportunities and challenges in advance. And that can make Bornholm a pioneering destination, says Andreas Skriver Hansen. - When it comes to the dialogue between tourism and energy, there has been a tendency to always drive into the negative impressions and people's protests in connection with new and large energy plants. You still have to be critical and relate to this challenge, but there is just a similar nuance on the other side. Now let's say that we get a new energy development, what is the more effect of this, and how can tourism also exploit it? It is there p.t. Not really insight into. Neither in the Bornholm context nor in the research literature, which surprises me, says Andreas Skriver Hansen.

Focus on business tourism His wonder has resulted in a recently published research note, which briefly sounds like more in -depth research attention is needed and more practical knowledge of how it is possible to bridge tourism and large green energy projects In coastal environments where tourism is a main industry and crucial contributor to the economy. - The research note is a way to draw attention to a topic that you would like to help develop. Something you think is problematic or interesting that should be examined more. That's what I put up with the publication and theme, says Andreas Skriver Hansen.

Increased business tourism is already focusing on today, but he himself also sees additional opportunities that can jump out of a greater collaboration between tourism and energy development.

- You have talked a little about the fact that you want to open the land plant. Could it be a new experience for tourists who can come down and get the story of energy history and the green development in Denmark? There is also the possibility that, for example, former fishermen can get a new bijob to sail people out to the mills and tell the story of the energy, while also reporting about the development of the Baltic Sea, Fishing, Culture, the Marine Environment and the Coast. If this is at the same time linked to some food from the local gastronomic scene on the boat, or when you come ashore, then you can create a complete experience and fusion of the Bornholm history and development, he says.

If there is an industrial park with Power-to-X, where the power is transformed into green fuel, a lot of surplus heat can come that can create new types of products and foods that can be transformed into new gastronomic experiences and thus increase food tourism on the island. That in itself can attract new tourist players, such as producers, chefs and restaurants. - It may also be that you can make some heated beaches. It has been out to investigate, for example with some visits to Iceland, I know. I don't know how realistic it is, but the point is that there can be more besides just a plant out on the sea and a plant in Sose, says Andreas Skriver Hansen.

100 percent green destination on the part of the authorities is working for the Bornholm electricity grid to be connected to the energy island's power connections, and if this happens, it can lead to the entire local tourism sector being driven by green energy - not least when ferries and aircraft switch to Green fuels.

- There is a clear opportunity for marketing and reinforcing our image as a 100 percent green destination if you have documentation of it all. It is something that is noticed and as a seller and which can be used campaign -wise to market Bornholm, says the researcher from CRT.

The meeting between tourism and energy was something that Andreas Skriver Hansen became aware of in connection with the development project National Center for Green Energy, which took place 2022-2023, and which involved many local players, including Baltic Energy Island, the municipality, Rønne Harbor, Campus Bornholm. In this connection he spoke, among other things, with people in Destination Bornholm, where one is aware that there may be opportunities associated with the energy island. In fact, it is part of the development plan for tourism on Bornholm until 2030, where it is mentioned as a possible fourth position of strength for Bornholm in line with local quality food, crafts and outdoor tourism.

- I know you want to try to get the energy dialog started in some way.

You certainly work with the energy island of business tourism, but if only business tourism is the focus, the other opportunities and their potentials will not be examined. The focus should therefore be expanded so that we really open up the full spectrum of opportunities that can be available. From my initial dialogue with Destination Bornholm, I have been confirmed that the destination supports the search of other options, he says.

Testø for the whole world as a researcher, Andreas Skriver, Hansen, sees many interesting perspectives, both for Bornholm and the rest of the world, and he wants to help illuminate them. He believes that Bornholm in this area can also become a test island.

- We can become Testø for how you can succeed in creating coexistence and synergy between tourism and energy and having them meet in a better way. Nobody has worked systematically and detailed yet, neither in research nor at the local level. It could be a really interesting task and challenge to help solve and then make Bornholm available as a model area, he says.

This is relevant as there are many other places around the world that are facing having to plan for the meeting between tourism and energy.

In the immediate vicinity, Bornholm has a partnership with Gotland, Åland and Saaremaa to be energy islands, and they are also tourist islands, and it will be logical to see the things in context.

- The subject is not something they have worked with yet on any of the other three islands, but they will need the knowledge we can build on Bornholm. So the faster we get the right people to talk together and describe these things, the better we are in terms of taking a pioneering position as an island that can solve this Gordian knot with planning for coexistence and synergic creation. No one has solved it yet, so why do we not use the opportunity we have right now to lift it as an example that can be used in the partnership, nationally, European and actually globally as well. That's the potential as I see it, says Andreas Skriver Hansen. If you want to read Andreas writes Hansen's English -language research note, you can find it on the internet via the address kortlink.dk/2qm9m.

Title: Nej, det er en dårlig idé!
Content:
Mayor Jacob Consolation (C) has this contribution about Bornholm's economy up to the budget negotiations and the municipal elections in 2025 in our series on the mayoral candidates.

It is an expression that we as politicians often encounter when the talk goes around savings.

It is now no secret that Bornholm Regional Municipality's economy is in trouble. The reasons are many; Everything from several elderly people (one third of us are 65+), more placement of children, increasing demands and thus the cost of operating a municipality, and of course the equalization between the municipalities in Denmark, and where Bornholm is not sufficiently compensated for our composition of citizens.

I will go a little more in depth with some of the things at the information meeting about BRK's economy on Campus on August 14.

No “one but back to no” a…

It is quite natural that we say no to what strikes ourselves, our family or someone we know, in a negative way - and in Bornholm we know each other really well.

But if you want to make our (politicians) task just a little easier, then no "one should be followed by a suggestion of where we should save. It's too easy to just say no without coming up with another suggestion for a Savings - because nobody says fine, grab in just a lot of money or employees with me.


The administration and the politicians

We politicians have asked our administration to come up with their best suggestions on where to save if we end up having to save, for example, DKK 64 million.

That is, it is the people with the greatest knowledge of the municipality who have presented their suggestions on how we can find 64 million, and still care for the things that a municipality must fit according to the law.

Then it is up to us politicians to decide which of the proposals we can best live with. Because there are virtually no some of the suggestions that we think is a great idea - unless it is a so -called investment case where some money is spent here and now to make a workflow more efficient and thus cheaper in the long term .

Fortunately, we have some of them every year, because our administration is of course also interested in the fact that we run the municipality as efficiently as possible.


Particularly difficult to put municipality

The big joker is, of course, how much money we get from the pool for particularly difficult municipalities.

This year we are applying for a development partnership with the Ministry of the Interior, because we can see that our financial situation is not changing in the next few years - probably on the contrary, if we look at the population development with more and more elderly people.

Such a partnership runs for four years, but even though we should succeed, we will still have to seek the pool going forward. It will just give us a security for a basic amount.

Better economy requires jobs If we are to create a better economy on Bornholm, then it requires more people to pay more in taxes.

We can only secure this by creating more jobs and knows that more people move to Bornholm throughout the year. Our tourism industry accounts for about 10 percent of our income on Bornholm, but many employees are here only during the high season and thus do not pay tax on Bornholm. If they have to move to Bornholm (and pay taxes here), then it requires them to get a job all year.

So we need to create more that people want to visit or use at Bornholm all year round (in Ystad they have, among other things, Saltsjöbadet and the film studios as the very big activities).

The other opportunity for jobs at Bornholm is other private companies - including of course our entrepreneurs.

We must ensure that it is attractive to run a business on Bornholm. We can say no to certain types of companies (and of course we have to be critical), but then we also say no to jobs and thus no to pay for our schools and care centers. Things are connected.

Lack of labor at the moment, many of our businesses are struggling with labor shortages.

At the same time, we have a lot of people who retire - either because they have to or because they can. Some of them really want to help contribute to the community and help solve the many of the society's tasks that we lack labor - both in the municipality and in private companies.

We need to do what we can to make anyone who has the opportunity and desire to work - whether it is one or 30 hours a week - can have the opportunity to bring their skills and energy into play to contribute to our Everyone's Society. We need everyone who can and will.

In addition, we also see that several of our education is lacking applicants. Our education is an important part of the food chain to ensure labor and activity on Bornholm. So, of course, it is also important that we do what we can to both maintain the current, but also attract new education for Bornholm.

Here it is a pleasure to see how, for example, DTU shows interest in Bornholm - both because we are working towards an energy island, but also because we have companies that prioritize development, new technology and projects very high.

My wish for Bornholm is that in the future we do not need to seek the pool for particularly difficult municipalities, but that we can stand on our own legs and run a municipality that is the best for children and young people to grow up in, and That Bornholm is still the best place in Denmark to live.

My wish for Bornholm is that in the future we do not need to seek the pool for particularly difficult municipalities. Jacob Consolation, Mayor (C)

Title: Energiøen kommer på særlig liste - åbner for støtte fra EU
Content:
Upon application from the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Supply, Energiø Bornholm has been given a list of cross-border energy projects that the EU can support.

The green transition and the establishment of more wind energy is a task that the EU wants Member States to cooperate with. To promote this cross -border cooperation, the European Commission has launched the financing program CEF Energy - Connecting Europe Facility for Energy, where specially designated energy projects can receive support. Energiø Bornholm has just come on the list that makes it possible to receive financial support from this program.

That's what the European Commission says.

Specifically, Energiø Bornholm has come up with CEF Energy's list of cross -border renewable energy projects that contribute to filling gaps in regional renewable electricity generation, to an open electricity market to increase Europe's energy independence and to reduce the consumption of fossil fuels.

About Energiø Bornholm, the European Commission writes, among other things, that with its two offshore wind farms and two interconnections from the transformer station in SOSE to the rest of Denmark and to Germany, it allows for trade and sharing of excess electricity. Millions in support of the Journal, the Danish Energy Agency tells us that it is the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Supply Ministry that has applied to get Energiø Bornholm on the list.

Energiø Bornholm is one of three new projects that have been on the list, which was launched in 2022, which now includes eight different renewable energy projects. The European Commission says the projects on the list are justified for financial support for studies and work under the CEF Energy program.

It confirms the Danish Energy Agency.

Tidende has also asked what the recording on the list really means for the energy island and the establishment of it. The Danish Energy Agency cannot disclose that, as it is still unclear, the answer reads.

The fact that there may be money to be gained in the CEF Energy program proves distributions to some of the other projects on the list. In the summer of 2023, two projects received a total of 22.2 million euros, and the following year four projects from the list were supported with DKK 67.4 million. In total, this corresponds to DKK 667.5 million, which is given, among other things, for preliminary surveys and initial construction work.

According to the European Commission, it also benefits Energiø Bornholm and the other projects that they get greater visibility by joining the list.


The projects on the European Commission's list

- Elwind - A Hybrid Sea Wind Wind Farm between Estonia and Latvia.

- Görlitz Zgorzelec - A district heating network based on renewable energy between Germany and Poland.

- Cicerone - A project for the production of renewable electricity in Italy, Spain and Germany for conversion, transport and use of green hydrogen in the Netherlands and Germany.

- Slowp - Wind power plant in Riga Bay in Estonian seawater.

- Ulp -Res WP - Wind farm on land in the northern part of Latvia and the southern part of Estonia with a joint connection to the transmission network in Latvia.

- TMNHSA - Initiative between Romania and Bulgaria, aimed at utilizing the Danube River's hydroelectric potential.

- Pontis - aims to push the construction of an integrated, cross -border sustained hydrogen supply chain in Europe.

Title: Ventede 14 år på drømmejobbet: Hun syntes, jeg var uregerlig
Content:
Most Bornholmers are on first name with the unstoppable chief archaeologist at the Bornholm Museum. On August 29, Finn Ole Sonne Nielsen turns 70.

- I am a Stone Age man, says Finn Ole Sonne Nielsen, chief archaeologist at the Bornholm Museum. For people who don't know who Finn Ole is, it might sound confusing. But it's not that Finn Ole is a Stone Age man, just as a grocer is a grocery store. He has worked with the Stone Age for 50 years of his life, and it is an age that has fascinated him since he as a boy read the legends about Skjold and Dan and the other Danish legends in the oldest work on Danish history, Saxo Grammaticus.

- I've known I was going to be an archaeologist since I was ten years old, he says. The 29th.

August he turns 70.

The trilogy There have been 40 years along the way Finn Ole Sonne Nielsen grew up in Klemensker, and was seen early by the local school inspector who took the covetous young student under his wings.

- He sent me the direct path to high school and on to the university, he says, sitting in a plastic chair at Vasagård, the outdoor excavation at Læsåen, which he opened almost 20 years ago. Around him, three volunteers work to dig and solve. Here you have found sunstones, traces of pallisads and a long mound with both the giant and nozzle chamber, and you still find bones and other good cases on the fifth thousand -year -old settlement south of Aakirkeby.

An archaeological Eldorado for a Stone Age man confirms Finn Ole Sonne Nielsen. But it was not specific findings that led the young Finn Ole towards archaeology.

- I think I had a connection with the cosmos and the universe. I have always been interested in the understanding of time and space. The feeling that here has lived genera before one, he says.

Finn Ole Sonne Nielsen himself has gone into a - at least seen with archaeological eyes - the footsteps of the subject. We are talking about Ole Klindt-Jensen, prehistoric archaeologist and professor at Aarhus University, who from 1958 to 1964 excavated the large Iron Age settlements at Slusegård.

Ole Klindt-Jensen came from Næstved but moved as a child with his parents to Bornholm, where he, like Finn Ole, was fascinated by the breadth of archaeology. Ole Klindt-Jensen died in a traffic accident when his career was at his highest.

- He was only 62 and he never managed to do what he dreamed of.

He put Bornholm on the map and worked with students from all over the world.

He was my first great example. I have tried to do some of the things he did not achieve, says Finn Ole Sonne Nielsen, who is currently working on the third and final book in a trilogy that began when he received a three -year fellow over 40 years ago From the Carlsberg Foundation on the recommendation of its then head of the National Museum, Poul Otto Nielsen. The idea was that he should do a doctoral dissertation, but it did not go quite as planned.

- I simply drowned in finds, remembers Finn Ole Sonne Nielsen. But the dissertation was not dropped. It was simply postponed indefinitely or pulled in the long run, and the many years of persistent work have now resulted in two scientific titles at the University of Southern Denmark. One about Vallensgård in 2020 and one about Limensgård in 2022. The third about Vasagård and Rispebjerg, according to Finn Ole Sonne Nielsen, is ready for release in four to five years.

I had to cancel all things take time, and Finn Ole Sonne Nielsen has throughout his career - how playfully it all has looked like from the outside - tackled resistance and personal tragedies that have both affected himself and worked with archaeology. In 2001, his wife, the potter Helle Theilgaard, was involved in a serious traffic accident that demanded care and presence in the years that followed.

- It's been my clearest project.

I had plans that I, like Klindt-Jensen, should be more international and cultivate the connections that are to Bornholm in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania and many other things. I had to cancel everything, says Finn Ole Sonne Nielsen, who together with Helle has two daughters and three grandchildren.

The injuries after the accident were so severe that the doctors predicted that Finn Ole's wife would be brain damaged for the rest of his life. Fortunately, this was not the case, among other things, thanks to Finn Ole's tireless care.

Today he is grateful for the choice he made.

- The girls were 11 and 14 when it happened. They needed a mom and I'm happy with my wife. She is just 70 and still works as a potter. It was difficult back then, but it has also been bad for them to have a father and a man who is nerdy. I usually say that it is a disease that does not exist, says Finn Ole Sonne Nielsen, who formally resigned as chief archaeologist at the Bornholm Museum in the spring of 2023 after 25 years in the post.

His way into the Bornholm Museum, however, did not go the direct way either. Finn Ole Sonne Nielsen says that it was 14 years before he got the dream job as an archaeologist at the Bornholm Museum. - I had to fight. My predecessor was not excited that I came back to Bornholm in 1984, so I was only hired in 1998, says Finn Ole Sonne Nielsen.

However, he subsequently got the most amazing collaboration with Margrethe Watt, who was a pioneer at the Iron Age settlement Black Muld in Svaneke.

- We've talked about it. She thought I was unruly and uncontrollable, laughs Finn Ole Sonne Nielsen, who in time as unruly published four books for the National Museum.

Has worked with everything Finn Ole Sonne Nielsen today has an agreement to work for the museum eight hours a week, and the scheme hopes he can be extended until he has completed the work on the book on Vasagård and Rispebjerg.

And then there is the regular clean -up.

At the moment, Finn Ole Sonne Nielsen, along with a group of dedicated volunteers, is working to shut down the excavations he has helped to start, including Vasagård excavation, which he began in 2007, which has been active continuously since 2012.

In a month there is only a teaching tomb left, but Finn Ole Sonne Nielsen hopes that the archaeological investigations that precede the establishment of Energiø Bornholm will continue.

- What is coming now is great.

They find a lot of settlements related to Vasagård and who tell us that they have used this plant. So we get a lot of new knowledge that we hadn't gained otherwise.

Black mud, where the first big gold-gubs were made back in 1985-87, is the archaeologist's second great love, which he took over after Watt and put in Michael Thorsen's hands. It was reopened in 2019, but finally shut down in 2023.

Finn Ole Sonne Nielsen has in his own words worked with everything in his time as an archaeologist at Bornholm. Among other things, he has spent a lot of effort on the restoration of Hammerhus, which has been ongoing since 2008.

Finn Ole Sonne Nielsen is an honorary doctor at Lund University, recipient of the Erik Westerby Prize and winner of TV2 Bornholm's Cultural Award in 2022.
