Title: Reaktion på BRKs forslag om besparelser på Business Center Bornholm
Content:
BCBs respond to the savings proposal.

We have received information about the proposed budget for 2025, which includes a saving of DKK 897,000 for Business Center Bornholm (BCB).

With this consultation response, we will express our concerns and disagreements with this proposal, which we believe will have long -range and serious consequences for the island's business and thus the general economic development.

Factual errors in the savings proposal It is not correct that BCB has two communication staff employed for the basic business service and projects covered by the action plan with BRK. BCB has half an employee dedicated to communication tasks.

It is not correct that most municipalities closed their business service after the new business promotion in 2019.

According to an overview from the Danish Business Promotion, 68 % of the municipalities have retained a local player, either municipal or private, which performs outreach business services.

One cannot expect, as it can be interpreted, the description of the Releases that the Capital of Business Capital will take on the task of the local business service. It is stated from the Business House Capital that it is not possible to increase the presence of the Business House on Bornholm.

The interpretation of BCB's accounting is incorrect and needs clarification to avoid further misunderstandings. The specified surplus is primarily accumulated due to period shifts and project -specific revenue, which is due to late changes in financial grants in projects.

Business Center Bornholm's role and contribution Our outreach work and communication efforts are crucial to reaching out to companies that would otherwise not use the business promotion system due to lack of resources to seek relevant offers themselves. Cutting down on this effort will not make us more demand driven, as claimed in the savings proposal, but will, on the other hand, limit our contact with businesses and reduce our ability to initiate strategic efforts with the companies at the center. Through our work with startups and existing companies, we support the supply of jobs, which is essential for the island's economy and population growth.

Through guidance and sparring, we strengthen the competitiveness of the Bornholm companies - both nationally and internationally. We play a significant role in ensuring that new companies get a good reception and the right sparring to get started on Bornholm.

Consequences of the suggested savings as mentioned, saving the proposed size will reduce both outreach work and communication as well as the number of value-creating workshops and sparring with companies, which will directly affect companies' development and threaten future jobs.

The ongoing positive development in green transition and participation in strategic efforts, such as Energiø Bornholm, can be slowed down. BCB's participation in tourism projects will also be weakened.

It is under the basic appropriation that BCB greatly contributes to the development and implementation of special business policy initiatives. These efforts strengthen companies' competitiveness and development, among other things in digitalisation and automation as well as green and sustainable change.

It is difficult to see that BCB, with the proposed savings, can continue to contribute optimally to ensure that we, as Ø, maintain the current positive momentum.

With the savings, Bornholm companies will face greater challenges in staying up to date on national offers and opportunities for business promotions, which will limit the initiation of necessary development projects and reduce both competitiveness and the level of innovation.

Savings almost every year.

Since the new business promotion in 2019, DKK 1,820,000 has already been saved at BCB. With the new proposed savings proposal of DKK 897,000, the total savings will reach up to DKK 2.7 million. This significant reduction in funds to support business will have long -term negative consequences for the Bornholm community, including loss of jobs and falling tax revenue.

The Bornholm business community is both developmental and adaptable and expresses great satisfaction with and great need for the local and confidence-creating business service. It is therefore essential that there are funds for the local business service BCB through a sustained effort to contribute to the companies' transition and development, not least in relation to the stricter demands of the future for an already pressed business community.

We strongly urge Bornholm Region Municipality to rethink the proposed savings at Business Center Bornholm. It is a continued investment in business development, which is crucial to the island's future economic health and sustainability.

Edited and abbreviated by the editor.

Approved by BCB

Title: Lad os gribe chancen.
Content:
Ferry connection to Poland provides opportunities.

A ferry connection to Poland, even a car ferry, is not an innovation.

Experience shows us that if it is to be a success, then it is required that we are actively preparing for the new connection from Bornholm from Bornholm - and it is not just about receiving Polish tourists! On August 1, 2024, the Kolobrzeg-Rønne Bornholm Tidende was able to publish the news that the largest Polish ferry operator, Polferries, from May 2025 establishes a new ferry route between Rønne and the Polish ferry town of Kolobrzeg.

Here in September, the shipping company expects a deal in place with a ferry for 500 people and 50 cars - initially with a lease for 20 years. An agreement must also be concluded with Rønne Harbor.

The plan is for the ferry in May, June, September and October to sail three days a week, and every day in July-August.

Arms in the weather There is nothing to say that the arms are raised high at Destination Bornholm, Rønne Handelsstandsforening, Horesta, our relocation service and probably many more at Bornholm.

A car ferry to Poland for half the year offers tremendous opportunities - both in terms of tourists and labor. The Polish summer vacation has August as its main month.

Schools only begin in September and universities only until October.

Ferry connection to Poland is not an innovation.

Already more than 100 years ago there was a permanent connection to Kolobrzeg - at that time a German city named Kolberg.

In the period 2000 and up to the Corona pandemic there has been a ferry connection between Nexø and Kolobrzeg as well as to the Polish coastal towns Darlowo and Ustka for a number of years.

However, it has not been car ferries, but only ferries to passengers and bicycles. Finally, there have also been car ferries from Rønne to Swinoujscie in July-August with weekly departures.

However, the announcement from Polferries goes far beyond the previous ferry connections, and therefore also has a much greater potential for Bornholm.

Tourists both ways With my 25 years of in -depth knowledge of Poland, I am absolutely convinced that it will not be the big problem to draw Polish tourists to Bornholm. Not least our bike path is known all over Poland, thanks to Polish TV, which has often shown long programs with bicycle paradise Bornholm.

Many of my Polish colleagues have had the family and bikes with Bornholm. With more than 200 Polish citizens with permanent residence on Bornholm, we have an impressive network of ambassadors, who have been very crucial to the many Polish tourists who can now become even more.

The capacity and sailing rate for the ferry next year will open up to 60,000 passengers.

But the experience of the previous ferry connections to Poland has been that they have mainly had Polish passengers both ways - and a very large proportion of one -day tourists.

It is not sustainable why we also have to actively help market from Bornholm to market not only the ferry connection, but also Poland as an obvious destination. Me and the family have even until several times vacationed in Poland. It is a fantastic country, both in relation to nature and culture.

At the same time, for a Dane it is very cheap to vacation in Poland - and the linguistic barrier is no longer a significant problem. For the past 30 years, all Polish children have had English on the school schedule from school start.

Labor - great potential The green transition with not least Energi Ø Bornholm contains a huge challenge in being able to obtain the necessary qualified labor.

Here, Poland offers enormous opportunities - partly because there is a high level of education in Poland, partly because they just have a large supply of labor in the technical areas such as engineers, welders and so on that Bornholm needs.

However, the challenge is that Poland itself has great ambitions with offshore wind energy, and is quite far with the first large offshore wind farm not far from Bornholm.

Our job center has previously had good contacts with partners in Poland, and I am quite convinced that they are ready to build contacts and cooperation with their Polish colleagues again.

The broad cooperation in addition to this is that we at Bornholm have more than 30 years of experience in collaboration with Poland - not least northern Poland - in a wide range of areas and with good experience.

Today, the collaboration is especially done within the Euroregion Baltic, which includes, among other things, the Pomerania region in northern Poland, with Gdansk as the main city - a region of almost 3 million inhabitants. Through the EU program South Baltic and the four-corner cooperation we also have good contacts with the northwestern part of Poland, West Pomerania with Szczecin, Kolobrzeg and Swinoujscie as capital cities.

There is a major challenge for Destination Bornholm, Horesta and the other Bornholm tourism players in making Bornholm even more well -known in northern Poland, including stands at tourist fairs in the larger cities.

We have from past good experience with such marketing, including with the participation of tourist attractions such as Naturbornholm and the Medieval Center.

The registration deadline for these tourist fairs is in November, to me.

Next, there is a major challenge for the Business Center Bornholm, Moving Service and other Bornholm Business Promotion Actors in making contacts and cooperation with their like -minded people in Poland - not least in and around Kolobrzeg, a city with almost 50,000 inhabitants and an exuberant business.

Rønne Harbor and Offshore Center Bornholm already have its good contacts, and several other Bornholm companies can find good partners in Poland and expand their markets.

Along with the construction of business cooperation, it will be obvious to make contacts in the cultural field and association level.

Here, too, we have good experiences from the past, and regularly get inquiries about collaboration from Kolobrzeg.

Use the experience and existing contacts in the preparations for the new ferry route, it is important to draw on the experiences that many at Bornholm have with Poland and the Polish market. It is not least important to draw on the Polish citizens we have on Bornholm, their networks and their in -depth knowledge of the country.

A concrete proposal may be recovery of the Task Force Poland, an open and informal network of Bornholm actors in the period 2007-2011, who met three or four times a year to exchange knowledge and experience to inspire each other and discuss joint initiatives.

In addition to the municipality, Destination Bornholm, Business Center Bornholm, CRT, Campus, Naturbornholm, Medieval Center, Nexø Harbor, Bornholm Airport and until several associations and Bornholm companies, such as Bornpol, which has many years of experience in serving trips to and from Poland.

Hereby the ball is given up and the question now is whether anyone grabs it.

I hope so!

If the cable is not established, Germany is currently the only real buyer of electricity from the offshore wind turbines off Bornholm, which is why more people are now saying that direct connections should be established abroad from offshore wind farms established on Danish seabed.

In this perspective, the prerequisites for establishing PTX and other Energitung Industry on Bornholm could suddenly be gone.

"The Great" warns what is coming to happen is unknown, but right now it seems most serious to consider these scenarios in an upcoming planning and development strategy for Bornholm.

At the same time, large Danish players such as CIP and Ørsted have scaled down, postponed or completely dropped the bet at PTX in Denmark in recent months. Nor does this seem to make an impression on the advocates of the power-to-growth strategy as the focal point of drafting the planning and development strategy for Bornholm.


Workplaces

On top of that, it is quite doubtful that the establishment of PTX and a business park for other Energitung Industry could lead to a number of workplaces that will not be able to bring us close to the goal of 42,000 inhabitants on Bornholm.

Yet the vast majority of PTX plants that are maternity in Denmark and the rest of Europe are only established on the drawing board or as a smaller experimental plant. For example, it is the experimental plant that has just been inaugurated in a frame in Jutland at only 10 MW.

Therefore, the figures for the employment effect of the PTX industry are based on calculations made based on experience from similar industries. Against this background, Ramboll has calculated the employment effect from a planned establishment of a 300 MW PTX plant in Lolland. Here, Ramboll expects a total lasting employment effect of 55 man-years over the 20-year operating period, equivalent to 2.75 full-time equivalents per year. year.

If it is imagined that the hydrogen is not only exported directly, but further processed into either methanol or ammonia, the employment effect rises to 160 full -time full -time years of the total period, equivalent to 8 full -time equivalents per year. year.

If you transfer the figures to Bornholm and assume that there are no economies of scale in establishing an, for example, twice as large facilities, then the establishment of a 600 MW plant for the production of ammonia could thus be expected to generate 16 jobs in the operational phase. This is a number that we in the Unity List have a hard time connecting with the statements that have come from, among others, Claus Larsen-Jensen that PTX and a business park for Energitung Industri will create "many new jobs".

That is why we have asked what these assumptions are based on, and although Claus Larsen-Jensen says that "there are reports of these possible green workplaces" when establishing PTX and more, it has not yet been possible to know which reports, reports, Reference is made - in addition to the report from CRT, which is based on the above figures from Ramboll.

Expansion of offshore wind In the Unity List, we have no doubt that there will be a significant expansion of offshore wind in the Baltic Sea in the coming years - and fortunately for that! We also have no doubt that a large part of the wind turbines to be raised in the Baltic Sea will be the ship out of Rønne. This potential is the Bornholm companies, among other things through the collaboration in the Offshore Center Bornholm, in the process of exploiting, and that is good!


Food, crafts and more

However, we are also sure that Bornholm continues to have a huge potential in developing the production of local, healthy, tasty and climate and environmentally friendly foods all the way from soil to table.

Bornholm also has a huge potential in terms of building on the success that the Bornholm craftsmanship is currently showing, and we believe that Bornholm has a huge potential to further develop the tourism sector in a more green, more climate -friendly and more locally rooted direction .

Although each farming, each mushroom, charcuterie, brewery, ceramic workshop, hiking organization, or guest house, and the many craftsmanship companies that create and improve the physical framework for citizens and businesses, each may seem like a drop in the sea, then must We do not forget that it is precisely these small businesses that create a large part of employment.

The latest business analysis for Bornholm from 2018 shows that almost half of the more than 2000 people who were employed in new Bornholm workplaces in 2015 were established in the period 2009 - 2015, was employed by small companies with between one and three employees.

If we want a development on Bornholm for the benefit of the many and for the benefit of Bornholm, and if we will now and not only in 10-15 years, then there is every reason to support and create the framework for establishing And the development of locally anchored companies that add value to what Bornholm has to offer, and not unilaterally betting on establishing a PTX industry on Bornholm.

Title: Samarbejde er vejen til velstand
Content:
This time about the connection between local cooperation and prosperity.

Despite the fact that Bornholm is the whole of Denmark's Solskinsø and is praised for the clouds in international media, the challenges are in line.

We lack money for important welfare tasks, lagging behind with the green transition, and the Cultural History Museum in Rø, which was to convey our rich cultural heritage, nevertheless does not turn into anything.

Politicians hope that more residents and tax money will solve the problems and they have a vision that we should be 42,000 Bornholmers in 2028. But they have probably been just a little too optimistic. According to the latest forecasts from 2024, the population will top with just over 39,800 in just 2028, but fall to 39,000 by 2035.

So even with Energiø Bornholm, we should probably assume that we ourselves must make a significant effort for our island to continue to be the world's best place to live. We - Citizens - must simply make us even more trouble to create what social scientists call social capital.

The invisible wealth - social capital in the book Bowling Alone describes American politologist Robert D. Putnam, how the connection to voluntary associations has sunk significantly, and more and more people are choosing to spend a significant part of their time alone - especially in front of the computer and television screen .

Putnam recorded that the changes have had fatal consequences for American society's social capital, which is a type of capital created when people are able to cooperate and support each other. Specifically, social capital is a result of norms that encourage cooperation, trust that makes you trust each other, and networks that create a framework for cooperation.

Social capital contributes to well -functioning democracies and promotes economic growth.

Workplaces and schools characterized by positive relationships and good cooperation will usually be rewarded with better well -being, less stress, lower sickness absence and higher productivity and quality.

Collaboration across it is not all forms of cooperation that create social capital.

The researchers talk about bounding and bridge -building social capital, respectively, and it is the latter - cooperation between people that are different in terms of ethnicity, residence, economy and political orientation, which we as a society benefit in particular.

In practice, for example, it could mean that it is good for our society and economy if the Danish People's Party and the Unity List, Agriculture and Nature Conservation Organizations, or Left on Østbornholm and Vestbornholm, manage to cooperate, rather than spending lots of time and resources on disagree.

A strong civil society An important prerequisite for high social capital is a strong civil society - that is. that the inhabitants engage in volunteers, non -commercial and socially beneficial organizations and associations.

Here at Bornholm, plenty of volunteer work is done every day. The many festivals, sports events, the National Assembly and the Culture Week can only be implemented because a large number of people choose to spend their time in favor of the community, and volunteering is also a prerequisite for recycling shops, museums, galleries, visiting schemes at institutions, integration of refugees and many many Other activities that benefit society and make our island a better place to live.

Volunteer welfare But there are also areas where we must in the future probably expect to make an even greater voluntary effort.

As Mads Roke Clausen points out in the book The Civil Potential, the classic welfare state is aimed at alleviating unemployment, illness, work accidents and old age in the industrial community, but falls short when it comes to post -industrial society's new types of social problems. If the welfare state is to survive, then volunteering must play a greater role - both to remedy and in particular prevent some of the new challenges.

Friendship instead of psychologist It can be, for example, in the field of children and youth.

Many children and adolescents wear out loneliness, dissatisfaction and mental illness, and if they do not get help to master their lives and break with negative patterns, then it will not only give them and their families poorer quality of life, but also hit the municipal economy hard.

The politicians' solution to the problem is more psychologists and special educators.

But perhaps it is not first and foremost expensive professional help needed, but good experiences, friendships, recognition and opportunities to experience mastery, and here we can all contribute. People with good social networks have better chances of managing without the help of the public.

Together about a new museum The planned museum in RØ is an example of a project where the Bornholmers failed to cooperate for the common good, and it has cost unnecessarily much time and a lot of money.

When we are now starting an alternative, it is therefore important that we can assure the large funds that there is broad popular support for the project. Of course, everyone does not have to agree that the solution we land is the best, but we must not counteract each other - because we will all lose that.

Local tripartite cooperation We have also not worked optimally in the green area.

Through international agreements, Denmark has committed to creating more nature and fighting the climate crisis, and it was decided by 2020 that 15 so -called natural parks will be established, including an Almindingen on Bornholm.

The goals have proved difficult to achieve because some actors prioritize their own individual interests over the best of society and the world. Meanwhile, the Baltic Sea, we get hotter, wetter and wilder weather, and it becomes more difficult to operate agriculture and forestry.

In order to combat the crises, a local tripartite cooperation should be established as soon as possible, where the parties agree on where the effort should be put into.

The art of working together to create good cooperation that can contribute to social capital is an art that requires certain skills of those who need to cooperate, including the ability to speak properly to each other and recognize the professionalism, experiences and differences of the others.

In short, it is about creating arenas for collaboration, where the actors feel valued, experience mutual respect, communicate effectively and are able to work towards common goals.

So simple - and yet so hard.

Title: Milliarder til grønt eventyr
Content:
At Bornholm they say no. In Skive they said yes. And for the latter, it has meant billion investments in green technology.

Skive (Bornholm's Journal) DKK 3,000,000,000. So much money has already been invested in Greenlab - a green business adventure in the northwestern city of Skive.

Today, 103 new jobs have been created, 500 more are underway within the next two years, and the next 500 jobs are only spade second in a gigantic field with room for many more green companies.

But why are the information relevant to readers of Bornholm Tidende at all? Because a majority in the regional municipality's municipal council will reject a proposal from municipal director Sine Sunesen to look for possible areas for a green business park in connection with the upcoming energy island.

Bornholm Tidende went to Skive to see what a green business park is for a size and what it does for Skive Municipality. You can read about it today and tomorrow.


Business tourists in heaps

In Skive, they cheer on their decision to bet hard on green energy. In addition to the rain of jobs in the Green Industrial Park's preliminary six companies, it also drips on other parts of the business community in the municipality.

- Our local contractors benefit from this. Companies that build roads, craftsmen who have helped erect all buildings, hauliers running land and sand just to name a few. We have become well known as a green municipality, which also attracts other types of companies. In addition, it has given a lot of business tourists to the benefit of the area's hotels and restaurants, says Mayor Peder Christian Kirkegaard. Every year, a five -digit number of business leaders, scientists and politicians from around the world is making their way past Skive to learn how to create green companies whose technology can support each other.


Denmark's first climate

Peder Christian Kirkegaard has been mayor of Skive Municipality since 2014. At that time they had long since begun to think green, and then Climate Minister Connie Hedegaard appointed Skive in 2008 as Denmark's first climate.

- In 2010, we set up a secretariat across the municipal administrations to create what we call our energy town, says the mayor.

Back then, Peder Christian Kirkegaard was already sitting in the city council. When he pulled the mayor chain on, the municipality had also become ready to realize the concrete thoughts of creating a green business adventure.

- I was presented with an idea that we here in the municipality should establish Denmark's first green business park. It is from there that the idea of ​​Greenlab is born, he says.


Then came millions

In 2016, the Energy Secretariat became a fund that went to work with a long-term strategy. Because like Rome, a green business park cannot be built in one day. The mayor of Skive Municipality should initially sit as chairman of the Energi City Foundation. But Peder Christian Kirkegaard decided was a mistake.

- We should have some skills that I don't have. So we found some business people in energy who have a knowledge of this area and could help create a symbiosis, says Peder Christian Kirkegaard.

And then the whole project began to accelerate.

After some swords with the authorities, Skive Municipality was allowed to lay out large area to erect the entire energy city or Greenlab, which is now the name. The municipality, together with Norlys and Spar Vest Fonden, shot DKK 75 million in Greenlab A/S in 2019 - a public -private collaboration model and the parent company to develop the entire park. And when the municipality was willing to invest financially on the project started, business was aware that they had a headwind from the first shovel. But the municipality's investment is not meant as an alms or gift booth.


No longer equal

- We have shot money into construction maturation with a rental agreement, where we get the money back over a number of years. It is probably the largest investment made by Skive Municipality, but we are sure it can pay off.

The alternative is that we had not done anything at all, and then this had not happened, says the mayor.

Initially, the municipality and the investors were equal capital stakeholders. This is no longer the case. First, the Spar Vest Foundation donated an additional DKK 30 million in 2021. Since then, more than DKK 500 million has been invested in the parent company GreenLab alone, and it has diluted the municipality's share considerably to ownership of 7.8 percent.

But that was also the intention, because a huge group of an economic muscle bundle that Norlys helps to set the pace. And then the companies are otherwise flowing to. Today's date, a total of DKK 3,000,000,000 has been invested in GreenLab, and that figure will increase significantly.


Well -educated return home

Bornholm Regional Municipality and Skive Municipality have many common features. Both are in what one with a not always praising term calls the outskirts of Denmark - the part of the kingdom that is often taken into account, jobs and companies with highly educated.

Skive Municipality has an area of ​​683.42 square kilometers. Bornholm's regional municipality extends over 589.38 square kilometers.

At the entrance to 2024, Skive Municipality had 44,739 inhabitants. Bornholm Regional Municipality housed 39,332 at the time. The two municipalities have an additional thing in common.

- We have the challenge just like Bornholm that there are many young people who move from the municipality to get a higher education and stay elsewhere. Now we see that the development is going the other way and many of the young people come home again. For they want to be on the exciting journey that is not only driven by GreenLab, but all the projects and companies in the municipality that are focusing on the green agenda.

Here in the western part of Jutland we are actually one of the municipalities that is high on the list of residents with long, higher education, says Peder Christian Kirkegaard


A local pride

The fact that Skive Municipality today is a green lighthouse throughout Denmark has only been possible in one way.

- I think it's been relatively easy. Because we have been completely together as a city council on this since 2014. And here in the recent city council period there has not been as much as we have had to deal with and use forces on, after Norlys has come along, he says.

The mayor is more than happy with what Greenlab is today and not least what it is about growing.

- When talking to others around the country, there are many who mention GreenLab.

It creates a local pride, he says.

Title: Energiø? Nej tak!
Content:
The think tank Kraka Economics calls Energiø Bornholm an economic catatrophe.

In their program perspective, TV2 has examined the Energiø project again and talked to both Kraka Economics and Denmark's economic sages, who unanimously say that Energiø Bornholm must be stopped.

The biggest problem for the energy island project is the many and long cables to be laid in the Baltic Sea from the offshore wind turbines and to Bornholm and then from Bornholm to Denmark and last but not least from Bornholm to Germany. Maybe there is also a cable for Poland, but it doesn't make the case better.

One thing is the huge expenses for the many cables, but another thing is the great loss of power that becomes when the power is to be transported first to Bornholm and then over long distances to the lands of land.


If a, then also b

In this giant project, things are connected.

When we say A, we will have to say B and C G so on until Bornholm is totally destroyed by heavy industry.

If the gigantic transformer station is built on Bornholm, then there is a risk that a gigantic business park will also be built next to hydrogen and ammonia factories and other heavy industry that can use a lot of power. (when it blows) How should this hydrogen or ammonia - which are otherwise dangerous substances - transported from Bornholm to, for example, Germany? The only sensible way to transport these large quantities of, for example, hydrogen is by a pipeline, but when is this pipeline completed? There are such great logistical challenges associated with Energiø Bornholm that I hope our dear politicians soon wake up and make some sensible decisions that have teams in reality and can be realized.


The North Sea, not the Baltic Sea

I believe that Energiø Bornholm should be moved to the North Sea, and that Denmark must build the large offshore wind farms in the North Sea and make hydrogen production in Esbjerg, where the hydrogen can be transported in the already designed pipeline to Germany.

In other words - Denmark must gather the forces and build the large offshore wind farms in the North Sea.

In the North Sea, the wind turbines can get further from land so that they do not bother the population - and there are many other benefits of building offshore winds in the North Sea.


Nature

One thing is the economy of Energiø Bornholm project, which will be an economic disaster. It's bad enough, but unfortunately not even the worst.

Energiø Bornholm also becomes a disaster for nature both - on Bornholm and in the sea and these permanent damage to nature cannot be settled in money.

With the Wnergiø Bornholm project, Denmark will trigger a development that will in the long run destroy Bornholm's nature. If all this energy industry is being built on Bornholm, it will result in more offshore wind turbines being built.

CIP has previously wanted to build offshore wind farms east of Bornholm, and they will probably try to realize their projects if Energiø Bornholm turns into something.

Unfortunately, the CIP project will probably not be the last either. This development will continue until Bornholm is totally destroyed and at that time without tourism.


Workplaces

The few permanent jobs that we are constantly lured with will not be able to offset all the jobs that we will lose due to lack of tourists.

Today, fortunately, there are some young people who choose to settle on Bornholm, and there are others moving to Bornholm Why do they do it? Most people who move to Bornholm do so because of our lovely nature - both on land and at sea. If in a few years we do not get these newcomers, then Bornholm Regional Municipality has lost it all on the floor, and instead of Energiø Bornholm wanting to develop Bornholm, it will destroy our island.


The politicians

If our politicians in Christiansborg continue to insist that the sea south of Bornholm should be destroyed by offshore wind farms, then I hope these are made with transformer platforms just like Kriegers Flak and send the current directly to Germany or Denmark.

Then I hope that Denmark will fr like the whole of Bornholm for the energy industry, and I hope that Bornholm's regional municipality will use the effort to help and nurture the companies that exist at Bornholm today at the same time that BRK is of course doing what they can to attract new businesses .


A good development is in progress

Bornholm is in a good development - now that it is moving forward for many professions.

Take good care and support this development.

That's, I think, better than the energy island project.

Bornholm politicians believe that the energy island can save Bornholm's economy, but our poor economy is largely due to social expenses, and if they are to be paid by the energy sector, then we get the world's highest power prices.

Bornholm's financial problems must be solved by a municipal distribution reform that can provide a fair distribution of tax revenue throughout Denmark instead of an equalization scheme that does not work.


Drop it in the Baltic Sea

Denmark and our politicians in Christiansborg will build Denmark's large offshore wind turbine venture in the North Sea and drop Energiø Bornholm.

It will save the North Sea project and save Bornholm's nature so that the Danes will also go on a school trip to Bornholm in the future.

I have often wondered that Energiø Nordsø project has been stopped several times without any special posture about it. Now that there is talk of stopping Energiø Bornholm project, there is a lot of attention.

Let me remind you that there has been talk of putting up 10,000 wind turbines in the North Sea.

This is equivalent to building 50 Energiø Bornholm projects.

So dear politicians - Think about and don't destroy Bornholm.

Title: Et skur på en mark
Content:
Skive has got its own energy island. Without water.

Skive (Bornholm's Journal). Highway 26 north of Skive is a place where the wind often comes to visit with a strong breath. At least when approaching Vester Lyby; 10 kilometers drive from the municipality's town hall. And it is basically very practical.

On the western side of the main road there are 12 large wind turbines in a undergrowth of solar panels. When the trip counter then shows 10.9 kilometers, there is suddenly science fiction in the trip, if you swing to the left and see mill number 13. For here is GreenLab - a collection of companies that produce everything differently. But with a common sign.

The mills and the solar cells are what drives all the glory.

Greenlab is the heart that develops and manages the entire green business park. Here are six production companies; A number that is coming up. Today, Stiesdal, Green Hydrogen Systems, Quantafuel, West Jutland's Andels Snarfabber, Greenlab Skive Vind and Greenlab Skive Biogas hold in the park.


Starfish and gas

But what do the six companies have in common? Among other things, they enchant old plastic, manure, remnants of invasive starfish, nitrogen and CO2 into fertilizer, green aircraft fuel, animal feed, heat, biogas, methanol and hydrogen and much more. With the help of technology called Power-to-X.

GreenLab is a circular economy where companies across each other exchange resources and where it is all powered by renewable energy.

GreenLab is also a test zone; A form of sanctuary that the Danish Energy Agency allowed the Municipality of Skive to erect in 2021. The purpose was to be able to work with new technologies and make them sustainable business. Here research and production work side by side.

No millions have been spent in heaps to make Greenlab's offices delicious and smart. This is not where the Skivonites believe that the money should be laid out in the first place. The head office is a temporary building, erected by containers, and is most reminiscent of an overgrown version of what you see in large construction sites.

- Everyone calls it the office pavilion. I usually call it the shed, says Thomas Helsgaun.


Excited about the municipality

He is CEO of GreenLab and very excited about the way Skive Municipality collaborates with business.

- When new companies arrive, you are invited to the municipal director and get help with all the practical. This does not only apply to the companies in Greenlab. This applies to all the companies in the municipality that I am talking to, he says.

However, Greenlab's head office should not consist of a stack of containers forever.

- We must have built an administration building so that all the area's companies have a common place to meet. This applies to both the current and the coming, because it will do very well for the park if we can all share canteen, meeting rooms and changing rooms.

It must also be a common innovation center, and we are betting that it was built in 2026, says the man behind the helm.


From port view to shed on a plow field

Thomas Helsgaun He has held top positions in Maersk and traveled around the world 200 days a year. Early he was 11 years old in defense and ended as a captain. Title: Tiden er inde til erhvervspark
Content:
Let's work together on the Energi-Erhvervsparken.

Last week, the plans for an energy business kick have filled the political discussion on Bornholm.

On the one hand, business has emphasized the importance of seizing the opportunity, while a majority in political treatment does not believe that the time has yet been for Bornholm Regional Municipality to use the effort to designate an area where the energy commercial park can be placed.

I understand well the confusion that is around an upcoming energy business kick.

What is it really, it should contain, how large an area is needed, and why should already consider something that is so far out in the future? I can also understand that it can be difficult to decide on an initiative that is so large and in many ways unclear.

We take the baton On this basis we will now take up the baton with the Bornholm business community in Baltic Energy Island.

We will continue the work on two tracks.

First, we will work to specify what a business park is. What can it contain and what will it mean for Bornholm? Secondly, we will invite to dialogue between business, citizens, organizations and of course not least the politicians.

The hope is that through dialogue we can reach a better understanding of what it is that we should say yes or no to.

The first step is that on Monday we have invited the municipal council members as well as the organizations of business and the trade union movement to a four -night meeting where we will tell about the thoughts that we have made so far and initiate the dialogue.

Why don't we just wait? But why don't we wait until we know if the energy island is coming and there are actually some companies that have asked for land? The question is logical, but there are also two good reasons why we are picking up the baton now.

First, we need to send a clear signal to the companies that will compete for the right to set up wind turbines south of Bornholm. When they have to prepare their bids in 2025, they need to know if they should consider investments at Bornholm.

Secondly, there is a legislative window that is open now. Bornholm was, as an exception, written in the "Law on State -appointed Energy Parks".

The law allows us to enroll an area from Bornholm, despite the fact that it is in the open country and in the coastal proximity zone.

This change in the law is primarily made to meet Bornholm's desire to use the energy island as a basis for lasting business development. The possibility of reporting area to the energy-commercial kick will disappear in 2025, which in practice means that an area must be reported during the first half of 2025.

It has been mentioned in the debate that we can ask to be allowed to sign up later.

We do not know if it is possible, as it will require a new political agreement. It is difficult to predict whether there will be openness to it in Christiansborg if we do not seize the chance now in the first place, where it actually makes sense in relation to the energy island's tender process and where there is certainly a legislative option.

Finally, in its rural proposal, the government has proposed that Baltic Energy Island will receive DKK 10 million to exploit the business opportunities associated with Energiø Bornholm and support Bornholm as a hub for development, testing and demonstration of green energy.

The concrete implementation of the funds awaits the play being finally decided, but it is my clear expectation that part of the funds should just be used to specify the idea of ​​an energy business park.


Let's start with the dialog

I hope all parties are willing to take part in the dialogue.

It takes a good time, many talks and good planning to deal with the major societal changes that Energiø Bornholm introduces on our island. But we have to put the long light on and take the big discussions about what we want with Bornholm, and not least how we will work to make the island more financially sustainable.

In those discussions we cannot put two lines under everything. We cannot expect guarantees, nor can we wait for the development to come to us. We need to formulate visions and set strategies that we stick to for a long time - through ups and downs.

However, the long strategic aim and the lack of guarantees make dialogue so much more important. It is through conversation that we can gain an understanding of the images that we each have of Bornholm's future, and it is through the dialogue that we can hopefully find a common image that we can strive together to realize.

Title: Er energiøerhvervsparken fremtiden?
Content:
Establishment of Energiø Bornholm calls for a renewed (security) assessment, says Knud Andersen.

When Bornholm was suggested as an energy hub in the Baltic Sea, no one could imagine war in our part of the world.

War and conflicts had for many years bypass the northern part of Europe, and if there was war, it would be at such a high technological level that it would not affect Denmark and the Baltic Sea area. But after Russia's assault on Ukraine, the situation has changed fundamentally.

The war that Russia initiated is no different from what has been seen in the past.

It takes place as a regular land war, where the parties seek to expand their territory.

At the same time, civilian targets are bombed in the cities to break down the resilience of the population - in addition, both the war in Ukraine and Gaza show that modern warfare is also taking place by attacks on critical infrastructure such as energy supply and communication centers.

Danish Focus It is precisely the two areas that we have focused on in Denmark over the last several years and which have led to ever -increasing systems with large overall centers.

It was rational and sensible in a world where there is no war and conflicts, but this is no longer the case.

After all, the war in Ukraine is not a local conflict limited to the areas of the Black Sea.

It is a conflict in which most Western countries have become part of financial support and weapons supplies to Ukraine. Denmark actively participates in the help of Ukraine.

It is risky in this changed security situation it is highly unwise to expand new green electricity supply in large central wind farms in the Baltic Sea and not least to place the hub on Bornholm.

A single drone in the plant on Bornholm will be able to turn off the light of thousands of people in the countries north and south of us - not to mention the risk of neighbors to the plant.

The new security situation in the Baltic Sea calls for smaller and decentralized plants, as a starting point for the development of green power.

Some might object that the Black Sea is far away. Yes, but not further away than the Nord Stream lines could be bombed here at Bornholm and that Russian ships are attacked in Kaliningrad. Or that the Russian Foreign Minister has threatened Denmark.

Russia's actions are unforeseen. We can't prevent it, but we don't have to wear ourselves stupidly.

The Law on Energy Island In contrast to the establishment of the many wind turbines in the sea surrounding Bornholm, the possibility of designating a commercial area in connection with the land facility for the wind park has led to large discussions.

MPs and others have called for Bornholm to utilize the window that the Law on Energy Parks gives to designate commercial areas with a number of flexible rights - without telling what special rights the law gives.

If, on the other hand, one reads the comments on the Law on Energy Parks, it is clearly seen that it is primarily made in order to find areas for large coherent wind and solar cell parks. Therefore, the law allows to disregard nature protection and coastal protection.

The purpose of the proposed state -designated energy parking law is to promote electricity production from renewable energy sources on land by designating energy parks on land with improved opportunities for setting up wind turbines and photovoltaic plants, with the necessary consideration of other societal interests in land use.

The law must, among other things, allow for the installation of wind turbines and photovoltaic systems in larger interconnected areas on land where, according to current rules, it would be difficult or not possible to establish wind turbines or photovoltaic systems.

It will should be done by a changed weighing of national interests in connection with the appointment and by further possibility to dispense from certain provisions in the applicable land regulation in, inter alia, The Nature Conservation Act, the Forest Act and the Museum Act (quote from the law notes). Bornholm Bornholm is separately mentioned in the law with the possibility of establishing business parks in connection with land facilities without the aforementioned nature considerations.

Furthermore, the possibility of establishing a PTX system is mentioned which requires a lot of energy to make hydrogen.

Once you have read the law on energy parks, it seems completely indifferent whether we designate the energetic business area now or at the time when there are realistic uses.

The opportunity to establish a PTX system is far out in the future. But without such a plant, it seems unrealistic to establish a new business area here. Therefore, the question is still open what the advocates of this area designation think of when you say that it is gambling with Bornholm's opportunities if one does not agree with their views.

Education makes us not only to more proficient labor, but to better citizens who have a strong inner compass and understand the value of the society they are part of. Formation is to be able to put themselves in the place of others, understand our history and culture and to be able to relate critically to the society that we meet. Niklas Stenbye

Title: Energiø Bornholm - et luftkastel?
Content:
We have become too slow.

A year ago, the Danish Energy Agency calculated that Energiø Bornholm is missing about DKK 31.5 billion to be a socio -economically profitable project, and thus about DKK 14 billion more than the DKK 17.6 billion that the government has set as a support fore The project.

It has led the magazine Engineer, the think tank Kraka and most recently the economic sages to propose the government to either completely drop the project or at least to rethink Energiø Bornholm.


Canceled - or exposed - projects

In that light, it is understandable that members of the municipal council on Bornholm together with several others are doubtful about the project, and including the possible energy park, which a narrow majority in the municipal council wants to put a ticket on.

In addition, an increasing number of green projects are either dropped or exposed by several years, among other things: - In August 2024, the energy company Ørsted decided to withdraw from the Swedish methanol project Flagship One and thus bear a loss of close to DKK 2 billion.

- The international energy group Shell has decided to drop another Swedish project to produce airline fuel.

- Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners has postponed a major hydrogen project in Esbjerg.

- The energy group Better Energy has postponed a number of major solar cell projects to after 2030.

And in the week before the autumn holidays, the government decided to postpone the initiation of the hydrogen pipe in Jutland from 2028 to 2031. This has consequences for planned hydrogen production in Jutland through the so-called PTX (PTER-T-X).

Without a hydrogen tube, no export, and without export, no large-scale-PATX production, stated board member Rasmus Bach Nielsen from the company H2 Energy Esbjerg, who works for a very large PTX plant in Esbjerg.

The global angle has Energiø Bornholm become an air castle, a fantasy project without financial realism, a mistake in the green transition that climate change otherwise calls so hard? Let's raise the helicopter and see the development of offshore wind energy at global level, and the development of the production of green fuels for, among other things. the aircraft and ship industry through PTX.

Here, the production of offshore wind energy from 2021 to 2023 (latest numbers) is more than doubled to 75 GW (Energiø Bornholm is intended for 3.0-3.8 GW).

By 2020, the EU accounted for 80 percent of the offshore wind energy, but now it is China and the UK that have the driver's jersey.

In China, the scope of offshore wind energy increased from 4.6 GW in 2020 to 31.5 GW by the end of 2023. During the same period, the scope in the UK increased from 10.4 GW to 27.6 GW. Here we are talking about completed projects, and not the many projects that are further planning - also in countries such as the USA, Australia, South Korea and Latin America.

We are slow in Denmark and the EU, on the other hand, is slowing down than planned.

Like solar cells and electric cars, China is also in this area to take over the market, helped by cheaper labor, state aid as well as far fewer legal and other regular obstacles.

So, the development of offshore wind energy - and for that matter energy islands - on a global scale roaring from there.

What about PTX? There are still many questions with PTX, not least around the economy.

But we are wrong if we have the impression that PTX development is still just at the research stage and that there is no production of hydrogen and green fuels yet on a larger scale.

By the end of 2023, at a global level, about 12 GW capacity within PTX was realized. Green hydrogen is produced, but also other forms of energy conversion such as synthetic fuels (e-fuel), green ammonia and e-metanol.

The first large Danish PTX plant at Kassø in Southern Jutland is one of the projects where investors have not withdrawn.

It is very far ahead and expects to initiate production before the end of the year with a production of approximately 32,000 tonnes of e-metanol annually. Demand is high - among other things, an agreement has been made with the shipping company Maersk, which has already inaugurated its first large container ship, based on e -metanol as fuel.


What about all the dropped and exposed projects?

The local angle

This is especially true in agriculture, traditional industries and followers - including as a result of various public initiatives such as CO -2 tax, and various adaptations to climate change.

Whether the figure 3,000 holds or becomes smaller, the development will entail a significant risk of a greater decline in population, and thus of the maintenance that what we can call socially critical infrastructures - education on campus, functions in the hospital and so on.

Energiø Bornholm with a business park may not be fully compensated for the loss of jobs and population that will come - but it is extremely difficult to find other development potentials.


Not just locally

We can sit back, await the development of offshore wind energy and PTX, leave the market to the Chinese and other global players. But will the consequence not simply be that Bornholm alone remains with the negative consequences of climate change in the form of loss of jobs and further decreases in the population? Title: Energiøen hænger på kablerne til Sjælland
Content:

Energiø Bornholm may need up to DKK 31.5 billion in public support.

This has prompted, among others, professor of energy planning Brian Vad Mathiesen from Aalborg University to speak to think of the energy island in a different way that will cost less money.

For example, by cutting the cable connection from Energiø to Zealand out of the project.

The cables for the Zealand electricity grid will cost about DKK 22 billion. According to the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Supply, this is the price of constructing cables over the 209 kilometers that will be needed.

However, dropping the cables to Zealand will also hurt other parts of the work with Energiø Bornholm, writes the Bornholm -based consortium Baltic Energy Island (BEI) in a new note. Other parts of the effort to finance Energiø Bornholm will also be damaged by the cables to Zealand. For example, it will be necessary to withdraw the application for up to five billion kroner in support from the EU back.

Initially, it must be emphasized that a removal of the connection to DK2 (Eastern Denmark) will change the project to an extent that will break with the intergovernmental agreement with Germany, demand a cancellation of Energinets and 50 Hertz's ongoing supply of stations and cables and mean, The fact that the project must withdraw the recently submitted billion dancing search for funds from the EU, says the memorandum from Baltic Energy Island's director Søren Møller Christensen.

Removing the connection to DK2 will therefore have great foreign policy and economic significance as well as result in a significant delay, he continues.

Bei goes so far as to write that Denmark will not get any significant value out of Energiø Bornholm if the cables to Zealand do not become part of the project.

Without a connection to DK2, the offshore wind fields will potentially be developed as traditional radial offshore wind, which is only linked to Germany. In addition to any revenue from tenders, Denmark will not achieve any of the many effects that the current project contains in the form of, among other things, security of supply, contributions to the redemption of RE-targets and innovation boundaries for the Danish business community on energy islands, writes Søren Møller Christensen in Bei "'s new note.

The companies in the Bei Consortium are Rønne Harbor, Beof, Offshore Center Bornholm, Technical University of Denmark, Ørsted, Siemens Gamesa and Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners. The regional municipality is also participating.

Bei "s President is Beof Director Claus M.

Andersen.

Much will be lost to writing the cables to Zealand out of the plans for Energiø Bornholm was first brought up by Professor Brian Vad Mathiesen almost a month ago.

- The poor economy of the energy island is not due to the wind turbines. This is due to the system setup that has been assumed so far. For example, by minimizing the amount of cables and by considering a local power to-x production, he said to the Journal on October 8.

- The point that it costs a lot when you want to cable so far is right.

But if you had chosen another design where you were connected to Sweden or Poland, then you might have reduced the price, Brian Vad Mathiesen said the same day to TV2/ Bornholm.

The bei now estimates that the chance of billionaire from the EU will be reduced, just as any EU support will certainly be delayed.

Without a connection to DK2, the project will lose its status as a project of common interest and thus the opportunity to get up to DKK 5 billion from the EU. (...) You are very busy creating the opportunity to send an excess of green power from Northern Europe down to southern Europe, where you have too little green power. Removing the connection to Zealand will also, according to Bei's new note, lead the Danish-German agreement on Energiø Bornholm into uncertainty.

The current intergovernmental agreement with Germany is based on the project having a connection to DK2 of 1.2 Gigawatt.

Therefore, if the connection is abandoned or changed to DK2, a renegotiation of the agreement will be necessary. Germany's approach to a renegotiation is unknown, and a renegotiation will certainly lead to a significant delay in the project. Without cables between Energiø Bornholm and the Zealand Elnet, Energiø Bornholm will, according to BEI, not be an energy island at all. To be it requires two energy markets to be linked.

Without a connection to DK2, Energiø Bornholm will not be an energy island, as there will no longer be a linking of DK2 and Germany, it is also stated in Bei's new note.

Title: Fra skolebænk til energiø
Content:
Comment - Future Education at Bornholm.

Bornholm stands at an exciting crossroads, and with the establishment of the energy island we have a unique opportunity to create new, meaningful jobs here on the island - and at the same time give our young people the knowledge and skills needed to seize the future.

But the question is whether we will also do the necessary thing to ensure that Bornholm can keep up with the development? The government's new educational reform can become a key to this if we manage to think visionary and adapt our education to the special needs and potentials we already have here on the island.


New skills

Energiø Bornholm is not only a green investment, but in particular a project that creates demand for everything from technical labor to engineers and IT people, but also on a formation and dissemination perspective that calls for broad competencies.

We have the opportunity to shape our education so that they can purposefully dress the young Bornholmers for these particular challenges. If we can then create a prayer connection between the broad competencies that the energy projects demand, and the opportunities we offer on Campus Bornholm, then we can equip our young people for the future labor market. However, it requires that we dare to think education in a new way and that we focus on both the practical and the academic skills.

If Energiø Bornholm is to succeed, then we must both attract new businesses and develop our own talents. We need educational offerings that unite theory and practice and that contain everything from green technology and sustainability, technical skills, education and dissemination - to support the development of energy island.

Campus Bornholm can play a key role here, but it requires that we as a community stand together to secure resources and support. For our young people have to build their future here on the island, then they must also see the way to a realistic and meaningful career.


The key is local cooperation

Campus Bornholm and Business can together create a basis where our young people gain concrete experience and can develop the skills that energy projects require.

Collaboration becomes crucial, and if we are to get the most out of the energy island, then we as an educational institution must have flexibility to adapt our offerings.

The energy island could be the case where young people are given the opportunity to test theory and gain insight into the reality they enter. The question is whether we can be allowed to realize that potential and whether Bornholm will support that effort , it takes.

Uncertainty? For many young people in Bornholm, the future may seem uncertain, and it can be tempting to search away for education and career in the larger cities.

But with Energiø Bornholm we can turn this trend and show the young people that there are opportunities here on the island, which also contains the future education and jobs in the green transition.

In order for them to benefit from the new opportunities, we must offer programs that match the need for both academic and practical skills. If the young people are to see a future here, it requires us to adapt the education to both their and Bornholm needs.


Unique chance

Energiø Bornholm represents more than a green transition - it is also a unique chance to create lasting opportunities and development for Bornholm.

But it requires that we dare to make a choice and invest in our young people and their education.

By tying the ambitions of the reform together with Bornholm's needs, we can show the rest of Denmark that we can bridge the gap between local development and the green future.

Let's take this step together so we can create a Bornholm where young people want to stay and return to, to contribute to the island's sustainable future.

Title: Stolt af vores historie - og blikket for fremtiden
Content:
When Bornholm builds new, we build on the past. Let's be proud of our commitment to history and the great knowledge we find and preserve for posterity.

It is not every day that we at Bornholm can witness an archaeological treasure chest so rich in traces of the past that it can give a historical overview of the Stone Age to the Middle Ages.

The extensive archaeological work at Energiø Bornholm's land facility southwest of Aakirkeby shows how strong we as a society protect our cultural roots before we put the bucket in the ground and build in the future.

When the Bornholm Museum with an upcoming team of 30 archaeologists opens the Earth and uncovers settlements, plots and objects that can tell about the life of the Bornholm ancestors, they do more than uncover ruins and dusty objects. They create a strong foundation for our own identity. Each new find adds a piece to the big puzzle that Bornholm's history constitutes, and the archaeologists' discoveries show a complex development pattern and settlements that over time can give us new insight into how many people lived on Bornholm for millennia.

This work does not only strengthen our cultural history. It is also an important part of the formation of future generations. The story lies here under our feet, and every time we unveil it, we give ourselves and our children a deeper perspective on our past. Bornholm Museum has already uncovered 30 settlements and traces of over 100 plots - a truly unique picture of human activity on the island during all periods of history. These data can help archaeologists to form a picture of the island's settlement development and bring Bornholm forward as one of Denmark's most important areas for development archaeological studies.

There is good reason why we prioritize this historical mapping.

Our deep respect for the story means that we dare to draw parallels between the development of the past and today. That we can build new with a deep understanding of what came before makes Bornholm an example in responsible construction and community planning. It is the kind of foresight that makes our island more than a temporary home - we are not only looking forward to the financial gain from an energy island, but also towards the long -term values ​​of culture and formation.

Of course, it requires both time and resources, and the work has only begun. But with the great societal support and Bornholm Museum's dedication to the project, we will be able to make a unique contribution to Danish history. Once we turn on the energy island's first bulb, we can do so with the pride that we have laid the new on top of a solid foundation of respect for the past.

- Denmark is a low cost area for energy, and Poland is a high price area. According to our simulations, this will make a profit of between DKK 15 and 20 billion over the entire life of the project. This is what happens everywhere you buy something cheap and sell it expensive, she says.

The profits will have to be shared between Denmark, Poland and Germany.

- In this model you can add different values ​​for, among other things, the production and consumption of electricity - and the extension of renewable energy. Initially, however, the Polish government was not interested in Energiø Bornholm.

- The fact that Denmark and Poland have agreed to analyze a connection means that it is not just birds on the roof. Of course, it also depends on the political climate of Poland.

Title: Skal vi hjælpe vores naboer?
Content:
It is one of the important issues in working with the future society - both in the welfare and energy field.

I have lived in Bornholm for just over four years now, and the words that I first and foremost think of when I look into Bornholm's DNA is helpfulness and community.

When I have doubts about a decision, I always step back and consider what my very basic values ​​are; We need to give opportunities to those who can themselves and help those who cannot.


Challenges

In everyday life we ​​all have our major or minor challenges, and from the mayor's chair I get insight into many of them - especially about the meeting between citizens and municipalities.

In between we can forget that the municipality is all of us.

The municipality is a community and it is our friends and family who are employed by the municipality and that we are all only interested in finding the best solution.

BRK's tight economy does not make everyday life and the solutions easier, and we all want more resources so that we can get even better kindergartens, schools and care centers, get laps in the roads, give more building permits and get more jobs and more labor for the island. Lobbyism I have been to Christiansborg several times to draw attention to our very special challenges here in the middle of the Baltic Sea, and so far it has been far along the way to secure grants - whether from the pool from particularly difficult municipalities, or That it is imperative to have the unequal equalization scheme between the municipalities and which puts us on Bornholm in a more difficult situation than necessary.

Bornholm is also marked on Christiansborg's map when it comes to compensation for neighbors and communities in connection with Energiø Bornholm. I believe and hope that it will succeed in getting a sensible solution that accommodates the neighbors and communities that are land and prospect of such large socially important infrastructure projects.


The energy island

The energy island is still up for debate.

Why should Bornholm put land and sea into such a large project? Why should we help Germany? Why should we spend so much money on it? Wasn't it better to get nuclear power? Last week we were a delegation with participants from Beof, Rønne Harbor, Baltic Energy Island Foundation and BRK on a study/ network trip to the North German state of Mecklenburg Vorpommern (MV).

Here are the cities of Rostock, Sassnitz and Schwerin.

In Germany, they are busy getting independent of gas from Russia. They have a lot of heavy industry and transport, which in the future cannot use either gas or batteries - just like in Denmark.

In Germany, they expect to have to import over 50 percent of their future green fuels, and they reach out to all their allied neighbors to secure their energy supply; Even up to Finland. A few weeks ago, Germany adopted their upcoming hydrogen infrastructure, which in the northern part of the country depends on supply from Denmark and other countries around the Baltic Sea.

The weakness of the wind turbines is, as you know, that they do not supply power when the wind is not blowing. On the other hand, they supply too much power when it blows a lot.

It is power that we usually cannot use and which we can only store to a lesser extent in batteries and the like; That is, there is a lot of wind that goes to waste. It is precisely here that production of hydrogen has its justification. Otherwise, when the wind turbines should have been kept down at speed, you can instead use the power to convert water into hydrogen and thus produce fuel for the days when the wind does not blow or the sun does not shine.

Other forms of energy For many years we have seen the large oil pumps stand and pump on the prairie in Texas or in the Arab countries.

It ensures them oil, money, jobs and development. Today, the wind turbines can do the same, just without oil and pollution.

Nuclear power costs twice the wind power and you still have not solved the challenge of the waste, and then it is rather expensive to dismantle a nuclear power plant when it is worn out. On the work we visited in Greifswald last week, the director on the spot thought the bill would run up to 70 billion, and it would take over 50 years before work was completed. Maybe new technology will come in the field in the future, but right now wind and sun are the best and cheapest that we have in Denmark.

The Environmental Business Park Municipal Council has decided to continue working with an energetic business park that gets electricity from offshore wind turbines.

It is my eyes the only possibility that we have if we even at Bornholm want to hold hands on the development in the area, the execution, and not least to ensure that Bornholm gets something out of that development. It is both in the form of new businesses, the attraction of new technology - and thus also educational institutions such as DTU - and not least workplaces. It will eventually have to pay for our kindergartens, schools and care centers.

Help so should we help our neighbors? Of course we should! Whether they are on the other side of the ligus hedge, in the rest of Denmark or on the other side of the Baltic Sea. We are dependent on each other and we come the longest with joint efforts.

Title: Bornholm risikerer at miste mange millioner fra EU
Content:
Leaked document from the EKINEMISSION talks about more difficult access to the large million amounts that Bornholm has received from Brussels in recent years.

Bornholm risks losing EU support in a very large style if a new plan from the European Commission becomes a reality.

The plan is partly about setting stricter conditions for which local and regional projects can get EU support. Partly about bringing together all the 530 EU programs that Bornholm has so far received money from one large pool for each Member State.

The idea has been posted in a document from budget officials in the EU that the US media Politico has read. At Bornholm, the municipality's EU coordinator Niels Chresten Andersen is very concerned.

- Bornholm has raised more than DKK 130 million from various programs over the past three to four years. For green transition, energy island, waste management, tourism and vocational education and other purposes, he says.

- Strong forces in the Circuit around Commission President von der Leyen in the European Commission will apparently centralize the majority of the EU's programs in the future, so that about 80 percent of the EU's budget is gathered in national pools, and once a year paid to the individual member states, says Niels Chresten Andersen.

- In the future, it could mean that national governments will unilaterally determine the prioritization of the EU's funds and that municipalities, regions, business and association life are completely linked to the development, he says.

- The intended reorganization of the funds - for example, funds for agricultural support and support for local development in rural areas - can in the extreme fall mean that individual countries' finance ministers will instead use the EU funds to cover gaps in the national budgets, says Niels Chresten Andersen.

Terms are becoming more difficult According to the internal EU document that Politico has seen, the EU's budgetary people are proposing EU support to be followed with significantly harder terms than before. According to Politico, the document states that EU countries will have to Take the gap between women and men to receive money for social housing - or promote organic farming to gain access to agricultural support.

With a diminishing economy and war that rages right outside the door, the European Commission is under enormous pressure to manage its investments away from unproductive subsidies - automatically distributed to traditional sectors such as agriculture - and against new priorities such as defense and building the pan -European industry , Writes Politico.

Overall, this model marks a dramatic shift from the EU's current practice with fewer requirements to finance local regions or national governments. Niels Chresten Andersen sees the same perspective.

The leaked proposal is to bring together EU funds for agriculture, environment, education, research, health and regional development and more in one fund, where the funds are then distributed in 27 national programs.

- Today, EU funds are communicated in various programs. The funds for regional development are mainly distributed through regional programs, where the regions, municipalities, business, environmental organizations and others have a decisive influence on the prioritization of funds, he says.

Research, innovation, education, defense and other things will, with the plan here, get its own budgetary framework, which will have a direct link to the current plans for a strong prioritization of funds for defense and security as well as promoting the EU '' s competitiveness.

As, for example, counterpoints to China and securing critical raw materials, says Niels Chresten Andersen.

Resistance on the way If the new times in the EU are to become something, it will be with the upcoming budget that Member States will agree on by 2027.

The resistance is already emerging.

According to Politico, more than 130 EU regions criticized in an open letter recently EU Commission's idea.

Niels Chresten Andersen also says that the idea may be contrary to five articles in the EU Treaty. Namely, articles 174 to 178.

He also says that the proposal requires agreement among all EU's 27 member states and a majority in the European Parliament in order to become something.
