Title: Polens egen havvind går forud for Energiø Bornholm
Content:
We are aiming to become self-sufficient with green energy, but do not exclude that we will later cooperate with other Baltic countries, Poland's Ministry of Energy reports out after calculations from Ørsted have shown a big probable billion surplus on allowing Energiø Bornholm to deliver power to Poland .

Poland's most important target around green energy from offshore wind turbines is to produce the electricity even with the mill projects that Poland is already working on.

Only in the second row will not rule out that the country at a later stage would also like to cooperate with other Baltic countries on electricity from offshore wind turbines. For example, from Energiø Bornholm.

This is stated by the press department of the Polish Energy Ministry to the Official, after model calculations from the energy company Ørsted have shown that Denmark, Poland and Germany can probably look forward to sharing a profit of between DKK 15 and 20 billion if Poland is connected to Energiø Bornholm.

At the ministerial level, Denmark and Poland agreed to analyze Poland on the energy island in May, but the Polish ministry now emphasizes that Poland thus did not commit to anything.

The discussions with the Danish government in the spring of 2024 were preliminary, and no concrete and binding statements have been made on our part, Poland's Ministry of Energy informs the Journal.

Poland: Maybe later compared to Energiø Bornholm's planned capacity of 3 gigawatts, Poland is waiting to have almost the double amount of green energy from offshore wind turbines as early as 2030. Poland prioritizes its own offshore wind projects before foreign collaborations.

At the moment and in the near future, Poland's goals are focused on completing the projects that are currently underway. So far, all projects to be implemented in the Polish maritime areas will be radically linked to the coast, the Polish ministry said.

With regard to the sea wind's place in Poland's energy strategy, it remains of great importance.

We expect the installed capacity for offshore wind to reach 5.9 gigawatts by 2030 and up to 18 gigawatts by 2040, which will not only enable economic development but also contribute to climate goals and goals of energy security.

Poland's own large projects with wind turbines close to the coast mean that import of green electricity from other countries' offshore wind turbines is secondary in Poland's energy strategy.

However, it cannot be ruled out that in the future Poland will participate in hybrid connections with other Baltic countries. But at this stage in the development of energy from offshore wind, Poland's main focus is on the development of national projects and the extent of the challenges that their integration poses to the country's energy system and the development or reinforcement of the electricity grid, the Polish Ministry of Energy writes in its answer.

However, it is important to remember that our overall goal is to ensure that the energy change is socially just and does not leave anyone in the lap. This is why we first and foremost plan to base it on the adequacy of domestic production capacity and energy self -supply, the Poles end by writing.

Not surprisingly from the old power plant in Rønne, the consortium Baltic Energy Islands director Søren Møller Christensen calls it quite natural that Poland's main focus is on the country's own projects with offshore wind. At the same time, he states that in June Denmark and Poland agreed to analyze a Polish connection to Energiø Bornholm.

- How much they want to tell about the work before it is completed, I should not be able to say.

There may also be a certain diplomatic game because a cable for Bornholm not only provides an important security of supply to Poland, but due to the price difference with cheap electricity from Bornholm will also be able to affect Polish self -production, he says.

- The fact that the Poles point to the major tasks that they prioritize for the present makes good sense. It is publicly known that Poland has tightened itself hard with the development of offshore wind, which they connect directly to the coast, says Søren Møller Christensen.

- In any case, Ørsted's calculations point to the potential that Energiø Bornholm has for further development and that a connection to Poland will accommodate a great financial gain.

- I don't think any of us had an idea that this connection would come in the first phase of energy island, but it lies as a potential that Denmark and Poland agree to analyze the opportunities to realize, says Søren Møller Christensen.

Title: Tænketank sår tvivl om milliardgevinst på energiø
Content:
We cannot see how Ørsted has come to the conclusion that a Polish connection to Energiø Bornholm is likely to give DKK 15-20 billion in profits. For Ørsted will not tell how they have figured it out, says the think tank Kraka after meeting with Ørsted.

How do the simulations and model calculations work that brought the energy company Ørsted up to the fact that it is likely to make a profit of between DKK 15 and 20 billion to send electricity to Poland from Energiø Bornholm? It tried the think tank Kraka on Tuesday to find out for about an hour long meeting with Ørsted. But it did not succeed because Ørsted would not let Kraka look into the finer details of the number machinery.

This is stated by senior economist Frederik Læsøe Nielsen from Kraka, who in August went out with such a sustaining criticism of Energiø Bornholm that Professor of Energy Planning Brian Vad Mathiesen in the Journal called the Kraka report a party submission.

- We basically think it is fine if some alternatives to Energiø Bornholm are counted in its current form. I also see Ørsted's calculation as an attempt to do, says Frederik Læsøe Nielsen.

- It's hard for us to say something about Ørsted's analysis, because we couldn't know how to make. It was hard to get quite a lot of details.

- It is very difficult to relate to the value of a model where you do not know the prerequisites that have been put into the calculations.

Much of what we asked about, Ørsted would not tell us because they said it was business secrets, says Frederik Læsøe Nielsen.

- That is why we find it difficult to relate to the method that Ørsted has made the calculations from. But Ørsted, for example, does not count on how a cable for Poland, which of course affects the electricity price in Denmark, will affect the consumer and producer surplus, which are important elements of the Danish Energy Agency's socio-economic analysis.

- Therefore, it is difficult to consider Ørsted's analysis as an actual socio -economic analysis. And that is why we also think it will be fine if the Danish Energy Agency makes an actual socio -economic analysis, says Frederik Læsøe Nielsen. Do you say that Ørsted's calculations are of no value? - No. But Ørsted has come with a party post.

In my world, politicians have to make decisions based on representations from their own government apparatus.

Is it to call Ørsted's calculations for a party submission the same as saying that Ørsted has manipulated with its simulations? - No. But Ørsted has an obvious interest in this case. The fact that Ørsted has an interest in the case does not mean that they have counted neither right nor wrong. We just can't figure that out when we can't know how they have done the analysis, says Frederik Læsøe Nielsen.

- As economists, we are preoccupied with the fact that things happen in the right order. You have to count before deciding, and not deciding before counting. Therefore, we encourage the project to be paused so that the Danish Energy Agency has time to rain things through.

Title: Energiø Bornholm vil styrke Danmarks sikkerhedspolitiske indflydelse i Østersøen
Content:
Juel-Jensen believes it can give Bornholm a new status. Reader letter.

We all know that Energiø Bornholm is important for the climate and contains great potential for local and national business development.

There is also much debate about the project's finances, and we are currently awaiting new calculations of the price of cables and land plants. While we wait for these numbers, I would like to focus on another aspect of the energy island, which deserves at least as much attention.

The security policy aspect of my view is Europe's dependence on Russian energy one of the biggest challenges we face in these years. In this context, Energiø Bornholm is one of the most important pieces to build an energy supply and infrastructure that strengthens and secures Denmark and Europe's independence and security.

The first phase of the energy island is about establishing a connection from Zealand via Bornholm to Germany - one of Europe's largest economies and energy markets - and connecting this with large quantities of green energy. Later phases may include connections to Poland and Sweden as well as an integration into an upcoming hydrogen network in the Baltic Sea.

Bornholm will thus become a strategic energy center in the Baltic Sea with great security policy significance for Europe. This will significantly reduce the dependence on Russian energy in Europe - especially because the project will be the stepping stone and learning platform for a long support extension in the Baltic Sea and the North Sea.

Therefore, an important piece of energy island is not just about climate and green transition, although these are the most obvious elements. The project is also an important piece in Europe's security and political cohesion. With the energy island we connect with our neighbors through energy infrastructure, creating concrete mutual dependence, commits us to stand together and show that we stand together.

Seen from Christiansborg, Bornholm's importance will fundamentally change. Bornholm will in the future become an energy hub - not only for Denmark, but for the Nordic countries.

The island thus becomes a key to Danish influence in the Baltic Sea, where Denmark has great security policy interests.

But the energy island will also give Denmark a completely different voice in the Baltic Sea area, and if one manages to translate this influence into politics, so many things can become possible, including a better ecological condition in the Baltic Sea, which is a prerequisite for fish and other things that can give A good bathing experience.

Title: Bornholm i klemme - Energiøen er truet
Content:
The government's offshore wind turbine fias on Thursday warns dark times for Bornholm.

With Thursday's catastrophic result, where not a single bid for the government's offering of the planned offshore wind farms in the North Sea, Bornholm is now in a worrying position. Not only does it undermine the national ambition to reinforce Denmark's position as a green superpower, but also casts shadows over the island's future energy security and economic prospects.

The lack of investment desire in the offshore wind turbine industry is poorly announcing the billion-dollar Energiø Plan on Bornholm.

If the energy production from the new offshore wind farms does not become a reality, it can result in serious financial setbacks for the Energiø Bornholm project.

Before Thursday, financial pressure on Energi Bornholm was already great. And now it is further aggravated by this latest development.

The reality is that Bornholm's future as a load -bearing part of Denmark's green transition hangs in a thin thread. Without the expected revenue from the offshore wind projects in the North Sea to finance parts of the energy island and associated infrastructure, Bornholm is facing a billion -dollar growth fuser.

The concern of the Social Democracy Bornholm MP, Lea Wermelins, who is known for being a governmental politician, emphasizes the seriousness of the situation. When she openly doubts the government's Bornholmer plans, it is a clear signal that not everything is as it should be.

Bornholm's business community, politician life and municipal administration have engaged deep in the Energiø project, deserves far better. They now stand with the rest of Bornholm to potentially - along with the climate - to become the biggest losers in a game where higher powers fall off.

It is a serious reminder that large state -run projects cannot always control the forces of the market. Investors have clearly shown that they are not willing to tie up with large sums of money without clearer financial incentives - especially not in a climate with rising commodity prices and interest rates. Perhaps it is time for the state to reassess its role and conditions in these projects to ensure that they are not only attractive in theory but also in practice.

Title: Når jeg bliver borgmester: Politik som et middagsselskab
Content:
Let's speak politics as to a dinner party.

A few weeks ago I enjoyed a lovely evening with good friends and acquaintances. We spoke childhood, food recipes and local politics.

We were the table around from all the wings, we both agreed and disagree, and the mood was good.

At one point, my sidekick exclaimed: Read Hal Koch, and then we can talk politics! Maybe there were several around the table who didn't know that Hal Koch was a Danish thinker who was most active during and after World War II . He thought that democracy is about talking together and listening to each other, not just voting.

For him, respect and conversation was more important than quarreling about who is right.

Politicians as a mirror of our population When you look out over Bornholm's 23 municipal councilors, the idea is that they should be exactly as different as the Bornholmers are most - young and old, red and blue, few or many years on the school bench.

Many times we do not see the same in Bornholm's future. Some are for or against an energy island, an art museum or a food school.

Some want more street lighting where others would rather see starry sky. When we vote for a politician, they become a mirror of us - and their task is to solve our common disagreements. Two sisters and an orange on an agenda Two sisters are quarreling about an orange. They agree to divide it in two, but both are disappointed: One really would only have the juice to make juice, and the other would only have the peel to bake a cake. If they had spoken together, they could both have got what they actually needed.

The story shows why we have citizen hearings and committees in politics. They need to prepare the agenda so that the municipal council votes on the right alternatives.

It is through dialogue that we create the best solutions. Without conversation, the decisions become easy - but often wrong.

The power of the majority or compromise Think of two villages discussing where the bridge over the river should be built.

The large village has the most inhabitants and insists that the bridge should be built closer to their trade area, as it is here that it will benefit them the most. The small village has fewer votes, but they want the bridge near their homes because it will give them easier access to the city on the other side.

The majority in the large village could easily force their will through, but what happens? The small village will feel overlooked and refuse to cooperate in the future.

After talking together, they agree on a compromise: The bridge is built in the middle.

Both must give a little, but in return the bridge ties them together and ensures peace and cooperation.

Unfortunately, the compromise between a pure yes and a contentious no is just a stagnant maybe. The compromise is therefore only powerful after an open conversation.

So let's talk politics: We can start by asking ourselves - how are the real debate going? How is the dialogue at Bornholm? In August, 11 Danish mayors had announced that they will not be re -elected at the next municipal elections.

Many mentioned difficult working conditions and harassment on social media as a decisive factor. In October, Bornholm Mayor Jacob followed the comfort.

At his announcement, the commentary traces swam over with rose words as a honorary man, but also with statements of how understandable that it is and how dysfunctional a municipal council we are sitting with.

Who is running for another round in the mane? Only 10 of the municipal council's 23 members also sat the final round. It creates uncertainty about many things.

Recently, I talked to one of the most experienced municipal politicians at Bornholm.

The important thing is not who, but that the person has always been hardworking and wordy and made an effort both to cooperate and to stand by his own political attitudes.

After all, a good politician must be able to both, and this politician has really seen a little of each.

Therefore, it also came as a shock to hear the abandoning words: Major changes must really happen if I have to line up next!.

Democracy is about talking and not setting right.

Imagine if we at Bornholm could speak local pole, as if we were with friends of a dinner party open, respectful and curious.

We could start with social media.

The commentary tracks that become too often for quarrels and slogans rather than a platform for dialogue and understanding. Thus, the opportunity to speak disappears.

Instead, we are all pushed away from the dialogue and may choose to withdraw completely.

An improper story or a strong emotional look can quickly go viral, influence the majority and create a mood that is not necessarily based on facts. It makes any vote fooled. The reflection and the compromise become impossible and it just creates a toxic climate. Imagine if we could agree to invite to real conversation.

Democracy requires patience and willingness to listen and understand.

The dream I dream of a broad, rewarding collaboration across the middle.

If I become mayor, then I will start by inviting all politicians to an agreement: At Bornholm we are talking to the right. We have to agree and disagree, but the mood must be open - because only this is how we find the best solutions.

The Bornholmers have deserved it.

What is not told in connection with the energy island is that a complete transition to wind and solar energy will require a comprehensive redevelopment of the electrical system (cables, transformers, etcetera) to very large amounts.

Back-up? When the mills stand still and the sun does not shine, a back-up battery like the one in Hasle is not far. Instead, wood chips of biomass are burned to produce electricity and heat.

In addition to the amount of biomass that can be obtained locally/nationally, Denmark imports almost four million tons of wood pellets from the United States, the Baltic countries and others - including wood pellets made of green, living trees.


Green changeover?

We have been informed that biomass is neutral with regard to CO2. This has been decided in the EU, but the burning of wood emits large amounts of CO2, and it takes several decades before a newly planted tree can absorb as much CO2 as the felled forest could. On top of that, biodiversity is destroyed in large areas.

Lars Aagaard believes that CO2 emissions from the burning of biomass should be counted in the country where the trees are felled! Between 50 and 60 percent of Danish energy consumption p.t. from coal, oil and gas.

In light of the above, there is a very long way to actual green transition.

Nuclear power When C-L-J in Bornholm Radio, Saturday 14/12, is quoted as nuclear power is very, very expensive, the establishment takes many years and that the waste from the uranium is dangerous and he in the Journal, Monday 9/12 claims, claims, That no one has been able to point to an alternative (to Energiø Bornholm), it is either an expression of an almost criminal ignorance or a conscious denial of the facts.

There are - and the undersigned have written about it in a view of the Journal - alternatives that are not only more sensible, but also cheaper and far better than wind turbines and solar cells: small modular reactors running on thorium.

Thorium is an element found, among other things, in South Greenland in a quantity that will be able to cover the whole of Denmark's energy needs for a few thousand years. It is available freely and easily accessible and should not be broken using mining and processed as uranium shell.

Compared to a traditional, uranium-based system, about a ton of thorium will be able to produce the same amount of energy as 200 tonnes of uranium or 3,500-000 tonnes of coal.

Advantages The benefit of small modular reactors is great: - They fill no more than a 30 -foot container - they can be transported by ship, train or truck - they can be mass produced and sent around the country/world - they are far cheaper and faster to produce than conventional power plants - they can use used fuel elements from conventional, uranium -based works - thorium is not practically applicable to nuclear weapons - safety is in much larger than conventional systems - they can be moved around as needed - they can be expanded as needed.

So you could easily imagine that instead of the monstrous transformer system at SOSE, one could establish a thorium reactor down at East Power, where it can easily be connected to what existing system -and then they are able to deliver stable , Renewable energy! Title: Flytter fra hovedstaden til Bornholm: Lisbeth er kommunens nye direktør
Content:
Da hendes tre børn snart flytter hjemmefra, synes Lisbeth Røgind, at det er et godt tidspunkt at prøve noget nyt. Derfor søgte hun jobbet som direktør for de tekniske områder i Bornholms Regionskommune, og den 1. februar har hun første arbejdsdag.

Hvilke overvejelser gjorde du dig i forhold til, at du skal flytte din tilværelse fra hovedstaden til Bornholm? - Jeg har tre børn, som næsten alle sammen er voksne. Min ene, hun læser på universitetet og flytter nok snart hjemmefra.

Min anden, han flytter hjemmefra lige om et øjeblik. Og min tredje, han bliver student til sommer. Han skal sikkert også noget værnepligt eller noget andet. Så lige om lidt er huset lidt tomt, for så er vi kun mig og min mand og vores hund og to katte.

Jeg tænkte, det er et meget godt tidspunkt, hvor vi kan forsøge noget andet. Vi bliver lidt en sammenbragt familie, kan man sige, fordi de bliver selvfølgelig her, hvor de nu har deres tilknytning med uddannelse og så videre. Så det er mig, der kommer til at skulle finde en lille bolig på Bornholm. Det glæder jeg mig meget til, fordi Bornholm er et fantastisk sted. Jeg er allerede ved at finde ud af, hvad jeg skal lave i min fritid, som jeg selvfølgelig håber at få noget af.

Hvad er din relation til Bornholm? - Det er lidt langt tilbage, men jeg er faktisk kvart bornholmer, for min farmor kom fra Bornholm. Min oldefar var smedemester i Klemensker og blev født i 1858, og min farmor fik børn lidt sent, og hun flyttede så til København og mødte sin mand. Så min far har været meget på Bornholm, da han var barn, men jeg har ikke været helt så meget på Bornholm. Jeg har jo nogle fjerne slægtninge, men jeg har besøgt Bornholm mere som turist og nydt det meget. Hvad vil du bruge din fritid på, når du flytter til Bornholm? - Jeg har været i kontakt med Bornholms Kajakklub, fordi jeg ror i kajak, og jeg begyndte med det som voksen. Jeg har også set, om der var nogle fine strikkebutikker, for jeg elsker at lave noget håndarbejde. Jeg elsker også kunsthåndværk, og der kommer jeg jo lige over til den rigtige ø, kan man sige. Og så er der hele det bornholmske landskab. De gange, når jeg har været turist på Bornholm, så har det jo altså handlet meget om at bevæge mig rundt på vandfald og på klipper og inde i Almindingen og ude på stranden. Der er jo ikke den landskabs- og naturtype, der ikke er på Bornholm.

Det er jo helt fantastisk, og jeg glæder mig så meget til at vandre rundt. Jeg kan også godt lide at tage rundt i de små byer, for som arkitekt er det vidunderligt at se et fortov med Hasleklinker og gader med bornholmsk granit.

Er der et stykke arkitektarbejde på Bornholm, som du sætter særlig pris på? - Nu har jeg været i Rønne et par gange, og jeg synes, det er en super fin by. Der er både de helt gamle og lave, klassiske byhuse, og så er der også et fint torv med en god købstadsstemning.

I den helt anden ende er det selvfølgelig Hammershus og det anlæg, de har lavet deroppe, hvor der er kommet noget moderne og spændende til. Og så er der kunstmuseet, hvor der både er noget sammenhængende og gammelt, men også kommet noget ny, fin arkitektur.

Hvorfor søgte du jobbet som direktør for de tekniske områder i BRK? - Først og fremmest er det en fantastisk spændende stilling. Der er flere tilsvarende stillinger lige nu, men her rammer vi ned i noget, som virkelig er vigtigt for landet med energiplaner og grøn trepart og grøn energiø.

Det er simpelthen så vigtigt, at vi får gjort noget ved de fysiske rammer i vores klima, så vi fortsat kan have et godt velfærdssamfund.

- I jobopslaget så jeg også, at Bornholm rigtig gerne vil udvikling og især boligudvikling.

Lige siden min tid som arkitekt har det ligget mit hjerte meget nært, at der er gode boligforhold. Og så synes jeg også, det er meget spændende, hvordan man kan understøtte erhvervslivet og sikre, at det bornholmske lokalsamfund hænger sammen.

Der bliver også lagt op til, at der kommer til at være et stort samarbejde mellem erhvervsliv og fonde og de lokale og borgerne, og det ser jeg meget frem til. Hvad kan du godt lide ved at arbejde for en kommune? - Jeg holder virkelig af det, fordi vi er fundamentet for den danske velfærdsmodel.

Kommunerne er dem, som har ansvaret for omsorg og uddannelse og infrastruktur, og det vil jeg bare så gerne bidrage til. Jeg synes, at den kommunale arbejdsplads er sindssygt vigtig i et demokrati. Og demokratierne er udfordret, når man kigger rundt omkring.

Så det vil jeg rigtig gerne bidrage til, at vi har gode arbejdspladser og give et godt bidrag til, at vores medarbejdere har det godt, for det er ikke altid, at de har det nemt.

Hvad er din professionelle baggrund? - Jeg er uddannet arkitekt, og så har jeg taget en HD i økonomistyring og en master i ledelse. Jeg kommer fra en stilling som centerchef i Lyngby-Taarbæk Kommune, hvor jeg har ansvaret for udvikling og drift af alle ejendomme, veje og parker. Vi har et meget stort anlægsprogram, så der bliver bygget rigtig meget. Der er en letbane, der kommer igennem, og vi har lige renoveret vores fredede rådhus, og det har fyldt meget i min kalender.

- Inden da var jeg i rigtig mange år på Copenhagen Business School, der ligger inde på Frederiksberg, og der havde jeg at gøre med ejendommen og den lille smule park, som universitet har. Der byggede vi også rigtig, rigtig meget. Det var sådan et universitet, der ekspanderede og blev helt op til tre gange så stort i de 17 år, jeg var der.

- I starten af min karriere havde jeg to kortere ansættelser. Lige inden CBS var jeg på en tegnestue, som havde med landskab og veje og bygninger at gøre. Den havde sådan en lillebitte filial i København, så der sad vi under taget i en bylejlighed og arbejdede tre-fire mand. Og i mit allerførste job sad jeg på en tegnestue i Helsingør, der kun havde med landskab at gøre. Der sad vi også fire mand. Så man kan sige, at jeg er gået fra at være i nogle meget små steder i det private, til at være i nogle større og større steder.

CBS var jo staten, og bagefter arbejdede jeg i en kommune, så jeg har ligesom været i alle sektorer.

Hvordan var det at gå fra at arbejde i en tegnestue til at arbejde for et universitet? - Da jeg startede på CBS, havde jeg en overvejelse, om jeg ville miste et eller andet i forhold til det kreative. Når man skifter job, så er det jo godt, at man får noget nyt, men hvad er det, man mister? Men jeg fandt ud af, at jeg træffede flere kreative beslutninger, når jeg var bygherre. Der er utrolig mange valg, man skal træffe, når man er med til at lede et projekt igennem, mens da jeg sad på tegnestuerne, var der utroligt meget administrativt arbejde. Vi skulle sidde og beskrive, lave tilbudslister og rette de samme tegninger igen og igen, fordi der var en lille ting, som skulle rettes. Så den fase, som var den egentlig kreative, den fyldte meget lidt.

- Jeg havde også troet, fordi jeg sad på en landskabstegnestue, at jeg ville komme til at bevæge mig meget ud. Jeg elsker at bevæge mig, jeg elsker at komme udenfor, men det meste af min dag sad jeg bag min computerskærm.

Så det er en af de ting, jeg har prøvet på i min karriere, at finde nogle jobs, hvor jeg kommer mere rundt og taler med nogle flere mennesker og får lov til at se nogle flere ting og være med til at træffe flere beslutninger, fordi det er der, jeg trives. Der er også kreativitet i mange forskellige beslutninger, som ikke kun handler om det æstetiske og fysiske, men om hvordan man får tingene til at lykkes. Det fandt jeg ud af på CBS, at det var super sjovt, og at jeg godt kunne lide det, og så blev det min vej.

På CBS gik du fra at være medarbejder til at være chef med ansvar for andre. Hvordan var det skifte? - Det er jo helt tilbage i 2011, så det er jo efterhånden mange år siden. Men jeg kan godt huske springet. Jeg blev forfremmet internt, så mine tidligere kollegaer blev nu mine medarbejdere, og der tænkte jeg, hold da op, jeg skal lige tænke mig lidt om her. Nu har jeg et andet ansvar. Der må godt være et professionelt venskab, men man skal passe på, fordi man får jo noget indflydelse over sine tidligere kollegaer. Derfor besluttede jeg, at jeg bliver nødt til at kunne det ordentligt og få noget ledelseshåndværk, så jeg startede på nogle små ledelseskurser. Fordi det at lede andre, det er også en faglighed, og det kræver, at man har nogle værktøjer, så man kan gøre det ordentligt og professionelt, så det var det, jeg gjorde.
